# @ledger/design-system 0.7.0

Ledger, the product design system, as one file for agents and tools that cannot reach the running Storybook. Generated by `npm run build:llms` from the Storybook pages under `src/stories`, with the props tables their `<ArgTypes>` blocks render (a part's own props and the Base UI props it inherits, from the same docgen and options as the Storybook; the DOM's own attributes are not listed and still apply where a part renders an element), the token sheet in `src/generated/docs.json` and the public API baseline in `api/public-api.json`; do not edit by hand. The running Storybook and its MCP server remain the contract for verifying a change. The repository's `packages/design-system/AGENTS.md` says how to work on the package.

<!-- page: Introduction (src/stories/docs/Introduction.mdx) -->

# Ledger

Ledger is the design system behind the programme assurance product: one set of decisions about colour, type, space, shape, motion and behaviour, shipped as a package that any React and Tailwind project can install.

It is built on three ideas.

**Every design value is a token.** A colour is `color.text.subtle`, not a hex code and not a Tailwind grey. A space is `space.200`, not `16px`. A control is `dimension.control.medium` tall. Tokens are named for their role, so a screen reads as intent and the visual DNA lives in one place. Change a token and every screen follows; add a colour mode and no component changes.

**States are tokens too.** Hovered, pressed, selected and disabled are their own tokens, never alpha on a base colour. That is what makes dark mode a mechanical flip instead of a redesign, and it is the rule the lint enforces most strictly.

**Layout goes through primitives.** Box, Stack, Inline, Flex and Grid take token-typed props. Product code says `<Stack space="space.200">` and never writes a margin.

## Where things are

- **Guidance** is where to start: [Getting started](?path=/docs/guidance-getting-started--docs) installs the package and mounts its providers, [Choosing a part](?path=/docs/guidance-choosing-a-part--docs) finds the part for a need, [Recipes](?path=/docs/guidance-recipes--docs) shows how parts compose into a register, a record, a preview and a form, and [Which token](?path=/docs/guidance-which-token--docs) gives the short answer by job. The grammar, the lint rules, story conventions and the review checklist follow, and [Upgrading](?path=/docs/guidance-upgrading--docs) says what each part's status promises, what each version breaks and deprecates, and what code written against an earlier API is written as now.
- **Tokens** are the sheets: the palette ramps, the semantic colours in both modes, the type ramp, the space scale, shape and the control metrics. Each sheet is read from the generated docs, so it is the build, not a drawing of it.
- **Primitives** are the layout and text elements every screen is made from.
- **Components** are the parts: buttons, badges, controls, tabs, overlays and the rest, each with representative examples and a page with usage guidance.
- **Layout** is the application frame: the Shell and its areas, PageHeader, Section and PageSkeleton, with page examples.
- **Patterns** are the repeated interactions built from components: DataTable and its Toolbar, the pickers, previews, Forms, Editable, Composer and Chart.

Switch the **Mode** toolbar above to see any page in dark, **Contrast** for the increased-contrast values, and **Direction** to lay it out right to left.

<!-- page: Guidance/Getting started (src/stories/docs/GettingStarted.mdx) -->

# Getting started

The package is `@ledger/design-system`. It ships TypeScript source, a generated CSS layer and an ESLint preset. Its only peers are React and Tailwind 4.

## Install

The package is private: install the approved internal artifact, or a tarball made with `npm pack` (the README says how).

```sh
npm install ./ledger-design-system-<version>.tgz
```

The package ships `dist/` (ESM with declarations, from `npm run build`) and `src/`. Every bundler and runtime resolves the package to dist, in development mode too. A workspace that wants the TypeScript source, so a kit edit hot-reloads, opts in with the package's named `@ledger/source` export condition: in its Vite dev server's `resolve.conditions`, added to Vite's `defaultClientConditions` or `defaultServerConditions` (a list there replaces the defaults), and in TypeScript's `customConditions`. The stylesheets always come from `src`, because `ledger.css` scans the source for the classes your build needs.

## CSS

One stylesheet, in this order. The reset must come before the system: it clears Tailwind's default namespaces (colours, spacing, radii, shadows, fonts) so that only token utilities exist, and it would clear the system's own mappings if it came after them.

```css
@import "tailwindcss";
@import "@ledger/design-system/reset.css";
@import "@ledger/design-system/ledger.css";
@import "@ledger/design-system/base.css";
@import "@ledger/design-system/fonts.css";
```

`ledger.css` carries an `@source` directive pointing at the package, so Tailwind generates the classes the components use even though they live in `node_modules`. `base.css` is optional: it sets the colour scheme, the default border colour and the body's type and colour. `fonts.css` is optional too: the self-hosted Geist faces the type tokens name, so no Google Fonts link or copied `@font-face` is needed.

## The root

Mount the providers once, around the whole application:

```tsx
import type { ReactNode } from "react";
import { LedgerProvider, ModeProvider, Toaster } from "@ledger/design-system";

export function Providers({ timeZone, children }: { timeZone: string; children: ReactNode }) {
  return (
    <ModeProvider>
      <LedgerProvider locale="en-US" timeZone={timeZone}>
        {children}
        <Toaster />
      </LedgerProvider>
    </ModeProvider>
  );
}
```

- **ModeProvider** owns the colour mode; put `modeScript` in the document head, above the stylesheet, so the stored choice applies before the first paint. See [Mode](?path=/docs/components-mode--docs).
- **LedgerProvider** gives every part the reader's locale, time zone and direction, and the kit's words. Pass the same values on the server and the client. Without it, dates format in UTC and en-US. See [Locale](?path=/docs/components-locale--docs).
- **Toaster**, once, inside the LedgerProvider so its labels follow the locale. See [Toaster](?path=/docs/components-toaster--docs).
- **Shell**, the application frame, mounts the tooltip provider and the [Announcer](?path=/docs/components-announcer--docs) itself. A product without a Shell mounts `TooltipProvider` and `<Announcer />` once near its root as well.

## Components

Import every part from the package root, never a file inside it. Families export flat, named parts (`Dialog`, `DialogContent`, `DialogFooter`; `Breadcrumb`, `BreadcrumbLink`), each with native props and a ref; a few parts are compounds, used through their name (`Shell.Panel`, `Stat.Grid`, `PageHeader.Title`). Each family's page lists its parts and their props.

```tsx
import { Button, Stack, Text } from "@ledger/design-system";

export function NoMatches({ onClear }: { onClear: () => void }) {
  return (
    <Stack space="space.200" alignInline="center">
      <Text color="color.text.subtle">No controls match these filters.</Text>
      <Button variant="primary" onClick={onClear}>
        Clear filters
      </Button>
    </Stack>
  );
}
```

A whole empty region is the kit's [Empty](?path=/docs/components-empty--docs), with an illustration, a title and the next step; the example above is only a composition of primitives.

Components never import a router. Breadcrumb uses `render` to compose your router's link;
the link must accept the merged attributes, handlers and ref:

```tsx
import { Link } from "@tanstack/react-router";
import {
  Breadcrumb,
  BreadcrumbItem,
  BreadcrumbLink,
  BreadcrumbList,
  BreadcrumbPage,
  BreadcrumbSeparator,
} from "@ledger/design-system";

export function ControlTrail() {
  return (
    <Breadcrumb aria-label="Breadcrumb">
      <BreadcrumbList>
        <BreadcrumbItem>
          <BreadcrumbLink render={<Link to="/controls" />}>Controls</BreadcrumbLink>
        </BreadcrumbItem>
        <BreadcrumbSeparator />
        <BreadcrumbItem>
          <BreadcrumbPage>New control</BreadcrumbPage>
        </BreadcrumbItem>
      </BreadcrumbList>
    </Breadcrumb>
  );
}
```

The list, links, current page and separators are explicit parts. The default list keeps one line:
when the trail does not fit its container, the middle levels fold behind the list's own ellipsis
menu. `overflow="wrap"` shows every level on as many lines as it needs; use it when you compose a
disclosure of your own around `BreadcrumbEllipsis`, a decorative mark, inside a named button. See
[Breadcrumb](?path=/docs/components-breadcrumb--docs) for the full anatomy.

Navigation that looks like a button is a [LinkButton](?path=/docs/components-linkbutton--docs):
a real link with Button's variants, sizes and icons, the router's Link passed through `render`.
Button is for an action on the page; TabsTrigger uses `render` with `nativeButton={false}` for a
navigation tab.

```tsx
import { Link } from "@tanstack/react-router";
import { LinkButton } from "@ledger/design-system";

<LinkButton variant="primary" render={<Link to="/controls/new" />}>
  New control
</LinkButton>;
```

## Colour mode and contrast

Tokens flip on `data-color-mode="dark"` on the root element, or on the system preference when no attribute is set; ModeProvider and ModeSwitch set it for the reader. Increased contrast follows `prefers-contrast: more`, or `data-contrast-mode="more"` on the root. Nothing in a component knows which mode it is in.

```html
<html data-color-mode="dark"></html>
```

## Lint

The package exports an ESLint flat config. `recommended` makes every token rule an error and layout-through-primitives a warning; the [Lint rules](?path=/docs/guidance-lint-rules--docs) page lists every rule and preset.

```js
import ledger from "@ledger/design-system/eslint";

export default [...ledger.configs.recommended];
```

## Utilities in product code

Token utilities (`bg-surface-raised`, `text-subtle`, `p-200`, `rounded-medium`) are legal in product code; primitives are preferred for layout. Tailwind's own design utilities (`bg-blue-500`, `text-sm`, `p-4`, `rounded-md`) do not exist after the reset and the lint reports them.

<!-- page: Guidance/Choosing a part (src/stories/docs/Choosing.mdx) -->

# Choosing a part

The catalog is organised by family. This page is organised by need: find the row that names what the reader has to do, then open the part's own page for its props and states. When two parts look alike, the row says which one and why. A need with no row is a gap to flag, not a reason to build a raw element.

## Show a value

| The reader needs to see                                                                    | Use                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   | Not                                                                                           |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| A record's status, one word in a pill                                                      | **Badge** with a tone. One pill per row, in the status column.                                                                                                                                                                        | Indicator, which is never a pill.                                                             |
| Severity or health beside a label                                                          | **Indicator** (a Dot and a word), or the bare **Dot** in a tight cell.                                                                                                                                                                | A second Badge in the row.                                                                    |
| How many: unread, rows behind a filter, findings                                           | **Count**, after the name of what it counts.                                                                                                                                                                                          | A Badge holding a number.                                                                     |
| An identifier: AC-2(3), FND-2231, a hash                                                   | **Id**. Tabular numerals, inherits everything else.                                                                                                                                                                                   | CodeBlock, or a Badge.                                                                        |
| An identifier the reader will paste into a ticket                                          | **Id** with an icon-only **CopyButton** (`label="Copy ID"`) beside it.                                                                                                                                                                | A CodeBlock around one id.                                                                    |
| A label and value on one baseline, above the fold                                          | **Fact**, and **Fact.Group** for the four to six facts under a title.                                                                                                                                                                 | KeyValue, which is a rail row.                                                                |
| A label and value in a rail, one per line                                                  | **KeyValue** in a **KeyValue.Group**, which shares the label width and puts the label over the value when narrow; **Inspector** for a folding group of them.                                                                          | A hand-written definition list.                                                               |
| A headline number                                                                          | **Stat**; **Stat.Tile** in a **Stat.Grid** when framed.                                                                                                                                                                               | A Heading holding a number.                                                                   |
| A value that is missing                                                                    | **Absent**, the muted dash, which a screen reader hears as "Not recorded"; `label` says more where the context knows more ("No due date").                                                                                            | An empty string, a hyphen typed by hand, or "N/A".                                            |
| A name or value that stays on one line in a row, a rail or a list, readable in full        | **Truncate**, or Text `maxLines`; KeyValue does it itself. **useIsTruncated** when you cut the text yourself.                                                                                                                         | Truncating a sentence, a heading, an error or a notification, which wrap.                     |
| A mark that stands for something with no word beside it: a boundary, a met check           | **Icon** with a `label`; without one when it sits beside its word.                                                                                                                                                                    | A bare glyph, or an Icon that acts, which is an IconButton.                                   |
| Words only a screen reader needs: a mark's meaning, a heading the outline needs            | **VisuallyHidden**.                                                                                                                                                                                                                   | An `sr-only` span written by hand.                                                            |
| A section's name in a rail, a record's kind over a title                                   | **Eyebrow**.                                                                                                                                                                                                                          | A small Heading.                                                                              |
| A labelled paragraph, or authored text in several paragraphs or Markdown                   | **Prose**: a string child keeps its paragraphs and line breaks; `markdown` with `renderLink` for Markdown. **Text** `preserveLineBreaks` for one short note.                                                                          | Text with a bold first line, or HTML set by hand.                                             |
| Two or more short points: messages, conflicts, steps                                       | **List**, `ordered` for steps.                                                                                                                                                                                                        | Records, which are an Item.Group or a DataTable; labelled values, which are a KeyValue.Group. |
| A person                                                                                   | **Person**; **Avatar** and **AvatarGroup** for the mark alone.                                                                                                                                                                        |                                                                                               |
| A file                                                                                     | **Attachment**; **Attachment.Link** when the card opens or downloads a URL; **formatFileSize** in its description. The application owns upload, retry and removal.                                                                    | An anchor with the overlay classes copied onto it, or a raw byte count.                       |
| A date or a moment: updated, collected, a milestone                                        | **DateTime**, in the provider's locale and zone.                                                                                                                                                                                      | `toLocaleString`, or a formatter of your own.                                                 |
| How long ago, for activity and recency                                                     | **RelativeTime**; the exact value is its tooltip.                                                                                                                                                                                     | "2h ago" written by hand.                                                                     |
| A due date, an expiry or a milestone the reader acts on                                    | **DateLabel**: overdue, due today and due soon in words and an icon.                                                                                                                                                                  | A date in red text.                                                                           |
| What changed between two versions of a text                                                | **Diff**, inline, or side by side on a wide page; **diffText** for the counts alone.                                                                                                                                                  | Two full copies side by side, or both values in table cells.                                  |
| Source, a log, a command to paste                                                          | **CodeBlock** with `copy` when the reader will take it.                                                                                                                                                                               | A `<pre>`.                                                                                    |
| A keyboard shortcut                                                                        | **KbdShortcut** with `keys="Mod+K"`: the platform's glyphs and one spoken name. **useFormatShortcut** or **formatShortcut** for the same shortcut as text or `aria-keyshortcuts`. **Kbd** and **KbdGroup** for caps composed by hand. | A ⌘ or Ctrl cap chosen per screen, or a branch on the platform.                               |
| Events in order                                                                            | **Timeline**.                                                                                                                                                                                                                         | A Table of dates.                                                                             |
| Steps through an ordered path                                                              | **Stepper**.                                                                                                                                                                                                                          | Tabs.                                                                                         |
| What an action or a step waits on: the checks before a create, the conflicts before a save | **Gates**: each condition met or not, with what is missing and the one action that meets it; a list, never a score.                                                                                                                   | Progress, or reasons in a bordered Box or a grey line beside a disabled button.               |
| A completion fraction                                                                      | **Progress**; **ProgressStacked** for parts of a whole.                                                                                                                                                                               | A Stat with a percentage, unless it is the headline.                                          |
| Numbers drawn                                                                              | **Chart** and one of its kinds: Bar, Line, Area, Donut, Scatter, Heatmap, Treemap, Sparkline. **Chart.Frame** holds the data, size and format once, for a bare part inside.                                                           | A hand-drawn SVG, or the same props on the Frame and the part.                                |
| A chart's numbers as a table                                                               | **Chart.Frame** around the part: its Table toggle and its CSV lay out what the part draws. Name the columns with `xLabel`, `columns`, Scatter `zLabel` and Treemap `levels`. A colour-scale Heatmap in a Frame also offers Values.    | A separate Table beside the chart, or a `title` on hover.                                     |

## Lay it out

| The layout is                                                                                                           | Use                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Things stacked top to bottom with one gap                                                                               | **Stack** with a `space` token.                                                                                                                                                                   |
| Things left to right with one gap, wrapping                                                                             | **Inline**.                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| Something Stack and Inline cannot say                                                                                   | **Flex**.                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| Columns                                                                                                                 | **Grid** with token gaps.                                                                                                                                                                         |
| A padded or coloured block                                                                                              | **Box**. Padding and background are token-typed; there are no margins.                                                                                                                            |
| A child escaping its parent's padding                                                                                   | **Bleed**, the only negative space.                                                                                                                                                               |
| A titled region of a page                                                                                               | **Section**, with `count`, `description` and `action` when needed.                                                                                                                                |
| A collapsed Details block on a page body: provenance, counts, derivation                                                | **Section** with `title` and `isCollapsible` (`defaultOpen` to start open). Not a subtle Button with a chevron, or a native `<details>`.                                                          |
| A folding group of facts in a Details rail                                                                              | **Inspector.Group**, `defaultOpen={false}` when it starts closed.                                                                                                                                 |
| A record's Details beside its body, a closed Details disclosure before the body on a phone                              | **Shell.Aside** holding an Inspector, with the record's status as its `summary`, rendered right after the PageHeader or first in Overview.                                                        |
| A column that stays in view beside a long form: a wizard's steps                                                        | **StickyRail**, `from="lg"` where the grid stacks it above the form below `lg`.                                                                                                                   |
| The page's name and its actions                                                                                         | **PageHeader**: Lead, Heading, Title, Description, Actions.                                                                                                                                       |
| A record's name in a preview or a sheet body                                                                            | **PageHeader.Title**, which takes its level from the context or `render`. Not a raw h2 with the Title's classes.                                                                                  |
| The application frame                                                                                                   | **Shell** and its areas: Banner, TopNav, SideNav, Main, Aside, Panel.                                                                                                                             |
| Focus and an announcement when a client-side route changes the page                                                     | **Shell** `locationKey` (the router's resolved pathname or route id), with `getPageTitle` for other words.                                                                                        |
| A phone side-nav overlay that stays open while its links change the page in place                                       | **Shell.SideNav** `closeOnNavigate={false}`.                                                                                                                                                      |
| The product's search in the top nav                                                                                     | **Shell.TopNav.Search** in TopNav.Middle: a field-shaped button in a top nav at least 48rem wide, an icon button narrower, ⌘K from anywhere. It opens a **SearchDialog**.                         |
| Actions and destinations at the end of the top nav                                                                      | **Shell.TopNav.Item** in **Shell.TopNav.End**: they fold into one More menu when the top nav is narrow; the ModeSwitch and `persistent` items stay. Not a hand-built `md:hidden` menu.            |
| A part that switches layout on its own width, in a panel, a rail, a card or a dialog                                    | A container query on a **dimension.container** size: name the container and query it by name (`@md/<name>:`). A new switch point is a new token; viewport breakpoints belong to page-level parts. |
| Two panes the reader resizes                                                                                            | **ResizablePanelGroup**.                                                                                                                                                                          |
| A region that scrolls with the platform's own scrollbar: a dialog's body, a panel, a list                               | Native overflow on the region the kit already gives it (DialogBody, SheetBody, Shell.Panel, DataTable's frame). Not a ScrollArea or Scroller added around it.                                     |
| A scrolling region with a visible bar the reader can drag                                                               | **ScrollArea** and **ScrollBar**.                                                                                                                                                                 |
| A list or a strip of your own that scrolls, with an arrow at each edge that can still scroll, as menus and line Tabs do | **Scroller**, with **ScrollerViewport** and a **ScrollerArrow** per edge; it reveals a focused item on its own axis. Not an `overflow-auto` div with arrows written by hand.                      |
| A hairline between things                                                                                               | **Separator**. The parent owns the spacing around it.                                                                                                                                             |
| A raised container for a table, chart or facts                                                                          | **Card**.                                                                                                                                                                                         |

Body copy is **Text**; titles are **Heading** with the size from the design and the level from where it sits. A part's own title (PageHeader.Title, a Section's title, a Heading without `as`) reads the heading-level context; put a **HeadingLevelProvider** where an outline starts, with `level` in a portal, a rail or a dialog body, rather than `as` on every heading inside.

## Collect input

| The reader enters                                                      | Use                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               | Not                                                                                                                                        |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Any control's label, hint and error                                    | **Field** and its parts: FieldLabel, FieldDescription, FieldError. Pass `invalid`, `required` and `disabled` to the Field, which wires the ids. Field owns layout; the form owns values and validation.                                           | Hand-wired ids and `aria-describedby`, or red text beside the control.                                                                     |
| What fixes one field                                                   | **FieldError** inside the Field, with children or `errors`.                                                                                                                                                                                       | An Alert, or `role="alert"` text.                                                                                                          |
| Every error after a failed submit, each leading to its field           | **ErrorSummary** above the form, `focusKey` the submit count; `onSelect` opens another step or tab.                                                                                                                                               | A list in an Alert, or FieldError alone in a long or multi-step form.                                                                      |
| A required field                                                       | Field `required`, announced with the asterisk; native `required` on the control only when the browser should check it.                                                                                                                            | A hand-written asterisk, or "(optional)" in a placeholder.                                                                                 |
| Fields locked while a save runs                                        | **FieldSet** `disabled`, which reaches every control inside.                                                                                                                                                                                      | A raw `<fieldset disabled>`.                                                                                                               |
| One line of text                                                       | **Input**; **InputGroup** when it carries an icon, a unit or a button.                                                                                                                                                                            |                                                                                                                                            |
| Several lines                                                          | **Textarea**.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |                                                                                                                                            |
| A query that finds or narrows records, as the reader types or on Enter | **SearchField**.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  | Input `type="search"` in a hand-built InputGroup; a search box for a value the record keeps.                                               |
| A quantity the reader types or steps: days, a budget, a count          | **NumberField**.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  | Input `type="number"`.                                                                                                                     |
| Digits that name something: an identifier, a build number, a postcode  | **Input** with `inputMode="numeric"`.                                                                                                                                                                                                             | NumberField, which drops leading zeros and adds steps and separators.                                                                      |
| One of a few known values                                              | **Select**; **RadioGroup** when all the choices should be visible.                                                                                                                                                                                |                                                                                                                                            |
| One of many values, by typing                                          | **Combobox**. It filters; Select does not.                                                                                                                                                                                                        | A SearchField with a hand-built list.                                                                                                      |
| Several values as chips                                                | **Combobox** with `ComboboxChips`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                |                                                                                                                                            |
| Yes or no                                                              | **Checkbox** in a form; **Switch** when it takes effect at once.                                                                                                                                                                                  |                                                                                                                                            |
| Several choices that can each be true                                  | **CheckboxGroup** with a FieldLegend, and **CheckboxGroupSelectAll** with `allValues` for select-all. Put the group in a Field to describe and validate it; a required Field's legend says "(required)". Each choice is its own horizontal Field. | A FieldSet of loose checkboxes, `aria-invalid` on every item, or records from a long list, which are DataTable selection or a PickerSheet. |
| A pressed state on a button                                            | **Toggle**; **ToggleGroup** for one-of or many-of.                                                                                                                                                                                                |                                                                                                                                            |
| A day                                                                  | **DatePicker**; `entry="type"` for a day the reader already knows; **Calendar** on its own when the month should stay open.                                                                                                                       |                                                                                                                                            |
| A time of day, with no date                                            | **TimeField**.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    | Input `type="time"`.                                                                                                                       |
| A moment: a day and a time                                             | **DateTimeField**, which names the zone.                                                                                                                                                                                                          | `datetime-local`.                                                                                                                          |
| A range of days                                                        | **DateRangePicker**, with presets for periods; two DatePickers with `min` and `max` when the ends stand apart.                                                                                                                                    |                                                                                                                                            |
| Files, from a compact spot: a form row, a composer, a toolbar          | **FileTrigger** in a Field, with the constraints in a FieldDescription.                                                                                                                                                                           | Input `type="file"`, which reads as a line of text.                                                                                        |
| Files, dropped or chosen, checked against types and a size             | **DropZone** in a Field, with the constraints as its FieldDescription child; the accepted files become Attachment rows.                                                                                                                           | A primary that stays disabled until a file is chosen.                                                                                      |
| A filter on a register                                                 | **FilterChip** in a **Toolbar**.                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |                                                                                                                                            |
| A short draft with mentions                                            | **Composer**.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |                                                                                                                                            |
| A whole form                                                           | The **Forms** pattern: Field, controls, primitives and Buttons. There is no Form component. A create or edit form in a Dialog follows the form recipe on Guidance/Recipes.                                                                        | A Sheet or a page, outside a product's named exceptions.                                                                                   |

## Pick records

| Choosing                                                      | Use                                                                                                                                                                         |
| ------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| One value from a short, fixed list                            | **Select**.                                                                                                                                                                 |
| One value from a long list, by typing                         | **Combobox**.                                                                                                                                                               |
| One record with an id, a name and a status, by typing         | **RecordPicker**: a Command dialog with record rows. The caller supplies the rows.                                                                                          |
| A record of any type, found by name or identifier, to open it | **SearchDialog**, opened by **Shell.TopNav.Search** or ⌘K. The caller hands over the records, or runs the search itself (`filter={null}`). Not a CommandPalette of records. |
| Many records from hundreds, with filters and a running count  | **PickerSheet**: a Sheet whose body is a DataTable with selection.                                                                                                          |
| Related records the reader must compare before choosing       | **RecordBrowser**: search, compare, preview and select without leaving the record.                                                                                          |
| A command, not a record                                       | **CommandPalette** (⌘K) over the page; **Command** parts to build a list of your own.                                                                                       |

## Tables and lists

| The collection is                                                                                                                                            | Use                                                                                                                                                           |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| A register with sort, filters, pages, selection or a toolbar                                                                                                 | **DataTable**, columns declared by kind, with **Toolbar** above it and `fill` when it takes the window.                                                       |
| Records the reader searches, sorts, selects or previews inside a record, a tab or a panel                                                                    | **DataTable**, without `fill`. The task decides it, not the number of rows.                                                                                   |
| Rows whose order is the content and whose task is one choice or a definition: a version history with its current version, a profile's ordered source imports | **Table**, the markup alone, in that order. No search, sort or preview eye.                                                                                   |
| A hierarchy the reader opens and closes                                                                                                                      | **Tree**; **DataTable** with nested rows when the rows also sort and filter.                                                                                  |
| A summary of linked records in a rail or a card: how many, a way to add one, the few that matter                                                             | **Related**: a card with a Count, a way to add one, a row or card per record. Linked records the reader works through are an embedded **DataTable**.          |
| One compact record row with aligned parts                                                                                                                    | **Item**.                                                                                                                                                     |
| A checklist or work queue row                                                                                                                                | **TaskRow**.                                                                                                                                                  |
| A long list decided one record at a time, the chosen record's detail beside it: tailoring controls, setting parameters                                       | **WorkPane**: side by side when wide, a drill-in with Back to the row when narrow. A list the reader scans, sorts and filters is a DataTable.                 |
| The next record without leaving the list                                                                                                                     | **PreviewNavigation** in a **Shell.Panel**; **PreviewSheet** only when the task must hold focus.                                                              |
| A record's summary on hover                                                                                                                                  | **HoverCard** holding a **Glance**.                                                                                                                           |
| Search, views, filters and actions above a table                                                                                                             | **Toolbar**: search, `views`, `filters`, children, `actions`.                                                                                                 |
| The sort, seen and set when the headers fold: a register on a phone or beside a panel                                                                        | **DataTable.Sort** among the Toolbar's display controls. A table that never folds keeps its headers' sort.                                                    |
| A column's width, set without dragging                                                                                                                       | `resizable` on useDataTable: the column menu's Wider, Narrower and Reset width.                                                                               |
| Columns or rows the reader puts in their own order                                                                                                           | `reorderable` on useDataTable for columns (a grip and Move left or right in the column menu); `reorderRows` for rows, which turns sorting off while it is on. |
| A register's displayed rows as a spreadsheet                                                                                                                 | **downloadCsv** (or **toCsv** for the text): the visible columns and every filtered, sorted row across the pages, formula-guarded, with a byte order mark.    |
| A collection that can hold more than about 200 rows                                                                                                          | `pageSize` on useDataTable (a page of 25 to 100), or `virtualize`; `manual` with `rowCount` when the server holds thousands. Never every row drawn at once.   |
| A thousand rows or more in one scrolling frame                                                                                                               | `virtualize` on useDataTable with a `maxHeight` on the table, and no `pageSize`.                                                                              |
| A register's search, sort, filters and page, kept after the reader opens a record and comes back                                                             | **useTableQuery** with `storage: "session"`, or `search` and `onSearchChange` for a shareable URL. A table in a dialog, sheet or picker keeps its own state.  |
| A link to a filtered register, without a table                                                                                                               | **tableQueryToString**, **tableQueryToSearch** and **tableQueryFromSearch**.                                                                                  |
| One status vocabulary (label, tone, order) shared by several columns                                                                                         | `c.status` with a **StatusMap**; `tone` for a one-off column.                                                                                                 |
| Page controls                                                                                                                                                | **Pagination**; DataTable draws its own.                                                                                                                      |

## Overlays

Eight surfaces float over the page. The Overlays page holds the full table with what opens and closes each; the short form:

| Need                                       | Use                                                         |
| ------------------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------- |
| A short label                              | **Tooltip**. IconButton already draws one from its `label`. |
| A peek at a record, no actions             | **HoverCard**                                               |
| A small task at its button                 | **Popover**                                                 |
| A list of actions                          | **DropdownMenu**                                            |
| A focused task over the page: create, edit | **Dialog**                                                  |
| A modal selection or review                | **Sheet**                                                   |
| A quick task on a narrow screen            | **Drawer**                                                  |
| A decision that needs a word first         | **AlertDialog**                                             |

A value edited where it sits, with no form and no Save, is **Editable**. A larger change is a Dialog.

Inside an overlay:

| Need                                                                       | Use                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| -------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| The scrolling content between the header and the footer                    | **DialogBody**, **SheetBody**, **DrawerBody** or **AlertDialogBody**. Not a hand-written overflow div, a Card or a ScrollArea.                                                                          |
| The overlay held open while its save runs                                  | `pending` on Dialog, Sheet or AlertDialog, with `<FieldSet disabled={pending}>` and the submit Button's `isLoading`.                                                                                    |
| A dialog's or a sheet's width                                              | `width` on DialogContent or SheetContent: small, medium, large, xlarge, fullscreen. AlertDialog takes `width`: xsmall, small (the default) or medium, on Dialog's widths. Not a pixel `style.maxWidth`. |
| What a destructive decision affects: the records a delete removes          | **AlertDialogBody** under the header, not a long AlertDialogDescription.                                                                                                                                |
| A sticky header, a pinned cell or a fade that matches the surface under it | `bg-surface-current`: every overlay records its surface.                                                                                                                                                |

## Navigate and act

| The reader                                                  | Use                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| ----------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Goes somewhere, reading as text                             | **TextLink** with a router link through `render`.                                                                                                                                                                            |
| Goes somewhere, looking like a button                       | **LinkButton** with a router link through `render`; **LinkIconButton**, with a required `label`, for an icon alone. Not a Button that navigates from `onClick`.                                                              |
| Does something                                              | **Button**; **IconButton** with a required `label` when the icon is unambiguous.                                                                                                                                             |
| Cannot do something yet, and needs to know why              | `disabledReason` on **Button**, **IconButton**, **LinkButton**, **DropdownMenuItem** or **Shell.TopNav.Item**: still reachable, with the reason as its description. Not `disabled` alone, or a `title` on a disabled button. |
| Tells two similar menu actions apart                        | DropdownMenuItem `description`. Not a Tooltip inside a menu.                                                                                                                                                                 |
| Copies a value to paste elsewhere: an id, a command, a link | **CopyButton**; `label` for the icon-only form.                                                                                                                                                                              |
| Downloads a file the page built: an export, a CSV           | A Button or an Attachment Trigger that calls **downloadBlob** or **downloadText** (`bom: true` for a CSV).                                                                                                                   |
| Chooses among joined actions                                | **ButtonGroup**.                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| Sees where they are                                         | **Breadcrumb** in `PageHeader.Lead`, its trail links made with the router's `createLink(BreadcrumbLink)` or matched exactly, so only BreadcrumbPage is current.                                                              |
| Switches between views of one page                          | **Tabs** with `TabsList variant="line"`.                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| Opens a region                                              | **Collapsible** with **CollapsibleHeader** for a titled disclosure; **Accordion** when only one opens at a time; **Item** `isCollapsible` for a row.                                                                         |
| Switches colour mode                                        | **ModeSwitch**, inside **ModeProvider**.                                                                                                                                                                                     |

## Feedback and states

| The situation                                                    | Use                                                                                                                                                                    |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| A region with nothing in it                                      | **Empty** with an illustration, a title, one line and the next step; `render={<h1 />}` on EmptyTitle when it is the page's only content. DataTable draws its own.      |
| Something about this record, inline                              | **Alert** with a title, a description and an action.                                                                                                                   |
| Something about the whole site                                   | **Banner**, one at a time, in the shell's Banner area.                                                                                                                 |
| Short feedback after an action                                   | **Toaster**, mounted once.                                                                                                                                             |
| A change that moves no focus: a result count, a save, a new page | **announce**, through the **Announcer** that Shell mounts; mount one near the root without a Shell. A field's error stays in FieldError, and a toast announces itself. |
| Content with a known shape still loading                         | **Skeleton**; **PageSkeleton** for a page's first paint.                                                                                                               |
| An action in flight                                              | **Spinner**, or Button's loading state.                                                                                                                                |
| A failure                                                        | An Alert with a retry. Never a blank region.                                                                                                                           |
| Density of a table                                               | **Table** `density`; DataTable's Columns menu offers Compact rows.                                                                                                     |

## Across the product

| The product needs                                                                     | Use                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| The reader's locale, time zone and direction, and the kit's words in another language | **LedgerProvider** once near the root, the same on the server and the client, and **useLedgerLocale** for its formatters in your own code; see [Locale](?path=/docs/components-locale--docs). Not `toLocaleString`, the host's zone, or a copy of a kit label. |
| More contrast for a reader who asks for it                                            | Nothing per part: `prefers-contrast: more`, or `data-contrast-mode="more"` on `html` (`"no-preference"` pins standard). The tokens follow. Not a contrast prop, a darker class or a bolder border picked for one control.                                      |
| Its typeface                                                                          | `@import "@ledger/design-system/fonts.css"` beside ledger.css: Geist Variable, self-hosted. Not a Google Fonts link or a copied `@font-face`.                                                                                                                  |

## Not in the kit

These have no part yet. A screen that needs one says so in writing, with a recommendation, before building anything:

- A slider or a range slider, and a one-time-code input.
- A navigation menu, a menubar, a context menu, a carousel.
- A rich-text editor beyond Composer's short drafts with mentions.
- A board of cards in columns (a kanban), and a calendar of events.
- A file upload service: DropZone and FileTrigger choose and check files, and the application uploads them.

<!-- page: Guidance/Recipes (src/stories/docs/Recipes.mdx) -->

# Recipes

How the parts compose into the screens a product is made of. Each recipe names the parts in order and the story that renders it. These are the package's neutral shapes; an application decides which recipe each of its screens uses and records that in its own contract, not here.

## A register

A page that is one collection.

1. **PageHeader** with the name in `PageHeader.Heading` and `PageHeader.Title`. Nothing under the title.
2. **DataTable** with `fill`, so the header sticks, the rows scroll inside and pagination sits at the bottom of the window. Frameless: the toolbar sits flush above and a hairline closes the last row.
3. Its **Toolbar**: search first, saved views in `views`, filters in `filters`, Columns and Settings as children, one small primary in `actions`. The create action lives here, not in the page header. A secondary collection command such as Export goes in a labelled overflow menu beside Columns and Settings; the children fold into More when the row runs out of room.
4. Columns from `defineColumns` by kind. A date column takes the raw value; the name is a **TextLink** to the record; the id column carries the preview eye.
5. Every product table is responsive, the default (never `responsive={false}`), with the name at `priority: 0`. Lower-priority fields move into the row's More fields, a labelled "+3"; nothing disappears.
6. The empty states are DataTable's own: bare (illustration, title, one line, the same create action) and filtered (Clear filters). A first load keeps the toolbar over skeleton rows; a failed refresh keeps the rows under one **Alert** with Retry.

Story: Layout/Pages, Register.

## A record page

1. **PageHeader**: the breadcrumb in `PageHeader.Lead`, the name in `PageHeader.Title`, one primary or an Actions **DropdownMenu** in `PageHeader.Actions`. No back chevron, no sentence, no status badge, no second action row.
2. **Tabs** with `TabsList variant="line"` when the record has more than one view.
3. **Shell.Aside** holding an **Inspector** group named Details: **KeyValue** rows for state, owner, identifiers and dates, with the record's status badge as the Aside's `summary`. Render it right after the PageHeader on a record without tabs, and first in Overview's panel on a tabbed record: beside Main it is the rail; below the aside breakpoint it is a closed Details disclosure before the body, its row carrying the state. A tab that is a register fills the work area without the rail.
4. Body content in **Section**s. A single record is never a table; a description is **Prose**. Linked records the reader works through (searches, sorts, previews) are an embedded **DataTable**; a summary of them in a rail or a card, how many and the few that matter, is **Related**.
5. A supported inline change is an **Editable**; a larger change is a Dialog (below).
6. Missing record: an **Empty** with the search illustration, a title, a line and a route back. Loading and a failed load are different states from not found.

Stories: Layout/Pages, Record; Components/Empty, Not found.

## A preview beside a register

1. **Shell.Panel** opened by the row's eye, named by its `label`. The collection stays mounted, so filters, sort and selection survive.
2. The panel's outer header holds global navigation only, never the record's name: **PreviewNavigation** in `Panel.Actions`, then `Panel.Close`, and Back first when a nested frame is open. Previous and next walk the collection's filtered and sorted order across all its pages, not one table page; the application turns the table's page as Next crosses it. `recordLabel` has the status say which record arrived with its position ("Access review evidence, 2 of 6 records"); `openLink` is a real link that opens the full record in a new tab.
3. The body starts with an inner **PageHeader**: the record's name as its **PageHeader.Title**, an h2 from the heading-level context or `render={<h2 />}`, and its actions in `PageHeader.Actions` (one small primary, the rest behind an overflow **DropdownMenu**).
4. **KeyValue** properties below, then the record's sections at the panel's width; **Tabs** in one scrolling row if the preview has views. Long authored text is a labelled **Prose**.
5. Close and Escape dismiss the whole preview, and the Shell returns focus to the control the reader last used in the collection. Back is the only way out of a nested frame, and returns focus to the control in the parent frame that opened it.
6. **PreviewSheet** replaces the panel only when the task must hold focus, such as a version review.

Stories: Layout/Pages, Queue with panel; Patterns/PreviewNavigation, In panel.

## A create or edit form

The default create and edit surface is a form dialog.

1. **Dialog**, controlled: `open` and `onOpenChange` in the caller, opened from state by a Button whose words are the operation and the singular noun (Create task). The title and the primary say the same words.
2. **DialogContent** with a `width` step (`medium` for a few fields, `large` for two columns) and `initialFocus` on the first field. Never `autoFocus`: inside a dialog opened from state it becomes where focus returns, and focus falls to the page on close. Base UI returns focus to the opener by itself.
3. **DialogHeader** with **DialogTitle** and, when it helps, one line of **DialogDescription**.
4. **DialogBody**, the one scroller, holding a `<form id noValidate onSubmit>`. Never make the form, a `fieldset` or a hand-written `div` the scroller.
5. Inside the form, in a **Stack**: an **ErrorSummary** of the last submission's issues, then a **FieldSet** (`disabled` while pending) of **Field** groups: `invalid` and `required` on the Field, **FieldLabel**, the control, **FieldError** saying what fixes it.
6. **DialogFooter**, outside the scroll: a **DialogClose** rendered as a subtle Button (Cancel), then the primary, `type="submit"` and joined to the form with `form`, `isLoading` while the save runs.
7. **Validate on submit** with the primary enabled. On failure, the ErrorSummary takes focus and each item moves focus to its field; the entered values stay.
8. **While the save runs**, set `pending` on the Dialog: Escape, the blanket, Close and Cancel do nothing and the popup is busy. Move focus to the submit button before the fields lock; it stays focusable while it loads. A failed save ends `pending`, keeps the dialog and the draft, and says what to change; a successful one closes it with `open={false}`.
9. **A dirty dismissal** is cancelled in `onOpenChange` (`details.cancel()`) and asks through an **AlertDialog** nested in the DialogContent: Keep editing keeps the values and the dialog, Discard closes both.

Stories: Components/Dialog, Form, Form save fails and Short window; Patterns/Forms for the fields and validation.

## A dashboard

A page that answers "what needs attention" and sends the reader to the register that holds it.

1. **PageHeader** with the name alone.
2. A **Stat.Grid** (`frame="band"`) of **Stat.Tile**s. Each tile's `link` opens the register it counts, already filtered to that count (`tableQueryToSearch` writes the register's query); a linked tile holds no other control. `isLoading` holds a tile's place while its number loads.
3. Where how a count splits is the question (open risks by likelihood and impact), one **Chart** Frame whose title says what it counts and how it splits it, at the widgets' heading level (`titleLevel`), with its table twin. A mark that stands for records links to the register filtered to them: `link` on **Chart.Heatmap** returns the register's link for a cell, and the twin carries the same links.
4. One **Section** per question, its `action` a View all link (TextLink or LinkButton) to the full register. Inside, the top few rows as a **DataTable** given only those rows, with no Toolbar and no `pageSize`, so it draws no Columns, Settings or pagination; its name column links to each record as a register's does.
5. The recent activity as a **Timeline**, newest first, each item's subject a link and its time a **RelativeTime**.
6. Each region loads, fails and empties on its own: a Skeleton while it loads (a chart's own skeleton), an Alert with Retry when it fails, a compact **Empty** when there is nothing to show.

Stories: Components/Stat, Linked and Loading and unavailable; Patterns/Chart/Heatmap, Links; Components/Timeline.

## Working through a list

A long list the reader decides one record at a time (tailoring a catalog's controls, setting its parameters) is a **WorkPane**: the list beside the chosen record's detail when the pane is wide, and a drill-in when it is narrow, where choosing a row replaces the list with its detail and Back returns to the row. A list the reader scans, sorts and filters is a DataTable instead.

Story: Patterns/WorkPane.

## Choosing records

- One record: **RecordPicker**.
- Many records from hundreds: **PickerSheet** with a search, filters, a DataTable body with selection and a footer that says how many and what happens to them. Pass the DataTable as `table`, with the whole collection as its data, so the search filters the table and a search with no match offers Clear filters. It may collect one shared rationale, focused through `initialFocus`. While the save runs, `pending` holds the sheet and the primary shows it is working; a failure goes in `error`, above the buttons, with the choice kept.
- Records the reader must compare first: **RecordBrowser**. Its preview belongs to the selection task and never becomes a second record workflow.

Stories: Patterns/PickerSheet, Search with no match and Pending and failure.

## States

- Loading a page: **PageSkeleton**. Loading a region with a known shape: **Skeleton**. An action in flight: **Spinner** or Button `isLoading`.
- Nothing here: **Empty** (`size="compact"` in a small region). A missing scalar: **Absent**.
- Failure: an **Alert** with a retry, with the stale content kept usable underneath. A failure is never a blank table.
- Empty data and an empty filter result are different states.

## A toolbar without a DataTable

**Toolbar** over a plain **Table** or a list: the same slots. When space runs out, `filters` and then the display controls fold into More; on a phone the row wraps into two in the same order, the search with the saved views, then More with the primary. Stories: Patterns/Toolbar, Constrained and Phone.

## Confirming a decision

**AlertDialog** with a title that names the decision, one line of consequence, Cancel and the verb. It may open over the Dialog or Sheet that owns the decision. While the verb's command runs, `pending` holds it and the Action shows `isLoading`; close it when the command succeeds, and say what went wrong inside it when it fails. When the decision needs more than a line (the records a delete removes), put them in an **AlertDialogBody**.

<!-- page: Guidance/Which token (src/stories/docs/WhichToken.mdx) -->

# Which token

The Token grammar page explains the naming; the token sheets list every value. This page is the short answer to "which one": the tokens a screen reaches for most, by job, with the utility class beside each. Primitive props (`<Stack space="space.200">`, `<Box padding="space.150" backgroundColor="elevation.surface.sunken">`) take the token name; classes take the utility.

## Text

| Job                                         | Token                                                                 | Utility                             |
| ------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------- |
| Body text                                   | `color.text`                                                          | `text-default`                      |
| Secondary: meta lines, labels, descriptions | `color.text.subtle`                                                   | `text-subtle`                       |
| Tertiary: placeholders, timestamps, Absent  | `color.text.subtlest`                                                 | `text-subtlest`                     |
| Disabled                                    | `color.text.disabled`                                                 | `text-disabled`                     |
| On a bold background                        | `color.text.inverse`                                                  | `text-inverse`                      |
| Selected item                               | `color.text.selected`                                                 | `text-selected`                     |
