| A link, the brand                           | `color.text.brand`                                                    | `text-brand`                        |
| Danger, warning, success, information       | `color.text.danger` and the rest; `.bolder` for text on a subtle tone | `text-danger`, `text-danger-bolder` |
| A categorical accent (charts, avatars)      | `color.text.accent.blue` … `purple`                                   | `text-accent-blue`                  |

Icons have their own ramp, `color.icon.*`, at the same roles.

## Surfaces

| Job                                       | Token                                                   | Utility                             |
| ----------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------- |
| The page                                  | `elevation.surface`                                     | `bg-surface`                        |
| A recessed region: a sunken table, a well | `elevation.surface.sunken`                              | `bg-surface-sunken`                 |
| A card                                    | `elevation.surface.raised`, `elevation.shadow.raised`   | `bg-surface-raised shadow-raised`   |
| A menu, popover, dialog                   | `elevation.surface.overlay`, `elevation.shadow.overlay` | `bg-surface-overlay shadow-overlay` |
| A scroll edge                             | `elevation.shadow.overflow`                             | `shadow-overflow`                   |

Each surface has `.hovered` and `.pressed` siblings; use those, never opacity on the base.

## Backgrounds by meaning

| Job                                   | Token family                                         | Utilities                                                                                   |
| ------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| A neutral control or chip             | `color.background.neutral`                           | `bg-neutral`, `-hovered`, `-pressed`, `-subtle`, `-bold`                                    |
| The primary action                    | `color.background.brand.bold`                        | `bg-brand-bold`, `-hovered`, `-pressed`                                                     |
| A tinted brand region                 | `color.background.brand.subtlest`                    | `bg-brand-subtlest`                                                                         |
| A selected row or item                | `color.background.selected`                          | `bg-selected`, `-hovered`, `-bold`                                                          |
| An input                              | `color.background.input`                             | `bg-input`, `-hovered`, `-pressed`                                                          |
| A switch's off track                  | `color.background.input.track`, 3:1 on every surface | `bg-input-track`                                                                            |
| Danger, warning, success, information | `color.background.danger` and the rest               | `bg-danger` (the tone), `-subtler`, `-subtle`, `-bold`, each with `-hovered` and `-pressed` |
| Something on a dark surface           | `color.background.inverse.subtle`                    | `bg-inverse-subtle`                                                                         |
| A blanket under a modal               | `color.blanket`                                      |                                                                                             |
| A skeleton                            | `color.skeleton`                                     |                                                                                             |

Text on a subtle tone is the `.bolder` text token of the same tone; text on a bold tone is `color.text.inverse`.

## Borders

| Job                              | Token                                                | Utility                                 |
| -------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------- |
| Every divider and default border | `color.border`                                       | `border-default`                        |
| A stronger border                | `color.border.bold`                                  | `border-bold`                           |
| A text field                     | `color.border.input`                                 | `border-input`                          |
| A checkbox or radio boundary     | `color.border.bold`, 3:1 on every surface            | `border-bold`                           |
| Focus ring                       | `color.border.focused`, 2px                          | `border-focused`                        |
| Selected                         | `color.border.selected`, 2px                         | `border-selected`                       |
| Disabled                         | `color.border.disabled`                              | `border-disabled`                       |
| A tone                           | `color.border.danger`, `.subtle` for a tinted region | `border-danger`, `border-danger-subtle` |

Widths: `border.width` 1px for everything, `border.width.selected` and `border.width.focused` 2px.

## Space

| Token        | Value | For                                                    |
| ------------ | ----- | ------------------------------------------------------ |
| `space.025`  | 2px   | A hairline.                                            |
| `space.050`  | 4px   | Tight: icon to text, dot to text.                      |
| `space.075`  | 6px   | Compact: the gap inside a control cluster.             |
| `space.100`  | 8px   | Standard small: control clusters, chip rows.           |
| `space.150`  | 12px  | Standard medium: cell padding, a card header's inset.  |
| `space.200`  | 16px  | Standard large: card padding, form grids, most Stacks. |
| `space.250`  | 20px  | Comfortable.                                           |
| `space.300`  | 24px  | Relaxed: between a header and its actions.             |
| `space.400`  | 32px  | Spacious: page gutters.                                |
| `space.500`  | 40px  | Generous.                                              |
| `space.600`  | 48px  | Between sections.                                      |
| `space.800`  | 64px  | Between page sections.                                 |
| `space.1000` | 80px  | A hero.                                                |

Utilities take the same key on any spacing or sizing property: `p-200`, `gap-100`, `w-400`. Margins exist only as `space.negative.*` through **Bleed**; product code never writes a margin.

## Type

| Token                  | Size  | For                                                                                                                                                                     |
| ---------------------- | ----- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `font.body`            | 13/18 | Controls, cells, tabs, inputs, menu items. The UI size.                                                                                                                 |
| `font.body.large`      | 15/22 | Reading text, dialog body.                                                                                                                                              |
| `font.body.small`      | 12/16 | Table headers, field labels, badges, KeyValue; labels add `font.weight.medium`.                                                                                         |
| `font.body.xsmall`     | 11/14 | Metadata under a name, a hint beside a control, a chart's subtitle.                                                                                                     |
| `font.heading.page`    | 20/26 | The page and record title (PageHeader.Title) and a Stat's figure, semibold; Heading `page`.                                                                             |
| `font.heading.overlay` | 15/22 | An overlay's title (DialogTitle, SheetTitle, AlertDialogTitle, DrawerTitle) and a card's; Heading `overlay`.                                                            |
| `font.heading.section` | 13/18 | A section's title (Section.Title): the body size at semibold; Heading `section`.                                                                                        |
| `font.heading.display` | 28/34 | Display: a figure bigger than a Stat's, or the one title of a screen with nothing else on it, such as sign-in. Semibold; Heading `display`. Not a page or record title. |
| `font.heading.xxsmall` | 11/14 | Eyebrows, group headings, menu section labels (the component adds the uppercase).                                                                                       |
| `font.code`            | 12/18 | Code blocks only.                                                                                                                                                       |

A Section's title is `font.heading.section`, the body size at semibold, the size of the text it heads. `font.heading.large`, `.medium`, `.small` and `.xsmall` are deprecated and stay for one version, and a new title never takes one: they are `display`, `page`, `page` (or `section` for a section's title) and `overlay`. Prose never grows past `dimension.layout.measure`, 720px (`max-w-layout-measure`).

## Sizes

| Token                      | Value | For                                                                 |
| -------------------------- | ----- | ------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `dimension.control.xsmall` | 24px  | Button `xsmall`.                                                    |
| `dimension.control.small`  | 28px  | Button `small`, chips, menu items, side nav items, a Toolbar's row. |
| `dimension.control.medium` | 32px  | The default: Button `medium`, inputs, selects, combobox triggers.   |
| `dimension.control.large`  | 36px  | Hero forms only.                                                    |
| `dimension.row`            | 40px  | A table row; `.compact` 36px; `.header` 32px; `.menu` 28px.         |
| `dimension.icon.small`     | 14px  | An icon inside a small or medium control.                           |
| `dimension.icon.medium`    | 16px  | A standalone icon, an icon button's glyph.                          |
| `dimension.layout.rail`    | 272px | The rail beside a record: Inspector, Aside.                         |
| `dimension.layout.panel`   | 320px | The preview panel before the reader resizes it.                     |
| `dimension.layout.sidenav` | 228px | The side nav, expanded.                                             |
| `dimension.layout.topnav`  | 48px  | The top nav, and the banner above it.                               |

`dimension.part.*` holds a part's own sizes, such as a popover's width or a menu's narrowest ([Metrics](?path=/docs/tokens-metrics--docs)). Each belongs to its part: size a part through its props, and never pick one of these for its value; `ledger/no-style-design-value` reports one read anywhere but its part.

## Radius

`radius.xsmall` 2px, `small` 3px, `medium` 5px, `large` 7px, `xlarge` 9px, `xxlarge` 12px and `full`, as `rounded-xsmall` to `rounded-full`. The bigger the surface, the larger the radius: a control is medium, a card large. Which part takes which is one table, on the [Shape](?path=/docs/tokens-shape--docs) sheet; a part you build takes the radius of the part it sits beside.

## Motion

| Token                                       | Value | For                                                                        |
| ------------------------------------------- | ----- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `motion.duration.micro`                     | 70ms  | A toggle's thumb, a checkbox's tick, a chevron turning.                    |
| `motion.duration.fast`                      | 110ms | Hover and press colour, a tooltip's fade, a menu leaving.                  |
| `motion.duration.medium`                    | 150ms | A menu arriving, a section expanding, a dialog leaving.                    |
| `motion.duration.moderate`                  | 240ms | A dialog or sheet arriving, the panel sliding in, a toast, content rising. |
| `motion.duration.slow`                      | 400ms | Chart marks arriving, a drill-down redrawing.                              |
| `motion.duration.slower`                    | 700ms | The blanket dimming the page.                                              |
| `motion.easing.standard`, `.enter`, `.exit` |       | `ease-standard`, `ease-enter`, `ease-exit`. Honour reduced motion.         |

## What has no token on purpose

Structural utilities carry no design value and are allowed as written: `flex`, `grid`, `relative`, `absolute`, `sticky`, `truncate`, `whitespace-nowrap`, `sr-only`, `overflow-auto`, `pointer-events-none` and their kin. Everything with a colour, a length, a weight or a duration goes through a token. A value you cannot find here or on the sheets is a token to propose, not a number to type.

<!-- page: Guidance/Agents (src/stories/docs/Agents.mdx) -->

# Working with Ledger as an agent

This Storybook is the contract. A coding agent that uses Ledger reads it the same way a person does: the family page says what a part is for, the generated props say what it accepts, and the stories show every state the part supports. Nothing about a part is true because another design system does it that way.

## Where the instructions are

| Question                                   | Read                                                                                                                                                                    |
| ------------------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Which part answers this need?              | Guidance/Choosing a part, then the family's page.                                                                                                                       |
| What is a part for, and what does it take? | The family's page here: Components, Patterns, Layout, Primitives. Its `ArgTypes` table is generated from the source.                                                    |
| I know shadcn or Radix; what is different? | Guidance/Coming from shadcn.                                                                                                                                            |
| How do the parts compose into a screen?    | Guidance/Recipes, and the Layout/Pages stories.                                                                                                                         |
| Which value or class do I use?             | Guidance/Which token for the short answer by job; the Tokens sheets and the Grammar page for everything. Tokens are the only styling.                                   |
| How do I install it and set up the root?   | Getting started: the stylesheet order and the providers (ModeProvider, LedgerProvider, Toaster). Components/Locale for the reader's locale and zone.                    |
| What does the lint reject?                 | The Lint rules page.                                                                                                                                                    |
| How do I add or change a part?             | The package `AGENTS.md`, which points at the "Adding to the kit" checklist in the component library guide; Guidance/Writing stories for the story and page conventions. |
| Which part does the application use here?  | Not this Storybook. The application's composition contract, `docs/guides/product-patterns.md`, decides that; app compositions stay out of these stories.                |

## Through the MCP server

The Storybook serves an MCP endpoint at `/mcp` while it runs (`npm run storybook`, port 6007). The repository's `.mcp.json` registers it as `storybook-mcp`. Use its tools in this order:

1. `get-storybook-story-instructions` before writing or editing a story. Its output is the source of truth for imports, story shape and test conventions.
2. `docs-list` once, then `docs-show` for a family before using any of its props. A prop exists when the family's page or its props table shows it, or the package's `.d.ts` declares it. The props table lists a part's own props and the Base UI props it inherits (a Dialog's `open` and `onOpenChange`, a Switch's `checked`); the DOM's own attributes are left out and still apply. A prop none of them shows does not exist; report the gap rather than guessing.
3. `stories-preview` after any change that alters how something looks: a component, a story, a stylesheet or a token. A shared file with no story of its own is previewed through its consumers' stories. Report the returned URLs.
4. `test-run` to run the affected stories, focused while iterating and broad before handoff. Fix failures before reporting completion.

## Without the MCP server

`packages/design-system/llms.txt` is this Storybook's pages, each with the props tables its `<ArgTypes>` blocks show, the token sheet and the public export list, generated into one file by `npm run build:llms`. It is committed and the package tests fail when it drifts, so a cold checkout and an agent without MCP access read the same contract. It never replaces the running Storybook for verifying a change.

## What an agent gets wrong most often

- Using a prop from shadcn, Radix or Base UI that Ledger's part does not expose. Look it up first.
- Writing a class the lint will reject: an arbitrary value, a Tailwind colour, a margin, a `dark:` variant. Use a token utility or a primitive prop.
- Copying a kit part into product code instead of importing it. `ledger/no-kit-shadow` names the part to import.
- Reaching for a part without reading its status, the first line of its page. A Deprecated part is not for new code, and its line names what replaces it; an Experimental part can still change ([Upgrading](?path=/docs/guidance-upgrading--docs#status)).
- Importing a story helper. `Matrix`, `Specimens` and `Pair` lay out the stories and are not package exports: the stories that use them stay out of `docs-show`, and a story page that shows one is not code to copy. Lay out with Stack, Inline and Grid.
- Formatting a date with `toLocaleString` or the host's zone. Dates go through DateTime, `c.date` or `useLedgerLocale()`, in the LedgerProvider's zone.
- Editing `src/generated/` by hand. Change `tokens/` and rebuild.
- Putting an application composition into a package story. The package documents neutral contracts; the application is verified in the running app.
- Rendering both colour modes in one story. The toolbar switches the mode; a story renders once.

<!-- page: Guidance/Coming from shadcn (src/stories/docs/FromShadcn.mdx) -->

# Coming from shadcn, Radix and Base UI

Ledger's families are built from shadcn's Base UI compositions, so most names are the ones you know. The APIs are not identical, and the differences are exactly where an agent invents a prop. Read this page once, then look every prop up on the family's page before using it.

## The three differences that matter most

**`render`, not `asChild`.** Ledger is on Base UI, not Radix. A part composes another element through `render={<a href="…" />}` (or a function). `asChild` does not exist anywhere in the package.

**Tokens, not the shadcn theme.** There is no `bg-background`, `text-muted-foreground` or `bg-primary` from shadcn's CSS variables, and no `dark:` variant. Every colour, space, radius and type value is a Ledger token utility (`bg-surface`, `text-subtle`, `border-default`, `p-200`, `font-body-small`) or a primitive prop. The lint rejects the rest; the theme names below say what each shadcn colour is in Ledger, and the Which token page lists what to reach for. Two names are the same in both: `border-input` and `bg-input` are Ledger's own tokens for a field's border and background.

**`cn` from the package.** Import it from `@ledger/design-system/cn`. There is no `lib/utils`.

## Theme names

shadcn's colour names and the Ledger class for the same job. The lint reports each of these with the class to write, which it also offers as an editor suggestion when the class does the same job; with an opacity modifier (`bg-muted/50`), it names the colour and leaves the shade to a state token, since Ledger never dims a token with alpha.

| shadcn | What it is | In Ledger |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `bg-background` | Page background | `bg-surface` |
| `bg-card` | Card background | `bg-surface-raised` |
| `bg-popover` | Popover background | `bg-surface-overlay` |
| `bg-primary` | Primary background | `bg-brand-bold` |
| `bg-secondary` | Secondary background | `bg-neutral` |
| `bg-muted` | Muted background | `bg-neutral` for a neutral fill, `bg-surface-sunken` for a recessed region; `bg-selected` on a selected, checked or pressed item |
| `bg-accent` | Hover background | `bg-neutral-subtle-hovered`; `bg-selected` on a selected, checked or pressed item. Ledger's `accent-*` colours are hues with no meaning. |
| `bg-destructive` | Destructive background | `bg-danger-bold` |
| `bg-foreground` | Text colour as a fill | `bg-neutral-bold` |
| `bg-border` | Border colour as a fill | `border-default`. A line between items is Separator, or a border side such as `border-t`. |
| `text-foreground` | Text colour | `text-default` |
| `text-card-foreground` | Text colour on a card | `text-default` |
| `text-popover-foreground` | Text colour in a popover | `text-default` |
| `text-muted-foreground` | Secondary text colour | `text-subtle`; `text-subtlest` for a placeholder |
| `text-primary` | Primary colour as text | `text-brand` |
| `text-primary-foreground` | Text colour on the primary background | `text-inverse` |
| `text-secondary-foreground` | Text colour on the secondary background | `text-default` |
| `text-accent-foreground` | Text colour on a hovered item | `text-default`; `text-selected` on a selected, checked or pressed item. Ledger's `accent-*` colours are hues with no meaning. |
| `text-destructive` | Destructive text colour | `text-danger` |
| `text-destructive-foreground` | Text colour on the destructive background | `text-inverse` |
| `text-background` | Page colour as text | `text-inverse` |
| `fill-foreground` | Text colour as an SVG fill | `text-default`. An SVG takes its text colour through `fill-current`, beside a `text-*` token. |
| `border-border` | Border colour | `border-default` |
| `border-primary` | Primary colour as a border | `border-brand` |
| `border-destructive` | Destructive border colour | `border-danger` |
| `border-ring` | Focused border colour | `border-focused` |
| `ring-ring` | Focus ring colour | `outline-focused` for a control, `outline-field-focused` for a field |
| `outline-ring` | Focus outline colour | `outline-focused` for a control, `outline-field-focused` for a field |
| `ring-destructive` | Invalid ring colour | `outline-danger` for a control, `outline-field-danger` for a field |
| `ring-offset-background` | Colour between a control and its focus ring | `outline-focused`. The focus outline sets its own offset. |
| `bg-sidebar` | Sidebar background | `bg-surface-sunken`. `Shell.SideNav` is the side navigation and sets its own colours. |
| `text-sidebar-foreground` | Sidebar text colour | `text-default`. `Shell.SideNav` is the side navigation and sets its own colours. |
| `bg-sidebar-accent` | Sidebar hover background | `bg-neutral-subtle-hovered`; `bg-selected` on a selected, checked or pressed item. `Shell.SideNav` is the side navigation and sets its own colours. |
| `text-sidebar-accent-foreground` | Text colour on a hovered sidebar item | `text-default`; `text-selected` on a selected, checked or pressed item. `Shell.SideNav` is the side navigation and sets its own colours. |
| `bg-sidebar-primary` | Sidebar primary background | `bg-brand-bold`. `Shell.SideNav` is the side navigation and sets its own colours. |
| `text-sidebar-primary-foreground` | Text colour on the sidebar primary background | `text-inverse`. `Shell.SideNav` is the side navigation and sets its own colours. |
| `border-sidebar-border` | Sidebar border colour | `border-default`. `Shell.SideNav` is the side navigation and sets its own colours. |
| `bg-sidebar-border` | Sidebar border colour as a fill | `border-default`. A line between items is Separator, or a border side such as `border-t`. |
| `ring-sidebar-ring` | Sidebar focus ring colour | `outline-focused`. `Shell.SideNav` is the side navigation and sets its own colours. |

## Name by name

| You know                                                                          | In Ledger                                                                                                                                         | What differs                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Button                                                                            | **Button**, **IconButton**, **LinkButton**, **LinkIconButton**                                                                                    | A focus-preserving `isLoading` state and `disabledReason`. IconButton needs a `label` and draws its own Tooltip. Navigation is a LinkButton or LinkIconButton: a real link, the router's Link through `render`. |
| Badge                                                                             | **Badge**                                                                                                                                         | Six variants plus semantic `tone`s and two sizes. A status is one Badge per row; severity is **Indicator**, a number is **Count**.                                                                              |
| Label, Field                                                                      | **Field** and its parts: **FieldLabel**, **FieldDescription**, **FieldError**; **FieldSet** and **FieldLegend** for a group                       | No standalone Label. Field is Base UI's Field.Root: it binds the control inside it and takes `invalid`, `required` and `disabled`. **ErrorSummary** lists a failed submission's errors.                         |
| Form (react-hook-form)                                                            | The **Forms** pattern                                                                                                                             | No Form component. TanStack Form owns state and validation; Field, the controls and the primitives are the presentation.                                                                                        |
| Input                                                                             | **Input**; **SearchField** for a query; **NumberField** for a quantity                                                                            | Input wraps Base UI's Input. Labels and errors belong to Field. A search box is SearchField and a stepped number NumberField, not `type="search"` or `type="number"`.                                           |
| Input Group                                                                       | **InputGroup** and its parts                                                                                                                      | Flat shadcn Base UI composition; addons, text, buttons and a textarea variant.                                                                                                                                  |
| Textarea                                                                          | **Textarea**                                                                                                                                      | A native textarea on Base UI's Field.Control, so a Field binds it as it does Input.                                                                                                                             |
| Select, Native Select                                                             | **Select**                                                                                                                                        | Native Select is removed. Select does not filter; a list that needs typing is **Combobox**.                                                                                                                     |
| Combobox, Command as a picker                                                     | **Combobox**; **RecordPicker** for records                                                                                                        | Combobox is flat Base UI composition with chips. A picker of records with ids and statuses is the RecordPicker pattern.                                                                                         |
| Command (cmdk)                                                                    | **Command** parts, **CommandPalette**                                                                                                             | The palette takes plain command objects and stays presentational.                                                                                                                                               |
| Checkbox, Radio Group, Switch                                                     | Same names; **CheckboxGroup** for several                                                                                                         | Base UI underneath; `render` for composition. CheckboxGroup names the group with a FieldLegend and takes **CheckboxGroupSelectAll**.                                                                            |
| Toggle, Toggle Group                                                              | Same names                                                                                                                                        | Icon-only toggles need `aria-label`.                                                                                                                                                                            |
| Calendar, Date Picker, date and time inputs                                       | **Calendar**, **DatePicker**, **DateRangePicker**, **TimeField**, **DateTimeField**; **DateTime**, **RelativeTime** and **DateLabel** to show one | react-day-picker underneath. DatePicker holds and reports an ISO day, DateRangePicker `{ start, end }` and TimeField an ISO time; DateTimeField a moment in the LedgerProvider's zone.                          |
| Dialog, Alert Dialog, Sheet, Drawer, Popover, Tooltip, Hover Card, Dropdown Menu  | Same names                                                                                                                                        | All Base UI. The Overlays page says which surface fits which task; Drawer is the gesture bottom sheet, Sheet the side panel.                                                                                    |
| Sonner, Toast                                                                     | **Toaster** and the Toast parts                                                                                                                   | Base UI Toast with a native manager API. Mount once near the root.                                                                                                                                              |
| Alert                                                                             | **Alert** with **AlertAction**                                                                                                                    | Explicit title, description and action parts.                                                                                                                                                                   |
| Tabs                                                                              | **Tabs**, `TabsList variant="line"`                                                                                                               | The line variant fills its container with one border and scrolls in one row; do not add wrapping or width classes.                                                                                              |
| Accordion, Collapsible                                                            | Same names                                                                                                                                        | Base UI.                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| Table                                                                             | **Table** for markup; **DataTable** for state                                                                                                     | DataTable is a TanStack Table 9 instance with columns declared by kind (`defineColumns`), a Toolbar and `fill`; it fits its frame unless `responsive={false}`.                                                  |
| Data Table (shadcn recipe)                                                        | **DataTable**                                                                                                                                     | It is a pattern with a hook, not a page recipe you copy.                                                                                                                                                        |
| Sidebar                                                                           | **Shell** and its areas                                                                                                                           | The whole application frame: Banner, TopNav, SideNav with an icon rail, Main, Aside, Panel. Not a standalone sidebar.                                                                                           |
| Breadcrumb                                                                        | **Breadcrumb**                                                                                                                                    | `BreadcrumbLink` takes a router link through `render`.                                                                                                                                                          |
| Card                                                                              | **Card**                                                                                                                                          | Same parts, token surfaces.                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| Avatar                                                                            | **Avatar**, **AvatarGroup**, **AvatarBadge**                                                                                                      | Flat shadcn Base UI composition with Ledger sizes and accents.                                                                                                                                                  |
| Skeleton, Spinner, Progress                                                       | Same names, plus **PageSkeleton** and **ProgressStacked**                                                                                         |                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| Empty, Item, Kbd, Button Group                                                    | Same names                                                                                                                                        | Same part structure. DataTable draws its own Empty.                                                                                                                                                             |
| Chart                                                                             | **Chart** and its kinds                                                                                                                           | Recharts underneath as in shadcn; Ledger adds the Frame, the table twin, drill-down, export and the chart tokens.                                                                                               |
| Resizable, Scroll Area, Separator, Pagination                                     | Same names                                                                                                                                        |                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| Typography (`<h1 className=…>`)                                                   | **Heading**, **Text**, **Eyebrow**, **Prose**                                                                                                     | Type is a composite token on a primitive, never a class list.                                                                                                                                                   |
| Navigation Menu, Menubar, Context Menu, Carousel, Aspect Ratio, Slider, Input OTP | Not in Ledger                                                                                                                                     | A need for one is flagged in writing before it is built.                                                                                                                                                        |

## Parts Ledger has that shadcn does not

These carry the product's vocabulary and have no shadcn analogue, so nothing you know applies: **Id**, **Count**, **Indicator** and **Dot**, **Fact**, **KeyValue** and **Inspector**, **Stat**, **Absent**, **Eyebrow**, **Prose**, **List**, **Truncate**, **VisuallyHidden**, **Icon**, **Person**, **Attachment**, **FileTrigger**, **DropZone**, **CopyButton**, **Diff**, **KbdShortcut**, **CodeBlock**, **Timeline**, **Stepper**, **Gates**, **Glance**, **Related**, **TaskRow**, **Composer**, **Editable**, **FilterChip**, **Toolbar**, **Scroller**, **PickerSheet**, **RecordBrowser**, **SearchDialog**, **PreviewSheet**, **PreviewNavigation**, **PageHeader**, **Section**, **CollapsibleHeader**, **HeadingLevelProvider**, **Tree**, **Banner**, **Announcer** and **LedgerProvider**. Read their pages; the Choosing a part page says when each one is the answer.

<!-- page: Guidance/Upgrading (src/stories/docs/Upgrading.mdx) -->

# Upgrading

What code written against an earlier Ledger API is written as now, family by family. A family's page documents its current API, with at most one line for a deprecated spelling that still works; the earlier spellings live here. Where a rename has one answer, `ledger/no-deprecated-name` reports it and its fix writes the new name ([Lint rules](?path=/docs/guidance-lint-rules--docs)); `CHANGELOG.md` says which version drops each deprecated alias.

## Status

Every family page opens with its status, the first line under its title.

| Status           | What it promises                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| ---------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Stable**       | The API is the contract. A change to it ships in a minor version and is listed in `CHANGELOG.md` under Breaking or Deprecated; a rename keeps an `@deprecated` alias for one version, with a `ledger/no-deprecated-name` fix where it has one answer, and this page says what to write. |
| **Experimental** | The part ships, is documented and passes every check, but its API is still open: no product screen has used it, so that first use can still change it before it is stable. The status line says why and who owns it.                                                                    |
| **Deprecated**   | The part still works for one version and then leaves the package. The status line names what to use instead, and this page says how to move.                                                                                                                                            |

A new part is Experimental until a product screen uses it and its page, plays and checks hold, and then Stable ([Testing and review](?path=/docs/guidance-testing-and-review--docs), Ownership and lifecycle). Stable names the contract, not this application's use: the kit serves more than one product, and a stable part that no screen here renders keeps its contract. A page that compares parts or describes a composition (Overlays, Forms, Page composition, Density, the Shell's icon rail and the Primitives overview) documents no part of its own and has no status.

## 0.7.0

What code written for 0.6.0 changes in 0.7.0. Each line links the section below that says what to write.

### Breaking

- **The package resolves `dist/` under every condition but `@ledger/source`**, `development` included; a workspace that compiled the TypeScript source opts in ([Package](?path=/docs/guidance-upgrading--docs#package)).
- **DataTable fits its frame unless it says `responsive={false}`**, and a row's More fields control is a labelled "+N" ([DataTable](?path=/docs/guidance-upgrading--docs#datatable)).
- **A tree's chevron is a leading column of its own**, `Table.Disclosure`, and `tree.column` is gone ([Table](?path=/docs/guidance-upgrading--docs#table)).
- **Chart.Donut's `label` names the ring**, as it names every plot; the words in the middle are `centerLabel` ([Chart](?path=/docs/guidance-upgrading--docs#chart)).
- **The page shapes that were parts are gone**: IndexPage, ShowPage, RecordHeader, PreviewRail, PreviewSplit, the standalone Panel and Block ([Pages](?path=/docs/guidance-upgrading--docs#pages)).
- **Below the aside breakpoint, Shell.Aside is a closed Details disclosure where the route renders it**, no longer a block after Main's content ([Shell](?path=/docs/guidance-upgrading--docs#shell)).
- **The kit's private layout classes are its parts' own**: `sticky-rail`, `sticky-bar`, `min-h-work`, `grid-cols-list-detail`, `grid-cols-main-rail` and the `shell-*` regions ([Layout classes](?path=/docs/guidance-upgrading--docs#layout-classes)).
- **The document-wide density is gone**: no provider, switch, hook, storage key or script ([Density](?path=/docs/guidance-upgrading--docs#density)).
- **Tailwind's `2xl` breakpoint is gone**: the kit's seven breakpoints stand, and `2xl:` generates nothing ([Layout classes](?path=/docs/guidance-upgrading--docs#layout-classes)).
- **`useRequired` is gone**, for a form library's validation ([Field](?path=/docs/guidance-upgrading--docs#field)).
- **The 0.5.0 disclosure API is gone**: `Collapsible.Group`, a Collapsible's or an Accordion's `title`, `count` and `headingLevel`, and `DisclosureHeading` ([Collapsible](?path=/docs/guidance-upgrading--docs#collapsible)).
- **`Tiles` and `Related.Row` are gone**, for Stat.Grid and Item ([Stat](?path=/docs/guidance-upgrading--docs#stat), [Related](?path=/docs/guidance-upgrading--docs#related)).
- **Stepper and Timeline need a `label`** ([Stepper and Timeline](?path=/docs/guidance-upgrading--docs#stepper-and-timeline)).
- **NativeSelect is gone**, for Select ([Select](?path=/docs/guidance-upgrading--docs#select)).
- **PickerSheet and RecordBrowser count in one phrase**, "N selected" or "N of M selected", and PickerSheet's `total` counts every row that can be chosen ([PickerSheet and RecordBrowser](?path=/docs/guidance-upgrading--docs#pickersheet-and-recordbrowser)).
- **These families take Base UI's parts and shadcn's composition**: named flat parts in place of configured props and compound members, `render` in place of `asChild`, and native props and a ref on each part's own element. [Alert](?path=/docs/guidance-upgrading--docs#alert), [AlertDialog](?path=/docs/guidance-upgrading--docs#alertdialog), [Avatar](?path=/docs/guidance-upgrading--docs#avatar), [Badge](?path=/docs/guidance-upgrading--docs#badge), [Breadcrumb](?path=/docs/guidance-upgrading--docs#breadcrumb), [ButtonGroup](?path=/docs/guidance-upgrading--docs#buttongroup), [Card](?path=/docs/guidance-upgrading--docs#card), [Checkbox](?path=/docs/guidance-upgrading--docs#checkbox), [Collapsible](?path=/docs/guidance-upgrading--docs#collapsible) and Accordion, [Combobox](?path=/docs/guidance-upgrading--docs#combobox), [Command](?path=/docs/guidance-upgrading--docs#command), [Dialog and Sheet](?path=/docs/guidance-upgrading--docs#dialog-and-sheet), [Drawer](?path=/docs/guidance-upgrading--docs#drawer), [DropdownMenu](?path=/docs/guidance-upgrading--docs#dropdownmenu), [Empty](?path=/docs/guidance-upgrading--docs#empty), [Field](?path=/docs/guidance-upgrading--docs#field), [HoverCard](?path=/docs/guidance-upgrading--docs#hovercard), [InputGroup](?path=/docs/guidance-upgrading--docs#inputgroup), [Pagination](?path=/docs/guidance-upgrading--docs#pagination), [Popover](?path=/docs/guidance-upgrading--docs#popover), [Progress](?path=/docs/guidance-upgrading--docs#progress), [RadioGroup](?path=/docs/guidance-upgrading--docs#radiogroup), [Resizable](?path=/docs/guidance-upgrading--docs#resizable), [ScrollArea](?path=/docs/guidance-upgrading--docs#scrollarea), [Select](?path=/docs/guidance-upgrading--docs#select), [Switch](?path=/docs/guidance-upgrading--docs#switch), [Tabs](?path=/docs/guidance-upgrading--docs#tabs), [TextLink](?path=/docs/guidance-upgrading--docs#textlink) and the [Shell](?path=/docs/guidance-upgrading--docs#shell)'s navigation, [Toaster](?path=/docs/guidance-upgrading--docs#toaster), [Toggle and ToggleGroup](?path=/docs/guidance-upgrading--docs#toggle-and-togglegroup), and [Tooltip](?path=/docs/guidance-upgrading--docs#tooltip).

### Deprecated

Each still works in 0.7.0 and goes in the next minor version.

- **Heading's `large`, `medium`, `small` and `xsmall`**: `display`, `page`, `section` and `overlay`, the titles the kit draws ([Heading](?path=/docs/guidance-upgrading--docs#heading)).
- **A KeyValue's `labelWidth` in pixels**: `narrow`, `default` or `wide`, or `auto` in a page body ([KeyValue](?path=/docs/guidance-upgrading--docs#keyvalue)).
- **Inspector's `groups`** and `InspectorGroupData`: Inspector.Group children ([Inspector](?path=/docs/guidance-upgrading--docs#inspector)).
- **ActionBar**: a PageHeader, with the record's state in its Details rail ([ActionBar](?path=/docs/guidance-upgrading--docs#actionbar)).
- **Chart**: Chart.Frame's `status`, Chart.Donut's `name`, Chart.Scatter's `name`, Chart.Area's `baseline` and `formatNumber` ([Chart](?path=/docs/guidance-upgrading--docs#chart)).
- **Size words**: AlertDialogContent's `size`; `sm`, `default` and `lg` on Card, Switch, SelectTrigger, Toggle and ToggleGroup; `xs`, `sm`, `icon-xs` and `icon-sm` on InputGroupButton ([AlertDialog](?path=/docs/guidance-upgrading--docs#alertdialog), [Card](?path=/docs/guidance-upgrading--docs#card), [Switch](?path=/docs/guidance-upgrading--docs#switch), [Select](?path=/docs/guidance-upgrading--docs#select), [Toggle and ToggleGroup](?path=/docs/guidance-upgrading--docs#toggle-and-togglegroup), [InputGroup](?path=/docs/guidance-upgrading--docs#inputgroup)).
- **Value and disclosure callbacks**: DatePicker's and Editable's `onChange`, Tree.Item's `expanded` and `onToggle`, and Table.Group's `open` and the table disclosures' `onToggle` ([DatePicker](?path=/docs/guidance-upgrading--docs#datepicker), [Editable](?path=/docs/guidance-upgrading--docs#editable), [Tree](?path=/docs/guidance-upgrading--docs#tree), [Table](?path=/docs/guidance-upgrading--docs#table)).
- **Names**: DropdownMenuItem's `variant="destructive"`, Item.Group's `labelledBy`, the Shell Profile's `role`, `SideNavSlotProps`, and the class helpers `controlBase` and `controlHeight` ([DropdownMenu](?path=/docs/guidance-upgrading--docs#dropdownmenu), [Item](?path=/docs/guidance-upgrading--docs#item), [Shell](?path=/docs/guidance-upgrading--docs#shell), [Input](?path=/docs/guidance-upgrading--docs#input)).
- **Message keys**: `moreFieldsFor` and the picker count keys ([Messages](?path=/docs/guidance-upgrading--docs#messages)).

## Package

Every export condition but the package's named `@ledger/source`, `development` included, resolves `dist/`. A workspace that compiled the TypeScript source in development, so that a kit edit hot-reloads, adds `@ledger/source` to its bundler's development conditions and to TypeScript's `customConditions` ([Getting started](?path=/docs/guidance-getting-started--docs), Install). A consumer of the packed tarball changes nothing.

## Layout classes

The kit's own layout rules belong to its parts, not to classes product code writes, and `ledger/no-non-token-class` reports each in product code.

| Written as                                                                                                                                               | Write                                                                                                                                                        |
| -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `lg:sticky-rail` on a column of a page's grid                                                                                                            | `<StickyRail from="lg">` ([StickyRail](?path=/docs/layout-stickyrail--docs))                                                                                 |
| `sticky-rail`                                                                                                                                            | `<StickyRail>`                                                                                                                                               |
| `min-h-work` and `grid-cols-list-detail`                                                                                                                 | A [WorkPane](?path=/docs/patterns-workpane--docs), which lays out its list and detail itself; a region as tall as the window is `min-h-dvh` or `fill-window` |
| `sticky-bar`                                                                                                                                             | A PageHeader; ActionBar, which pinned itself, is deprecated ([ActionBar](?path=/docs/guidance-upgrading--docs#actionbar))                                    |
| `grid-cols-main-rail`                                                                                                                                    | Shell.Main and Shell.Aside, the Shell's own columns                                                                                                          |
| `shell-root`, `shell-main`, `shell-banner`, `shell-topnav`, `shell-topnav-start`, `shell-sidenav`, `shell-sidenav-overlay`, `shell-panel`, `shell-scrim` | The Shell's parts, which style themselves; a selector reads their `data-slot` (`[data-slot="shell-scrim"]`)                                                  |
| `2xl:`                                                                                                                                                   | `wide:` (110rem), the kit's widest breakpoint, `xl:` (80rem), or a container query ([Metrics](?path=/docs/tokens-metrics--docs), Breakpoints)                |

## Messages

The LedgerProvider message keys that changed. A product that passes its own `messages` translates the new keys; the deprecated ones stay for one version and are no longer shown.

| Written as                                                                                     | Write                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `moreFieldsFor`                                                                                | `showMoreFieldsForOne` and `showMoreFieldsForOther` (`"Show {count} more fields for {label}"`), `hideMoreFieldsForOne` and `hideMoreFieldsForOther` while the fields show, and `showMoreFieldsOne`, `showMoreFieldsOther`, `hideMoreFieldsOne` and `hideMoreFieldsOther` for a row with no name |
| `pickerNothingChosen`, `pickerChosenOne`, `pickerChosenOther`                                  | `selectedCount` (`"{count} selected"`)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `pickerChosenOfOne`, `pickerChosenOfOther`, `pickerToChooseFromOne`, `pickerToChooseFromOther` | `selectedCountOf` (`"{count} of {total} selected"`)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |

## ActionBar

ActionBar is deprecated and goes in the next minor version, and `ledger/no-deprecated-name` reports the kit's. Its parts are a record page's ([ActionBar](?path=/docs/patterns-actionbar--docs)):

| Written as                   | Write                                                                                                                                                                              |
| ---------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `crumbs` and `id`            | A Breadcrumb in `PageHeader.Lead`, its last level the record                                                                                                                       |
| `title` and `context`        | `PageHeader.Title`; the context is a row of the record's Details                                                                                                                   |
| `states`                     | The record's Details: [Shell.Aside](?path=/docs/layout-shell--docs) holding an [Inspector](?path=/docs/patterns-inspector--docs), with the headline state as the Aside's `summary` |
| `actions` with one `primary` | `PageHeader.Actions`: one primary Button, and the rest in an overflow DropdownMenu                                                                                                 |
| An action's `blocked` reason | The Button's `disabledReason`                                                                                                                                                      |
| `tabs`                       | A line `TabsList` under the PageHeader                                                                                                                                             |

## Alert

- Compose the content as children: `AlertTitle`, `AlertDescription` and `AlertAction`, with `AlertIcon` for the tone's icon.
- The role follows the tone ([Alert](?path=/docs/components-alert--docs)). A caller that needs `role="alert"` on a tone that is not danger passes it.

## AlertDialog

Compose AlertDialogContent with AlertDialogHeader (AlertDialogMedia, AlertDialogTitle, AlertDialogDescription) and AlertDialogFooter (AlertDialogCancel, then AlertDialogAction). AlertDialogAction stays open while its command runs; `pending` on the root holds the decision, and the caller closes it on success.

`size` on AlertDialogContent is `width`, on Dialog's steps: `size="sm"` is `width="xsmall"` (320px), and `size="default"` is `width="small"` (400px), the default, so it is left out. `width="medium"` (520px) is for a decision whose body lists what it affects ([AlertDialog](?path=/docs/components-alertdialog--docs), Widths).

## Attachment

A card-wide anchor styled with `buttonVariants` and the overlay classes, and an `Attachment.Trigger` with `asChild` around a link, are `Attachment.Link`: an anchor with the same overlay that keeps native link behaviour and takes `render` for a router link.

## Avatar

- Compose the mark: `Avatar` holding an `AvatarImage` and an `AvatarFallback` with the initials (`avatarInitials(name)`), and an `AvatarBadge` for a status mark.
- A group is `AvatarGroup` with the avatars it shows and an `AvatarGroupCount` for the rest; the caller decides how many show and counts the overflow.
- `Person`, `avatarInitials` and `avatarHue` keep their contracts.

## Badge

| Written as                                          | Write                                                                                     |
| --------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `<Badge tone="success">Verified</Badge>`            | `<Badge variant="secondary" tone="success">`, the subtle status. Spell the variant.       |
| A neutral `<Badge>Draft</Badge>`                    | `<Badge variant="secondary" tone="neutral">Draft</Badge>`. The default is brand and bold. |
| `appearance="bold"`, `size="xsmall"`, or `icon={…}` | The same props, on a `secondary` Badge for a status.                                      |
| A clickable span                                    | A real anchor through `render`, for navigation.                                           |

`Count`, `Dot`, `Indicator`, `Tone`, `tones` and `toneClasses` keep their contracts, and `Avatar.Badge` and `AvatarGroupCount` are Avatar's own parts.

## Breadcrumb

| Written as                     | Write                                                                                                                 |
| ------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Breadcrumb.Item`              | A `BreadcrumbItem` inside a `BreadcrumbList`, holding a `BreadcrumbLink`, or a `BreadcrumbPage` for the current level |
| `isCurrent`                    | `BreadcrumbPage`                                                                                                      |
| `asChild` around a router link | `BreadcrumbLink render={<Link to="/programs" />}`                                                                     |
| Root `label`                   | `aria-label`                                                                                                          |
| Separators the root drew       | A `BreadcrumbSeparator` between items, and `BreadcrumbEllipsis` for folded levels                                     |

The list wraps rather than cutting every crumb, and the current page is the regular weight ([Breadcrumb](?path=/docs/components-breadcrumb--docs)).

## ButtonGroup

- `label` is `aria-label`.
- Text inside the group is a `ButtonGroupText`, and a rule between its buttons a `ButtonGroupSeparator`. The root takes a div's props, a ref and `orientation`.

## Card

- `Card.Header` with `title`, `description` and `action` is a CardHeader holding CardTitle, CardDescription and CardAction; `Card.Body` is CardContent.
- Put a heading inside CardTitle, or set its element with `render`, where the card's title belongs in the outline.
- `size="sm"` is `size="small"`; `size="default"` is left out.

## Chart

| Written as                                  | Write                                                                             |
| ------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `status` on Chart.Frame                     | `state`, the word DataTable uses for the same thing                               |
| `name` on Chart.Donut, the ring's name      | `label`, as on every plot                                                         |
| `label` on Chart.Donut, the middle's words  | `centerLabel`; `label` names the ring                                             |
| `name` on Chart.Scatter, the key of a point | `nameKey`; `label` names the plot on every part                                   |
| `baseline` on Chart.Area                    | Nothing: an Area always starts at zero                                            |
| `formatNumber` for a chart's values         | `useLedgerLocale().formatNumber`; the parts already format in the reader's locale |

`ledger/no-deprecated-name` writes the Donut's: it fixes `name` to `label`, and moves a `label` that is a number, a figure written as text (`"75%"`, `` `${n}%` ``) or an element, or one beside `name`, to `centerLabel`. Any other words stay as the ring's name.

## Checkbox

| Written as                                     | Write                                                                                                                          |
| ---------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| A label or a description given to the Checkbox | A horizontal Field: the Checkbox, then a FieldLabel and a FieldDescription ([Checkbox](?path=/docs/components-checkbox--docs)) |
| `checked="indeterminate"`                      | `indeterminate`, with `checked={false}` so that choosing it selects all; Table.Selection takes the same                        |

## Collapsible

- `Collapsible.Trigger` and `Collapsible.Content` are the flat CollapsibleTrigger and CollapsibleContent. `asChild` is `render`, and `forceMount` is `keepMounted`.
- A selector on Radix's `data-state` reads `data-open` and `data-closed` on the Root and `data-panel-open` on the trigger ([Collapsible](?path=/docs/components-collapsible--docs), State selectors).
- A Details block built from a subtle Button and a ChevronDown is a CollapsibleHeader, or a collapsible Section on a page.
- `Collapsible.Group` is an [Accordion](?path=/docs/components-accordion--docs) with `multiple` and an AccordionItem per section. A Collapsible's `title` and `count` are a CollapsibleHeader's children, and `headingLevel` is the heading-level context: wrap the disclosure in a HeadingLevelProvider. `DisclosureHeading` is a CollapsibleHeader.

## Combobox

The configured Combobox is composed from flat parts on Base UI's Combobox: the root holds the items and the value, `ComboboxInput` is the field, and `ComboboxContent` holds a `ComboboxList` of `ComboboxItem`s, with `ComboboxEmpty` for no match; several values are `ComboboxChips` of `ComboboxChip`s. Resetting a form sets the value; the Combobox does not reset itself ([Combobox](?path=/docs/components-combobox--docs)).

## Command

- `Command.Input`, `.List`, `.Group`, `.Item` and the rest are the flat exports. A key hint is CommandItem's `shortcut`; other trailing content goes in its children.
- `Command.Dialog` is CommandDialog, with an explicit Command inside it; the filtering and value props belong on Command.
- On the dialog, `onClose` is `onOpenChange`, `label` is `title`, and `returnFocusRef` is `finalFocus`. The palette's width is a `style` or a `className`.

## DataTable

| Written as                                                     | Write                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| -------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `responsive`                                                   | Nothing: a DataTable fits its frame unless it says otherwise, folding lower-priority fields into each row's More fields. Give the name `priority: 0`. `ledger/product-responsive-table`, where a product turns it on, reports `responsive={false}` and no longer asks for `responsive`. |
| A table that relied on scrolling sideways                      | `responsive={false}`, which keeps every column in the row and scrolls the frame                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| A test or a query for a row's "More fields for REQ-001" button | "Show 3 more fields for REQ-001", and "Hide 3 more fields for REQ-001" while they show: the control is a labelled "+3" ([Data table](?path=/docs/patterns-data-table--docs), Responsive containers)                                                                                     |
| `tree.column`                                                  | Nothing: the tree's chevron is a leading column of its own ([Table](?path=/docs/guidance-upgrading--docs#table))                                                                                                                                                                        |

## DatePicker

`onChange` is `onValueChange`, the name every value control uses; it reports the same ISO day, and `""` when the day is cleared.

## Density

There is no document-wide density: no provider, switch, hook, storage key or before-paint script. Remove their imports and unwrap the provider's children; a table sets its own `density`, and a DataTable offers the reader Compact rows ([Density](?path=/docs/components-density--docs)).

## Dialog and Sheet

The configured title, body, footer and action props are composed parts:

```tsx
<Dialog open={open} onOpenChange={setOpen}>
  <DialogTrigger render={<Button />}>Create task</DialogTrigger>
  <DialogContent width="medium">
    <DialogHeader>
      <DialogTitle>Create task</DialogTitle>
    </DialogHeader>
    <DialogBody>…the form…</DialogBody>
    <DialogFooter>
      <DialogClose render={<Button variant="subtle" />}>Cancel</DialogClose>
      <Button variant="primary" type="submit" form="create-task">
        Create task
      </Button>
    </DialogFooter>
  </DialogContent>
</Dialog>
```

- The root's `onOpenChange` can cancel a close, and `pending` holds the dialog while a save runs; the content owns `initialFocus` and `finalFocus`.
- A Sheet composes the same parts (`SheetContent`, `SheetHeader`, `SheetTitle`, `SheetBody`, `SheetFooter`, `SheetClose`) and takes `side`: `start` and `end`, which follow the reading direction, or a physical edge.
- Both take a `width` step, never pixels ([Overlays](?path=/docs/components-overlays--docs), Sizes).

## Drawer

Compose `DrawerContent` with `DrawerHeader` (`DrawerTitle`, `DrawerDescription`), `DrawerBody`, `DrawerFooter` and `DrawerClose`. The root takes Base UI's open state, cancellable dismissal, snap points and swipe directions; the content owns `initialFocus` and `finalFocus` and takes a `width` step. The package no longer depends on Vaul ([Drawer](?path=/docs/components-drawer--docs)).

## DropdownMenu

- The configured `trigger` prop is DropdownMenuTrigger's `render`; placement and width move to DropdownMenuContent.
- `DropdownMenu.Item`, `.Label` and `.Separator` are the flat exports.
- On an item, `onSelect` is `onClick` for an action, `isSelected` is a CheckboxItem's or a RadioGroup's state, `closeOnSelect` is `closeOnClick`, `tone="danger"` and shadcn's `variant="destructive"` are `variant="danger"`, and `trailing` is `shortcut`.
- Children written as a `close` callback go: items close through Base UI, and the root takes controlled state or `actionsRef` to close the menu from code.

## Editable

On `Editable.Text` and `Editable.Select`, `onChange` is `onValueChange`, the name every value control uses; it is called with the same values, and the deprecated `onChange` only where `onValueChange` is not given. `ledger/no-deprecated-name` renames it.

## Empty

`message` and `action` are composed parts: an `EmptyHeader` holding `EmptyMedia` (an `EmptyIllustration`), `EmptyTitle` and `EmptyDescription`, then `EmptyContent` with the action ([Empty](?path=/docs/components-empty--docs)). Card and Empty are components now; imports from the package root are unchanged.

## Field

- A Field's `label`, `hint` and `error` are parts inside it: `FieldLabel`, `FieldDescription` and `FieldError`, which bind to the control with no ids ([Field](?path=/docs/components-field--docs)).
- A group of choices is a Field around a `FieldSet` with a `FieldLegend`. The child cloning and `useFieldControl` are gone.
- `invalid`, `required` and `disabled` stay on the Field.
- `useRequired` is gone. A form library's validation (TanStack Form's validators) says a required field is empty, and the Field's FieldError shows it ([Forms](?path=/docs/patterns-forms--docs)).

## Heading

The sizes are the titles the kit draws ([Heading](?path=/docs/primitives-heading--docs)):

| Written as                           | Write                                                                                                                                                                  |
| ------------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `size="large"`                       | `size="display"`, the same style                                                                                                                                       |
| `size="medium"`                      | `size="page"`, PageHeader.Title's 20/26; `medium` drew 22/28                                                                                                           |
| `size="small"`                       | `size="page"` (20/26 semibold) for a page or record title, with `as="h2"` to keep the element `small` drew, or `size="section"` (13/18 semibold) for a section's title |
| `size="xsmall"`                      | `size="overlay"`, the same style and element                                                                                                                           |
| A raw `h1`–`h6` with heading classes | A `Heading` at the size it matches, or the part that draws that title: PageHeader.Title, Section.Title, DialogTitle                                                    |

The deprecated sizes draw the steps that replace them for one version: `medium` draws `page`'s 20/26, and `small` draws `page` at medium weight. The `font.heading.large`, `.medium`, `.small` and `.xsmall` steps are deprecated and stay for one version, and `ledger/no-deprecated-token` writes `font-heading-display`, `font-heading-page`, `font-heading-page` and `font-heading-overlay` in their place; a new title takes `page`, `overlay`, `section` or `display` ([Typography](?path=/docs/tokens-typography--docs)).

## HoverCard

| Written as                           | Write                              |
| ------------------------------------ | ---------------------------------- |
| `content`                            | HoverCardContent's children        |
| The trigger element                  | HoverCardTrigger's `render`        |
| `delay` and `closeDelay` on the root | The same props on HoverCardTrigger |
| The width shortcut                   | HoverCardContent's `style`         |

## Input

The kit's control classes are not parts. `controlBase`, the class string, is a composed Input, Textarea or InputGroup, which carries the control's classes; `controlHeight` is the `size` prop on Input, Select or a date field.

## InputGroup

Compose the group from its parts: `InputGroupAddon` (with `align`) holding an icon, an `InputGroupText` or an `InputGroupButton`, beside the control, `InputGroupInput` or `InputGroupTextarea`.

On InputGroupButton, `size="xs"` is `size="xsmall"`, the default, and `size="sm"` is `size="small"`. `size="icon-xs"` and `size="icon-sm"` are `size="xsmall"` and `size="small"` with `icon={<Icon />}` and a `label` that names the button.

## Inspector

`groups` is Inspector.Group children, and `InspectorGroupData` goes with it ([Inspector](?path=/docs/patterns-inspector--docs)):

```tsx
// groups={[{ title: "Ownership", rows: [{ label: "Owner", value: owner }] }]}
<Inspector>
  <Inspector.Group title="Ownership">
    <KeyValue label="Owner">{owner}</KeyValue>
  </Inspector.Group>
</Inspector>
```

## Item

`labelledBy` on Item.Group is `aria-labelledby`, which reaches the list.

## Kbd

`Kbd`, its `label` and `Kbd.Group` keep their meaning. A hand-written `⌘` or `Ctrl` cap is a `KbdShortcut keys="Mod+…"`, which draws the platform's modifier.

## KeyValue

`labelWidth` on a KeyValue or a KeyValue.Group takes a step, not pixels ([KeyValue](?path=/docs/components-keyvalue--docs)):

| Written as                                     | Write                                                                                            |
| ---------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| A number up to 96                              | `labelWidth="narrow"` (5.5rem)                                                                   |
| A number from 97 to 131                        | `labelWidth="default"` (6.5rem), the width without one, so it can be left out                    |
| A number from 132                              | `labelWidth="wide"` (10rem)                                                                      |
| A width picked for a page body's longest label | `labelWidth="auto"`: the group's longest label, up to `wide`, stacking where the group is narrow |

## Pages

The page shapes that were parts are compositions of the layout parts ([Pages](?path=/docs/layout-pages--docs)):

| Written as              | Write                                                                                                   |
| ----------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `IndexPage`             | A PageHeader over a frameless DataTable with `fill`                                                     |
| `ShowPage`              | A PageHeader, Section bodies and the Details rail in Shell.Aside                                        |
| `RecordHeader`          | A PageHeader: the trail in PageHeader.Lead, the name in PageHeader.Title, actions in PageHeader.Actions |
| `PreviewRail`           | Shell.Aside                                                                                             |
| `PreviewSplit`, `Panel` | Shell.Panel, the Shell's panel area                                                                     |
| `Block`                 | Section                                                                                                 |

RecordHeader's `facts` are the record's Details in the rail, Shell.Aside holding an Inspector, and Stepper.Item's `first` and `last` are gone: the Stepper knows its ends. `ledger/no-deprecated-name` reports an import of each removed part from the package with what to write.

## Pagination

The configured Pagination is the flat navigation parts: `Pagination`, `PaginationContent`, `PaginationItem`, `PaginationLink`, `PaginationPrevious`, `PaginationNext` and `PaginationEllipsis`, with PaginationLink a real anchor. The page arithmetic and the row summary ("9–16 of 23") are DataTable's, which draws its own pager ([Pagination](?path=/docs/components-pagination--docs)).

## PickerSheet and RecordBrowser

The count under the rows is one phrase: "3 of 120 selected" where the rows to choose from are known, and "3 selected" while they load, after a failed load, or when there are none. PickerSheet's `total` counts every row that can be chosen, before the search and the filters, so it no longer follows the search ([PickerSheet](?path=/docs/patterns-pickersheet--docs), [RecordBrowser](?path=/docs/patterns-recordbrowser--docs)). A test that read "Nothing chosen yet", "N chosen" or "N to choose from" reads the new phrase; the message keys are under [Messages](?path=/docs/guidance-upgrading--docs#messages).

## Popover

| Written as                             | Write                                                               |
| -------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| The configured `trigger`               | PopoverTrigger with `render`                                        |
| `Popover.Close`                        | `PopoverClose`, with `render` for its Button                        |
