| Placement and `aria-label` on the root | The same props on PopoverContent                                    |
| `width` and `matchTriggerWidth`        | PopoverContent's `style`; `var(--anchor-width)` matches the trigger |

The content is 288px wide unless its style says otherwise ([Popover](?path=/docs/components-popover--docs)).

## Progress

- `label` is `aria-label` or a `ProgressLabel`; `valueText` is `aria-valuetext`; `showValue` is a `ProgressValue` child.
- `Progress.Stacked` is `ProgressStacked`, with the same tone, size and segments.

## RadioGroup

- `RadioGroup.Item` is the flat `RadioGroupItem`, and each item's label and description are composed beside it, in a horizontal Field with a FieldLabel ([RadioGroup](?path=/docs/components-radiogroup--docs)).
- `orientation` goes: the layout places the items, and the arrow keys move along either axis.

## Related

`Related.Row` and `RelatedRowProps` are an [Item](?path=/docs/components-item--docs): `leading` for `lead`, `title` for `label`, and `onSelect` or `link` for `onClick`.

## Resizable

| Written as                         | Write                                                             |
| ---------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------- |
| The compound parts                 | `ResizablePanelGroup`, `ResizablePanel` and `ResizableHandle`     |
| A size as a bare number of percent | A string, `"30%"`; a number is pixels                             |
| Saved sizes                        | `useResizableLayout`, with stable ids on the group and its panels |

([Resizable](?path=/docs/components-resizable--docs))

## ScrollArea

- `label` is `viewportProps` holding `role="region"` and an `aria-label`. Sizing classes go on ScrollArea.
- A root `orientation="horizontal"` or `"both"` is a horizontal ScrollBar child; the overflow decides which bars show.
- The bar's visibility shortcut and fixed hide delay are gone; Base UI's `data-hovering` and `data-scrolling` style the bar where needed.

## Select

- A configured root is Select, SelectTrigger, SelectValue and SelectContent.
- The trigger's ref, ARIA, `size`, styles and handlers go on SelectTrigger, where `size` takes `small` or `medium`: shadcn's `size="sm"` is `size="small"`, and `size="default"` is `medium`, the default. The placeholder goes on SelectValue.
- The compound Item, Group and Separator are the flat exports, with SelectLabel inside a SelectGroup.
- Labels come through `items` or SelectValue, and a single value that can be empty is handled as `null`.

NativeSelect is gone. A native `<select>` in a form or a filter is a Select: the options' labels in the root's `items`, and the change through `onValueChange`, which reports `null` when the value is cleared.

## Separator

`orientation`, `isDecorative` and a string `className` keep their meaning; nothing is renamed.

## Shell

| Written as                     | Write                                                                       |
| ------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Shell.Sidebar`                | `Shell.SideNav`, with Header, Body and Footer; the brand is in TopNav.Start |
| `Shell.TopBar`                 | `Shell.TopNav`, with Start, Middle and End                                  |
| `Shell.Brand`                  | `Shell.AppLogo`; its `detail` is `secondaryName`                            |
| `Shell.NavGroup`               | `Shell.SideNav.Section`; its `label` is `heading`                           |
| `Shell.NavItem`                | `Shell.SideNav.Item`                                                        |
| `Shell.User`                   | `Shell.Profile`                                                             |
| `role` on Profile, a job title | `description`                                                               |
| `SideNavSlotProps`             | `SideNavHeaderProps`, `SideNavBodyProps` or `SideNavFooterProps`            |

A side nav or top nav item that navigates takes the router link through `render`, with its label as the item's children, outside the Link, so its icon and badge stay; an action item renders a button.

Below the aside breakpoint, wherever it would not sit beside Main, Shell.Aside is a closed Details disclosure where the route renders it, no longer a block after Main's content. Render it where a record's Details belong on a phone: right after the PageHeader, or first in a tabbed record's Overview panel, rendered only while that tab is selected. Pass the record's state as `summary`, which the disclosure's row carries, and `heading` for a title other than Details ([Shell](?path=/docs/layout-shell--docs)).

## Skeleton

Shapes, line counts, dimensions and style overrides keep their meaning. A waiting region that set `aria-busy` alone adds a line that names the wait ([Skeleton](?path=/docs/components-skeleton--docs)).

## Stat

`Tiles` is `Stat.Grid` (by name, `StatGrid`): the same row of `Stat.Tile` cells, under the Stat name.

## Stepper and Timeline

`label` is required on both: the list's name, such as "Program setup" or "Activity", so neither renders as an unnamed list. An `aria-label` still overrides it ([Stepper](?path=/docs/components-stepper--docs), [Timeline](?path=/docs/components-timeline--docs)).

## Switch

`size="sm"` is `size="small"`; `size="default"` is `medium`, the default, so it is left out.

The label and the description are composed beside the switch, in a horizontal Field with a FieldLabel; the Switch draws only its track and thumb.

## Table

- `open` on Table.Group is `expanded`.
- `onToggle` on Table.Group, Table.Tree and Table.Disclosure is `onExpandedChange`, which is called with the next state: `onToggle={() => setOpen(!open)}` is `onExpandedChange={setOpen}`. A caller that passes both hears only `onExpandedChange`.

- A tree's chevron is `Table.Disclosure`, a leading column of its own beside the checkbox, the drag handle and the detail chevron: always first and pinned, so it stays put when the reader reorders, hides or pins a column. DataTable's `tree.column` option is gone, and a folded row's `hint` follows its first value.

## Tabs

| Written as                                                           | Write                                                                        |
| -------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Tabs.List`, `Tabs.Tab`, `Tabs.Panel`                                | `TabsList`, `TabsTrigger`, `TabsContent`                                     |
| Root `activation="automatic"`                                        | List `activateOnFocus` (left out for manual activation)                      |
| List `label`                                                         | `aria-label`                                                                 |
| Trigger `count` or `trailing`                                        | A `Count`, a `Badge` or other children; `max={9999}` caps a count of rows    |
| `asChild`                                                            | `render`, with `nativeButton={false}` for a link trigger                     |
| `TabListProps`, `TabProps`, `TabPanelProps`                          | `TabsListProps`, `TabsTriggerProps`, `TabsContentProps`                      |
| An underline strip with no variant                                   | List `variant="line"`; the default is the filled strip                       |
| Line List `w-full justify-start`, `overflow-x-auto` or `flex-wrap`   | Nothing: a horizontal line strip fills and scrolls through ScrollArea        |
| `gap-*` on Tabs, `pt-*` on TabsContent or on the panel's first child | Nothing: TabsContent starts its content `space.150` under a horizontal strip |

## TextLink

`asChild`, or a router link passed as the child, is `render`: `<TextLink render={<Link to="/risks" />}>Risks</TextLink>`. `asChild={false}` on a native anchor is left out. The size, the weight and the styles stay as they were.

## Toaster

`toast.success(message, options)` is `toast.add({ title: message, type: "success", ...options })`: `close` for `dismiss`, `timeout` for `duration`, `0` for `Infinity`, and `actionProps.children` for `action.label`. A manager shows nothing until a provider is mounted.

## Toggle and ToggleGroup

- A ToggleGroup's choices are `ToggleGroupItem` children, with an array `value` or `defaultValue`, `onValueChange` and `multiple`; the scalar `items` and `onChange` wrapper and the icon shortcut are gone. Icons, labels, counts and tooltips are the item's children.
- A group can clear its selection; a caller that requires one keeps the rule in its own `onValueChange`.

On Toggle, ToggleGroup and ToggleGroupItem, `size="sm"` is `size="small"` (28px), `size="default"` is `medium` (32px), the default, and `size="lg"` is `size="large"` (36px).

## Tooltip

| Written as                         | Write                        |
| ---------------------------------- | ---------------------------- |
| `content`                          | TooltipContent's children    |
| The trigger as the Tooltip's child | TooltipTrigger with `render` |

`TooltipProvider` groups the tooltips under it and waits 300ms before the first opens; keyboard focus opens one at once ([Tooltip](?path=/docs/components-tooltip--docs)).

## Tree

On Tree.Item, `expanded` is `isExpanded`, the name that matches `isSelected`, and `onToggle` is `onExpandedChange`, which is called with the branch's next state.

<!-- page: Guidance/Token grammar (src/stories/docs/Grammar.mdx) -->

# Token grammar

Tokens are named on one grammar: **property . role . emphasis . state**.

| Segment  | Examples                                                                                                       | What it says                                                                                                           |
| -------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| property | `color.background`, `color.text`, `color.icon`, `color.border`, `elevation.surface`, `space`, `font`, `radius` | What is being painted. Text, icon, border and background are separate properties because they need different contrast. |
| role     | `brand`, `neutral`, `selected`, `success`, `warning`, `danger`, `information`, `disabled`, `input`, `inverse`  | Why. A role names the meaning, not the colour.                                                                         |
| emphasis | `subtlest`, `subtler`, `subtle`, (default), `bold`, `bolder`, `boldest`                                        | How loud. Default sits in the middle; bold is a solid fill with inverse text.                                          |
| state    | `hovered`, `pressed`, `selected`, `focused`                                                                    | Interaction. A state is always its own token, never alpha on the default.                                              |

Every token has one CSS variable, `--ds-<name with dashes>`, and most have one Tailwind utility.

| Token                                 | CSS                                        | Utility                                   |
| ------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------- |
| `color.background.brand.bold.hovered` | `--ds-color-background-brand-bold-hovered` | `bg-brand-bold-hovered`                   |
| `color.text.subtle`                   | `--ds-color-text-subtle`                   | `text-subtle`                             |
| `color.icon.danger`                   | `--ds-color-icon-danger`                   | `icon-danger`                             |
| `color.border.focused`                | `--ds-color-border-focused`                | `border-focused`                          |
| `elevation.surface.raised`            | `--ds-elevation-surface-raised`            | `bg-surface-raised`                       |
| `elevation.shadow.overlay`            | `--ds-elevation-shadow-overlay`            | `shadow-overlay`                          |
| `space.200`                           | `--ds-space-200`                           | `p-200`, `gap-200`, `h-200` …             |
| `radius.medium`                       | `--ds-radius-medium`                       | `rounded-medium`                          |
| `font.body.small`                     | `--ds-font-body-small`                     | `font-body-small`                         |
| `dimension.control.medium`            | `--ds-dimension-control-medium`            | `h-control-medium`, `size-control-medium` |
| `motion.duration.fast`                | `--ds-motion-duration-fast`                | `duration-fast`                           |

## Tiers

1. **Palette.** Eight ramps (neutral, dark neutral, blue, green, orange, red, teal, purple) with numbered step names, plus alpha steps for translucent fills. Never used directly.
2. **Semantic.** Colour and elevation tokens that reference the ramps. Each has a light value and a dark value. This is the only tier a component reads for colour.
3. **Typography, space, shape, dimension, motion.** Mode independent.
4. **Component.** Where a component needs a value no semantic token gives it, the value is added to the tokens, not written in the component.

## Where a value comes from

- **Surface.** `elevation.surface` is the page; `raised` is a card; `overlay` is a menu or dialog; `sunken` is a well. Box sets `utility.elevation.surface.current` when it paints a surface, so children can read the surface they sit on.
- **Text.** `default` for content, `subtle` for secondary, `subtlest` for hints and captions, `disabled` for off. Status text (`success`, `warning`, `danger`, `information`) sits on the matching status background.
- **Border.** `default` for hairlines, `bold` for emphasis, `input` for fields, `focused` and `selected` for those states.
- **Type.** Composite tokens: `body` (13/18) for interface text, `body.small` (12/16) for captions, `body.xsmall` (11/14) for micro labels, `body.large` (15/22) for reading; four heading sizes, one per title the kit draws (`heading.page`, `heading.overlay`, `heading.section`, `heading.display`; the Which token page says which title takes which), and `heading.xxsmall` for the Eyebrow; `code`.
- **Space.** 0, 2, 4, 6, 8, 12, 16, 20, 24, 32, 40, 48, 64, 80. A name counts hundredths of an 8px step: `space.100` is 8px, `space.025` is 2px, `space.1000` is 80px.
- **Radius.** `xsmall` 2, `small` 3, `medium` 5, `large` 7, `xlarge` 9, `xxlarge` 12, `full`. Which part takes which is the [Shape](?path=/docs/tokens-shape--docs) sheet's table.
- **Metrics.** Controls are 24, 28, 32, 36 tall; a table row is 40, with `compact` 36, `header` 32 and `menu` 28; icons 14 and 16.

<!-- page: Guidance/Lint rules (src/stories/docs/Lint.mdx) -->

# Lint rules

The package exports an ESLint plugin, `@ledger/design-system/eslint`, whose allowlist is generated by the token build, so the rules and the tokens cannot drift. It has two presets: `package`, what this package lints itself with, and `recommended`, for a product. This is the one table of the rules; the repository's component library guide links here. Each rule also has a page, `eslint-plugin/docs/<rule>.md`, which ships with the plugin and which every finding's `meta.docs.url` points at: what the rule reports, why, what to write instead, examples, its fixes, its allowances and its limits. The [Lint rules reference](?path=/docs/guidance-lint-rules-reference--docs) carries every page, and the table's Page column links each rule's section.

| Rule | Reports | Instead | `package`⁴ | `recommended` | Page |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `no-arbitrary-value` | A class with an arbitrary value (`text-[13px]`, `w-[240px]`, `bg-[#eee]`), which bypasses the tokens | A token utility or a primitive prop, chosen by the value's role. | error¹ | error | [ledger/no-arbitrary-value](?path=/docs/guidance-lint-rules-reference--docs#ledgerno-arbitrary-value) |
| `no-alpha-token` | An opacity modifier on a colour class (`bg-brand-bold/80`): a state is a token, never alpha on a base token | The token that names the state: its hovered, pressed, subtle or disabled form. | error | error | [ledger/no-alpha-token](?path=/docs/guidance-lint-rules-reference--docs#ledgerno-alpha-token) |
| `no-dark-variant` | A class with the `dark:` variant: every colour is a token that flips by itself, so a `dark:` class means a token is missing, or sets something that should not change with the mode | Drop the `dark:` class and keep the token: `bg-neutral` is already right in both modes. | error | error | [ledger/no-dark-variant](?path=/docs/guidance-lint-rules-reference--docs#ledgerno-dark-variant) |
| `no-unknown-variant` | A class whose variant Tailwind does not generate, so the class adds no CSS, and an `aria-` variant that names no ARIA attribute or a variant whose value is a CSS variable, so its selector never matches | A misspelt variant: the spelling the message names, or the editor suggestion that writes it. | error | error | [ledger/no-unknown-variant](?path=/docs/guidance-lint-rules-reference--docs#ledgerno-unknown-variant) |
| `no-margin` | A margin class: the space between siblings comes from Stack, Inline and Bleed, never from a margin | Space between siblings: a Stack for a column or an Inline for a row, with `space` at the key the margin had. | error² | error | [ledger/no-margin](?path=/docs/guidance-lint-rules-reference--docs#ledgerno-margin) |
| `no-static-design-value` | A stock Tailwind utility that fixes a design value the tokens own: a radius, an opacity, a duration, a border or ring width, or a literal colour | The token for the value's role, by kind: a radius, an opacity, a duration, a border width, a focus mark or a colour. | error | error | [ledger/no-static-design-value](?path=/docs/guidance-lint-rules-reference--docs#ledgerno-static-design-value) |
| `no-non-token-class` | A class that is neither a token utility nor a documented structural utility | The token utility for the job; [Which token](?path=/docs/guidance-which-token--docs) is the short answer by job. | error¹ | error | [ledger/no-non-token-class](?path=/docs/guidance-lint-rules-reference--docs#ledgerno-non-token-class) |
| `no-deprecated-token` | A class that paints a deprecated token, and names the class that replaces it | The class the message names. | error | error | [ledger/no-deprecated-token](?path=/docs/guidance-lint-rules-reference--docs#ledgerno-deprecated-token) |
| `no-deprecated-name` | A kit part, prop or value that was renamed or removed, with its replacement; one-to-one renames are fixed | The replacement the report names, following its note where it has one; `--fix` writes the one-to-one renames. | error | error | [ledger/no-deprecated-name](?path=/docs/guidance-lint-rules-reference--docs#ledgerno-deprecated-name) |
| `readable-classes` | A `className` on a kit part that the class rules cannot read, because it comes from another prop, another module, a call or a value the lint cannot follow | Use the part's own prop for its look (`variant`, `size`, `tone`, `isSelected`), and write a class for layout the part leaves to its caller in the file: in the attribute, or in a `const` or a map keyed by a typed prop. | error | error | [ledger/readable-classes](?path=/docs/guidance-lint-rules-reference--docs#ledgerreadable-classes) |
| `cell-plain` | A neutral colour, weight or type token on a Table.Cell, where only a status colour may differ | Drop the class: the cell's type and colour are the table's. | off | error | [ledger/cell-plain](?path=/docs/guidance-lint-rules-reference--docs#ledgercell-plain) |
| `id-not-blue` | An Id coloured `text-brand` with no link or button around it: an Id is blue only inside a link or a button | Drop `text-brand`, and when the id opens its record, make it the text of a TextLink: `<TextLink render={<Link … />}><Id>…</Id></TextLink>`. | off | error | [ledger/id-not-blue](?path=/docs/guidance-lint-rules-reference--docs#ledgerid-not-blue) |
| `no-kit-shadow` | A component that product code declares under the name of a kit part, or under an old name for one, instead of importing the part | Import the part from the package root: `import { Badge } from "@ledger/design-system"`. | off | error | [ledger/no-kit-shadow](?path=/docs/guidance-lint-rules-reference--docs#ledgerno-kit-shadow) |
| `prefer-text-link` | A link that imitates TextLink by hand, and a link that opens a new tab without saying so | A link that reads as text: `<TextLink href="…">`, or `<TextLink render={<Link to="…" />}>` for a router link. | error | error | [ledger/prefer-text-link](?path=/docs/guidance-lint-rules-reference--docs#ledgerprefer-text-link) |
| `no-colgroup` | A `<colgroup>`: a column's width is a content decision and goes on its Table.Header as `width`, not in a colgroup | `width={180}` on a Table.Header fixes its column; `minWidth={200}` gives the name column a floor (180 to 220) and lets it take the slack. | error | error | [ledger/no-colgroup](?path=/docs/guidance-lint-rules-reference--docs#ledgerno-colgroup) |
| `button-icon-slot` | An icon sized by hand as a child of a Button or an IconButton, where the icon belongs in `iconBefore`, `iconAfter` or `icon` and the button sizes it | A leading icon is `iconBefore={<Plus />}`, a trailing one `iconAfter={<ChevronDown />}`, each passed bare, with no size class. | error | error | [ledger/button-icon-slot](?path=/docs/guidance-lint-rules-reference--docs#ledgerbutton-icon-slot) |
| `no-native-confirm` | A call to the browser's `confirm()`, bare or through `window`, `globalThis` or `self` | An `AlertDialog`, with `AlertDialogCancel` before `AlertDialogAction`. | off | error | [ledger/no-native-confirm](?path=/docs/guidance-lint-rules-reference--docs#ledgerno-native-confirm) |
| `text-link-navigation` | A TextLink with no destination, or one that renders a button or a native element other than an anchor | An `href`, or a router link in `render`: `<TextLink render={<Link to="/programs/$programId" params={{ programId }} />}>`. | off | error | [ledger/text-link-navigation](?path=/docs/guidance-lint-rules-reference--docs#ledgertext-link-navigation) |
| `dialog-footer-order` | A Cancel or close control that comes after the primary action in a dialog, alert dialog, sheet or drawer footer | The cancel first, then the primary. | off | error | [ledger/dialog-footer-order](?path=/docs/guidance-lint-rules-reference--docs#ledgerdialog-footer-order) |
| `no-overlay-autofocus` | `autoFocus` inside an overlay's content, where it takes over from the overlay's own focus handling | `initialFocus` on the content, with the first field's ref. | error¹ | error | [ledger/no-overlay-autofocus](?path=/docs/guidance-lint-rules-reference--docs#ledgerno-overlay-autofocus) |
| `no-disabled-while-loading` | An element or a props object whose `disabled` reads the same pending flag as its `isLoading` | `isLoading={pending}` alone. | error¹ | error | [ledger/no-disabled-while-loading](?path=/docs/guidance-lint-rules-reference--docs#ledgerno-disabled-while-loading) |
| `overlay-width-preset` | A width set on Dialog, Sheet, AlertDialog or Drawer content through `style` or a width class | A `width` step on `DialogContent`, `SheetContent`, `AlertDialogContent` and `DrawerContent`. | error¹ | error | [ledger/overlay-width-preset](?path=/docs/guidance-lint-rules-reference--docs#ledgeroverlay-width-preset) |
| `no-plain-alert-role` | `role="alert"` written on a plain HTML element | `<Alert role="alert">` for a result about the whole form, `FieldError` for one field, `ErrorSummary` for several issues. | off | error | [ledger/no-plain-alert-role](?path=/docs/guidance-lint-rules-reference--docs#ledgerno-plain-alert-role) |
| `link-button-navigation` | A Button or IconButton that renders a link, or whose `onClick` does nothing but navigate | `LinkButton` with the router's link in `render`, or `LinkIconButton` for the icon-only form. | error¹ | error | [ledger/link-button-navigation](?path=/docs/guidance-lint-rules-reference--docs#ledgerlink-button-navigation) |
| `no-style-design-value` | A literal length, colour, font weight, font family or margin written in a `style` object, a literal colour or length in a custom property, a part's own size read by anything but that part, and a `<style>` element | A token utility in `className`, or a primitive's prop. | error¹ | error | [ledger/no-style-design-value](?path=/docs/guidance-lint-rules-reference--docs#ledgerno-style-design-value) |
| `no-raw-colour` | A literal colour in an SVG element's or a recharts part's colour attribute, in the colour keys of a recharts part's object props and of the records its data holds, and in a module's list of colours | On an icon or a mark, `fill="currentColor"` or `stroke="currentColor"` with a text or icon token class on the element or its parent (`text-subtle`, `text-danger`). | error | error | [ledger/no-raw-colour](?path=/docs/guidance-lint-rules-reference--docs#ledgerno-raw-colour) |
| `no-inline-config` | A comment that configures a ledger rule, turns one off beyond a line, or turns one off for a line without saying why after `--` | Fix what the rule reports, using the advice in its own finding: a margin becomes Stack or Inline space, a literal colour its role token. | error⁵ | error⁵ | [ledger/no-inline-config](?path=/docs/guidance-lint-rules-reference--docs#ledgerno-inline-config) |
| `no-restyle` | A class on a kit part that changes what the part sets itself, and a class that styles the elements inside the one it is on | Write the prop the finding names: `numeric`, `align="end"`, `isFullWidth`, `color="color.text.subtle"`, `maxLines={1}`. | off | error | [ledger/no-restyle](?path=/docs/guidance-lint-rules-reference--docs#ledgerno-restyle) |
| `use-heading` | A raw `h1` to `h6` that carries type classes, which copy a title's look by hand | A title the kit draws: `PageHeader.Title` for the page or record, `Section.Title` for a section, `DialogTitle` (or `SheetTitle`, `AlertDialogTitle`, `DrawerTitle`) for an overlay. | off | error | [ledger/use-heading](?path=/docs/guidance-lint-rules-reference--docs#ledgeruse-heading) |
| `use-primitives` | Layout written as classes: on a plain element, where a primitive belongs, and on a primitive, where its props belong | The primitive for the layout, with its props in place of the classes: Stack, Inline, Box, Grid or Flex. | off | warn | [ledger/use-primitives](?path=/docs/guidance-lint-rules-reference--docs#ledgeruse-primitives) |
| `product-responsive-table` | A kit DataTable that turns `responsive` off, or leaves it to a prop spread | Leave `responsive` out: `<DataTable table={table} />`. | off | off³ | [ledger/product-responsive-table](?path=/docs/guidance-lint-rules-reference--docs#ledgerproduct-responsive-table) |
| `product-line-tabs` | A kit TabsList without `variant="line"` after any prop spread, or one given a class or style that changes how its strip wraps, sizes or scrolls | `<TabsList variant="line">`, after any prop spread, with no layout class or style. | off | off³ | [ledger/product-line-tabs](?path=/docs/guidance-lint-rules-reference--docs#ledgerproduct-line-tabs) |

1. In the package's stories, `no-arbitrary-value` is off: a story's own frame may take a fixed width. A class has one owner, so no other rule reports an arbitrary value or a variable shorthand there. `no-non-token-class` is an error there as everywhere, so the parts a story demonstrates stay on the tokens. The five usage rules (`no-overlay-autofocus`, `no-disabled-while-loading`, `overlay-width-preset`, `link-button-navigation`, `no-style-design-value`) are off there too, because a Don't story shows the mistake on purpose.
2. Off in `primitives/bleed.tsx`, the one place a negative margin is written. A class has one owner, so no other rule reports a margin there, at any key; a `dark:` margin is `no-dark-variant`'s, which is on there.
3. Opt-in product layout rules, off in both presets: filled tabs and horizontally scrolling comparison tables remain supported by the kit. A product that adopts the contract turns them on for its product files; this repository's application does. Each required prop must follow any spread so the spread cannot override it.
4. Inside the package, a file may keep a counted allowance for a rule in `test/lint-allow.json`: the rule fails when the file has more reports than its allowance, and when it has fewer, until the allowance is lowered. The list may only shrink, and the package keeps none.
5. On in stories and in `bleed.tsx` too. A configuration comment or a block disable turns a rule off for the rest of the file, so it is reported even with a reason; a line or next-line disable keeps one site out, and says why. A next-line disable that names no rule, bare or with a list of only commas or empty quotes, turns every rule off for its line, so it is reported too. Comments are read as ESLint reads them, so a rule name written with an escape (`"ledger\u002fno-margin"`) is still that rule. In this repository `scripts/check-allow-lists.mjs` counts every inline directive that names a ledger rule, and every disable that names none, per file in the application's and the package's source; the counts may only shrink, and the application keeps none. An entry under a rule is where that rule's count starts only in the change that adds the rule to the plugin and to this page. A disable that silences nothing fails the lint (`reportUnusedDisableDirectives: "error"`), and neither the application nor the package keeps an `eslint-suppressions.json`, which ESLint would apply by itself; one that names a ledger rule is reported for that too.

The table's rows are generated from the rules' pages by `npm run build:lint`, and `test/lint-docs.test.mjs` checks them against the plugin: it fails when a rule has no page, a page's sections are not the seven in order, a reported example is not reported by its rule or is reported by another, an allowed example is reported at all or does not compile against the kit, a preset column disagrees with the preset, a rule's `meta.docs.url` is not its page, or this table or the reference has drifted from the pages.

`test/lint-meta.test.mjs` holds every rule to its kind, its description, its page, its words in `meta.messages` and a preset (or the two opt-in rules), and to a case file in `test/lint-cases/` whose invalid cases reach every message id. `test/lint-messages.test.mjs` renders every message into `test/lint-messages.snap.md`, with every value a rule's data gives its words (advice, presets, retired names), and fails when one changes; each is at most 300 characters before its note, ends with a period and pairs its brackets and quotes, and every rule is held to leading with its subject and to giving no configuration advice, as What a finding names describes. In this repository `npm run check:lint-changelog` fails a change to the plugin or its token data that has no entry in the package's CHANGELOG, unless every commit that changed those files ends its message with the line "Lint: no behaviour change"; a change not yet committed always needs the entry.

Inside the package a portability rule also blocks any import from a consumer (`@/…`), from the prototype, or from a router.

## One owner per class

Each class the eight class rules read is reported by one of them, the one whose fix takes the whole class away or rewrites it; a rule whose fix would leave the class broken never owns it. The owner is the first of these the class fails: `no-dark-variant` (any `dark:` class, a margin included), `no-margin` (any other margin, at a token key, a stock key, an arbitrary value or a variable), `no-unknown-variant` (any other class under a variant Tailwind does not generate, such as `hovr:`, `tablet:` or `hover/row:`, which generates no CSS whatever its base, or under an `aria-` variant that names no ARIA attribute or a variant whose value is a CSS variable, `nth-(--n):`), `no-arbitrary-value` (a bracketed value, or Tailwind 4's variable shorthand such as `w-(--rail)`; a Ledger token's variable with a token class that generates the same CSS, `bg-(--ds-elevation-surface)`, is fixed to it), `no-alpha-token` (alpha on a token colour), `no-static-design-value`, `no-deprecated-token`, then `no-non-token-class` for the rest, with a cause in its message: a shadcn theme name (`text-muted-foreground`, `bg-muted/50`), a Tailwind palette colour with alpha (`bg-red-500/50`), a minus on a padding, gap or size, which Tailwind does not negate (`-p-200`, `-w-full`), a physical side whose logical twin passes (`text-left`, `pl-200`, `right-0`, `border-l`), named by that twin, a class built at runtime, or an unknown class, which it names further when it can: a stock colour or step (`bg-red-500`, `p-4`), a stock width or height (`w-4`), a key off the space scale (`p-210`), a step past a numbered series (`fill-chart-categorical-9`) or a misspelt token class (`bg-surfce`). So `mt-[13px]` is a margin, `dark:bg-white` and `dark:mt-4` dark classes and `bg-red-500/50` a palette colour, each reported by one rule. A rule about a part may quote a class too: `overlay-width-preset` names the width class on a DialogContent, SheetContent or AlertDialogContent (`max-w-[520px]`), which the class's owner also reports. `classify` in `eslint-plugin/classes.js` holds the order, and `test/lint-ownership.test.mjs` shows that no stock class is reported twice and that every rule reports the same alone, with the others or after them. `no-restyle` judges what is left on a kit part: a class one of these rules owns, the padding, gap, display or grid template `use-primitives` judges on a layout primitive, and the type or neutral colour `cell-plain` judges on a `Table.Cell` stay theirs, and `test/lint-restyle.test.mjs` shows that a class it reports is reported by no other rule.

## What a finding names

Every message keeps one contract, which `eslint-plugin/report.js` states and `test/lint-messages.test.mjs` holds for every rule: the subject first, as written (a quoted class, a `<Tag>`, a `style.x`, a `call()`), then what it is, one clause of why when that is not obvious, and what to write instead, the Ledger token, prop value or part, at most two, computed from what was written. It never offers the configuration as the fix: no allowance, no disable, no "declare a token" or "add a variant", since a missing token is a kit change through `/ledger-add-part`. What it names is chosen by role, never by value alone:

- **A value names the nearest token of its role's family.** A stock step, an arbitrary value, a numeric utility or a literal in a style is named by the token nearest its value, from the family its property's role takes and no other: `space.*` for padding, gap, inset and translate, `border.width.*` for a border or outline width, `radius.*` for a corner, `font.*` for a text size and then a weight, `motion.duration.*` for a duration, the two opacities and the drop shadows. A value one token holds names it (`"p-4" is Tailwind's spacing step 4 (16px), … 16px is p-200 (space.200).`), a value between two steps names both, and one off the scale names the scale's range. A width or a height names no token, whatever its value: a container or breakpoint threshold, a layout region's width and a part's own size (`dimension.part.*`, that part's alone) are never offered, and the message says `A width is a layout part's, a part's preset or computed from its container (w-full, a grid track).`, with an example of the dimension (`h-full` for a height), except that 1px is its own spelling (`h-px`). A viewport length is structure and gets no hint. Zero is `space.0`, a radius from 32px up is a pill's (`rounded-full`), and a text size whose type style also sets a weight names the weight. On an element `use-primitives` reads, in a product, a padding or a gap is named as its primitive's prop (`padding="space.200" on a Box`), since that rule reports the class there; `space-x` and `space-y` name the parent's space.
- **A colour names the roles its hue plays** (decision 8 of the lint hardening plan): at most two, each with its purpose (`Red is bg-danger-bold (a vibrant background for critical information…) or bg-accent-red-bolder (…)`), in the state its variant asks for, a hovered token under `hover:` and a disabled one under `disabled:`. It names one token alone only when one role holds the colour within ΔE 0.02 in both modes, which a palette colour alone never is, since no token keeps one colour in both; when two roles hold it, it names both. Greys differ by elevation, not by value (a white page is the surface, a grey as pale is sunken or raised), so a grey pair gets one token only where the site names its role with a token twin. A pale tint is its hue's, read by its lightness as well as its chroma (`#fef2f2` is red). A `dark:` colour is ranked with its light twin on the same site, in both modes: `no-dark-variant` says when the twin is a token that already changes with the mode, so dropping the `dark:` class is the whole fix, and otherwise which tokens replace both classes.
- **A shadcn theme name names the Ledger class for its job.** `text-muted-foreground`, `bg-background`, `ring-ring` and the rest of shadcn's 39 colour names generate no CSS here, and `no-non-token-class` names each by the class that does its job (`text-subtle`, `bg-surface`, `outline-focused`), from one table, `build/vocabulary-aliases.json`. The token build checks it (each name is no Ledger class and generates no CSS; each class it names is one the allowlist lists, and neither deprecated nor for one purpose only), and `npm run build:lint` writes it onto the [Coming from shadcn](?path=/docs/guidance-coming-from-shadcn--docs) page. `bg-accent` adds that Ledger's `accent-*` colours are hues with no meaning. Under a state variant its entry keys, a name takes that state's class: `bg-selected` for a selected, checked or pressed item, `text-subtlest` for a placeholder.
- **Layout names the part, and a prop its value.** `use-primitives` names the part a plain element's classes make, with its props and their values: a flex row is an Inline, a flex column a Stack, a grid a Grid (`<Inline space="space.100">`). `no-margin` names the parent's `space` at the margin's step, and Bleed for a negative margin, bracketed ones included, up to Bleed's widest step, `space.400`. `no-alpha-token` names the token's own states by the alpha: its tints at `/30` and under, only ones quieter than the token, its hovered and pressed states at `/60` and over (its quieter tints where it has no state), one of each between, and the state its variant asks for first; a band with nothing names nothing. `overlay-width-preset` names the nearest step of the part's own width map (`width="medium"` (520px)), which `npm run build:lint` reads from Dialog, Sheet and AlertDialog into `eslint-plugin/components.json`; the steps are the parts', not tokens.
- **A restyle names the prop or the part, never a way around it.** `no-restyle` names the prop whose value is the class (`"tabular-nums" on <Text> is its numeric prop. Write numeric and drop the class.`), a primitive's prop that sets the same thing (`"font-heading-page" is Heading size="page"`), or the part that sets it, with what it sets and where (`"pt-200" on <TabsContent> changes the padding it sets itself (pt-150, components/tabs.tsx:125). Drop it; a different padding is a change to Tabs.`); a different look for a part is a change to the part. In a table cell it says `Cells are one style: drop "font-body-small".`, and it never names a margin, or a wrapper that would carry the class past the part.

While the lint data is stale, nothing is taken from `lint-values.json`: a finding keeps its rule's general words and offers nothing.

**Fixes and suggestions.** `--fix` writes only what has one answer: `no-deprecated-token`'s and `no-deprecated-name`'s one-to-one replacements, and `no-arbitrary-value`'s token variable to the token class that generates the same CSS. Where one class stands for the class written, a finding also carries an editor suggestion: a misspelt variant's or token class's respelling (`hovr:`, `bg-surfce`; within the class's own utility, never another emphasis of one token, and never a class Tailwind names by a value keyword such as `min-h-dvw`), a stock or arbitrary value that one token of its role holds exactly (`p-4` becomes `p-200`, `text-[13px]` `font-body`), a colour one role holds within ΔE 0.02 in both modes, a theme name's Ledger class, one for each where the table names two, and on a kit part the prop whose value puts that one class there (`numeric` for `tabular-nums` on a Text, where it renders the same). A suggestion is the reader's choice, applied in the editor; `eslint --fix` never runs one. It keeps the class's variants and `!`, rewrites that class alone where it is written (a class in a template gets none), and writes only a class no Ledger rule reports, which `test/lint-fix-safety.test.mjs` and `test/lint-nearest.test.mjs` check for every suggestion they reach. A value between two steps, a value two tokens hold (`border-2`, selected or focused), a width, a colour's roles, a padding or a gap that `use-primitives` reports on its element, and a class `no-restyle` reports on its element (`bg-surface` on a Box, whose `backgroundColor` sets it) are named and never offered, since which one is right depends on the part.

## What a part sets

`no-restyle` asks what a kit part sets itself, and reads the answer from `eslint-plugin/parts.json`, which `npm run build:lint` writes from the kit's source (`build/lint-parts.mjs`). For each public part and member (`Text`, `Table.Cell`, `Shell.TopNav.Item`) it holds the file and line of the function that renders it, its kind (a layout primitive, a type primitive or a component), the classes its root always puts on the element a caller's `className` reaches, the classes each value of a prop puts there, the classes it makes from several props, and where the reader stopped. The reader is the lint's own, run over the kit's source with typescript-eslint and the TypeScript program the inventory builds: it follows a string, a condition, a map lookup, a `cva` recipe, a helper's returns (`buttonVariants`), the token tables a primitive reads (`spaceClasses`) and the parts a part renders, asking the type checker only where syntax stops. Each class is filed under its tailwind-merge group and that group's category (layout, spacing, color, typography, shape, effects or motion), which the token build writes into `lint.json`: tailwind-merge's grammar merged with the kit's merge config, as `cn()` merges, so a class in a group that replaces another counts as changing it (`py-200` over a part's `pt-150`). The plugin reads both as data and never loads tailwind-merge. `test/lint-categories.test.mjs` holds the grammar to tailwind-merge's, and `test/lint-parts.test.mjs` fails when `parts.json` is not the source's own reading, so a change to Button's variants or Tabs' gap without `npm run build:lint` is caught.

A part owns only what it sets itself (decision 7 of the lint hardening plan). A class that changes its root's setting is a restyle in any state, and one that changes a prop's setting is a restyle in the states the prop sets it. Layout the part does not set (where it sits, how wide it is, a border on a Stack, the dividers between a RadioGroup's choices) is the caller's. So is the part's own layout, except where a prop sets nothing else (Button's `isFullWidth`), and so are hiding the part and laying it out at a breakpoint or a container size. Inside a table cell (a column's `cell` renderer, or a `Table.Cell` around the element) a part takes the cell's type, so the type and neutral colours `cell-plain` forbids on the cell are reported on the parts inside it too.

Where a part's `className` has a contract, the kit writes it beside the prop as an `@accepts` tag, and `no-restyle` reports a class outside it: the date, time, number and search fields and the search dialog take `layout`, and Id takes `color typography break-all`. An entry is a category or one class; the build stops on any other, naming the nearest (`Id: @accepts "colr" is not a category … Did you mean "color"?`). A product adds no contract of its own. One exception is built in: a focus target, an element with a literal `tabIndex={-1}` that script moves focus to (a step's heading, a page's main), may carry `outline-none`, `outline-hidden` and `outline-focused`, as the kit's own do.

The rule is an error in `recommended` and runs on product code only. It is off in `package`: the kit's patterns compose its components by design, and a part's look is decided in the part.

## What counts as structural

Display, position, alignment, overflow, text flow and interaction utilities are allowed as written, because they carry no design value: `flex`, `grid`, `relative`, `absolute`, `sticky`, `truncate`, `whitespace-nowrap`, `select-none`, `pointer-events-none`, `overflow-auto`, `overscroll-none`, `sr-only`, `cursor-pointer`, `transition-colors`, `animate-spin` and their kin. Alignment takes the values Tailwind generates for each property: `items-center-safe` and `items-baseline-last`, `justify-evenly` and `content-between`, but no `items-between`. Sizes with a token key are allowed on every sizing property: `w-200`, `min-h-800`, `size-150`. A leading minus is allowed where Tailwind negates the utility (`-inset-x-100`, `-translate-y-full`, `-indent-200`), never on padding, gap or a size (`-p-200` generates no CSS), and never before `auto`. A number is written as Tailwind reads it, with no leading zero and at most 15 digits (`order-2`, `line-clamp-3`, not `order-02`). A part's stacking inside itself takes `z-0`, `z-10`, `z-20` and `z-auto`; between the page's regions a layer token stacks it (`z-chrome`, `z-blanket`, `z-overlay`, `z-toast`, `z-tooltip`; the `layer.*` tokens on Tokens/Color), so `z-30`, `z-50` and any other number is reported with the layer of its number. A side is written logically, so it mirrors when the page reads right to left: `start-0`, `end-0`, `text-start`, `ps-200`, `border-s` and `rounded-e-large`, where `left-0`, `right-0`, `text-left`, `pl-200`, `border-l` and `rounded-r-large` are reported with that twin. A physical side passes under a variant that names a side or a direction (`data-[side=left]:`, `rtl:`), and at a half inset that centres (`left-1/2` with `-translate-x-1/2`). Every spelling the lint admits generates CSS, which `test/lint-tailwind.test.mjs` asks Tailwind, with two kinds of exception that generate none by design: the name markers `group` and `peer` (named or not, `group/row`), which a variant reads, and `recharts-cartesian-axis-tick-value`, the tick class the chart library reads to measure its ticks. A grid template whose tracks carry no length is structure too, since it sizes to content or shares the free space: `grid-cols-[auto_1fr]`, `grid-cols-[minmax(0,1fr)_auto]`, tracks of `auto`, `min-content`, `max-content`, `<n>fr` or `minmax(0,…)` of one of those, or a lone `subgrid`. A template with a length, `repeat()` or `var()` in it is still an arbitrary value. Two classes that read a variable are structure as well: Grid's responsive columns (`grid-cols-(--ds-grid-md)`, one per breakpoint) and a disclosure panel's measured height (`h-(--accordion-panel-height)`, `h-(--collapsible-panel-height)`). The kit's own utilities are allowed as well, by the name each `@utility` in its CSS declares, which the token build reads into `lint.json`: the layout rules in `layout.css` (`page-header`, `section-header` and `fill-window`), `stat-grid` with `stat-grid-2` to `stat-grid-6` in `stat.css`, the hit areas `touch-target`, `touch-target-block` and `touch-target-block-after` in `touch.css`, and the motion, drawer and toast utilities. A utility the CSS gains passes with no edit to the lint, and one it loses fails.

## What the lint cannot see

The rules read one file at a time, as it is written. Each rule's page lists its own limits; across the rules they do not see:

- **A value from another file.** A class, a style object or a handler imported from another module is not read where it is used. A module-level class string, or a module-level map or list of them, is checked where it is declared instead, when it reads as classes: at least half of a string's words are classes the lint knows, or each is one it knows or one no data is spelt like and one at least is the latter (a bracketed value, a class with alpha or a palette colour: `export const width = "w-[240px]"`), and most of a map's strings are, a bare word left out (`"flex"` is also a CSS value, `"hidden"` an attribute, so a style object or a list of attributes or views is no class map). What the map holds is read through an `Object.freeze`, a same-file spread, each branch of a condition, a template's own text and the values of `Object.fromEntries` or `new Map`. The token build's output under `src/generated` is not read there. A string of other stock classes exported for another file passes (`"p-4 shadow-md"`), and so does a bare word exported alone (`"rounded"`) and a map's data: a bare word no rule knows (`"danger"`, `"none"`), or a key whose values across its records are mostly not classes. A map a call builds (`(() => ({ … }))()`, a function that returns one) is read only where a class site in the file reads it.
- **What only runtime knows.** A prop, a spread of props, a variable changed other than by assigning it (`k++`, `k.a = …`, `list.push(…)`) and a function from another module are not read; `readable-classes` reports such a variable on a kit part as written again. What the file writes itself is: a `const`, a `let` or `var` with each value assigned to it, a destructured slot, an entry of a map, a list, an enum or an `Object.freeze` (every entry, a computed key's too, for a key such as `tones[tone]` known only at runtime), a key a helper's object computes from a same-file value (`cn({ [active]: on })`), each entry of a same-file list a `.map` callback walks, a same-file function's, a `useMemo`'s or a `useCallback`'s result, with each parameter read as the call gives it (`note("text-danger")`), `useState`'s first value, a spread of a same-file object, and a DOM element's classes written to `className` or given to `classList.add` and `classList.toggle`. A `Map` read with `.get`, and a pair destructured from `Object.entries(…)`, are not followed to their values. A class built in a template or a concatenation (`` `bg-${tone}` ``, `"bg-" + tone`) is never read as its fragments: `no-non-token-class` reports it once as a class built at runtime. A class glued together by a list's `.join("")` or a string's `.concat(…)` is the same. A hole whose values bring their own space (`` `flex${on ? " gap-100" : ""}` ``) builds nothing, and is read. On a kit part's `className`, in an object spread onto the part or in a slot map it is given, what the rules cannot read is not passed in silence: `readable-classes` reports it where it enters, whether a prop, an import from the product's own modules (held in a `const` too), another package's function the file hands values to, or a call, and offers the part's own props.
- **A restyle from outside the file.** `no-restyle` reports a variant that reaches into the elements inside (`*:`, `**:`, `[&_button]:`, `[&>li]:`) on a kit part, or on an element that holds one written in the same file; a part another component renders there, or `children` handed in, is not seen, and a variant that reaches a sibling (`[&+div]:`) is not judged. What a part sets is what the build could read in its source: where its reader stopped (`unread` in `parts.json`), the part may set more than the rule knows, and a class in no category is not judged.
- **A part behind a component from another file.** A rule that judges a kit part knows it by its import from `@ledger/design-system`, by name, alias or namespace (inside the kit, by a relative import), and a type of the same name hides nothing; `cell-plain`, `id-not-blue`, `use-primitives`, `button-icon-slot` and `no-restyle` also follow a `render` that puts the part in an element's place. A component of the same file that hands a prop on to a part, through up to four such components, is judged as that part where it is written, when its first parameter carries the prop: the props object or a rest that still holds it, spread onto the element, or the prop destructured and written onto it. Its `className` is the part's for `button-icon-slot`, `cell-plain`, `id-not-blue`, `overlay-width-preset`, `readable-classes`, `use-primitives` and `no-restyle`, its `style` for `overlay-width-preset`, its children for `button-icon-slot`, `dialog-footer-order` and `no-overlay-autofocus`, its `render` and `onClick` for `link-button-navigation` and `text-link-navigation`, and its `target` for `prefer-text-link`; the finding names both (`<Pane> forwards className to <Stack>, …`). A component imported from another file is not the part: a class passed to `<NameCell className="font-semibold">`, where `NameCell` comes from another module and forwards to a `Table.Cell`, is checked as a class where it is written, not as the cell's.
- **A style written elsewhere, and what a style may hold.** `no-style-design-value` and `overlay-width-preset` follow a style to where the file writes it: either branch, a `const` or a map's entry, an object spread in or merged by `Object.assign`, a Base UI style callback (memoised by `useCallback` too), and what a same-file function returns, with each parameter read as the call gives it, or `useMemo` memoises. In a style's values `no-style-design-value` also follows a prop's default, a string in a template's hole or a concatenation, a number written before a length unit (`` `${W}px` ``), a named number in a sum and a product whose every factor the file writes, and a `var()`'s fallback; `no-raw-colour` follows a colour attribute's value, and the records a chart's data holds, the same way. A finding on a literal written elsewhere says where. A received `style`, the value a caller passes, a call the file cannot follow, a factor the page computes (`depth * INDENT`), `token()` and `var()` without a fallback are what only the running page knows, and pass. A viewport length (`100dvh`, `90vw`, `10dvh` inside `min()`) is the window's own size, structure as `100%` is, and in the kit's own source the widths and heights of the Dialog and Sheet preset maps (`dialogWidths`, `sheetWidths`) are the one place for their steps, so neither is read as a design value. A part's own size (`dimension.part.*`) is read by that part alone.
- **What a value is for.** A finding's advice reads the class or the style property, its variants and the other classes on the same site, never what the element is for: it names a value from its property's family, a width by no token and a colour by the roles its hue plays, and which role is right is the reader's call (`bg-white dark:bg-gray-800` names `bg-surface-overlay` and `bg-neutral`, the nearest in both modes, whatever the element is). A `dark:` colour's light twin is found only on the same site, one class of its utility on each side, and a palette colour on a utility where its hue plays no role (`ring-*`, `outline-*`, `divide-*`, `border-teal-500`) is reported with no name.
- **Plain CSS.** A stylesheet is outside the rules, so a product's CSS is not read: a utility or a variant it declares (`@utility`, `@custom-variant`) is not in `lint.json`, which the token build reads from the kit's CSS alone, and a class that uses one is reported, unless `settings.ledger.customVariants` names the variant. The kit's own, `src/styles/*.css`, is held to the tokens by `test/css-tokens.test.mjs` instead: no literal colour outside a `var()` reference and `theme()`, a length only as 0, 1px (the hairline, which a style reports as any other length), a percentage, a viewport or container length or a token (a `var()`'s fallback read as a value of its own, and a number times a length read as that length), `@media` and `@container` conditions from the theme, and no `@apply`. Every `theme()` and `var(--ds-…)` names a key the token build writes. A literal that no token of its value and role holds is counted, with its reason, in `test/css-token-allow.json`, which may only shrink: it holds the text floor of a field on a coarse pointer, `max(1rem, 16px)`, the reader's text size and iOS Safari's zoom threshold. In a component file, a `<style>` element is `no-style-design-value`'s, and a colour attribute on an SVG element or a recharts part is `no-raw-colour`'s.
- **The files where a rule is off, and the sites that waive one.** In the package's stories `no-arbitrary-value` and the five usage rules are off, and in `primitives/bleed.tsx` `no-margin` is. A class has one owner, so where its owner is off no other rule reports it: an arbitrary value or a variable shorthand in a story (`w-[240px]`, `w-(--rail)`, `bg-brand-bold/[0.5]`), and a margin at any key in `bleed.tsx` (`mt-4`, `mt-[13px]`); a `dark:` class is `no-dark-variant`'s in both. The same holds at one site: a line disable, an allowance or a bulk suppression of a class's owner waives the whole class, so a margin that is also a stock key or an arbitrary value (`my-2`, `-mx-[13px]`) under a disable of `no-margin`, or a variable shorthand under an allowance of `no-arbitrary-value`, is reported by no other rule. `test/lint-ownership.test.mjs` pins all three.
- **The plugin under another name.** `no-inline-config` and this repository's directive count know the rules as `ledger/…`. Registered under another name (`plugins: { ds: ledger }`), a comment that turns `ds/no-margin` off is not reported or counted. The presets register it as `ledger`; keep that name.

What crosses files, such as where focus returns or whether a custom link renders an anchor, is checked by the browser suites.

## What the lint knows of Tailwind

The rules never load Tailwind. The token build asks it once, in `build/lint-data.mjs`, which `npm run build:tokens` runs after the tokens, and writes the answers beside the allowlist. `src/generated/lint.json` holds what a file may need: the name of every `@utility` the kit's CSS declares; the utilities a leading minus negates; the variant grammar, with the breakpoints and container sizes and their values, the static variants that are a media query around a selector (`hover`), which a negation splits in two, and the roots that take a CSS variable as their value (`nth-(--n)`), which no selector reads; the ARIA attribute names, aria-query's and the three ARIA 1.3 adds that it lacks; shadcn's theme names, so a class is known as one without the values; the class categories, tailwind-merge's grammar merged with the kit's merge config with each group's category and each `@utility`'s by the properties its CSS sets, which `no-restyle` reads (What a part sets); and the hash of each file the data was built from. `no-unknown-variant` checks every variant of every class against that grammar, compounds through to the variant they wrap. `src/generated/lint-values.json` holds what only a finding's advice needs: each `@utility`'s file, line and the properties it sets; each token's value (a length in px, a duration in ms, a colour in OKLab as the reader sees it in each mode); the token behind each token class; which token class generates the same CSS as a token's variable written in a class (`bg-(--ds-elevation-surface)` is `bg-surface`, `p-[var(--ds-space-200)]` is `p-200`), each pair checked against Tailwind, which `no-arbitrary-value` fixes to; the properties of each utility that takes a space but no minus, which `no-non-token-class` names; the Ledger classes for each of shadcn's theme names, from `build/vocabulary-aliases.json` as the build checked it; and Tailwind's stock scales and palette, which a finding's nearest token is ranked against. A rule reads `lint.json` on the first file that needs it and `lint-values.json` only when a finding needs a value. Both ship with the package, in `src/generated` and `dist/generated`, and are read from the same one; `ledger.css` keeps them out of Tailwind's scan, since they spell classes no element renders.

The data reflects Tailwind 4.3.3, the release the kit is built and tested with, and `lint.json` records it; on another Tailwind 4 release a variant or a utility may generate CSS the data does not describe. The breakpoints are the kit's seven (`sm`, `md`, `lg`, `aside`, `panel`, `wide`, and `xl`, the alias of `panel` behind Grid's `xl` column count): the reset clears Tailwind's, so `2xl:` generates nothing. The data is stale when, in the kit's checkout, a file it was built from (the allowlist, the token docs, a stylesheet or the theme-name table) has changed since the build, or when `lint-values.json` comes from another build than `lint.json`. Whichever of `no-arbitrary-value`, `no-unknown-variant` and `no-non-token-class` runs first on a file says so once, at line 1, naming the file that changed; `no-arbitrary-value` writes no token class until the data is fresh; no allowance counts the finding; and `npm run build:tokens` fixes it. A product's installed package ships without the token docs, so its lint compares no file and pays nothing for the check. A missing or unreadable file stops the lint with an error that names it.

## When a finding looks wrong

- **Read the rule's page first.** Its examples show what it reports and what it allows, and its Limits say what it cannot see.
- **The tokens or the exports changed.** The allowlist and the theme-name table come from the token build, and the part names, each part's styling props, what each part sets and the overlays' width steps from the source: run `npm run build:tokens` after a change to the tokens or to `build/vocabulary-aliases.json`, and `npm run build:lint` after a change to the exports, a part's props or classes or an overlay's width steps, then lint again.
- **A cached run.** The plugin reads its data once per process, the first time a rule needs it, so `eslint --cache` or an editor's ESLint server can keep a result across a token rebuild. Run without `--cache`, delete `.eslintcache`, or restart the server.
- **The kit is linted on its own.** The repository's root `npm run lint` ignores `packages/`; the kit lints itself with `npm run lint -w packages/design-system`, under `configs.package`.
- **Tailwind generates a class the lint rejects.** The lint admits the tokens and the documented structural utilities only. A missing token or part is a kit change through `/ledger-add-part`, never an allowance or a disable.

## Corpus ratchets

In this repository `npm run lint:corpus` lints two corpora, and `npm run lint:corpus -- --check`, a step of CI, holds them to `scripts/lint-corpus-baseline.json` as committed at the base ref.

- **The clean corpus** is the application's product files and this package's source, stories included, each under its own config, with every allowance and inline disable taken off. Its count per rule may only fall: a rise means a rule now reports code it passed before, so the code or the rule changes, never the count. A rule new to the plugin starts its count. A rule the base counts and the plugin no longer has fails until the baseline says what became of it: `"renamed": {"ledger/old": "ledger/new"}` holds the new name to the old count, and `"removed": ["ledger/old"]` lets the count go.
- **Where each rule runs** is recorded beside the counts: the configs' global ignores, and every block that sets a ledger rule, with its files and ignores. A block that turns a rule off for a file, an ignore or a narrower glob hides reports the way an allowance does, with no count, so every file the base had keeps each rule the base's config ran on it. A new file takes the reach its config gives it.
- **The stock corpus** is `test/fixtures/stock-classes.json`: the class strings of shadcn's registry, from `@shadcn/lint` under its MIT notice and pinned to that file's hash by the script's tests, and a hand list of Tailwind's palette and scales. Each class is linted on its own element in a product file, and the baseline names the classes no rule reports on. The corpus may only grow, so a class cannot leave with its verdict. A class the base reported that starts to pass is named in the baseline's `stock.admitted` in the same change, with a pointer to the page that makes it structural, `docs/guides/component-library.md` or this page's What counts as structural (`packages/design-system/src/stories/docs/Lint.mdx#what-counts-as-structural`); that page names it in backticks, as written, as its utility without variants, or as its utility's prefix followed by an asterisk. The number of the base's classes that two or more rules report may only fall.

After a change that moves a count, the reach or the corpus, `npm run lint:corpus -- --update` rewrites the baseline and lists what moved, each rule that gained or lost a file and each stock class that changed verdict included; commit it with the change, since `--check` also fails when the baseline is not the tree's own measurement. `--update` keeps `renamed`, `removed` and `stock.admitted` and never writes them. `-- --rule <rule>` prints every finding of one rule in both corpora. `-- --digest` prints a hash of every finding (file, line, column, rule and message), the same on every run over the same tree, which shows that a refactor of the lint changes no finding. In CI a push's all-zero base stands for the commit before HEAD, and a shallow clone without it fails rather than compare with nothing.

## Measuring

In this repository `npm run bench:lint` times the lint as it runs here: the product files under the root config and this package's source under its own, each through the ESLint API in a fresh process. It reports the median wall time over `--runs` (5 by default) after one warm-up, with its spread, files per second, peak memory, the time per rule from ESLint's `stats`, what the rules cost over a parse-only run, and the cold start: importing the plugin, the first file against the same file warm, and which data files the plugin reads on the way (`lint.json` on the first file with a class site, `lint-values.json` on the first finding that needs a value). A run whose findings differ from the others fails, and says whether the tree changed underneath it. It is not a CI step, since timings depend on the machine: compare two runs on one machine with `-- --json <file>` and `-- --compare <file>`, and write results outside the checkout.

## Running it

```js
// eslint.config.js in a product
import ledger from "@ledger/design-system/eslint";

export default [
  ...ledger.configs.recommended,
  // The two opt-in layout rules, for the files that follow the product contract.
  {
    files: ["src/routes/**/*.tsx"],
    rules: {
      "ledger/product-responsive-table": "error",
      "ledger/product-line-tabs": "error",
      // A rule's findings end with its note: where this product's own part stands in for the kit's.
      "ledger/no-native-confirm": ["error", { note: "In this app: useConfirmation." }],
    },
  },
];
```

Every rule takes a `note` option, a sentence of at most 200 characters that each of its findings ends with, for what the kit cannot know: the product's own binding of the advice. `settings.ledger.note` gives every rule one, before the rule's own. A note that is not a string, or is too long, is named once on stderr and ignored.

The class rules read the helpers `cn`, `clsx`, `twMerge` and `classes`, and `cx`, `twJoin` and `classNames` where the file imports them (a chart's own `cx` is not one), clsx-style (an object's keys are classes); and `cva`, and `tv` where the file imports it, by their configs (`base`, `slots`, `variants` and a `class` or `className` are classes; `defaultVariants`, `responsiveVariants`, `extend` and compound selectors are names; tv's first argument is always a config, and cva's is its base unless it has a config's key). An import of `cn` from the kit, or of clsx, classnames, tailwind-merge, class-variance-authority or tailwind-variants, counts under another name (`import { cn as merge }`) and through a namespace (`u.cn`), and so does a const that holds a helper (`const merge = cn`). `settings.ledger.classFunctions` names a product's own helpers read as `cn` is, and `settings.ledger.variantFunctions` those read as `tv` is; each takes a name, or a list of names, as the helper is called. `settings.ledger.customVariants` names the variants a product declares in its own CSS with `@custom-variant`, as a class writes them before the colon, which `no-unknown-variant` then knows, alone and inside a compound, in every file of the run. A value the lint cannot use is named once on stderr and ignored.

`configs.package` sets `settings.ledger.kit` to `"self"`. In the kit's own source a part imported by a relative path (`./button`, `../components/table`, a barrel) is then the part, as an import from `@ledger/design-system` is in a product, and so is a part's own top-level declaration; an import from `src/stories` or `src/lib`, and a story's or a helper's own component of a part's name, is no part. A product leaves it unset, and any other value is named once on stderr and ignored.

```sh
# inside the package
npm run lint

# in a product, after adopting the preset
npx eslint src
```

## Asking the lint without ESLint

`@ledger/design-system/eslint` also exports, by name, what the lint knows, for a tool, an editor or an agent that asks about one class, one tag or one value rather than a file. Each function is synchronous and pure, reads the same data the rules read the first time it needs it (`eslint-plugin/api.js`), and loads no ESLint; stale lint data is an error that names the fix.

```js
import {
  classify,
  suggestClass,
  kitPartOf,
  tokensOfValue,
  tokenValue,
  tokenOfClass,
  classCategories,
  partsSetting,
} from "@ledger/design-system/eslint";

classify("mt-4").rule; // "ledger/no-margin": the one rule that reports the class
suggestClass("p-4").replacements; // ["p-200"], the editor suggestion: the same 16px
suggestClass("dark:bg-gray-900", { siblings: "bg-white" }).advice[0]; // the roles of its colour
kitPartOf("T.Cell", "@ledger/design-system", { imported: "Table" }); // "Table.Cell"
tokensOfValue("16px").map(({ name, role }) => `${name} (${role})`); // dimension.icon.medium (icon-size), space.200 (space)
tokenValue("motion.duration.medium").ms; // 150
tokenOfClass("gap-150"); // "space.150"
classCategories("hover:p-200").categories; // ["spacing"]
partsSetting("font-body-small")[0].part; // "Text", through its size prop
```

- **`classify(cls)`** names the rule that reports a class and why, the one owner every class has, with the data its message reads.
- **`suggestClass(cls, { siblings })`** gives what the finding says to write: the `cause` (its message id), the `advice` its words are fitted from, and the `replacements`, flagged `fixable` when `--fix` writes the first and `suggested` when an editor suggestion writes each; otherwise they are the choices the advice names. `siblings` are the other classes on the element, which a `dark:` colour is read with. The class is read by itself: on a kit part or a plain layout element the finding may name a prop instead.
- **`kitPartOf(name, source, { imported, kit, filename })`** is the part identity the rules judge a tag by, from plain data instead of a file's syntax tree: the name as written in JSX, the module its root comes from, and the name the import names when it is an alias, `"*"` for a namespace. `kit: "self"` with the importing file's absolute path reads a relative import as the kit's own source does. It returns `""` for no kit part.
- **`tokenValue(name)`**, **`tokensOfValue(value, { kind, role, mode })`** and **`tokenOfClass(cls)`** look tokens up by name, by value (a length, a part's size in ch or vw, an em, a duration, a number or a colour, in either mode) and by the class that writes them, each record with its kind, family, role and purpose.
- **`classCategories(cls)`** and **`partsSetting(cls)`** say what a class changes and which parts set it themselves, as `ledger/no-restyle` reads them.

A function that takes a class takes exactly one, with any variants, and throws a `TypeError` for anything else. Every other argument is checked the same way: an options value that is not an object, an option of the wrong type, a `mode` other than `"light"` or `"dark"`, a `kind` or `role` the lint data does not hold, and `kit: "self"` without an absolute `filename` each throw a `TypeError` that names it. An answer is a frozen copy, so changing it changes nothing a rule reads. `test/lint-api.test.mjs` holds each answer to the finding ESLint reports for the same class or import.

The API is plain JavaScript and the package ships no type declarations for `@ledger/design-system/eslint`: its types are the JSDoc in `eslint-plugin/api.js`. A strict TypeScript file that imports it needs a declaration of its own, which types each answer as `any`:

```ts
declare module "@ledger/design-system/eslint";
```

<!-- page: Guidance/Lint rules reference (src/stories/docs/LintRules.mdx) -->

# Lint rules reference

Every rule of `@ledger/design-system/eslint`, one section each, from the pages the plugin ships in `eslint-plugin/docs/`, where each finding's `meta.docs.url` points. A section says what the rule reports, why, what to write instead, its fixes, its allowances and what it cannot see, with examples that `test/lint-docs.test.mjs` lints on every run: each reported example is reported by its rule and by no other, since a class has one owner, and each allowed example is reported by no rule. The [Lint rules](?path=/docs/guidance-lint-rules--docs) page has the table of rules and presets.

## ledger/no-arbitrary-value

Reports a class with an arbitrary value (`text-[13px]`, `w-[240px]`, `bg-[#eee]`), which bypasses the tokens.

### Reports

- A class whose value is written in square brackets: after a utility (`w-[240px]`, `text-[13px]`, `bg-[#eee]`, `grid-cols-[200px_1fr]`), as an opacity (`bg-brand-bold/[0.5]`), or as a whole property (`[mask:none]`), with or without variants (`md:w-[240px]`). It says the class is an arbitrary value, then names the token of the value's role nearest it, only from the family the utility's role names: a space for padding, gap, inset and translate (`"p-[13px]" is an arbitrary value. Nearest: p-150 (12px) or p-200 (16px).`), a type style for a text size (`13px is font-body.`), a radius, a border width (1px is the utility's own `border` or `border-t`), a duration, the two opacities, and the roles a colour's hue plays, each with its purpose. A width or a height names no token: `"w-[240px]" is an arbitrary value. A width is a layout part's, a part's preset or computed from its container (w-full, a grid track).` (a height's example is `h-full`), except 1px, which is its own spelling (`h-[1px]` is `h-px`). Zero is `space.0` (`top-[0px]` is `top-0`); a radius from 32px up rounds a pill's ends and names `rounded-full` (9999px is it exactly); an outline's width names the border widths and `outline-focused`, a ring's width the focus outline, a weight in brackets its weight (`font-[500]` is `font-medium`) and a delay a duration token in style. On an element [`ledger/use-primitives`](#ledgeruse-primitives) reads, in a product, a padding or a gap is named as its primitive's prop (`16px is space.200: padding="space.200" on a Box.`), with no class suggestion. A colour's hue is read from its lightness too, so a pale status tint (`bg-[#fef2f2]`) is its hue's, not a grey's. Any other value asks for a token utility or a primitive prop.
- Tailwind 4's variable shorthand, for a value or an opacity, typed or not (`w-(--rail)`, `bg-(image:--hero)`, `bg-brand-bold/(--alpha)`): `"w-(--rail)" reads a CSS variable the lint cannot compare with a token.`
- A Ledger token's own variable, in the shorthand or in brackets, typed or not (`bg-(--ds-elevation-surface)`, `bg-[var(--ds-elevation-surface)]`, `bg-(color:--ds-elevation-surface)`). Where a token class generates the same CSS, the finding names it and `--fix` writes it: `"bg-(--ds-elevation-surface)" writes a token's variable by hand. Use "bg-surface", the token utility that generates the same CSS.` Where none does (`divide-[var(--ds-color-border)]`, or a type hint that sends the value to another property, `bg-(length:--ds-elevation-surface)`), it is reported as an arbitrary value.

One report per class. The rule reads classes wherever the class rules do: `className`, `class` (a `class` value that reads as no classes, such as OSCAL's `"sp800-53a"`, is data), any `*ClassName` attribute or object key, any `*Class` attribute of an element (`containerClass`, `iconClass`) for the strings in it that read as classes or are each a class Tailwind places (a word no class is spelt like is the prop's data: `impactClass="high"`, react-scroll's `activeClass="active"`), a slot map (a `classNames` object, by its values at any depth; a `classNames` string is a prefix), a readable object spread onto an element, the class helpers (`cn`, `clsx`, `twMerge` and `classes`; `cx`, `twJoin` and `classNames` where the file imports them; `cva`, and `tv` where imported, by their configs; the names in `settings.ledger.classFunctions` and `settings.ledger.variantFunctions`; a known helper imported under another name or read from a namespace; and a const that holds a helper, `const merge = cn`), a className callback, and what a class site reads in the same file: a `const`; a `let` or `var` with each value assigned to it, and text appended after a space; a destructured slot; the defaults a component gives its props; an entry of a map, a list, an enum or an `Object.freeze` (every entry, for a key known only at runtime); a key a helper's object computes from a same-file value (`cn({ [active]: on })`); each entry of a list a `.map` callback walks; what a function, a `useMemo`, a `useCallback` or a `useState` gives, and what each call gives a same-file function's parameter (`note("text-danger")`); a `[…].join(" ")`, `.filter(Boolean)`, `.trim()`, `.concat()`, `Object.values()` or a spread argument; a template hole that brings its own space (`` `flex${on ? " gap-100" : ""}` ``); and a DOM element's classes, written to `className` (`el.className = "…"`, `+=`) or given to `classList.add` and `classList.toggle`. A module-level string or map whose strings read as classes is reported where it is declared, through an `Object.freeze`, a same-file spread, each branch of a condition, a template's own text and the values of `Object.fromEntries` or `new Map`, but not its data: a bare word no rule knows (`"danger"`, `"none"`), or a key whose values across its records are mostly not classes. A bare word is no evidence that a map holds classes (`"flex"` is also a CSS value, `"hidden"` an attribute), so a style object, a list of attributes or a list of views is no class map.

Not reported: a grid template whose tracks carry no length (`grid-cols-[auto_1fr]`, `grid-cols-[minmax(0,1fr)_auto]`, `grid-rows-[subgrid]`). Its tracks size to content or share the free space, which is structure. Nor are the two variables the kit reads as structure: Grid's responsive columns (`grid-cols-(--ds-grid-md)`) and a disclosure panel's measured height (`h-(--accordion-panel-height)`, `h-(--collapsible-panel-height)`).
