## Related

- [Inline](?path=/docs/primitives-inline--docs) and [Stack](?path=/docs/primitives-stack--docs): the row and the column, first.
- [Grid](?path=/docs/primitives-grid--docs): columns of a template, for a layout with widths.
- [Space](?path=/docs/tokens-space--docs): the scale.

## Don't

A row with one gap is an Inline, a column a Stack and two columns with a fixed rail a Grid; Flex is for what those cannot say, never a stand-in for them.

_Example: story `Stories.Dont`._

<!-- page: Primitives/Grid (src/stories/primitives/Grid.mdx) -->

# Grid

**Status: Stable.**

Columns and rows on a template. The template is a string, the CSS value itself, or one string per breakpoint; the gaps are tokens. It is the primitive for a layout with widths: a main column and a rail, a label column and a value column, cards of equal width, a form's fields in two columns that become one on a narrow page. The one thing past a plain grid is the template per breakpoint, which travels as a CSS variable a static class reads, so a page never writes an arbitrary class. A page grid with gutters and margins is the Shell's areas' job, not this.

_Example: story `Stories.GridMatrix`._

## Anatomy

| Part      | What it is                                                                                                                                            |
| --------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Container | A grid: a `div`, or the layout element `as` names. `as="dl"` for label and value pairs.                                                               |
| Template  | `templateColumns`, a `grid-template-columns` value, or `{ base, sm, md, lg, xl }`, each applying from that width up; `templateRows`; `templateAreas`. |
| Gap       | `gap` on both axes; `rowGap` and `columnGap` over it. Tokens.                                                                                         |
| Alignment | `alignItems` on the block axis, `justifyContent` on the inline axis.                                                                                  |
| Flow      | `autoFlow`: `row`, `column`, `dense`, `row-dense`, `column-dense`.                                                                                    |

## Variants

| Grid            | Use                                                                                                                                                               |
| --------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Equal columns   | `repeat(n, minmax(0, 1fr))`: cards, stats, fields of a form.                                                                                                      |
| Label and value | `104px 1fr` as a `dl`: the facts of a rail, a settings list. KeyValue draws one row of it.                                                                        |
| Main and rail   | `minmax(0, 1fr) 272px`: a body and a rail at `dimension.layout.rail` inside a region. A record page's rail is the Shell's Aside, which places itself beside Main. |
| Named areas     | `templateAreas` with `templateRows`: a head over two columns, a form with a full-width row.                                                                       |
| Responsive      | One template per breakpoint of the window: one column, two from `md`, main and rail from `lg`.                                                                    |

Not built, and why: a column count per breakpoint as a number (the template says the widths as well as the count, and `repeat(3, minmax(0, 1fr))` is one string); a page grid with gutters and margins (the Shell's areas and the page's gutter tokens do this, and a page here is a form or a register, not a magazine); `justifyItems` and `alignContent` (no layout here has needed them, and a cell that sits differently carries its own class); `templateAreas` as an array of rows (one string is the CSS value, and the reader can paste it).

## Sizes

The gaps are the space scale: `space.050` between facts, `space.100` between cells, `space.200` between cards and form fields, `space.300` between the main column and the rail. The breakpoints, the `dimension.breakpoint.*` tokens (`md` and `lg` on Tailwind's values; the shell's `aside`, `panel` and `wide` are on the Metrics page):

| Key    | From   |
| ------ | ------ |
| `base` | 0      |
| `sm`   | 640px  |
| `md`   | 768px  |
| `lg`   | 1024px |
| `xl`   | 1280px |

The widths a template names come from the layout tokens where one exists: `dimension.layout.rail` 272px, `.panel` 320px, `.list` 340px, `.measure` 720px, on the [Metrics](?path=/docs/tokens-metrics--docs) sheet.

## Modifiers

- **`templateColumns`**: a string, or an object with `base` and any of `sm`, `md`, `lg`, `xl`. Write `minmax(0, 1fr)`, never a bare `1fr`: a fraction's minimum is its content, and a long file name would widen its column past the frame.
- **`templateRows`**, **`templateAreas`**: strings.
- **`gap`**, **`rowGap`**, **`columnGap`**: tokens.
- **`alignItems`**: `start`, `center`, `end`, `baseline`, `stretch`. **`justifyContent`**: the six distributions and `stretch`.
- **`autoFlow`**: `dense` to fill holes in a grid of spanning cells.
- **`shrink`**: `none` keeps the Grid's size when its parent row runs out of room.
- **`as`**: `dl` for pairs, `ul` for a list of cards; the layout elements.

## Content

- **Widths in the template, once.** Not on the children in three places.
- **`minmax(0, 1fr)`**, so a column can shrink below its content and the content truncates or wraps inside it.
- **One template per breakpoint** when the layout changes with width. Three columns at every width is 90px each in a rail.
- **The breakpoints are the window's, not the grid's.** A responsive template suits the page's own layout, as Atlassian's Grid does; inside a Shell.Panel, an aside or a sheet the window stays wide while the space is narrow, and the template keeps its wide columns. A part that lives in a panel lays out by its own width with one intrinsic template, `repeat(auto-fit, minmax(min(100%, 144px), 1fr))`: six columns on the page, two in a 320px panel.
- **Chips are not a grid.** Things of their own width that wrap are an Inline; a Grid stretches each to its column and leaves a hole in the last row.
- **Pairs are a `dl`.** A label column and a value column with `dt` and `dd` children, so the pairs are pairs to a screen reader.

_Example: story `Stories.IntrinsicInAPanel`._

## Style

| Element   | Token                                                                                                               |
| --------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Gap       | `space.*`, as `gap-*`, `gap-x-*`, `gap-y-*`                                                                         |
| Template  | Inline `grid-template-columns` for a string; `grid-cols-(--ds-grid-<bp>)` per breakpoint, the value in the variable |
| Widths    | `dimension.layout.rail`, `.panel`, `.list`, `.measure` where the template names a layout width                      |
| Alignment | `items-*`, `justify-*`, `grid-flow-*`                                                                               |

## Accessibility

- **Visual order is DOM order.** `autoFlow="dense"` can fill a hole with a later cell, moving it before an earlier one to the eye; use it for cells that have no order, tiles of a dashboard, never for fields of a form.
- **Pairs are a `dl`**, list cards a `ul`; a grid of cells with no relation stays a `div`.
- **A responsive template does not reorder.** The cells keep their order at every width; only the columns change.
- **`templateAreas` may reorder.** A named area can place a later cell first; a form's fields keep their template in order.

## Props

_Props of `Grid`, generated from its types:_

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `as` | `LayoutElement` | `div` | The element: a container, a list or a description list (`dl` for label and value pairs). Never a link or a button. |
| `ref` | `Ref<HTMLElement>` |  |  |
| `templateColumns` | `string \| ResponsiveTemplate` |  | A grid-template-columns value, or one per breakpoint (`base` applies always, the others from that width up). The breakpoints are the window's, for page layout; a grid inside a panel uses one intrinsic template, such as `repeat(auto-fit, minmax(min(100%, 144px), 1fr))`, which follows its own width. Template strings stay strings; the gaps are tokens. |
| `templateRows` | `string` |  | A grid-template-rows value. |
| `templateAreas` | `string` |  | A grid-template-areas value: quoted rows, one string. |
| `gap` | `"space.0" \| "space.025" \| "space.050" \| "space.075" \| "space.100" \| "space.150" \| "space.200" \| "space.250" \| "space.300" \| "space.400" \| "space.500" \| "space.600" \| "space.800" \| "space.1000"` |  | Space between cells on both axes. |
| `rowGap` | `"space.0" \| "space.025" \| "space.050" \| "space.075" \| "space.100" \| "space.150" \| "space.200" \| "space.250" \| "space.300" \| "space.400" \| "space.500" \| "space.600" \| "space.800" \| "space.1000"` |  | Space between rows, over `gap`. |
| `columnGap` | `"space.0" \| "space.025" \| "space.050" \| "space.075" \| "space.100" \| "space.150" \| "space.200" \| "space.250" \| "space.300" \| "space.400" \| "space.500" \| "space.600" \| "space.800" \| "space.1000"` |  | Space between columns, over `gap`. |
| `alignItems` | `"baseline" \| "center" \| "end" \| "start" \| "stretch"` |  |  |
| `justifyContent` | `"center" \| "end" \| "space-around" \| "space-between" \| "space-evenly" \| "start" \| "stretch"` |  |  |
| `autoFlow` | `"column-dense" \| "column" \| "dense" \| "row-dense" \| "row"` |  |  |
| `shrink` | `"none"` |  | As a flex item: `none` keeps its size when the row runs out of room, for a fixed label such as an id; the default lets it shrink. |
| `className` | `string` |  |  |
| `style` | `CSSProperties` |  | Runtime values only: a template computed at render. A design value is a token or a class. |

### Playground

_Example: story `Stories.Playground`._

_Rendered in the Storybook: Controls._

## Related

- [Inline](?path=/docs/primitives-inline--docs): things of their own width, wrapping.
- [Flex](?path=/docs/primitives-flex--docs): a row or a column distributed, without widths.
- [KeyValue](?path=/docs/components-keyvalue--docs): one row of the label and value grid.
- [Stat](?path=/docs/components-stat--docs): `Stat.Grid`, a grid of tiles with the grid's own rules.
- [Pages](?path=/docs/layout-pages--docs): the record page's main column and rail, which the Shell's Main and Aside lay out.
- [Space](?path=/docs/tokens-space--docs) and [Metrics](?path=/docs/tokens-metrics--docs): the gaps and the layout widths.

## Don't

Columns are `minmax(0, 1fr)`, never a bare `1fr` that a long word widens. A layout that changes with the width takes a template per breakpoint, never three columns at every width, and chips are an Inline, never a Grid.

_Example: story `Stories.Dont`._

<!-- page: Primitives/Heading (src/stories/primitives/Heading.mdx) -->

# Heading

**Status: Stable.**

A title. The size is the title it matches and the level is the page's: `size` picks one of the titles the kit draws (the page and record title, an overlay's title, a section's title) or a figure bigger than a Stat's, with an element to go with it, and `as` overrides the element when the outline needs another level. The kit draws its own titles as Headings at these sizes: PageHeader.Title, Section.Title, DialogTitle, SheetTitle, AlertDialogTitle, DrawerTitle and a Stat's figure. A title set with Heading therefore matches the screen around it. The colour is the text colour, or its inverse on a bold fill, which a Box sets for you; a tone is not a heading colour. Inside a `HeadingLevelProvider` the level comes from the context, as below.

_Example: story `Stories.Sizes`._

## Anatomy

| Part    | What it is                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| ------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Element | The contextual level inside a HeadingLevelProvider; otherwise by size: `page` an `h1`, `section` an `h2`, `overlay` an `h3`, `display` a `div`. `as` overrides either with a `HeadingElement`: a level, a `div` or a `span`. |
| Size    | `page`, `overlay`, `section`, `display`: the four `font.heading` tokens of the same names.                                                                                                                                   |
| Colour  | `color.text`, inherited; `color.text.inverse` or `color.text.warning.inverse` from a bold Box.                                                                                                                               |

_Example: story `Stories.HeadingMatrix`._

## Roles

| Heading   | The title it matches                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| --------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `page`    | The page and record title, the one `h1`: what PageHeader.Title draws on a page, and as a preview's record name at the level its outline gives it. A Stat's figure is this size as a `div`.                                                    |
| `overlay` | An overlay's title: what DialogTitle, SheetTitle, AlertDialogTitle and DrawerTitle draw, each its overlay's `h2`. A group heading inside an overlay takes it, an `h3` there; a card's title is the same style, and CardTitle draws it itself. |
| `section` | A section's title: what Section.Title draws, an `h2` under the page's title and one level below inside a titled Section. A step's heading in a wizard and a rail's group heading take it at their level.                                      |
| `display` | A figure bigger than a Stat's, or the one title of a screen with nothing else on it (sign-in) given `as="h1"`. A `div` by default and in every context, because a number is not a title. Never a page or record title.                        |

Not built, and why: a size between `display` and `page` (the page title is the biggest title the product sets, and nothing in it is a hero); a size for the Eyebrow (it is uppercase and subtle, `font.heading.xxsmall` on the Typography page, and not a title); a separate size for a Stat's figure (it is the page title's size, so the two stay level); a subtitle slot (the line under a title is a Text, and the PageHeader draws it); an icon before (a Heading is words; the mark beside a record's title is the PageHeader's); a tone (a red heading says the word is the problem; the count beside it is).

## Sizes

| Size      | Token                  | Size / leading / weight | Element | Drawn by                                                       |
| --------- | ---------------------- | ----------------------- | ------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `page`    | `font.heading.page`    | 20 / 26 / semibold      | `h1`    | PageHeader.Title; a Stat's figure, as a `div`.                 |
| `overlay` | `font.heading.overlay` | 15 / 22 / medium        | `h3`    | DialogTitle, SheetTitle, AlertDialogTitle, DrawerTitle (`h2`). |
| `section` | `font.heading.section` | 13 / 18 / semibold      | `h2`    | Section.Title.                                                 |
| `display` | `font.heading.display` | 28 / 34 / semibold      | `div`   | A figure bigger than a Stat's.                                 |

`section` is the body size at semibold, the size of a disclosure's header, so a section's title sits level with the controls in its row. Under the ramp, `font.heading.xxsmall` at 11 / 14, uppercase, is the Eyebrow.

## The titles the kit draws

PageHeader.Title, Section.Title, the overlays' titles and a Stat's figure render a Heading at their size, so changing a size on the ramp changes every title drawn at it, and a Heading beside one of them is the same type. A part that renders as another through `render` keeps its own size: a PageHeader.Title rendered as SheetTitle, a preview's record name, stays at `page` as the sheet's `h2`.

_Example: story `Stories.KitTitles`._

A screen built from those parts needs no Heading for them. Heading is for a title those parts do not draw: a step's heading in a wizard, a group inside a dialog, the title of a screen that has no PageHeader. A raw `h1`–`h6` with a type class copies a title's look and misses the next change to it; write the Heading at the size it matches.

## Level from context

`HeadingLevelProvider` sets which level a heading placed inside takes. With `level` it starts an outline (a portalled region, a rail that sits under the page's h1 at 2); without it, it goes one below the surrounding level, and the first one gives 2, the level under the page's title. `useHeadingLevel()` reads it, `undefined` outside every provider.

The kit's own titles read the same context, and each keeps its default where nothing sets one. On a page without a provider, PageHeader.Title is an h1, Section.Title an h2, EmptyTitle an h2, Shell.Panel.Title an h2, CollapsibleHeader, AccordionTrigger, Inspector.Group, Item.Group and Related an h3. An overlay's title is its `h2` whatever the context, and headings inside the overlay start at 3. A titled Section gives its content the next level, and a Shell.Panel starts at 2 with its body one below a title. A Heading without `as` takes the contextual level too; `display`, a displayed number, stays a div.

_Example: story `Stories.LevelFromContext`._

Context follows the React tree, portals included: content portalled into another region (a panel, a dialog) keeps the level of the place it was rendered from. A portal that starts a new outline wraps its content in `HeadingLevelProvider level={n}`.

## Deprecated sizes

`large`, `medium`, `small` and `xsmall` are deprecated for one version, each drawn with the step that replaced it. `large` is `display`, `medium` is `page` and `xsmall` is `overlay`, each keeping its element, and `ledger/no-deprecated-name` writes the new names. `small` draws `page` at medium weight, 20 / 26 medium, as an h2: a page or record title is `page`, and a section's title is `section`.

_Example: story `Stories.DeprecatedSizes`._

## Modifiers

- **`size`**: required. The title it matches.
- **`as`**: the page's choice, over the context's. `h2` for a rail's group at the section size; `h4` for a subsection; `div` for a title-sized line where the outline already has its `h1`.
- **`color`**: `color.text`, `color.text.inverse`, `color.text.warning.inverse`. Left off, it follows the surface.
- **`id`**, for a section's `aria-labelledby`.
- **No `style`.** A heading has no computed dimension.

## Content

- **One `h1`.** The page's title; every other title is `as="h2"` or below, whatever its size.
- **The outline in order.** No `h3` under an `h1` without an `h2` between, and no level chosen for its size.
- **A title is a noun phrase**, sentence case, no full stop: "Assessment results", "Schedule assessment".
- **The size is the title's job.** A page or record title is `page`, a section's title `section`, an overlay's `overlay`; a title is never set bigger to stand out.
- **`display` is display**, not a page or record title: a figure bigger than a Stat's, or the one title of a screen that has nothing else (sign-in), given `as="h1"`.
- **A tone goes on the fact beside the title**, never on the title.

## Style

| Element | Token                                                                                                         |
| ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Size    | `font.heading.page` · `.overlay` · `.section` · `.display`, family, size, leading, weight and tracking in one |
| Colour  | `color.text` · `color.text.inverse` · `color.text.warning.inverse`                                            |

## Accessibility

- **The level is the element**, and the element is the page's decision, through the context or `as`. The size says nothing to a screen reader.
- **A section is named by its heading.** `<Box as="section" aria-labelledby>` pointing at the Heading's `id`.
- **The outline is a map.** A screen reader's user jumps by heading; two `h1`s are two pages, a skipped level is a missing floor.
- **`display` is a `div`** so a displayed number is not a heading in the outline. A Stat's label is its heading, if it needs one.
- **Contrast is the token's.** `color.text` on every surface and `color.text.inverse` on every bold fill are measured on the Color sheet.

## Props

_Props of `Heading`, generated from its types:_

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `as` | `"div" \| "h1" \| "h2" \| "h3" \| "h4" \| "h5" \| "h6" \| "span"` |  | The element, when the outline needs a level other than the contextual one. Without it a Heading takes the level from the nearest HeadingLevelProvider (or titled Section, or panel body), and outside every provider the size's default: `page` an h1, `section` an h2, `overlay` an h3, `display` a div. Level is semantic and chosen by the page; size is visual and chosen by the design. |
| `ref` | `Ref<HTMLElement>` |  |  |
| `size` (required) | `"display" \| "large" \| "medium" \| "overlay" \| "page" \| "section" \| "small" \| "xsmall"` |  | The title it matches: `page` (font.heading.page, 20/26 semibold: the page and record title, and a Stat's figure as a div) · `overlay` (font.heading.overlay, 15/22 medium: an overlay's title, a card's title, a group inside an overlay) · `section` (font.heading.section, 13/18 semibold: a section's title) · `display` (font.heading.display, 28/34 semibold: a figure bigger than a Stat's, or the sign-in screen's title). `large`, `medium`, `small` and `xsmall` are deprecated. |
| `color` | `"color.text.inverse" \| "color.text.warning.inverse" \| "color.text"` |  | `color.text` by default; `color.text.inverse` on a bold fill, which a Box with a bold background sets for you. A tone is not a heading colour. |
| `className` | `string` |  |  |

_Props of `HeadingLevelProvider`, generated from its types:_

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `level` | `1 \| 2 \| 3 \| 4 \| 5 \| 6` |  | The level a heading placed directly inside takes, 1 to 6. Leave it out to go one below the surrounding level; outside every provider the surrounding level is the page title's, so the first provider gives 2. |

### Playground

_Example: story `Stories.Playground`._

_Rendered in the Storybook: Controls._

## Related

- [Text](?path=/docs/primitives-text--docs): everything that is not a title.
- [Typography](?path=/docs/components-typography--docs): the Eyebrow, the uppercase label under the ramp.
- [PageHeader](?path=/docs/layout-pageheader--docs): where the `h1` is drawn at `page`, and the record title in a preview at the context's level.
- [Section](?path=/docs/layout-section--docs): where a section's `h2` is drawn at `section`.
- [Dialog](?path=/docs/components-dialog--docs), [Sheet](?path=/docs/components-sheet--docs), [AlertDialog](?path=/docs/components-alertdialog--docs) and [Drawer](?path=/docs/components-drawer--docs): where an overlay's `h2` is drawn at `overlay`.
- [Stat](?path=/docs/components-stat--docs): a figure with its label, at `page`; `display` is for a figure bigger than that.
- [Typography tokens](?path=/docs/tokens-typography--docs): the ramp.
- [Upgrading](?path=/docs/guidance-upgrading--docs#heading): `large`, `medium`, `small` and `xsmall`, and the size each is now.

## Don't

A page has one h1 and its outline in order, each title at the size of its job: a page title is `page`, never `display`. A heading is `color.text`, and its tone goes on the fact beside it.

_Example: story `Stories.Dont`._

<!-- page: Primitives/Inline (src/stories/primitives/Inline.mdx) -->

# Inline

**Status: Stable.**

A row with one gap. Children sit start to end with one space token between them, aligned on the block axis as the row says, wrapping when told to with a row space of their own. A separator is drawn between children and hidden from a screen reader. A separator does not belong on a list element. Here it also renders inline-level, as a `span` with `display="inline-flex"`, so a chip and a word can sit inside a sentence.

_Example: story `Stories.InlineMatrix`._

_Example: story `Stories.WrappedSeparator`._

_Example: story `Stories.GrowFillTruncates`._

## Anatomy

| Part      | What it is                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| --------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Container | A flex row: a `div`, a `span`, a list or a list item, as `as` names. `display="inline-flex"` keeps it inline-level.                                                                                     |
| Space     | `space`, one token between every pair of children on the inline axis; `rowSpace` between rows when wrapping, `space` if unset.                                                                          |
| Alignment | `alignBlock`, where the children sit on the block axis: `start`, `center`, `end`, `baseline`, `stretch` (the default, the browser's for a flex row); `alignInline`, where they sit along the row.       |
| Spread    | `spread="space-between"`: a label at the start and a count at the end.                                                                                                                                  |
| Separator | A string or node drawn between children, `aria-hidden`: the dot of a meta line, the slash of a path. In a wrapping row each child keeps the separator after it, and the one that ends a line is hidden. |
| Wrap      | `shouldWrap`, rows of chips; off, the children overflow.                                                                                                                                                |
| Grow      | `grow="fill"` takes the free space along the parent's main axis and may shrink below its content; `hug` is as big as the children.                                                                      |
| Shrink    | `shrink="none"` keeps the row's size when its parent runs out of room.                                                                                                                                  |

## Variants

| Inline       | Use                                                                                           |
| ------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Row          | An id beside a title beside a status: one token between each, on the baseline or centred.     |
| Wrapping row | Chips, tags, filters: `shouldWrap` with a `rowSpace` tighter than `space`.                    |
| Meta line    | Facts separated by a dot: `separator="·"` on subtle small text.                               |
| Spread       | A label and a count, a title and its action: `spread="space-between"`.                        |
| In text      | `as="span" display="inline-flex"`: a chip inside a sentence, the sentence's line height kept. |
| List         | `as="ul"` with `as="li"` children: a list of chips, a set of links.                           |

Not built, and why: a reverse order (the tab order would run against the eye); a `separator` that is read (the dot is decoration; a list that needs its items separated for a screen reader is a list, `as="ul"`); a per-child alignment (a child that sits differently is in its own Inline, or is a Flex); a truncating row (the children truncate themselves with Text's `maxLines`; the row does not know which one should).

## Sizes

`space` on the inline axis, `rowSpace` between wrapped rows:

| Token       | px  | Where                                           |
| ----------- | --- | ----------------------------------------------- |
| `space.050` | 4   | An icon and its word, a dot and its label.      |
| `space.075` | 6   | A small control and its neighbour.              |
| `space.100` | 8   | Chips, buttons in a group, facts on a line.     |
| `space.150` | 12  | Facts under a title, a control cluster.         |
| `space.200` | 16  | Actions at a header's end, columns of a header. |
| `space.300` | 24  | A header's title from its actions.              |

When wrapping, `rowSpace` is one step tighter than `space`: `space.100` across, `space.050` down.

## Modifiers

- **`space`** and **`rowSpace`**.
- **`alignBlock`**: `center` for controls of one height; `baseline` for text of two sizes, a title beside its id; `start` for a mark beside two lines. Left off, it is `stretch`: every child is as tall as the tallest.
- **`alignInline`**: `start`, `center`, `end`, where the children sit along the row when it is wider than they are.
- **`spread`**: `space-between`.
- **`shouldWrap`**.
- **`separator`**: a string or a node. With `shouldWrap`, each child and the separator after it wrap as one, so no line starts with a separator, and a separator that ends a line is hidden. Not with `as="ul"`, `"ol"` or `"dl"`: there it is dropped, and the console says so once.
- **`grow`**: `fill` for the Inline that takes the space between a fixed start and a fixed end. It drops the automatic minimum width, so a one-line Text inside it cuts with an ellipsis instead of pushing the row past its frame.
- **`shrink`**: `none` for the fixed part beside a filling one, an id or a count, so it never wraps inside itself.
- **`display`**: `inline-flex` for a row that sits in a run of text.
- **`as`**: `span` in text; `ul`, `ol`, `li` for a list; the layout elements.
- **No `style`.** A row of a fixed width sits in a Box with the width.

## Content

- **The dot is the separator.** Never a child: it would be read, and it would take a gap on each side.
- **Text of two sizes sits on the baseline.** A title beside an id is `alignBlock="baseline"`; controls beside each other are `center`.
- **A row that can grow wraps.** Chips, tags and filters get `shouldWrap`; a row that cannot wrap (a header's actions) has a count that is fixed.
- **A list is a list.** Chips that are a set are `as="ul"` with `li` children, and no separator.

## Style

| Element   | Token                                                                  |
| --------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Space     | `space.*`, as `gap-x-*`; `rowSpace` as `gap-y-*`                       |
| Alignment | `items-*` for `alignBlock`, `justify-*` for `alignInline` and `spread` |
| Separator | The children's font and colour; the row's `space` on each side         |
| Grow      | `flex-1 min-w-0 min-h-0` for `fill`; `shrink-0` for `shrink="none"`    |

## Accessibility

- **The separator is hidden.** It is `aria-hidden`; a screen reader hears the children, one after the other.
- **Not on a list.** A span between `li` elements is not a valid child of a list, so a list with a separator is no longer a list.
- **Visual order is DOM order.** No reverse: what is first on the line is first in the tab order.
- **A row in text is a `span`.** `as="span" display="inline-flex"` keeps a chip inside a paragraph's flow, so the paragraph is one paragraph to a screen reader.

Keyed children keep their state when separated items are reordered or removed. Use stable keys for dynamic children.

## Props

_Props of `Inline`, generated from its types:_

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `as` | `LayoutElement` | `div` | The element: a container, a list (`ul`, `ol`) or a list part (`li`). Never a link or a button. |
| `ref` | `Ref<HTMLElement>` |  |  |
| `space` | `"space.0" \| "space.025" \| "space.050" \| "space.075" \| "space.100" \| "space.150" \| "space.200" \| "space.250" \| "space.300" \| "space.400" \| "space.500" \| "space.600" \| "space.800" \| "space.1000"` |  | Space between children on the inline axis. |
| `rowSpace` | `"space.0" \| "space.025" \| "space.050" \| "space.075" \| "space.100" \| "space.150" \| "space.200" \| "space.250" \| "space.300" \| "space.400" \| "space.500" \| "space.600" \| "space.800" \| "space.1000"` |  | Space between rows when wrapping. |
| `alignBlock` | `"baseline" \| "center" \| "end" \| "start" \| "stretch"` |  | Position along the block (vertical) axis. |
| `alignInline` | `"center" \| "end" \| "start"` |  | Position along the inline (horizontal) axis. |
| `spread` | `"space-between"` |  | Distribute children with the free inline space between them. |
| `shouldWrap` | `boolean` |  | Wrap onto more rows when the children do not fit. Off, they overflow. |
| `separator` | `ReactNode` |  | Rendered between children, "·" or "/". Decorative and hidden from assistive tech. With `shouldWrap`, each child keeps the separator after it on its line, and a separator that ends a line is hidden. Not on a list element (`ul`, `ol`, `dl`): a span between list items is not a list, so it is dropped, with a warning in the console. |
| `grow` | `"fill" \| "hug"` |  | As a flex item: `fill` takes the free space along its parent's main axis (the width in a row, the height in a column) and may shrink below its content, so a truncating child inside it cuts instead of overflowing; `hug`, the default, is as big as its children. |
| `shrink` | `"none"` |  | As a flex item: `none` keeps its size when the row runs out of room, for a fixed label such as an id; the default lets it shrink. |
| `display` | `"flex" \| "inline-flex"` | `flex` | `inline-flex` keeps the row inline-level, so it can sit in a run of text: a chip, a count beside a label. |
| `className` | `string` |  |  |

## Related

- [Stack](?path=/docs/primitives-stack--docs): the column.
- [Flex](?path=/docs/primitives-flex--docs): the row an Inline cannot say.
- [Grid](?path=/docs/primitives-grid--docs): columns of a fixed template, when the children should line up across rows.
- [ButtonGroup](?path=/docs/components-buttongroup--docs): a row of buttons with the row's own rules.
- [Fact](?path=/docs/components-fact--docs): the facts a meta line is made of.
- [Space](?path=/docs/tokens-space--docs): the scale.

## Don't

A dot between items is `separator`, never a child. A row that can grow wraps with `shouldWrap`, and a list of chips is `as="ul"` with `li` children and no separator.

<!-- page: Primitives/Overview (src/stories/primitives/Primitives.mdx) -->

# Primitives

Layout and text, modelled on `@atlaskit/primitives`. Every prop that carries a design value is typed to a token, so an invalid value is a type error and a valid one is a literal class the scanner sees. Every layout primitive renders a container, a landmark or a list element, never a link or a button.

- [Box](?path=/docs/primitives-box--docs)
- [Stack](?path=/docs/primitives-stack--docs)
- [Inline](?path=/docs/primitives-inline--docs)
- [Flex](?path=/docs/primitives-flex--docs)
- [Grid](?path=/docs/primitives-grid--docs)
- [Bleed](?path=/docs/primitives-bleed--docs)
- [Text](?path=/docs/primitives-text--docs)
- [Heading](?path=/docs/primitives-heading--docs)

| Primitive                | For                                                                                                                                      | Key props                                                                                                                    |
| ------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Box**                  | Padding and a fill. No margins, ever. A bold fill paints its text inverse; a surface publishes itself to sticky children.                | `padding`, `paddingInline`, `paddingBlock` (space tokens), `backgroundColor` (a background or surface token), `shrink`, `as` |
| **Stack**                | A column with one gap.                                                                                                                   | `space`, `alignInline`, `alignBlock`, `spread`, `grow`, `shrink`, `as`                                                       |
| **Inline**               | A row with one gap, optionally wrapping. `display="inline-flex"` keeps it inline-level for a chip or a count beside a label.             | `space`, `rowSpace`, `alignBlock`, `alignInline`, `spread`, `shouldWrap`, `separator`, `grow`, `shrink`, `display`           |
| **Flex**                 | The escape hatch when Stack and Inline are not enough. No reverse.                                                                       | `direction`, `gap`, `alignItems`, `justifyContent`, `wrap`, `shrink`                                                         |
| **Grid**                 | Columns or rows on a template. `templateColumns` takes a string, or one per breakpoint (`{ base, sm, md, lg, xl }`).                     | `templateColumns`, `templateRows`, `templateAreas`, `gap`, `alignItems`, `justifyContent`, `shrink`                          |
| **Bleed**                | The one place a negative margin is written: pulling a child out to the edge of its parent's padding, by the padding's token.             | `all`, `inline`, `block` (`space.025` to `space.400`)                                                                        |
| **Text**                 | Interface text on the body ramp.                                                                                                         | `size` (large, medium, small, xsmall), `weight`, `color` (a text token), `align`, `maxLines`, `numeric`, `as`                |
| **Heading**              | A title: the size from the design, the level from the page.                                                                              | `size` (large, medium, small, xsmall), `as`, `color` (text, inverse, warning inverse)                                        |
| **HeadingLevelProvider** | The level a heading inside takes, for Heading and every kit part that renders a title. Without `level`, one below the surrounding level. | `level` (1 to 6); `useHeadingLevel()` reads it                                                                               |

## Rules of thumb

- A component decides its inside; its parent decides the space around it. That is why Box has no margin props and Stack and Inline own the gaps.
- Reach for Stack and Inline first. Flex and Grid are for the layouts those cannot express.
- In a row, the part that takes the free space is `grow="fill"`, which lets it shrink below its content so a one-line Text inside cuts with an ellipsis; the fixed part beside it (an id, a count) is `shrink="none"`. No `min-w-0` in a class.
- Visual order is DOM order. No primitive reverses, reorders or floats its children.
- Text and Heading take colour tokens, not classes. `color="color.text.subtle"` is checked by the compiler.
- The outline comes from the context. A titled Section, a panel's body and a HeadingLevelProvider set the level; a Heading without `as` and the kit's titles follow it, so a level is written only where an outline starts.
- When a Box paints a surface it records that surface, so a child that needs "the surface I am on" can read `bg-surface-current`. When it paints a bold fill, the text inside is inverse.
- A link is a TextLink and a button is a Button. `as` on a primitive will not render either: the layout primitives take a `LayoutElement`, Text a `TextElement`, Heading a `HeadingElement`.
- `style` is for runtime values, on Box and Grid only. A Stack, an Inline or a Text of a fixed width sits in a Box with the width.

<!-- page: Primitives/Stack (src/stories/primitives/Stack.mdx) -->

# Stack

**Status: Stable.**

A column with one gap. Children sit top to bottom with one space token between them, and the children carry no margin of their own: the parent owns the distance, so the rhythm of a form, a rail or a page body changes in one place. `space`, `alignBlock`, `alignInline`, `spread`, `grow` and `shrink`, on a `div`, a `span` or a list element. The child has no margin; the container has the distance. Here the orientation is the primitive's name; a row is an Inline.

_Example: story `Stories.StackMatrix`._

## Anatomy

| Part      | What it is                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| --------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Container | A flex column: a `div`, or the container, landmark or list element `as` names.                                                                                                                              |
| Space     | `space`, one token between every pair of children. No first or last exception: a Stack has no outer space.                                                                                                  |
| Alignment | `alignInline`, where the children sit across the column; `alignBlock`, where they sit along it when it is taller than they are.                                                                             |
| Spread    | `spread="space-between"`, the free block space divided between the children: a footer pinned to a panel's bottom.                                                                                           |
| Grow      | `grow="fill"`, the Stack takes the free space along its parent's main axis (the height in a column, the width in a row) and may shrink below its content; `hug`, the default, it is as big as its children. |
| Shrink    | `shrink="none"`, the Stack keeps its size when its row runs out of room.                                                                                                                                    |

## Variants

| Stack         | Use                                                                                                       |
| ------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Column        | Rows of a form, sections of a rail, paragraphs of a body: one token between each.                         |
| Spread column | A panel's content over its footer: `spread` with the Stack filling the panel's height.                    |
| List          | `as="ul"` or `"ol"` with `li` children, when the rows are a list: steps, linked records, a menu of links. |

Not built, and why: a horizontal orientation (a row is an Inline, which has what a row needs: wrapping, a separator, baseline alignment); dividers between children (a Separator is a child, and rows that want hairlines are an Item.Group); a responsive space (one token at every width; the layout that changes at a breakpoint is a Grid); a `space` per child (a different distance is a different Stack, or a Section).

## Sizes

One space token between every child:

| Token       | px  | Where                                             |
| ----------- | --- | ------------------------------------------------- |
| `space.025` | 2   | A label over its control's helper line.           |
| `space.050` | 4   | A title over its description, lines of one thing. |
| `space.075` | 6   | Rows of facts in a rail.                          |
| `space.100` | 8   | Rows of a compact list, chips' rows.              |
| `space.150` | 12  | Fields of a dense form, cards in a rail.          |
| `space.200` | 16  | Fields of a form, cards in a body.                |
| `space.300` | 24  | Sections of a rail, a header over its body.       |
| `space.400` | 32  | Sections of a page body.                          |
| `space.600` | 48  | Page sections with their own headings.            |

## Modifiers

- **`space`**: the one token. Leave it off for children that touch: rows with their own hairlines.
- **`alignInline`**: `start`, `center`, `end`, `stretch`. `stretch` is the browser's default for a flex column, so a Button in a Stack is as wide as the Stack unless the Stack says `start`.
- **`alignBlock`**: `start`, `center`, `end`, when the Stack is taller than its children.
- **`spread`**: `space-between`, the free block space between the children.
- **`grow`**: `fill` to take the free space along the parent's main axis: the parent's height in a column, the case for `spread` and `alignBlock` to have any effect, or the width left in a row. A filled Stack drops its automatic minimum size on both axes, so a truncating child inside it cuts rather than pushing its parent wider or taller.
- **`shrink`**: `none` for a Stack that must keep its size beside a filling sibling: a fixed column of labels, a date.
- **`as`**: `ul` or `ol` for rows that are a list; `section` or `aside` for a region; the layout elements. A group of fields is a [FieldSet](?path=/docs/components-field--docs), which takes `disabled` and a legend and passes them to its controls; `as="fieldset"` only groups, and it drops a fieldset's content-wide minimum so the column stays in its frame.
- **No `style`.** A Stack of a fixed width sits in a Box with the width; the Stack has no computed dimension of its own.

## Content

- **Reading order is the order.** A Stack renders its children as written; there is no reverse. What is first is first to the eye and to a screen reader.
- **Two things, two Stacks.** A card's title over its description is one Stack at `space.050`; the cards themselves are another at `space.200`. Nesting is the way to two distances.
- **One child needs no Stack.** The primitive is for the distance between children; a Stack around one child spaces nothing.
- **Steps are a list.** `as="ol"` with `li` children, so a screen reader says how many and where it is.

## Style

| Element   | Token                                                                  |
| --------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Space     | `space.*`, as `gap-*`                                                  |
| Alignment | `items-*` for `alignInline`, `justify-*` for `alignBlock` and `spread` |
| Grow      | `flex-1 min-w-0 min-h-0` for `fill`                                    |
| Shrink    | `shrink-0` for `none`                                                  |

## Accessibility

- **Visual order is DOM order.** No reverse, no `order`: the tab order and the reading order are the order the children are written in.
- **A list is `as="ul"` or `"ol"`** with `li` children, so the count and the position are announced. Rows that are not a list stay a `div`.
- **A region is `as="section"`** with a name, or `"aside"` for a rail. The Stack's element is the semantics; the space is not.
- **`stretch` is not a size.** A full-width Button from `alignInline="stretch"` is still one target; its label sits at its start.

## Props

_Props of `Stack`, generated from its types:_

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `as` | `LayoutElement` | `div` | The element: a container, a landmark or a list (`ul`, `ol` for rows that are a list). Never a link or a button. |
| `ref` | `Ref<HTMLElement>` |  |  |
| `space` | `"space.0" \| "space.025" \| "space.050" \| "space.075" \| "space.100" \| "space.150" \| "space.200" \| "space.250" \| "space.300" \| "space.400" \| "space.500" \| "space.600" \| "space.800" \| "space.1000"` |  | Space between children. |
| `alignBlock` | `"center" \| "end" \| "start"` |  | Position along the block (vertical) axis. |
| `alignInline` | `"center" \| "end" \| "start" \| "stretch"` |  | Position along the inline (horizontal) axis. |
| `spread` | `"space-between"` |  | Distribute children with the free block space between them, when the Stack is taller than its children. |
| `grow` | `"fill" \| "hug"` |  | As a flex item: `fill` takes the free space along its parent's main axis (the height in a column, the width in a row) and may shrink below its content, so a truncating child inside it cuts instead of overflowing; `hug`, the default, is as big as its children. |
| `shrink` | `"none"` |  | As a flex item: `none` keeps its size when the row runs out of room, for a fixed label such as an id; the default lets it shrink. |
| `className` | `string` |  |  |

- [Inline](?path=/docs/primitives-inline--docs): the row.
- [Box](?path=/docs/primitives-box--docs): the inset around a Stack, which the Stack never sets.
- [Flex](?path=/docs/primitives-flex--docs): the column a Stack cannot say.

## Don't

The Stack's `space` sets the distance between its children, never a margin under each. Steps are `as="ol"` with `li` children, and one child needs no Stack.

<!-- page: Primitives/Text (src/stories/primitives/Text.mdx) -->

# Text

**Status: Stable.**

Body text on the body ramp. The size is a composite type token, so the family, the size, the leading and the tracking always agree; the weight is one of three; the colour is a text token, or inherited, so a Text inside a bold Box is inverse without being told. `as`, `size`, `weight`, `color`, `align`, `maxLines` (which shows the whole text while it is cut), `preserveLineBreaks`, `numeric`, and a colour that inverts inside a bold fill. `font.body` at 13px is the UI size; `small` at 12px is a label's and a hint's. The rules on colour and weight: running text is neutral, colour is functional, semibold is for a heading and not a paragraph.

_Example: story `Stories.TextMatrix`._

_Example: story `Stories.MaxLinesReveal`._

_Example: story `Stories.PreserveLineBreaks`._

_Example: story `Stories.OneLineOnASpan`._

_Example: story `Stories.UnbrokenWord`._

## Anatomy

| Part     | What it is                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Element  | A `span` by default, or the `TextElement` `as` names: `p`, `div`, `strong`, `em`, `small`, `label`, `legend`, `figcaption`, `dt`, `dd`, `li`. Never a heading, a link or a button.                                                                                        |
| Size     | `large`, `medium`, `small`, `xsmall`: the four `font.body` tokens.                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| Weight   | `regular`, `medium`, `semibold`. Over the token's own weight.                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| Colour   | A `color.text` token, or inherited: `color.text` from the page, `color.text.inverse` from a bold Box.                                                                                                                                                                     |
| Clamp    | `maxLines` 1, 2 or 3, with an ellipsis, and the whole text in a tooltip while it is cut (through [Truncate](?path=/docs/components-truncate--docs)). A one-line clamp makes an inline element (`span`, `strong`, `em`, `small`, `label`) a block, so it has a box to cut. |
| Breaks   | `preserveLineBreaks` keeps the line breaks and spaces of authored text (`white-space: pre-wrap`).                                                                                                                                                                         |
| Numerals | `numeric` sets tabular numerals, every digit one width, for a count or a date that lines up with the one above it.                                                                                                                                                        |

## Variants

| Text      | Use                                                                                                    |
| --------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Paragraph | `as="p"`: a statement, a description, a note, at `medium` or `large`, at the reading measure.          |
| Run       | The default `span`: a value in a cell, a word in a row, a count beside a label.                        |
| Label     | `as="label"` with `htmlFor`, or `as="dt"` in a pair: `small` medium, subtle.                           |
| Meta      | `small` or `xsmall`, `subtle` or `subtlest`: a date, an id, a count.                                   |
| Emphasis  | `weight="medium"` on a word in a sentence; `as="strong"` when the emphasis is for a screen reader too. |

Not built, and why: a `bold` weight (the ramp's top is `semibold`, the page title's weight, and a paragraph above it shouts); italic (for the titles of works and technical terms, and the product has neither in running text); an underline (a link is a TextLink; an underline that is not a link reads as one); a separate truncate prop (`maxLines` clamps and reveals; a [Truncate](?path=/docs/components-truncate--docs) cuts a composed value); an escape below the ramp (`xsmall` is the floor, and nothing is set below 11px); a text transform (an Eyebrow sets its own uppercase; nothing else is transformed).

## Sizes

| Size     | Token              | Size / leading | Where                                                                                               |
| -------- | ------------------ | -------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `large`  | `font.body.large`  | 15 / 22        | Reading text: a statement, a dialog's body, a note at the measure.                                  |
| `medium` | `font.body`        | 13 / 18        | The UI size: controls, cells, tabs, menu items, descriptions. The default, inherited from the page. |
| `small`  | `font.body.small`  | 12 / 16        | Table headers, field labels, badges, KeyValue, meta lines.                                          |
| `xsmall` | `font.body.xsmall` | 11 / 14        | Counts, dates, ids beside something. Never a sentence.                                              |

The UI size is 13, a point under the usual 14, because a register's rows are the page.

## Modifiers

- **`size`**, **`weight`**, **`color`**, **`align`**, **`maxLines`**, **`as`** as in Anatomy.
- **`color`** is left off where the text should follow its surface: inside a bold Box, inside a Button.
- **`maxLines`** is 1, 2 or 3. A longer clamp is a Section with a "Show more". While the text is cut, hovering it, or focusing the link or button it sits in with the keyboard, shows the whole in a tooltip; nothing opens while it fits. A `title` of your own replaces the tooltip.
- **`numeric`** for numbers that are compared down a column or change in place: a count, a percentage, a date in a list. A table's cells have tabular numerals already.
- **`preserveLineBreaks`** for authored text read as written: a comment, a note, a statement with its line breaks. A one-line clamp keeps none. Several paragraphs, or Markdown, are a [Prose](?path=/docs/components-typography--docs).
- **No `style`.** A width for a label column is a Box's, or a Grid's template.

## Content

- **Running text is neutral.** `color.text` for a paragraph, `subtle` for a description, `subtlest` for meta.
- **Colour says something.** `danger` on an overdue count, `success` on a passed check, `brand` on nothing that is not a link.
- **Sentence case, one idea per sentence.** A description ends with a full stop; a label and a meta line do not.
- **Emphasis is a weight, and rare.** One word in `medium`; never a sentence in `semibold`.
- **A title is a Heading.** A Text in `large` `semibold` is not in the outline and is not on the heading ramp.
- **A long word breaks.** An id, a hash, a URL or a file name longer than its line breaks where it would overflow (`base.css` sets `overflow-wrap: break-word` on the body), so it never widens its block or the page; a row field that should stay on one line takes `maxLines={1}` instead, with its reveal.
- **The reading measure.** A paragraph at `large` or `medium` is capped at `dimension.layout.measure`, 720px, by its parent.

## Style

| Element  | Token                                                                                                                                                                  |
| -------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Size     | `font.body.large` · `font.body` · `font.body.small` · `font.body.xsmall`, the family, size, leading and tracking in one                                                |
| Weight   | `font.weight.regular` · `.medium` · `.semibold`                                                                                                                        |
| Colour   | `color.text` · `.subtle` · `.subtlest` · `.disabled` · `.brand` · `.selected` · `.danger` · `.warning` · `.success` · `.information` · `.inverse` · `.warning.inverse` |
| Clamp    | one line clipped across (`overflow-x: clip`, ellipsis); `line-clamp-2`, `line-clamp-3`                                                                                 |
| Numerals | `tabular-nums` for `numeric`                                                                                                                                           |
| Measure  | `dimension.layout.measure`, set by the parent                                                                                                                          |

## Accessibility

- **A clamped text is still all there.** `maxLines` hides with CSS; a screen reader reads the whole. The eye gets the rest from the tooltip, on hover and on keyboard focus of the link or button the text sits in; the tooltip is hidden from assistive technology, so the text is not read twice. A touch screen has no hover: where a phone reader needs the whole, let it wrap or let the row open the record.
- **`as="strong"` for emphasis that must be heard**; `weight="medium"` for emphasis that is only seen.
- **A label is a `label`** with `htmlFor`, so the control is named. Text as a label without the element names nothing.
- **Colour is never the only signal.** A red count has the word beside it: "2 past due", not "2".
- **Contrast is the token's.** Every `color.text.*` on every `color.background.*` it is paired with is measured on the Color sheet; a Text inherits the pair its Box chose.

## Props

_Props of `Text`, generated from its types:_

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `as` | `TextElement` | `span` | The element: a `span` by default; `p` for a paragraph; `label`, `dt`, `dd`, `li`, `legend`, `figcaption`, `strong`, `em`, `small`, `div`. Never a heading, a link or a button. |
| `htmlFor` | `string` |  | The associated control's DOM id when `as="label"`. |
| `ref` | `Ref<HTMLElement>` |  |  |
| `size` | `"large" \| "medium" \| "small" \| "xsmall"` |  | font.body.large · font.body · font.body.small · font.body.xsmall |
| `weight` | `"medium" \| "regular" \| "semibold"` |  |  |
| `color` | `TextColorToken` |  | A color.text token. Defaults to inheriting: the page's text colour, or the inverse a bold Box sets. |
| `align` | `"center" \| "end" \| "start"` |  |  |
| `maxLines` | `1 \| 2 \| 3` |  | Clamp to this many lines with an ellipsis. While the text is cut, hovering it, or focusing the link or button it sits in with the keyboard, shows the whole in a tooltip; a `title` of your own replaces the tooltip. |
| `preserveLineBreaks` | `boolean` |  | Keeps the line breaks and spaces typed into authored text (a comment, a statement, a note) instead of running it into one line: `white-space: pre-wrap`. A one-line clamp keeps none. |
| `numeric` | `boolean` |  | Tabular numerals: every digit the same width, so a count, a percentage or a date lines up with the one above it and does not jitter as it changes. A table's cells have them already. |
| `className` | `string` |  |  |

- [TextLink](?path=/docs/components-textlink--docs): a link in text.
- [Box](?path=/docs/primitives-box--docs): the fill that sets a Text's colour.
- [Typography tokens](?path=/docs/tokens-typography--docs): the ramp, with every token's value.

## Don't

Running text is neutral, and a colour says something, never decoration. Body copy is `medium`, or `large` for a statement read at length, never `xsmall`, and a title is a Heading, never a Text made to look like one.

_Example: story `Stories.Dont`._

<!-- page: Primitives/VisuallyHidden (src/stories/primitives/VisuallyHidden.mdx) -->

# VisuallyHidden

**Status: Stable.**

Words for assistive technology alone. They stay in the accessibility tree and in reading order, and take no space on screen. Use them where the eye has what it needs from the layout and a screen reader does not: the meaning of a mark beside a name, a heading for a region whose content is its own heading, the word an empty value stands for.

```tsx
<Icon color="color.icon.subtle">
  <Shield />
</Icon>
<VisuallyHidden>Authorization boundary:</VisuallyHidden>
<Text>Tactical edge segment</Text>
```

_Example: story `Stories.Uses`._

## When to use it

- **Beside a mark, read inline with the text:** "Authorization boundary: Tactical edge segment". For a mark that stands alone, an [Icon](?path=/docs/components-icon--docs) with a `label` names it as an image.
- **A heading the outline needs** and the screen does not show: `as="h2"` inside a region that is otherwise clear to the eye.
- **An empty value:** [Absent](?path=/docs/components-typography--docs) with a `label` uses it for "Not recorded".
- **Not for a control's name.** A button or a field is named by its `label`, `aria-label` or a FieldLabel; hidden text inside a button works but is harder to keep right.
- **Not to hide content from everyone.** Content no one should see is not rendered.

## Accessibility

- **It is read, not skipped.** `sr-only` clips the text to a 1px box; `display: none` or `visibility: hidden` would remove it from the accessibility tree.
- **It is read where it sits**, so put it in the order the sentence needs; punctuation ("Authorization boundary:") keeps a screen reader from running it into the next words.
- **It is never a substitute for visible text** a sighted reader needs.

## Props

_Props of `VisuallyHidden`, generated from its types:_

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `as` | `VisuallyHiddenElement` | `span` | The element: a `span` by default; `div` or `p` for a block, `h1` to `h6` for a heading only the outline needs, `label` or `legend` to name a control or a group. |
| `children` | `ReactNode` |  | What a screen reader hears: the meaning of a mark beside it ("Authorization boundary"), a heading for a region that shows none. |
| `ref` | `Ref<HTMLElement>` |  |  |
| `className` | `string` |  |  |

### Playground

_Example: story `Stories.Playground`._

_Rendered in the Storybook: Controls._

## Don't

What a mark means is VisuallyHidden text read in its place, never a `title` on a span, which reaches a mouse after a wait and no one else.

_Example: story `Stories.Dont`._

<!-- page: Components/Accordion (src/stories/components/Accordion.mdx) -->

# Accordion

**Status: Stable.**

A coordinated set of expandable sections, implemented with the shadcn Base UI composition. Use Collapsible for one independent disclosure.

## Anatomy

Compose the flat `Accordion`, `AccordionItem`, `AccordionTrigger`, and `AccordionContent` exports. Each item needs a stable value; values are always arrays, and `multiple` allows more than one open item.

```tsx
<Accordion defaultValue={["delivery"]}>
  <AccordionItem value="delivery">
    <AccordionTrigger>What delivery options are available?</AccordionTrigger>
    <AccordionContent>Delivery information.</AccordionContent>
  </AccordionItem>
</Accordion>
```

| Part             | What it is                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| ---------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Accordion        | The set: a column of items, `flex` and full width.                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| AccordionItem    | One section, with a hairline between items.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| AccordionTrigger | The heading and, inside it, the button: the title at the start and a chevron at the end that turns with `aria-expanded`. The row tint under the pointer reaches `space.100` before a title that sits flush with the content, and the chevron sits `space.100` inside the end. |
| AccordionContent | The panel that folds, with `data-open` and the measured `--accordion-panel-height`, and a `space.200` box under the content inside it.                                                                                                                                        |

`AccordionTrigger` renders the item's heading itself. `headerProps` reach that heading (a `className`, native attributes, a ref, or `render` for another element), and `icon` replaces the chevron with another mark, or `null` for none; a custom mark shows the state itself, from the trigger's `aria-expanded`. Every part's `className` is a string or Base UI's state function, and `AccordionContent`'s reaches the panel, not the box inside it.

_Example: story `Stories.Parts`._

## Variants and states

_Example: story `Stories.Examples`._

Use `value` with `onValueChange` for controlled state and `defaultValue` otherwise. Use `disabled` on the root or an item. `keepMounted` preserves panel state while closed; `hiddenUntilFound` additionally lets browser find-in-page reveal closed content.

_Example: story `Stories.ControlledAndRetained`._

## When to use it

- **A set that belongs together**, where the reader opens one section or several: the parts of a long form's help, the groups of a settings page.
- **Not** for one titled block that folds: that is a [CollapsibleHeader](?path=/docs/components-collapsible--docs), a collapsible [Section](?path=/docs/layout-section--docs) on a page, or an [Inspector.Group](?path=/docs/patterns-inspector--docs) in a rail of facts.
- **Not** for switching between views of one record: those are [Tabs](?path=/docs/components-tabs--docs).
- **Not** for a row that discloses more of itself: Item's `isCollapsible` and Table's disclosure column own their chevrons.

## Content

- Each trigger names its section as a noun or as the question the section answers ("Delivery options", "What delivery options are available?"), the same open and closed; the chevron shows the state.
- Sections are parallel: the same kind of content under each, in an order the reader expects (the form's order, then the rest).
- Open the section the reader most needs with `defaultValue`; never hide the only content on a page in a closed item.
- Keep a section's content short. A section that holds a page of its own belongs on that page, linked from here.

A trigger named "Show more" says nothing about its section; two of them read as one heading twice.

_Example: story `Stories.DoDont`._

## Accessibility

Triggers are native buttons with Enter, Space, and normal Tab behavior. Base UI follows current APG guidance and does not add arrow-key roving focus. The trigger wrapper supplies the heading and associates every panel with its trigger. The chevron is decoration, turned by the expanded state rather than by colour; under reduced motion it turns without moving and the panel opens without the fold.

Each heading takes the contextual level from the nearest [HeadingLevelProvider](?path=/docs/primitives-heading--docs), titled Section or panel body, and is an h3 when nothing sets one. Wrap the Accordion in a HeadingLevelProvider for another level: `level={2}` where it is a page rail's first heading under the h1. `headerProps.render` sets one item's element.

_Example: story `Stories.HeadingLevel`._

A panel clips only while it folds: settled open, its overflow is visible, so the focus ring of a link or a button at its edge shows whole. Each panel folds on its own measured height, so a Collapsible inside an open item eases rather than snapping (Components/Collapsible, Nested motion).

## Props

_Props of `Accordion`, generated from its types:_

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `value` | `AccordionValue<any>` |  | The controlled value of the item(s) that should be expanded. To render an uncontrolled accordion, use the `defaultValue` prop instead. |
| `defaultValue` | `AccordionValue<any>` |  | The uncontrolled value of the item(s) that should be initially expanded. To render a controlled accordion, use the `value` prop instead. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | Whether the component should ignore user interaction. |
| `hiddenUntilFound` | `boolean` | `false` | Allows the browser's built-in page search to find and expand the panel contents. Overrides the `keepMounted` prop and uses `hidden="until-found"` to hide the element without removing it from the DOM. |
| `keepMounted` | `boolean` | `false` | Whether to keep the element in the DOM while the panel is closed. This prop is ignored when `hiddenUntilFound` is used. |
| `loopFocus` | `boolean` |  | Deprecated following the [APG guidance update](https://github.com/w3c/aria-practices/pull/3434) to remove roving focus. This prop no longer affects keyboard focus behavior. @deprecated |
| `onValueChange` | `((value: AccordionValue<any>, eventDetails: AccordionRootChangeEventDetails) => void)` |  | Event handler called when an accordion item is expanded or collapsed. Provides the new value as an argument. |
| `multiple` | `boolean` | `false` | Whether multiple items can be open at the same time. |
| `orientation` | `"horizontal" \| "vertical"` | `'vertical'` | Deprecated following the [APG guidance update](https://github.com/w3c/aria-practices/pull/3434) to remove roving focus. This prop no longer affects keyboard focus behavior. @deprecated |
| `className` | `string \| ((state: State<any>) => string)` |  | CSS class applied to the element, or a function that returns a class based on the component's state. |
| `render` | `ReactElement<unknown, string \| JSXElementConstructor<any>> \| ComponentRenderFn<HTMLProps, State<any>>` |  | Allows you to replace the component's HTML element with a different tag, or compose it with another component. Accepts a `ReactElement` or a function that returns the element to render. |
| `style` | `CSSProperties \| ((state: State<any>) => CSSProperties)` |  | Style applied to the element, or a function that returns a style object based on the component's state. |
