<!-- page: Components/Alert (src/stories/components/Alert.mdx) -->

# Alert

**Status: Stable.**

An inline message about a record or a region: what happened, what it means, and the way out. It stays where it is while it is true, beside the content it is about.

_Example: story `Stories.Playground`._

## Choosing between them

| The message                                     | Part                                                      |
| ----------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------- |
| About this record or region, while it holds     | Alert                                                     |
| About one field of a form                       | [FieldError](?path=/docs/components-field--docs) under it |
| Several problems with a submitted form          | [ErrorSummary](?path=/docs/components-errorsummary--docs) |
| About the whole site, for every reader          | [Banner](?path=/docs/components-banner--docs)             |
| Feedback after an act that needs nothing more   | A [toast](?path=/docs/components-toaster--docs)           |
| A decision the reader must take before going on | [AlertDialog](?path=/docs/components-alertdialog--docs)   |

## Anatomy

```tsx
<Alert variant="danger">
  <AlertIcon />
  <AlertTitle>Import failed</AlertTitle>
  <AlertDescription>The file is missing record identifiers.</AlertDescription>
  <AlertAction>
    <TextLink href="#format">Read the required format</TextLink>
    <Button size="small">Try the import again</Button>
  </AlertAction>
</Alert>
```

| Part               | What it is                                                                                                                                      |
| ------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Alert`            | The region, in the tone's subtle fill. An svg as its first child (AlertIcon) takes a column of its own.                                         |
| `AlertIcon`        | The tone's icon: Info, CircleCheck, TriangleAlert or CircleAlert, the same glyphs as Banner and the toast list. `icon` replaces it. Decorative. |
| `AlertTitle`       | What happened, in medium weight. An unbroken code or hash wraps inside it.                                                                      |
| `AlertDescription` | What it means or what to do, one or two lines.                                                                                                  |
| `AlertAction`      | The way out: a TextLink to where it is fixed, or a small Button that fixes it. Links are underlined here as in the title and the description.   |

Content and icons are the caller's. Actions stay in normal flow under the message, so a long recovery link fits a narrow panel.

## Variants and states

`tone` is the Ledger meaning and picks the fill, the icon and the default role. `variant` is shadcn's treatment: `default` is the neutral tone and `destructive`, or its Ledger spelling `danger`, the danger tone; a `tone` overrides either.

_Example: story `Stories.Variants`._

_Example: story `Stories.Tones`._

_Example: story `Stories.LongContent`._

The application owns action handlers and feedback.

_Example: story `Stories.WithAction`._

## Content

- **The title says what happened** in the reader's words: "Import failed", "Records could not be refreshed". Not "Error", not the server's message.
- **The description says what it means or what to do**, in one or two lines. A server message is detail: put it after the plain sentence, or leave it out.
- **One way out**, named for where it goes or what it does. A link navigates; a small Button acts.
- **No Alert for a result the reader did not ask about.** Feedback after an act is a toast.

## Accessibility

The role follows the tone, and `role` overrides it:

| The message                                                     | Role                                 |
| --------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------ |
| A failure after the reader's act, which stops the task          | `alert`, the danger tone's default   |
| A result or an update the reader should hear when idle          | `status`, every other tone's default |
| Standing guidance that is read in place (a permission, a draft) | `note`                               |
| Said already by the page's own live region                      | `role={undefined}`, none             |

An Alert rendered with the page is not a change, so it is not announced whatever its role; the role matters when it appears after an act. Name it with `aria-labelledby` on its title when a screen reader should meet it as a landmark-like region. AlertIcon is hidden from assistive technology. On every tone's fill the icon and the focus ring hold 3:1, and a TextLink 4.5:1 in the standard modes; under increased contrast the neutral fill darkens, and the link holds 4.5:1 on the status tones only. The contrast test checks each pair. In forced colours the fill is replaced, so the Alert keeps a CanvasText edge and its icon.

## Props

_Props of `Alert`, generated from its types:_

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `variant` | `"danger" \| "default" \| "destructive"` | `default` | shadcn's treatment: `default` is the neutral tone, `destructive` (or its Ledger spelling `danger`) the danger tone. |
| `tone` | `"danger" \| "information" \| "neutral" \| "success" \| "warning"` |  | Ledger visual meaning; overrides the variant's neutral/danger tone. It also picks the default role and AlertIcon's glyph. |

_Props of `AlertIcon`, generated from its types:_

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `icon` | `AlertGlyph` |  | The glyph, a Lucide icon or any svg component. Unset, the Alert's tone picks it: Info, CircleCheck, TriangleAlert or CircleAlert, the same as Banner's and the toast list's. |

All parts accept native div attributes and refs (AlertIcon's are the svg's). `title` is the native tooltip attribute.

## Related

[Banner](?path=/docs/components-banner--docs), [Toaster](?path=/docs/components-toaster--docs), [AlertDialog](?path=/docs/components-alertdialog--docs), [ErrorSummary](?path=/docs/components-errorsummary--docs), [Field](?path=/docs/components-field--docs), [Upgrading](?path=/docs/guidance-upgrading--docs#alert).

Sources: [shadcn Alert](https://ui.shadcn.com/docs/components/base/alert), [implementation](https://github.com/shadcn-ui/ui/blob/main/apps/v4/registry/bases/base/ui/alert.tsx), [WAI-ARIA alert role](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/alert/).

## Don't

An Alert says what happened in its title and offers the way out as one small action beside it, never a red bar with the server's words and a page-wide button under it. A standing note is `role="note"`, read in place, never a danger Alert that interrupts the page when nothing failed.

_Example: story `Stories.Dont`._

<!-- page: Components/AlertDialog (src/stories/components/AlertDialog.mdx) -->

# AlertDialog

**Status: Stable.**

A decision that needs a word before it happens: delete, archive, discard a draft. Built on [Base UI Alert Dialog](https://base-ui.com/react/components/alert-dialog) with [shadcn’s composition](https://ui.shadcn.com/docs/components/base/alert-dialog) and Ledger's tokens.

_Example: story `Stories.ConfirmationAndPending`._

## When to use it

- **Before a destructive or irreversible command**, or before throwing away a draft.
- **Over the Dialog or Sheet that owns the decision**, the one stack overlays allow.

Not for a form: that is a [Dialog](?path=/docs/components-dialog--docs). Not for a result the reader only needs to know about: that is a toast or an [Alert](?path=/docs/components-alert--docs). Not for a question the reader can undo in one step: do it, then offer Undo.

## Anatomy

- **AlertDialogHeader** holds an optional AlertDialogMedia, the title (the question, an h2, a [Heading](?path=/docs/primitives-heading--docs) at `overlay`, 15/22 medium) and the description (the consequence).
- **AlertDialogBody** holds what the decision affects when one line is not enough: the records a delete removes, a field for a reason. It follows the header with its inset and no divider, and scrolls between the header and the footer so the answers stay in view.
- **AlertDialogFooter** holds AlertDialogCancel, the safe answer, before AlertDialogAction, the verb, on the dialog's own surface below a hairline.
- AlertDialogContent records the overlay surface as the current one; AlertDialogPortal and AlertDialogOverlay are exported for a custom popup.

_Example: story `Stories.WithBody`._

## Widths

`width` on AlertDialogContent picks a step, in [Dialog](?path=/docs/components-dialog--docs)'s words for Dialog's widths, so a `small` alert dialog is as wide as a `small` dialog. Do not set pixels in `style`.

| `width`  | Size               | For                                                    |
| -------- | ------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------ |
| `xsmall` | 320px              | A one-line question                                    |
| `small`  | 400px, the default | A question and its consequence                         |
| `medium` | 520px              | A decision whose AlertDialogBody lists what it affects |

Every step keeps a `space.200` gutter on each side of the window, so on a phone the popup is the phone's width less the gutter. `size` is the deprecated spelling: `size="sm"` is `width="xsmall"` and `size="default"` is `width="small"`; `ledger/no-deprecated-name` rewrites the prop and its value in one fix.

_Example: story `Stories.SmallConfirmation`._

_Example: story `Stories.Widths`._

## Pending

`pending` on the AlertDialog holds it while the command runs: Escape and AlertDialogCancel are cancelled, Cancel is disabled but stays focusable (`aria-disabled`), since focus starts there, and the popup is `aria-busy`. Give the Action `isLoading`, which keeps its focus, and close with `open={false}` when the command succeeds. On a failure, end the pending state and say inside the dialog what went wrong, with the Action as the retry. The Action never closes the dialog by itself; render it as an AlertDialogCancel (`render={<AlertDialogCancel />}`) only when the verb needs no command to finish first.

## Accessibility

- **The role is `alertdialog`**, named by the title and described by the description.
- **The blanket never dismisses it**; Escape and Cancel do, unless it is pending. A press on the blanket leaves focus where it was.
- **Focus goes to Cancel** when the decision is destructive: pass it as `initialFocus`. Focus returns to what opened the dialog, recorded as it opens, or to `finalFocus` when that went away.
- **Over a Dialog or Sheet**, render it inside the parent's content: Base UI draws no second blanket for it, and the parent dims under it instead, so the prompt stands apart in both modes.
- **Forced colours keep the edge**: the popup draws a CanvasText outline.

## Content

- The title is the question: "Delete 24 drafts?". The description is the consequence, not the question again: "These drafts are removed for everyone." A record's name or code in the title wraps rather than running past the edge; a failure's cause goes in the body, through an Alert.
- The Action says the verb ("Delete drafts"); Cancel says the safe way out ("Keep drafts", "Keep editing").

_Example: story `Stories.LongValues`._

"Are you sure?" with OK repeats the question, says no consequence and hides the verb.

_Example: story `Stories.DoDont`._

## Props

AlertDialog takes Base UI AlertDialog's root props, `open`, `defaultOpen`, `onOpenChange` (with the change's `reason` and `cancel()` in its details), `onOpenChangeComplete`, `actionsRef` and `handle`, and Ledger's `pending`; it has no `modal` or `disablePointerDismissal`, since an alert dialog is always modal and ignores the blanket. AlertDialogContent takes the popup's `initialFocus`, `finalFocus`, `render`, `className` and `style`, and Ledger's `width`. Every part takes its element's native attributes, and its `data-slot` comes after them, so a caller's attribute never renames the part (Native attributes, below). The title, the description and AlertDialogCancel are the exception: another part renders as them through `render` (a PageHeader.Title as the title, an AlertDialogAction as Cancel) and its `data-slot` names the element, as it does on a Button. The types are in [Base UI's API reference](https://base-ui.com/react/components/alert-dialog#api-reference).

_Props of `AlertDialog`, generated from its types:_

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `onOpenChange` | `((open: boolean, eventDetails: AlertDialogRootChangeEventDetails) => void)` |  | Event handler called when the alert dialog is opened or closed. |
| `actionsRef` | `RefObject<DialogRootActions \| null>` |  | A ref to imperative actions. - `unmount`: Manually unmounts the alert dialog. Call this after any externally controlled closing animation finishes. - `close`: Closes the alert dialog imperatively when called. |
| `handle` | `AlertDialogHandle<Payload>` |  | A handle to associate the alert dialog with a trigger. If specified, allows external triggers to control the alert dialog's open state. Can be created with the AlertDialog.createHandle() method. |
| `children` | `ReactNode \| PayloadChildRenderFunction<Payload>` |  | The content of the dialog. This can be a regular React node or a render function that receives the `payload` of the active trigger. |
| `open` | `boolean` |  | Whether the dialog is currently open. |
| `defaultOpen` | `boolean` | `false` | Whether the dialog is initially open. To render a controlled dialog, use the `open` prop instead. |
| `onOpenChangeComplete` | `((open: boolean) => void)` |  | Event handler called after any animations complete when the dialog is opened or closed. |
| `triggerId` | `string \| null` |  | ID of the trigger that the dialog is associated with. This is useful in conjunction with the `open` prop to create a controlled dialog. There's no need to specify this prop when the dialog is uncontrolled (that is, when the `open` prop is not set). |
| `defaultTriggerId` | `string \| null` |  | ID of the trigger that the dialog is associated with. This is useful in conjunction with the `defaultOpen` prop to create an initially open dialog. |
| `pending` | `boolean` | `false` | The decision's command is in flight. Escape and AlertDialogCancel are cancelled before `onOpenChange` hears of them, Cancel is disabled and the popup is `aria-busy`. Give the Action `isLoading`, and close when the command succeeds (`open={false}`); on a failure, end the pending state and say what went wrong inside the dialog. |

### AlertDialogContent

_Props of `AlertDialogContent`, generated from its types:_

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `initialFocus` | `boolean \| RefObject<HTMLElement \| null> \| ((openType: InteractionType) => boolean \| void \| HTMLElement \| null)` |  | Determines the element to focus when the dialog is opened. By default, focus moves to the first tabbable element inside the popup, except when the dialog is opened by touch — then the popup itself is focused to avoid opening the virtual keyboard. - `false`: Do not move focus. - `true`: Move focus based on the default behavior (first tabbable element or popup). - `RefObject`: Move focus to the ref element. - `function`: Called with the interaction type (`mouse`, `touch`, `pen`, or `keyboard`). Return an element to focus, `true` to use the default behavior, `null` to fall back to the default behavior, or `false`/`undefined` to do nothing. |
| `finalFocus` | `boolean \| RefObject<HTMLElement \| null> \| ((closeType: InteractionType) => boolean \| void \| HTMLElement \| null)` |  | Determines the element to focus when the dialog is closed. - `false`: Do not move focus. - `true`: Move focus based on the default behavior (trigger or previously focused element). - `RefObject`: Move focus to the ref element. - `function`: Called with the interaction type (`mouse`, `touch`, `pen`, or `keyboard`). Return an element to focus, `true` to use the default behavior, `null` to fall back to the default behavior, or `false`/`undefined` to do nothing. |
| `className` | `string \| ((state: DialogPopupState) => string)` |  | CSS class applied to the element, or a function that returns a class based on the component's state. |
| `render` | `ReactElement<unknown, string \| JSXElementConstructor<any>> \| ComponentRenderFn<HTMLProps, DialogPopupState>` |  | Allows you to replace the component's HTML element with a different tag, or compose it with another component. Accepts a `ReactElement` or a function that returns the element to render. |
| `style` | `CSSProperties \| ((state: DialogPopupState) => CSSProperties)` |  | Style applied to the element, or a function that returns a style object based on the component's state. |
| `width` | `"medium" \| "small" \| "xsmall"` | `"small"` | The popup's width, on Dialog's steps: `small` 400px for a question and its consequence, `xsmall` 320px for a one-line question, `medium` 520px for a decision whose AlertDialogBody lists what it affects. Every step keeps a `space.200` gutter on each side, so it narrows to the window less the gutter. A `style.maxWidth` still wins. |
| `size` | `"default" \| "sm"` |  | @deprecated Use `width`: `size="sm"` is `width="xsmall"` and `size="default"` is `width="small"`. `width` wins when both are set. |

<!-- page: Components/Announcer (src/stories/components/Announcer.mdx) -->

# Announcer

**Status: Stable.**

One channel for status messages a screen reader should hear while focus stays where it is: a result count after a search, a save, a page change. `announce(message, { politeness })` speaks through the page's two persistent live regions, and `Announcer` renders them, visually hidden.

```tsx
import { announce } from "@ledger/design-system";

announce("3 of 24 records");
announce("The file could not be uploaded. Try again.", { politeness: "assertive" });
```

_Example: story `Stories.Playground`._

## Where the regions come from

Shell mounts one Announcer, so a product with a Shell has nothing to add. A product without one mounts `<Announcer />` once near its root. `announce` speaks through the newest Announcer mounted. With none mounted it creates the regions at the end of the body and speaks once they have settled, so a part can announce before the product mounts one. On the server `announce` does nothing, and `Announcer` renders its empty regions into the markup, so they are in the page before the first message.

_Example: story `Stories.WithoutAnAnnouncer`._

## Politeness

`polite`, the default, waits until the reader is idle: the outcome of a search, a filter, a save, a new page. `assertive` interrupts whatever is being read, so keep it for the one failure that stops the task. An error that belongs to a field stays beside the field; the form announces one summary.

_Example: story `Stories.Politeness`._

## When to use it

- A change that is visible but silent: a result count, a page range, a saved state, a new page after client-side navigation (Shell does this with `locationKey`).
- A change whose visible form is far from focus, such as a count in the toolbar after typing in the search.

Not for:

- Text the reader is already focused on, or that a focus move will read. Moving focus is the announcement.
- A toast. Toaster announces its own messages.
- A persistent status the page shows, such as a Saving indicator beside a control. Keep that as visible text in the page; announce only the change.
- A modal decision. Use AlertDialog.

A form whose check fails announces one polite summary through `announce` once the check has run ("2 fields need attention"), never a `role="alert"` on each field's error: inserted together, those interrupt one another, and a region added with its text already in it is often not heard at all.

_Example: story `Stories.Dont`._

## Accessibility

The regions are `role="log"` with `aria-live` and `aria-relevant="additions"`. Each message is a new line in its region, so the same words said twice are heard twice, and each line leaves after seven seconds, so the region never becomes a log a reader browses into. Base UI's modal dialogs keep `aria-live` regions exposed when they hide the page, so a message sent while one is open is still heard. Blank messages are dropped. Write the message as the sentence a sighted reader would take from the screen: "3 of 24 records", not "Search complete".

_Example: story `Stories.InADialog`._

## Props

_Props: generated from `Announcer`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._

`Announcer` takes a div's native props and ref; it has no children. `announce(message: string, options?: { politeness?: "polite" | "assertive" })` returns nothing.

The model is [React Aria's live announcer](https://github.com/adobe/react-spectrum/tree/main/packages/%40react-aria/live-announcer); see [WCAG 2.2 Understanding 4.1.3 Status Messages](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/status-messages.html).

<!-- page: Components/Attachment (src/stories/components/Attachment.mdx) -->

# Attachment

**Status: Stable.**

One file or image with its name, metadata and optional actions: a base component for file presentation. Choosing files is [FileTrigger](?path=/docs/components-filetrigger--docs) or [DropZone](?path=/docs/components-dropzone--docs); the application owns uploading, retries, removal and preview dialogs, and shows each file as an Attachment.

## Anatomy

Compose only the parts the file needs:

| Part                   | Responsibility                                                                                      |
| ---------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Attachment             | Surface, size, orientation and upload state.                                                        |
| Attachment.Media       | Icon or image preview.                                                                              |
| Attachment.Content     | Groups the name, metadata and optional progress.                                                    |
| Attachment.Title       | Filename, cut in the middle so its end and extension stay in view; read whole.                      |
| Attachment.Description | File type, size, status or a wrapping failure explanation.                                          |
| Attachment.Trigger     | Optional card-wide action button: preview, download a file the page builds.                         |
| Attachment.Link        | Optional card-wide link: a file the server holds (`href`, `download`), or a router link (`render`). |
| Attachment.Actions     | Independent controls above the trigger or link.                                                     |
| Attachment.Action      | IconButton with a required `label` and `icon`.                                                      |
| Attachment.Group       | Horizontally scrollable row.                                                                        |

Each part is also exported by name (`AttachmentTitle`, `AttachmentLink`, …) for its props table.

```tsx
<Attachment>
  <Attachment.Media aria-hidden="true">
    <FileText />
  </Attachment.Media>
  <Attachment.Content>
    <Attachment.Title>quarterly-report.pdf</Attachment.Title>
    <Attachment.Description>PDF · {formatFileSize(file.size)}</Attachment.Description>
  </Attachment.Content>
  <Attachment.Trigger aria-label="Preview quarterly-report.pdf" onClick={openPreview} />
  <Attachment.Actions>
    <Attachment.Action label="Remove quarterly-report.pdf" icon={<X />} onClick={removeFile} />
  </Attachment.Actions>
</Attachment>
```

## Variants

`orientation="horizontal"` places media beside metadata; `vertical` places it above. `Media variant="image"` crops a caller-rendered image into a square preview. Supply `alt=""` when it repeats the filename without adding useful information; otherwise describe the image. The caller owns unavailable-image fallbacks and object URL cleanup.

_Example: story `Stories.Images`._

## Sizes

`medium` is the default, with 12px padding and 40px media. `small` uses 8px padding and 32px media; `xsmall` uses 6px padding and 24px media. Small sizes use the small body token. Metadata remains visible at every size. Action buttons keep their minimum 28px target. Vertical media fills the card width. Override width on the root or constrain its container.

_Example: story `Stories.AttachmentMatrix`._

## States

`idle` uses a dashed border; `uploading` and `processing` set `aria-busy`; `error` changes the border and description to danger; `done` is the default resting surface. These are caller-supplied states, with no internal transitions. Write the status or error in Description so color is never its only signal. Compose Spinner or Progress when useful; filename animation is not imposed. Spinner respects reduced motion.

An upload in progress offers a Cancel named for the file ("Cancel uploading quarterly-report.pdf"); a failure offers a Retry and a Remove. When a result replaces the control that had focus (Cancel goes with the upload), move focus to the control that replaces it. `aria-busy` marks the work but announces nothing when it ends, so say each result through `announce` ("Uploaded quarterly-report.pdf.", "Cancelled the upload of quarterly-report.pdf."). [DropZone](?path=/docs/components-dropzone--docs) shows the whole flow.

_Example: story `Stories.UploadStates`._

## Long content

`Attachment.Title` cuts a plain-text name in the middle: the start ends in an ellipsis and the end, the extension and the ten characters before it, stays whole, so `acas-vulnerability-scan-ws-x90-2026-09-01.pdf` and `…-09-15.pdf` stay apart. Assistive technology reads the whole name once, and copying a selection inside the title gives the name as it is written. The kept end follows the name's own direction, so an English name on a right-to-left page still ends with its extension. `truncate="end"` cuts at the end instead; a Title whose children are elements always does. With a card-wide Trigger or Link over the card, a `title` on the Title is covered: put the full name in the Trigger's or Link's `title` for a pointer, as well as in its `aria-label`.

_Example: story `Stories.LongNames`._

## Links and downloads

Trigger is an action button with `type="button"` by default; use `render` to compose a custom button that forwards its props and ref. For navigation or a file the server holds, use `Attachment.Link`: an anchor with the same overlay, which keeps native link behaviour (open in a new tab, copy the address, `download`) and takes `render` for a router link. A file the page builds (an export, a CSV) is a Trigger that calls `downloadBlob(blob, name)` or `downloadText(text, name, { type, bom })`; they click a hidden anchor and revoke the object URL 40 seconds later (`DOWNLOAD_REVOKE_DELAY`), never in the same task, which can cancel the save in Safari and Firefox. Pass `bom: true` for a CSV a reader will open in a spreadsheet.

The card takes the raised hover surface while its Trigger or Link is hovered (where the pointer can hover) and the pressed surface while it is pressed, so an interactive card looks different from a static one. A disabled Trigger does neither. Hovering an action in Actions leaves the card at rest.

_Example: story `Stories.LinksAndDownloads`._

## File sizes

`formatFileSize(bytes, { locale })` says a byte count as a reader does: "512 bytes", "840 kB", "2.4 MB". Units are decimal (1 kB is 1,000 bytes), as their names mean and as macOS and iOS report sizes, with at most one decimal in the locale's numerals; pass `useLedgerLocale().locale` in a component. Express a limit in the same units (`50_000_000` for 50 MB) so the Description, a DropZone's refusal and the hint agree.

_Example: story `Stories.FileSizes`._

## Content

Keep the filename recognizable, including its extension. Description supports multiple lines so failure reasons and recovery instructions remain visible. Place all interactive content in Actions when using the card-wide Trigger or Link; avoid wrapping the whole card in a button or link. Actions accepts ordinary Button, IconButton, menus or links when its icon-button shortcut does not fit.

_Example: story `Stories.WithActions`._

## Style

Ledger surface, border, text, spacing, icon, radius and focus tokens. Horizontal cards fit their content; vertical cards default to the rail width. Actions remain in normal flow even on images so they do not cover the preview or its metadata. Group preserves the scrollbar and uses proximity snapping. No external stylesheet, uploader dependency or runtime media inference is required.

_Example: story `Stories.Group`._

## Accessibility

Every Trigger and Link needs `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`; it is an empty overlay with no text of its own. Icon actions require a descriptive `label`, such as “Remove quarterly-report.pdf”. The overlay and the actions are sibling controls with independent focus and activation. Put the Trigger or Link before Actions in the DOM for open-then-actions tab order. Return focus to a surviving control after removal; the With Actions example offers Undo.

No live region is imposed. `aria-busy` identifies in-progress content but does not announce completion; say upload results through `announce`, the page's polite status. Give Progress a label. Hide decorative icons explicitly. For a group containing no interactive attachments, add `tabIndex={0}`, `role="group"` and an accessible name to make horizontal scrolling available from the keyboard. Interactive attachments are reached by Tab, which scrolls them into view.

| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `state` | `"done" \| "error" \| "idle" \| "processing" \| "uploading"` |  | Caller-owned lifecycle. Changes appearance and aria-busy; performs no file operations. |

| `orientation` | `"horizontal" \| "vertical"` |  | Media beside the content, or above it. |

### Attachment.Link

_Props of `AttachmentLink`, generated from its types:_

Every part is exported by name as well as a member (`AttachmentMedia` is `Attachment.Media`), and all compound part prop types are exported. Do not build upload orchestration or infer preview behavior inside Attachment. Do not nest a remove button inside the card's trigger. Do not communicate upload failure through a red border alone, hide recovery copy with truncation, or force every group into a carousel with hidden scrollbars.

<!-- page: Components/Avatar (src/stories/components/Avatar.mdx) -->

# Avatar

**Status: Stable.**

A mark that a person, a team or a system is meant: initials by default, a photo when there is one, in five sizes, built on Base UI's Avatar and shadcn's flat parts. Use it beside a name (an owner, an assessor, a reviewer), as a group of the people on a record, or as the account in the side nav. A person's name in a row is a `Person`: the small avatar and the visible name.

It is not a status: presence, health and verification are words beside the person, and a status is a [Badge](?path=/docs/components-badge--docs). It is not a picture of a record; a record's kind is an [Icon](?path=/docs/components-icon--docs).

## Anatomy

```tsx
<Avatar role="img" aria-label="Dana Whitfield" size="medium">
  <AvatarImage src="/dana.png" alt="" />
  <AvatarFallback>DW</AvatarFallback>
  <AvatarBadge tone="success" />
</Avatar>
```

| Part               | What it is                                                                                                       |
| ------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Avatar`           | The circle or square. Base UI's Root, which tracks the photo's loading.                                          |
| `AvatarImage`      | The photo, drawn only once it has loaded.                                                                        |
| `AvatarFallback`   | The initials (or an icon) the caller writes, shown while the photo loads, when it fails, and when there is none. |
| `AvatarBadge`      | A mark on the corner, ringed in the colour of the surface it sits on: a dot, or an icon from `medium` up.        |
| `AvatarGroup`      | Overlapping avatars; the overlap is a quarter of their size, near enough on the spacing scale.                   |
| `AvatarGroupCount` | The +n circle after the avatars the group draws, at their size. With `render={<button />}`, it opens the rest.   |
| `Person`           | An xsmall avatar, hidden, beside the person's visible name.                                                      |

The caller chooses the members and writes the overflow count; there is no `max`.

## Variants

| `variant`  | Use                                                                                                       |
| ---------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `neutral`  | The default. The fill of a Badge with a hairline, so a person never reads as a status.                    |
| `tinted`   | A soft accent fill, the hue stable per person (`avatarHue(name)`), where several people sit side by side. |
| `bold`     | A strong accent fill with inverse initials, for the one person a view is about.                           |
| `gradient` | Two neighbouring accents, for the account in the shell.                                                   |

Shapes are `circle` for a person and `square` for a team, a system or an organization. The accent colours carry no meaning; a hue only tells two people apart.

_Example: story `Stories.AvatarMatrix`._

_Example: story `Stories.People`._

## Sizes

| `size`   | Box  | Initials | Initials' type                      | Use                                         |
| -------- | ---- | -------- | ----------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------- |
| `xsmall` | 16px | one      | `font.body.xsmall` at medium, 11/14 | Beside a name in a row: `Person`.           |
| `small`  | 24px | two      | `font.body.xsmall` at medium, 11/14 | The default. A group of reviewers in a row. |
| `medium` | 32px | two      | `font.body` at medium, 13/18        | A card, a rail, the account menu.           |
| `large`  | 40px | two      | `font.body.large` at medium, 15/22  | A record's owner in its header.             |
| `xlarge` | 64px | two      | `font.heading.page`, 20/26 semibold | A person's own record.                      |

In a group, the +n circle takes its members' size and a type size under theirs, and the overlap scales with them: 4px at xsmall, 6px at small, 8px at medium and large, 16px at xlarge.

_Example: story `Stories.GroupSizes`._

The ring between overlapping circles, and around a badge, is 2px (`border.width.selected`) of the surface the avatars sit on, `utility.elevation.surface.current`: the page's colour on the page, a card's on a card, a dialog's in a dialog, in both modes.

_Example: story `Stories.OnACard`._

## States

Base UI shows the fallback while the image loads or fails. `AvatarFallback.delay` can delay its appearance so a fast photo never flashes initials. Changing Image's `src` retries loading. Once the photo has loaded, the circle takes the neutral paint behind it.

_Example: story `Stories.ImageLoading`._

## Modifiers

- **`size`**, **`shape`**, **`variant`** and **`hue`** on Avatar; `hue` matters only to `tinted`, `bold` and `gradient`.
- **`avatarInitials(name, count)`** writes the fallback: one letter at xsmall, two above. **`avatarHue(name)`** gives a person the same hue everywhere.
- **AvatarBadge `tone`**: `neutral`, the default, for a mark that is not a status (a lock, a role, an invite); `success` for a verified or active person; `warning` for one who needs attention.
- **AvatarGroupCount `render`**: a button, for a Popover or HoverCard that lists the members the group does not draw.

## Content

- **Initials from the name as the person writes it**, one or two letters. Never a placeholder silhouette in place of a known name.
- **Presence is its own vocabulary**, in words: "online", "away", "invited". Say it in the avatar's `aria-label` ("Dana Whitfield, online") or beside the name, never as a red or green dot alone. A tone on the corner is a status, and presence is not one.
- **A group says who is in it.** Name the group ("Reviewers: Dana Whitfield, Grace Hoppel and three others"), and let the +n open the rest.

A corner mark with no word for it is colour alone: say what it marks in the avatar's name ("Dana Whitfield, verified").

_Example: story `Stories.DoDont`._

## Long content

An avatar holds one or two letters and never overflows. A `Person`'s name is a row field: longer than its column, it ends in an ellipsis and shows whole on hover while it is cut. The group does not count its room: where it would run past its container, the caller draws fewer avatars and a larger +n, and makes the +n a button whose Popover lists the hidden names.

_Example: story `Stories.HiddenMembers`._

## Accessibility

- **Name an informative avatar** with `role="img"` and `aria-label`, including meaningful presence ("Dana Whitfield, online"). Give Image an empty `alt` when the root supplies the name.
- **Hide an avatar beside its visible name** with `aria-hidden="true"`; `Person` does. A named group can hide its avatars and count when its own name describes the whole group.
- **The +n as a button** is named for what it holds ("3 more reviewers"), opens with Enter or Space, and its Popover returns focus to it on Escape. It takes the focus ring and a 24px hit area where a pointer is coarse.
- **Not colour alone.** A corner mark in a tone always has words beside it or in the avatar's name.
- **Contrast:** tinted initials on their fill and inverse initials on the bold fill pass 4.5:1 in every accent, and the neutral paint is a Badge's; the contrast gate holds them.

## Props

Root, Image and Fallback take their native Base UI props, refs, `render`, and state-based classes and styles. Badge takes a span's native props and `tone`; Group takes a div's; GroupCount a div's and `render`. Each part names itself last with its `data-slot` (`avatar`, `avatar-image`, `avatar-fallback`, `avatar-badge`, `avatar-group`, `avatar-group-count`, `person`), and Avatar reports `data-size`, `data-variant` and `data-shape`.

<!-- page: Components/Badge (src/stories/components/Badge.mdx) -->

# Badge

**Status: Stable.**

A compact label built on the shadcn Base UI Badge foundation and adapted to Ledger. One Badge combines six visual treatments with semantic tones, subtle or bold emphasis, two density sizes, optional icons, and rendered-link composition. Every combination uses the same pill anatomy.

`variant` chooses the treatment and its defaults; `tone` chooses the palette; `appearance` adjusts the emphasis of filled treatments; `size` adjusts density. With no props, Badge is the standard brand-filled `default` variant. A `tone` without a `variant` is a status: the `secondary` treatment, the subtle fill in that tone, so `<Badge tone="warning">` never renders a loud bold pill by accident. Bold is asked for, with `appearance="bold"` or an explicit `variant="default"`.

_Example: story `Stories.Matrix`._

## When to use it

- **A record's status, in one or two words**: Verified, In review, Overdue. A `tone` alone makes it the subtle status pill, one to a row, in the status column or beside the title.
- **A category the reader scans a list for**: a record's type, or a marker such as "Inherited".

Not for a number: that is a [Count](?path=/docs/components-count--docs), after the name of what it counts. Not for severity or health beside a label, where a dot and a word say it: that is an [Indicator](?path=/docs/components-indicator--docs), never a pill. Not for a filter the reader can change or clear: that is a [FilterChip](?path=/docs/components-filterchip--docs). Not for something the reader presses: a badge with a click handler has no keyboard behaviour, so an action is a [Button](?path=/docs/components-button--docs), and a destination is a link through `render` (Links, below).

## Anatomy

| Export or part  | Responsibility                                                                                                              |
| --------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Badge`         | A `span` by default, or the element supplied through Base UI's `render` prop.                                               |
| `badgeVariants` | The shared class recipe for treatment, tone, emphasis, and size. Consumers composing their own element can use it directly. |
| Label           | Concise children that remain meaningful without color or an icon. Text children sit in a truncating span inside the pill.   |
| Icon            | An optional leading `icon`, or explicit icon children with `data-icon="inline-start"` / `"inline-end"`.                     |

Badge emits `data-slot="badge"` and its resolved `data-variant`, `data-tone`, `data-appearance`, and `data-size`. Palette choices do not select a different component or change the shape.

```tsx
import { Badge, badgeVariants } from "@ledger/design-system";
import { ArrowUpRight, CircleCheck } from "lucide-react";

<Badge>Featured</Badge>;
<Badge variant="secondary" tone="neutral">
  Draft
</Badge>;
<Badge variant="secondary" tone="success" icon={<CircleCheck aria-hidden="true" />}>
  Verified
</Badge>;
<Badge variant="secondary" tone="danger" appearance="bold" size="xsmall">
  Overdue
</Badge>;
<Badge variant="outline" tone="success" render={<a href="/evidence" />}>
  Verified evidence
  <ArrowUpRight aria-hidden="true" data-icon="inline-end" />
</Badge>;

<span className={badgeVariants({ variant: "secondary", tone: "success", size: "xsmall" })}>
  Verified
</span>;
```

The recipe supplies classes only. A consumer using `badgeVariants` directly owns its element, attributes, refs, semantics, and composition.

_Example: story `Stories.Recipe`._

_Example: story `Stories.ToneWithoutVariant`._

## Variants

All six treatments accept the same tone and size axes.

| `variant`     | Default palette / emphasis | Treatment                                                                                                |
| ------------- | -------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `default`     | Brand / bold               | Filled. A rendered anchor or button uses the palette's hover fill. The default.                          |
| `secondary`   | Neutral / subtle           | Filled. A rendered anchor or button uses the palette's hover fill.                                       |
| `destructive` | Danger / subtle            | Filled. Its default danger tone uses the danger focus outline.                                           |
| `outline`     | Neutral                    | Transparent with a visible border; a rendered anchor or button gains the palette's subtle fill on hover. |
| `ghost`       | Neutral                    | Transparent; a rendered anchor or button gains the palette's subtle fill on hover.                       |
| `link`        | Brand                      | Palette-colored text; a rendered anchor or button underlines on hover.                                   |

Every hover belongs to a badge that is a link or a button: a label on a span never answers the pointer, whatever its treatment. A brand badge link draws its words in `color.text.selected` on the hovered fill, where `color.text.brand` would fall under 4.5:1.

_Example: story `Stories.HoverOnlyWhenInteractive`._

`appearance="subtle"` or `"bold"` overrides the filled treatments' default emphasis. Outline, ghost, and link retain their treatment when an appearance is supplied. `tone` overrides the palette across every variant, including outline borders and link text. Semantic colors adapt to light and dark modes; bold warning badges use the dark `color.text.warning.inverse` text token.

| Tone          | Meaning                                                                      |
| ------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `brand`       | Branding or a featured label. The default palette for `default` and `link`.  |
| `neutral`     | A category, kind, or state without a judgment: Inspection, Draft, Inherited. |
| `information` | In progress: In review, In assessment.                                       |
| `success`     | Done and good: Verified, Satisfied, Closed.                                  |
| `warning`     | Needs attention soon: Due soon, Partial, Suspect.                            |
| `danger`      | Wrong or late: Overdue, Other than satisfied, Invalidated.                   |

These are the kit's meanings, and the words are examples of them. A product keeps its own values, each value's words and its tone, in one status map that follows these meanings, so a value reads the same on every screen; that map, not this table, decides where a product word such as In remediation or Accepted falls.

_Example: story `Stories.SemanticMatrix`._

The next matrix applies every status tone to all six variants at the compact size. Outline and link examples render actual anchors. The radius, icon anatomy, and density are shared across the matrix.

_Example: story `Stories.SemanticVariants`._

## Sizes

| `size`   | Height / text | Use                                                 |
| -------- | ------------- | --------------------------------------------------- |
| `small`  | 20px / 12px   | Default. Beside a title, in a rail, or in a header. |
| `xsmall` | 16px / 11px   | A table row, a tab, or a dense list item.           |

Both sizes use the same pill radius and 12px icons. Small badges use 8px horizontal padding, reduced to 6px beside a marked icon; xsmall badges keep 4px padding for density. The width follows the label, which stays on one line. Containers should wrap separate badges when space is limited; keep long labels readable.

### Long content

A badge is one line and never wraps. It is never wider than its container: a label longer than the room it has (the RMF "Other than satisfied" in a status column, a category in a narrow panel) ends in an ellipsis, and the whole label shows in a tooltip on hover, and on keyboard focus of a badge that links, while it is cut. The whole label stays in the DOM, so a screen reader reads it all. A badge with a `title` of its own shows that instead. Keep status words short so the cut is rare: size a status column from its longest word. An id, a URL or a file name is never a badge.

_Example: story `Stories.InRows`._

_Example: story `Stories.DenseAndLongContent`._

## States

| State           | Behavior                                                                                            |
| --------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Plain label     | Native span semantics. No default tab stop or action.                                               |
| Rendered anchor | Native link semantics, Tab focus, Enter activation, and treatment-specific hover styling.           |
| Focus visible   | Focus border and Ledger's 2px outline with a 2px offset. A danger tone uses the danger outline.     |
| Invalid         | Caller-owned `aria-invalid` selects the danger border and outline color. It does not validate data. |

Badge manages no selection, dismissal, loading, or disabled state. Use an appropriate interactive control for those behaviors. A variant supplies presentation; a rendered element supplies its native interaction semantics.

_Example: story `Stories.States`._

## Composition

### Links

Keep the destination on the rendered anchor or router element. A router adapter must forward every received prop and its ref to the actual anchor so that styles, handlers, and accessibility attributes reach the same element.

```tsx
import { forwardRef, type ComponentProps } from "react";
import { Badge } from "@ledger/design-system";

type RouterLinkProps = Omit<ComponentProps<"a">, "href"> & { to: string };

const RouterLink = forwardRef<HTMLAnchorElement, RouterLinkProps>(function RouterLink(
  { to, ...props },
  ref,
) {
  return <a ref={ref} href={to} {...props} />;
});

<Badge variant="outline" tone="information" render={<RouterLink to="/programs" />}>
  Programs
</Badge>;
```

Base UI merges attributes, classes, styles, event handlers, and both refs onto the same rendered element.

_Example: story `Stories.RenderLink`._

### Icons and conditional content

Use `icon={<CircleCheck aria-hidden="true" />}` for a leading icon, or place icons explicitly among the children. Explicit leading and trailing icons use `data-icon="inline-start"` and `data-icon="inline-end"` to select the corresponding padding. An icon element supplied through the shorthand receives the leading marker. Keep the label meaningful whether an optional icon is present or absent.

_Example: story `Stories.ConditionalIcons`._

## Content

- Use one or two words that remain useful without color: Verified, In review, Overdue.
- Use the state rather than the tone name: Overdue, not Danger.
- Keep categories neutral; their words distinguish them.
- Use one vocabulary for each state throughout the product.
- Keep bold emphasis for the status that needs the most attention.
- Give rendered links labels that make their destinations understandable.

_Example: story `Stories.Categories`._

_Example: story `Stories.OneBold`._

A badge that goes somewhere is a link through `render` (`render={<a href="#evidence" />}`), never a Badge with an `onClick`: that is a span, with no link and no keyboard behaviour.

_Example: story `Stories.Dont`._

_Example: story `Stories.StatusGuidance`._

## Accessibility

- A plain Badge is inline text. A click handler does not make it a keyboard control.
- A link requires an actual anchor with a destination through `render`; `variant="link"` supplies presentation only.
- A badge rendered as an anchor or a button takes a hit area of at least 24px where any pointer is coarse, and stops clipping so the area reaches past the pill. A label badge stays unpositioned.
- Native attributes and refs reach the actual element. Custom router adapters must forward them.
- Pair semantic colors with visible words and hide decorative icons from assistive technology.
- Use native controls for selection or dismissal. Badge does not implement those behaviors.

_Example: story `Stories.NativeAttributes`._

## Props

`BadgeProps` combines native span props and Base UI's `render` composition with the shared recipe's variant, tone, appearance, and size axes, plus the optional icon. `React.ComponentProps<typeof Badge>` derives the same component props. The ref receives the actual rendered element; anchor-specific props such as `href` belong on the anchor supplied through `render`.

_Props of `Badge`, generated from its types:_

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `render` | `ReactElement<unknown, string \| JSXElementConstructor<any>> \| ComponentRenderFn<HTMLProps, {}>` |  | Allows you to replace the component's HTML element with a different tag, or compose it with another component. Accepts a `ReactElement` or a function that returns the element to render. |
| `size` | `"small" \| "xsmall"` | `small` | Small is 20px; xsmall is 16px for dense rows and tabs. |
| `variant` | `BadgeVariant \| null` |  | The treatment. `default`, the brand bold fill, when neither it nor `tone` is given; `secondary`, the subtle fill, when only `tone` is. |
| `tone` | `"brand" \| "danger" \| "information" \| "neutral" \| "success" \| "warning"` |  | Overrides the variant's palette. Brand, or one of the five semantic status tones. |
| `appearance` | `"bold" \| "subtle"` |  | Overrides the subtle or bold fill on default, secondary and destructive variants. |
| `icon` | `ReactNode` |  | An optional leading icon. Explicit icon children and their position attributes also work. |

_Example: story `Stories.Playground`._

<!-- page: Components/Banner (src/stories/components/Banner.mdx) -->

# Banner

**Status: Stable.**

A message about the whole site, at the top of the screen in the shell's Banner area: the loss of data or a function, or something site-wide that changes what the reader can do. One at a time, never dismissible, gone when no longer true. On a bar 42rem wide or more it is one line; narrower, on a phone, the message wraps and the bar grows with it. The action is one link or button drawn in the banner's own colour. The kit's inline message is the [Alert](?path=/docs/components-alert--docs).

An Alert is about the record; a Banner is about the site. Feedback after an act is a toast. If the message would be true for one reader and not the next, it is not a banner.

_Example: story `Stories.BannerMatrix`._

## Anatomy

| Part    | What it is                                                                                                                                                            |
| ------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Bar     | At least 48px, `dimension.layout.banner`, the tone's bold fill, `space.200` inside at each end; its content centred on a wide bar, from the start on a narrow one.    |
| Icon    | The tone's icon at `dimension.icon.small`: Info, TriangleAlert, CircleAlert, on the first line's centre. `icon` replaces it.                                          |
| Message | `font.body` medium in the inverse text colour: one line on a wide bar, cut with an ellipsis and its whole text as its title when it must be; wrapped on a narrow one. |
| Action  | One link or button after the message's last word, underlined, in the banner's own text colour.                                                                        |

## Variants

Banner has one appearance; the tone is what varies, and there are three.

| Tone          | Use                                                                                                      |
| ------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `information` | Something changed for everyone: the catalogue moved to a new revision, a maintenance window is booked.   |
| `warning`     | The default. Something is about to change what the reader can do: the audit window closes, uploads lock. |
| `danger`      | Something is lost: the connection to the evidence store, the session's writes. Announced at once.        |

There is no success banner and no neutral one: a banner is gone when it is no longer true, and good news is feedback, which is a toast. The kit has the bold fill only, no low-contrast form, since a banner is by definition the one thing on the screen that outranks the page.

Where it lives: `Shell.Banner` is the area, above the top navigation. It holds the Banner and pushes the page down by the banner's height while one is rendered; see [Shell](?path=/docs/layout-shell--docs).

## Sizes

One: the width of the screen. The bar is its own container, so its width, not the window's, decides the form. From 42rem it is one 48px line. Narrower it wraps: `space.100` above and below, the icon on the first line, the action after the last word, and the bar as tall as its lines. `Shell.Banner` measures it, so the top navigation, the side navigation and the panel sit under a banner that wraps.

_Example: story `Stories.LongMessage`._

## States

Present or absent. A banner is rendered while its condition holds and unmounted when it stops; there is no dismissed state, no hover, and no collapsed form. Its action has the kit's focus outline.

## Modifiers

- **`tone`** as in Variants; `warning` when unsaid.
- **`action`** for the one link or button: an anchor, a button, or the router's Link. The Banner colours it and underlines it; it keeps its own `onClick` or `to`.
- **`icon`** to replace the tone's icon with a more specific one, rarely.
- **`className`** for the shell's layout, not for colour.

_Example: story `Stories.Banners`._

## Content

- **One sentence: the fact and what it changes.** "The audit window closes in three days; evidence uploads lock after that."
- **Present tense, plain.** No "Please note", no "Attention".
- **The action names where it goes:** "See what changed", "Ask for an extension". One.
- **Not feedback, not a greeting, not a record.** Those are a toast, nothing, and an Alert.

## Style

| Element | Token                                                                                                                                           |
| ------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Bar     | `dimension.layout.banner` 48px, the minimum · `color.background.<tone>.bold` · `space.200` inline · `space.100` gap and, wrapped, block padding |
| Text    | `font.body` medium · `color.text.inverse`, `color.text.warning.inverse` on warning                                                              |
| Icon    | `dimension.icon.small` 14px in the text colour                                                                                                  |
| Action  | Underlined, `radius.xsmall` for its focus outline                                                                                               |

The bold fills are Badge's bold appearance, so a danger banner and a danger bold Badge are the same red.

## Accessibility

- **A danger Banner is `role="alert"`**, announced at once; the rest are `role="status"`. The shell's Banner area is a region named "Banner".
- **Nothing is hidden on a phone:** the message wraps there. On a wide bar a message too long for its line is cut for sighted readers only, and its whole text is the message's title; a screen reader hears it all. Keep it to one sentence so everyone gets the same message.
- **The action is in the tab order; the banner is not.** It sits first in the page, before the top navigation, so it is the first thing a keyboard reader meets, which is the point.
- **The bold fills pass 4.5:1** with the inverse text in both modes; the contrast test covers them.

Action focus rings inherit the banner’s contrasting text color, keeping the ring visible against every bold tone.

## Props

Native `div` props and refs target the outer message. IDs, ARIA, data attributes, styles and handlers are forwarded; `className` merges with the default layout. The default role remains `status`, or `alert` for danger. An explicit `role` or live-region attribute controls delivery when the enclosing page needs different announcement behavior.

The `action` keeps its own element, ref, ID, attributes, styles and handlers while receiving the banner’s action classes. A root click handler receives the action’s bubbled click. Default icons are decorative.

_Props of `Banner`, generated from its types:_

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `tone` | `"danger" \| "information" \| "warning"` | `warning` | `information` for something that changed, `warning` for something about to, `danger` for something lost. `warning` is the default; there is no success banner. |
| `icon` | `ComponentType<{ className?: string; }>` |  | Replaces the tone's icon. |
| `action` | `ReactElement<{ className?: string; }, string \| JSXElementConstructor<any>>` |  | One link or button, rendered in the banner's own colour: an anchor, a button, or the router's Link. |

### Playground

_Example: story `Stories.Playground`._

_Rendered in the Storybook: Controls._

- [Alert](?path=/docs/components-alert--docs): the message about a record.
- [Toaster](?path=/docs/components-toaster--docs): feedback after an act.

- [Badge](?path=/docs/components-badge--docs): the tone table.

## Don't

A Banner is about the whole site, in one sentence with one action. A message about one record is an Alert and feedback after an act is a toast, never a banner; two sentences and two actions are cut on a wide bar and fill the top of a phone's screen.
