<!-- page: Components/Breadcrumb (src/stories/components/Breadcrumb.mdx) -->

# Breadcrumb

**Status: Stable.**

Show where the reader is in the record tree and provide links to its parent levels. Breadcrumb follows the shadcn Base UI component structure, with Ledger's typography, color, spacing, icon, focus, and motion tokens.

Compose the list, items, links, separators, and current page explicitly. The component does not generate separators or infer the current page. The list keeps the trail on one line in any container: when it does not fit, the middle levels fold behind an ellipsis whose menu lists them as links.

_Example: story `Stories.BreadcrumbMatrix`._

## When to use it

- **Where a page sits in a record tree**: the levels above the record, each a link to its page, ending at the current page. On a record page the trail sits in [PageHeader](?path=/docs/layout-pageheader--docs)'s Lead, above the title.
- **A path that changes in place**, such as a chart's drill-down: its levels are buttons that choose a level (In-place state, below).

Not for the steps of a task: that is a [Stepper](?path=/docs/components-stepper--docs). Not for the reader's history or the tabs of one page: a trail is the hierarchy, not the way the reader came. Not for browsing the hierarchy itself: that is a [Tree](?path=/docs/components-tree--docs).

## Anatomy

All seven parts are named exports from `@ledger/design-system`.

| Part                  | Default element and responsibility                                                                                            |
| --------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Breadcrumb`          | A `nav` named "Breadcrumb" (the `breadcrumb` message) unless `aria-label` names it. Contains the list.                        |
| `BreadcrumbList`      | An `ol` that keeps one line and folds levels behind an ellipsis menu, or wraps.                                               |
| `BreadcrumbItem`      | An `li` for one level, on the list's line or in its wrapping text. Contains a link, page, or composed control.                |
| `BreadcrumbLink`      | An `a`, or the element supplied through Base UI's `render` prop. Always an ancestor: it drops an `aria-current` it is handed. |
| `BreadcrumbPage`      | A `span` with `role="link"`, `aria-disabled="true"`, and `aria-current="page"`.                                               |
| `BreadcrumbSeparator` | A decorative `li` between items. A chevron by default; accepts custom children.                                               |
| `BreadcrumbEllipsis`  | A decorative `span` containing a horizontal ellipsis. Provides no interaction by itself.                                      |

```tsx
import {
  Breadcrumb,
  BreadcrumbItem,
  BreadcrumbLink,
  BreadcrumbList,
  BreadcrumbPage,
  BreadcrumbSeparator,
} from "@ledger/design-system";

<Breadcrumb aria-label="Program hierarchy">
  <BreadcrumbList>
    <BreadcrumbItem>
      <BreadcrumbLink href="/programs">Programs</BreadcrumbLink>
    </BreadcrumbItem>
    <BreadcrumbSeparator />
    <BreadcrumbItem>
      <BreadcrumbLink href="/programs/atlas">Atlas payments platform</BreadcrumbLink>
    </BreadcrumbItem>
    <BreadcrumbSeparator />
    <BreadcrumbItem>
      <BreadcrumbPage>Controls</BreadcrumbPage>
    </BreadcrumbItem>
  </BreadcrumbList>
</Breadcrumb>;
```

_Example: story `Stories.Basic`._

## Variants

The component has one appearance. Its parts support different compositions without adding variant props.

| Composition       | How to build it                                                                                                                                                                         |
| ----------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Standard trail    | Place `BreadcrumbLink` in each parent item and `BreadcrumbPage` in the final item.                                                                                                      |
| Custom separator  | Pass text or an icon to `BreadcrumbSeparator`, such as `<BreadcrumbSeparator>/</BreadcrumbSeparator>`.                                                                                  |
| Collapsed parents | Automatic: the list folds middle levels behind its own ellipsis menu. For a disclosure of your own, set `overflow="wrap"` and put `BreadcrumbEllipsis` inside a named button.           |
| Icon or badge     | Put an icon inside `BreadcrumbLink` with `className="inline-flex items-center gap-050"`, and a badge in the `BreadcrumbItem` beside the link. The level keeps its whole width or folds. |
| Local hierarchy   | Render an actual button through `BreadcrumbLink` for a level that changes state in place.                                                                                               |
| Single page       | One `BreadcrumbItem` containing `BreadcrumbPage`, without separators.                                                                                                                   |

_Example: story `Stories.CustomSeparator`._

### Collapsed parents

The list folds levels by itself when its container is too narrow (see [Sizes](#sizes)). To own the disclosure instead, set `overflow="wrap"` on the list so the two do not compete.

The ellipsis is hidden from assistive technology. Give the enclosing control its own accessible name and implement its behavior. This example uses a disclosure button with `aria-expanded`, reveals the parents inline, and retains keyboard focus on the button.

```tsx
import { BreadcrumbEllipsis, BreadcrumbItem } from "@ledger/design-system";

<BreadcrumbItem>
  <button
    type="button"
    aria-label={expanded ? "Hide parent levels" : "Show parent levels"}
    aria-expanded={expanded}
    onClick={() => setExpanded((value) => !value)}
  >
    <BreadcrumbEllipsis />
  </button>
</BreadcrumbItem>;
```

_Example: story `Stories.Collapsed`._

## Sizes

One default size: `font.body.small`. The trail follows the width of its container, not the window, so it behaves the same on a page, in a panel and on a phone.

With `overflow="collapse"` (the default) the trail stays on one line. When it does not fit, it gives up space in this order:

1. The middle levels fold behind the ellipsis, nearest the root first.
2. The parent's and the current page's names share what is left. The longer one shortens first, down to 80px, so the shorter keeps its whole name while it can.
3. The root folds, and the ellipsis leads the line.
4. The parent folds, leaving the ellipsis and the page.

A shortened name keeps its full text as its title, and a link never shrinks below 80px (or its whole name, when that is shorter). The ellipsis menu lists the folded levels as links in order, and every level returns when the space does. The line never starts or ends with a separator.

Only `BreadcrumbPage` and a `BreadcrumbLink` whose children are text shorten. A level composed from other content, such as an icon beside the name or a plain `span` for a level the reader cannot go back to, keeps its whole width or folds; folded, it appears in the ellipsis menu under its link's name, or as a disabled item when it has no link. The line keeps the height of its tallest level whether that level shows or folds, so the page below does not move as levels fold.

_Example: story `Stories.CollapsesToFit`._

_Example: story `Stories.LongerNameGivesWay`._

_Example: story `Stories.ShortTrailFoldsTheRoot`._

_Example: story `Stories.RootFoldsLast`._

_Example: story `Stories.UnlinkedParentFolds`._

_Example: story `Stories.ComposedLevels`._

The trail folds to the width it is given: a block such as `PageHeader.Lead`, or a flex item with `min-width: 0`, which `Breadcrumb` has by itself. Beside an action it may size to its content; it still follows the row as it narrows and widens. A wrapper around it in a flex row needs `min-w-0` too; without it, the row grows to the whole trail.

_Example: story `Stories.BesideAnAction`._

With `overflow="wrap"` every level shows and the trail wraps at word boundaries; each separator starts its line with the level it leads to.

_Example: story `Stories.LongWrappingTrail`._

_Example: story `Stories.AboveTitle`._

## States

| State             | Behavior                                                                                                                      |
| ----------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Parent link       | Subtle text, default text color on hover; native Tab and Enter behavior.                                                      |
| Keyboard focus    | Ledger's focus outline on the rendered link or button.                                                                        |
| Current page      | Regular-weight default text. Announced as the current, disabled link; no `href` or default tab stop.                          |
| Folded levels     | Out of the line and the accessibility tree; listed as links in the ellipsis menu, whose button is named "Show hidden levels". |
| Shortened name    | Ends in an ellipsis; the full name is the link's or page's `title`.                                                           |
| Collapsed parents | With `overflow="wrap"`, application-owned state on the enclosing control; the ellipsis is decorative.                         |

`BreadcrumbPage` preserves shadcn's accessible semantics: it is a noninteractive span exposed as a disabled current link. Its role does not make it an anchor or add keyboard behavior.

A level that folds while it holds focus hands focus to the ellipsis, which now lists it, without scrolling the page, so a keyboard reader's place stays in the trail when the window narrows (the Collapses To Fit story).

In a right-to-left page the trail reads from the right, and the default chevrons turn to point along the reading direction; it folds the same way. A custom separator's content is the caller's: turn a directional glyph with `rtl:rotate-180`.

_Example: story `Stories.RightToLeft`._

## Modifiers

- **`aria-label`** on `Breadcrumb` names the navigation landmark. The default is "Breadcrumb" (the `breadcrumb` message, which a `LedgerProvider` can translate).
- **`overflow`** on `BreadcrumbList`: `"collapse"` (default) keeps one line and folds levels; `"wrap"` shows every level on as many lines as it needs.
- **`render`** on `BreadcrumbLink` composes a router link or another suitable element through Base UI's `useRender` and `mergeProps`.
- **`children`** on `BreadcrumbSeparator` replaces the default chevron.
- **Native props and `ref`** reach each part's rendered DOM element. Use `className` and `style` on the relevant part for a deliberate layout adjustment.

### Router link composition

The custom component must forward its received props and ref to its actual anchor. This allows Base UI to compose event handlers, classes, attributes, and both refs on the same element.

```tsx
import { forwardRef, type ComponentProps } from "react";
import { BreadcrumbItem, BreadcrumbLink } from "@ledger/design-system";

type RouterLinkProps = Omit<ComponentProps<"a">, "href"> & { to: string };

const RouterLink = forwardRef<HTMLAnchorElement, RouterLinkProps>(function RouterLink(
  { to, ...props },
  ref,
) {
  return <a ref={ref} href={to} {...props} />;
});

<BreadcrumbItem>
  <BreadcrumbLink render={<RouterLink to="/programs" />}>Programs</BreadcrumbLink>
</BreadcrumbItem>;
```

The example below verifies that props and both refs reach the anchor, and that mouse and keyboard activation each invoke the adapter and breadcrumb handlers. Its adapter prevents navigation to keep the demonstration in the canvas.

_Example: story `Stories.RenderLink`._

### The current page and router links

Only `BreadcrumbPage` is the current page. A router link marks itself `aria-current="page"` whenever the current path starts with its own, so on `/programs/atlas/controls` a trail of plain router links announces Programs and the program as the current page too, and a screen reader says so on every level. A trail must have exactly one current page, and it is the last level.

BreadcrumbLink is always an ancestor, so it drops an `aria-current` it is handed. That covers a router that renders through the part. With TanStack Router, create the trail link once:

```tsx
import { createLink } from "@tanstack/react-router";
import { BreadcrumbLink } from "@ledger/design-system";

// The router works out the href and the active state, then renders BreadcrumbLink with them.
export const TrailLink = createLink(BreadcrumbLink);

<BreadcrumbItem>
  <TrailLink to="/programs">Programs</TrailLink>
</BreadcrumbItem>;
```

A router Link given as a `render` element sets the attribute inside itself, after the kit's props, where BreadcrumbLink cannot reach. Give it exact matching instead, so an ancestor is never active:

```tsx
<BreadcrumbLink render={<Link to="/programs" activeOptions={{ exact: true }} />}>
  Programs
</BreadcrumbLink>
```

Either way, compose the trail once in the application, next to its record links, rather than at every page. The kit does not strip the attribute from the DOM after the router sets it: React and the router own it. A trail that marks more than one level as the current page, or a level other than its last, says so once in the console ("Ledger: a breadcrumb trail marks …"), so the mistake shows in development without breaking the page.

_Example: story `Stories.RouterLinks`._

### In-place state

Use an anchor for page navigation. For a hierarchy that updates local state, supply a native button explicitly:

```tsx
<BreadcrumbItem>
  <BreadcrumbLink render={<button type="button" onClick={() => selectLevel("programs")} />}>
    Programs
  </BreadcrumbLink>
</BreadcrumbItem>
```

The rendered control remains a button, including its Enter and Space behavior. This is a local record hierarchy; use [Stepper](?path=/docs/components-stepper--docs) for sequential tasks.

_Example: story `Stories.InPlaceButtons`._

## Content

- Use the level's actual name: "Programs", "Atlas payments platform", "Controls".
- Order the trail from the highest relevant parent to the current page.
- Include the record's identifier when it is needed to distinguish that record.
- Keep tabs and browsing history out of the hierarchy.
- Retain readable names at narrow widths; reveal omitted parents through a labeled, working control.

## Style

| Element                     | Ledger tokens and classes                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| --------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| List typography             | `font.body.small` / `font-body-small`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| Parent links and separators | `color.text.subtle` / `text-subtle`; links use `color.text` / `text-default` on hover                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| Current page                | `color.text` / `text-default`, `font-regular`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| List gap                    | `space.075` / `gap-075`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| Item gap                    | `space.050` / `gap-050`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| Chevron                     | `dimension.icon.small` / `size-icon-small`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| Ellipsis                    | `size-250` container with a `dimension.icon.medium` / `size-icon-medium` icon; the list's own menu trigger uses `size-200` to keep the line 16px tall                                                                                                                                                                |
| Touch                       | Links and the ellipsis trigger take `touch-target`, a 24px hit area centred on the control wherever a pointer is coarse, without moving the line. With `overflow="wrap"`, links take `touch-target-block` instead: a band the link's own width, so a link that wraps never takes a tap meant for the words beside it |
| Focus                       | `radius.xsmall` / `rounded-xsmall`, `focus-visible:outline-focused`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| Link transition             | `duration-fast`, `ease-standard`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |

These defaults use the same semantic tokens in light and dark modes. Customize presentation through Ledger tokens while retaining the component anatomy and prop contract.

## Accessibility

- `Breadcrumb` creates a named navigation landmark containing an ordered list supplied by `BreadcrumbList`.
- Use distinct `aria-label` values for distinct breadcrumb landmarks on one page. The matrix does this without disabling the landmark uniqueness check.
- Parent anchors are reached by Tab and activated by Enter. Keep their real destinations so users can open them in another tab.
- Exactly one level is the current page: `BreadcrumbPage`, last. BreadcrumbLink drops an `aria-current` a router hands it; a router link through `render` needs exact matching (see [The current page and router links](#the-current-page-and-router-links)).
- `BreadcrumbPage` identifies the current page through `aria-current="page"`, with `role="link"` and `aria-disabled="true"`. It has no default tab stop.
- Separators and ellipsis have `role="presentation"` and `aria-hidden="true"`. Do not put interactive content inside a separator.
- A level that folds while focused hands focus to the ellipsis button, so focus never falls to the page.
- A folded level leaves the accessibility tree. The list's ellipsis is a menu button named "Show hidden levels" (the `showHiddenLevels` message, which a `LedgerProvider` can translate), and it keeps its place in the reading and tab order when the root folds and it leads the line; its items are links with the folded levels' real hrefs. Choosing one runs the folded link itself, so a router link keeps its client-side navigation; a modified click opens the href in a new tab.
- Ellipsis alone is not an accessible control. Its button or menu trigger needs a name, keyboard behavior, and appropriate state attributes.
- Custom render components must forward props and refs to preserve native attributes and keyboard behavior.

## Props

Each part accepts its native element's props, including DOM attributes, event handlers, `className`, `style`, and `ref`. `BreadcrumbLink` additionally accepts Base UI's `render` prop.

| Export                | Native props                                                       | Ref target                                                  |
| --------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Breadcrumb`          | `React.ComponentProps<"nav">`                                      | `HTMLElement` (`nav`)                                       |
| `BreadcrumbList`      | `BreadcrumbListProps`: `React.ComponentProps<"ol">` and `overflow` | `HTMLOListElement`                                          |
| `BreadcrumbItem`      | `React.ComponentProps<"li">`                                       | `HTMLLIElement`                                             |
| `BreadcrumbLink`      | `useRender.ComponentProps<"a">`                                    | Anchor by default; the composed element when using `render` |
| `BreadcrumbPage`      | `React.ComponentProps<"span">`                                     | `HTMLSpanElement`                                           |
| `BreadcrumbSeparator` | `React.ComponentProps<"li">`                                       | `HTMLLIElement`                                             |
| `BreadcrumbEllipsis`  | `React.ComponentProps<"span">`                                     | `HTMLSpanElement`                                           |

### BreadcrumbList

_Props of `BreadcrumbList`, generated from its types:_

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `overflow` | `"collapse" \| "wrap"` | `collapse` | `collapse` keeps the trail on one line at the width of its container. When it does not fit, the middle levels fold first, nearest the root first, behind an ellipsis whose menu lists them as links. Then the parent's and the current page's names share what is left: the longer shortens first, down to 80px, so the shorter keeps its whole name while it can. Then the root folds, and last the parent, leaving the ellipsis and the page. A shortened name keeps its full text as a title, a link never shrinks below 80px (or its whole name), and every level comes back when the space does. Only `BreadcrumbPage` and a `BreadcrumbLink` whose children are text shorten; a level composed from other content (an icon and a name, a plain span) keeps its whole width or folds. The trail folds to the width its container gives it: a block, or a flex item with `min-width: 0` (a wrapper in a flex row needs it too), including one that sizes to its content beside an action. `wrap` shows every level, wrapping onto further lines; each separator starts the line with the level it leads to, never ending a line. Use it when the product composes its own disclosure. |

<!-- page: Components/Button (src/stories/components/Button.mdx) -->

# Button

**Status: Stable.**

Button starts an action. Use a short label that names what happens, such as “Save changes” or “Export report.”

Use it for something that happens on this page: saving, opening a dialog or a menu, changing state. Do not use it to go somewhere: navigation that looks like a button is a [LinkButton](?path=/docs/components-linkbutton--docs), a real anchor the reader can open in a new tab, and a link in text is a [TextLink](?path=/docs/components-textlink--docs). An icon-only action is an [IconButton](?path=/docs/components-iconbutton--docs); an on/off state is a [Toggle](?path=/docs/components-toggle--docs).

_Example: story `Stories.Matrix`._

Leading and trailing icons use a smaller inset on their own side; icon-only controls stay centered. Open popup triggers retain their pressed surface through `aria-expanded` while the popup is open. Toggle selection continues to use `aria-pressed`.

## Choosing between them

| Need                                                                        | Part                                                                                           |
| --------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Something happens on this page: save, open a dialog or a menu, change state | Button                                                                                         |
| The same, shown only as an icon                                             | [IconButton](?path=/docs/components-iconbutton--docs)                                          |
| Go somewhere, with a button's look                                          | [LinkButton](?path=/docs/components-linkbutton--docs) or LinkIconButton                        |
| Go somewhere from inside a sentence, or a record's name in a row            | [TextLink](?path=/docs/components-textlink--docs)                                              |
| One setting that is on or off                                               | [Toggle](?path=/docs/components-toggle--docs) or [Switch](?path=/docs/components-switch--docs) |
| One choice among a few, shown at once                                       | [ToggleGroup](?path=/docs/components-togglegroup--docs)                                        |
| Copy a value                                                                | [CopyButton](?path=/docs/components-copybutton--docs)                                          |

## Hierarchy

One primary per region: a page header, a dialog footer, a toolbar, a card. It is the action the region exists for, and the reader finds it without reading the rest. Every other action beside it is secondary, or subtle where there are several; a destructive action is `danger`, and its confirmation's primary is `danger` too. When a region seems to need two primaries, one of them belongs in an overflow menu or in another region. A collection among others in a record body or a preview creates through a small secondary; the page header or the preview's record header keeps the one primary. A split primary, a ButtonGroup of the action and its menu, is one control.

_Example: story `Stories.Emphasis`._

## Content

- **Name what happens, as a verb and its object:** “Create requirement revision”, “Export report”, “Remove allocation”. The trigger, the dialog's title and its primary use the same words.
- **Never OK, Submit, Save or Yes alone.** A reader who lands on the button hears only its name.
- **Sentence case, no end punctuation,** and short enough for one line: a label that needs to wrap is a sentence, and belongs in the region's text.
- **The visible words are the name.** Do not put `aria-label` on a Button that shows text: a speech-input user says the words they see (WCAG 2.5.3, Label in Name). Add context with `aria-describedby` instead. A Button whose `aria-label` leaves out its visible text says so once in the console, with a message that starts “Ledger:”.
- **Keep the label while loading.** Do not swap it for “Saving…”: `isLoading` keeps the name and the width, and `loadingLabel` says what is happening.

## Variants and sizes

| Variant     | Use                                                      |
| ----------- | -------------------------------------------------------- |
| `secondary` | Default raised action: Export, Edit, Open.               |
| `primary`   | The main action in a header, form or dialog.             |
| `subtle`    | Low emphasis actions in toolbars, rows and footers.      |
| `danger`    | Destructive actions, with confirmation when appropriate. |
| `link`      | A text styled action, such as Show more.                 |

| Size     | Height | Typical placement                       |
| -------- | ------ | --------------------------------------- |
| `medium` | 32px   | Default for forms, headers and footers. |
| `small`  | 28px   | Toolbars and rows.                      |
| `xsmall` | 24px   | Dense inline actions.                   |

The `link` variant has no fixed height and ignores `size`: it is as tall as its text. `iconBefore` and `iconAfter` take an icon element; Button sizes it to 14px and keeps a 6px gap. `isSelected` applies the selected palette and `aria-pressed`.

The family shares one height axis: `xsmall` 24px, `small` 28px and `medium` 32px on Button, IconButton, LinkButton and LinkIconButton, and the icon-only two add `xxsmall`, the 20px row control. Button defaults to `medium` and IconButton to `small`, so an IconButton beside a default Button takes `size="medium"`. Toggle and ToggleGroup take the same words: `small` 28px, `medium` 32px, and `large`, a 36px step Button does not have. ButtonGroupText takes the `size` of the controls beside it.

## Long labels

A label is short enough for one line in the slot it sits in; a longer one is a sentence and belongs in the region's text. For the one slot that cannot grow, such as a rail, a card's footer or a table cell, `truncate` lets the button narrow to its container and cuts the label with an ellipsis, its icons whole. The whole label stays the accessible name, and a tooltip shows it on hover and on keyboard focus while it is cut; with `disabledReason`, the reason's tooltip names the action. With `isFullWidth` the button fills the slot and cuts the label at its edge. Without `truncate`, a label never wraps or cuts.

_Example: story `Stories.TruncatedLabel`._

## Loading and forms

Button defaults to `type="button"`. Set `type="submit"` for a form's submit action. Native form attributes, event handlers and refs reach the button element. `isFullWidth` fills its container.

`isLoading` blocks activation and preserves focus while work is pending, and the button keeps its width and its name. The decorative spinner takes the leading icon's place; without one, the trailing icon's; without either, it sits over the label, which keeps its space and stays the accessible name. It sets `aria-busy`, which the major screen readers do not announce, so pass `loadingLabel` (“Saving requirement revision”) to say once, through the page's polite live region, what started; leave it out when a toast or a status on the page already says it. Do not also pass the pending flag to `disabled`: an explicitly `disabled` button remains disabled and leaves the normal tab order, so focus falls to the page (`ledger/no-disabled-while-loading` reports it). Base UI's `focusableWhenDisabled` is available when a disabled action needs to remain focusable.

_Example: story `Stories.Loading`._

_Example: story `Stories.LoadingKeepsItsWidth`._

## Disabled with a reason

Keep actions enabled where you can, and explain on use: a form's submit stays enabled and reports what is missing. When an action truly cannot run, say why with `disabledReason` instead of `disabled`. The button takes the disabled face but stays in the tab order with `aria-disabled`, so a keyboard reader reaches it; the reason is its accessible description and shows in a tooltip on hover, on keyboard focus and on a tap. Activation is blocked. Write the reason as what would make the action available: “Add content to this version before publishing it.”, not “Disabled.” A `title` on a disabled button never shows, because a disabled button takes no pointer events.

`disabledReason` disables the button by itself and keeps it focusable even when `disabled` is also set. An empty string is no reason. A Button with a reason owns its tooltip; do not put it inside another TooltipTrigger.

_Example: story `Stories.DisabledWithAReason`._

A reason that comes or goes while the button has focus leaves focus where it is. Publishing a version can make Publish unavailable at once: focus stays on it and its tooltip says why. A scan that finishes while the reader is on Download leaves them on an enabled Download.

_Example: story `Stories.ReasonChangesWhileFocused`._

## Composition

`render` accepts an element or a render function for an action control. Render elements merge native props, handlers, refs, classes and styles. Render functions receive the props and state and must apply those props to their result. Custom components must forward them to their DOM element. Button's root ref describes a native button; put a ref for another target on the render element itself.

Use `nativeButton={false}` when the rendered action is not a native button; it receives button semantics and Enter/Space activation. `className` and `style` also accept callbacks with Base UI's `{ disabled }` state, including while loading.

Navigation is a [LinkButton](?path=/docs/components-linkbutton--docs): an anchor, or the application's router Link through `render`, with Button's variants, sizes, icon slots and insets. Do not render a link through Button's `render`: [Base UI Button enforces button semantics](https://base-ui.com/react/components/button#rendering-links-as-buttons), logs an error for an anchor, and `nativeButton={false}` would give the link `role="button"`.

```tsx
<LinkButton variant="primary" render={<Link to="/requirements" />}>
  View requirements
</LinkButton>
```

`buttonVariants` is the lower-level recipe LinkButton uses. It accepts `variant`, `size`, `isSelected`, `isFullWidth` and `className`, and supplies classes without adding ARIA, icon insets or disabled behavior; reach for it only where a part cannot take LinkButton.

_Example: story `Stories.AsLink`._

## Accessibility

- Tab reaches an enabled button. Enter and Space activate it; the focus outline appears on keyboard focus.
- Disabled buttons are skipped by Tab by default. For an action that cannot run, `disabledReason` keeps it focusable with `aria-disabled` and gives it the reason as its description; for form validation, keep the submit action available so the form can report errors.
- Loading blocks click, Enter and Space activation, including handlers on the rendered action. It keeps the accessible name and the width stable, and `loadingLabel` is announced when it starts.
- A button that is unavailable but stays focusable (loading, `disabledReason` or `focusableWhenDisabled`) blocks activation only: Escape still reaches the panel, side nav or dialog around it.
- In forced colours a primary, secondary or danger button keeps a ButtonText edge, a selected one is Highlight, and the spinner takes the text colour.
- Use [IconButton](?path=/docs/components-iconbutton--docs) for an icon only action with a required accessible label, and [Toggle](?path=/docs/components-toggle--docs) for an on/off control.
- `variant="link"` is as tall as its text. Where any pointer is coarse it takes an invisible hit area of at least 24px, centred on it, so nothing around it moves.

_Example: story `Stories.OnTouch`._

## Props

_Props of `Button`, generated from its types:_

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `focusableWhenDisabled` | `boolean` | `false` | Whether the button should be focusable when disabled. |
| `nativeButton` | `boolean` | `true` | Whether the component renders a native `<button>` element when replacing it via the `render` prop. Set to `false` if the rendered element is not a button (for example, `<div>`). |
| `className` | `string \| ((state: ButtonState) => string)` |  | CSS class applied to the element, or a function that returns a class based on the component's state. |
| `render` | `ReactElement<unknown, string \| JSXElementConstructor<any>> \| ComponentRenderFn<HTMLProps, ButtonState>` |  | Allows you to replace the component's HTML element with a different tag, or compose it with another component. Accepts a `ReactElement` or a function that returns the element to render. |
| `style` | `CSSProperties \| ((state: ButtonState) => CSSProperties)` |  | Style applied to the element, or a function that returns a style object based on the component's state. |
| `variant` | `"danger" \| "link" \| "primary" \| "secondary" \| "subtle"` | `secondary` | Secondary is the default; primary emphasizes the main action. |
| `size` | `"medium" \| "small" \| "xsmall"` | `medium` | Medium is 32px, small 28px and xsmall 24px. `variant="link"` ignores it: a link-styled action is as tall as its text. |
| `isSelected` | `boolean` |  | Paint the selected state and, on Button, set aria-pressed. |
| `isFullWidth` | `boolean` |  | Fill the available width. |
| `iconBefore` | `ReactElement<unknown, string \| JSXElementConstructor<any>>` |  | Decorative leading icon, replaced by a spinner while loading. |
| `iconAfter` | `ReactElement<unknown, string \| JSXElementConstructor<any>>` |  | Decorative trailing icon. |
| `isLoading` | `boolean` |  | Block activation and show a spinner while keeping focus unless explicitly disabled. The button keeps its width and its name: the spinner takes the leading icon's place, else the trailing icon's, else it sits over the label, which keeps its space. |
| `loadingLabel` | `string` |  | What the pending work is, said once through the page's polite live region when loading starts, such as "Saving requirement revision". `aria-busy` alone is not announced by the major screen readers. Leave it out when something else on the page already says it. |
| `disabledReason` | `string` |  | Why the action is unavailable, for an action that truly cannot run. The button is disabled but stays in the tab order with `aria-disabled`, so the reader can reach it and learn why: the reason shows in a tooltip on hover, on keyboard focus and on a tap, and is the button's accessible description. It disables the button by itself and keeps it focusable even with `disabled`. An empty string is no reason. Prefer an enabled action that explains on use, such as a submit that reports what is missing. |
| `truncate` | `boolean` |  | For a slot narrower than the label, such as a rail, a card's footer or a table cell: the button narrows to its container and cuts the label with an ellipsis, its icons whole. The whole label stays the accessible name and shows in a tooltip on hover and keyboard focus while it is cut. Write labels short enough not to need it; this is for the slot that cannot grow. |

_Example: story `Stories.Playground`._

_Rendered in the Storybook: Controls._

[IconButton](?path=/docs/components-iconbutton--docs) · [LinkButton](?path=/docs/components-linkbutton--docs) · [CopyButton](?path=/docs/components-copybutton--docs) · [ButtonGroup](?path=/docs/components-buttongroup--docs) · [TextLink](?path=/docs/components-textlink--docs) · [DropdownMenu](?path=/docs/components-dropdownmenu--docs) · [AlertDialog](?path=/docs/components-alertdialog--docs) · [Forms](?path=/docs/patterns-forms--docs)

## Don't

A region has one primary, named for what happens, never two primaries or an OK. The visible words are the Button's name: an `aria-label` that replaces them leaves a speech-input reader saying words that do nothing, so context goes in a description.

_Example: story `Stories.Dont`._

<!-- page: Components/ButtonGroup (src/stories/components/ButtonGroup.mdx) -->

# ButtonGroup

**Status: Stable.**

Join related actions, split buttons or controls. Each child keeps its own behavior and accessible name.

## When to use it

- **Actions that belong together**, joined into one control: Export and Print, a zoom's out and in.
- **A split action**: the primary action, then an icon menu of the other ways to do it ("Create system", then "More ways to create a system").
- **A field and the action it takes**: a number of days and Save.

Not for one choice among several: a ButtonGroup adds no selection, so that is a [ToggleGroup](?path=/docs/components-togglegroup--docs), whose pressed item says which is chosen. Not for a row of unrelated actions: that is a toolbar or an `Inline`. Not for a list of actions that do not all earn a button: that is a [DropdownMenu](?path=/docs/components-dropdownmenu--docs).

_Example: story `Stories.DoDont`._

## Content

- Each button is a verb ("Export", "Print"), or an IconButton whose `label` names its action ("Zoom out").
- The group's `aria-label` names the set ("Export", "Zoom"), or `aria-labelledby` points at a visible name.
- A split action's menu button is named for what it opens: "More ways to create a system".
- ButtonGroupText is a label or a value beside the buttons ("110%" between Zoom out and Zoom in), at their `size`.

## Anatomy

```tsx
<ButtonGroup aria-label="Export">
  <Button>Export</Button>
  <ButtonGroupSeparator isDecorative />
  <Button>Print</Button>
</ButtonGroup>
```

ButtonGroup joins the outer corners of children with `data-slot` attributes. ButtonGroupText adds a label, value or prefix. ButtonGroupSeparator adds a visible rule. Nested groups may separate related sets of actions.

_Example: story `Stories.Composition`._

## Variants and states

`orientation` accepts `horizontal` (default) or `vertical`. Horizontal joins use logical edges in RTL. Child controls choose their size, disabled state and loading behavior. Give ButtonGroupText the same `size` as the buttons beside it, `xsmall`, `small` or `medium` (the default, as on Button): it is never shorter than they are, so a vertical group's text keeps their height, and its content is centred. The separator's orientation describes its own line; use a horizontal separator between vertically stacked controls.

_Example: story `Stories.Orientations`._

A split primary is one control: the primary action, a ButtonGroupSeparator, and an IconButton with `variant="primary"` that opens the other ways to do it. Beside a primary half the separator draws the bold border (`color.border.bold`), so the two halves read as one button rather than two with a light seam between them, in both modes; forced colours draw it in the system's border colour.

_Example: story `Stories.SplitPrimary`._

## Accessibility

Name the group with `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`. Each enabled control remains in the normal tab order. A group does not add arrow-key navigation or selection behavior. Use ToggleGroup for a selection among options. Decorative separators may use `isDecorative`.

ButtonGroupText supports Base UI `render`, including a native label with `htmlFor`. Rendered elements must accept merged attributes, events and refs.

## Props

_Props of `ButtonGroup`, generated from its types:_

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `orientation` | `"horizontal" \| "vertical" \| null` | `horizontal` |  |

_Props of `ButtonGroupText`, generated from its types:_

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `render` | `ReactElement<unknown, string \| JSXElementConstructor<any>> \| ComponentRenderFn<HTMLProps, {}>` |  | Allows you to replace the component's HTML element with a different tag, or compose it with another component. Accepts a `ReactElement` or a function that returns the element to render. |
| `size` | `"medium" \| "small" \| "xsmall"` | `medium` | The size of the controls beside it, so the text is never shorter than they are: `medium` 32px (the default, as on Button), `small` 28px or `xsmall` 24px. In a vertical group, where it would otherwise be only as tall as its words, it takes the controls' height. |

_Props of `ButtonGroupSeparator`, generated from its types:_

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `orientation` | `"horizontal" \| "vertical"` | `vertical` | The orientation of the separator. |
| `className` | `string \| ((state: SeparatorState) => string)` |  | CSS class applied to the element, or a function that returns a class based on the component's state. |
| `render` | `ReactElement<unknown, string \| JSXElementConstructor<any>> \| ComponentRenderFn<HTMLProps, SeparatorState>` |  | Allows you to replace the component's HTML element with a different tag, or compose it with another component. Accepts a `ReactElement` or a function that returns the element to render. |
| `style` | `CSSProperties \| ((state: SeparatorState) => CSSProperties)` |  | Style applied to the element, or a function that returns a style object based on the component's state. |
| `isDecorative` | `boolean` |  | Hide a purely visual rule from assistive technology. Native role and ARIA props can override these defaults. |

The root forwards native div attributes and refs. Text uses Base UI useRender/mergeProps; Separator uses the existing Base UI Separator. `buttonGroupVariants` exports the same orientation classes for composition.

# Calendar

**Status: Stable.**

A month to pick a day, several days or a range from, following [shadcn’s Calendar](https://ui.shadcn.com/docs/components/base/calendar) on React DayPicker, with Ledger tokens and the LedgerProvider's locale.

Use it inside a picker. A day in a form is a [DatePicker](?path=/docs/components-datepicker--docs), a range a [DateRangePicker](?path=/docs/components-daterangepicker--docs); an inline month takes the room of six fields for one answer. Use Calendar on its own where the month is the content, such as a schedule panel.

_Example: story `Stories.DoDont`._

```tsx
const [date, setDate] = useState<Date>();
<Calendar mode="single" selected={date} onSelect={setDate} />;
```

Calendar takes DayPicker's own props: `mode` (single, multiple or range), `selected` and `onSelect`, disabled matchers, `startMonth` and `endMonth`, `numberOfMonths`, `captionLayout="dropdown"`, `showWeekNumber`. Custom `components`, `formatters`, `labels` and `classNames` merge with Calendar's defaults; customize a day with the exported CalendarDayButton so DayPicker's focus, selection and events stay intact. `buttonVariant` sets the navigation buttons. Days are 32px cells, above the 24px touch minimum.

_Example: story `Stories.Single`._

## Days and zones

Calendar's Dates stand for calendar days: the local year, month and day, never an instant. They are labelled with `formatCalendarDate`, so a provider's `timeZone` never moves a day. Today is the reader's own day.

## Locale

Under a LedgerProvider the month speaks its locale: `lang` on the root, the first day of the week (Monday in de-DE, Saturday in ar-EG, Sunday in en-US), the caption, weekday names and their spoken names (the short form heads each column, or the narrow one where the short names are whole words, as in Arabic, and the full name is always the spoken one), the day digits, the year dropdown and week numbers. A caller's own date-fns `locale`, `weekStartsOn`, `lang`, `labels` and `formatters` win. Two calendars on one page name their navigation apart through `labels.labelNav`, or the navigation landmark repeats.

_Example: story `Stories.Localized`._

## Ranges

With `mode="range"` the first and last days are the blue budget and the days between take the selected tint; `numberOfMonths={2}` spans a range across months. Below the `sm` window the months always stack; above it the calendar's own space decides, so a range in a 320px panel stacks on a wide screen. The range's ends say which end they are ("Start of range", "End of range") and a completed range is announced once, politely: "September 7, 2026 to October 9, 2026 selected", or "September 7, 2026 selected" for a one-day range.

_Example: story `Stories.CalendarRange`._
_Example: story `Stories.InANarrowPanel`._
_Example: story `Stories.RangeInAPopover`._

## Disabled days

A disabled matcher makes a day unchoosable and skips it in the keyboard order. `describeDay(date, modifiers)` adds the reason to its name ("Weekends are closed."), after the kit's date, today, selected and range words. Keep the rule in the field's hint too; DatePicker and DateRangePicker do both from `min`, `max` and `isDateUnavailable`.

_Example: story `Stories.DisabledDayReasons`._
_Example: story `Stories.DropdownsAndWeekNumbers`._

## Navigation

`navLayout="around"` places Previous beside the first month's caption and Next beside the last, in either direction. The default and `"after"` share one navigation bar; `"after"` puts it later in the keyboard order.

_Example: story `Stories.NavigationLayouts`._

## Content

- **Name a month that stands alone by its task**: a visible heading over it, or an `aria-label` such as "Review days", never "Calendar". In a DatePicker the month's dialog takes the field's label.
- **A disabled day says why** in a sentence through `describeDay` ("Weekends are closed."), and the field's hint states the same rule, since the reader meets the hint before the month.
- **Two months on one page name their navigation apart** through `labels.labelNav` ("Review window navigation").
- **Leave the caption and the weekday names to the locale.** A `formatters` override wins over the LedgerProvider, so one that writes English words stays English under every locale.

## Accessibility

- DayPicker owns the grid keyboard: arrows by day and week, Page Up and Page Down by month, Shift with them by year, Home and End by week, one tab stop. The day button takes focus when DayPicker marks it focused.
- Every day's name is the full date in the locale, with today, selected or its range end, and any reason from `describeDay`.
- Selection is shown by fill and survives forced colours: the selected day and the range keep their own colours there.
- Give a standalone Calendar a visible heading or an accessible name.

## Props

_Props of `Calendar`, generated from its types:_

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `buttonVariant` | `"danger" \| "link" \| "primary" \| "secondary" \| "subtle"` | `subtle` |  |
| `describeDay` | `((date: Date, modifiers: Modifiers) => string)` |  | More words for a day's accessible name, after the kit's date, today, selected and range words: why a disabled day is not available ("Weekends are closed"), what a marked day holds. Return undefined to add nothing. Keep the rule itself in the field's hint as well, where everyone reads it. |

_Props: generated from `CalendarDayButton`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._

## Related

[DatePicker](?path=/docs/components-datepicker--docs) · [DateRangePicker](?path=/docs/components-daterangepicker--docs) · [Popover](?path=/docs/components-popover--docs) · [Dialog](?path=/docs/components-dialog--docs)

<!-- page: Components/Card (src/stories/components/Card.mdx) -->

# Card

**Status: Stable.**

A raised container for a table, chart, form or set of facts. Compose its header, content and footer as needed. A card whose whole purpose is to open one record or register is a linked card: its title's link stretches over it.

## When to use it

- **A block that stands beside others**: a chart, a short table, a small form or a set of facts among other cards, on a dashboard, in a grid or in a rail.
- **A whole card that opens one record or register**: a linked card, whose title's link covers it.

Not for a titled block of a page's own body: that is a [Section](?path=/docs/layout-section--docs), a heading over its content on the page. Not for a register that is the page: its [DataTable](?path=/docs/patterns-data-table--docs) has no frame and fills the window. Not for a headline count: that is a linked [Stat.Tile](?path=/docs/components-stat--docs). Not for related records that carry their own actions: that is [Related](?path=/docs/patterns-related--docs), whose titles link and whose actions sit apart. Not for one fact: that is a [KeyValue](?path=/docs/components-keyvalue--docs).

## Content

- The title names what the card holds, as a noun: "Evidence", "Open findings by family". A linked card's title is the destination's name, since it names the link.
- The description adds what the title cannot, a count or a scope: "Three linked artifacts".
- One action in CardAction, a verb and its object ("Add evidence"); a linked card has none.
- The content is the card's one job. A card that needs a second heading inside it is two cards, or a page.

## Anatomy

```tsx
<Card>
  <CardHeader>
    <CardTitle>
      <h2>Evidence</h2>
    </CardTitle>
    <CardDescription>Three linked artifacts</CardDescription>
    <CardAction>
      <Button size="small">Add evidence</Button>
    </CardAction>
  </CardHeader>
  <CardContent>Assessment details</CardContent>
  <CardFooter className="border-t">
    <Button>Save</Button>
  </CardFooter>
</Card>
```

CardHeader arranges the title, description and optional action, and keeps the title's readable measure beside the action, as Section.Header does: 12rem, about twenty-five characters a line, or the title's own width when that is shorter. The action sits at the end of the title's row while the header holds that measure and the action side by side, and has 16rem inside its inset, that is while the card is about 18rem wide or more (about 17.5rem at `size="small"`), as a full-width card on a 340px phone is. Otherwise, in a rail, in a full-width card on a 320px phone, or beside an action too wide for the measure, it takes its own row after the description, at the end, so the title keeps the full width and never breaks mid-word. The header reads its own width and the action's, not the window's, so a card that is resized follows. CardContent supplies the horizontal inset. CardFooter holds actions or secondary content. The root supplies vertical padding and spacing between parts, and records its raised surface so sticky table headers remain opaque.

Headers and footers are undivided by default. Add `className="border-b"` to CardHeader or `className="border-t"` to CardFooter when a rule separates distinct work areas; the part adds padding beside that rule. Form titles usually need spacing only, while a footer with submission actions can earn a divider.

_Example: story `Stories.Playground`._

## Variants and states

`size="medium"`, the default, uses Ledger's standard inset; `size="small"` reduces the inset and gaps, for a rail or a grid of cards. `default` and `sm` are the deprecated spellings of `medium` and `small`, kept for one version, and render the same. Tables and charts that own their spacing can sit directly inside Card. For a table flush against a divided header and the bottom edge, use `className="gap-0 pb-0"` on Card and `className="border-b"` on CardHeader. Loading, empty and error behavior belongs to the content.

_Example: story `Stories.Sizes`._
_Example: story `Stories.EdgeToEdge`._
_Example: story `Stories.InARail`._
_Example: story `Stories.BesideAWideAction`._

### A linked card

`link` on CardTitle takes a link element (a router's Link, or `<a href>`) and makes the title's text that link, stretched over the card: a click anywhere on the card opens it, the card takes `elevation.surface.raised.hovered` under the pointer and `elevation.surface.raised.pressed` while pressed, the title underlines, and the focus ring is drawn inside the card's edge, where its clipping cannot cut it. A linked card holds no other control: no CardAction, no button or link in its content, because a card that carries its own actions cannot also be one click target. For a card with actions, keep the title a link and the actions separate, as [Related](?path=/docs/patterns-related--docs) cards do. For a headline count, use a linked [Stat.Tile](?path=/docs/components-stat--docs).

_Example: story `Stories.Linked`._

A button inside a linked card sits under the title's link, so a press on it opens the card's destination instead.

_Example: story `Stories.DoDont`._

## Accessibility

Every part is a native div by default. CardTitle does not choose a heading level: set it with `render={<h2 />}` (or h3, one below the heading the card sits under), or compose a heading inside it. Name a region with `role="region"` and `aria-labelledby` when a landmark is useful. Links and buttons inside the card keep their own semantics and focus.

A linked card's link is named by its title alone, and it is the card's one Tab stop. Keep the title the heading and the link inside it (`render={<h3 />}` with `link`), so a heading list and a link list both find the card.

## Props

_Props of `Card`, generated from its types:_

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `size` | `"default" \| "medium" \| "sm" \| "small"` | `medium` | `medium`, Ledger's standard inset, by default; `small` reduces the inset and the space between parts for a rail or a grid of cards. `default` and `sm` are the deprecated spellings of `medium` and `small`. |

_Props: generated from `CardHeader`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._

_Props of `CardTitle`, generated from its types:_

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `render` | `ReactElement<unknown, string \| JSXElementConstructor<any>> \| ComponentRenderFn<HTMLProps, {}>` |  | Allows you to replace the component's HTML element with a different tag, or compose it with another component. Accepts a `ReactElement` or a function that returns the element to render. |
| `link` | `ReactElement<{ className?: string; children?: ReactNode; }, string \| JSXElementConstructor<any>>` |  | A link element (a router's Link, or `<a href>`) that becomes the title's text and stretches over the card, so a click anywhere on the card opens it. The link's name is the title. A linked card holds no other control: leave CardAction out, and put nothing that takes a click or focus in its content. |

_Props: generated from `CardDescription`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._
_Props: generated from `CardAction`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._
_Props: generated from `CardContent`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._
_Props: generated from `CardFooter`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._

Every part accepts native div props and refs, and names itself last with `data-slot` (`card`, `card-header`, `card-title`, `card-description`, `card-action`, `card-content`, `card-footer`; a title's link is `card-link`). Root `style` overrides merge with the raised-surface default. CardTitle takes `render` for its element, as Section.Title does, and `link`, which keeps the supplied link's own props, ref and handlers.

## Related

[Section](?path=/docs/layout-section--docs), [Table](?path=/docs/components-table--docs), [Empty](?path=/docs/components-empty--docs), [Related](?path=/docs/patterns-related--docs), [Upgrading](?path=/docs/guidance-upgrading--docs#card).

<!-- page: Components/Checkbox (src/stories/components/Checkbox.mdx) -->

# Checkbox

**Status: Stable.**

An independent yes or no, on the shadcn Base UI root and indicator. The 16px box draws the tick or the mixed-state dash; the label and hint come from a horizontal [Field](?path=/docs/components-field--docs), which ties them to the box with no ids and aligns the box with the label's first line.

```tsx
<Field orientation="horizontal">
  <Checkbox name="pii" value="yes" defaultChecked />
  <FieldContent>
    <FieldLabel>Handles PII</FieldLabel>
    <FieldDescription>The package includes records about a person.</FieldDescription>
  </FieldContent>
</Field>
```

_Example: story `Stories.CheckboxMatrix`._

## When to use it

- **Use a Checkbox** for a choice that stands on its own and waits for the form's primary: include this family, handles PII, I have reviewed the evidence.
- **Several related choices** are a [CheckboxGroup](?path=/docs/components-checkboxgroup--docs) under one legend.
- **Not for one answer from two or more options.** "Accept" or "Not applicable" is a [RadioGroup](?path=/docs/components-radiogroup--docs); two boxes that untick each other are announced as two independent choices and ignore the arrow keys.
- **Not for a setting that applies the moment it changes.** That is a [Switch](?path=/docs/components-switch--docs).
- **Not for a fact.** A ticked, disabled box reads as a choice someone made. A value the reader cannot change is a labelled property ([KeyValue](?path=/docs/components-keyvalue--docs)), or a read-only box with a hint that says why.

The [Forms](?path=/docs/patterns-forms--docs) page has the table of which control answers which question.

## Selection and mixed state

Use boolean `checked` with `onCheckedChange(checked, details)`, or `defaultChecked` for local state. `details.cancel()` rejects a change. `disabled` prevents interaction and removes the box from the tab order; `readOnly` keeps it focusable without allowing changes.

Mixed state uses a separate boolean `indeterminate` prop. [Table.Selection](?path=/docs/components-table--docs) derives it from the rows it selects. For a list of choices with select-all, use a [CheckboxGroup](?path=/docs/components-checkboxgroup--docs): it owns the ticked values and its CheckboxGroupSelectAll derives the checked and mixed states.

_Example: story `Stories.Parent`._

## Read-only

A read-only box keeps its answer and its Tab stop but not the brand fill or the hover: a sunken box with a dashed edge, the tick in the text colour. Give it a FieldDescription that says why it cannot change ("Set by the system categorization."): the hint describes the box, so a reader who reaches it hears the reason. Prefer this to `disabled` whenever the reason must stay reachable, since a disabled box leaves the tab order and takes its reason with it.

_Example: story `Stories.ReadOnly`._

## Choice cards

When each option needs a title and a line of explanation, wrap a horizontal Field in a FieldLabel: a press anywhere on the card chooses, the card shows hover, the chosen state and the one keyboard focus ring, and a disabled card keeps a quiet surface. Put the title in a FieldTitle, which names the box on its own, and the explanation in a FieldDescription, which describes it once.

```tsx
<FieldLabel>
  <Field orientation="horizontal">
    <Checkbox value="second-review" />
    <FieldContent>
      <FieldTitle>Require a second reviewer</FieldTitle>
      <FieldDescription>A colleague confirms the determination.</FieldDescription>
    </FieldContent>
  </Field>
</FieldLabel>
```

_Example: story `Stories.ChoiceCard`._

A card often needs more than its title:

- **Facts that tell the options apart** (a kind, a version, a size) follow the title in the FieldDescription: a [Badge](?path=/docs/components-badge--docs) for a kind, then the plain facts, "Version 5 · 287 of 1,196 catalog controls". They describe the box; the title alone names it.
- **A link to the option's own record** sits beside the card, in an Inline with the card in a `grow="fill"` Stack, never inside it: inside the label a link is a second control in the card's hit area, and its words would join the box's name. Give it `newTab` where following it would leave a draft.
- **An error that belongs to one option** is a FieldError in that card's FieldContent, under the facts, with `invalid` on its Field: it describes that box alone and edges the card in danger, chosen or not. An error about the whole choice (none chosen, too many) goes after the group, on the group's Field.

_Example: story `Stories.ChoiceCardDetails`._

## Labels, Field and forms

In a Field the FieldLabel names the box and toggles it when clicked, the FieldDescription and FieldError describe it, and the Field's `invalid`, `required` and `disabled` reach it; nothing needs an id. Outside a Field, a wrapping label or a sibling label with `htmlFor` and the checkbox's `id` names it, and `aria-describedby` links supporting text; the box is inline, so a plain label keeps its text on the box's line. Use `aria-label` only for a box with no visible label: inside a wrapping label an `aria-label` is added to the label's text, not put in its place. Requiring a CheckboxGroup does not require every box. Native `required` on the box is a browser and Base UI constraint; the Field's `required` only announces and marks.

_Example: story `Stories.InAPlainLabel`._

`name`, `value` and `form` control native submission. A checked checkbox submits its value (or `on` when omitted); an unchecked checkbox is omitted unless `uncheckedValue` is supplied. Native form reset is caller-owned in Base UI 1.7: restore controlled `checked` state in `onReset`.

_Example: story `Stories.InField`._

## Content

- **Name the choice, not its state.** The label stays the same ticked and unticked: "Seed AC-2 on the payments platform", never a label that flips between "Will seed" and "Excluded", and "Complete: Rotate the signing keys", never "Reopen: …" once ticked. The box shows the state; a status beside it can repeat it.
- **Say what ticking does**, in the positive: "Notify the owner", not "Do not notify the owner".
- **Do not disable a box to show a fact** (see When to use it).

A label that flips with the state ("Excluded", then "Will seed") reports the state and never names the choice.

_Example: story `Stories.DoDont`._

## Accessibility

- The box's boundary is `color.border.bold`, 3:1 against every surface, so an unticked box can be found (WCAG 1.4.11); text fields keep their lighter `color.border.input`, which increased contrast raises.
- Invalid is the danger border. The keyboard focus outline stays the focus colour on an invalid box, so focus is visible while the reader moves through a list of errors.
- A FieldSet's `disabled` disables the boxes inside it, which a native `<fieldset disabled>` alone does not.
- In forced colours the box keeps its boundary and the tick in system colours.

_Example: story `Stories.InvalidAndFocused`._
_Example: story `Stories.Boundary`._

## Native props and keyboard

The default root is a span with `role="checkbox"`, plus a hidden input. `ref` targets the visible control; `inputRef` and `id` target the input. For a native button root, use `nativeButton` with `render={<button />}`; `id` then belongs to that button. The render element's props, classes, styles, handlers and refs are merged. `className` and `style` accept Base UI state callbacks.

Each enabled checkbox is a Tab stop. Space toggles it. Enter does not toggle it; inside a form it activates the default submitter. Mixed state is announced as `aria-checked="mixed"` and drawn with a dash.

## Props

_Props of `Checkbox`, generated from its types:_

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | `string` |  | The id of the input element. |
| `name` | `string` | `undefined` | Identifies the field when a form is submitted. |
| `form` | `string` |  | Identifies the form that owns the hidden input. Useful when the checkbox is rendered outside the form. |
| `checked` | `boolean` | `undefined` | Whether the checkbox is currently ticked. To render an uncontrolled checkbox, use the `defaultChecked` prop instead. |
| `defaultChecked` | `boolean` | `false` | Whether the checkbox is initially ticked. To render a controlled checkbox, use the `checked` prop instead. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | Whether the component should ignore user interaction. |
| `onCheckedChange` | `((checked: boolean, eventDetails: { reason: "none"; event: Event; cancel: () => void; allowPropagation: () => void; isCanceled: boolean; isPropagationAllowed: boolean; trigger: Element; }) => void)` |  | Event handler called when the checkbox is ticked or unticked. |
| `readOnly` | `boolean` | `false` | Whether the user should be unable to tick or untick the checkbox. |

| `nativeButton` | `boolean` | `true` | Whether the component renders a native `<button>` element when replacing it via the `render` prop. Set to `false` if the rendered element is not a button (for example, `<div>`). |

| `style` | `CSSProperties \| ((state: CheckboxRootState) => CSSProperties)` |  | Style applied to the element, or a function that returns a style object based on the component's state. |

Accepts a `ReactElement` or a function that returns the element to render. |

<!-- page: Components/CheckboxGroup (src/stories/components/CheckboxGroup.mdx) -->

# CheckboxGroup

**Status: Stable.**

Several choices that can each be true, under one legend. It is Base UI's CheckboxGroup rendered as a FieldSet: it owns the ticked values, names the group by its FieldLegend, and with `allValues` drives a select-all box.

```tsx
<CheckboxGroup defaultValue={["ac"]} allValues={["ac", "au", "cm"]}>
  <FieldLegend variant="label">Control families</FieldLegend>
  <CheckboxGroupSelectAll>Every family</CheckboxGroupSelectAll>
  <Field orientation="horizontal">
    <Checkbox value="ac" name="families" />
    <FieldLabel>AC · Access control</FieldLabel>
  </Field>
  {/* … one horizontal Field per family */}
</CheckboxGroup>
```

_Example: story `Stories.Playground`._

## When to use it

- **Several independent answers** to one question: the channels to notify, the families to include, the parameters that apply.
- **A list with select-all**, where the reader ticks most or all of the items.

Use [RadioGroup](?path=/docs/components-radiogroup--docs) when only one answer can be true, [Checkbox](?path=/docs/components-checkbox--docs) on its own for a single yes or no, a [Switch](?path=/docs/components-switch--docs) for a setting that takes effect at once, and the selection column of a [DataTable](?path=/docs/patterns-data-table--docs) or a [PickerSheet](?path=/docs/patterns-pickersheet--docs) for choosing records from a long list.

_Example: story `Stories.DoDont`._

## Values and select-all

The group owns the ticked values as an array of the checkboxes' `value`s: `defaultValue` for local state, or `value` and `onValueChange(value, details)` when the form holds it; `details.cancel()` rejects a change. Each Checkbox takes a `value`, and a `name` for native submission, so `FormData.getAll(name)` returns the ticked values.

`CheckboxGroupSelectAll` needs `allValues`, the value of every checkbox in the group. It is ticked when all are, mixed (`aria-checked="mixed"`, drawn with a dash) when some are, and a press ticks them all or clears them. Its label defaults to the locale's "Select all"; pass children to name what it selects. A disabled checkbox keeps its state when select-all changes the rest.

_Example: story `Stories.DefaultSelectAll`._

## In a form

A CheckboxGroup inside a Field takes the Field's hint and error and its `invalid` state, which marks every box; a required Field shows the asterisk on the legend and requires the group, not each box. No checkbox announces that requirement and a group cannot, so the legend adds the locale's "(required)" for assistive technology, hidden on screen. The form checks "at least one" itself. Put the FieldDescription and FieldError inside the group, after the legend.

_Example: story `Stories.InField`._

`disabled` reaches every box, the select-all box included, and so does the `disabled` of a FieldSet or a Field around the group.

_Example: story `Stories.Disabled`._

## Accessibility

- The group is a `fieldset`, named by its FieldLegend. Start the children with the legend. In a required Field the name ends in "(required)".
- Each box is its own Tab stop; Space ticks it. Give each one its own label: a horizontal Field with a FieldLabel needs no ids.
- A hint or an error describes the group and each box in it.

## Props

_Props of `CheckboxGroup`, generated from its types:_

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `className` | `string \| ((state: CheckboxGroupState) => string)` |  | CSS class applied to the element, or a function that returns a class based on the component's state. |
| `defaultValue` | `string[]` |  | Names of the checkboxes in the group that should be initially ticked. To render a controlled checkbox group, use the `value` prop instead. |
| `style` | `CSSProperties \| ((state: CheckboxGroupState) => CSSProperties)` |  | Style applied to the element, or a function that returns a style object based on the component's state. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | Whether the component should ignore user interaction. Disables every checkbox in the group. An ancestor FieldSet's `disabled` also reaches it. |
| `value` | `string[]` |  | Names of the checkboxes in the group that should be ticked. To render an uncontrolled checkbox group, use the `defaultValue` prop instead. |
| `onValueChange` | `((value: string[], eventDetails: { reason: "none"; event: Event; cancel: () => void; allowPropagation: () => void; isCanceled: boolean; isPropagationAllowed: boolean; trigger: Element; }) => void)` |  | Event handler called when a checkbox in the group is ticked or unticked. Provides the new value as an argument. |
| `allValues` | `string[]` |  | Names of all checkboxes in the group. Use this when creating a parent checkbox. The `value` of every checkbox in the group. Needed for a CheckboxGroupSelectAll, which ticks them all and shows mixed while only some are ticked. |
| `ref` | `Ref<HTMLFieldSetElement>` |  |  |

Accepts a `ReactElement` or a function that returns the element to render. |
