# CodeBlock

**Status: Stable.**

Source shown as source: a configuration excerpt, a serialised record, a log, a command the reader will paste. One row per line in the code face, a line-number gutter that stays put when the block scrolls sideways, a cap on the height so a long document scrolls inside the block and not the page, and a Copy when the reader will take the text away. The caller owns highlighting and passes rendered lines, or passes the text as `code` and the block splits it.

It is not a field: a value the reader edits is a [Textarea](?path=/docs/components-textarea--docs). It is not prose: a paragraph is [Text](?path=/docs/primitives-text--docs). A single identifier in a sentence is an [Id](?path=/docs/components-id--docs).

_Example: story `Stories.Code`._

## Anatomy

| Part   | What it is                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| ------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Frame  | A box in `elevation.surface.sunken` with a 1px `color.border` and `radius.medium`. It scrolls both ways inside itself; while it has more than it shows, it is a tab stop so the keyboard can scroll it.                                               |
| Gutter | The line numbers, `color.text.subtlest`, tabular, right-aligned, on a column that sticks to the start edge when the lines scroll sideways, with a 1px rule at its end. `showLineNumbers={false}` leaves it out.                                       |
| Line   | One row per entry of `lines`, or per line of `code`, `space.150` from the gutter, in `font.code`. A string, or the caller's spans.                                                                                                                    |
| Copy   | With `copy`, the kit's [CopyButton](?path=/docs/components-copybutton--docs), icon-only and subtle, at the top end on the block's own surface. The frame is at least as tall as it, and the lines keep room at their end to scroll out from under it. |

## Variants

One. What changes is what the lines are: a string per line, or nodes the caller has coloured, because a kit tokenizer for every format the product meets is not the kit's job. A log or a serialised value is a string, passed as `code`; a highlighted file is its lines, each coloured.

_Example: story `Stories.Highlighted`._

A value that is not a file (a record's JSON, a profile's tailoring rules) takes `code` and `showLineNumbers={false}`: a line number points at nothing in it. With `wrap`, its long values fold.

_Example: story `Stories.Value`._

Not built, and why: a highlighted line (the one a validation error points at, the changed lines of a revision), because no screen asks for it yet; a language picker or a tokenizer. Two versions of a text compared line by line are a [Diff](?path=/docs/components-diff--docs).

## Sizes

One face, `font.code`, at the body size. The block is as wide as its container and as tall as its lines up to `maxHeight`, 560px by default (`dimension.part.codeBlock`); a short excerpt never scrolls. The gutter is as wide as the last line number needs, three digits at least.

## States

| State      | Look                                                                                                                                  |
| ---------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Rest       | The lines, the gutter, the frame.                                                                                                     |
| Focus      | The kit's focus outline on the frame, on keyboard focus, while it scrolls, so a keyboard reader can scroll it.                        |
| Scrolled   | Sideways, the gutter stays and the lines pass under it. Down, the gutter goes with the lines.                                         |
| Copied     | The Copy's icon is a check in `color.icon.success` and its tooltip and a polite status say Copied, for a moment; its name stays Copy. |
| Not copied | When the browser refuses the write, the icon is an alert in `color.icon.danger` and the tooltip and status say Could not copy.        |

_Example: story `Stories.CodeBlockMatrix`._

_Example: story `Stories.OneLineCommand`._

## Modifiers

- **`lines`** or **`code`**: the lines one entry each, or the text as one string split at its line breaks.
- **`start`**: the number of the first line, for an excerpt of a longer file.
- **`showLineNumbers`**: on by default; off for a value that is not a file.
- **`maxHeight`**: pixels before the block scrolls inside itself.
- **`wrap`**: long lines fold at the block's edge. Off by default so code keeps its columns; on for a log or a value with no columns to keep.
- **`copy`**: the text a Copy puts on the clipboard, usually the lines joined. Unsaid, there is no button.
- **`label`**: the block's accessible name, the file or the format. "Code" by default; say which.

_Example: story `Stories.Wrapped`._

_Example: story `Stories.Capped`._

## Content

- **Lines are the source as it is,** indentation included. Do not trim, reflow or re-indent for the page.
- **`label` names the thing:** "control.json", "Ingest log", "Router configuration". Not "Code".
- **`start` is the real line number** when the block is an excerpt, so a reader can find the line in the file.
- **A Copy where the reader will paste:** a command, a configuration, a document. Not on a log they read.
- **Highlighting colours the grammar, in the kit's text colours:** keys in `color.text.brand`, strings subtle, comments subtlest. Never a rainbow.

## Long content

Code keeps its columns: a long line scrolls sideways inside the block, never the page, and the gutter stays. A log, a value or a line with no columns to keep takes `wrap`, which folds long lines at the block's edge and breaks an unbroken token (a hash, a URL) where it must. A long document scrolls down inside the block past `maxHeight`. A CodeBlock never truncates: the reader must be able to read and copy all of it.

## Style

| Element | Token                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Frame   | `elevation.surface.sunken` · 1px `color.border` · `radius.medium` · `space.050` block inside                                                                                                                                          |
| Gutter  | `font.code` · `color.text.subtlest` · tabular · `space.100` inline · 1px `color.border` at its end                                                                                                                                    |
| Line    | `font.code` · `color.text` · `space.150` from the gutter                                                                                                                                                                              |
| Copy    | CopyButton, icon-only, `subtle` `small`, at `space.050` from the top and the end on `elevation.surface.sunken` · the frame at least `dimension.control.large` tall · `space.500` at the lines' end · `color.icon.success` when copied |
| Focus   | The kit's focus outline, `color.border.focused`                                                                                                                                                                                       |

## Accessibility

- **The frame is a group named by `label`**, and a tab stop while it has more than it shows, so a keyboard reader can reach a block that scrolls and move it with the arrows; a block that shows everything takes no stop. A block with a bare "Code" name is a block the screen reader cannot tell from the next one.
- **Line numbers are not selectable,** so a copied selection is the code alone.
- **The Copy is a CopyButton:** named Copy, with the kit's tooltip, and a status region says Copied, or Could not copy when the browser refuses.
- **The gutter is hidden from assistive technology,** so browse mode reads the code, not a line number before every line.
- **Contrast:** the gutter's `color.text.subtlest` passes on the sunken surface in both modes; the caller's highlight colours are the kit's text tokens, which do too.
- **The a11y gate** checks the name, the tab stop and the contrast in the matrix.

## Props

_Props of `CodeBlock`, generated from its types:_

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `lines` | `ReactNode[]` |  | The lines, one entry each: strings, or spans the caller has coloured. |
| `code` | `string` |  | The text as one string, split at its line breaks, in place of `lines`: a serialised record, a log. |
| `start` | `number` | `1` | The number of the first line. 1 by default; the line the excerpt starts at when it is a slice of a file. |
| `showLineNumbers` | `boolean` | `true` | The line-number gutter. On by default; off for a value that is not a file (a record's JSON, a rule), where a line number points at nothing. |
| `maxHeight` | `number` |  | Pixels before the block scrolls inside itself. 560 by default (`dimension.part.codeBlock`); a short excerpt never reaches it. |
| `wrap` | `boolean` | `false` | Long lines wrap at the block's edge instead of scrolling sideways. Off by default, so code keeps its columns; on for logs and long values. |
| `copy` | `string` |  | The text a Copy button puts on the clipboard, usually the lines joined. Unsaid, there is no button. |
| `label` | `string` |  | The block's accessible name: the file, the format. "Code" by default. |

Native div props and a ref reach the outer box, which names itself last with `data-slot="code-block"`.

### Playground

_Example: story `Stories.Playground`._

_Rendered in the Storybook: Controls._

## Related

- [Textarea](?path=/docs/components-textarea--docs): code the reader edits.
- [Id](?path=/docs/components-id--docs): one identifier in running text.
- [Text](?path=/docs/primitives-text--docs): prose.
- [CopyButton](?path=/docs/components-copybutton--docs): the Copy, on its own beside an identifier or a command.
- [ScrollArea](?path=/docs/components-scrollarea--docs): a region that scrolls with the kit's bar; the CodeBlock uses the platform's, so the gutter can stick.

## Don't

Source is shown in a CodeBlock, with its gutter and a Copy where the reader will paste it, never in a read-only Textarea. Prose stays Text, never a sentence set in a code block.

_Example: story `Stories.Dont`._

<!-- page: Components/Collapsible (src/stories/components/Collapsible.mdx) -->

# Collapsible

**Status: Stable.**

One independent disclosure: content the reader opens when they need it. Based on [shadcn’s Base UI source](https://ui.shadcn.com/docs/components/base/collapsible) and [Base UI](https://base-ui.com/react/components/collapsible). Ledger retains its tokens and application layouts.

## Anatomy

`Collapsible` holds the state, `CollapsibleContent` the content that folds, and one of two triggers opens it:

- **`CollapsibleHeader`**, the disclosure header: the trigger inside a heading, the title at the start and a chevron at the end that turns while the content is open, the row tint under the pointer and the focus ring on the keyboard. The tint reaches `space.100` before a title that sits flush with the content under it, so the title lines up with the rows and the tint still reads as a row; the chevron sits `space.100` inside the end. Use it whenever the disclosure has a title: a rail's group, a block of details, a folded list.
- **`CollapsibleTrigger`**, the bare trigger with no heading and no chevron, for a trigger that is something else already (a Button through `render`, a row's own control).

```tsx
<Collapsible>
  <CollapsibleHeader>Provenance</CollapsibleHeader>
  <CollapsibleContent>…</CollapsibleContent>
</Collapsible>
```

_Example: story `Stories.Header`._

Counts and marks are ordinary children of the header: `<CollapsibleHeader>Derivation <Count value={3} /></CollapsibleHeader>`; they are part of the button's name. An action for the block goes after the header in a flex row, where the header grows; never inside it, because a button cannot hold another.

## Heading level

The header's heading takes the contextual level from the nearest [HeadingLevelProvider](?path=/docs/primitives-heading--docs), a titled Section or a panel's body, and is an h3 when nothing sets one, as Accordion's is. Wrap it in a HeadingLevelProvider for another level: `level={2}` for a page's rail, whose groups sit under the h1. The content under the header is not raised a level; a heading inside it goes one below through a HeadingLevelProvider.

_Example: story `Stories.HeaderLevels`._

## When to use it

- **CollapsibleHeader** for a titled block the reader may not need: provenance, counts, derivation, reference notes. On a page, a collapsible [Section](?path=/docs/layout-section--docs) (`isCollapsible`) is the same header with the Section's count, description and action; in a rail of facts, [Inspector.Group](?path=/docs/patterns-inspector--docs).
- **Not** a subtle Button with a chevron as the trigger: it sits outside the outline and its chevron does not turn. **Not** a native `<details>`: its marker and motion are the browser's.
- **Not** for a coordinated set where opening one closes another: that is an [Accordion](?path=/docs/components-accordion--docs). **Not** for a row that discloses more of itself: Item's `isCollapsible` and Table's disclosure column own their chevrons.

## Content

- The header names what is inside, as a noun: "Provenance", "Derivation", "Reference notes"; not "Show more" or "Details" when a more exact word exists.
- A count of what is inside goes in the header as a [Count](?path=/docs/components-count--docs), so the reader knows what opening it shows before they do.
- What the reader needs to act is never only inside a closed block: a warning, a missing prerequisite or an error stays in view.
- The header's words stay the same open and closed; the chevron shows the state.

A warning inside a closed block is read only by someone who opens it: keep it in view above the block.

_Example: story `Stories.DoDont`._

## Variants

_Example: story `Stories.RetainedState`._

_Example: story `Stories.IndependentAndDisabled`._

_Example: story `Stories.SearchableContent`._

## Accessibility

Base UI owns expanded state, trigger/panel association, disabled behavior and keyboard activation: Tab reaches the trigger, Enter and Space toggle it, and focus stays on it. CollapsibleHeader's trigger is a button inside a heading, so the block is in the heading outline and its state is announced ("Provenance, collapsed, button"); the chevron is decoration, turned by the same state rather than by colour. Under reduced motion the chevron turns without moving and the content opens without the fold. Retained closed panels stay hidden and unfocusable. `hiddenUntilFound` lets supported browser find-in-page reveal closed content. Nested disclosures keep independent state, and each folds on its own measured height: a Collapsible inside an open Accordion item eases open instead of snapping to the item's settled height.

_Example: story `Stories.NestedMotion`._

## Props

The parts expose native Base UI props, refs, `render`, state classes and styles, and a cancellable `onOpenChange`. Content uses the measured `--collapsible-panel-height` for Ledger motion, through its own `--ds-collapse-height` so an ancestor disclosure's height never reaches it, and respects reduced motion. It clips only while it folds: settled open, its overflow is visible, so the focus ring of a link or a button at its edge shows whole. CollapsibleHeader passes its props, its ref and `render` to the trigger; its children are the title.

### State selectors

The Root carries `data-open` and `data-closed`; the trigger carries `data-panel-open` while its content is open. Style a trigger's own chevron from the trigger (`group-data-panel-open/…`), not from `data-open`, which the trigger never has, and never from Radix's `data-state`.

Item's disclosure, a collapsible Section, Inspector.Group and DataTable's Metrics are built on the same Base UI Collapsible; a Stepper step's details are a Collapsible placed in it.

# Combobox

**Status: Stable.**

Search for a value and choose it, with shadcn's Base UI Combobox composition. Root owns the selection, filtering, popup state and form serialization. ComboboxInput composes the shared InputGroup with its chevron and clear controls.

```tsx
const frameworks = ["React", "Vue", "Svelte"];

<Field>
  <FieldLabel>Framework</FieldLabel>
  <Combobox items={frameworks}>
    <ComboboxInput placeholder="Choose a framework" />
    <ComboboxContent>
      <ComboboxEmpty>No frameworks found.</ComboboxEmpty>
      <ComboboxList>
        {(item: string) => (
          <ComboboxItem key={item} value={item}>
            {item}
          </ComboboxItem>
        )}
      </ComboboxList>
    </ComboboxContent>
  </Combobox>
</Field>;
```

Root renders no DOM wrapper. Content includes Portal, Positioner and Popup, as wide as the input group (or the `anchor`, such as the chips container). List renders the filtered items inside a [Scroller](?path=/docs/components-scroller--docs): hover arrows at each overflowed edge, and the native scrollbar for a list too long to cross by hovering. Group, Label, Collection and Separator compose categorized results.

_Example: story `Stories.Defaults`._

## When to use it

Use a Combobox when the reader finds the value by typing: records by name or identifier (a person, a system, a control), or any list longer than a dozen options. The choice table under [Forms](?path=/docs/patterns-forms--docs) decides between the choice controls:

- A fixed set of a few known values is a [Select](?path=/docs/components-select--docs), even inside a form full of comboboxes; a Combobox for four priorities makes the reader type where a glance would do.
- Two or three options the reader should compare are a [RadioGroup](?path=/docs/components-radiogroup--docs).
- Choosing many records by their attributes, with a table to compare them, is a [PickerSheet](?path=/docs/patterns-pickersheet--docs); one record from one kind outside a form is a [RecordPicker](?path=/docs/patterns-recordpicker--docs).
- Finding a record to open is the [SearchDialog](?path=/docs/patterns-searchdialog--docs), and running a command is the [CommandPalette](?path=/docs/patterns-commandpalette--docs).

Four priorities in a Combobox make the reader type where a glance would do: they are a Select.

_Example: story `Stories.DoDont`._

## Variants and states

Typing highlights the first match, so Enter chooses it (`autoHighlight` is on; pass `autoHighlight={false}` to leave the highlight to the arrow keys). ComboboxInput's `showTrigger` (on) draws the chevron and `showClear` (off) the clear button; children of ComboboxInput follow them in the input group, for a composition of your own.

_Example: story `Stories.Searchable`._

Group, Label and Separator draw the same section headings and hairlines as the Select's. `description` on ComboboxItem adds a second line that tells similar options apart; it is the option's accessible description, never part of its name, and filtering never reads it. An option that cannot be chosen takes `disabledReason`: it stays reachable with the arrow keys, is announced as unavailable, and shows the reason as its description line, readable on the faded row.

_Example: story `Stories.Groups`._

For multiple selection, use an array value with ComboboxChips, ComboboxValue, ComboboxChip and ComboboxChipsInput. Each chip has a remove button named "Remove" and the chip's words ("Remove React"); `label` on the chip supplies the words when its children are not plain text, and `showRemove={false}` leaves the button to your own ComboboxChipRemove. Use `useComboboxAnchor()` to hang the popup from the whole chips container.

_Example: story `Stories.Multiple`._

## Long lists

A list the reader crosses by typing does not need every option in the page. Two ways, neither a new part:

- `limit` on Root mounts the first matches only. ComboboxStatus with `total` (the number of matches before the cut) says "Showing 50 of 312. Type to narrow the list." while the list shows fewer, and says nothing once every match fits. Filter with your own `filter` function and count with the same one, so the count and the list agree.
- A virtualized list: Root takes `virtualized` and `filteredItems`, ComboboxList is the scroll element (pass its `ref` to the virtualizer), and each ComboboxItem takes its `index`, `aria-setsize` and `aria-posinset`. Scroll the virtualizer to the highlighted index in `onItemHighlighted`. The arrow keys walk the whole set.

_Example: story `Stories.LongList`._

_Example: story `Stories.Virtualized`._

## Loading, failure and more results

Own the query and the request, and pass `filter={null}` when the server filters. Each state is said in the popup, outside the options:

- Loading is a ComboboxStatus message ("Loading people…") with `aria-busy` on ComboboxList; ComboboxEmpty stays empty while the request runs, so a search in progress never reads as no results.
- A failed request says so in ComboboxStatus ("The search could not load people.") with a Try again button under it, which Tab reaches from the input. ComboboxEmpty stays empty: a failure is never "No results".
- A server that returns one page of matches passes its total to ComboboxStatus `total`.

ComboboxStatus is a polite live region, so each of these is announced as it changes.

_Example: story `Stories.AsyncResults`._

_Example: story `Stories.FailedSearch`._

## Content

- The placeholder says the action and the noun: "Choose a framework", "Search people". It never says "Optional" or repeats the label; the Field marks a required field.
- The empty text names what was not found: "No people found.", not "No results".
- Option text is the record's name, with its identifier first where the reader knows records by it ("AC-2 · Account management"). Put the difference between similar options in `description`.

## Accessibility

Inside a [Field](?path=/docs/components-field--docs) the FieldLabel names the input, the chevron and the list, the hint and error describe the input, and the Field's `invalid`, `required` and `disabled` reach it, with no ids. Outside one, give ComboboxInput `aria-labelledby` (the id of its visible label) or `aria-label`; the chevron and the list take the same name. A label joined by `htmlFor` alone names only the input: the chevron is then "Show options" and the list "Options". Root's `required` enables native constraint validation separately.

The chevron is Base UI's trigger: it is not a tab stop, since the arrow keys open the list from the input, so Tab moves from the input to the next field. Typing filters, the arrow keys highlight, Enter chooses, and Escape closes the popup before the surrounding dialog. While the list is open, Base UI hides the rest of the page from assistive technology so a screen reader stays in the combobox.

_Example: story `Stories.BoundInField`._

Opened while its dialog is still arriving, the list takes the field's layout width, not its width in the dialog's entrance scale, so filtering during the entrance resizes nothing.

_Example: story `Stories.InDialog`._

## A searchable trigger

A value that shows as text until the reader edits it (the Editable searched list) puts ComboboxTrigger in the page and ComboboxInput inside the popup, with `showTrigger={false}`. The trigger is then the tab stop and the combobox, and the popup is as wide as the trigger; a style width on Content wins.

```tsx
<Combobox items={people} value={owner} onValueChange={setOwner}>
  <ComboboxTrigger aria-label="Owner">{owner}</ComboboxTrigger>
  <ComboboxContent aria-label="Owner">
    <ComboboxInput aria-label="Owner" placeholder="Search" showTrigger={false} />
    <ComboboxEmpty>No people found.</ComboboxEmpty>
    <ComboboxList>
      {(person: string) => <ComboboxItem value={person}>{person}</ComboboxItem>}
    </ComboboxList>
  </ComboboxContent>
</Combobox>
```

## Props

`ComboboxProps<Value, Multiple>` is the generic Base UI root contract, with Ledger's locale and direction defaults and `autoHighlight` on. Root's `value` is one value or `null`, or an array; `onValueChange(value, details)` supports cancellation. Use `name`, `form`, `inputRef`, serialization and equality callbacks on Root. With Base UI 1.7, reset controlled selections in the owning form's `onReset`. Explicit ids and ARIA on the input and the list win over the Field's.

_Example: story `Stories.NativeForms`._

ComboboxInput forwards native input refs, events, render composition, classes and styles, and takes the control scale's `small` and `medium`. Content forwards popup props plus positioning, `portalContainer` and `keepMounted`. Clear, ChipRemove and Status are flat native parts.

# Command

**Status: Stable.**

A list the reader filters from the keyboard: the parts behind the [CommandPalette](?path=/docs/patterns-commandpalette--docs) and the [RecordPicker](?path=/docs/patterns-recordpicker--docs). Based on [shadcn’s Base UI source](https://ui.shadcn.com/docs/components/base/command) and [cmdk](https://cmdk.paco.me), which does the filtering, the arrow keys and the roles; Ledger draws the rows as a menu's rows and adds what cmdk leaves out: an active descendant that follows the selection, the count spoken as it settles, and an empty sentence that waits while rows load. Finding a record of any type is the [SearchDialog](?path=/docs/patterns-searchdialog--docs), and choosing a value in a form is a [Combobox](?path=/docs/components-combobox--docs).

## When to use it

- **A list the reader filters by typing and acts on from the keyboard**: a palette of commands, a picker of records, each built from these parts.

Not for finding a record of any type across the product: that is the [SearchDialog](?path=/docs/patterns-searchdialog--docs). Not for a value in a form: that is a [Combobox](?path=/docs/components-combobox--docs) or a [Select](?path=/docs/components-select--docs). Not for a short list of actions at a button: that is a [DropdownMenu](?path=/docs/components-dropdownmenu--docs). A CommandDialog is a [Dialog](?path=/docs/components-dialog--docs) at the top of the window; [Overlays](?path=/docs/components-overlays--docs) says how the overlays relate.

## Content

- The input's placeholder says what the list holds and what typing does: "Search commands", "Find a control".
- A row's label is a verb and its object for a command ("Create task", "Go to settings") and the record's name for a record; its shortcut is its keys, drawn by `shortcut`.
- CommandEmpty says what was not found and what to try ("No controls match. Check the code or clear the search.").
- A group heading is a plural noun ("Navigation", "Recent records").

An empty list says what was not found and what to try. "No results" under "Search" does neither.

_Example: story `Stories.DoDont`._

## Anatomy

Compose Command, CommandInput, CommandList, CommandGroup, CommandItem, CommandEmpty, CommandLoading, CommandSeparator, CommandShortcut, CommandFooter and CommandCount, in a CommandDialog or inline.

_Example: story `Stories.Usage`._

| Part            | What it is                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| --------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| CommandInput    | A search icon, the field and a hint at the end: the Escape key by default, which is decoration; `null` for none; a CommandCount for a picker, which the field is then described by.                               |
| CommandList     | The listbox, named "Results" by default (`label`), scrolling inside itself past 340px. While no row shows and nothing loads it holds CommandEmpty's sentence as a plain container, with no role or name.          |
| CommandGroup    | Rows under a heading; the heading goes when every row under it is filtered out.                                                                                                                                   |
| CommandItem     | One row: an icon if the rows are of kinds, the label, and at the end its `shortcut` or other trailing content. The selected row tints as a menu row does and, while the field has focus, draws the focus outline. |
| CommandEmpty    | What the list says when no row shows. `noMatch` says what a query that matches nothing finds, where the children say the list has no rows. It never shows while a CommandLoading does.                            |
| CommandLoading  | The kit's Spinner and "Searching…", beside the list while rows are fetched; give the list `aria-busy` while it shows.                                                                                             |
| CommandShortcut | A shortcut's keys at the end of a row, hidden from assistive technology. CommandItem's `shortcut` draws one.                                                                                                      |
| CommandCount    | "12 matches", in the locale's words and plural rules; `one` and `many` put other words after the number, and a word left out is the locale's.                                                                     |
| CommandFooter   | The keys and what they do, and the count at the end.                                                                                                                                                              |
| CommandDialog   | The list in a Dialog at the top of the window: 80px down, or a tenth of the window's height where that is less, and at most as tall as the space below.                                                           |

## Variants

_Example: story `Stories.Filtering`._

_Example: story `Stories.Palette`._

On short screens the command list scrolls while the search and footer remain visible, and the top inset gives way to a tenth of the window's height, so a landscape phone keeps room for the rows.

_Example: story `Stories.ShortViewport`._

_Example: story `Stories.Loading`._

A search that matches nothing shows CommandEmpty's `noMatch` sentence where the rows were, and the count reads 0.

_Example: story `Stories.NoMatch`._

A picker counts its own kind of row: `one="record"` reads "1 record", and the other count keeps the locale's words.

_Example: story `Stories.CountWords`._

## Accessibility

- **Name it.** Give Command a descriptive `label` (cmdk uses it to name the field), and CommandDialog a `title`. The title defaults to "Command palette" and is then read with "Search for a command to run."; a title of the caller's own is read with its own `description` or none.
- **The active descendant follows the selection.** The field's `aria-activedescendant` names the selected row on open, after every keystroke and after every arrow, and is absent while no row shows, so a screen reader always hears the row Enter would choose.
- **The count is spoken.** Once the query holds still for 600ms, the page's [Announcer](?path=/docs/components-announcer--docs) says "1 match" or the empty sentence. Nothing is said before a query or while a CommandLoading shows.
- **A load is not an empty list.** While CommandLoading shows, CommandEmpty and the spoken count wait.
- **An empty list is not a listbox.** A listbox must hold an option, so while no row shows and nothing loads, CommandList drops its `listbox` role and its name and holds the empty sentence as a plain container. Its id stays, so the field's `aria-controls` still names it, and the listbox returns with the first row. A busy list (`aria-busy`, or a CommandLoading showing) stays a listbox while its rows are on their way.
- **A shortcut is not part of the name.** CommandItem's `shortcut` draws the keys and sets `aria-keyshortcuts`, so the row is "Export report", not "Export report Ctrl E". Give such a row a `value`, since cmdk otherwise matches its text content.
- **The field shows its focus, and so does the row Enter would choose.** The field's row draws the field's focus ring while the field has focus, in a dialog and inline. Focus stays in the field, so the selected row, its active descendant, draws the same outline over its tint while the field has focus and gives it up when focus leaves; the row under the pointer keeps the tint alone.
- **The rest is cmdk's and Base UI's.** cmdk handles filtering, disabled choices, option navigation and selection; Base UI Dialog handles focus, modality and dismissal. CommandSeparator is presentational within the listbox. Item `onSelect` owns the action and any palette closing. When `showCloseButton` is false, compose a DialogClose so touch and screen-reader users have a dismissal control; the palette and record picker make their Escape footer hint a close button.
- **In forced colours** the selected row is Highlight and a disabled row GrayText.

Every word the parts show comes from the locale's messages (`commandPaletteTitle`, `commandMatchOne`, `commandListLabel`, `searching` and the rest), so a localised product reads in one language.

## Props

Command parts forward their native cmdk props and refs. CommandDialog accepts the native generic Dialog root contract plus title, description, className, style, showCloseButton and finalFocus. CommandInput adds `hint`, CommandItem `shortcut` and CommandEmpty `noMatch`. CommandFooter takes its div's props and ref, and CommandCount its span's.

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |

_Props of `CommandDialog`, generated from its types:_

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |

# CopyButton

**Status: Stable.**

Puts a value on the clipboard: an identifier the reader will paste into a ticket, a command, a link, a configuration. It is a [Button](?path=/docs/components-button--docs), or with `label` an [IconButton](?path=/docs/components-iconbutton--docs), that copies `text` and says whether it worked. [CodeBlock](?path=/docs/components-codeblock--docs) uses it for its Copy.

Use it where the reader takes a value away. Do not use it for a value they only read, and do not use it to share a record: a link to the record is a [TextLink](?path=/docs/components-textlink--docs) the reader can copy with the browser.

_Example: story `Stories.Labelled`._

## Two forms

| Form      | How                                              | Where                                                        |
| --------- | ------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Labelled  | Children, “Copy” (the `copy` message) by default | Beside a command or a block, where there is room for a word. |
| Icon-only | `label`, such as “Copy ID”                       | Beside an identifier in a line, a row or a details rail.     |

The two are one prop apart and exclusive: with `label` there are no children. `variant` is `secondary` by default, or `subtle` beside an identifier or inside a block; `primary` is available and rarely right. `size` is `medium` for the labelled form and `small` (28px) for the icon-only one by default.

_Example: story `Stories.IdCopy`._

## What the reader sees

- **Copied.** The icon becomes a check, and “Copied” shows in a tooltip for two seconds, which opens by itself, so a touch reader sees it too. A polite status message says “Copied” to a screen reader.
- **Could not copy.** When the browser refuses the write (no permission, an insecure page, no clipboard), the icon becomes an alert, the tooltip and the status say “Could not copy” for four seconds, and `onCopyError` receives the error. A reader never pastes stale contents thinking they copied.
- **Stable.** The button keeps its name and its width through both. Escape or a tap elsewhere closes the tooltip early.
- **Said again.** A second copy while the first result still shows is a new status message, so a screen reader hears it too.

`onCopied` receives the text once the clipboard holds it; announce anything further there. `onClick` runs first, and calling `preventDefault()` in it skips the copy. The messages are `copy`, `copied` and `copyFailed`, which a `LedgerProvider` can translate.

_Example: story `Stories.CopyFails`._

## Accessibility

- The icon-only form is named by `label`, which is also its tooltip. Name what is copied (“Copy ID”, “Copy record id”) so several copy buttons on one screen can be told apart.
- The result is a status message (WCAG 4.1.3), polite, in a region that is always present; the tooltip and the icon are the visible half. The name never changes, so a voice command keeps working.
- Focus stays on the button through the copy.
- The icon change is a shape, check or alert, not only a colour.

## Props

_Props of `CopyButton`, generated from its types:_

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `className` | `string \| ((state: ButtonState) => string)` |  | CSS class applied to the element, or a function that returns a class based on the component's state. |
| `style` | `CSSProperties \| ((state: ButtonState) => CSSProperties)` |  | Style applied to the element, or a function that returns a style object based on the component's state. |
| `nativeButton` | `boolean` | `true` | Whether the component renders a native `<button>` element when replacing it via the `render` prop. Set to `false` if the rendered element is not a button (for example, `<div>`). |
| `focusableWhenDisabled` | `boolean` | `false` | Whether the button should be focusable when disabled. |
| `isFullWidth` | `boolean` |  | Fill the available width. |
| `loadingLabel` | `string` |  | What the pending work is, said once through the page's polite live region when loading starts, such as "Saving requirement revision". `aria-busy` alone is not announced by the major screen readers. Leave it out when something else on the page already says it. |
| `truncate` | `boolean` |  | For a slot narrower than the label, such as a rail, a card's footer or a table cell: the button narrows to its container and cuts the label with an ellipsis, its icons whole. The whole label stays the accessible name and shows in a tooltip on hover and keyboard focus while it is cut. Write labels short enough not to need it; this is for the slot that cannot grow. |
| `text` (required) | `string` |  | The text put on the clipboard. |
| `variant` | `"primary" \| "secondary" \| "subtle"` | `secondary` | Secondary is the default, as on Button and IconButton; subtle beside an identifier or in a block. |
| `size` | `"medium" \| "small"` |  | Medium (32px) by default for the labelled form, small (28px) for the icon-only form. |
| `onCopied` | `((text: string) => void)` |  | Called with the text once the clipboard holds it. |
| `onCopyError` | `((error: unknown) => void)` |  | Called when the browser refuses the write (no permission, an insecure page, no clipboard). |
| `label` | `string` |  | The icon-only form: the accessible name and the tooltip, such as "Copy ID". Name what is copied when more than one copy sits on the screen. |
| `children` | `ReactNode` |  | The visible label of the labelled form. "Copy" (the `copy` message) by default. |

## Don't

Where a screen has several, each CopyButton names what it copies (Copy ID), never a bare Copy beside every identifier. Copying is secondary or subtle, never a primary that competes with the page's action.

<!-- page: Components/Count (src/stories/components/Count.mdx) -->

# Count

**Status: Stable.**

A number in a pill: unread items, rows in a group, results behind a filter, findings on a control. It sits after the name of what it counts and is named by it. Anything above `max`, 99 by default, renders as `99+`. Not the notification circle on a corner.

_Example: story `Stories.CountMatrix`._

## Anatomy

| Part   | What it is                                                                                                                                                                   |
| ------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Pill   | 20px tall, at least 20px wide, round, `space.075` at each end: the neutral fill or one of four others.                                                                       |
| Number | `font.body.small` medium, tabular, centred, in the reader's locale (1,189; 1.189 in German). Never a word. An added count carries a plus and a removed one a minus (U+2212). |

## Variants

| Appearance  | Use                                                                                           |
| ----------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `default`   | Rows in a group, results behind a filter, items in a section. The neutral fill.               |
| `primary`   | The one count on the screen that must be seen: unread, new since you last looked. Brand fill. |
| `important` | What needs attention now: overdue, blocked. Danger fill.                                      |
| `added`     | Rows a change adds. Success fill, subtle, and a plus: +12.                                    |
| `removed`   | Rows a change removes. Danger fill, subtle, and a minus: −3.                                  |

Not built, and why: a corner placement on an avatar or an icon (a notification circle); the shell's navigation has no unread counts yet, and when it does the Count will sit after the item's label, not on its icon. No count in a tone's text colour without a fill; the number alone is a Stat.

## Sizes

One size, 20px, the height of a small Badge, so the two sit on one line. The width grows with the digits and stops at three and a plus.

## States

A Count has one state. Zero is a number: where the reader asks how many (a Section, a Related card, an Item group, a tab's rows), a 0 says "none" where no pill could mean "not counted", so Section, Related and Item.Group show a Count of 0, and a tab shows 0 once its rows have loaded. A count not yet known is no Count: while the rows load or after they failed, leave it out rather than show 0 or the last number. A Table.Group hides it, since an empty group has no rows to head. A section with nothing in it still says so in words, in its Empty.

_Example: story `Stories.InContext`._

_Example: story `Stories.Locale`._

## Modifiers

- **`value`** as a number, formatted in the reader's locale, or a string shown as given, when the text is not a number the pill should cap ("12 of 40" is not a Count).
- **`max`** for the ceiling: 99 by default, for a count of things to attend to; `max={9999}` for a count of rows, the one ceiling on every tab strip in a product. A Section's, a Related card's and an Item.Group's `count` take the same cap through their `countMax`. 9999 is the most a pill holds; a larger total is a Stat.
- **`appearance`** as in Variants; `default` when unsaid.

## Content

- **A number.** Digits only; the word before it says what they count.
- **Named by its label.** "Findings 3", "Evidence 7": the Count follows the label at `space.100`.
- **Capped, not exact.** Past the ceiling the reader needs the order of magnitude; the exact number is a Stat.
- **Long content.** A Count never truncates and never wraps: it caps at `max`. A number too long for a pill (an amount, a total past 9999) is a Stat or text.

## Style

| Element   | Token                                                                                        |
| --------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Pill      | `dimension.control.xsmall` 20px tall and at least as wide · `radius.full` · `space.075` ends |
| Number    | `font.body.small` medium · tabular                                                           |
| default   | `color.background.neutral` · `color.text.subtle`                                             |
| primary   | `color.background.brand.bold` · `color.text.inverse`                                         |
| important | `color.background.danger.bold` · `color.text.inverse`                                        |
| added     | `color.background.success` · `color.text.success`                                            |
| removed   | `color.background.danger` · `color.text.danger`                                              |

## Accessibility

- **It is text**, read in the flow after its label: "Findings, 3". The label names it; a Count on its own says only a number.
- **`99+` is read as "99 plus"**, which is the meaning.
- **Not colour alone.** An important count sits beside a label that says why; the red ranks it. An added or removed count carries its sign, so a screen reader hears "plus 12" and "minus 3", and forced colours, which drop the fills, keep the difference.
- **Nothing to focus.** A Count inside a Tab or a Collapsible is part of that control's name.

## Props

_Props of `Count`, generated from its types:_

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `value` (required) | `string \| number` |  | The number. Anything above `max` renders as `max+`; a string renders as given. |
| `max` | `number` | `99` | The ceiling, 99 by default: the pill never grows past three characters and a plus. |
| `appearance` | `"added" \| "default" \| "important" \| "primary" \| "removed"` | `default` | `default` is the neutral pill; `primary` the brand fill for the one count that must be seen; `important` the danger fill for what needs attention now; `added` and `removed` for a diff. |
| `className` | `string` |  |  |

Count takes a span's native props and a ref, and names itself last with `data-slot="count"` and its `data-appearance`.

_Example: story `Stories.NativeAttributes`._

### Playground

_Example: story `Stories.Playground`._

_Rendered in the Storybook: Controls._

## Related

- [Badge](?path=/docs/components-badge--docs): the tone table, and which of Badge, Count, Indicator and Dot to use.
- [Stat](?path=/docs/components-stat--docs): the exact number, big.
- [Section](?path=/docs/layout-section--docs), [Related](?path=/docs/patterns-related--docs), [Item](?path=/docs/components-item--docs) groups and [Table](?path=/docs/components-table--docs) groups take a `count`; a [Tabs](?path=/docs/components-tabs--docs) trigger or a [Collapsible](?path=/docs/components-collapsible--docs) trigger composes one after its label.

## Don't

A Count is a number beside the label that says what it counts, capped at `max`. A severity is an Indicator, a state a Badge and an exact large number a Stat, never a number alone, a word in the pill or six digits.

_Example: story `Stories.Dont`._

# DatePicker

**Status: Stable.**

One calendar day in a form, held and reported as an ISO day (`"2026-09-18"`, the contract of `input type="date"`) and shown in the LedgerProvider's locale ("Sep 18, 2026"). A day has no time and no zone, so it never shifts between readers. It is Ledger's composition of [Popover](?path=/docs/components-popover--docs) and [Calendar](?path=/docs/components-calendar--docs), with Today and Clear under the month.

Use it for a day: a due date, a planned completion, a milestone. For a moment in time (collected at, due at 5 PM) use [DateTimeField](?path=/docs/components-datetimefield--docs); for a time of day alone, [TimeField](?path=/docs/components-timefield--docs); for a range, [DateRangePicker](?path=/docs/components-daterangepicker--docs). An approximate or remembered date ("March 2024") is an [Input](?path=/docs/components-input--docs) with the format in its hint.

```tsx
<Field>
  <FieldLabel>Scheduled completion</FieldLabel>
  <DatePicker name="due" value={due} onValueChange={setDue} />
  <FieldDescription>When the milestone is due.</FieldDescription>
</Field>
```

_Example: story `Stories.Open`._

## Picking or typing

`entry` chooses how the reader gives the day.

| `entry`          | What the reader sees                            | For                                                            |
| ---------------- | ----------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `pick` (default) | A button that reads the day and opens the month | A day the reader looks for: the next review, a due date        |
| `type`           | A text field with a button that opens the month | A day the reader already knows: a signed date, a date of birth |

A typed day is read in the provider's locale when the reader presses Tab or Enter, never while typing: "Sep 18, 2026", "9/18/2026" (en-US order), "18.9.2026" (de-DE), "2026-09-18" and "9/18" (this year) all read, in the locale's digits or Latin ones. The field then shows the day in the locale's words. Text that is not a day, or a day outside `min`, `max` or `isDateUnavailable`, stays as the reader typed it, the field reports `""` and says what fixes it under itself: "Enter a date such as Sep 25, 2026.", "Enter Sep 1, 2026 or later." Escape puts back the last day. Alt+Down opens the month from the text.

The message is a FieldError inside the Field, so it describes the input and marks the Field invalid. `onEntryError` receives it (and `null` once the entry reads), for a form library that should show it in place of its own "Required.".

_Example: story `Stories.TypedEntry`._
_Example: story `Stories.TypedInGerman`._

## Days the reader may not choose

`min` and `max` are ISO days; `isDateUnavailable(iso)` returns `true` or the reason as a sentence ("Weekends are closed."). Those days are disabled in the month and their names carry the reason ("Saturday, September 19, 2026, Not available. Weekends are closed."); the month does not page before `min` or after `max`; when today may not be chosen, Today is disabled but stays in the tab order and says why ("The latest date is Dec 31, 2025."), as Button's `disabledReason`; a typed day outside them is an error that names the limit. Say the rule in the hint as well, where every reader sees it before choosing.

`calendarProps` passes the month's own options: `captionLayout="dropdown"` for the year dropdown when the day is a year or more away, `startMonth` and `endMonth`, `showWeekNumber`, `fixedWeeks`.

_Example: story `Stories.MinMaxAndReasons`._
_Example: story `Stories.TodayUnavailable`._
_Example: story `Stories.YearDropdown`._

## Values and forms

Use `value` and `onValueChange` for controlled state or `defaultValue` for uncontrolled; `onChange` is the older spelling of `onValueChange`, deprecated and kept for one version. Choosing reports an ISO day and clearing reports `""`. A value that is not an ISO day warns once in the console: a timestamp is read as its day in the provider's zone, and anything else ("2026-02-30") as empty, so the field never shows one day and submits another. A hidden input carries the day under `name`, including for an owning form named by `form`; a disabled picker submits nothing. A native form reset restores an uncontrolled default; a controlled caller resets its own value.

_Example: story `Stories.NativeForm`._

## Accessibility

- Inside a Field the picker is the Field's control: the FieldLabel names it without ids, and the hint, the error and the Field's `invalid` and `disabled` reach it. Outside one, give it `aria-label`.
- The picking button's name is its label, and it is described by the chosen day first, then the hint and the error, so a reader tabbing through a form hears the value without opening the month. The month is named after its field.
- The month takes focus when it opens. Choosing, Clear and Escape return focus to the field, including inside a Dialog, which stays open.
- A typed field is a text input and announces required; a button cannot carry `aria-required`, so the picking form says required in the label's asterisk and the form's check.
- The month keeps the Calendar's keyboard: arrows by day and week, Page Up and Page Down by month, Shift with them by year, Home and End by week, one tab stop.

_Example: story `Stories.InField`._
_Example: story `Stories.FocusIntegration`._

## Props

_Props of `DatePicker`, generated from its types:_

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `min` | `string` |  | The earliest day the reader may choose, as an ISO day. Earlier days are disabled with the reason in their name, and typing one is an error. |
| `max` | `string` |  | The latest day the reader may choose, as an ISO day. |
| `isDateUnavailable` | `((iso: string) => string \| boolean)` |  | Other days the reader may not choose: return true, or the reason as a sentence ("Weekends are closed."), which the day's accessible name and the typed-entry error carry. Say the rule in the field's hint as well, where everyone reads it. |
| `value` | `string` |  | The chosen day as an ISO date ("2026-09-14"), controlled; pair it with `onValueChange`. Anything else warns: a timestamp is read as its day in the provider's zone, other text as empty. |
| `defaultValue` | `string` |  | The starting day when uncontrolled, as an ISO date. |
| `onValueChange` | `((iso: string) => void)` |  | Called with the new ISO date, or "" when cleared or when typed text is not a day. The kit's name for a value callback, as on Select, NumberField and the other date fields. |
| `onChange` | `((iso: string) => void)` |  | Called with the new ISO date, as `onValueChange` is; both run when both are given. @deprecated Use `onValueChange`, the name every other value control uses. Kept for one version. |
| `placeholder` | `string` |  | What the field says with no day chosen: "Choose a date" when picking, nothing when typing. |
| `size` | `"medium" \| "small"` | `medium` | `medium` (32px) in a form; `small` (28px) in a toolbar. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` |  | Not available. The last resort. A Field's or FieldSet's `disabled` also reaches it. |
| `name` | `string` |  | The form field's name; a hidden input carries the ISO date on submit. |
| `form` | `string` |  | An external owning form, matching the native form attribute. |
| `id` | `string` |  |  |
| `aria-labelledby` | `string` |  | Names the field. Inside a Field it defaults to the FieldLabel. |
| `defaultOpen` | `boolean` | `false` | Open on first render; for a sheet that exists to pick this day, and for the docs. |
| `className` | `string` |  | Layout only. @accepts layout |
| `aria-label` | `string` |  | The name when there is no visible label. |
| `aria-invalid` | `boolean` |  | Set when form validation fails; the border turns. A typed entry that is not a day sets it too. |
| `aria-required` | `boolean` |  | Accepted and not rendered when picking: a button may not carry `aria-required`. The asterisk and the form's check say required. A typed field announces it. |
| `aria-describedby` | `string` |  | IDs of the hint or error describing the control. The chosen day is described first. |
| `entry` | `"pick" \| "type"` | `pick` | `pick` (the default): a button that opens the month. `type`: a text field that reads the day in the provider's locale ("Sep 18, 2026", "9/18/2026", "2026-09-18", "9/18") with a button that opens the month, for a date the reader already knows. Its label, hint, error, invalid, disabled and required come from the Field around it, and native props and the ref reach the input. |
| `onEntryError` | `((message: string \| null) => void)` |  | With `entry="type"`: called with the message when the typed text is not a day the field accepts, and with null once it is. The field then reports "" and shows the message under itself; a form library can show it in place of its own "Required.". |
| `calendarProps` | `Pick<CalendarProps, "captionLayout" \| "startMonth" \| "endMonth" \| "showWeekNumber" \| "fixedWeeks">` |  | The month's own options: the year dropdown (`captionLayout="dropdown"`), the months it reaches, week numbers. |

<!-- page: Components/DateRangePicker (src/stories/components/DateRangePicker.mdx) -->

# DateRangePicker

**Status: Stable.**

A range of calendar days from one field: a trigger that reads the range ("Sep 7 – 11, 2026") and a popover with two months and, optionally, named presets. It holds and reports two ISO days, `{ start, end }`, both inclusive, and never shifts them across zones. Built on [Calendar](?path=/docs/components-calendar--docs)'s range mode.

Use it for a period the reader thinks of as one thing: a reporting period, a program period, a date filter. A single day is a [DatePicker](?path=/docs/components-datepicker--docs). A start and an end that the reader sets at different times, or that carry their own rules, are two DatePickers whose `min` and `max` follow each other.

```tsx
<Field>
  <FieldLabel>Reporting period</FieldLabel>
  <DateRangePicker value={period} onValueChange={setPeriod} presets={quarters} />
</Field>
```

_Example: story `Stories.WithPresets`._

## Choosing

The first day the reader chooses starts a new range and the second ends it, in either order; choosing the same day twice makes a one-day range. Until the end is chosen the footer says "Choose the end date." and a screen reader hears it. Once both ends are chosen the popover closes, focus returns to the trigger and `onValueChange` receives the range. Escape or a click outside closes without a change; a half-chosen range is never reported. Clear reports `{ start: "", end: "" }`.

`presets` are named ranges beside the months: choosing one sets the range and closes. The preset that matches the value is pressed and carries a check. On a phone the presets wrap above the month. A preset whose start or end may not be chosen (outside `min` or `max`, or unavailable) is disabled but stays in the tab order, and its reason ("The earliest date is Sep 1, 2026.") is its description and shows in a tooltip, as Button's `disabledReason`.

_Example: story `Stories.Playground`._

## Limits

`min`, `max` and `isDateUnavailable` work as on DatePicker: those days are disabled with their reason in their names, and the months do not page past the limits. A range may span an unavailable day, such as a weekend inside a reporting week.

_Example: story `Stories.MinAndMax`._

## Values and forms

Each end is an ISO day; an end that is not one warns once and is treated as empty, and ends out of order are no range. `startName` and `endName` put the ends in two hidden inputs for a native form.

## Accessibility

- Inside a Field the trigger is the Field's control: the FieldLabel names it, and the hint, the error and the Field's state reach it.
- The trigger's name is its label and its description is the range in full words, "September 7, 2026 to September 11, 2026", so a screen reader does not read the dash. The popover is named after the field.
- The months keep the Calendar's keyboard and name each range end; the presets are toggle buttons in a group named "Presets".

## Props

_Props of `DateRangePicker`, generated from its types:_

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `min` | `string` |  | The earliest day the reader may choose, as an ISO day. Earlier days are disabled with the reason in their name, and typing one is an error. |
| `max` | `string` |  | The latest day the reader may choose, as an ISO day. |
| `isDateUnavailable` | `((iso: string) => string \| boolean)` |  | Other days the reader may not choose: return true, or the reason as a sentence ("Weekends are closed."), which the day's accessible name and the typed-entry error carry. Say the rule in the field's hint as well, where everyone reads it. |
| `value` | `DateRangeValue` |  | The chosen range, controlled; pair it with `onValueChange`. Each end is an ISO day. |
| `defaultValue` | `DateRangeValue` |  | The starting range when uncontrolled. |
| `onValueChange` | `((range: DateRangeValue) => void)` |  | Called with the new range once both ends are chosen, or with two "" when cleared. A half-chosen range is not reported. |
| `presets` | `DateRangePreset[]` |  | Named ranges beside the month; choosing one sets the range and closes. The one that matches the value is marked. |
| `placeholder` | `string` |  | What the field says with no range chosen: "Choose dates". |
| `size` | `"medium" \| "small"` | `medium` | `medium` (32px) in a form; `small` (28px) in a toolbar or a filter. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` |  | Not available. A Field's or FieldSet's `disabled` also reaches it. |
| `startName` | `string` |  | The start's form field name; a hidden input carries its ISO day on submit. |
| `endName` | `string` |  | The end's form field name. |
| `form` | `string` |  | An external owning form, matching the native form attribute. |
| `id` | `string` |  |  |
| `numberOfMonths` | `1 \| 2` | `2` | Months shown side by side where there is room; 2 by default. |
| `defaultOpen` | `boolean` | `false` | Open on first render; for the docs. |
| `aria-labelledby` | `string` |  | Names the field. Inside a Field it defaults to the FieldLabel. |
| `aria-label` | `string` |  | The name when there is no visible label. |
| `aria-invalid` | `boolean` |  | Set when form validation fails; the border turns. |
| `aria-describedby` | `string` |  | IDs of the hint or error describing the field. The chosen range is described first. |
| `calendarProps` | `Pick<CalendarProps, "captionLayout" \| "startMonth" \| "endMonth" \| "showWeekNumber" \| "fixedWeeks">` |  | The month's own options, as on DatePicker. |
| `className` | `string` |  | Layout only. @accepts layout |

# DateTime, RelativeTime and DateLabel

**Status: Stable.**

Every date the product shows, through one formatter: the LedgerProvider's locale and time zone. Each renders a `<time>` with its ISO value, and the full value ("Friday, September 18, 2026 at 5:30 PM Pacific Daylight Time") opens in a tooltip on hover and keyboard focus and is the description a screen reader hears.

| Part         | Shows                                                 | For                                                      |
| ------------ | ----------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------- |
| DateTime     | "Sep 18, 2026" or "Sep 18, 2026, 5:30 PM"             | A date or a moment in a property, a cell, a sentence     |
| RelativeTime | "5 minutes ago", "yesterday", "in 3 days"             | Activity, updated and saved times, where recency matters |
| DateLabel    | "Sep 22, 2026 · Overdue", "Due today", "Due tomorrow" | A due date, expiry or milestone the reader acts on       |

Use them wherever the product prints a date, in place of `toLocaleString`, `toLocaleDateString` or a formatter of its own, so one record reads the same day on every screen. Inside DataTable a date column is `c.date`, which reads the same locale and zone; it shows an instant's day by default and its time with `format: "medium"`. A date the reader enters is a [DatePicker](?path=/docs/components-datepicker--docs) or a [DateTimeField](?path=/docs/components-datetimefield--docs).

```tsx
<DateTime value={record.updated_at} />
<RelativeTime value={comment.created_at} />
<DateLabel value={task.due_on} complete={task.status === "done"} />
```

## Days and instants

An ISO day (`"2026-09-18"`) is a calendar day: it never shifts, whoever reads it. An instant (an ISO timestamp with an offset, a Date or epoch milliseconds) is shown in the provider's zone, UTC unless the product sets one, so the same instant reads Sep 18 in Los Angeles and Sep 19 in Tokyo. Mount one LedgerProvider with the reader's zone near the root and keep it the same on the server and the client. Nothing (`null`, `undefined`, `""`) shows [Absent](?path=/docs/components-typography--docs), which a screen reader hears as "Not recorded", or as `absentLabel` ("No due date") where the context says more. A string that is neither warns once and shows as written.

`format` is `date` (a day's default), `datetime` (an instant's default), `time`, or Intl options of your own; `showTimeZone` adds the zone's short name to an instant.

_Example: story `Stories.Formats`._

## The full value

The tooltip opens on hover and on keyboard focus, never on hover alone. A date standing alone takes a tab stop so a keyboard reaches it; inside a link, a button or a row that takes focus itself (one with a `tabindex`, as in a grid or tree) the host's focus opens it and the date takes none. A row that cannot take focus, as in a plain table, is no host, so the date keeps its tab stop. Turn the tab stop off (`focusable={false}`) in a dense list whose preview or record already shows the full value, and the tooltip off (`isTooltipDisabled`, as on IconButton) where the text is already full.

_Example: story `Stories.FullValue`._

## Long content

A date is one line and never wraps or truncates: its words are short, and a cut date would say a different day. Where a column cannot hold the default format, choose a shorter `format` (`date` in place of `datetime`) rather than letting the column cut it; the tooltip carries the full value either way.

## RelativeTime

Words from `Intl.RelativeTimeFormat` in the provider's locale: under a minute either way is "now"; then minutes, hours, days ("yesterday", "tomorrow"), weeks, months and years. The words follow the clock without a reload, updating when they would change. A fixed `now` stops the updates, for a test or a snapshot. A calendar day reads relative to the reader's today. `unitStyle` is `long`, `short` or `narrow`.

_Example: story `Stories.Relative`._
_Example: story `Stories.Updating`._

## DateLabel

A due date that says where it stands. Overdue (danger), due today and due within `soonWithin` days (warning, 2 by default) each carry an icon and words beside the date as well as a tone, so the state never rests on colour and survives forced colours. A later date shows plainly with a calendar icon, and `complete` shows a finished item's date plainly, never overdue. A day is judged against the reader's today; an instant against now, in the provider's zone.

_Example: story `Stories.DueDates`._

An expiry is not work that falls due: the day an authorization or a piece of evidence stops holding takes `kind="expiry"`, with the same states and tones and its own words, Expired, Expires today and Expires tomorrow.

_Example: story `Stories.Expiries`._

## Accessibility

- The `<time>` element carries the machine value; the words are the visible text and the full value is the description on focus.
- The tooltip is a visual copy of that description, hidden from assistive technology.
- DateLabel's state is in its words ("Overdue", "Due today", or "Expired" for an expiry), which a screen reader reads with the date.

## Props

_Props of `DateTime`, generated from its types:_

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `value` (required) | `DateTimeValue` |  | An ISO day ("2026-09-18"), which never shifts; an ISO instant, a Date or epoch milliseconds, shown in the LedgerProvider's time zone. Nothing shows Absent. |
| `format` | `DateTimeFormat` |  | `date` ("Sep 18, 2026", a day's default), `datetime` ("Sep 18, 2026, 5:30 PM", an instant's default), `time` ("5:30 PM"), or Intl options. |
| `showTimeZone` | `boolean` |  | Adds the zone's short name to an instant: "Sep 18, 2026, 5:30 PM PDT". The tooltip always names the zone. |
| `isTooltipDisabled` | `boolean` |  | Leaves out the full value ("Friday, September 18, 2026 at 5:30 PM Pacific Daylight Time"), which otherwise opens in a tooltip on hover and keyboard focus and is the description a screen reader hears on focus. Off by default, as on IconButton. |
| `focusable` | `boolean` |  | Takes a tab stop so the keyboard reaches the tooltip. On by default; inside a link, a button or a row the host's focus opens it instead and the date takes no tab stop. Turn it off in a dense list whose rows or preview already show the full value. |
| `absentLabel` | `string` |  | What a screen reader hears where there is no value, as Absent's `label`: "No due date". Without it, "Not recorded", the locale's default. |
| `ref` | `Ref<HTMLTimeElement>` |  |  |

<!-- page: Components/DateTimeField (src/stories/components/DateTimeField.mdx) -->

# DateTimeField

**Status: Stable.**

A moment: a day and a time together, typed or picked, in the LedgerProvider's time zone, which it names after the time ("PDT"). It holds and reports an ISO instant in UTC (`"2026-09-19T00:30:00.000Z"`), so the moment a reader enters is the moment stored, and every reader sees it in their provider's zone.

Use it for a point in time: evidence collected at, a response due at 5 PM, a scheduled start. A day with no time (a due date, a planned completion) is a [DatePicker](?path=/docs/components-datepicker--docs); a wall time that repeats is a [TimeField](?path=/docs/components-timefield--docs). It replaces `input type="datetime-local"`, which ignores the provider and leaves the zone unsaid.

```tsx
<Field>
  <FieldLabel>Evidence collected</FieldLabel>
  <DateTimeField name="collected_at" value={collectedAt} onValueChange={setCollectedAt} />
</Field>
```

_Example: story `Stories.InField`._

## The two halves

The day is a typed [DatePicker](?path=/docs/components-datepicker--docs) input with its month, and the time a [TimeField](?path=/docs/components-timefield--docs) input with its stepping; each reads what the reader types in the locale, and the time shows the zone's short name. Where the field's container holds them they sit side by side; below 256px the time goes under the day.

The field reports an instant once both halves read, and `""` while either is missing or not valid. `defaultTime` (an ISO time such as `"17:00"`) fills the time when the reader picks a day first. When focus leaves the field with one half filled, it says "Enter both a date and a time." Enter in either input with one half filled says the same and does not submit the form around the field, so focus stays where the reader is typing; so does Enter on a day or a time that does not read, or a moment outside the limits, with that message. With both halves read, Enter submits as in any text field. A day and a wall time become an instant in the provider's zone: a time a daylight-saving change skips moves forward by the gap, and a time that happens twice takes the earlier moment.

_Example: story `Stories.DefaultTimeAndIncomplete`._
_Example: story `Stories.EnterWithHalfAnEntry`._

## Limits

`min` and `max` are instants. Days outside them are disabled in the month with their reason; a time before `min` on its first day is an error that names the limit: "Enter Sep 21, 2026, 9:00 AM or later." `isDateUnavailable` works as on DatePicker.

_Example: story `Stories.MinAndMax`._

## Values and forms

`value` is an instant with an offset or `Z`. A value with no offset (`"2026-09-18T17:30"`, what `datetime-local` holds) is read as a wall time in the provider's zone, which makes moving a native field over a one-line change; anything else warns once and is treated as empty. A hidden input carries the instant under `name`; put `name` here, not on the Field. A native form reset puts the field back as it was, a half entry and its message included. One message under the field speaks for both halves: a day or time that does not read, a moment outside the limits, or a missing half.

_Example: story `Stories.FormReset`._

## Accessibility

- Inside a Field the day input is the Field's control, so the FieldLabel points at it. The whole field is a group named by the label; the day input is named "Evidence collected Date" and the time "Evidence collected Time Pacific Daylight Time", so a screen reader hears the zone that the eye reads as "PDT".
- The Field's hint and error describe both inputs, and its invalid state reaches both.
- Keep `showTimeZone` on. A time without its zone reads as two moments to readers in two offices.

_Props of `DateTimeField`, generated from its types:_

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |

| `defaultValue` | `string` |  | The starting moment when uncontrolled. |
| `onValueChange` | `((instant: string) => void)` |  | Called with the new instant in UTC ("2026-09-19T00:30:00.000Z"), or "" while the day or the time is missing or not valid. |
| `min` | `string` |  | The earliest moment the reader may enter, as an instant. Earlier days are disabled in the month; an earlier time on the same day is an error that names it. |
| `max` | `string` |  | The latest moment the reader may enter, as an instant. |
| `isDateUnavailable` | `((iso: string) => string \| boolean)` |  | Days the reader may not choose, as on DatePicker: true, or the reason as a sentence. |
| `defaultTime` | `string` |  | The time a day takes when the reader picks it before any time, as an ISO time ("17:00"). Without it the time waits for the reader. |
| `step` | `number` | `15` | Minutes the Up and Down arrows move the time by. 15 by default. |

| `name` | `string` |  | The form field's name; a hidden input carries the instant on submit. Put it here, not on the Field. |
| `form` | `string` |  | An external owning form, matching the native form attribute. |

| `id` | `string` |  | The day input's id: a FieldLabel's `htmlFor` points at it. |
| `size` | `"medium" \| "small"` | `medium` | `medium` (32px) in a form; `small` (28px) in a toolbar. |
| `aria-labelledby` | `string` |  | Names the field. Inside a Field it defaults to the FieldLabel. |

| `calendarProps` | `Pick<CalendarProps, "captionLayout" \| "startMonth" \| "endMonth" \| "showWeekNumber" \| "fixedWeeks">` |  | The month's own options, as on DatePicker. |
