<!-- page: Components/Density (src/stories/components/Density.mdx) -->

# Density

Row density belongs to each table. `default` gives rows 40px of height; `compact` gives them 36px. Headers, controls and typography keep their sizes.

## Usage

Set `density` on a plain Table. The frame sets `data-density="compact"`, which changes the row-height token for its contents. Keep that attribute on the table frame so nearby lists and cards retain their spacing. The `Density` type names the two values.

_Example: story `Stories.Tables`._

## Reader preference

A DataTable's Columns menu offers Compact rows. With a `view` name, the choice persists with its column settings; Reset view restores the author's default.

_Example: story `Stories.RegisterStory`._

For a compact default, pass `density: "compact"` to `useDataTable`. The reader can still change it.

_Example: story `Stories.ByDesign`._

## Accessibility

Changing row height preserves labels, focus order and control targets. The Columns menu exposes the current choice as a checkbox item. Offer density per table, so a choice in one view does not change unrelated content.

## Related

- [Table](?path=/docs/components-table--docs): native table structure and density prop.
- [DataTable](?path=/docs/patterns-data-table--docs): view preferences, Columns menu and reset.
- [Upgrading](?path=/docs/guidance-upgrading--docs#density): the earlier API's spellings and what they are now.

<!-- page: Components/Dialog (src/stories/components/Dialog.mdx) -->

# Dialog

**Status: Stable.**

A focused task over the page: a create or edit form, a review, a choice that needs more than a sentence. Built on [Base UI Dialog](https://base-ui.com/react/components/dialog) with [shadcn’s composition](https://ui.shadcn.com/docs/components/base/dialog) and Ledger's tokens.

_Example: story `Stories.Form`._

## When to use it

- **A create or edit form**, titled with the operation: Create task, Edit member. The trigger, the title and the primary say the same words.
- **A task the reader finishes or abandons** before going back to the page.

Not for a decision that needs one sentence: that is an [AlertDialog](?path=/docs/components-alertdialog--docs). Not for a task at its button (a filter, a reason): that is a [Popover](?path=/docs/components-popover--docs). Not for work beside a list the reader keeps using: that is the Shell's panel. A modal edge panel is a [Sheet](?path=/docs/components-sheet--docs), and a phone's bottom sheet a [Drawer](?path=/docs/components-drawer--docs).

## Anatomy

```tsx
<Dialog open={open} onOpenChange={setOpen} pending={pending}>
  <DialogContent width="medium" initialFocus={firstField}>
    <DialogHeader>
      <DialogTitle>Create task</DialogTitle>
      <DialogDescription>Describe the work.</DialogDescription>
    </DialogHeader>
    <DialogBody>
      <form id={formId} noValidate onSubmit={submit}>
        …fields
      </form>
    </DialogBody>
    <DialogFooter>
      <DialogClose render={<Button variant="subtle" />}>Cancel</DialogClose>
      <Button type="submit" form={formId} variant="primary" isLoading={pending}>
        Create task
      </Button>
    </DialogFooter>
  </DialogContent>
</Dialog>
```

- **DialogContent** brings its portal, the blanket and a close button at the top end, an IconButton named Close with no tooltip. The close button is first in the Tab order, where it is drawn; the first field still takes focus when the dialog opens. It records the overlay surface as the current one, so a sticky header, a pinned cell or a scroll arrow inside paints the dialog's colour, not the page's.
- **DialogHeader** holds the title and the description; the title is the dialog's h2, a [Heading](?path=/docs/primitives-heading--docs) at `overlay` (15/22 medium), and headings inside the dialog start at h3. Both wrap an unbroken value, such as a record's code or a server's error, inside the popup.
- **DialogBody** is the one scrolling region, with the dialog's inset. Put the form in it and the buttons in the footer; never make a `fieldset` or a hand-written `div` the scroller.
- **DialogFooter** stays outside the scroll, on the dialog's own surface below a hairline, with Cancel, a subtle button, before the primary. `showCloseButton` adds a subtle Close in Cancel's place, before the children.
- DialogPortal and DialogOverlay are exported for a custom popup.

## Widths

`width` on DialogContent picks a step; do not set pixels in `style`.

| `width`      | Size                        | For                                  |
| ------------ | --------------------------- | ------------------------------------ |
| `small`      | 400px                       | A short question with a field or two |
| `medium`     | 520px, the default          | A form of a few fields               |
| `large`      | 760px                       | A form in two columns, or a table    |
| `xlarge`     | 960px                       | A table beside a preview             |
| `fullscreen` | The window, less the gutter | A task that needs the whole window   |

Every step keeps a `space.200` gutter on each side of the window, so a dialog on a phone is the phone's width less the gutter. Choose the width by the task, so dialogs of the same kind open at the same size. An [AlertDialog](?path=/docs/components-alertdialog--docs) takes the same words for the same widths, `small` by default, and `xsmall` 320px below them for a one-line question.

_Example: story `Stories.Widths`._

## Scrolling and short windows

The body takes the height the header and footer leave, at least 80px, and scrolls. Read-only content that overflows makes it a tab stop, named "Content, scrolls", so the keyboard can scroll what a pointer can.

_Example: story `Stories.Scrollable`._

In a window under 30rem tall (a landscape phone, or a laptop at 200% to 400% zoom) the popup becomes the one scroller: the header scrolls away with the body, the footer stays at the bottom, and every field and the primary can still be reached and seen. The footer keeps its height as the popup's scroll padding, so a field that takes focus scrolls clear of it rather than under it.

_Example: story `Stories.LongForm`._

_Example: story `Stories.ZoomedWindow`._

## Pending

`pending` on the Dialog holds it while a save or another command runs. Every request to close is cancelled before `onOpenChange` hears of it (Escape, the blanket, the close button, any DialogClose), the close controls are disabled, the built-in close button and a DialogClose rendered as a kit Button stay focusable while they are (`aria-disabled`), and the popup is `aria-busy`. Close the dialog yourself when the command succeeds, with `open={false}`. `pending` does not disable the form: wrap the fields in `<FieldSet disabled={pending}>`, give the submit button `isLoading`, and move focus to that button before the fields lock, since it stays focusable while it loads.

_Example: story `Stories.PendingAndNestedPopup`._

A failed save keeps the dialog and the draft, ends the pending state and says what to change.

_Example: story `Stories.FormSaveFails`._

## Accessibility

- **A title names the dialog**; a DialogDescription, when there is one, describes it.
- **Focus moves in and comes back.** The first field takes focus through `initialFocus` on DialogContent, never through `autoFocus` on the field. A Dialog opened from state records the element that had focus as it opens and returns focus there when it closes, even when a field took focus as it mounted, as long as that element is still on the page and enabled; when it goes away with the task, pass `finalFocus`. Keep the opener enabled while its dialog is open.
- **Base UI owns** the focus trap, Escape, the outside press and nested popups: a Select or a DatePicker inside closes on its own Escape first.
- **One stack is allowed:** an AlertDialog over the Dialog that owns the decision, such as the discard prompt for a dirty draft. Render it inside DialogContent: the dialog under the prompt dims, so its buttons read as out of play, and the page keeps one blanket. An independent record workflow replaces the dialog instead of stacking.
- **Forced colours keep the edge.** The popup draws a CanvasText outline where its fill and shadow are replaced, and the blanket stays a veil of Canvas. A press on the blanket while the dialog is `pending` keeps focus where it was.

_Example: story `Stories.FocusReturnFromState`._

## Content

- The title is the operation and the singular noun; the primary says the same words, never OK, Submit or Save alone.
- Cancel, a subtle DialogClose, comes before the primary. A dialog whose choices apply as they are made has no draft to cancel, so its secondary is Close.
- Validate on submit with the primary enabled. Errors say what fixes the field; an [ErrorSummary](?path=/docs/components-errorsummary--docs) lists them all when the form is longer than a few fields.
- Button labels stay on one line.
- A title that names a record may hold its code; it wraps rather than running past the edge. Say a failure's cause in the body, through an Alert or a FieldError, not in the title.

_Example: story `Stories.LongValues`._

## Props

Dialog takes Base UI Dialog's root props, `open`, `defaultOpen`, `onOpenChange` (its details say why: `reason` is `escape-key`, `outside-press`, `close-press` or another, and `cancel()` keeps the dialog open), `onOpenChangeComplete`, `modal`, `disablePointerDismissal`, `actionsRef` and `handle`, and Ledger's `pending`. DialogContent takes the popup's `initialFocus`, `finalFocus`, `render`, `className` and `style`, and Ledger's `width` and `showCloseButton`. DialogTrigger, DialogClose, DialogTitle and DialogDescription take Base UI's part props, `render` among them. Every part takes its element's native attributes, and its `data-slot` comes after them, so a caller's attribute never renames the part (Native attributes, below). The title and the description are the exception: another part renders as them through `render` (a PageHeader.Title as the title) and its `data-slot` names the element, as it does on a Button. The types are in [Base UI's API reference](https://base-ui.com/react/components/dialog#api-reference).

_Props of `Dialog`, generated from its types:_

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `open` | `boolean` |  | Whether the dialog is currently open. |
| `defaultOpen` | `boolean` | `false` | Whether the dialog is initially open. To render a controlled dialog, use the `open` prop instead. |
| `modal` | `boolean \| "trap-focus"` | `true` | Determines if the dialog enters a modal state when open. - `true`: user interaction is limited to just the dialog: focus is trapped, document page scroll is locked, and pointer interactions on outside elements are disabled. - `false`: user interaction with the rest of the document is allowed. - `'trap-focus'`: focus is trapped inside the dialog, but document page scroll is not locked and pointer interactions outside of it remain enabled. When `modal` is `true` or `'trap-focus'`, render `<Dialog.Close>` inside `<Dialog.Popup>` so touch screen readers can escape the popup. |
| `onOpenChange` | `((open: boolean, eventDetails: DialogRootChangeEventDetails) => void)` |  | Event handler called when the dialog is opened or closed. |
| `onOpenChangeComplete` | `((open: boolean) => void)` |  | Event handler called after any animations complete when the dialog is opened or closed. |
| `disablePointerDismissal` | `boolean` | `false` | Whether to prevent the dialog from closing on outside presses. For non-modal dialogs, this also prevents the dialog from closing when focus moves outside of it. |
| `actionsRef` | `RefObject<DialogRootActions \| null>` |  | A ref to imperative actions. - `unmount`: Manually unmounts the dialog. Call this after any externally controlled closing animation finishes. - `close`: Closes the dialog imperatively when called. |
| `handle` | `DialogHandle<Payload>` |  | A handle to associate the dialog with a trigger. If specified, allows external triggers to control the dialog's open state. Can be created with the Dialog.createHandle() method. |
| `children` | `ReactNode \| PayloadChildRenderFunction<Payload>` |  | The content of the dialog. This can be a regular React node or a render function that receives the `payload` of the active trigger. |
| `triggerId` | `string \| null` |  | ID of the trigger that the dialog is associated with. This is useful in conjunction with the `open` prop to create a controlled dialog. There's no need to specify this prop when the dialog is uncontrolled (that is, when the `open` prop is not set). |
| `defaultTriggerId` | `string \| null` |  | ID of the trigger that the dialog is associated with. This is useful in conjunction with the `defaultOpen` prop to create an initially open dialog. |
| `pending` | `boolean` | `false` | A save or another command is in flight. Every request to close is cancelled before `onOpenChange` hears of it (Escape, the blanket, the close button, a DialogClose), the close controls are disabled (the built-in close button, and a close rendered as a kit Button, stay focusable with `aria-disabled`, so focus on them is kept), and the popup is `aria-busy`. An imperative close through `actionsRef`, or `open={false}`, still closes: end the pending state when the command settles. It does not disable the form; wrap the fields in `<FieldSet disabled={pending}>` and give the submit button `isLoading`. |

_Example: story `Stories.NativeAttributes`._

### DialogContent

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `initialFocus` | `boolean \| RefObject<HTMLElement \| null> \| ((openType: InteractionType) => boolean \| void \| HTMLElement \| null)` |  | Determines the element to focus when the dialog is opened. By default, focus moves to the first tabbable element inside the popup, except when the dialog is opened by touch — then the popup itself is focused to avoid opening the virtual keyboard. - `false`: Do not move focus. - `true`: Move focus based on the default behavior (first tabbable element or popup). - `RefObject`: Move focus to the ref element. - `function`: Called with the interaction type (`mouse`, `touch`, `pen`, or `keyboard`). <!-- page: Components/Diff (src/stories/components/Diff.mdx) -->

# Diff

**Status: Stable.**

What changed between two versions of a text: a revised statement, a library update against the copy in use, a tailored narrative against its baseline. Removed lines are marked −, added lines +, the words that changed inside an edited line are struck through or underlined, and unchanged runs fold behind a button so the reader sees the change, not two full copies.

It compares; it does not edit or decide. The caller owns what the two texts are and what happens next (accept the update, keep the tailoring). One text on its own is [CodeBlock](?path=/docs/components-codeblock--docs) for source or [Text](?path=/docs/primitives-text--docs) for prose; what happened to a record over time is a [Timeline](?path=/docs/components-timeline--docs); two values per record across many records is a [DataTable](?path=/docs/patterns-data-table--docs) column, with a Diff in the row's preview when the reader needs the change.

_Example: story `Stories.Inline`._

## Anatomy

| Part       | What it is                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| ---------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Frame      | A group named `Changes from {beforeLabel} to {afterLabel}`, on the surface it sits on (`utility.elevation.surface.current`) with a 1px `color.border` and `radius.medium`.                  |
| Header     | The legend (− and the earlier text's label, + and the later's) and the summary at the end: "3 changed, 1 added, 1 removed", or "No differences". Side by side, each label heads its column. |
| Line       | A row: optional line numbers, the marker (+, − or blank) and the text, which keeps its spacing and wraps. Removed lines on `color.background.danger.subtler`, added on `.success.subtler`.  |
| Word marks | Inside an edited line, the removed words in a `<del>`, struck through on `color.background.danger.subtle`; the added words in an `<ins>`, underlined on `color.background.success.subtle`.  |
| Fold       | An unchanged run, behind a subtle xsmall button: "Show 4 unchanged lines", then "Hide 4 unchanged lines".                                                                                   |

## How it compares

Lines first, then words. A line is what sits between line breaks, so in a narrative a paragraph is a line: pass the text as it is stored, not wrapped at a width, or every reflow reads as a change. The comparison is the shortest edit script (Myers' algorithm, in the component, no dependency), so the unchanged lines are as many as they can be.

A block of removed lines is then paired with the added lines that replaced them, in order, by how much text they share. A pair that keeps at least half its characters is an **edited** line and gets word marks; a pair that keeps less is a **rewrite**, shown as a removed and an added line with no word marks, because marking every word of a rewritten paragraph says nothing. A space between two changed words joins them, so "shall enforce" to "must require" reads as one change; the spaces at the ends of a changed run are left unmarked, so no mark hangs at a line's edge, and a change of spacing alone marks its line but no words. Words are runs of letters and digits, each punctuation mark, and each CJK character, cut by the same rule on the server and in the browser so hydration matches. Past 1,000 line edits, or 500 word edits in one line, it stops searching for the shortest script: it anchors on the lines each version has exactly once, in order, and compares the gaps between them, so a long text with many scattered edits keeps its unchanged lines. Only a gap with nothing to anchor on is shown replaced whole.

The same comparison is exported as `diffText(before, after)`: the rows of the side-by-side view and the counts (`changed`, `added`, `removed`, `unchanged`), for a section's count or for deciding whether a Diff is worth showing.

_Example: story `Stories.Counts`._

## Layouts

`layout="inline"`, the default, is one column: each edited line's earlier version directly above its later one, then any lines only one version has. `layout="side-by-side"` puts the earlier text beside the later, row for row, and suits a wide page where the reader compares long paragraphs.

_Example: story `Stories.SideBySide`._

Side by side measures its own width, not the window's. Below 36rem of its own (a panel, a rail, a phone), the halves stack and the view reads as inline: the second copy of each unchanged line and the empty halves go. Nothing is lost, and the reader's place does not change.

_Example: story `Stories.InANarrowContainer`._

The Diff fills the width it is given. It measures itself for that fallback, so its own lines never size it: in a flex row it takes the row's free width, and in a box that shrinks to its content (a popover, a table cell with no width), give it a width.

_Example: story `Stories.BesideOtherContent`._

## States

| State          | What shows                                                                                   |
| -------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Changed        | The marked lines, the unchanged context and the folds, with the counts in the header.        |
| No differences | "No differences" in the header and the whole text behind one fold.                           |
| New text       | Every line added (`before=""`); no word marks.                                               |
| Removed text   | Every line removed (`after=""`).                                                             |
| Rewritten      | A removed and an added line with no word marks, counted as one change.                       |
| Fold open      | The unchanged lines in place, and the same button, now Hide, keeping focus.                  |
| Blank lines    | A blank line keeps a full line's height; one added or removed is marked like any other line. |

_Example: story `Stories.States`._

_Example: story `Stories.BlankLines`._

## Modifiers

- **`beforeLabel`, `afterLabel`**: what the two texts are, "Version 3" and "Now", "Library" and "This program". They head the legend and name the group. "Before" and "After" by default; say which.
- **`context`**: unchanged lines kept on each side of a change, 3 by default. A longer unchanged run folds, unless the fold would hide a single line. `Infinity` shows every line.
- **`lineNumbers`**: a gutter with each version's numbers, both inline and each side's own side by side. Off by default, because a narrative's lines are paragraphs.
- **`code`**: the code face, for source and configuration.
- **`label`**: the group's name when the default does not say enough ("Access policy, Version 3 to Now").

Long unbroken text, such as a link or a hash, wraps at the frame's edge instead of widening it.

_Example: story `Stories.LongUnbrokenText`._

_Example: story `Stories.Code`._

## Content

- **Name both versions** in the labels: a version number, a date, "Library" or "Now". "Before" and "After" leave the reader to work out which is which.
- **Compare what the reader will decide on.** Pass the statement, not the whole record serialized; field-by-field changes belong in labelled properties.
- **Keep paragraphs as lines.** Text hard-wrapped at a width turns one edited sentence into several changed lines.
- **One Diff per text.** Several fields that changed are several Diffs under their own headings, or a DataTable with a preview.

## Long content

A Diff never truncates: every changed word must be readable. Lines wrap at the column's edge, and an unbroken token (a URL, a hash, an id) breaks anywhere, so a side-by-side Diff in a narrow panel stays inside it; below the container's `xl` width the two sides stack.

## Accessibility

- **Never colour alone.** Every change is marked three ways: the + or − marker, a visually hidden "Added:" or "Removed:" before the line, and a text decoration on changed words (struck through for removed, underlined for added) in native `<del>` and `<ins>` elements. In forced-colours mode the tints go and the markers and decorations stay.
- **The group is named** `Changes from {beforeLabel} to {afterLabel}`, and a visually hidden legend says which version the removed and added lines come from.
- **A fold is a disclosure:** a button with `aria-expanded` and `aria-controls`. Opening it keeps focus on the same button, which now hides the lines again, so focus is never dropped. Folded lines are `hidden="until-found"`, so the browser's find-in-page reaches them and opens their fold.
- **Read once:** side by side, the second copy of an unchanged line is hidden from assistive technology; line numbers and markers are hidden too, and are not selectable, so a copied selection is the text alone.
- **Touch:** the fold buttons are 24px tall; nothing depends on hover.
- **Direction:** the gutter, marker and column rule use logical properties, so a right-to-left page mirrors them: the line numbers, the marker and the earlier column sit at the right. Each line of prose takes its direction from its own text (`dir="auto"`), so a Latin statement on a right-to-left page keeps its full stop at its end; with `code`, every line reads left to right, so a brace never mirrors.
- **Contrast:** text and line numbers on the tinted rows meet 4.5:1 in both modes; the a11y gate checks every story.

_Example: story `Stories.RightToLeft`._

_Example: story `Stories.Localized`._

The legend, the summary, the hidden prefixes and the fold's words come from the locale's messages (`diffLabel`, `diffLegend`, `diffChangedCount`, `diffAdded`, `diffShowLinesOne`, `diffShowLinesOther` and the rest), and the counts from its number and list formats.

## Props

_Props of `Diff`, generated from its types:_

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `render` | `ReactElement<unknown, string \| JSXElementConstructor<any>> \| ComponentRenderFn<HTMLProps, {}>` |  | Allows you to replace the component's HTML element with a different tag, or compose it with another component. Accepts a `ReactElement` or a function that returns the element to render. |
| `before` (required) | `string` |  | The earlier text. Lines split on line breaks; in a narrative, a paragraph is a line. |
| `after` (required) | `string` |  | The later text. |
| `layout` | `"inline" \| "side-by-side"` | `inline` | `"inline"` (the default) shows one column: each edited line's earlier version above its later one. `"side-by-side"` puts the earlier text beside the later, row for row, and falls back to inline wherever its own container is narrower than 36rem. |
| `beforeLabel` | `string` |  | What the earlier text is: "Version 3", "Library". Heads its column and the legend. "Before" by default. |
| `afterLabel` | `string` |  | What the later text is: "Now", "This program". "After" by default. |
| `context` | `number` | `3` | Unchanged lines kept on each side of a change. A longer unchanged run folds behind a button that shows it (and the browser's find-in-page opens it). 3 by default; `Infinity` shows every line. |
| `lineNumbers` | `boolean` | `false` | Line numbers in a gutter: both versions' inline, each side's side by side. Off by default, since a narrative's lines are paragraphs. |
| `code` | `boolean` | `false` | Sets the lines in the code face, for source and configuration. Off by default. |
| `label` | `string` |  | The comparison's accessible name. "Changes from {beforeLabel} to {afterLabel}" by default. |

### Playground

_Example: story `Stories.Playground`._

_Rendered in the Storybook: Controls._

## Related

- [CodeBlock](?path=/docs/components-codeblock--docs): one version of source, with a Copy.
- [Timeline](?path=/docs/components-timeline--docs): what happened to a record, in order.
- [DataTable](?path=/docs/patterns-data-table--docs): many records, each with a value that changed; open one to see its Diff.
- [Collapsible](?path=/docs/components-collapsible--docs): the disclosure under each fold.

## Don't

What changed is a Diff, which marks the changed words in more than colour, never two full copies the reader compares by eye.

_Example: story `Stories.Dont`._

<!-- page: Components/Drawer (src/stories/components/Drawer.mdx) -->

# Drawer

**Status: Experimental.** No product screen opens a Drawer, so its API can still change before it is stable; owner: Ledger maintainers.

A gesture-driven panel using [shadcn’s Base UI composition](https://ui.shadcn.com/docs/components/base/drawer) and [Base UI Drawer](https://base-ui.com/react/components/drawer). Use Sheet for a side panel that needs no swipe gestures.

## When to use it

- **A quick task under the thumb on a narrow screen**: the actions for a selected item, a sort or a filter choice, a short confirmation, which the reader can swipe away.
- **Content at a snap point** that the reader drags open further when they need it.

Not for a create or edit form: that is a [Dialog](?path=/docs/components-dialog--docs). Not for a modal selection or review beside the page on a wide screen: that is a [Sheet](?path=/docs/components-sheet--docs). Not for a short list of actions on a wide screen: that is a [DropdownMenu](?path=/docs/components-dropdownmenu--docs). Not for a record's details while the list stays usable: that is the Shell's panel. [Overlays](?path=/docs/components-overlays--docs) compares them all.

## Content

- The title says what the drawer acts on or the task ("Control actions"); the description names the object ("For the selected control").
- Each action is a verb and its object; the drawer ends with Done or Cancel, never OK.
- One screen of content at its snap point; more than that is a page.

Each action names its object and the drawer ends with Done; "Options", bare verbs and OK leave the reader to remember what they selected.

_Example: story `Stories.DoDont`._

## Anatomy

```tsx
<Drawer showSwipeHandle>
  <DrawerTrigger render={<Button />}>Quick actions</DrawerTrigger>
  <DrawerContent>
    <DrawerHeader>
      <DrawerTitle>Control actions</DrawerTitle>
      <DrawerDescription>For the selected control.</DrawerDescription>
    </DrawerHeader>
    <DrawerBody>Actions</DrawerBody>
    <DrawerFooter>
      <DrawerClose render={<Button />}>Done</DrawerClose>
    </DrawerFooter>
  </DrawerContent>
</Drawer>
```

Content composes Portal, the modal Overlay, Base UI Viewport/Popup and the text-selectable Content region inside Base UI's VirtualKeyboardProvider, and records the overlay surface as the current one, so a sticky header or pinned cell inside matches the drawer. Header, Body, Title, Description, Footer and Close are explicit parts; the title is the drawer's h2, a [Heading](?path=/docs/primitives-heading--docs) at `overlay` (15/22 medium), and headings inside start at h3. Portal, Overlay and SwipeHandle are also exported for custom native compositions.

DrawerBody is the one scrolling region between the header and the footer, with the drawer's inset, at least 80px tall. Base UI lets a swipe that starts in it scroll it, and dismiss once it is at its edge. Read-only content that overflows makes it a tab stop, "Content, scrolls". In a window under 30rem tall the drawer scrolls as one, with the footer held at the bottom.

_Example: story `Stories.Actions`._

## Variants and states

`swipeDirection` is `down` by default; `up`, `left` and `right` use physical edges. `showSwipeHandle` defaults to false. Root supports controlled or uncontrolled open state, native snap points and modal modes. Put long content in DrawerBody. A bottom or top drawer leaves space above or below the panel.

_Example: story `Stories.Positions`._

`width` on DrawerContent is how wide the drawer grows, at the default text size and growing with the reader's:

| `width`            | Width | Use                                                     |
| ------------------ | ----- | ------------------------------------------------------- |
| `small`            | 320px | A short list of actions, a sort or one filter.          |
| `medium` (default) | 384px | A few actions with their descriptions, a filter.        |
| `large`            | 760px | Content that needs a table's width: a list with fields. |

A bottom or top drawer takes its width centred on a window from `sm` (640px) up, so on a desktop it reads as a panel under the thumb rather than a band across the screen, and runs edge to edge on a phone. A side drawer takes its width within 75% of the window, so a strip of the page stays in view to tap. The widths are `dimension.part.drawerSmall`, `dimension.part.drawer` and `dimension.part.drawerLarge`.

_Example: story `Stories.Widths`._
_Example: story `Stories.SnapPoints`._

Drawer has no `pending` prop. For pending work, cancel the native `onOpenChange` event details while the command runs, and disable the close controls; the same callback receives Escape, outside press, close button and swipe requests. Dialog, Sheet and AlertDialog have `pending`.

_Example: story `Stories.NestedPopups`._

## Accessibility

Supply a Title or an accessible name. Description is optional and creates its relationship only when rendered. Include an accessible Close action; the swipe handle is decorative. Base UI handles focus trapping, restoration, Escape, scroll locking and nested popups. On a phone, Base UI's VirtualKeyboardProvider, which DrawerContent wraps, keeps a focused field clear of the software keyboard: it scrolls DrawerBody so the field shows above the keyboard, rather than moving the drawer, and sets `--drawer-keyboard-inset` on the viewport while the keyboard is up. A footer that holds a field of its own offsets itself by `var(--drawer-keyboard-inset, 0px)`. Content accepts native `initialFocus`, `finalFocus`, refs, render and state callbacks. Specify a surviving finalFocus target if the opener disappears.

Nested drawers must be nested in the React tree. Ledger’s CSS follows Base UI’s measured swipe, snap and stack variables and honors reduced motion.

_Example: story `Stories.NestedDrawers`._

## Props

Drawer takes Base UI Drawer's root props, `open`, `defaultOpen`, `onOpenChange` (with the change's `reason` and `cancel()` in its details), `onOpenChangeComplete`, `modal`, `disablePointerDismissal`, `actionsRef`, `handle`, `swipeDirection`, `snapPoints`, `snapPoint`, `defaultSnapPoint`, `onSnapPointChange` and `snapToSequentialPoints`, and Ledger's `showSwipeHandle`. DrawerContent takes Ledger's `width` and the popup's `initialFocus`, `finalFocus`, refs, `render` and `className`. A custom composition puts Base UI's `Drawer.VirtualKeyboardProvider` around the portal, as the Custom Composition story does. The types are in [Base UI's API reference](https://base-ui.com/react/components/drawer#api-reference).

_Props of `Drawer`, generated from its types:_

<!-- page: Components/DropdownMenu (src/stories/components/DropdownMenu.mdx) -->

# DropdownMenu

**Status: Stable.**

Actions and view options anchored to a button, using shadcn's Base UI Menu composition. Ledger supplies the menu surface, row geometry, colors and motion.

```tsx
<DropdownMenu>
  <DropdownMenuTrigger render={<Button variant="secondary" iconAfter={<ChevronDown />} />}>
    Actions
  </DropdownMenuTrigger>
  <DropdownMenuContent>
    <DropdownMenuItem onClick={edit} shortcut="Mod+E">
      Edit
    </DropdownMenuItem>
    <DropdownMenuSeparator />
    <DropdownMenuItem variant="danger" onClick={archive}>
      Archive
    </DropdownMenuItem>
  </DropdownMenuContent>
</DropdownMenu>
```

## When to use

- **Actions on one thing** that do not all earn a button: a record's Actions menu, a row's overflow, a More behind an icon button. The one primary action stays a button beside the menu.
- **View options** that change how a collection reads: its columns, its sort, its density.
- **Places to go** from one record: a labelled group of LinkItems, each a real link.

Use something else when:

- one value in a form is chosen: a [Select](?path=/docs/components-select--docs), or a [RadioGroup](?path=/docs/components-radiogroup--docs) for a few visible choices;
- the reader types to find a command or a record: a [Command](?path=/docs/components-command--docs) list, the [CommandPalette](?path=/docs/patterns-commandpalette--docs) or the [SearchDialog](?path=/docs/patterns-searchdialog--docs);
- a single action needs no menu: a Button;
- the choice needs a sentence of explanation per option, or fields: a [Dialog](?path=/docs/components-dialog--docs).

## Content

- **A menu item is a verb and its object**: "Edit program", "Export as CSV", "Remove allocation". A LinkItem names the place: "Traceability matrix".
- **Order by use**: the common action first, the rare ones after, and a destructive one last, after a separator, with `variant="danger"`.
- **Group what belongs together** under a Label: the record's actions, then its Views. Keep checkbox and radio items in their own labelled Group, apart from actions, so an option that is off never reads as an action.
- **One line per label.** A label wider than the window leaves ends in an ellipsis, so write the short form; say the difference between two similar actions in `description`, and why an action cannot run in `disabledReason`.
- **The trigger says it opens a menu.** A labelled trigger carries a trailing ChevronDown (`render={<Button iconAfter={<ChevronDown />} />}`); an icon trigger such as More is a menu by its icon. A create action that asks how to create is a [ButtonGroup](?path=/docs/components-buttongroup--docs): the one create action, then a labelled icon menu for the other ways.

A place to go is a LinkItem, a real link the reader can open in a new tab, never an item that navigates in its click handler; a destructive item comes last, never first.

_Example: story `Stories.DoDont`._

## Composition and states

Root owns controlled or uncontrolled open state, modality, generic trigger payloads and cancellable `onOpenChange(open, details)`. Trigger defaults to a native button and composes existing buttons through `render`. Custom rendered components must accept merged props and refs; use `nativeButton={false}` only when replacing a button with a non-button action target.

Content includes its portal and positioner. It defaults to bottom/start, with a 4px side offset and zero alignment offset. Its width fits its contents and is at least the trigger width or 128px (`dimension.part.menu`), within the available viewport. Set no fixed `width`: the labels size the menu. A `minWidth` in `style` is capped at the available width, so it never pushes the menu off a phone. A narrow trigger never forces action labels to wrap. It scrolls when the available space is smaller than its contents, inside a [Scroller](?path=/docs/components-scroller--docs) whose hover arrows mark each overflowed edge. Native `style`, `className`, `render` and refs target the popup; classes and styles accept state callbacks. Content's `dir` overrides Ledger's inherited positioning direction.

Use Group around related items and Label first inside that Group; the Label names the Group. A Label outside any Group or RadioGroup names nothing: it still renders, in a group of its own, and says so once in the console. Items compose icons and text as children. An action that destroys or cannot be undone uses `variant="danger"`, the word Button uses, so a Delete button and the Delete item beside it say the same thing; a disabled danger item fades like any other, so it never looks ready to run. `variant="destructive"` is the deprecated spelling, kept for one version: it renders as `danger`; write `danger`. `inset` aligns labels and items without icons. The row uses Ledger's 28px menu height.

Action labels stay on one line. The menu is as wide as its longest label within the window; where a label is still wider, it ends in an ellipsis at the menu's edge instead of being cut mid-word, and a pointer resting on it shows the whole label. Its accessible name is always the whole label.

_Example: story `Stories.ActionLabelWidths`._

`shortcut` on an Item names the keys that run the same action from the page, written once for every platform as [KbdShortcut](?path=/docs/components-kbd--docs) takes them ("Mod+E", "Shift+D"). They are drawn at the end in the platform's glyphs and given to the item as `aria-keyshortcuts`, so the item's name stays its label ("Edit", not "Edit E"). Binding the keys stays with the caller. Shortcut, the part the prop draws, is hidden from assistive technology; other content at the end of a row that a reader needs, such as a count, passes `aria-hidden={false}` to it.

_Example: story `Stories.Actions`._

_Example: story `Stories.LabelOutsideAGroup`._

## Descriptions and disabled reasons

`description` on DropdownMenuItem adds a second line under the label, in smaller subtle text that wraps inside the menu: what tells two similar actions apart (“Keeps the current version as the baseline”), or a prerequisite. The label and the line share one column between the item's icon and its Shortcut. The line is the item's accessible description, not part of its name, so the arrow keys and typeahead still find the label alone. Keep it to a short phrase; a menu that needs a paragraph per item is a dialog.

An action that cannot run takes `disabledReason` instead of `disabled`: the item is disabled, the arrow keys still reach it, a screen reader announces it as unavailable and reads the reason, and the reason shows as its description line, readable on the faded row. Write what would make it available: “Add content to this version before publishing it.” A tooltip cannot do this job inside a menu, and a disabled item without a reason leaves the reader guessing.

_Example: story `Stories.DescriptionsAndReasons`._

## Choices and closing

Use CheckboxItem with `checked` and `onCheckedChange` for independent options; a check marks one that is on. Use RadioGroup with `value` and `onValueChange`, and RadioItem with `value`, for exclusive options; a dot marks the chosen one. Put each kind in its own Group with a Label, apart from the actions and separated from them, so an unchecked option and a plain action never look alike. A change callback's `details.cancel()` rejects the change. The installed Base UI radio value contract is not generic; callers can validate values against their own options.

Ordinary Item actions use `onClick` and close by default. CheckboxItem and RadioItem stay open by default; set `closeOnClick` when selecting should close the menu. Columns keep the menu open while toggling visibility; saved views and sorting close after a choice. Essential form values still belong in labeled form controls.

_Example: story `Stories.Toggles`._

## Submenus and links

Sub, SubTrigger and SubContent create a nested menu. SubContent defaults to start alignment, -3px alignment offset, zero side offset and a 96px minimum (`dimension.part.submenu`). Its logical `inline-end` side and chevron follow the locale. Escape closes the submenu first; Root's `closeParentOnEsc` can change that behavior.

LinkItem is Base UI's native anchor part. Give it `href`, or `render` a router Link, to retain navigation and modified clicks. It stays open by default; `closeOnClick` closes after navigation. Item with a rendered action button instead uses `nativeButton`. The public Portal part is available for custom Base UI compositions; Content already includes one.

_Example: story `Stories.Submenus`._

## Accessibility and dialogs

The trigger exposes `aria-haspopup="menu"` and expanded state. Items use `menuitem`, `menuitemcheckbox` or `menuitemradio`, with checked state where appropriate; a Label names its Group. Enter, Space or ArrowDown opens from the trigger; arrows, Home, End and typeahead navigate; Enter or Space activates an action. Disabled items remain focusable and announce their disabled state, but cannot activate; give them a `disabledReason` so the reason is announced with them. An item's shortcut is `aria-keyshortcuts`, not part of its name. Root defaults to modal with looping keyboard navigation. In forced colours the highlighted row is Highlight and a disabled row GrayText.

A row-action button must remain keyboard-reachable. Use `opacity-0 focus-visible:opacity-100 group-hover/row:opacity-100 data-popup-open:opacity-100` for visual concealment, rather than `visibility: hidden`, which removes it from keyboard navigation.

Content owns `finalFocus`. Ledger's modal wrappers resolve an activating menu item to its stable menu trigger, so closing the dialog returns there. For custom modal compositions, give the dialog an explicit return ref and use `finalFocus={false}` if menu focus return must be suppressed. A menu inside a Base UI dialog shares its portal boundary; Escape dismisses the menu before its parent dialog.

_Example: story `Stories.Dialogs`._

## Props

DropdownMenu follows [shadcn Dropdown Menu](https://ui.shadcn.com/docs/components/base/dropdown-menu) and [Base UI Menu](https://base-ui.com/react/components/menu), whose pages give the native APIs. DropdownMenuContent adds the four positioning props to Base UI's Popup; Ledger adds the token styling and the locale and dialog integration.

| `inset` | `boolean` |  |  |

### DropdownMenuContent

_Props of `DropdownMenuContent`, generated from its types:_

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | `string` |  | @ignore |
| `finalFocus` | `boolean \| RefObject<HTMLElement \| null> \| ((closeType: InteractionType) => boolean \| void \| HTMLElement \| null)` |  | Determines the element to focus when the menu is closed. - `false`: Do not move focus. - `true`: Move focus based on the default behavior (trigger or previously focused element). - `RefObject`: Move focus to the ref element. - `function`: Called with the interaction type (`mouse`, `touch`, `pen`, or `keyboard`). Return an element to focus, `true` to use the default behavior, or `false`/`undefined` to do nothing. |

| `side` | `"bottom" \| "inline-end" \| "inline-start" \| "left" \| "right" \| "top"` | `bottom` | Which side of the anchor element to align the popup against. May automatically change to avoid collisions. |
| `align` | `"center" \| "end" \| "start"` | `start` | How to align the popup relative to the specified side. |
| `sideOffset` | `number \| OffsetFunction` | `4` | Distance between the anchor and the popup in pixels. Also accepts a function that returns the distance to read the dimensions of the anchor and positioner elements, along with its side and alignment. The function takes a `data` object parameter with the following properties: - `data.anchor`: the dimensions of the anchor element with properties `width` and `height`. - `data.positioner`: the dimensions of the positioner element with properties `width` and `height`. - `data.side`: which side of the anchor element the positioner is aligned against. - `data.align`: how the positioner is aligned relative to the specified side. @example ```jsx <Positioner sideOffset={({ side, align, anchor, positioner }) => { return side === 'top' \|\| side === 'bottom' ? anchor.height : anchor.width; }} /> ``` |

# DropZone

**Status: Stable.**

A region files can be dropped on, with a [FileTrigger](?path=/docs/components-filetrigger--docs) inside for the keyboard, a screen reader and a touch screen, which cannot drag. Every drop and every choice is checked against `accept`, `maxSize` and `multiple`; accepted files go to `onSelect`, each refused file gets a message, and the result is announced.

Use it where attaching files is the task: an upload form, an import, a record's files. For an attach button in a compact spot (a composer, a toolbar), use a FileTrigger on its own. DropZone chooses files and checks them; it does not upload them. Show the accepted files as [Attachment](?path=/docs/components-attachment--docs) rows and run the upload yourself.

_Example: story `Stories.Playground`._

## Anatomy

```tsx
<Field required>
  <FieldLabel>Supporting files</FieldLabel>
  <DropZone accept="application/pdf,image/*" maxSize={5_000_000} multiple onSelect={upload}>
    <FieldDescription>PDF or image, up to 5 MB each.</FieldDescription>
  </DropZone>
</Field>
```

- **Title**: the instruction for a pointer, "Drag a file here" or "Drag files here" with `multiple`; `title` replaces it.
- **Children**: the constraints, as a FieldDescription, under the title. In a Field they describe the trigger.
- **Trigger**: a FileTrigger with the zone's `accept`, `multiple` and `disabled`, labelled "Choose a file" or "Choose files"; `triggerLabel` replaces the words and `triggerRef` reaches the button.
- **Refusals**: one line per refused file (a drop of too many files is one line), under the trigger.

Put the zone in a [Field](?path=/docs/components-field--docs). The FieldLabel names the trigger, the FieldDescription describes it, `required` adds "(required)" to its name, and a FieldError of your own, for a problem found on submit, describes it too. Leave the Field's `invalid` unset unless a form library owns it: a FieldError that shows marks the Field invalid by itself, the zone's or yours. Outside a Field the trigger is named by its own words alone (give it `triggerLabel` words that say what to choose), and a refusal still describes it and marks it invalid.

_Example: story `Stories.WithoutAField`._

## Checking files

The zone reads `accept` as the file input does: a media type matches the file's type, a wildcard (`image/*`) its family, an extension (`.pdf`) the end of its name, and `*/*` any file. `maxSize` is bytes per file; write it in decimal units (`5_000_000` for 5 MB), since the message formats it with `formatFileSize`. Without `multiple`, a drop of several files refuses them all with one message.

| Reason  | Message (locale key)                                            |
| ------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `type`  | "notes.docx is not an accepted file type." (`fileTypeRejected`) |
| `size`  | "survey.pdf is larger than 5 MB." (`fileTooLarge`)              |
| `count` | "Add one file at a time." (`fileCountRejected`)                 |

Accepted files in the same drop still go to `onSelect`; `onReject` receives the refusals, each with its `file`, `reason` and `message`. The refusals show in the zone as the Field's FieldError: they describe the trigger, turn the Field invalid (the label and the border take the danger colour, and the trigger `aria-invalid`), and stay until the next drop or choice replaces them. A Field's explicit `invalid={false}` keeps the label at rest, but the trigger and the border still show the refusal.

_Example: story `Stories.Validation`._

## Dragging

While files are dragged over it the zone's border turns solid and takes the selected colour, and its title reads "Drop the file to add it" or "Drop the files to add them", so the state does not rest on colour and survives forced colours. Text or a link dragged across the page does not light it. A click on the zone's surface opens the picker, for a pointer; the trigger is still the only tab stop.

_Example: story `Stories.DragAndDrop`._

`disabled`, on the zone, its Field or a FieldSet, disables the trigger and refuses drops; the zone still takes the drag, so the browser does not open a file dropped on it.

## The upload flow

The caller owns what happens to the files. The pattern the stories show:

- Each accepted file becomes an Attachment row in `uploading`, with a labelled [Progress](?path=/docs/components-progress--docs) and a Cancel named for the file ("Cancel uploading plan.pdf").
- A failed upload keeps its row in `error` with the reason in the Description, a Retry and a Remove, each named for the file.
- A finished row is `done`, with the type and the size (`formatFileSize`) and a Download.
- Each result is announced (`announce`: "Uploaded plan.pdf.", "Could not upload scan.png."). After a removal, focus goes to the trigger (`triggerRef`).
- The primary stays enabled. On submit, say what is missing in a FieldError and move focus to the trigger: no file yet, a file still uploading, a failed upload not yet retried or removed.

_Example: story `Stories.UploadFlow`._

## Accessibility

- One tab stop, the trigger. Enter or Space opens the picker; a click on its label does too.
- The result of a drop or a choice is announced politely, since focus stays on the trigger: "Added plan.pdf.", "Added 2 files.", and each refusal. The messages are in the locale (`fileAdded`, `filesAddedOne`, `filesAddedOther`, `dropFileHere`, `dropFilesHere`, `dropFileRelease`, `dropFilesRelease`, `chooseFile`, `chooseFiles` and the three above), so a LedgerProvider can translate them.
- The drag state is a border style and a title as well as a colour. The icon is decorative.
- A refusal is text in the zone and the trigger's description, never only the danger border.
- The zone responds to its own width: its content is one centred column that wraps, and a long file name in a refusal breaks inside it.

## Props

_Props of `DropZone`, generated from its types:_

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `accept` | `string \| readonly string[]` |  | The accepted types, as the file input's `accept`: media types (`application/pdf`), wildcards (`image/*`) and extensions (`.csv`). Checked on every drop and choice. Any file by default. |
| `maxSize` | `number` |  | The largest accepted file, in bytes, checked per file. Write it in decimal units (`50_000_000` is 50 MB) so the message matches a "50 MB" hint. No limit by default. |
| `multiple` | `boolean` | `false` | Accepts several files at once. One by default; several dropped then are all refused. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` |  | Refuses drops and disables the trigger. A Field's or FieldSet's `disabled` also reaches it. |
| `onSelect` | `((files: File[]) => void)` |  | Called with the accepted files of each drop or choice, when there is at least one. |
| `onReject` | `((rejections: FileRejection[]) => void)` |  | Called with the refused files of each drop or choice, when there is at least one. |
| `title` | `ReactNode` |  | The instruction for a pointer. "Drag a file here", or "Drag files here" with `multiple`. While files are dragged over the zone it reads "Drop the file to add it". |
| `triggerLabel` | `ReactNode` |  | The trigger's label. "Choose a file", or "Choose files" with `multiple`. |
| `triggerRef` | `Ref<HTMLButtonElement>` |  | The trigger button, to move focus to it after a removal or a failed submit. |
| `icon` | `ReactElement<unknown, string \| JSXElementConstructor<any>> \| null` |  | Replace the upload icon, or `null` for none. Decorative. |
| `children` | `ReactNode` |  | Under the title: the constraints, as a FieldDescription ("PDF or image, up to 50 MB each"). |

_Rendered in the Storybook: Controls._

## Related

[FileTrigger](?path=/docs/components-filetrigger--docs) · [Attachment](?path=/docs/components-attachment--docs) · [Field](?path=/docs/components-field--docs) · [Progress](?path=/docs/components-progress--docs). Reference: [Carbon file uploader](https://carbondesignsystem.com/components/file-uploader/usage/), [React Aria DropZone](https://react-spectrum.adobe.com/react-aria/DropZone.html), [Polaris DropZone](https://polaris-react.shopify.com/components/selection-and-input/drop-zone).

## Don't

The primary stays enabled and names what is missing on submit, never disabled until a file is chosen, which tells the reader nothing about what it waits for.

_Example: story `Stories.DoDont`._

<!-- page: Components/Empty (src/stories/components/Empty.mdx) -->

# Empty

**Status: Stable.**

A region with nothing in it says why, and offers the next step. The picture, the message and the actions sit at the centre of the region; the caller composes them from the parts. A [DataTable](?path=/docs/patterns-data-table--docs) draws its own, so a register never needs to.

_Example: story `Stories.Playground`._

## When to use it

- **A region with nothing in it yet**: a list, a card or a panel before its first record, with the step that creates one.
- **A search or a filter that leaves nothing**: what matched nothing, and the way to widen it (**Clear filters**).
- **A record that is not there, or a region that failed with nothing else to show**: what is missing or what failed, and the way back or **Try again**.

Not for a load in progress: that is a [Skeleton](?path=/docs/components-skeleton--docs) or a [Spinner](?path=/docs/components-spinner--docs). Not for a failure beside content that stays on the page: that is an [Alert](?path=/docs/components-alert--docs). Not for one value that is missing: that is [Absent](?path=/docs/components-typography--docs), heard as "Not recorded". Not for a register's table: a [DataTable](?path=/docs/patterns-data-table--docs) draws its own empties.

## Anatomy

```tsx
<Empty>
  <EmptyMedia aria-hidden>
    <EmptyIllustration kind="records" />
  </EmptyMedia>
  <EmptyHeader>
    <EmptyTitle>No programs yet</EmptyTitle>
    <EmptyDescription>Create one to define its systems and their work.</EmptyDescription>
  </EmptyHeader>
  <EmptyContent>
    <Button variant="primary" iconBefore={<Plus />}>
      New program
    </Button>
    <Button variant="secondary">Import</Button>
  </EmptyContent>
</Empty>
```

| Part                | What it is                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| ------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Empty`             | The region: a column, centred, on a dashed frame. `size="compact"` for the rail's row; `frame="none"` on a surface that already bounds it.                                                    |
| `EmptyMedia`        | The picture. Holds an `EmptyIllustration`, or `variant="icon"` draws a Lucide icon in the neutral circle. Anything else fits: an avatar, a chart's ghost.                                     |
| `EmptyIllustration` | The kit's picture, on the surface tokens: a scene of ghost records the shape of what the region will hold, sometimes with a badge that says why it is empty. Twelve kinds, below. Decorative. |
| `EmptyHeader`       | The title and its description, at a readable measure.                                                                                                                                         |
| `EmptyTitle`        | A heading in the default size, at the contextual level (an h2 when nothing sets one); body text in a div in compact. `render` sets another element.                                           |
| `EmptyDescription`  | One or two lines: why there is nothing, what creates it.                                                                                                                                      |
| `EmptyContent`      | The actions, centred, wrapping. A second `EmptyContent` holds a quieter row: a link, suggested searches.                                                                                      |

## Variants

Which empty this is decides the picture and the action. The picture is the shape of what the region will hold, so a reader who has never seen a record still learns what one is:

| The region                                      | `kind`             | Action                                                                             |
| ----------------------------------------------- | ------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Nothing exists yet                              | `records`          | The primary: create the first, import                                              |
| A search or a filter left nothing               | `search`           | Clear filters; suggestions under it                                                |
| Empty because the work is finished              | `done`             | A link to the closed items, or none                                                |
| Nothing assigned or waiting for you             | `inbox`            | None, or a link to everything                                                      |
| Waiting on someone else (a review, an approval) | an icon (Clock)    | None; the description says who acts. Never `done`, which says the work is finished |
| The reader may not see this                     | `locked`           | Request access                                                                     |
| No controls or requirements yet                 | `shield`           | Allocate, map, import a catalog                                                    |
| No files, evidence or documents                 | `document`         | Upload, attach                                                                     |
| No tasks or work items                          | `tasks`            | Add a task                                                                         |
| No people, owners or assignees                  | `people`           | Assign, invite                                                                     |
| No systems, components or parts                 | `tree`             | Add the first node                                                                 |
| No data to chart                                | `chart`            | None; the records make the chart                                                   |
| Nothing scheduled                               | `calendar`         | Schedule                                                                           |
| The record does not exist                       | `search`           | The route back, a link                                                             |
| It could not load, and nothing else shows       | an icon (CloudOff) | Try again                                                                          |
| A tab or a card body with no items              | an icon            | One small action                                                                   |
| A rail's related list                           | compact            | One link                                                                           |

A [DataTable](?path=/docs/patterns-data-table--docs) with no records at all is only its Empty: the toolbar, the header and the hairline go, the frame stays, and the action in it creates the first record. While a search or a filter is what emptied it, the toolbar and header stay and the Empty sits under them without a frame.

_Example: story `Stories.NoMatches`._

_Example: story `Stories.Illustrations`._

_Example: story `Stories.Icon`._

_Example: story `Stories.Compact`._

_Example: story `Stories.NotFound`._

_Example: story `Stories.FailedToLoad`._

## Sizes

`default` is the hero: the picture, a small heading, body copy, medium buttons, `space.300` between the three, `space.600` above and below. `compact` is the rail's row: an icon beside the message, a medium-weight body title, small body copy, a small link.

The hero's buttons are medium even when the caller hands over a small one. A collection passes its toolbar's create action as it is, so an `EmptyContent` in the default size that holds a small primary kit button (Button, IconButton, LinkButton or LinkIconButton) draws every small kit button in that row at medium: the button itself, the halves of a split `ButtonGroup`, and a menu trigger's `render` element. A row without a small primary keeps its sizes, so the suggestions' small secondary buttons and an icon Empty's one small action stay small. Compact never changes a size.

_Example: story `Stories.HeroActions`._

The order is the same in both sizes: `EmptyMedia`, then `EmptyHeader`, then `EmptyContent`, each a direct child of `Empty`. In the default size that puts `space.300` between the picture and the title; in compact the grid puts the media in the first column and the message and the actions in the second. An `EmptyMedia` inside `EmptyHeader` sits `space.100` above the title, and an `EmptyIllustration` in a compact Empty is a 128 by 84 scene in a row drawn for an icon; each says so once in the browser console, as a warning that never stops the Empty from rendering.

## States

Empty has no states of its own. Loading is [Skeleton](?path=/docs/components-skeleton--docs) or [Spinner](?path=/docs/components-spinner--docs), never an Empty. A failure where other content stays on the page is an [Alert](?path=/docs/components-alert--docs) beside that content; a page or a region that failed and has nothing else to show is an icon Empty that says what failed, with **Try again** (Failed to load, above). A DataTable chooses between its two empties itself: the caller's message when there are no records, the kit's **Nothing matches** with **Clear filters** while a search, a column filter or the caller's own narrowing is active.

## Modifiers

- **`size`**: `default` or `compact`.
- **`frame`**: `dashed` (the default region) or `none`, for a table cell, a page body, a panel that has its own edges. Compact never draws a frame.
- **`kind`** on `EmptyIllustration`: the twelve above. Every scene is 128 by 84px, so empty states sit at one height across a page.

_Example: story `Stories.OnAPage`._

## Content

- **The title says what is missing, in the reader's words**: "No programs yet", "Nothing matches", "Nothing open". Not "Empty", not "No data".
- **The description says why, or what creates it**, in one or two lines. Never advice that points at another control ("Choose another tab").
- **One primary action**, the same verb as the page's own; a secondary beside it at most. In a filtered table the action is **Clear filters**.
- **Suggestions are small secondary buttons** in a second row, after a "Try" in `color.text.subtlest`.
- **One action on the page.** Where a Section's header or a toolbar already carries the create action, the Empty under it says what is missing and stops; it does not repeat the button a tab stop later.
- **A missing record names what is missing and the way back**: "Task not found", why, and a link to the list it came from.

## Long content

A title or a description with an unbroken code, hash or address breaks where it must (`overflow-wrap: anywhere`) inside the message's 400px measure (`dimension.part.emptyMeasure`), so the centred block never widens past its frame or the page.

_Example: story `Stories.LongContent`._

## Style

| Element      | Token                                                                                                                                             |
| ------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Frame        | `color.border` dashed · `radius.large` · `space.300` × `space.600`                                                                                |
| Gaps         | `space.300` between picture, message and actions · `space.100` between title and description                                                      |
| Title        | `font.heading.page` at medium · `color.text`                                                                                                      |
| Description  | `font.body` · `color.text.subtle` · `dimension.part.emptyMeasure`, a 400px measure                                                                |
| Icon circle  | `dimension.control.large` · `color.background.neutral` · `color.icon.subtle`                                                                      |
| Illustration | 128 × 84px · `elevation.surface.raised` and `.sunken` · `color.border` and `.bold` · `color.skeleton` · `color.background.neutral`                |
| Badge        | `dimension.control.medium` · `color.background.neutral.bold`, `.success.bold` or `.brand.bold` · `color.icon.inverse` · `elevation.shadow.raised` |
| Compact      | no frame · `space.150` between media and message · `font.body` medium · `font.body.small`                                                         |

## Accessibility

The parts are divs with no automatic landmark or announcement, except the title. In the default size EmptyTitle is a real heading at the contextual level, so a page whose content is an Empty (a first run, a missing record, a route that failed) keeps it in the heading outline: an h2 under the page's h1 when nothing sets a level, one below a titled Section. Where the Empty is the page's only content and there is no PageHeader, give it the page's level with `render={<h1 />}`; where it must not be in the outline, `render={<div />}`. In compact, a rail's row, the title is body text. Give the root `role="region"` and `aria-labelledby` the title when the region is a page's main content; inside a table the cell is enough.

_Example: story `Stories.TitleLevel`._

The illustration and the icon circle are decorative: `EmptyIllustration` hides itself, and `EmptyMedia` takes `aria-hidden`. Text precedes the actions in reading order, so a screen reader hears why before what. In forced colours a scene keeps its drawing: its surfaces are Canvas with a CanvasText edge, its ghost lines and bars GrayText, a badge a CanvasText disc with a Canvas glyph, and the icon circle keeps its edge.

## Props

_Props of `Empty`, generated from its types:_

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `size` | `"compact" \| "default"` | `default` | `default` centres the message under its media; `compact` puts media beside it, for a rail or a card. |
| `frame` | `"dashed" \| "none"` | `dashed` | The dashed border is the default region. `none` for a surface that already bounds it: a table, a page. Compact never has a frame. |

_Props of `EmptyMedia`, generated from its types:_

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `variant` | `"icon" \| "default" \| null` | `default` |  |

_Props of `EmptyIllustration`, generated from its types:_

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `kind` | `EmptyIllustrationKind` | `records` | Which scene. `records` by default. |

_Props: generated from `EmptyHeader`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._

_Props of `EmptyTitle`, generated from its types:_

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `render` | `ReactElement<unknown, string \| JSXElementConstructor<any>> \| ComponentRenderFn<HTMLProps, {}>` |  | Allows you to replace the component's HTML element with a different tag, or compose it with another component. Accepts a `ReactElement` or a function that returns the element to render. |

_Props: generated from `EmptyDescription`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._
_Props: generated from `EmptyContent`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._

Every part accepts native div attributes, events, styles and refs; EmptyTitle takes its heading's and `render`. Icon children retain their own props, classes and refs.

### In other parts

The default is the centred hero: a heading, the description at a measure, the actions under it. A left-aligned row with a body-weight title is `size="compact"`. `Related`, `Item.Group` and `DataTable` compose the parts themselves; a DataTable's `empty` takes `illustration`, `secondary` and `filtered`, and draws **Nothing matches** with **Clear filters** on its own while a search, a filter or the caller's `narrowed` is active.

_Example: story `Stories.EmptyMatrix`._

## Related
