Sources: [shadcn Empty](https://ui.shadcn.com/docs/components/base/empty), [ReUI empty state](https://reui.io/blocks/empty-state), [Atlassian Empty state](https://atlassian.design/components/empty-state), [Carbon empty states pattern](https://carbondesignsystem.com/patterns/empty-states-pattern).

## Don't

A filtered table's empty says what emptied it and offers Clear filters, never a grey line where the rows were. An empty state's action is the page's own verb, never advice that points at another control, and under a header that already carries the create action it says what is missing and stops.

_Example: story `Stories.Dont`._

<!-- page: Components/ErrorSummary (src/stories/components/ErrorSummary.mdx) -->

# ErrorSummary

**Status: Stable.**

Every issue with a submitted form in one place. A danger Alert titled "There is a problem" that lists each issue as a button; the button moves focus to the field, with its label in view. The summary takes focus when it appears, so a reader who submits lands on the list of what to fix.

```tsx
<ErrorSummary
  focusKey={attempts}
  issues={[
    { message: "Enter a task title.", target: titleId },
    { message: "Choose a program.", target: () => programRef.current },
  ]}
/>
```

_Example: story `Stories.OnSubmit`._

## When to use it

- **A long form or a dialog that scrolls**, where some invalid fields are out of sight after a submission.
- **A multi-step flow**, on the last step, for issues on earlier steps.

Each field still shows its own [FieldError](?path=/docs/components-field--docs). A short form whose fields all fit on screen needs no summary: focus the first invalid control instead. A failure that is not about a field (a lost connection, a refused permission) is an [Alert](?path=/docs/components-alert--docs) with `role="alert"`.

_Example: story `Stories.DoDont`._

## Issues

- **`message`** says what fixes the field and names it, in the same words as its FieldError: "Enter a task title.", not "Required.".
- **`target`** is the control: its `id`, the element, or a function that finds it. A RadioGroup or a FieldSet focuses its first focusable control; a Checkbox or Switch `id`, which names the hidden input, focuses the visible box.
- **`onSelect`** runs before focus moves, to open the step or tab that holds the field; the summary then focuses the field once it has rendered.
- An issue with neither `target` nor `onSelect` (a rule across two fields) is listed as text, not a button, because it leads nowhere.

List the issues in the order the fields appear, and pass the ones found at the last submission. Recomputing them on every keystroke re-announces the alert while the reader types; the fields' own errors update as the reader repairs them.

_Example: story `Stories.EarlierStep`._

## Focus

The summary focuses itself when it appears. Change `focusKey` on each failed submission (a submit count) to bring focus back to a summary already showing. `autoFocus={false}` leaves focus where it is, for a summary rendered on arrival at a step. With no issues it renders nothing, so it can stay in place above the form.

With TanStack Form, an error returned from `onSubmitAsync` is cleared on the field's next blur, and the summary taking focus is that blur: keep a server rejection in your own state until the reader changes the value, as the Forms recovery story does.

_Example: story `Stories.NoIssues`._

## Accessibility

- `role="alert"` announces the summary when it appears; focus lands on it, named by its title, and Tab reaches the first item.
- The title is a heading at the contextual level (an h2 outside every HeadingLevelProvider, an h3 under a level-3 provider), so the summary is in the page's outline.
- Items are buttons, because they act on the page; each moves focus with the keyboard focus ring showing and brings the field's label into view.
- The icon is decorative; the title and the danger surface say it is an error, not the colour alone.

_Example: story `Stories.InSection`._

## Props

_Props of `ErrorSummary`, generated from its types:_

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `issues` (required) | `readonly ErrorSummaryIssue[]` |  | Every issue from the last submission, in the order the fields appear. Renders nothing when empty. |
| `title` | `ReactNode` |  | The title, a heading at the contextual level (an h2 outside every HeadingLevelProvider). Defaults to the locale's "There is a problem". |
| `focusKey` | `string \| number` |  | Change it on every failed submission (a submit count) to bring focus back to a summary already showing. |

_Example: story `Stories.Playground`._

_Rendered in the Storybook: Controls._

## Related

[Field](?path=/docs/components-field--docs) · [Forms](?path=/docs/patterns-forms--docs) · [Alert](?path=/docs/components-alert--docs) · [GOV.UK error summary](https://design-system.service.gov.uk/components/error-summary/)

<!-- page: Components/Fact (src/stories/components/Fact.mdx) -->

# Fact

**Status: Stable.**

An inline label and value on one baseline: Owner Dana Whitfield, Frequency Quarterly. A row of them is a `Fact.Group`, the facts strip under a record's title: the four to six facts the reader acts on, above the fold, so that needing to open a panel to find out who owns a thing is never the problem. The rest belong in the rail as [KeyValue](?path=/docs/components-keyvalue--docs) rows. The strip most page headers write by hand.

_Example: story `Stories.FactMatrix`._

## Anatomy

| Part  | What it is                                                                                                                   |
| ----- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Label | `dt` in `font.body.small` and `color.text.subtle`, one or two words.                                                         |
| Value | `dd` after it, `space.075` away, `font.body` medium in `color.text`: a word, a number, a date, a Person, a Badge, an Absent. |
| Group | A `dl` that wraps: `space.300` between facts, `space.075` between lines, every fact whole on its line.                       |

## Variants

Fact has one appearance. What varies is where the strip is:

| Where                  | What it holds                                                         |
| ---------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Under a record's title | The facts the reader acts on: owner, due, method, count. At most six. |
| In a Sheet's header    | The same, for the record the sheet shows.                             |
| In a Glance            | Three or four, for the record previewed.                              |

Not built, and why: a stacked label-over-value grid, which is [KeyValue.Group](?path=/docs/components-keyvalue--docs)'s `stacked` layout; a Fact that edits in place, because the value is an [Editable](?path=/docs/patterns-editable--docs) and the Fact only frames it.

## Sizes

One size: the label `font.body.small`, the value `font.body`. The strip is as wide as its header and wraps between facts when narrower, so each fact that fits keeps its line.

_Example: story `Stories.UnderHeader`._

## Long content

A fact is short by rule (one or two words, one value), but a value the data makes long does not push the strip wider: it wraps under itself, and an unbroken token (a URN, a hash, a URL) breaks where it must. The label never truncates and never wraps. A Fact never cuts its value; a value that needs a reveal is a KeyValue in the rail, where a row field truncates with one.

_Example: story `Stories.LongValue`._

## States

A Fact has one state. Its value may: a Badge is a state, a Person is a person, an Editable value opens. The Fact does not.

## Modifiers

- **The value** is the modifier: text, a Person, a Badge at `xsmall`, an Id, an Absent, an Editable.
- **Group `className`** for the rule above the strip under a header.

## Content

- **The label is one or two words, a noun:** "Owner", "Next due", "Open findings".
- **The value is one thing that fits on a line:** a name, a number, a date, a state. A sentence is Prose or a wrapping KeyValue.
- **Four to six facts, the ones acted on.** Reference joins (created by, framework, family) go in the rail.
- **A missing value stays, as an Absent**, so the strip says what is missing.

## Style

| Element | Token                                                                     |
| ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Label   | `font.body.small` · `color.text.subtle`                                   |
| Value   | `font.body` medium · `color.text` · `space.075` after the label           |
| Group   | `space.300` between facts · `space.075` between wrapped lines · baselines |

## Accessibility

- **A group is a definition list** and each Fact a `dt` and `dd`, so a screen reader hears "Owner, Dana Whitfield" as a pair. A Fact belongs inside a Fact.Group; the headers and sheets that take a `facts` slot wrap it.
- **The strip is read in order**, so the order is the order of importance.
- **An Absent is heard, not skipped**: a screen reader hears "Owner, Not recorded" in place of the dash. Give it a `label` where the fact says more ("None", "No due date").
- **Contrast:** the label in `color.text.subtle` passes 4.5:1; the gate runs the matrix.

## Props

_Props of `Fact`, generated from its types:_

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `label` (required) | `string` |  | The fact's name, one or two words: "Owner", "Frequency". |
| `children` (required) | `ReactNode` |  | The value: a word, a number, a Person, a Badge, an Absent. |

### Fact.Group

_Props of `FactGroup`, generated from its types:_

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `children` (required) | `ReactNode` |  | Fact children, the ones the reader acts on. At most six under a header. |

Fact takes a div's native props and a ref, and Fact.Group a `dl`'s; each names itself last with `data-slot` (`fact`, `fact-group`).

_Example: story `Stories.NativeAttributes`._

### Playground

_Example: story `Stories.Playground`._

_Rendered in the Storybook: Controls._

## Related

- [KeyValue](?path=/docs/components-keyvalue--docs): the row, for the rail.
- [PageHeader](?path=/docs/layout-pageheader--docs), [Sheet](?path=/docs/components-sheet--docs), [Glance](?path=/docs/patterns-glance--docs): the `facts` slots.
- [Typography](?path=/docs/components-typography--docs): `Absent`, and `Prose` for the sentence that is not a fact.

## Don't

A Fact strip holds the four to six facts the reader acts on, each one value that fits a line, and keeps a missing one as an Absent. Reference joins go in the rail and a sentence is Prose, never eleven facts in a strip or an empty fact dropped.

_Example: story `Stories.Dont`._

<!-- page: Components/Field (src/stories/components/Field.mdx) -->

# Field

**Status: Stable.**

One control with its label, hint and error. Field is Base UI's Field underneath, so the parts tie themselves to the control: no ids, no `htmlFor`, no `aria-describedby` and no `aria-invalid` written by hand. The form still owns values and validation; the Field carries what the form decided.

```tsx
<Field invalid={invalid} required>
  <FieldLabel>Owner</FieldLabel>
  <Input value={owner} onValueChange={setOwner} />
  <FieldDescription>Use the full name.</FieldDescription>
  <FieldError errors={errors} />
</Field>
```

The label names the control and its click focuses it; the hint and the error describe it, in that order; `invalid` reaches the control as `aria-invalid` and `data-invalid` and turns the label and the error to the danger colour; `required` announces the requirement and adds the label's asterisk, which is hidden from the accessible name. The same binding reaches Input, Textarea, InputGroupInput, the Select trigger, the Combobox input, Checkbox, RadioGroup and Switch.

_Example: story `Stories.EveryControl`._

## When to use it

- **Every form control** a reader fills in: an Input, a Textarea, a Select, a Combobox, a NumberField, a date or time field, a Checkbox, a RadioGroup or a Switch takes its label, hint and error through a Field, so a form writes no ids and no ARIA.
- **A group of choices**: a Field around a FieldSet, with a legend that names the group (Groups, below).
- **A choice card**: a FieldLabel wrapping a horizontal Field, where the whole card chooses.

Not for a value that is read where it is shown and not edited there: that is a [KeyValue](?path=/docs/components-keyvalue--docs). Not for a result that is about the whole form, such as a failed save or choices that did not load: that is an [Alert](?path=/docs/components-alert--docs) at the top of the form, and several issues are an [ErrorSummary](?path=/docs/components-errorsummary--docs). Not for one value edited in place on a record: that is an [Editable](?path=/docs/patterns-editable--docs), which names its own control.

## Content

- **The label names the value**, in a few words and sentence case, with no colon and no verb: "Owner", "Review frequency", "Program name", not "Enter the owner:". It stays visible; a placeholder never stands in for it.
- **The hint says what the value is for, or what form it takes**, in one line the reader sees before they type: "Use the full name.", "As it appears on the authorization package." A rule the value must keep is in the hint, so the error is never the first time the reader hears of it.
- **The error says what fixes the value**, in the field's words: "Enter an owner", "Choose a review frequency", "Use a day after the start date". Never "Invalid", "Error" or "This field is required".
- **The Field marks a required field**; a label or a placeholder never says "Optional" or "Required". Where most of a form is required, `FieldLabel required={false}` hides the asterisks and the few optional fields say so.
- **A group's legend asks what the choices answer** ("Review frequency"), and each choice's label names the choice, not its state.

## Parts

`FieldLabel`, `FieldDescription` and `FieldError` bind inside a Field and stay plain elements outside one. `FieldSet` and `FieldLegend` group related controls, and a RadioGroup inside a FieldSet is named by its legend. `FieldGroup` spaces fields and is a size container, so a form's grid can collapse by the form's own width (see [Forms](?path=/docs/patterns-forms--docs), Layout); `FieldContent` stacks text beside a control; `FieldTitle` is a choice card's title, where a wrapping label makes the whole card choose: it names the control on its own, so the card's FieldDescription describes the control once instead of also becoming its name. `FieldSeparator` divides sections, with optional text; its rules stop on either side of the text, so it works on any surface.

_Example: story `Stories.Composition`._

## States

- **`invalid`** comes from the form library (TanStack Form: `isTouched && !isValid`). A FieldError that shows a message also marks the Field invalid, so `<FieldError errors={errors} />` is enough when the errors are already filtered. A hand-set `data-invalid` is read as `invalid`.
- **`required`** is announced (`aria-required`) and marked; it is not a native constraint, so a form library that checks it is not second-guessed by the browser. Put native `required` on the control itself when Base UI or the browser should check it. `FieldLabel required={false}` hides the asterisk where most of a form is required and only the optional fields say so. A group Field requires the group, not each checkbox in it.
- **`disabled`** disables the control and dims the label. A Field or a FieldSet inside a disabled Field is disabled too, so a disabled group's legend and choices follow it. `disabled` on a FieldSet reaches every control inside, including the Checkbox, Radio and Switch roots that a native `<fieldset disabled>` leaves live. The label also dims when its control is disabled on its own or by a native fieldset, and a disabled choice dims only its own label.
- **Read-only** is the control's own `readOnly`: the sunken surface with a dashed edge and no hover on the text fields, Checkbox and Radio, and the neutral fill in place of the brand one on a Switch that is on. The label keeps its colour, since the value can still be read and copied. A value never edited where it is shown is a [KeyValue](?path=/docs/components-keyvalue--docs) instead.

_Example: story `Stories.Disabled`._

A focused invalid text field thickens its danger border to the 2px focus edge; a focused invalid Checkbox or Radio keeps its danger border with the focus outline around it, and a Switch swaps its danger outline for the focus outline, so focus is always visible.

A FieldSet is a form's lock while it saves: `disabled` holds every field and choice inside it, and it adds no border, padding or content-sized minimum, so a wide table inside it scrolls or clips within its frame instead of widening a dialog. It stacks its children `space.100` apart; `className` changes the gap.

_Example: story `Stories.SavingLock`._

In a horizontal Field a Checkbox, a Radio or a Switch sits on the first line of its label, however many lines the label wraps to, beside a bare FieldLabel or a FieldContent; beside a medium Switch the text steps down `space.025`, so its first line centres on the track. Any other control centres on its label.

_Example: story `Stories.ChoiceAlignment`._

A FieldLabel wrapping a horizontal Field becomes a choice card, with hover, the chosen state and one keyboard focus ring, drawn by the card rather than the control; a disabled card keeps a quiet surface, and an invalid Field edges its card in danger. The card's facts are its FieldDescription, its error a FieldError in its FieldContent, and a link to the option's record sits beside the card, never in the label. See the choice cards on [Checkbox](?path=/docs/components-checkbox--docs) and [RadioGroup](?path=/docs/components-radiogroup--docs).

## Validation

With a form library, pass `invalid` and the messages. Validate on submit, then on change; focus the first invalid control after a failed submission, or an [ErrorSummary](?path=/docs/components-errorsummary--docs) when the form is long.

_Example: story `Stories.Validation`._

Without one, Base UI validates: native constraints on the control, `validate` on the Field for your own rules, `validationMode` for when (`onSubmit`, then on change, by default), and a FieldError with `match` for each message. A FieldError with no children shows Base UI's own message whenever the Field fails.

_Example: story `Stories.NativeValidation`._

FieldError takes children or an `errors` array of message objects, drops duplicates and empty entries, and renders nothing when none remain; children win. It is not a live region: focus and the control's description carry it, and a form-level failure belongs in an Alert or an ErrorSummary.

_Example: story `Stories.Errors`._

## Groups

A group of choices is a Field around a FieldSet: the legend names the group, the Field's hint and error describe it, and `invalid` and `required` reach the RadioGroup (or the checkboxes of a [CheckboxGroup](?path=/docs/components-checkboxgroup--docs)) once; `disabled` reaches every choice. Each choice is its own horizontal Field with a FieldLabel, so it keeps its own name. A RadioGroup announces the requirement itself; a CheckboxGroup's legend says "(required)" to assistive technology, since a group cannot.

```tsx
<Field invalid={invalid} required>
  <FieldSet>
    <FieldLegend variant="label">Review frequency</FieldLegend>
    <RadioGroup value={frequency} onValueChange={setFrequency}>
      <Field orientation="horizontal">
        <RadioGroupItem value="quarterly" />
        <FieldLabel>Quarterly</FieldLabel>
      </Field>
    </RadioGroup>
    <FieldError errors={errors} />
  </FieldSet>
</Field>
```

## Accessibility

- The label names the control through `htmlFor` and `aria-labelledby`, and a Select or Combobox list inside the Field is named by it too. Ids are generated per instance, so a form can appear more than once.
- Hint and error ids reach `aria-describedby` in the order they render; ids the caller already references are listed once.
- Explicit ids, `htmlFor` and ARIA on the parts still win, and wrappers between Field and control do not break the binding. Hand-written ids, `aria-describedby`, `aria-invalid` and `data-invalid` keep working; a Field needs none of them.
- The date and number fields (DatePicker, DateRangePicker, TimeField, DateTimeField, NumberField) and SearchField take the binding as Input does.
- A Field is not a group of its own: it takes `role="group"` only when it is given a name (`aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`), so one control is not wrapped in an unnamed group.

_Example: story `Stories.ExplicitAssociations`._

An error is the Field's FieldError, which marks the control invalid and describes it, never red text beside a bare input, which nothing marks and a screen reader does not hear when focus reaches the input.

_Example: story `Stories.DoDont`._

## Props

_Props of `Field`, generated from its types:_

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `orientation` | `"horizontal" \| "vertical" \| "responsive" \| null` | `vertical` |  |
| `name` | `string` |  | Identifies the field when a form is submitted. Takes precedence over the `name` prop on the `<Field.Control>` component. |
| `actionsRef` | `RefObject<FieldRootActions \| null>` |  | A ref to imperative actions. - `validate`: Validates the field when called. |
| `validate` | `((value: unknown, formValues: Record<string, any>) => string \| string[] \| Promise<string \| string[] \| null> \| null)` |  | A function for custom validation. Return a string or an array of strings with the error message(s) if the value is invalid, or `null` if the value is valid. Asynchronous functions are supported, but they do not prevent form submission when using `validationMode="onSubmit"`. |
| `validationMode` | `"onBlur" \| "onChange" \| "onSubmit"` | `'onSubmit'` | Determines when the field should be validated. This takes precedence over the `validationMode` prop on `<Form>`. - `onSubmit`: triggers validation when the form is submitted, and re-validates on change after submission. - `onBlur`: triggers validation when the control loses focus. - `onChange`: triggers validation on every change to the control value. |
| `validationDebounceTime` | `number` | `0` | How long to wait between `validate` callbacks if `validationMode="onChange"` is used. Specified in milliseconds. |
| `dirty` | `boolean` |  | Whether the field's value has been changed from its initial value. Useful when the field state is controlled by an external library. |
| `touched` | `boolean` |  | Whether the field has been touched. Useful when the field state is controlled by an external library. |
| `invalid` | `boolean` |  | Marks the field invalid: the control gets `aria-invalid` and `data-invalid`, and the label and FieldError the danger colour. Pass it from the form library (TanStack Form: `isTouched && !isValid`). Defaults to true while a FieldError inside shows a message, and to Base UI's own result when `validate` or a native constraint fails. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` |  | Disables the control and dims the label. A FieldSet's `disabled` also reaches it, and so does an ancestor Field's, so each choice in its own Field follows a disabled group Field. |
| `required` | `boolean` |  | Announces the requirement on the control (`aria-required`) and shows the FieldLabel's or FieldLegend's asterisk. It is not a native constraint: the form library checks it, or the control's own `required` makes Base UI and the browser check it. A group Field requires the group, not every checkbox in it. |
| `render` | `ReactElement<unknown, string \| JSXElementConstructor<any>> \| ComponentRenderFn<HTMLProps, FieldRootState>` |  | Replace the field's element, or compose it with another component. |
| `data-invalid` | `boolean \| "true" \| "false"` |  | Earlier callers set this by hand; it is still read as `invalid`. Prefer `invalid`. |
| `data-disabled` | `boolean \| "" \| "true" \| "false"` |  | Dims the label without disabling the control, for a control disabled on its own. Prefer `disabled`. |

_Props of `FieldLabel`, generated from its types:_

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `required` | `boolean` |  | Shows the required marker, an asterisk hidden from assistive technology (the control announces the requirement). Defaults to the Field's `required`; `false` hides it where most of a form is required and only the optional fields are marked. |

_Props of `FieldError`, generated from its types:_

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `errors` | `({ message?: string; })[] \| undefined` |  | Messages from a form library (TanStack Form's `field.state.meta.errors`); duplicates and empty entries drop out. Children win. |
| `match` | `boolean \| keyof ValidityState` |  | Base UI validation inside a Field: the validity state that shows this message (`"valueMissing"`, `"typeMismatch"`, …). Without it, a FieldError with messages always shows them and marks the Field invalid, and one without shows Base UI's message whenever the Field fails its `validate` or a native constraint. |

_Props of `FieldSet`, generated from its types:_

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `render` | `ReactElement<unknown, string \| JSXElementConstructor<any>> \| ComponentRenderFn<HTMLProps, FieldsetRootState>` |  | Replace the fieldset element, or compose it with another component. |

_Props of `FieldLegend`, generated from its types:_

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `variant` | `"label" \| "legend"` | `legend` |  |
| `required` | `boolean` |  | Shows the required marker, as FieldLabel does. Defaults to the `required` of a Field around the FieldSet. In a CheckboxGroup, where no checkbox announces the requirement, the legend also says it to assistive technology (the locale's "(required)"). |

_Props: generated from `FieldTitle`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._

Every part forwards the native attributes and ref of its element: Field, FieldGroup, FieldContent, FieldTitle, FieldError and FieldSeparator are divs, FieldLabel a label, FieldDescription a paragraph, FieldSet a fieldset and FieldLegend a legend. Field and FieldSet take `render`. A test finds a FieldError by its text or `data-slot="field-error"`, not by a live role.

<!-- page: Components/FileTrigger (src/stories/components/FileTrigger.mdx) -->

# FileTrigger

**Status: Stable.**

A [Button](?path=/docs/components-button--docs) that opens the browser's file picker and hands the chosen files to `onSelect`. The native file input is in the document, hidden, so it takes no space, no focus and no place in the accessibility tree; the button is the control, and the picker returns focus to it when it closes.

Use it where the reader attaches a file from a compact spot: a form row, a composer, a toolbar. Where files can also be dropped, or where the files must be checked against a type or a size, use [DropZone](?path=/docs/components-dropzone--docs), which puts a FileTrigger inside a drop region and does the checking. Do not use `<Input type="file">`: its button loses its frame and the control reads as a line of text.

_Example: story `Stories.InAField`._

## Choosing files

- `accept` is the input's own attribute, as a string or a list: media types (`application/pdf`), wildcards (`image/*`) and extensions (`.csv`). The picker filters by it, but a reader can still pick another file, so check what you receive (DropZone does).
- `multiple` lets the reader choose several files at once; one by default. The label follows: "Choose a file" or "Choose files" (the `chooseFile` and `chooseFiles` messages).
- `onSelect` receives the files as an array once the picker closes with a choice. Cancelling calls nothing. The input is emptied after each choice, so choosing the same file again, after a removal or a failed upload, calls `onSelect` again.
- `capture` offers the camera directly on a phone: `environment` the rear one, `user` the front.
- `onClick` runs first; calling `preventDefault()` in it keeps the picker shut.
- The files are the caller's: FileTrigger does not submit them with a form. Show them as [Attachment](?path=/docs/components-attachment--docs) rows and upload them.

_Example: story `Stories.ChosenFilesAsAttachments`._

## In a Field

Inside a [Field](?path=/docs/components-field--docs) the button is the Field's control, as Base UI's own controls are:

- The FieldLabel points at it (`for`), so a click on the label opens the picker, as a native file input's label does.
- It is named by the label and then its own words, "Signed agreement Choose a file", so a speech command can use what the reader sees. `required` on the Field adds "(required)" to the name; a button cannot carry `aria-required`.
- The FieldDescription and FieldError describe it, and the Field's `invalid` reaches it as `aria-invalid`.
- The Field's or a FieldSet's `disabled` disables it.

An `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` of your own replaces the composed name.

## States

Every Button prop applies. `isLoading` keeps focus and blocks the picker while a choice is being read; `disabledReason` keeps the button reachable and says why it is unavailable; `disabled` takes it out.

_Example: story `Stories.States`._

In a [ButtonGroup](?path=/docs/components-buttongroup--docs) a FileTrigger is a segment like any Button: the hidden input is not counted, so the group rounds the trigger when it comes last.

_Example: story `Stories.InAButtonGroup`._

## Accessibility

- One tab stop: the button. The hidden input cannot be reached by Tab, is not read, and does not count as a second control.
- Enter and Space open the picker; the browser's picker is keyboard operable and returns focus to the button.
- Say the constraints next to the button in a FieldDescription ("PDF, up to 10 MB"), so they are read with it.
- What happens after the choice is the caller's to say: add the files as rows the reader can reach, and announce the result through a status (the `announce` helper, or a `role="status"` line) if nothing else changes where focus is.

## Props

_Props of `FileTrigger`, generated from its types:_

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `className` | `string \| ((state: ButtonState) => string)` |  | CSS class applied to the element, or a function that returns a class based on the component's state. |
| `style` | `CSSProperties \| ((state: ButtonState) => CSSProperties)` |  | Style applied to the element, or a function that returns a style object based on the component's state. |
| `nativeButton` | `boolean` | `true` | Whether the component renders a native `<button>` element when replacing it via the `render` prop. Set to `false` if the rendered element is not a button (for example, `<div>`). |
| `render` | `ReactElement<unknown, string \| JSXElementConstructor<any>> \| ComponentRenderFn<HTMLProps, ButtonState>` |  | Allows you to replace the component's HTML element with a different tag, or compose it with another component. Accepts a `ReactElement` or a function that returns the element to render. |
| `size` | `"medium" \| "small" \| "xsmall"` |  | Medium is 32px, small 28px and xsmall 24px. `variant="link"` ignores it: a link-styled action is as tall as its text. |
| `focusableWhenDisabled` | `boolean` | `false` | Whether the button should be focusable when disabled. |
| `variant` | `"danger" \| "link" \| "primary" \| "secondary" \| "subtle"` |  | Secondary is the default; primary emphasizes the main action. |
| `isSelected` | `boolean` |  | Paint the selected state and, on Button, set aria-pressed. |
| `isFullWidth` | `boolean` |  | Fill the available width. |
| `iconBefore` | `ReactElement<unknown, string \| JSXElementConstructor<any>>` |  | Decorative leading icon, replaced by a spinner while loading. |
| `iconAfter` | `ReactElement<unknown, string \| JSXElementConstructor<any>>` |  | Decorative trailing icon. |
| `isLoading` | `boolean` |  | Block activation and show a spinner while keeping focus unless explicitly disabled. The button keeps its width and its name: the spinner takes the leading icon's place, else the trailing icon's, else it sits over the label, which keeps its space. |
| `loadingLabel` | `string` |  | What the pending work is, said once through the page's polite live region when loading starts, such as "Saving requirement revision". `aria-busy` alone is not announced by the major screen readers. Leave it out when something else on the page already says it. |
| `disabledReason` | `string` |  | Why the action is unavailable, for an action that truly cannot run. The button is disabled but stays in the tab order with `aria-disabled`, so the reader can reach it and learn why: the reason shows in a tooltip on hover, on keyboard focus and on a tap, and is the button's accessible description. It disables the button by itself and keeps it focusable even with `disabled`. An empty string is no reason. Prefer an enabled action that explains on use, such as a submit that reports what is missing. |
| `truncate` | `boolean` |  | For a slot narrower than the label, such as a rail, a card's footer or a table cell: the button narrows to its container and cuts the label with an ellipsis, its icons whole. The whole label stays the accessible name and shows in a tooltip on hover and keyboard focus while it is cut. Write labels short enough not to need it; this is for the slot that cannot grow. |
| `accept` | `string \| readonly string[]` |  | The file types the picker offers, as the input's `accept`: media types (`application/pdf`), wildcards (`image/*`) and extensions (`.csv`), in a string or a list. The picker filters by it but a reader can still choose another file, so check the files you receive; DropZone does. |
| `multiple` | `boolean` | `false` | Lets the reader choose several files at once. One by default. |
| `capture` | `"environment" \| "user"` |  | On a phone, offers the camera directly: `environment` the rear one, `user` the front. |
| `onSelect` | `((files: File[]) => void)` |  | Called with the chosen files once the picker closes with a choice; not called when the reader cancels. The input is emptied after each choice, so choosing the same file again (after a removal or a failed upload) calls it again. |
| `inputRef` | `Ref<HTMLInputElement>` |  | The hidden file input, for a test or a caller that opens the picker itself. |

### Playground

_Example: story `Stories.Playground`._

_Rendered in the Storybook: Controls._

## Related

[DropZone](?path=/docs/components-dropzone--docs) · [Attachment](?path=/docs/components-attachment--docs) · [Button](?path=/docs/components-button--docs) · [Field](?path=/docs/components-field--docs). Reference: [React Aria FileTrigger](https://react-spectrum.adobe.com/react-aria/FileTrigger.html).

## Don't

A file is chosen through a FileTrigger, a real button named by its field, never an Input with `type="file"`, whose browser button loses its frame and reads as text.

_Example: story `Stories.DoDont`._

<!-- page: Components/FilterChip (src/stories/components/FilterChip.mdx) -->

# FilterChip

**Status: Stable.**

A filter the reader adds to a [Toolbar](?path=/docs/patterns-toolbar--docs): dashed with a plus until it is on, then solid and selected, with the chosen value after its label. A chip is one question of the register, Owner or Status or Gaps; the chips together are the question the table answers.

A chip asks; a [Badge](?path=/docs/components-badge--docs) tells. A coordinated set of single or multiple choices is a [ToggleGroup](?path=/docs/components-togglegroup--docs); a thing to do is a [Button](?path=/docs/components-button--docs).

_Example: story `Stories.FilterChipMatrix`._

## Anatomy

| Part   | What it is                                                                                                          |
| ------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Plus   | "+" before the label while the chip is off: add this filter. Hidden from a screen reader; gone once the chip is on. |
| Label  | The column or the question, `font.body`, `color.text.subtle` at rest and `color.text.selected` on.                  |
| Value  | After the label, `font.weight.medium` in `color.text`: the value chosen, or "3 chosen". Truncates past 20ch.        |
| Border | Dashed `color.border.bold` at rest; solid `color.border.selected` on `color.background.selected` once on.           |

## Variants

FilterChip has one appearance. What varies is what a click does:

| The question                                | Use                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| ------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Yes or no about the rows: Gaps, Hide closed | A toggle: `isActive` flips, no value.                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| A column with a value: Owner, Status, Due   | The trigger of a [Popover](?path=/docs/components-popover--docs); the DataTable's `Filter` builds one from the column (checkboxes, a range, a contains field) and the value reads on the chip. One value from a few (an owner) is a popover of radios. |
| Exclusive choices: All, High, Medium        | A ToggleGroup, not chips.                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| A saved question with its count             | The DataTable's `Presets`, a ToggleGroup with Count children.                                                                                                                                                                                          |

There is no remove cross on the chip: a click on an active toggle turns it off, and a popover chip has Clear. There is no chip with an icon, and no chip with a count: the rows a question would leave belong to a preset's Count. There is no toggle that cycles through values: it would stay pressed while its name changed from "Owner" to "Owner Dana Whitfield" to "Owner Priya Natarajan", so a screen reader could not tell which value is on or how to reach the next; a value is chosen in a popover.

## Sizes

One: `dimension.control.small` 28px, the Toolbar's height, `space.100` each side.

A chip is one line at every width, and it never shrinks below its plus and its label. A value longer than about twenty characters truncates with an ellipsis; its full text is the value's title and stays in the chip's accessible name. In a frame narrower than the chip, the value gives way first.

_Example: story `Stories.Narrow`._

## Long content

The label is one or two words and never truncates. The value is the only part that may: past about twenty characters, or when the frame is narrower than the chip, it ends in an ellipsis and keeps its full text as its title and in the chip's name. A chip never wraps onto a second line.

_Example: story `Stories.InToolbar`._

## States

| State        | What changes                                                                                                  |
| ------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Rest         | Dashed `color.border.bold`, the plus, `color.text.subtle`.                                                    |
| Hover        | The border to `color.border`, the text to `color.text`.                                                       |
| Active       | Solid `color.border.selected` on `color.background.selected`, `color.text.selected`; no plus; pressed.        |
| With a value | The value after the label in `color.text` at `font.weight.medium`.                                            |
| Open         | As a Popover's trigger, `aria-expanded`; the chip is active only while it holds a value.                      |
| Focus        | The focus outline.                                                                                            |
| Disabled     | `color.border.disabled`, `color.text.disabled`, no pointer: a filter with nothing to choose. Better left out. |

## Modifiers

- **`label`** and **`value`**.
- **`isActive`** paints the chip on and says pressed.
- **`disabled`**.
- **`onClick`** and the rest of a button's props. A Popover passes `aria-expanded` to its trigger, and the chip stops saying pressed.

## Content

- **The label is the column or the question as a noun**, sentence case: Owner, Status, Gaps, Hide closed. Not "Filter by owner".
- **The value is what was chosen, as the cell shows it**: "Dana Whitfield", "Overdue", "≥ 10", "3 chosen". Never a count of rows.
- **A toggle reads as what it turns on**: Gaps shows the gaps, Hide closed hides them; both are true while the chip is on.
- **Four or five chips** in a toolbar. Past that the table has too many questions, and the answers are presets.

## Style

| Element  | Token                                                                                           |
| -------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Chip     | `dimension.control.small` · `radius.medium` · `space.100` sides · gap `space.075` · `font.body` |
| Rest     | border dashed `color.border.bold` · `color.text.subtle` · hover `color.border`, `color.text`    |
| Active   | border `color.border.selected` · `color.background.selected` · `color.text.selected`            |
| Value    | `font.weight.medium` `color.text`                                                               |
| Disabled | `color.border.disabled` · `color.text.disabled`                                                 |
| Focus    | The focus outline                                                                               |
| Motion   | `motion.duration.fast` on the colours                                                           |

## Accessibility

- **A button.** On its own it is a toggle: `aria-pressed` follows `isActive`, so a screen reader hears "Gaps, toggle button, pressed". As a Popover's trigger it takes the popover's `aria-expanded` and does not say pressed; the value in its text says what is applied.
- **Named by its text**, label and value together: "Owner Dana Whitfield".
- **Keyboard.** Tab reaches it; Space or Enter flips it or opens the popover; Escape closes the popover and returns focus to the chip.
- **Not colour alone.** The plus and the dashed border say off; the solid border and the pressed state say on.
- **Disabled is the last resort.** A filter with nothing to choose is left out of the row.

## Props

Native button props, including `ref`, pass through to the button. Refs target `HTMLButtonElement`;
when composed with `PopoverTrigger render={<FilterChip label="Status" />}`, both parts' refs and
event handlers reach the same button. The Popover owns opening, dismissal and focus return. The
chip names itself last with `data-slot="filter-chip"`; its label and value are `filter-chip-label`
and `filter-chip-value`.

_Props of `FilterChip`, generated from its types:_

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `label` (required) | `string` |  | The column or the question, as a noun: Owner, Status, Gaps. |
| `value` | `string \| (string & readonly string[])` |  | The chosen value, after the label: "Dana Whitfield", "3 chosen". |
| `isActive` | `boolean` | `false` | The filter is applied: solid and selected, and pressed for a screen reader. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` |  |  |
| `className` | `string` |  |  |

### Playground

_Example: story `Stories.Playground`._

_Rendered in the Storybook: Controls._

## Related

- [Toolbar](?path=/docs/patterns-toolbar--docs): where chips live.
- [DataTable](?path=/docs/patterns-data-table--docs): `Filter` builds a chip and its popover from a column; `Presets` are saved questions.
- [ToggleGroup](?path=/docs/components-togglegroup--docs): single or multiple toggle buttons. [Popover](?path=/docs/components-popover--docs): what a value chip opens.
- [Badge](?path=/docs/components-badge--docs): a status told, not asked.

## Don't

Exclusive choices are a ToggleGroup and a thing to do is a Button, never a chip. A chip's value is what was chosen, as the cell shows it, never a count of rows.

_Example: story `Stories.Dont`._

<!-- page: Components/HoverCard (src/stories/components/HoverCard.mdx) -->

# HoverCard

**Status: Stable.**

A supplementary preview of a link's destination, built from shadcn's Base UI PreviewCard composition. The trigger stays a link; the preview can contain a [Glance](?path=/docs/patterns-glance--docs) or other supporting content available at that destination.

```tsx
<HoverCard>
  <HoverCardTrigger href="/controls/CTRL-0412">CTRL-0412</HoverCardTrigger>
  <HoverCardContent style={{ width: 300 }}>
    <Glance id="CTRL-0412" title="Segregation of duties, payables" />
  </HoverCardContent>
</HoverCard>
```

## When to use it

- **A peek at a link's destination**: a record's code, name, state and owner in a [Glance](?path=/docs/patterns-glance--docs), so the reader can decide whether to follow the link.

Not for an action: the card holds no button the reader must reach, since a keyboard or touch reader may never open it; actions sit at the destination or in a [Popover](?path=/docs/components-popover--docs). Not for a short label: that is a [Tooltip](?path=/docs/components-tooltip--docs). Not for the record itself: the link goes there, and a preview the reader works in is the Shell's panel or a [PreviewSheet](?path=/docs/patterns-previewsheet--docs). [Overlays](?path=/docs/components-overlays--docs) compares them all.

Hold the card on a link to the record, never on plain text, and put no action in it: a keyboard or a touch never opens a card on text.

_Example: story `Stories.DoDont`._

## Content

- The record's own words, as its page has them: its code and name first, then the two or three facts a reader decides on.
- Nothing that is not also at the destination, and no instruction the reader needs.

## Composition and placement

`HoverCard` owns the open state. `HoverCardTrigger` renders an anchor and accepts native link props, a ref, state callbacks and `render` for a custom link. `HoverCardContent` includes the portal and positioner; its native props, ref and `render` target the popup.

An action trigger can use `render={<button type="button" />}`. Its native button owns click and keyboard activation; Trigger has no `nativeButton` prop.

Content is 256px wide by default (`dimension.part.hoverCard`) and centred under its trigger: `side="bottom"`, `sideOffset={4}`, `align="center"` and `alignOffset={0}`. Override its width through `style`, including a state callback. It is capped at the height the window leaves on its side and scrolls within it. Content also takes the positioner's `anchor` (a cell or a virtual point instead of the trigger), `collisionPadding`, `collisionBoundary`, `collisionAvoidance`, `sticky` and `positionMethod`. The positioner handles collisions; logical sides and alignment follow the Ledger locale, with Content's `dir` available as an override.

The trigger draws the kit's focus ring. Compose it with [TextLink](?path=/docs/components-textlink--docs) (`<TextLink render={<HoverCardTrigger href="…" />}>`) for link styling.

The surface uses Ledger's overlay, border, text in `font.body` (it previews the record's own words), radius, spacing and motion tokens, and records the overlay surface as the current one, so a child painted with `bg-surface-current` (a sticky label, a fade at an edge) matches the card. Content `className` and `style` callbacks receive Base UI popup state; render props, classes, styles and refs are merged.

_Example: story `Stories.HoverCardMatrix`._

## Interaction

The trigger opens the preview after pointer hover or keyboard focus. `delay` defaults to 600ms and `closeDelay` to 300ms, both on Trigger. Pointer passage from trigger to popup keeps the preview open. Leaving both, moving focus away, an outside press or Escape dismisses it. Escape leaves focus where it was.

Clicking or pressing Enter on the trigger follows the link. A trigger press does not itself guarantee dismissal; navigation or caller-controlled state may close the card. Touch follows the link without the mouse-hover behavior.

Use Root's `defaultOpen`, or controlled `open` with `onOpenChange(open, details)`. `details.cancel()` rejects a change. Multiple triggers can share one Root: pass `payload` on each trigger and render the active payload through Root's children function.

_Example: story `Stories.OnAnId`._

## Accessibility

Keep the preview supplementary. Essential information and actions belong at the linked destination or in a [Popover](?path=/docs/components-popover--docs). Opening the preview does not move focus or add a popup Tab stop, and it is not a dialog announcement. The link remains the way to navigate for keyboard, touch and assistive-technology users.

## Props

HoverCard inherits Base UI's [Root props](https://base-ui.com/react/components/preview-card#root), and HoverCardTrigger inherits its [Trigger props](https://base-ui.com/react/components/preview-card#trigger). HoverCardContent inherits [Popup props](https://base-ui.com/react/components/preview-card#popup) plus the positioner's props described above.

_Props of `HoverCardContent`, generated from its types:_

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `className` | `string \| ((state: PreviewCardPopupState) => string)` |  | CSS class applied to the element, or a function that returns a class based on the component's state. |
| `render` | `ReactElement<unknown, string \| JSXElementConstructor<any>> \| ComponentRenderFn<HTMLProps, PreviewCardPopupState>` |  | Allows you to replace the component's HTML element with a different tag, or compose it with another component. Accepts a `ReactElement` or a function that returns the element to render. |
| `style` | `CSSProperties \| ((state: PreviewCardPopupState) => CSSProperties)` |  | Style applied to the element, or a function that returns a style object based on the component's state. |
| `sticky` | `boolean` | `false` | Whether to maintain the popup in the viewport after the anchor element was scrolled out of view. |
| `side` | `"bottom" \| "inline-end" \| "inline-start" \| "left" \| "right" \| "top"` | `bottom` | Which side of the anchor element to align the popup against. May automatically change to avoid collisions. |
| `align` | `"center" \| "end" \| "start"` | `start` | How to align the popup relative to the specified side. |
| `sideOffset` | `number \| OffsetFunction` | `4` | Distance between the anchor and the popup in pixels. Also accepts a function that returns the distance to read the dimensions of the anchor and positioner elements, along with its side and alignment. The function takes a `data` object parameter with the following properties: - `data.anchor`: the dimensions of the anchor element with properties `width` and `height`. - `data.positioner`: the dimensions of the positioner element with properties `width` and `height`. - `data.side`: which side of the anchor element the positioner is aligned against. - `data.align`: how the positioner is aligned relative to the specified side. @example ```jsx <Positioner sideOffset={({ side, align, anchor, positioner }) => { return side === 'top' \|\| side === 'bottom' ? anchor.height : anchor.width; }} /> ``` |
| `alignOffset` | `number \| OffsetFunction` | `0` | Additional offset along the alignment axis in pixels. Also accepts a function that returns the offset to read the dimensions of the anchor and positioner elements, along with its side and alignment. The function takes a `data` object parameter with the following properties: - `data.anchor`: the dimensions of the anchor element with properties `width` and `height`. - `data.positioner`: the dimensions of the positioner element with properties `width` and `height`. - `data.side`: which side of the anchor element the positioner is aligned against. - `data.align`: how the positioner is aligned relative to the specified side. @example ```jsx <Positioner alignOffset={({ side, align, anchor, positioner }) => { return side === 'top' \|\| side === 'bottom' ? anchor.width : anchor.height; }} /> ``` |
| `anchor` | `Element \| VirtualElement \| RefObject<Element \| null> \| (() => Element \| VirtualElement \| null) \| null` |  | An element to position the popup against. By default, the popup will be positioned against the trigger. |
| `collisionAvoidance` | `CollisionAvoidance` |  | Determines how to handle collisions when positioning the popup. `side` controls overflow on the preferred placement axis (`top`/`bottom` or `left`/`right`): - `'flip'`: keep the requested side when it fits; otherwise try the opposite side (`top` and `bottom`, or `left` and `right`). - `'shift'`: never change side; keep the requested side and move the popup within the clipping boundary so it stays visible. - `'none'`: do not correct side-axis overflow. `align` controls overflow on the alignment axis (`start`/`center`/`end`): - `'flip'`: keep side, but swap `start` and `end` when the requested alignment overflows. - `'shift'`: keep side and requested alignment, then nudge the popup along the alignment axis to fit. - `'none'`: do not correct alignment-axis overflow. `fallbackAxisSide` controls fallback behavior on the perpendicular axis when the preferred axis cannot fit: - `'start'`: allow perpendicular fallback and try the logical start side first (`top` before `bottom`, or `left` before `right` in LTR). - `'end'`: allow perpendicular fallback and try the logical end side first (`bottom` before `top`, or `right` before `left` in LTR). - `'none'`: do not fallback to the perpendicular axis. When `side` is `'shift'`, explicitly setting `align` only supports `'shift'` or `'none'`. If `align` is omitted, it defaults to `'flip'`. @example ```jsx <Positioner collisionAvoidance={{ side: 'shift', align: 'shift', fallbackAxisSide: 'none', }} /> ``` |
| `collisionBoundary` | `Boundary` | `'clipping-ancestors'` | An element or a rectangle that delimits the area that the popup is confined to. |
| `collisionPadding` | `Padding` | `5` | Additional space to maintain from the edge of the collision boundary. |
| `positionMethod` | `"absolute" \| "fixed"` | `'absolute'` | Determines which CSS `position` property to use. |

_Example: story `Stories.Playground`._

## Related

[Glance](?path=/docs/patterns-glance--docs) · [PreviewSheet](?path=/docs/patterns-previewsheet--docs) · [Tooltip](?path=/docs/components-tooltip--docs) · [Overlays](?path=/docs/components-overlays--docs) · [shadcn Hover Card](https://ui.shadcn.com/docs/components/base/hover-card) · [Base UI Preview Card](https://base-ui.com/react/components/preview-card)

<!-- page: Components/Icon (src/stories/components/Icon.mdx) -->

# Icon

**Status: Stable.**

A Lucide glyph with its size, colour and name decided in one place. With a `label` the icon is an image with that name, for a mark that stands for something on its own: an authorization boundary on a tree row, a met check in a cell, an overdue clock. Without one it is decoration beside the word that says the same, and it is hidden from assistive technology. The sizes and colours are the ones on [Tokens/Icons](?path=/docs/tokens-icons--docs).

```tsx
<Icon label="Authorization boundary" color="color.icon.subtle">
  <Shield />
</Icon>
```

_Example: story `Stories.IconMatrix`._

## When to use it

- **A mark that carries meaning with no word beside it** takes an Icon with a `label`. The label is the value, not the glyph: "Met", not "Check"; "Authorization boundary", not "Shield".
- **An icon beside its word** takes an Icon without a label, or no wrapper at all where the part draws it (Button `iconBefore`, Item `leading`, a Badge's icon). Those parts already hide it.
- **A clickable icon is an [IconButton](?path=/docs/components-iconbutton--docs)**, whose `label` is its name and its tooltip. An Icon is never a target.
- **A status with a word** is an [Indicator](?path=/docs/components-indicator--docs) or a Badge; colour alone never carries the meaning.

_Example: story `Stories.Named`._

## Anatomy

| Part    | What it is                                                                                                                                         |
| ------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Wrapper | A `span` (or the element `render` names), `inline-flex`, the icon's size. `role="img"` and `aria-label` with a `label`; `aria-hidden` without one. |
| Glyph   | The Lucide element passed as the child, sized by the wrapper to `dimension.icon.small` (14px) or `.medium` (16px), at Lucide's stroke.             |
| Colour  | A `color.icon` token, or the surrounding text colour when left out.                                                                                |

## Accessibility

- **A named icon is an image with a name.** A screen reader says "Authorization boundary, image"; a generic element with `aria-label` is ignored, which is the mistake this part replaces.
- **A decorative icon is hidden**, so the word beside it is not read twice.
- **A sighted reader needs the meaning too.** A named mark with no word beside it is fine in a dense row where the column or legend says what it means; elsewhere put the word beside it. An Icon has no tooltip, because a tooltip on something that cannot take focus is hover-only.
- **Forced colours**: the glyph is drawn in `currentColor`, so it takes the system text colour.

## Props

_Props of `Icon`, generated from its types:_

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `render` | `ReactElement<unknown, string \| JSXElementConstructor<any>> \| ComponentRenderFn<HTMLProps, {}>` |  | Allows you to replace the component's HTML element with a different tag, or compose it with another component. Accepts a `ReactElement` or a function that returns the element to render. |
| `children` (required) | `ReactNode` |  | The glyph, passed bare: `<Shield />`. The wrapper sizes and colours it. |
| `label` | `string` |  | What the icon means when it stands for something on its own: "Authorization boundary", "Met", "Overdue". The icon becomes an image with this name. Without it the icon is decoration beside a word, hidden from assistive technology. The name is the value, not the glyph: "Met", not "Check". |
| `size` | `"medium" \| "small"` | `small` | `dimension.icon.small` (14px, beside body text; the default) or `.medium` (16px, standing alone or beside a heading). |
| `color` | `IconColorToken` |  | A `color.icon` token. Defaults to inheriting the colour of the text around it. |

### Playground

_Example: story `Stories.Playground`._

_Rendered in the Storybook: Controls._

## Related

- [Tokens/Icons](?path=/docs/tokens-icons--docs): sizes, stroke, colours and naming.
- [VisuallyHidden](?path=/docs/primitives-visuallyhidden--docs): hidden words beside a mark, read inline with the text.
- [IconButton](?path=/docs/components-iconbutton--docs): an icon that acts.

## Don't

A mark that stands alone is an Icon with a `label`, never an `aria-label` on a span, which names nothing. Beside its word an icon takes no label, or the word is said twice.

_Example: story `Stories.Dont`._

<!-- page: Components/IconButton (src/stories/components/IconButton.mdx) -->

# IconButton

**Status: Stable.**

A square [Button](?path=/docs/components-button--docs) with an icon, a required `label` and a tooltip. Name the action, such as “Search” or “Close.” Use a labelled Button when the icon alone would be unclear, a [LinkIconButton](?path=/docs/components-linkbutton--docs) when the icon goes somewhere (opening a record in a new tab), and a [CopyButton](?path=/docs/components-copybutton--docs) with `label` to copy a value.

_Example: story `Stories.IconButtonMatrix`._

An icon stands alone only where every reader takes it the same way: search, close, more, edit, previous and next. Request evidence or Export to OSCAL keeps its words in a Button. The label says the action and what it acts on (Edit owner), never the drawing (Pencil).

_Example: story `Stories.DoDont`._

## Variants and sizes

| Variant     | Use                                                                      |
| ----------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `secondary` | Default raised action.                                                   |
| `subtle`    | Toolbars, rows and header controls.                                      |
| `primary`   | Emphasized actions, including the options beside a primary split action. |

| Size      | Button                    | Icon | Typical placement                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| --------- | ------------------------- | ---- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `medium`  | 32px square               | 16px | Beside a default (medium) Button, in a header or a footer.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| `small`   | 28px square, the default  | 14px | Toolbars, the top navigation, a card's corner.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `xsmall`  | 24px square               | 14px | Beside an xsmall Button, such as the options of a dense split action.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| `xxsmall` | 20px square, small radius | 14px | The row control: a table or tree row's disclosure, the preview eye, a list row's chevron (a row's More fields is its count, "+3", at the same height). Table, DataTable, Tree and Item draw theirs with it. In a row pass `isTooltipDisabled`, so a long list mounts no tooltip per row; the name still says the action. |

The sizes are Button's (`xsmall` 24px, `small` 28px, `medium` 32px) plus the 20px row control; Button defaults to `medium` and IconButton to `small`, so beside a default Button pass `size="medium"`. Where any pointer is coarse every size takes a hit area of at least 24px, centred, so a row keeps its height.

Pass the icon element with `icon`. IconButton sizes it and hides it from assistive technology; `label` provides the accessible name. `isSelected` applies the selected palette and `aria-pressed`. `isLoading` replaces the icon with a decorative spinner while retaining the label and focus.

_Example: story `Stories.InPlace`._

## Composition and accessibility

IconButton shares Button's native props, form behavior, refs and Base UI `render` support. The rendered component must forward props and refs to its DOM element. Use `nativeButton={false}` for a custom action that is not a native button. For navigation, use [LinkIconButton](?path=/docs/components-linkbutton--docs), never an IconButton that navigates from `onClick`: a real link can be opened in a new tab.

`disabledReason` works as on Button: the action is disabled but focusable with `aria-disabled`, and one tooltip shows the label and then the reason, on hover, focus and a tap. The reason is the button's accessible description. With `isTooltipDisabled` the label's tooltip goes, and the reason still shows alone. A reason that comes or goes while the button has focus leaves focus on it.

_Example: story `Stories.DisabledWithAReason`._

- The tooltip shows `label` on hover and when keyboard focus arrives. Escape closes it.
- Focus that comes back from a popup the button opened, a menu closed with Escape or by choosing a command, or a dialog closed, leaves the tooltip shut, so one Escape closes the menu and the next reaches whatever holds the button.
- A disclosure's content is not a popup, even inside a dialog, menu or listbox that also holds the button: focus that comes back from it, or from anywhere else in that surface, shows the tooltip.
- `isTooltipDisabled` suppresses the tooltip when a parent supplies one or the label is already visible; the accessible name remains.
- Tab reaches an enabled control; Enter and Space activate it. Disabled controls leave the normal tab order unless `disabledReason` or `focusableWhenDisabled` is set.
- A disabled IconButton's tooltip is its only visible label, and a plain `disabled` one shows it to no one: the pointer and the keyboard both pass it by. When the reader still needs to find it, as with a pair of previous and next controls at either end, set `focusableWhenDisabled`: it stays in the tab order with `aria-disabled`, its tooltip shows on hover and focus, and one that becomes disabled while it has focus keeps focus. Escape still reaches the panel, side nav or dialog around it: only activation is blocked. When it needs to say why, use `disabledReason`. Do not make every disabled control focusable; one that leaves nothing to learn can leave the tab order.
- Loading sets `aria-busy`, blocks activation and retains focus. An explicitly disabled control stays disabled.
- Keep sufficient space around compact controls; choose a larger labelled Button when a touch interaction needs a larger target.
- `size="xxsmall"`, the 20px row control, keeps a hit area of at least 24px, centred on it, where any pointer is coarse; the row keeps its height.

_Example: story `Stories.InADenseRow`._

_Example: story `Stories.DisabledButReachable`._

_Example: story `Stories.OpensAMenu`._

_Example: story `Stories.InADialog`._

## Props

_Props of `IconButton`, generated from its types:_

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `className` | `string \| ((state: ButtonState) => string)` |  | CSS class applied to the element, or a function that returns a class based on the component's state. |
| `style` | `CSSProperties \| ((state: ButtonState) => CSSProperties)` |  | Style applied to the element, or a function that returns a style object based on the component's state. |
| `nativeButton` | `boolean` | `true` | Whether the component renders a native `<button>` element when replacing it via the `render` prop. Set to `false` if the rendered element is not a button (for example, `<div>`). |
| `render` | `ReactElement<unknown, string \| JSXElementConstructor<any>> \| ComponentRenderFn<HTMLProps, ButtonState>` |  | Allows you to replace the component's HTML element with a different tag, or compose it with another component. Accepts a `ReactElement` or a function that returns the element to render. |
| `focusableWhenDisabled` | `boolean` | `false` | Whether the button should be focusable when disabled. |
| `isSelected` | `boolean` |  | Paint the selected state and, on Button, set aria-pressed. |
| `isLoading` | `boolean` |  | Block activation and show a spinner while keeping focus unless explicitly disabled. The button keeps its width and its name: the spinner takes the leading icon's place, else the trailing icon's, else it sits over the label, which keeps its space. |
| `loadingLabel` | `string` |  | What the pending work is, said once through the page's polite live region when loading starts, such as "Saving requirement revision". `aria-busy` alone is not announced by the major screen readers. Leave it out when something else on the page already says it. |
| `disabledReason` | `string` |  | Why the action is unavailable, for an action that truly cannot run. The button is disabled but stays in the tab order with `aria-disabled`, so the reader can reach it and learn why: the reason shows in a tooltip on hover, on keyboard focus and on a tap, and is the button's accessible description. It disables the button by itself and keeps it focusable even with `disabled`. An empty string is no reason. Prefer an enabled action that explains on use, such as a submit that reports what is missing. |
| `label` (required) | `string` |  | Accessible action name, also used by the tooltip. |
| `icon` (required) | `ReactElement<unknown, string \| JSXElementConstructor<any>>` |  | Decorative icon, replaced by a spinner while loading. |
| `variant` | `"primary" \| "secondary" \| "subtle"` |  |  |
| `size` | `"medium" \| "small" \| "xsmall" \| "xxsmall"` | `small` | Small is 28px, the default; medium 32px with a larger icon; xsmall 24px, beside an xsmall Button; xxsmall 20px, the row control in a table, tree or list row. Where any pointer is coarse each takes a hit area of at least 24px. |
| `isTooltipDisabled` | `boolean` |  | Keep the accessible name while omitting the tooltip. A `disabledReason` still shows its own. |

_Example: story `Stories.Playground`._

_Rendered in the Storybook: Controls._
