# Id

**Status: Stable.**

An identifier: CTRL-0412, AC-2(3), FND-2231, a hash. One typeface app-wide, so an Id inherits the font, the size and the colour of wherever it sits and adds only tabular numerals, which is what makes a column of ids line up. It is kept as a component for the semantics, and so every id in the product can be found. A code snippet is for code, which an id is not.

_Example: story `Stories.IdMatrix`._

## Anatomy

| Part | What it is                                                                                                             |
| ---- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Id   | A span with tabular numerals. Nothing else: no fill, no face, no colour of its own.                                    |
| List | `Id.List`: a wrapping run of ids at `font.body.xsmall` in `color.text.subtle`, `space.050` apart; or the `empty` word. |

## Variants

| Variant   | Use                                                                           |
| --------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Id`      | One id, in text, in a title, in a link, in a cell.                            |
| `Id.List` | Several ids: the controls a requirement traces to, the CCIs a package covers. |

Not built, and why: a monospace face (the old habit; the kit has one typeface and tabular numerals do the aligning); a link inside the Id, because the link is outside it, a TextLink whose text is an Id; a copy button inside the Id. An id is not selected like a word: a double-click stops at its punctuation, so it takes "CTRL" or "0412" from CTRL-0412 and "2" from AC-2(3), and a reader drags across it instead. Where readers copy ids as part of the work, put a [CopyButton](?path=/docs/components-copybutton--docs) with a `label` beside the id, in the record's Details. Never `user-select: all`, which would take the whole cell, sentence or link with it.

## Sizes

None of its own. An Id is the size of its line: `font.body` in a sentence, `font.body.small` in a row, `font.heading` in a title. `Id.List` is `font.body.xsmall`, the size of a list of references.

_Example: story `Stories.InRows`._

## States

None. An Id is text. The link around it hovers; the cell around it is selected; the Id does neither.

## Modifiers

- **`className`** for the colour or the size it takes from its place: `text-subtle` in a row's id column, `font-body-small` in a rail, `break-all` for a hash that must break anywhere.
- **List `empty`** for the word that stands where there are no ids; a muted dash by default.

## Content

- **The id as the record writes it:** "CTRL-0412", "AC-2(3)". Never a prose rendering ("Control 412", "AC 2.3").
- **One id per Id.** Several are an `Id.List`, never a comma-joined string.
- **A hash is an Id** too, with `break-all` so it wraps inside its column.
- **Subtle beside a name, default alone.** In a row the id column is `color.text.subtle` and the name is `color.text`; in a sentence the Id takes the sentence's colour.

## Long content

An id, a hash, a URN and a URL are unbroken tokens, so they wrap anywhere: `break-all` on the Id, or the `wrap` of the cell or value it sits in. In a row field that truncates (a table cell, an Item's id), the row cuts it with an ellipsis and reveals the whole on hover and keyboard focus. An `Id.List` wraps between ids, never inside one.

## Style

| Element | Token                                                              |
| ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Id      | Tabular numerals; the surrounding font, size and colour            |
| List    | `font.body.xsmall` · `color.text.subtle` · `space.050` between ids |
| Empty   | `font.body.small` · `color.text.subtlest`                          |

## Accessibility

- **An Id is text**, read as its characters. Nothing to focus, nothing to operate.
- **A screen reader spells an id as it reads it.** Punctuation inside it, the parentheses in AC-2(3), is read or skipped by the reader's own rules; the kit does not rewrite an id to help.
- **The colour is not the meaning.** An Id in `color.text.subtle` is an id; an Id in the link colour is a link, because a TextLink is around it.
- **`break-all` is for a hash**, so a long id never widens its column past the viewport.

## Props

_Props of `Id`, generated from its types:_

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `children` (required) | `ReactNode` |  | The identifier: CTRL-0412, AC-2(3), FND-2231. |

Id takes a span's native props and a ref, and names itself last with `data-slot="id"`; Id.List takes the same on its run, with `data-slot="id-list"` and `data-empty` when there are none.

_Example: story `Stories.NativeAttributes`._

### Id.List

_Props of `IdList`, generated from its types:_

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `ids` (required) | `string[]` |  | The identifiers, in order. |
| `empty` | `string` | `—` | What to say when there are none; a muted dash by default. |

### Playground

_Example: story `Stories.Playground`._

_Rendered in the Storybook: Controls._

## Related

- [TextLink](?path=/docs/components-textlink--docs): the link an Id sits inside.
- [Item](?path=/docs/components-item--docs), [Table](?path=/docs/components-table--docs): the id column.
- [PageHeader](?path=/docs/layout-pageheader--docs): the id above a title.

## Don't

An Id takes the colour of its sentence, never the link colour with nothing to click. Several ids are an Id.List, never a comma-joined string, and an id is written as the record writes it, never as prose ("Control 412").

_Example: story `Stories.Dont`._

<!-- page: Components/Indicator (src/stories/components/Indicator.mdx) -->

# Indicator

**Status: Stable.**

A Dot with a word: severity or health beside a label, in a row or a rail. High, Medium, Low; Healthy, Degraded. Never a pill, so the status column stays the only pill in the row and the eye can tell the rank from the state. The Dot is a 6px circle in the tone's icon colour, tuned to read at small sizes; it marks a status whose word is visible beside it (a row's meta, a gate's name, a timeline entry) and is never the status alone, which would be colour alone. Where there is no room for the word, make room: an Indicator, not a bare Dot. A status indicator is usually an icon per state; this uses the Dot.

_Example: story `Stories.IndicatorMatrix`._

## Anatomy

| Part | What it is                                                                                                                                              |
| ---- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Dot  | 6px, round, `color.icon.<tone>`. It never shrinks.                                                                                                      |
| Word | `font.body` after the Dot, `space.075` away: `color.text`, or `color.text.subtle` when the tone is neutral. It truncates, with the whole word on hover. |

## Variants

| Variant     | Use                                                                                                                 |
| ----------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Indicator` | Severity or health with its word: a column in a table, a fact in a rail.                                            |
| `Dot`       | The mark beside a status that is already written: a timeline entry, an unmet gate, a row whose meta says the state. |

The tone is a rank, not a state: `danger` High, `warning` Medium, `neutral` Low, `success` Healthy, `information` Informational. Neutral mutes the word as well as the Dot, so a scale reads from loud to quiet. A record's state, Verified or Overdue, is a [Badge](?path=/docs/components-badge--docs).

Not built, and why: an icon per tone (failed, warning, in progress), because the Dot is the kit's one status mark and the word says the rest; a large Dot; an Indicator in a pill.

## Sizes

One size. The Dot is 6px whatever the text beside it; the word is `font.body`, the row's size, and in a `font.body.small` line it takes that size from the parent. An Indicator is as wide as its word and truncates when the column is narrower.

## Long content

An Indicator is one line. A word longer than its column ("Obligation not stated by the consumer") ends in an ellipsis, and the whole shows in a tooltip on hover while it is cut, and on keyboard focus of the link or button it sits in; the whole stays in the DOM for a screen reader. The Dot never shrinks. Keep the words to the scale's rungs ("High", "Medium", "Low") so the cut is rare.

_Example: story `Stories.Truncation`._

## States

An Indicator has one state and does not hover, focus or disable. The tone is the whole variation.

_Example: story `Stories.InRows`._

## Modifiers

- **`tone`** as in Variants; `neutral` when unsaid.
- **Dot `label`** makes the Dot an image with that name, for a screen reader, where the Dot must stand without its word. A sighted reader still sees colour alone, so it is the last resort: write the word, as an Indicator.
- **`className`** for placement, never for colour.

## Content

- **The word is the rank:** High, Medium, Low; Healthy, Degraded, Down. One word, two at most.
- **The same scale everywhere.** A severity is High, Medium or Low on every screen, never Critical on one and Severe on another.
- **A Dot's label is the same word** the Indicator would show: "Suspect", "Blocked".

## Style

| Element | Token                                                                         |
| ------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Dot     | 6px · `color.icon.<tone>` · `color.icon.subtlest` at neutral                  |
| Word    | `font.body` · `color.text` · `color.text.subtle` at neutral · `space.075` gap |

The icon colours are Badge's, so a danger Dot and a danger Badge's text are one red, and the icon colour is the step tuned for a 6px mark.

## Accessibility

- **The word carries the rank**; the Dot reinforces it and is hidden from a screen reader, so "High" is read once.
- **A Dot alone is colour alone**, for every reader who sees it (WCAG 1.4.1). A status gets its word: an Indicator, or visible text beside the Dot. Without a label the Dot is hidden, which is right because that text says the same thing. A `label` names it for a screen reader only.
- **Neutral is muted, not disabled.** `color.text.subtle` passes the contrast test; the gate runs every tone.
- **Nothing to focus.** An Indicator is a span in the row's reading order.

## Props

_Props of `Indicator`, generated from its types:_

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `tone` | `"danger" \| "information" \| "neutral" \| "success" \| "warning"` | `neutral` | The severity or the health the Dot carries. `neutral` mutes the text as well: the lowest rung. |
| `children` (required) | `ReactNode` |  | The word beside the Dot: "High", "Healthy", "Obligation not stated". It truncates when the row is narrower than it, and shows whole on hover while it is cut. |
| `className` | `string` |  |  |

### Dot

_Props of `Dot`, generated from its types:_

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `tone` | `"danger" \| "information" \| "neutral" \| "success" \| "warning"` | `neutral` |  |
| `label` | `string` |  | The status as a word ("Suspect"), read by a screen reader: with it the dot is an image named by the label; without it the dot is hidden and the text beside it carries the status. A sighted reader still sees colour alone, so a status shows its word beside the dot, or is an Indicator; the label is the last resort. |
| `className` | `string` |  |  |

Indicator takes a span's native props and a ref, Dot an svg's; each names itself last with `data-slot` (`indicator`, `dot`) and its `data-tone`.

_Example: story `Stories.NativeAttributes`._

### Playground

_Example: story `Stories.Playground`._

_Rendered in the Storybook: Controls._

## Related

- [Badge](?path=/docs/components-badge--docs): the tone table, and which of Badge, Count, Indicator and Dot to use.
- [Gates](?path=/docs/patterns-gates--docs): the Dot on an unmet gate.
- [Timeline](?path=/docs/components-timeline--docs): the Dot as a mark.
- [Alert](?path=/docs/components-alert--docs): the Dot before a title.

## Don't

A severity is an Indicator and a record's state a Badge, so a row has one pill; the word shows beside the Dot, never a Dot alone, and the lowest rung is neutral, never success green.

_Example: story `Stories.Dont`._

# Input

**Status: Stable.**

One line of free text, using shadcn's Base UI Input implementation with Ledger control styling. Labels and validation messages belong to Field.

## When to use it

- **One line the reader types**: a name, a title, a reference number, an email address, a web address.
- **Digits that name something**, such as an identifier, a build number or a postcode, with `inputMode="numeric"`: they are text, not a quantity.

Not for several lines, a description or a statement: that is a [Textarea](?path=/docs/components-textarea--docs). Not for a quantity the reader steps or that has a range: that is a [NumberField](?path=/docs/components-numberfield--docs). Not for one value from a known list: that is a [Select](?path=/docs/components-select--docs), or a [Combobox](?path=/docs/components-combobox--docs) when the list is long enough to search. Not for a day, a time or a moment: that is a [DatePicker](?path=/docs/components-datepicker--docs), a [TimeField](?path=/docs/components-timefield--docs) or a [DateTimeField](?path=/docs/components-datetimefield--docs). Not for searching a collection: that is a [SearchField](?path=/docs/components-searchfield--docs). Not for a value that is read where it is shown and never edited there: that is a [KeyValue](?path=/docs/components-keyvalue--docs).

## Content

- The label, the hint and the error are the Field's, in its words ([Field](?path=/docs/components-field--docs), Content).
- A placeholder is an example of the value ("CTRL-0412", "name@example.org"), never the label, an instruction or "Optional": it is gone as soon as the reader types.
- The width says how long the answer is: a year or a code is narrow, a title is wide. The layout sets it, not the Input.

## Anatomy

```tsx
<Field invalid={invalid} required>
  <FieldLabel>Program name</FieldLabel>
  <Input name="program" value={name} onValueChange={setName} />
  <FieldDescription>As it appears on the authorization package.</FieldDescription>
  <FieldError errors={errors} />
</Field>
```

Inside a [Field](?path=/docs/components-field--docs) the Input takes the label, the hint and the error with no ids, and the Field's `invalid`, `required` and `disabled`.

_Example: story `Stories.BoundInField`._

Use `InputGroupInput` inside InputGroup when the field has addons. Input itself remains a single input element.

## Variants and states

`medium` is 32px; `small` is 28px beside toolbar actions. Native `type`, `inputMode`, `readOnly`, `disabled`, `maxLength` and form attributes retain their meanings. The layout sets width. Disabled controls leave the tab order; read-only values remain focusable and copyable. Read-only is the sunken surface with a dashed edge and no hover, so a value that cannot change never looks like a field under the pointer; a value never edited where it is shown is a [KeyValue](?path=/docs/components-keyvalue--docs), not a read-only Input. Prefer a soft limit to `maxLength` for anything pasted: `maxLength` cuts the paste off without a word, where a schema check on submit says what fixes it.

Focus draws one continuous 2px edge over the field border, without a gap or a second ring. Invalid fields keep that edge in the error color. The field and its text stay in place when focus changes; InputGroup owns the edge when the input has addons.

_Example: story `Stories.InputMatrix`._
_Example: story `Stories.InField`._
_Example: story `Stories.Kinds`._

## Accessibility

In a Field the label, hint, error, invalid state and requirement reach the input without ids. Outside one, use a label with `htmlFor` and the input’s `id`, `aria-describedby` for hints, and `aria-invalid` and `aria-required` on the input. The Field's `required` only announces; native `required` on the Input is a browser and Base UI constraint. A placeholder gives an example and never replaces the label.

Native `onChange` remains supported. Search clearing and application shortcuts are caller-owned; Input does not install an Escape handler. Use an accessible InputGroupButton when a clear action is needed.

## Props

`InputProps` extends Base UI Input with Ledger's `size`. Refs and events target the native input; `render`, state callbacks for `className`/`style`, and `onValueChange(value, details)` are forwarded. A value change may be cancelled with `details.cancel()`.

_Props of `Input`, generated from its types:_

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `className` | `string \| ((state: InputState) => string)` |  | CSS class applied to the element, or a function that returns a class based on the component's state. |
| `defaultValue` | `string \| number \| readonly string[]` |  | The default value of the input. Use when uncontrolled. |
| `style` | `CSSProperties \| ((state: InputState) => CSSProperties)` |  | Style applied to the element, or a function that returns a style object based on the component's state. |
| `value` | `string \| number \| readonly string[]` |  | The value of the input. Use when controlled. |
| `render` | `ReactElement<unknown, string \| JSXElementConstructor<any>> \| ComponentRenderFn<HTMLProps, InputState>` |  | Allows you to replace the component's HTML element with a different tag, or compose it with another component. Accepts a `ReactElement` or a function that returns the element to render. |
| `onValueChange` | `((value: string, eventDetails: { reason: "none"; event: Event; cancel: () => void; allowPropagation: () => void; isCanceled: boolean; isPropagationAllowed: boolean; trigger: Element; }) => void)` |  | Callback fired when the `value` changes. Use when controlled. |
| `size` | `"medium" \| "small"` | `medium` | Medium is 32px in a form; small is 28px beside toolbar actions. |

_Example: story `Stories.NativeComposition`._
_Example: story `Stories.Playground`._

<!-- page: Components/InputGroup (src/stories/components/InputGroup.mdx) -->

# InputGroup

**Status: Stable.**

Compose an input or textarea with icons, units and actions using shadcn's InputGroup parts. The group supplies the shared border and focus/invalid appearance.

## When to use it

- **A field with something joined to it**: a unit ("days"), a prefix ("$"), an icon, a keyboard hint, or a button that acts on the value (clear, copy).

Not for a field with nothing beside it: that is an [Input](?path=/docs/components-input--docs) or a [Textarea](?path=/docs/components-textarea--docs). Not for buttons joined with no field: that is a [ButtonGroup](?path=/docs/components-buttongroup--docs). Not for searching a collection: that is a [SearchField](?path=/docs/components-searchfield--docs).

## Content

- A unit or a prefix is the shortest form the reader knows ("days", "$") and never repeats the label.
- An icon-only button's `label` names its action and its object: "Clear link", "Clear search".
- The label is the Field's; an addon never stands in for it.

## Anatomy

```tsx
<Field>
  <FieldLabel>Retention</FieldLabel>
  <InputGroup>
    <InputGroupInput type="number" defaultValue="90" />
    <InputGroupAddon align="inline-end">
      <InputGroupText>days</InputGroupText>
    </InputGroupAddon>
  </InputGroup>
</Field>
```

InputGroupInput inside a [Field](?path=/docs/components-field--docs) takes the label, hint and error with no ids, and the whole group draws the Field's invalid border.

_Example: story `Stories.BoundInField`._

Addons are InputGroupAddon children, and the control is InputGroupInput or InputGroupTextarea, never a plain Input inside the frame (that draws a second border). Set the width through native style or the surrounding layout.

## Variants and states

Addon alignment is `inline-start` (default), `inline-end`, `block-start` or `block-end`. Inline positions follow text direction. Block addons create a header or footer around the control.

InputGroupButton takes Ledger Button variants (`subtle` by default) and Button's `xsmall` (24px, the default) or `small` (28px). With `icon` and `label` it is an icon-only square that `label` names: a clear, a copy or a calendar button. It shows no tooltip, since the field beside it says what it acts on; a control that needs one outside a field is an [IconButton](?path=/docs/components-iconbutton--docs). `xs` and `sm` are the deprecated spellings of `xsmall` and `small`, and `icon-xs` and `icon-sm` the deprecated square forms that `icon` and `label` replace, each kept for one version. The group takes its height from the control in it: a `size="small"` Input or SelectTrigger makes it 28px, and a small button in an addon leaves it as it is.

_Example: story `Stories.Buttons`._

`align` places an addon; the DOM places it in the focus order. Write the control first and the addons after it: an addon takes its position from `align`, so an interactive addon aligned `inline-start` still follows the input in the Tab order, the order a screen reader meets them in.

The input or textarea supplies the group's focus, invalid, read-only and disabled looks: focus is one continuous 2px edge around the whole group, in the error colour when the field is invalid, as on Input and Textarea; read-only is the sunken surface with a dashed edge. Disabling an addon button does not disable or dim the editable field.

_Example: story `Stories.Units`._
_Example: story `Stories.Multiline`._
_Example: story `Stories.States`._

## Narrow

A keyboard hint, an InputGroupText holding a [Kbd](?path=/docs/components-kbd--docs), shows while the group is 256px or wider and steps aside below that, so the input keeps the room; units, prefixes and buttons stay at every width. A group with a hint measures itself as a size container, so give it a definite width (the layout's, `w-full` or a style width), not a shrink-to-fit parent. Squeezed narrower than its addons, the group clips them at its own edge and never paints over its neighbours, but the field is unusable at that width: a row that crowded takes the search as an icon button instead, as the [Shell's top nav](?path=/docs/layout-shell--docs) does below `md` (see Don't).

_Example: story `Stories.Narrow`._

## Accessibility

Label the control with Field or an explicit accessible name. The group and its addons are not groups of their own to assistive technology: InputGroup takes `role="group"` only when it is given a name (`aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`), for a frame that holds several controls, and drops an unnamed `group` role a composing part hands it, as Combobox's input does. Decorative icons use `aria-hidden`; explanatory text and actions remain available to assistive technology. Give icon buttons accessible names. Addon buttons are real keyboard stops and default to `type="button"`. Clicking non-interactive addon space focuses the input or textarea; custom click handlers can cancel this.

_Example: story `Stories.SearchBox`._

## Props

Group and Addon accept native div props and refs; Text accepts span props. Input and Textarea parts preserve their control contracts and refs. Button preserves Ledger Button's native Base UI composition, loading and disabled behavior. There are no configured content slots.

_Props: generated from `InputGroup`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._

<!-- page: Components/Item (src/stories/components/Item.mdx) -->

# Item

**Status: Stable.**

A compact record row with aligned identifiers, descriptions, dates and independent actions. Item retains Ledger's record-list layout; Base UI owns link composition and disclosure behavior.

## Anatomy

Item.Group renders an ordered list inside a div. Rows share a six-column grid: disclosure, leading mark, record id, title/body, trailing value and actions. Expanded content starts under the title. A group can supply its heading, count (capped at `countMax`, Count's `max`: 99 unsaid, `9999` for a count of rows), trailing action and empty message.

_Example: story `Stories.Lists`._

## Variants and states

Use `link` to navigate, `onSelect` for an action, or neither for a plain row. `isActive` marks the row open beside the list: a selected fill (in forced colours, which remove the fill, a Highlight outline inside the row's edge), and `aria-current="true"` on its link or button. A link takes precedence over onSelect. Secondary actions and disclosure buttons remain outside the title link/button.

A row that opens a record is a link, never an `onSelect` that changes the address: a button cannot be opened in a new tab or copied.

_Example: story `Stories.DoDont`._

The title is one line by default. A title, an id or a meta that is cut shows in full in a tooltip on hover, and a cut title also when its row's link or button takes keyboard focus. `maxTitleLines` gives a list of long names two or three lines before the ellipsis. Beside a meta, the title gives way first: a short meta ("CAT I") keeps its words, and a long one is cut only past half the line, so it cannot crowd the title out. A group heading wraps rather than cutting.

_Example: story `Stories.OpenRowAndDescription`._

_Example: story `Stories.LongNames`._

`children` display below the row; add `isCollapsible` to fold them. Use `defaultOpen` or controlled `open` with Base UI's `onOpenChange(open, details)`. Call `details.cancel()` to reject a change.

Group `size="compact"` reduces vertical padding. `flush` extends separators and hover backgrounds to the card edges, and draws a row's focus ring inside its edge, so the card's clipping cannot cut its sides. `idWidth` defaults to 72px (`dimension.part.itemId`); align it across related rows.

A group shows its `empty` when its children render nothing: empty arrays, `false` and empty fragments count as nothing, so a list fed from several mapped sources that are all empty shows its empty state.

_Example: story `Stories.EmptyFromSeveralSources`._

_Example: story `Stories.ItemMatrix`._
_Example: story `Stories.Nested`._

## Accessibility

The title is a real anchor or button. Enter follows links; Space activates buttons. Disclosure buttons announce expanded state and reference the linked title's id. The chevron is the kit's 20px row control (`IconButton size="xxsmall"`), named by the title and with no tooltip of its own; it sits above the title's stretched link, so a click or a tap on it opens the row and never follows the link, and where any pointer is coarse its hit area is 24px. Actions are independent tab stops. Plain rows stay out of the tab order unless the caller explicitly supplies tabIndex for programmatic focus.

A group title names the list. It is a heading at the contextual level: an h3 when nothing sets one, one below a titled Section, an h2 in a rail that starts its outline at 2 with `HeadingLevelProvider level={2}`. When a surrounding card or section already draws the heading, point `aria-labelledby` at it; with no visible heading, `aria-label` names the list. Both reach the `ol`, not the wrapper, and the group's own `title` wins over them. `labelledBy` is the deprecated name of `aria-labelledby`, kept for one version. A compact `empty` message is body text, not a heading.

_Example: story `Stories.GroupHeadingLevel`._

_Example: story `Stories.GroupNamedFromOutside`._

Keep link titles descriptive; meta and trailing values are separate from the link's accessible name. The id, the meta and the description are the link's or button's accessible description, in that order, so rows that share a name ("personnel or roles") read apart: "personnel or roles, button, ac-01_odp.01 Assignment". The trailing value is not.

_Example: story `Stories.NativeIntegration`._

In a right-to-left document the columns run from the right, the id first, and every title, a link, a button or a disclosure, starts at its start edge.

_Example: story `Stories.RightToLeft`._

## Props

_Props of `Item`, generated from its types:_

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `leading` | `ReactNode` |  | Before the id, centred on the title's line: a Dot, an Avatar, an icon. A 20px slot, so the marks of a list line up. |
| `id` | `ReactNode` |  | The record's id, in its own column so a list of ids lines up. |

| `title` (required) | `ReactNode` |  | The row's name, one line by default. A name that is cut shows in full in a tooltip on hover and on keyboard focus of the row. The link or button of a row is this element, stretched over the row. |

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |

| `title` | `ReactNode` |  | A heading over the rows, semibold with a rule under it: "Milestones". It names the list, and a long one wraps. The heading takes the contextual level, an h3 outside every HeadingLevelProvider. |

Item forwards native li attributes, styles, events and refs. Its existing `id`, `title` and `onSelect` props keep their record-content/action meanings. Item.Group forwards native div attributes and refs to the outer wrapper, except `aria-label` and `aria-labelledby`, which name the list; its `title` remains the visible group heading. Each part names itself last with `data-slot` (`item`, `item-group`). Styles merge with the standalone row grid.

`link={<Link to="/record" />}` uses Base UI useRender to preserve the supplied link's attributes, ref, handlers and id. Leave the link empty to use Item's configured title. Explicit link children follow Base UI's rendered-element precedence. No router dependency is added.

<!-- page: Components/Kbd (src/stories/components/Kbd.mdx) -->

# Kbd

**Status: Stable.**

Keyboard input displayed as a keycap, in text, tooltips and menu hints. Use `KbdShortcut`
for a shortcut written once for every platform (`"Mod+K"` is ⌘ K on a Mac and Ctrl K
elsewhere), and `KbdGroup` to compose the caps of a shortcut by hand. The existing
`Kbd.Group` alias also works.

_Example: story `Stories.KbdMatrix`._

## Anatomy

All three parts render native `<kbd>` elements and accept their native props and refs.
`Kbd` draws a 16px-tall cap, at least 16px wide, using the sunken surface, default
border, extra-small radius and small text tokens. `KbdGroup` and `KbdShortcut` space
their caps 4px apart.

```tsx
import { Kbd, KbdGroup, KbdShortcut } from "@ledger/design-system";

<KbdShortcut keys="Mod+K" />

<KbdGroup>
  <Kbd>Ctrl</Kbd>
  <Kbd>[</Kbd>
</KbdGroup>
```

Use separate caps when that makes a multi-key shortcut easier to read.

## Shortcuts on every platform

Write a shortcut once, as keys joined by `+`, with `Mod` for the platform's modifier:
`"Mod+K"`, `"Mod+Shift+P"`, `"Ctrl+["`, `"Escape"`. `Mod` is Command on macOS, iOS and
iPadOS and Control elsewhere. `KbdShortcut` draws the keys in the platform's glyphs and
order (⇧⌘P on a Mac, Ctrl Shift P elsewhere), capitalizes a single character, and names the
named keys once: the arrows, Enter (↵), Escape (Esc), Tab, Space, Backspace and Delete.
Use `Mod` for a chord that follows the platform, and `Ctrl` for one that is Control
everywhere, like the side nav's Ctrl [; on Apple platforms Control is drawn ⌃, so it
reads ⌃ [ there.

_Example: story `Stories.Shortcuts`._

A shortcut that follows the platform is never drawn with one platform's glyph: a hand-written ⌘ names a key a Windows reader does not have, and a screen reader reads it as its character name. Write `Mod` and let KbdShortcut draw it.

_Example: story `Stories.DoDont`._

The platform is read once for the page, and every shortcut in the kit reads the same
answer:

- **`useModifierKey()`** for a render: `"meta"` or `"ctrl"`. The server and the first
  client render say `"ctrl"`, so hydration matches; the browser's answer follows straight
  after. `KbdShortcut` uses it.
- **`getModifierKey()`** for a key handler, which runs in the browser: test `event.metaKey`
  when it says `"meta"` and `event.ctrlKey` when it says `"ctrl"`.
- **`useFormatShortcut()`** returns a function that gives a shortcut as a string, following
  the locale and the platform: `format("Mod+K")` is the text for a hint or a title ("⌘K",
  "Ctrl+K"), `format("Mod+K", "label")` what a screen reader says ("Command K"), and
  `format("Mod+K", "aria")` the value for `aria-keyshortcuts` on the control the shortcut
  runs ("Meta+K"). `formatShortcut(shortcut, { modifier, messages, as })` is the same,
  pure, for code outside React; in a render, prefer the hook, which hydrates safely.
- **`shortcutKeys(shortcut, options)`** gives each key's cap, spoken name and
  `aria-keyshortcuts` name, for a caller that draws its own.

Pass `modifier` to show one platform's keys regardless of the reader's, as documentation
does. The kit draws shortcuts; binding one to an action stays with the caller.

_Example: story `Stories.PlatformModifier`._

## Accessibility

`<kbd>` marks up keyboard input. Caps and groups have no built-in focus or activation
behavior; the surrounding button or menu item owns the action. Keep the action's name
in the surrounding text, such as “Press Command K to search.”

`KbdShortcut` hides its caps from assistive technology and adds one visually hidden line
with the keys' names ("Shift Command P"), so a screen reader never reads a glyph's
character name. Put `aria-keyshortcuts` (from `useFormatShortcut`) on the control the
shortcut runs.

On `Kbd`, `label` gives a glyph its spoken name. ARIA names no `<kbd>`, so the glyph is
hidden from assistive technology and one visually hidden word is read in its place: "Press ⌘
K to search." is heard as "Press Command K to search.". `KbdGroup` takes `label` for the
whole chord ("Command K"), read once in place of its caps. An `aria-label` on either is read
the same way and takes precedence; it is never set on the element. For a shortcut that
follows the platform, prefer `KbdShortcut`.

Key names and word caps come from the locale's messages (`keyCommand`, `keyControl`,
`keyCapControl` and the rest), so a German product shows Strg and says Steuerung.

## Props

`className`, `style`, attributes, events and `ref` target each part's own `<kbd>`.
All refs use `HTMLElement`. Parts expose `data-slot="kbd"`, `data-slot="kbd-group"` and
`data-slot="kbd-shortcut"`; a shortcut also carries `data-modifier`, the platform it drew.

_Props of `Kbd`, generated from its types:_

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `label` | `string` |  | A glyph's spoken name, such as "Command" for ⌘. The glyph is hidden from assistive technology and one visually hidden word says the name in its place, since ARIA does not name a `<kbd>`. An `aria-label` is read the same way and takes precedence. |

_Props of `KbdGroup`, generated from its types:_

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `label` | `string` |  | The chord's spoken name, such as "Command K". The caps are hidden from assistive technology and the name is read once in their place. An `aria-label` is read the same way and takes precedence. |

_Props of `KbdShortcut`, generated from its types:_

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `keys` (required) | `string` |  | The shortcut, written once for every platform: "Mod+K", "Mod+Shift+P", "Ctrl+[", "Escape". `Mod` is Command on Apple platforms and Control elsewhere. |
| `modifier` | `"ctrl" \| "meta"` |  | What `Mod` stands for. The platform's by default; set it to show one platform's keys, as documentation does. |

_Example: story `Stories.Playground`._
_Rendered in the Storybook: Controls._

<!-- page: Components/KeyValue (src/stories/components/KeyValue.mdx) -->

# KeyValue

**Status: Stable.**

One rail row: a label column and a value. Owner, Frequency, Last verified, each on its own line with the label in one column so the values make a column too. On its own it is a definition list of one pair, valid wherever it sits; a rail's rows go in one **KeyValue.Group**, which makes them one definition list and gives them one label width.

It is one of two ways to write a fact. A [Fact](?path=/docs/components-fact--docs) is inline, label then value on one baseline, for the strip under a record's title; a KeyValue is a row, for the rail and the inspector.

_Example: story `Stories.KeyValueMatrix`._

## Anatomy

| Part  | What it is                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| ----- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Label | `dt` in the label column, `labelWidth` wide (`default`, 104px, without one, or the group's), `font.body` in `color.text.subtle`. A label longer than its column wraps to the next line, its first line on the value's baseline; it is never cut (the Cut Value, Whole Label story).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| Value | `dd` in the rest, `font.body` in `color.text`: text, a Badge, a Person, a TextLink, an Absent. Truncates unless `wrap`, which also breaks an unbroken identifier or timestamp inside the rail (the Unbroken story). A cut value, plain or composed (a code and a title, a TextLink), shows its whole text in a tooltip on hover and when a control inside it takes keyboard focus, through [Truncate](?path=/docs/components-truncate--docs). It truncates across only, at its own box, so a control in the value keeps its focus ring and touch area above and below the row (the Control In A Value story). Across, a link draws its ring inside its own edge and a link that is the whole value is cut to the value's width with its own ellipsis; the value keeps `space.050` at its end for a control that ends there; a value that is an [Editable](?path=/docs/patterns-editable--docs) does not clip, so the Editable's tint, ring and field keep their sides and its text stays on the column (the Ring Room story). |
| Row   | `space.050` above and below, `space.150` between label and value, baselines aligned.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |

## Variants

KeyValue has one appearance. What varies is the value:

| The value              | Use               |
| ---------------------- | ----------------- |
| A word, a name, a date | Text.             |
| A state                | A Badge.          |
| A person               | A Person.         |
| A record               | A TextLink.       |
| A statement            | Text with `wrap`. |
| Nothing                | An Absent.        |

Not built, and why: an editable value, because that is an [Editable](?path=/docs/patterns-editable--docs) inside the value.

## KeyValue.Group

One `dl` for a rail, an inspector group or a row's More fields. Its KeyValues become its rows (a `div` holding the `dt` and `dd`, which HTML allows), share its `labelWidth` through context, and follow its `layout`:

| `layout`         | Rows                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| ---------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `auto` (default) | Label beside value while the value has at least 8rem beside the label; label over value when the group is narrower (a phone, a narrow panel). Every row changes together, because every row has the same width and the same label and value bases. It is intrinsic layout (a wrapping row), so it responds to the group's own width, not the window. |
| `columns`        | Label beside value at any width: a rail of one-line rows.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| `stacked`        | Label over value, always; each takes the row's width, so a long value truncates in it.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |

A row's own `labelWidth` overrides the group's; give the width to the group once instead. A screen reader hears one list of pairs instead of one list per fact. The group ends at each value: a KeyValue inside a value (a peek's facts, a HoverCard's) is its own definition list again (the Group Ends At The Value story).

_Example: story `Stories.Group`._

_Example: story `Stories.GroupInANarrowPanel`._

_Example: story `Stories.GroupLayouts`._

_Example: story `Stories.GroupEndsAtTheValue`._

## Sizes

One size, `font.body`. The row is as wide as its rail; the label column is `labelWidth`, the same for every row in one rail, and the value takes the rest. The column is a named step on the dimension tokens, drawn in rem, so it grows with the reader's text size as the label does: `default` is 104px at 16px and 130px at 20px (the Group Layouts story).

| `labelWidth`        | Column                                  | Token                                  | Use                                                                                                       |
| ------------------- | --------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `narrow`            | 88px                                    | `dimension.part.keyValueLabelNarrow`   | Short labels in a card, a Glance or a chart's details: Owner, Open, Target.                               |
| `default` (or none) | 104px                                   | `dimension.part.keyValueLabel`         | A rail: Owner, Frequency, Last verified.                                                                  |
| `wide`              | 160px                                   | `dimension.part.keyValueLabelWide`     | Labels of about twenty characters: Authorizing official.                                                  |
| `auto`              | The group's longest label, up to `wide` | `dimension.part.keyValueLabelWide` cap | A page body, whose labels the screen does not know ahead: the column fits them, and a longer label wraps. |

`auto` makes the group one grid whose rows share its two columns, so every value starts after the longest label. In the `auto` layout the group is a container, and below 20rem (`dimension.container.xs`) each label goes over its value, as the named steps do when the value has less than 8rem. A rail keeps a named step: its width is known, and `auto` would move the values whenever a label changes.

A number of pixels (`labelWidth={144}`) is deprecated for one version: it is drawn as its rem, and `ledger/no-deprecated-name` writes the nearest step (up to 96 `narrow`, under 132 `default`, from 132 `wide`); in a page body, write `auto` instead.

_Example: story `Stories.LabelWidths`._

_Example: story `Stories.AutoLabelColumn`._

_Example: story `Stories.InRail`._

## States

A KeyValue has one state. Its value may: a Badge is a state, a TextLink hovers. The row does not.

## Modifiers

- **`labelWidth`**: the label column, `narrow`, `default`, `wide` or `auto`, the same down one rail; on the KeyValue.Group once.
- **`wrap`** for a value that is a sentence.
- **The value** as in Variants.

## Content

- **The label is a noun**, one or two words, no colon: "Owner", "Last verified", "Next due". The column is the colon.
- **Keep a label to one line at its width**: about 14 characters at `default`, about 20 at `wide`. A longer label wraps rather than being cut, so nothing is lost, but a rail of two-line labels reads slowly: give the KeyValue.Group the step that fits its longest label ("Authorizing official" takes `wide`), `auto` in a page body, or shorten the label. Three lines means the label is a sentence; say it in the value or a description.
- **The value is one thing.** Two facts are two rows.
- **Nothing there is an Absent**, not an empty row and not "N/A", which is a different fact.
- **The order is the order the reader asks:** who, how often, when last, when next, then the rest.

## Style

| Element | Token                                                                  |
| ------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Label   | `font.body` · `color.text.subtle` · `labelWidth` column                |
| Value   | `font.body` · `color.text` · `space.050` at the end while it truncates |
| Row     | `space.050` block · `space.150` between columns · baselines aligned    |

## Accessibility

- **It is a definition list**: `dl`, `dt`, `dd`, so a screen reader hears "Owner, Dana Whitfield" as a pair. In a KeyValue.Group a rail is one list of pairs.
- **The label is never cut.** It wraps inside its column, so a sighted reader, a screen reader and a touch reader all read the same label.
- **A cut value shows its whole text** in a tooltip on hover and on keyboard focus of a control inside it. The tooltip is a visual copy: the full text is in the DOM and read by a screen reader. A value that matters whole takes `wrap`, so no one has to hover; a touch screen has no hover.
- **A control in the value keeps its ring and its touch area,** in every browser, with no clip margin. The value clips with the ellipsis across and leaves the block axis visible, so a control keeps its focus ring above and below and, where a pointer is coarse, a touch area at least 24px tall. Across: a [TextLink](?path=/docs/components-textlink--docs) draws the kit's ring inside its own edge, as a link in a table cell does; a link that is the whole value is cut to the value's width, so its ring and its ellipsis are its own and focus on it reveals the whole text; the value keeps `space.050` at its end for a control that ends there; and a value that is an [Editable](?path=/docs/patterns-editable--docs) does not clip, since the Editable truncates its own text and keeps its reach inside its box at the end. A link inside a composed value (a code and a title) stays inline, so where it runs past the value's end its ring is cut there; focus on it still shows the whole value in the tooltip.
- **The label is text, not a heading.** A rail's sections are headed by an Eyebrow or a Collapsible; the label names one fact.
- **Contrast:** the label in `color.text.subtle` passes 4.5:1; the gate runs the matrix.

_Example: story `Stories.ControlInAValue`._

_Example: story `Stories.RingRoom`._

_Example: story `Stories.CutValueAndLabel`._

## Props

Native props and refs target the row's root: the `dl` on its own, the row `div` inside a KeyValue.Group. Use IDs, data attributes and event handlers directly; `className` merges with the default row classes, and caller `style` can override the columns computed from `labelWidth`. On a KeyValue.Group with an `auto` column, the caller's `style` can override the group's columns. The inner `dt`/`dd`, the wrapping label and the reveal of a cut value are preserved.

_Props of `KeyValue`, generated from its types:_

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `label` (required) | `string` |  | The fact's name, in the label column: "Owner", "Last verified". A label longer than its column wraps to the next line; it is never cut. |
| `labelWidth` | `number \| KeyValueLabelWidth` | `"default"` | The label column: `narrow` (88px) for short labels in a card, a glance or a chart's details, `default` (104px) for a rail, `wide` (160px) for labels of about twenty characters, each at the default text size and growing with the reader's; `auto`, as wide as the longest label up to `wide`, in a page body. Inside a KeyValue.Group it is the group's; every KeyValue in one rail takes the same, so give it to the group once. A number of CSS pixels is deprecated: write the nearest step, which `ledger/no-deprecated-name` writes. |
| `wrap` | `boolean` |  | Lets a long value run to several lines instead of truncating: a statement, an objective. |

### KeyValue.Group

Native `dl` props, a ref and `render` target the group's list.

_Props of `KeyValue.Group`, generated from its types:_

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `render` | `ReactElement<unknown, string \| JSXElementConstructor<any>> \| ComponentRenderFn<HTMLProps, {}>` |  | Allows you to replace the component's HTML element with a different tag, or compose it with another component. Accepts a `ReactElement` or a function that returns the element to render. |
| `labelWidth` | `number \| KeyValueLabelWidth` | `"default"` | The label column for every row: `narrow` (88px), `default` (104px, a rail's), `wide` (160px), each at the default text size and growing with the reader's, or `auto`, as wide as the group's longest label up to `wide`, for a page body. In an `auto` layout an `auto` column puts each label over its value when the group is under 20rem (`dimension.container.xs`). A row's own `labelWidth` overrides it. A number of CSS pixels is deprecated: write the nearest step, which `ledger/no-deprecated-name` writes. |
| `layout` | `"auto" \| "columns" \| "stacked"` | `auto` | `auto` (the default) keeps each label beside its value while the value has at least 8rem (`dimension.part.keyValue`), and puts the label over the value when the group is narrower: a rail, a phone, a narrow panel. `columns` never stacks; `stacked` always does. |

# LinkButton

**Status: Stable.**

Navigation that looks like a button: “View requirements”, “Create program” when it opens a page, “Open my work”. LinkButton is an anchor, or the application's router Link through `render`, with [Button](?path=/docs/components-button--docs)'s variants, sizes, icon slots and insets. Because it is a real link, the reader can middle-click it, copy its address or open it in a new tab, and Base UI's native-button check never sees it. LinkIconButton is its icon-only form.

Use Button for an action that happens on this page, and [TextLink](?path=/docs/components-textlink--docs) for a link inside a sentence or a record name in a table. A Button that navigates from `onClick`, or a Button that renders a router Link, is the mistake this part replaces.

_Example: story `Stories.Matrix`._

## Variants and sizes

| Variant     | Use                                                              |
| ----------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `secondary` | The default: a destination beside other actions.                 |
| `primary`   | The main destination of a region, such as Continue to review.    |
| `subtle`    | A low-emphasis destination in a toolbar, a row or a card footer. |
| `danger`    | A destination that leads to a destructive task, rarely.          |

Sizes are Button's: `medium` 32px (the default), `small` 28px and `xsmall` 24px. `iconBefore` and `iconAfter` take an icon element, drawn at 14px and hidden from assistive technology, and the icon's side takes the smaller inset. `isFullWidth` fills the container. There is no `link` variant: a link that looks like text is a TextLink.

## Router links

Pass the router's Link through `render`. It keeps its href, its client-side navigation and its active state; LinkButton supplies the look, the icons and the children. A custom component must forward the props and the ref it receives to its anchor.

```tsx
import { Link } from "@tanstack/react-router";
import { LinkButton } from "@ledger/design-system";

<LinkButton variant="primary" iconBefore={<Plus />} render={<Link to="/programs/new" />}>
  Create program
</LinkButton>;
```

TanStack Router's `createLink(LinkButton)` works too, and gives a component that takes the router's `to`, `params` and `search` directly. A router marks a link to the current page with `aria-current="page"`; that is right for a LinkButton that points at the page the reader is on.

_Example: story `Stories.RouterLink`._

## LinkIconButton

The icon-only form, with a required `label` that names the destination and shows in its tooltip on hover and keyboard focus, as on [IconButton](?path=/docs/components-iconbutton--docs). Its sizes are IconButton's: `small` 28px (the default), `medium` 32px with a 16px icon, `xsmall` 24px and `xxsmall` 20px, the row control. Where any pointer is coarse it takes a hit area of at least 24px. Say where it goes, including a new tab: “Open CTRL-0412 in a new tab”. `isTooltipDisabled` drops the tooltip when the label is already visible nearby.

_Example: story `Stories.IconOnly`._

## Disabled with a reason

A destination that is not ready takes `disabledReason`. The link loses its href and stays in the tab order as a disabled link (`role="link"`, `aria-disabled="true"`), so a keyboard reader reaches it and learns why: the reason is its accessible description and shows in a tooltip on hover, on keyboard focus and on a tap. Clicks and Enter do nothing. While a reason is set the `render` element is not rendered, only its children, so a router link cannot navigate or appear in the browser's link menu. On LinkIconButton the tooltip shows the label and then the reason.

Prefer a destination that is always available and explains on arrival; use a reason when following the link would only lead to an error.

_Example: story `Stories.DisabledWithAReason`._

A reason that comes or goes while the link has focus leaves focus on it: a report that becomes ready while the reader is on View report gets its href and router link back, and Enter follows it.

_Example: story `Stories.ReasonChangesWhileFocused`._

## Accessibility

- It is a link: Tab reaches it, Enter follows it, and Space does not, as for any link. A screen reader announces a link, so the label names a destination (“View requirements”), not an operation (“Save”).
- An external or new-tab destination says so in its label, or in a visible icon with the words in `label` for LinkIconButton.
- The icons are decorative; the name comes from the children or `label`.
- The focus ring, the hit area on touch and the disabled face are Button's.

## Props

_Props of `LinkButton`, generated from its types:_

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `render` | `ReactElement<unknown, string \| JSXElementConstructor<any>> \| ComponentRenderFn<HTMLProps, {}>` |  | Allows you to replace the component's HTML element with a different tag, or compose it with another component. Accepts a `ReactElement` or a function that returns the element to render. |
| `variant` | `"danger" \| "primary" \| "secondary" \| "subtle"` | `secondary` | Secondary is the default; primary emphasizes the main destination. A link in text is TextLink. |
| `size` | `"medium" \| "small" \| "xsmall"` | `medium` | Medium is 32px, small 28px and xsmall 24px, as on Button. |
| `isFullWidth` | `boolean` |  | Fill the available width. |
| `iconBefore` | `ReactElement<unknown, string \| JSXElementConstructor<any>>` |  | Decorative leading icon. |
| `iconAfter` | `ReactElement<unknown, string \| JSXElementConstructor<any>>` |  | Decorative trailing icon, such as an arrow or an external-link mark. |
| `disabledReason` | `string` |  | Why the destination is unavailable. The link loses its href and stays in the tab order as a disabled link (`role="link"`, `aria-disabled`); the reason shows in a tooltip on hover, on keyboard focus and on a tap, and is the link's accessible description. While it is set, a `render` element is not rendered, only its children, so a router link cannot navigate. An empty string is no reason. |

### LinkIconButton

_Props of `LinkIconButton`, generated from its types:_

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |

Accepts a `ReactElement` or a function that returns the element to render. |

While it is set, a `render` element is not rendered, only its children, so a router link cannot navigate. An empty string is no reason. |
| `label` (required) | `string` |  | The destination's accessible name, also used by the tooltip. |

| `isTooltipDisabled` | `boolean` |  | Keep the accessible name while omitting the tooltip. A `disabledReason` still shows its own. |

# List

**Status: Stable.**

Bulleted and numbered lists on one inset and two spacings: validation messages, conflicts, the steps of an instruction, the points of a narrative. The marker hangs in the inset, so each item's text lines up with the text above the list. It is a real `ul` or `ol`, so a screen reader says how many items there are.

```tsx
<List>
  <List.Item>Choose a profile.</List.Item>
  <List.Item>Add at least one system.</List.Item>
</List>
```

_Example: story `Stories.ListMatrix`._

## When to use it

- **Two or more short points** a reader should see as separate: what is missing before a program can be created, the conflicts in a selection.
- **`ordered`** when the order matters (steps, a ranking, an order the text refers to); bullets otherwise.
- **`spacing="loose"`** when items are sentences or wrap; `tight`, the default, for short lines.
- **Not for records.** A list of records a reader opens or acts on is an [Item.Group](?path=/docs/components-item--docs), a [Timeline](?path=/docs/components-timeline--docs) or a DataTable.
- **Not for facts.** Labelled values are [KeyValue](?path=/docs/components-keyvalue--docs) rows in a KeyValue.Group.
- **Authored Markdown** renders its lists through this part: [Prose](?path=/docs/components-typography--docs) with `markdown`.

_Example: story `Stories.Semantics`._

## Anatomy

| Part      | What it is                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| --------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| List      | `ul` (`list-disc`, `space.200` inset) or `ol` with `ordered` (`list-decimal`, `space.300` inset, for two-digit numbers). The inset is logical: it moves to the right in a right-to-left locale. |
| List.Item | `li`, `space.025` from its marker; it wraps and breaks a long word rather than running past the list.                                                                                           |
| Spacing   | `space.025` between items when `tight`, `space.100` when `loose`.                                                                                                                               |

The list takes its size and colour from where it sits: an Alert's description, a Field's error, a paragraph's size. `start` numbers an ordered list from where the text left off. A List inside a List.Item nests.

_Example: story `Stories.InAnAlert`._

## Accessibility

- **A list is announced as a list** with its count, and each item as one of that count. Bullets typed into text are read as characters.
- **Markers are drawn by CSS**, so they are not read as words.
- **Links in items** are TextLinks; an item that is a whole record is not a list item but an Item.

## Props

### List

_Props of `List`, generated from its types:_

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `render` | `ReactElement<unknown, string \| JSXElementConstructor<any>> \| ComponentRenderFn<HTMLProps, {}>` |  | Allows you to replace the component's HTML element with a different tag, or compose it with another component. Accepts a `ReactElement` or a function that returns the element to render. |
| `ordered` | `boolean` |  | Numbers the items (`ol`) instead of bulleting them (`ul`): steps, a ranked order, an order the text refers to. |
| `spacing` | `"loose" \| "tight"` |  | The space between items: `tight` (the default) for short lines such as validation messages, `loose` for items that are sentences or wrap. |
| `start` | `number` |  | The number of the first item of an ordered list. |

### List.Item

_Props of `ListItem`, generated from its types:_

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `render` | `ReactElement<unknown, string \| JSXElementConstructor<any>> \| ComponentRenderFn<HTMLProps, {}>` |  | Allows you to replace the component's HTML element with a different tag, or compose it with another component. Accepts a `ReactElement` or a function that returns the element to render. |
