# Locale

**Status: Stable.**

**LedgerProvider** gives every part under it the reader's locale, time zone and writing direction, and the kit's own words. Every date, number and label a part shows goes through it: DateTime, RelativeTime and DateLabel, DataTable's `c.date`, the Calendar's first day of the week, a typed day in a DatePicker, Pagination's words, Shell's landmark names. Mount one near the root, with the reader's zone.

_Example: story `Stories.ReadersZone`._

## At the root

```tsx
import { LedgerProvider, ModeProvider, Toaster } from "@ledger/design-system";

<ModeProvider>
  <LedgerProvider locale="en-US" timeZone={readerTimeZone}>
    <App />
    <Toaster />
  </LedgerProvider>
</ModeProvider>;
```

The provider renders one element around its children, carrying `lang` from `locale` and `dir` from `direction`. Parts that draw in a portal outside it and depend on direction, such as the Toaster, a Combobox popup, the Calendar and a chart's tooltip, read it from the provider instead.

| Option      | Without it                             | What it decides                                                                                                                                               |
| ----------- | -------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `locale`    | `en-US`, never the host's              | A BCP 47 tag: the words and numerals of dates and numbers, plural rules, 12- or 24-hour clocks, the first day of the week, and how a typed day or time reads. |
| `timeZone`  | `UTC`                                  | The IANA zone instants show in, such as `America/New_York`. A calendar day never shifts, whatever the zone.                                                   |
| `direction` | `ltr`                                  | `rtl` for a right-to-left language.                                                                                                                           |
| `messages`  | The English words in `defaultMessages` | The kit's labels, announcements and templates, by key. Pass a module constant: a new object on every render rebuilds the formatters.                          |

A nested provider inherits every option it does not set, and merges its `messages` over its parent's, so a region can take another zone or a few other words without repeating the rest.

## Days and instants

An ISO day (`"2026-09-18"`) is a calendar day: a due date, a milestone. It reads the same day everywhere. An instant (an ISO timestamp with an offset, a `Date`, epoch milliseconds) is a point in time, shown in the provider's zone, so the same instant is the evening of Sep 18 in Los Angeles and the morning of Sep 19 in Tokyo. Without a `timeZone`, every instant shows in UTC, and an evening entered in the Americas reads as the next day.

_Example: story `Stories.InstantsAndDays`._

## The same on the server and the client

Pass the same locale and zone to the provider on the server and on the client, or the markup will not match on hydration. The server knows the reader's zone only when the product stores it, as an account preference or a cookie; pass the stored value on both sides. Otherwise render the server's zone first and take the reader's once the client has hydrated:

```tsx
import { useSyncExternalStore } from "react";

const subscribe = () => () => {};
const readerZone = () => Intl.DateTimeFormat().resolvedOptions().timeZone;

/** The reader's zone on the client, and `serverZone` while rendering on the server and hydrating. */
export function useReaderTimeZone(serverZone = "UTC") {
  return useSyncExternalStore(subscribe, readerZone, () => serverZone);
}
```

React renders the server snapshot during hydration, then renders again with the client's, so the first paint matches the server and the dates settle into the reader's zone straight after. Never read the host's locale or zone during a server render.

## Formatters in your own code

Show a date with DateTime, RelativeTime or DateLabel, and a date column with `c.date`. Where no part fits, such as an export, a message you `announce`, or a document title, `useLedgerLocale()` returns the provider's formatters:

| Returns                                                        | For                                                                                                                             |
| -------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `formatDate(value, options?)`                                  | An instant (a `Date` or epoch milliseconds, not a string), in the provider's zone. `options` are `Intl.DateTimeFormat` options. |
| `formatDay(day, options?)`, `formatDayRange`                   | A calendar day `{ year, month, day }`, or two, never shifted.                                                                   |
| `formatCalendarDate(date, options?)`                           | A `Date` read as the local year, month and day it was picked on, such as a Calendar's, never shifted.                           |
| `formatTime(time, options?)`                                   | A wall-clock time `{ hour, minute }`, on the locale's clock.                                                                    |
| `formatRelative(value, now?, style?)`                          | "5 minutes ago", "tomorrow": `{ text, next }`, `next` being the milliseconds until the words change.                            |
| `formatNumber(value, options?)`                                | A number, with `Intl.NumberFormat` options.                                                                                     |
| `formatPlural(count, forms)`                                   | The form for a count, from `{ one, other }` and the locale's other categories, with `{count}`.                                  |
| `t(key, params?)`                                              | One of the kit's messages, with its `{name}` placeholders filled.                                                               |
| `zonedParts(value)`, `toInstant(day, time)`                    | The day and time an instant falls on in the zone, and the instant a day and time name there.                                    |
| `timeZoneName(value, style?)`                                  | The zone's name at an instant: "PDT", or "Pacific Daylight Time" with `"long"`.                                                 |
| `parseDay(text)`, `parseTime(text)`                            | A day or time typed in the locale's words, or `null`.                                                                           |
| `locale`, `timeZone`, `direction`, `hourCycle`, `weekStartsOn` | The resolved values.                                                                                                            |

`createLedgerLocale(options)` returns the same object without React, for server code, a worker or a test.

_Example: story `Stories.Formatters`._

## Messages

Every word the kit writes itself (Close, Clear filters, "2 of 3 records", "Sort by", the landmarks' names) is a message. `defaultMessages` lists every key with its English text. Translate a template whole, placeholders included, so the word order follows the language: `recordPosition` is `"{position} of {total} records"`. A part's own `label` prop still overrides one instance.

_Example: story `Stories.Messages`._

## Direction

_Example: story `Stories.RightToLeft`._

## Props

_Props of `LedgerProvider`, generated from its types:_

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `locale` | `string` |  | BCP 47 locale shared by server and client. Defaults to en-US, never the host environment. |
| `direction` | `"ltr" \| "rtl"` |  | Logical writing direction, applied to the provider scope and exposed for portals. |
| `timeZone` | `string` |  | Time zone for timestamps. Date-only calendar values use formatCalendarDate instead. |
| `messages` | `Partial<LedgerMessages>` |  | Translated messages. Nested providers inherit untranslated messages. |
| `children` (required) | `ReactNode` |  | The localized subtree. Keep locale and timeZone identical on the server and client. |

## Related

[DateTime](?path=/docs/components-datetime--docs) · [DatePicker](?path=/docs/components-datepicker--docs) · [DateTimeField](?path=/docs/components-datetimefield--docs) · [Calendar](?path=/docs/components-calendar--docs) · [Mode](?path=/docs/components-mode--docs) · [Getting started](?path=/docs/guidance-getting-started--docs)

<!-- page: Components/Mode (src/stories/components/Mode.mdx) -->

# Mode

**Status: Stable.**

The colour mode: light, dark, or whatever the machine says. It is one attribute on the root, `data-color-mode`, and every token reads it, so the whole product flips at once and no component knows. The choice is the reader's, per browser, in `localStorage` under `ledger.color-mode`; never per account, so a shared machine keeps each person's choice. **`modeScript`** applies the stored choice before the first paint, **`ModeProvider`** owns it, **`ModeSwitch`** is the control.

It is the one setting that belongs to the document. Row [density](?path=/docs/components-density--docs) is a table's; the shell's widths are the shell's.

_Example: story `Stories.Live`._

## Anatomy

| Part      | What it is                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| --------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Attribute | `data-color-mode="light"` or `"dark"` on the root pins a mode; no attribute lets `prefers-color-scheme` decide. `tokens.css` and `base.css` read it.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| Script    | `modeScript`: a string for the document head, above the stylesheet. It applies the stored choice before the first paint so nothing flashes. `modeScriptFor(key)` for another storage key.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| Provider  | `ModeProvider`: owns the choice. It reads storage as an external store, so the switch shows the stored mode from the first client render (the server renders System), a second provider with the same key on the page hears a change, and a choice made in another tab reaches this one through the `storage` event. On mount it applies the stored mode (a no-op after the script); every change is stored and applied at once, and a choice storage refuses lives for the page. `useMode()` returns `{ mode, setMode, resolved }`, `resolved` being what is on screen. |
| Switch    | `ModeSwitch`: a ToggleGroup of three, sun, moon and monitor, `sm`. Icons only in chrome, each with its name in a tooltip; `showLabels` in a settings form.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |

## Variants

One control, in two forms. **Icons only**, in the top navigation's end, where the reader expects it and a label would be noise. **With labels**, `showLabels`, in a settings form, where the three words sit in a row of other settings.

There is no two-state form. A light-or-dark toggle has no answer for a machine that changes at dusk, and it pins a choice the reader never made; system is the default and the third state.

_Example: story `Stories.ControlledStory`._

_Example: story `Stories.StoredAndShared`._

## Sizes

One: the ToggleGroup's `sm`, 28px, the height of the chrome it sits in.

## States

| State                  | Look                                                                                                              |
| ---------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Light                  | The root pinned light; the sun is the selected item.                                                              |
| Dark                   | The root pinned dark; the moon.                                                                                   |
| System                 | No attribute; the monitor. What is on screen follows the machine, and `resolved` says which.                      |
| Hover, focus, selected | The ToggleGroup's: the item tints, takes the kit's focus outline, and the selected one carries the selected fill. |

_Example: story `Stories.ModeMatrix`._

## Modifiers

- **`value` and `onChange`** on the switch override the provider, for a settings form that commits later, or for a story.
- **`showLabels`**, as in Variants.
- **`storageKey`** on the provider and **`modeScriptFor(key)`**, when a product keeps its own key. The two must agree.
- **`aria-label`** on the switch: "Appearance" by default.

## Content

- **The three words are Light, Dark and System.** Not "Match system", not "Auto", not "Night".
- **The switch's name is Appearance.** The reader is choosing how the product looks, not a "theme".
- **Never a colour by hand.** A hex value written into a component does not flip; every colour is a token, and the mode flips the tokens.
- **Never a mode-specific screen.** A page does not know which mode it is in; if a figure needs a different colour in dark, that colour is a token with two values.

## Style

| Element   | Token                                                                                              |
| --------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Switch    | The ToggleGroup, `sm`: `dimension.control.small` 28px · `dimension.icon.small` 14px                |
| Attribute | `data-color-mode` on `html` · every `color.*` and `elevation.*` token has a light and a dark value |
| Motion    | None. A mode changes at once; a fade across every surface reads as a fault.                        |

## Accessibility

- **The switch is a group of toggle buttons** named Appearance. Each button has `aria-pressed` and an accessible name, including Light, Dark and System when only icons are visible; icons only, each name also shows in a tooltip on hover and keyboard focus, as an IconButton's does.
- **Keyboard:** Tab enters and leaves the group as one stop, and that stop is the pressed mode, so the reader lands on the current choice; Left and Right move focus, and Space or Enter selects. The switch retains a selected mode when it is pressed again.
- **System honours the reader's machine,** including `prefers-color-scheme` set for a vision reason, so it is the default and never overridden by the product.
- **Contrast is tested in both modes:** every pairing on the Colour sheet, and the a11y gate runs each matrix in the mode the toolbar sets.
- **No flash:** the script marks the root before the first paint, so a reader who chose dark never sees a light page load.

## Props

_Props of `ModeSwitch`, generated from its types:_

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `style` | `CSSProperties \| ((state: ToggleGroupState) => CSSProperties)` |  | Style applied to the element, or a function that returns a style object based on the component's state. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | Whether the toggle group should ignore user interaction. |
| `render` | `ReactElement<unknown, string \| JSXElementConstructor<any>> \| ComponentRenderFn<HTMLProps, ToggleGroupState>` |  | Allows you to replace the component's HTML element with a different tag, or compose it with another component. Accepts a `ReactElement` or a function that returns the element to render. |
| `size` | `ToggleSize \| null` |  | `small` 28px, `medium` 32px (the default) or `large` 36px, Button's heights. `sm`, `default` and `lg` are the deprecated spellings of `small`, `medium` and `large`. |
| `variant` | `"default" \| "outline" \| null` |  | `default` is unbordered; `outline` draws a border. |
| `orientation` | `"horizontal" \| "vertical"` | `horizontal` |  |
| `spacing` | `number` |  | The gap between items in 4px steps on the space scale: 2 (8px, `space.100`) by default, 0 joins the items. 1 to 6, 8, 10, 12 and 16 are the steps; a number between two steps takes the smaller. |
| `loopFocus` | `boolean` | `true` | Whether to loop keyboard focus back to the first item when the end of the list is reached while using the arrow keys. |
| `value` | `"dark" \| "light" \| "system"` |  | The mode shown as chosen. Unsaid, the provider's. |
| `onChange` | `((mode: ColorMode) => void)` |  | Called with the chosen mode. Unsaid, the choice goes to the provider, unless `value` is given. |
| `showLabels` | `boolean` | `false` | Text beside each icon. Off in chrome, on in a settings form. |
| `aria-label` | `string` |  | The group's name: the locale's "Appearance" by default. |
| `className` | `string` |  |  |

The provider and the script, by hand:

| Export                               | What it is                                                                          |
| ------------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `ModeProvider`                       | Wraps the app; `storageKey` for a key of the product's own. Renders nothing itself. |
| `useMode()`                          | `{ mode, setMode, resolved }`. Throws outside a provider.                           |
| `modeScript`                         | The before-paint script for the default key; `modeScriptFor(key)` for another.      |
| `readMode`, `writeMode`, `applyMode` | The three steps the provider takes, for a product that wires them itself.           |

### Wiring it

Plain HTML: put the script in the head, above the stylesheet.

```html
<script>
  (function () {
    try {
      var m = localStorage.getItem("ledger.color-mode");
      if (m === "light" || m === "dark") document.documentElement.dataset.colorMode = m;
    } catch (e) {}
  })();
</script>
```

A framework with a `head()` hook renders the same string inline:

```tsx
import { modeScript, ModeProvider, ModeSwitch } from "@ledger/design-system";

head: () => ({ scripts: [{ children: modeScript }] });
// …
<ModeProvider>
  <Shell>
    <Shell.TopNav>
      …
      <Shell.TopNav.End>
        <ModeSwitch />
      </Shell.TopNav.End>
    </Shell.TopNav>
    …
  </Shell>
</ModeProvider>;
```

Do not also pin `data-color-mode` on the root in markup: the pin wins over the script and the switch cannot move it. Put `suppressHydrationWarning` on the `<html>` element: the script marks it before React hydrates, and React would otherwise report the mismatch.

_Example: story `Stories.Playground`._

- [Density](?path=/docs/components-density--docs): the setting that is a table's, not the document's.

## Don't

The choice has three states, Light, Dark and System, with System the default, never a two-state toggle. Every colour is a token, never one written by hand, which no mode can flip.

<!-- page: Components/NumberField (src/stories/components/NumberField.mdx) -->

# NumberField

**Status: Stable.**

A number the reader types or steps: a retention period, a budget, a count of reviewers. Base UI NumberField underneath, so the value is parsed and formatted in the reader's locale, kept within `min` and `max`, and stepped by `step` from the keyboard or the decrement and increment buttons.

_Example: story `Stories.Keyboard`._

## When to use it

- **A quantity**: a count, a period, an amount, a percentage, a score, which the reader types or steps.
- **A number with bounds or a unit**: `min` and `max` keep it in range, and `format` writes it with its unit ("90 days") or currency in the reader's locale.

Not for digits that name something, such as an identifier, a build number or a postcode: those are text, an [Input](?path=/docs/components-input--docs) with `inputMode="numeric"`, because a number field drops leading zeros, adds grouping separators and offers steps that mean nothing. Not for one value from a short fixed set (1, 3 or 5 reviewers): that is a [Select](?path=/docs/components-select--docs) or a [RadioGroup](?path=/docs/components-radiogroup--docs). For a value chosen along a range with a pointer, a slider may suit better; the kit has none yet.

## Content

- The label names the quantity, and the unit goes in `format`, not in the label: "Retention" with `{ style: "unit", unit: "day" }`, not "Retention (days)".
- The hint gives the range or the rule in words ("Between 30 and 365 days"), since a button that stops at a bound does not say why.
- The error says the bound or the fix: "Enter 365 days or fewer", never "Invalid number".
- An empty field is `null`, not `0`: a value nobody entered stays empty until someone does.

## Stepping

| The reader                                | What happens                                                            |
| ----------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Presses Up or Down                        | The value steps by `step` (1 by default).                               |
| Holds Shift, or Alt                       | It steps by `largeStep` (10), or `smallStep` (0.1).                     |
| Presses Home or End                       | It goes to `min` or `max`, when they are set.                           |
| Presses the decrement or increment button | It steps once; holding the button repeats.                              |
| Types                                     | The text is parsed in the locale; on blur it is formatted and clamped.  |
| Turns the wheel                           | Nothing, unless `allowWheelScrub`, and then only for the focused field. |

At a bound, the button that would pass it is unavailable. A read-only field keeps its value selectable and has no buttons. `onValueChange` runs on every change; `onValueCommitted` runs once the reader is done (on blur after typing, on releasing a button, at once for a key), which is the moment to save.

_Example: story `Stories.TypedAndFormatted`._
_Example: story `Stories.Wheel`._

## Formatting and locale

`format` takes `Intl.NumberFormat` options: a unit (`{ style: "unit", unit: "day", unitDisplay: "long" }` shows "90 days"), a currency, a percentage, fraction digits. The number is formatted and parsed in the closest `LedgerProvider`'s locale, not the browser's, so the server and the client agree; `locale` overrides it for one field. The value itself is always a plain number, or `null` when the field is empty, and a form receives the raw number under the Field's or the field's `name`.

Right to left, the buttons move to the field's end (the left), decrement nearest the number; Up still increases it.

_Example: story `Stories.Localized`._
_Example: story `Stories.RightToLeft`._
_Example: story `Stories.InAForm`._

## Sizes and states

`medium` (32px) in a form; `small` (28px) in a toolbar, a row or a rail. `className` and `style` go to the root, where the width is set, and `render` replaces the root element; the ref, `placeholder`, `autoFocus` and the `aria-*` props go to the input; `inputRef` is Base UI's hidden input that carries the value in a form.

_Example: story `Stories.States`._

## In a Field

Inside a [Field](?path=/docs/components-field--docs) the FieldLabel names the input and both buttons ("Increase Retention"), the FieldDescription and FieldError describe it, and the Field's `invalid`, `required` and `disabled` reach it, with no ids written by hand. The Field's `required` is announced; the NumberField's own `required` is the native constraint that also blocks an empty submit.

_Example: story `Stories.BoundInField`._

## Accessibility

- **A text box that says it holds a number.** The input is a textbox, so text editing works as in any field on every platform, with the role description "Number field" (the `numberField` message).
- **The buttons** are named "Decrease" and "Increase" (the `decreaseValue` and `increaseValue` messages), followed by whatever names the input: the FieldLabel inside a Field, or the `aria-labelledby` element ("Increase Retention"). A field named only by `aria-label` names them through the `decreaseValueFor` and `increaseValueFor` messages ("Increase Retention days"), so two fields side by side never have two buttons called "Increase". They are not Tab stops, because the arrow keys do the same; a touch screen reader reaches them by swiping. Each takes a 24px target under a coarse pointer, and a press with a mouse keeps focus in the input.
- **At a bound** a button is unavailable (`aria-disabled`), not only dimmed.
- **The wheel** never changes a value the reader is not working on: off by default, and with `allowWheelScrub` it steps only the focused field.

## Props

_Props of `NumberField`, generated from its types:_

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `defaultValue` | `number` |  | The uncontrolled value of the field when it's initially rendered. To render a controlled number field, use the `value` prop instead. |
| `form` | `string` |  | Identifies the form that owns the hidden input. Useful when the number field is rendered outside the form. |
| `id` | `string` |  | The id of the input element. |
| `step` | `number \| "any"` | `1` | Amount to increment and decrement with the buttons and arrow keys, or to scrub with pointer movement in the scrub area. To always enable step validation on form submission, specify the `min` prop explicitly in conjunction with this prop. Specify `step="any"` to always disable step validation; interactive stepping then uses a base amount of `1`, while the alt and shift keys still step by `smallStep` and `largeStep`. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | Whether the component should ignore user interaction. |
| `name` | `string` |  | Identifies the field when a form is submitted. |
| `value` | `number \| null` |  | The raw numeric value of the field. |
| `render` | `ReactElement<unknown, string \| JSXElementConstructor<any>> \| ComponentRenderFn<HTMLProps, NumberFieldRootState>` |  | Allows you to replace the component's HTML element with a different tag, or compose it with another component. Accepts a `ReactElement` or a function that returns the element to render. |
| `max` | `number` |  | The maximum value of the input element. |
| `min` | `number` |  | The minimum value of the input element. |
| `format` | `NumberFormatOptions` |  | Options to format the input value. |
| `onValueChange` | `((value: number \| null, eventDetails: NumberFieldRootChangeEventDetails) => void)` |  | Callback fired when the number value changes. The `eventDetails.reason` indicates what triggered the change: - `'input-change'` for parseable typing or programmatic text updates - `'input-clear'` when the field becomes empty - `'input-blur'` when formatting (and clamping, if enabled) occurs on blur - `'input-paste'` for paste interactions - `'keyboard'` for arrow-key/Home/End stepping (typing digits uses `'input-change'`/`'input-clear'`) - `'increment-press'` / `'decrement-press'` for button presses on the increment and decrement controls - `'wheel'` for wheel-based scrubbing - `'scrub'` for scrub area drags |
| `readOnly` | `boolean` | `false` | Whether the user should be unable to change the field value. |

| `allowOutOfRange` | `boolean` | `false` | When true, direct text entry may be outside the `min`/`max` range without clamping, so native range underflow/overflow validation can occur. Step-based interactions (keyboard arrows, buttons, wheel, scrub) still clamp. |
| `smallStep` | `number` | `0.1` | The small step value of the input element when incrementing while the alt key is held. Snaps to multiples of this value when `snapOnStep` is enabled. |
| `largeStep` | `number` | `10` | The large step value of the input element when incrementing while the shift key is held. Snaps to multiples of this value when `snapOnStep` is enabled. |
| `allowWheelScrub` | `boolean` | `false` | Whether to allow the user to scrub the input value with the mouse wheel while focused and hovering over the input. Whether the mouse wheel steps the value. It only ever steps the field that has focus and sits under the pointer, so scrolling a form past it never changes it. Off by default. |
| `snapOnStep` | `boolean` | `false` | Whether the value should snap to the nearest step when incrementing or decrementing. |
| `onValueCommitted` | `((value: number \| null, eventDetails: NumberFieldRootCommitEventDetails) => void)` |  | Callback function that is fired when the value is committed. It runs simultaneously with `onValueChange` when interacting with the keyboard or the mouse wheel. **Warning**: This is a generic event not a change event. |
| `placeholder` | `string` |  | An example value, never the label. |
| `aria-label` | `string` |  |  |
| `aria-labelledby` | `string` |  |  |
| `aria-describedby` | `string` |  |  |
| `aria-invalid` | `boolean \| "true" \| "false"` |  |  |
| `aria-required` | `boolean \| "true" \| "false"` |  |  |
| `autoFocus` | `boolean` |  |  |
| `size` | `"medium" \| "small"` | `medium` | Medium (32px) in a form; small (28px) in a toolbar, a row or a rail. Medium by default. |
| `locale` | `LocalesArgument` |  | The locale that formats and parses the number. Defaults to the closest LedgerProvider's locale (en-US without one), not the browser's, so the server and the client agree. |
| `ref` | `Ref<HTMLInputElement>` |  | The visible input. `inputRef` is Base UI's hidden input that carries the value in a form. |

<!-- page: Components/Overlays (src/stories/components/Overlays.mdx) -->

# Overlays

Everything that floats over the page, from the smallest label to a full task. Four are anchored to the thing that opened them and four cover the page under a blanket. The anchored and modal overlays all use Base UI. Modal overlays manage focus and page scrolling; anchored previews keep focus on their trigger. The surfaces share one recipe, `elevation.surface.overlay`, `elevation.shadow.overlay`, the large radius, the enter and exit motion, so a product's overlays read as one family.

Each part has its own page: [Tooltip](?path=/docs/components-tooltip--docs), [HoverCard](?path=/docs/components-hovercard--docs), [Popover](?path=/docs/components-popover--docs), [DropdownMenu](?path=/docs/components-dropdownmenu--docs), [Dialog](?path=/docs/components-dialog--docs), [Sheet](?path=/docs/components-sheet--docs), [Drawer](?path=/docs/components-drawer--docs), [AlertDialog](?path=/docs/components-alertdialog--docs). The patterns built on them have theirs: [PickerSheet](?path=/docs/patterns-pickersheet--docs) and [PreviewSheet](?path=/docs/patterns-previewsheet--docs) on Sheet, and [Command](?path=/docs/components-command--docs)'s CommandDialog, the [CommandPalette](?path=/docs/patterns-commandpalette--docs) and the [SearchDialog](?path=/docs/patterns-searchdialog--docs) on Dialog.

## Variants

| Need                                                             | Use              | Opens on                            | Closes on                              |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------- | ----------------------------------- | -------------------------------------- |
| A short label                                                    | **Tooltip**      | Hover after 300ms; focus at once    | Leaving, Escape                        |
| A peek at a record: a few facts, no actions                      | **HoverCard**    | Hover or focus, after 600ms         | Leaving, Escape                        |
| A small task at its button: a filter, a reason, a picker         | **Popover**      | Click                               | Escape, outside click, Done            |
| A list of actions                                                | **DropdownMenu** | Click, Enter, Space, the down arrow | Choosing, Escape, outside click        |
| A focused task over the page                                     | **Dialog**       | The caller's state                  | Escape, the blanket, Cancel, the verb  |
| A modal selection, review or explicitly scoped parent-draft task | **Sheet**        | The caller's state                  | Escape, the blanket, the footer's verb |
| The bottom sheet, for a narrow screen and a quick task           | **Drawer**       | The caller's state                  | A drag down, Escape, the blanket       |
| A decision that needs a word before it happens                   | **AlertDialog**  | The caller's state                  | Cancel, Escape, the verb               |

_Example: story `Stories.Anchored`._

_Example: story `Stories.Modal`._

## Anatomy

- **The anchored four** sit beside their trigger, 4px off it and centred on it, flipping when there is no room, with Tooltip adding a small arrow. A Tooltip is the dark one, `color.background.neutral.bold` with inverse text; the other three are the overlay surface with a hairline border. Popover, HoverCard and DropdownMenu are capped at the height the window leaves on their side and scroll within it, so a calendar or a long list never opens past the edge. Content can anchor to something other than its trigger (a cell, a chart mark, a virtual point) through `anchor`, and takes `collisionPadding`, `collisionBoundary`, `collisionAvoidance`, `sticky` and `positionMethod`.
- **Text size follows the job.** A Tooltip's label and a Popover's loose text are `font.body.small`, since they sit beside the control they explain and a Popover's own fields set their size; a HoverCard is `font.body`, since it previews the record's own words.
- **The blanketed four** paint `color.blanket` over the page; nothing else paints it. Their surface is `elevation.surface.overlay` with `radius.xxlarge` (a Sheet has square corners, since it is an edge), a header with the title a Heading at `overlay` (`font.heading.overlay`), a body part that scrolls (DialogBody, SheetBody, DrawerBody, AlertDialogBody), and a footer on the same surface, divided by a hairline, with the buttons at the end. The title is the overlay's h2; headings inside start at h3. Titles and descriptions wrap an unbroken value, such as a code or a server's error, instead of running past the edge.
- **Overlays record their surface.** The Dialog, Sheet, Drawer, AlertDialog, Popover and HoverCard popups set `utility.elevation.surface.current` to the overlay surface, so a sticky table header, a pinned cell or a scroll arrow inside paints the overlay's colour, not the page's.
- **The close** is one shared icon button at the top end, `dimension.control.small`, and first in the Tab order, where it is drawn; the first field still takes focus when the overlay opens. AlertDialog and Drawer compose explicit action buttons; a Drawer’s optional swipe handle is decorative.

## Accessibility

- **Focus moves in** when a blanketed overlay opens (Drawer focuses its popup by default; initialFocus can target an action or field) and **returns** to what opened it when it closes. A Dialog, Sheet or AlertDialog opened from state records the element that had focus as it opens, so focus comes back to it even when a field inside took focus as it mounted; `finalFocus` names another element when the opener goes away with the task. The page behind is hidden from assistive technology and does not scroll.
- **Escape closes** every overlay. An outside click closes the anchored ones and the blanket closes a Dialog, a Sheet and a Drawer; an AlertDialog ignores it. A press on a blanket that does not close its overlay (an AlertDialog's, a pending one's) leaves focus where it was.
- **Forced colours keep the edges.** A Dialog, AlertDialog, Sheet, Drawer and Tooltip draw a CanvasText outline, since forced colours replace their fill and remove their shadow, and the blanket stays a veil of Canvas; Popover and HoverCard keep their border.
- **Pending holds.** `pending` on a Dialog, Sheet or AlertDialog cancels every request to close (Escape, the blanket, Close), disables the close controls while keeping them focusable (`aria-disabled`), so focus on one is kept, and marks the popup `aria-busy` until the command returns; PickerSheet's `pending` is its Sheet's. A Drawer cancels in its own `onOpenChange`.
- **A tooltip never holds a control**, a hover card never holds an action, a popover never holds a task the reader must finish.

## Style

- **One blanket at a time.** An AlertDialog may open over a Sheet or a Dialog, for the decision the task ends in; that is the only stack. Render it inside the Dialog or Sheet that owns the decision: only the top dialog then dismisses, the page keeps its one blanket, and the Dialog or Sheet under the prompt dims under `color.blanket`, fading on the motion tokens, so its own buttons read as out of play in both modes. Independent stacked record workflows should navigate or replace the current frame. A selection workflow owns its internal preview.
- **A sheet's next record is its next frame**, not a second sheet: the same surface, a Back chevron before the title (PreviewSheet's and PickerSheet's `onBack`), the stack in the URL so the browser's back agrees.
- **Anchored overlays stack on anything.** A Tooltip in a Dialog, a DropdownMenu in a Sheet, a Popover in a Drawer are fine; a Popover in a Popover is not.

_Example: story `Stories.Stacked`._

## Props

- **Trigger composition follows each component's API**: Popover uses `PopoverTrigger render={<Button />}`; DropdownMenu uses `DropdownMenuTrigger render` and `DropdownMenuContent`; Tooltip uses `TooltipTrigger render` and `TooltipContent`. HoverCard uses `HoverCardTrigger`, an anchor by default, with `render` for a custom link. Custom trigger components must forward their props and ref.
- **The blanketed four are opened by state**: `open` and `onOpenChange`. An act sets it; the caller clears it. Nothing opens a Dialog for the reader who did not ask.
- **Where the task lives decides the overlay.** At the button: Popover. An independent focused form: Dialog. Beside a usable list: Shell.Panel. A specifically modal selection or review task: Sheet. Under the thumb: Drawer.

## Content

- The blanket is `color.blanket`; nothing else paints it.
- A blanketed overlay's title is the act's verb (a Dialog), the record's name (a Sheet), or the question (an AlertDialog). Its primary button says the verb, never OK.
- What the reader must know is on the page or in the body, never only in a tooltip or a hover card.
- An overlay is never the record. The record has a page; the overlay is the way to it or the task on it.

## Sizes

Choose the smallest surface that fits the task. Dialog and Sheet take a `width` step (`small`, `medium`, `large`, `xlarge`, `fullscreen`) rather than pixels, so tasks of the same kind open at the same size; AlertDialog takes `width` on Dialog's `xsmall`, `small` and `medium`. Drawer takes `width` (`small` 320px, `medium` 384px, `large` 760px): a side drawer within 75% of the window, a bottom or top drawer centred from `sm` up and edge to edge on a phone. Popover and HoverCard keep a runtime `style.width`. Content must reflow at a 320 CSS pixel viewport: the body part scrolls between a fixed header and footer, and in a window under 30rem tall the whole popup scrolls with the footer held in view. Check long titles, translated buttons, and browser zoom. A large task with navigation belongs on a page.

## States

Closed, open, pending, failed and completed are separate states. Keep the surface and draft open on failure and explain how to retry. A pending operation must settle or expose a recovery path. Close only after a successful command or an explicit cancel.

## Modifiers

Modal content takes Base UI's `initialFocus` and `finalFocus`. Base UI returns focus to the element that had it before the surface opened; pass `finalFocus` when that element goes away with the task, and move focus to a first field with `initialFocus`, never with `autoFocus`, which becomes the return target instead. `pending` on Dialog, Sheet and AlertDialog prevents dismissal while a command is in flight.

## Related

See Forms for validation and focus on error, Button for activation semantics, and Toaster for nonblocking completion feedback. Each overlay's page documents its exact dismissal contract.

## Don't

Do not rely on a toast as the only record of a failure, hide required instructions in a tooltip, nest independent modal tasks, or remove the opener without specifying a meaningful focus destination. Do not make a hover-only surface the sole route to an action.

<!-- page: Components/Pagination (src/stories/components/Pagination.mdx) -->

# Pagination

**Status: Stable.**

Navigation between pages using [shadcn’s flat Pagination parts](https://ui.shadcn.com/docs/components/base/pagination). The caller owns page state, URLs and result counts.

## When to use it

- **Pages whose address names them**: a feed or a list whose page is in its URL (`?page=2`), composed from these parts with PaginationLink.
- **Pages of a table that pages in memory**: TablePagination, which a [DataTable](?path=/docs/patterns-data-table--docs) draws itself whenever it pages.

Not for the steps of a task: that is a [Stepper](?path=/docs/components-stepper--docs). Not for moving from one record to the next in a preview: that is [PreviewNavigation](?path=/docs/patterns-previewnavigation--docs). Not for a long list the reader scrolls through: a DataTable with `virtualize` draws only the rows in view.

## Content

- Name each region for what it pages ("Control pages", "Evidence pages"). Unnamed, it is "Pagination", and two on one page cannot be told apart.
- A page is its number. Previous and Next keep their words, or `text` says the order the list reads in ("Newer", "Older").
- The current page is `isActive`, never only bold text: it is said as the current page and drawn as one.
- TablePagination's range says the rows shown and the total ("9–16 of 23").

_Example: story `Stories.DoDont`._

## Anatomy

```tsx
<Pagination aria-label="Control pages">
  <PaginationContent>
    <PaginationItem>
      <PaginationPrevious href="?page=1" />
    </PaginationItem>
    <PaginationItem>
      <PaginationLink href="?page=2" isActive>
        2
      </PaginationLink>
    </PaginationItem>
    <PaginationItem>
      <PaginationEllipsis />
    </PaginationItem>
    <PaginationItem>
      <PaginationNext href="?page=3" />
    </PaginationItem>
  </PaginationContent>
</Pagination>
```

Root is a nav, Content a list and Item a list item. Link uses a real anchor with the shared Button recipe. Base UI 1.7 Button adds button semantics even when rendered as an anchor, so Ledger preserves native link semantics here. Previous and Next are links with localized names, optional `text` and direction-aware icons. Ellipsis stands for the pages skipped between two links and says "More pages" to a screen reader.

_Example: story `Stories.Links`._

## Variants and states

`isActive` sets `aria-current="page"`. The current page is marked from that state by its PaginationItem, whether it holds a link or a button: a semibold figure in the default text colour over a 2px bar in the selected colour, which holds 3:1 on every surface in both modes. Every page, the current one included, is otherwise the subtle appearance, and in forced colours the current page is Highlight. All links accept native anchor attributes, events and refs, including href, target and rel.

Previous and Next carry their words where the pagination has 384px (`dimension.container.sm`) of its own width and are arrows below it, named for a screen reader either way. The region measures itself, not the window, so the same pagination has words on a page and arrows in a 320px panel on the same screen. A pagination holding Previous or Next is a size container, so its width comes from where it sits, not from its links. It spans its container by default. At the end of a row, give it the rest of the row with `min-w-0 flex-1 justify-end`: its words show where that leaves 384px, and a narrower row shrinks it to arrows. Sized to its content instead (`w-auto`, an `auto` grid column), a pagination with words is 384px whatever its links need, so a longer list wraps inside it. Previous and Next read that width from their `Pagination` root; outside one they show arrows only. The list wraps rather than running past a narrow frame, and every link is at least 28px.

_Example: story `Stories.InANarrowPanel`._
_Example: story `Stories.AtTheEndOfARow`._

## TablePagination

`TablePagination` is the pager under a table that pages in memory, built from these parts: the row range ("9–16 of 23", "0 rows"), then Rows per page when `pageSizes` offers more than one size, then the pages at the end. Each page is a subtle small Button with `aria-current="page"` on the current one; the first, the last, the current page and its neighbours show, with an ellipsis where pages are skipped. The arrows take `disabled` with `focusableWhenDisabled` at the first and last page, so they stay in the tab order with `aria-disabled` and a reader who presses Next to the end keeps focus on it instead of falling to the page. The caller owns `page`, `pageSize` and `total`, and says a new page back through `onPageChange`; the pager says nothing itself, so a caller that pages without DataTable says the new range in its own status. DataTable draws one whenever it pages and says the range after every page. A pager of URLs composes the parts above with PaginationLink instead.

_Example: story `Stories.InMemoryTable`._
_Example: story `Stories.ManyPages`._

`text` replaces the word on Previous or Next, for a feed read newest first ("Newer", "Older"), and names the link as well, so what a reader sees is what a speech user says.

_Example: story `Stories.OwnWords`._

## Accessibility

Name each navigation region distinctly; unnamed, it is "Pagination". Use links for URLs and buttons for local state changes. An unavailable link needs caller-owned semantics and activation handling; anchors have no native disabled attribute. Prefer omitting unavailable navigation links, or, in an in-memory pager, a Button that is `disabled` with `focusableWhenDisabled`. The current page is `aria-current="page"`, never `aria-pressed`. Previous and Next are named "Previous page" and "Next page", or by their `text`. RTL arrows follow the enclosing direction.

## Props

Pagination owns no page state: it takes native `aria-label` and explicit children. DataTable has the page-size and table-state API and composes these parts for its result counts and page controls. Every part takes its element's native props and a ref, and keeps its own `data-slot` after them.

_Example: story `Stories.NativeAttributes`._

_Props: generated from `Pagination`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._

_Props of `PaginationLink`, generated from its types:_

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `size` | `"medium" \| "small" \| "xsmall"` | `small` | Medium is 32px, small 28px and xsmall 24px. `variant="link"` ignores it: a link-styled action is as tall as its text. |
| `isActive` | `boolean` |  |  |

_Props of `PaginationPrevious`, generated from its types:_

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `size` | `"medium" \| "small" \| "xsmall"` |  | Medium is 32px, small 28px and xsmall 24px. `variant="link"` ignores it: a link-styled action is as tall as its text. |
| `isActive` | `boolean` |  |  |
| `text` | `string` |  | The visible word in place of "Previous", such as "Older". It also names the link. |

_Props of `PaginationNext`, generated from its types:_

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `size` | `"medium" \| "small" \| "xsmall"` |  | Medium is 32px, small 28px and xsmall 24px. `variant="link"` ignores it: a link-styled action is as tall as its text. |
| `isActive` | `boolean` |  |  |
| `text` | `string` |  | The visible word in place of "Next", such as "Newer". It also names the link. |

_Props of `TablePagination`, generated from its types:_

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `page` (required) | `number` |  | The page shown, from 1. |
| `pageCount` (required) | `number` |  | How many pages there are; at least 1. |
| `onPageChange` (required) | `(page: number) => void` |  | Called with the page the reader asks for. The caller owns the page and says it back through `page`. |
| `total` | `number` |  | Every row across the pages. With `pageSize` it draws the range: "21–40 of 1,391", or "No rows". |
| `pageSize` | `number` |  | Rows per page: the range reads it, and so does Rows per page. |
| `pageSizes` | `number[]` |  | The sizes the reader can choose from; the choice shows when there is more than one and `onPageSizeChange` is given. |
| `onPageSizeChange` | `((size: number) => void)` |  | Called with the size the reader chooses under Rows per page. |
| `label` | `string` |  | The navigation's name, after the table: "Findings pagination". "Pagination" unsaid. |

## Related

[DataTable](?path=/docs/patterns-data-table--docs), [Table](?path=/docs/components-table--docs), [Button](?path=/docs/components-button--docs).

<!-- page: Components/Popover (src/stories/components/Popover.mdx) -->

# Popover

**Status: Stable.**

An anchored dialog for controls, forms and supporting content. It follows shadcn's Base UI composition, with Ledger's surface, spacing and motion tokens.

```tsx
<Popover>
  <PopoverTrigger render={<Button />}>Review schedule</PopoverTrigger>
  <PopoverContent>
    <PopoverHeader>
      <PopoverTitle>Review schedule</PopoverTitle>
      <PopoverDescription>Reviews occur every quarter.</PopoverDescription>
    </PopoverHeader>
    <PopoverClose render={<Button />}>Done</PopoverClose>
  </PopoverContent>
</Popover>
```

## When to use it

- **A small task at its button**, finished in place: a filter's values, a reason for a change, a date, the settings of one view.
- **Controls that act on what sits beside them**, applied as they change or with one button that says what it does.

Not for a label or a shortcut: that is a [Tooltip](?path=/docs/components-tooltip--docs). Not for a preview of a link's destination: that is a [HoverCard](?path=/docs/components-hovercard--docs). Not for a list of actions: that is a [DropdownMenu](?path=/docs/components-dropdownmenu--docs). Not for a create or edit form, or a task with several fields: that is a [Dialog](?path=/docs/components-dialog--docs). Never a popover inside a popover. [Overlays](?path=/docs/components-overlays--docs) compares them all.

A create form of several fields belongs in a Dialog, never in a popover that a press outside closes.

_Example: story `Stories.DoDont`._

## Content

- A title, where there is one, names the task or the setting ("Review schedule", "Owner"), and the trigger says the same words or shows the current value.
- A button says what it does ("Apply filter", "Clear owner"). A popover whose changes apply as they are made ends with Done, never Save or OK.
- One short task, whose button the reader sees without scrolling the popover in a window of ordinary height.

## Composition

Root owns open state. Trigger and Close render native buttons by default; use `render` to compose Button, IconButton or FilterChip. Trigger's `nativeButton={false}` supports a custom element with button semantics. Custom components must forward their props and ref.

Content includes the portal and positioner. Native props, `ref`, `render`, and state callbacks for `className` or `style` apply to the popup. Title and Description connect their content to the dialog's accessible name and description; Header supplies their layout. When no visible title fits, give Content an `aria-label`.

Content paints the overlay surface and records it as the current one, so a child painted with `bg-surface-current` (a sticky list label, a pinned cell) matches the popover rather than the page. Its loose text is `font.body.small`; its fields set their own size. It defaults to 288px wide (`dimension.part.popover`), `side="bottom"`, `sideOffset={4}`, `align="center"` and `alignOffset={0}`. Override width with `style={{ width: 300 }}` or match the trigger with `style={{ width: "var(--anchor-width)" }}`. It is capped at the height the window leaves on its side (`var(--available-height)`) and scrolls within it, so a calendar or a long list of filters never opens past the window's edge; do not add a cap of your own. The positioner handles collisions. Logical sides and alignment follow the Ledger locale; Content's `dir` can override it.

_Example: story `Stories.ShortWindow`._

## Anchoring

Content can sit against something other than its trigger: `anchor` takes an element, a ref or a virtual point, such as a chart mark or a table cell, and `collisionPadding`, `collisionBoundary`, `collisionAvoidance`, `sticky` and `positionMethod` pass to the positioner. A popover opened from state with an `anchor` needs no trigger; focus returns to what had it.

_Example: story `Stories.Anchored`._

_Example: story `Stories.PopoverMatrix`._

## Focus and dismissal

Click, Enter or Space activates the trigger. Focus moves to the first tabbable control, or the popup if it has none. Touch opening focuses the popup to avoid opening a virtual keyboard. Content's `initialFocus` and `finalFocus` support explicit focus destinations.

The default `modal={false}` leaves the page reachable. Tab moves through controls and can leave the popup, dismissing it. Escape and Close dismiss it and return focus to the trigger; an outside press dismisses it while allowing the clicked control to receive focus.

For focus trapping, use Root's `modal="trap-focus"` and include `PopoverClose` inside Content. `modal={true}` additionally restricts outside interaction; see the upstream API for its scrolling behavior. Base UI 1.7 requires the Close part inside the popup to enable its focus trap.

Inside an existing Dialog, Sheet or Drawer, the popup stays within that surface's focus scope. Escape closes the popup first and returns focus to its trigger; a subsequent Escape can dismiss the enclosing surface.

_Example: story `Stories.Options`._

## Controlled tasks

Use `defaultOpen` for local initial state, or `open` and `onOpenChange(open, details)` for caller-owned state. `details.cancel()` rejects an open-state change. Keep form drafts in caller state when they should survive dismissal, and close after the task succeeds.

_Example: story `Stories.Task`._

## Props

The flat parts retain their upstream props: [Root](https://base-ui.com/react/components/popover#root), [Trigger](https://base-ui.com/react/components/popover#trigger), [Popup](https://base-ui.com/react/components/popover#popup), [Title](https://base-ui.com/react/components/popover#title), [Description](https://base-ui.com/react/components/popover#description), and [Close](https://base-ui.com/react/components/popover#close). Content additionally takes the positioner's props above; Header accepts native div props. See [shadcn's composition examples](https://ui.shadcn.com/docs/components/base/popover).

_Props of `PopoverContent`, generated from its types:_

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `initialFocus` | `boolean \| RefObject<HTMLElement \| null> \| ((openType: InteractionType) => boolean \| void \| HTMLElement \| null)` |  | Determines the element to focus when the popover is opened. By default, focus moves to the first tabbable element inside the popup, except when the popover is opened by touch — then the popup itself is focused to avoid opening the virtual keyboard. - `false`: Do not move focus. - `true`: Move focus based on the default behavior (first tabbable element or popup). - `RefObject`: Move focus to the ref element. - `function`: Called with the interaction type (`mouse`, `touch`, `pen`, or `keyboard`). Return an element to focus, `true` to use the default behavior, `null` to fall back to the default behavior, or `false`/`undefined` to do nothing. |
| `finalFocus` | `boolean \| RefObject<HTMLElement \| null> \| ((closeType: InteractionType) => boolean \| void \| HTMLElement \| null)` |  | Determines the element to focus when the popover is closed. - `false`: Do not move focus. - `true`: Move focus based on the default behavior (trigger or previously focused element). - `RefObject`: Move focus to the ref element. - `function`: Called with the interaction type (`mouse`, `touch`, `pen`, or `keyboard`). Return an element to focus, `true` to use the default behavior, `null` to fall back to the default behavior, or `false`/`undefined` to do nothing. |
| `className` | `string \| ((state: PopoverPopupState) => string)` |  | CSS class applied to the element, or a function that returns a class based on the component's state. |
| `render` | `ReactElement<unknown, string \| JSXElementConstructor<any>> \| ComponentRenderFn<HTMLProps, PopoverPopupState>` |  | Allows you to replace the component's HTML element with a different tag, or compose it with another component. Accepts a `ReactElement` or a function that returns the element to render. |
| `style` | `CSSProperties \| ((state: PopoverPopupState) => CSSProperties)` |  | Style applied to the element, or a function that returns a style object based on the component's state. |
| `sticky` | `boolean` | `false` | Whether to maintain the popup in the viewport after the anchor element was scrolled out of view. |
| `side` | `"bottom" \| "inline-end" \| "inline-start" \| "left" \| "right" \| "top"` | `bottom` | Which side of the anchor element to align the popup against. May automatically change to avoid collisions. |
| `align` | `"center" \| "end" \| "start"` | `start` | How to align the popup relative to the specified side. |
| `sideOffset` | `number \| OffsetFunction` | `4` | Distance between the anchor and the popup in pixels. Also accepts a function that returns the distance to read the dimensions of the anchor and positioner elements, along with its side and alignment. The function takes a `data` object parameter with the following properties: - `data.anchor`: the dimensions of the anchor element with properties `width` and `height`. - `data.positioner`: the dimensions of the positioner element with properties `width` and `height`. - `data.side`: which side of the anchor element the positioner is aligned against. - `data.align`: how the positioner is aligned relative to the specified side. @example ```jsx <Positioner sideOffset={({ side, align, anchor, positioner }) => { return side === 'top' \|\| side === 'bottom' ? anchor.height : anchor.width; }} /> ``` |
| `alignOffset` | `number \| OffsetFunction` | `0` | Additional offset along the alignment axis in pixels. Also accepts a function that returns the offset to read the dimensions of the anchor and positioner elements, along with its side and alignment. The function takes a `data` object parameter with the following properties: - `data.anchor`: the dimensions of the anchor element with properties `width` and `height`. - `data.positioner`: the dimensions of the positioner element with properties `width` and `height`. - `data.side`: which side of the anchor element the positioner is aligned against. - `data.align`: how the positioner is aligned relative to the specified side. @example ```jsx <Positioner alignOffset={({ side, align, anchor, positioner }) => { return side === 'top' \|\| side === 'bottom' ? anchor.width : anchor.height; }} /> ``` |
| `anchor` | `Element \| VirtualElement \| RefObject<Element \| null> \| (() => Element \| VirtualElement \| null) \| null` |  | An element to position the popup against. By default, the popup will be positioned against the trigger. |
| `collisionAvoidance` | `CollisionAvoidance` |  | Determines how to handle collisions when positioning the popup. `side` controls overflow on the preferred placement axis (`top`/`bottom` or `left`/`right`): - `'flip'`: keep the requested side when it fits; otherwise try the opposite side (`top` and `bottom`, or `left` and `right`). - `'shift'`: never change side; keep the requested side and move the popup within the clipping boundary so it stays visible. - `'none'`: do not correct side-axis overflow. `align` controls overflow on the alignment axis (`start`/`center`/`end`): - `'flip'`: keep side, but swap `start` and `end` when the requested alignment overflows. - `'shift'`: keep side and requested alignment, then nudge the popup along the alignment axis to fit. - `'none'`: do not correct alignment-axis overflow. `fallbackAxisSide` controls fallback behavior on the perpendicular axis when the preferred axis cannot fit: - `'start'`: allow perpendicular fallback and try the logical start side first (`top` before `bottom`, or `left` before `right` in LTR). - `'end'`: allow perpendicular fallback and try the logical end side first (`bottom` before `top`, or `right` before `left` in LTR). - `'none'`: do not fallback to the perpendicular axis. When `side` is `'shift'`, explicitly setting `align` only supports `'shift'` or `'none'`. If `align` is omitted, it defaults to `'flip'`. @example ```jsx <Positioner collisionAvoidance={{ side: 'shift', align: 'shift', fallbackAxisSide: 'none', }} /> ``` |
| `collisionBoundary` | `Boundary` | `'clipping-ancestors'` | An element or a rectangle that delimits the area that the popup is confined to. |
| `collisionPadding` | `Padding` | `5` | Additional space to maintain from the edge of the collision boundary. |
| `positionMethod` | `"absolute" \| "fixed"` | `'absolute'` | Determines which CSS `position` property to use. |

<!-- page: Components/Progress (src/stories/components/Progress.mdx) -->

# Progress

**Status: Stable.**

How far a task has gone, as a bar: an upload, an import, a package build. `Progress` is a progressbar on Base UI's Progress, with Ledger's tones and sizes. `ProgressStacked` is the other bar: a share of a whole, such as control coverage, drawn as segments.

_Example: story `Stories.ValuesAndRanges`._

## Choosing between them

| What the reader is watching                                  | Part                                                                                                  |
| ------------------------------------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| A task that finishes, with a known amount done               | `Progress` with `value`                                                                               |
| A task that finishes, of unknown length, in a region         | `Progress` with `value={null}`: a hatched bar                                                         |
| A short wait for an action, beside its control               | [Spinner](?path=/docs/components-spinner--docs), or the Button's own `isLoading`                      |
| Content on its way, whose shape is known                     | [Skeleton](?path=/docs/components-skeleton--docs)                                                     |
| A share of a whole: coverage, controls by state, a breakdown | `ProgressStacked`, or the number in words                                                             |
| A measure against a target that does not finish (a score)    | A number in words, or a [Chart](?path=/docs/patterns-chart-overview--docs) gauge; never a progressbar |

A progressbar says a task is under way and will end. A quantity that is not a task's completion is not one: a screen reader would hear "73 percent" of a job that is not running.

## Anatomy

```tsx
<Progress value={41} max={80} tone="success">
  <ProgressLabel>Controls verified</ProgressLabel>
  <ProgressValue>{(_, value) => `${value} of 80`}</ProgressValue>
</Progress>
```

| Part                | What it is                                                                                                                                     |
| ------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Progress`          | The progressbar: Base UI's root, a row that wraps, with its own track and indicator after the children.                                        |
| `ProgressLabel`     | The visible name, in small medium text. It names the bar.                                                                                      |
| `ProgressValue`     | The value after the label, at the row's end, in small subtle tabular figures: the formatted percentage, or what its children function returns. |
| `ProgressTrack`     | The track, `color.background.neutral`, rounded, at the size's height. For a custom composition under Base UI's root.                           |
| `ProgressIndicator` | The fill, in the tone's bar colour; the hatched bar while the value is unknown. For a custom composition.                                      |
| `ProgressStacked`   | The segmented bar: each segment its share of the total, solid or hatched, optionally a button that filters what is under it.                   |

_Example: story `Stories.LabelAndValue`._

## Variants and sizes

`tone` is the Ledger meaning: `information` by default, `success` for a task that is going well, `warning` or `danger` for one at risk, `neutral` for one that carries no judgement. Each fill holds 3:1 against its track on every surface, `elevation.surface.sunken` included, in both modes. A warning bar, filled or waiting, is `color.chart.warning.bold`, a step darker than a chart's warning series in light, because `color.background.warning.bold` is a light orange made to carry dark text and the series orange is under 3:1 on the track over the sunken surface. `size` is `small` (4px, in a cell or beside a name), `medium` (6px, the default, in a row) or `large` (8px, a band).

_Example: story `Stories.Tones`._

## States

- **Determinate**: `value` between `min` and `max` (0 and 100 unless set). Base UI clamps a value past either end, and the bar's width and its accessible value follow.
- **Unknown length**: `value={null}` is a wait. The bar is hatched the width of the track, in the tone's icon colour (a warning bar's in its fill's orange), and its stripes move one tile every `motion.duration.slower`; under reduced motion they stand still and the bar stays hatched. It never looks like a finished bar.
- **Done**: remove the bar, or replace it with what the task made. A full bar left on the page reads as a task still running.

## Content

- **Name what is progressing**, with `ProgressLabel` or `aria-label`: "Uploading evidence", "Importing the catalogue". Not "Progress", not "Loading".
- **Show the value when the reader needs it**, as a count where a count means more than a percentage ("41 of 80").
- **One bar per task.** Several uploads are several bars, each named for its file.

## Stacked

`ProgressStacked` draws each segment as its share of the total; a zero segment is skipped. A `hatched` segment is what is not known or not covered, a hole in the record rather than a colour. With `label`, the bar is an image named by the label and its segments' titles; when segments have `onClick`, it is a group of buttons named by the label, each segment's button named by its title, and a segment that does not click is read as its title, so no part of the breakdown is lost. Without `label` it is decorative and the numbers beside it carry the values.

_Example: story `Stories.StackedCoverage`._

## Accessibility

- **Progress is a progressbar** with `aria-valuenow`, `aria-valuemin` and `aria-valuemax`, and `aria-valuetext` from Base UI's formatting in the provider's locale. While the value is unknown it has no `aria-valuenow`, and its value text is the locale's "In progress". `getAriaValueText` replaces either.
- **A clickable segment is a button** in the tab order. The bar does not clip its segments, so a focused segment's ring shows whole around it, in Highlight under forced colours. On a touch screen its hit area is 24px tall across the segment's own width, so neighbours never overlap.
- **Reduced motion** stops the stripes and the width transition; the hatching and the value stay.
- **Forced colours** keep the track's boundary and the fill, the segments and the hatching in system colours.

<!-- page: Components/RadioGroup (src/stories/components/RadioGroup.mdx) -->

# RadioGroup

**Status: Stable.**

One answer from a set of visible choices, on the shadcn Base UI composition. `RadioGroupItem` draws the circle and its dot; the question and the options' labels come from a Field around a FieldSet, which ties them together with no ids and aligns each circle with its label's first line.

```tsx
<Field invalid={invalid} required>
  <FieldSet>
    <FieldLegend variant="label">Review frequency</FieldLegend>
    <RadioGroup value={frequency} onValueChange={setFrequency}>
      <Field orientation="horizontal">
        <RadioGroupItem value="monthly" />
        <FieldLabel>Monthly</FieldLabel>
      </Field>
      <Field orientation="horizontal">
        <RadioGroupItem value="quarterly" />
        <FieldLabel>Quarterly</FieldLabel>
      </Field>
    </RadioGroup>
    <FieldError errors={errors} />
  </FieldSet>
</Field>
```

_Example: story `Stories.RadioGroupMatrix`._

## When to use it

- **Use a RadioGroup** for one answer from two to about seven options the reader should see side by side: a frequency, an impact level, a decision such as Accept or Not applicable.
- **Not two checkboxes that untick each other.** An either/or decision is a RadioGroup, so it is announced as one question and the arrow keys move between its answers.
- **More options, or plain words**, belong in a [Select](?path=/docs/components-select--docs); a long or searchable list in a [Combobox](?path=/docs/components-combobox--docs).
- **Not for a fact.** An answer the reader cannot change is a labelled property, or a read-only group with a hint that says why.

The [Forms](?path=/docs/patterns-forms--docs) page has the table of which control answers which question.

Two checkboxes that untick each other are heard as two separate choices, with no question and no arrow keys.

_Example: story `Stories.DoDont`._

## Selection and layout

Use `defaultValue` for local state, or `value` and `onValueChange(value, details)` for controlled state. A controlled group with no answer yet passes a value no item has, such as `""`, never `undefined`: `undefined` leaves the group uncontrolled on its first render, and Base UI keeps that mode. Selecting an item clears the previous selection; selecting it again keeps it selected. `details.cancel()` rejects a change. `disabled` blocks interaction; `readOnly` allows focus while keeping the selected value unchanged. Both props can apply to the group or an individual item.

_Example: story `Stories.ControlledWithNoAnswer`._

The indicator is a 16px circle with an 8px dot. The selected circle uses Ledger's brand fill and a contrasting dot. The group defaults to a grid with an 8px gap. Use classes such as `flex flex-row flex-wrap gap-200` for a horizontal layout; there is no `orientation` prop.

Tab enters and leaves the group as one stop. All four arrow keys move focus and select, skipping disabled items and wrapping at the ends. Horizontal arrows follow the Ledger locale direction, which `dir` on the group can override. Space selects the focused item; Enter does not select it. Home/End and configurable focus wrapping are not part of the installed API.

_Example: story `Stories.Orientation`._

## Read-only

A read-only group keeps its answer and its Tab stop but not the brand fill or the hover: each circle is sunken with a dashed edge, and the chosen one keeps a dark dot. Put the reason in the group's FieldDescription ("Set by the system categorization."), which describes the group.

_Example: story `Stories.ReadOnly`._

## Choice cards

When each option needs a title and a line of explanation, wrap each option's horizontal Field in a FieldLabel: a press anywhere on the card chooses it, and the card shows hover, the chosen state and the one keyboard focus ring. The FieldTitle names the radio and the FieldDescription describes it once. See [Checkbox](?path=/docs/components-checkbox--docs#choice-cards) for the same card around a checkbox, and for a card with the facts that tell options apart, a link to the option's record beside it, and an error that belongs to one option: the radio card takes them the same way. An error about the choice as a whole (nothing chosen) is the group Field's FieldError.

_Example: story `Stories.ChoiceCard`._

## Labels, Field and forms

The short path is a Field around a FieldSet: the FieldLegend names the group, the Field's hint and error describe it, and its `invalid` and `required` reach the group once. Each item is a horizontal Field with a FieldLabel, so it keeps its own name and needs no id. Invalid is the item's danger border, set once on the group; a focused item keeps the focus outline.

_Example: story `Stories.BoundInField`._

Outside a Field, name the group with `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`; inside a FieldSet the legend names it. A wrapping label or a sibling label with `htmlFor` names each item and selects it when clicked, and `aria-describedby` links supporting text. `aria-invalid` on the group marks every item. Native `required` on RadioGroup makes its hidden radio inputs take part in browser and Base UI validation; the Field's `required` only announces and marks. A FieldSet's `disabled` disables the items.

`name` and `form` associate the hidden inputs with native submission. The selected item's value is submitted. Native form reset is caller-owned in Base UI 1.7: restore controlled `value` in the form's `onReset` handler.

_Example: story `Stories.InField`._

## Content

- **The legend asks the question; each label is one answer.** "Review frequency", then "Monthly", "Quarterly".
- **Keep each answer's name stable**, and put what it means in its hint, not in a name that changes.
- **Do not disable an option to show a fact**; say in the hint why an answer is not available.

## Accessibility

- Each radio's boundary is `color.border.bold`, 3:1 against every surface, so an unchosen option can be found (WCAG 1.4.11).
- In forced colours, the selected radio keeps a contrasting system-colour dot and a visible boundary.

_Example: story `Stories.Boundary`._

## Native props and composition

The group renders a div with `role="radiogroup"`. Each item renders a span with `role="radio"` and `aria-checked`, plus a hidden input. Item `ref` targets the visible control; `inputRef` and `id` target its hidden input. Group `inputRef` follows the selected input, or an enabled input when none is selected.

`render` composes a custom element and merges props, classes, styles and refs. An item rendered as a button uses `nativeButton` with `render={<button />}`; its `id` then targets the visible button. `className` and `style` accept Base UI state callbacks.

## Props

_Props of `RadioGroup`, generated from its types:_

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | Whether the component should ignore user interaction. |
| `readOnly` | `boolean` | `false` | Whether the user should be unable to select a different radio button in the group. |
