<!-- page: Components/Resizable (src/stories/components/Resizable.mdx) -->

# Resizable

**Status: Stable.**

User-sized panes following [shadcn’s Resizable source](https://ui.shadcn.com/docs/components/base/resizable), built on react-resizable-panels. A plain dividing rule is a Separator; the application shell's side nav and panel have their own splitters.

## When to use it

- **Two or three panes whose share the reader decides**: a list beside its detail, a tree beside the record it opens, a source beside its preview.

Not for a fixed line between content: that is a [Separator](?path=/docs/components-separator--docs). Not for the application's side nav or panel: [Shell](?path=/docs/layout-shell--docs) has its own splitters. Not side by side in a narrow container, a phone or a narrow panel: stack the panes with `orientation="vertical"`, or show one at a time (Narrow containers).

## Content

- Name each handle for what it resizes: `aria-label="Resize the list"`. The default, "Resize", tells several splits apart by nothing.
- A button that folds a pane says what it will do next: "Hide the tree", then "Show the tree" (Without dragging).

## Anatomy

```tsx
import { ResizableHandle, ResizablePanel, ResizablePanelGroup } from "@ledger/design-system";

<ResizablePanelGroup>
  <ResizablePanel defaultSize="30%" minSize="20%">
    List
  </ResizablePanel>
  <ResizableHandle aria-label="Resize the list" withHandle />
  <ResizablePanel>Detail</ResizablePanel>
</ResizablePanelGroup>;
```

Give the group a sized parent. Panels clip their contents; put ScrollArea inside a scrolling pane. `withHandle` adds a visible grip.

_Example: story `Stories.Panes`._

Sizes are strings for percentages (`"30%"`) and numbers for pixels. A share of the split is written `defaultSize="30%"`, never `defaultSize={30}`, which opens a pane 30 pixels wide.

_Example: story `Stories.DoDont`._

## Variants and states

`orientation="vertical"` stacks panes. Native panel props include minimum and maximum sizes, collapse behavior and resize callbacks. The library owns layout, pointer resizing and keyboard behavior.

_Example: story `Stories.Vertical`._
_Example: story `Stories.Collapsible`._

## Without dragging

A split that only a drag can change fails a reader who cannot drag (WCAG 2.5.7). The keyboard has the arrows, Home, End and Enter. Give a pointer a way that needs no drag as well: a button that folds and unfolds the pane through its `panelRef`'s `collapse()` and `expand()`, or buttons for the sizes the task needs. Every product split needs one.

_Example: story `Stories.WithoutDragging`._

## Persisting and driving a split

Persist a layout with `useResizableLayout` (the upstream `useDefaultLayout`) from the package root: give the group a stable `id` and the panels stable `id`s, and pass the hook's `defaultLayout` and `onLayoutChanged` to the group. Keep an existing id to read its saved layout. Supply server-safe `storage` when the hook renders on the server; the story does. Drive a split with the group's `groupRef` (`ResizablePanelGroupHandle`) and a panel's `panelRef` (`ResizablePanelHandle`); `ResizableLayout` and `ResizableLayoutStorage` type what the hook saves. Nothing is imported from react-resizable-panels directly.

_Example: story `Stories.Persisted`._

## Narrow containers

Panels keep their minimum sizes, so a group needs the width of its minimums; below that it overflows its parent. In a narrow container (a phone, a narrow panel) do not split side by side: stack the panes with `orientation="vertical"`, or show one pane at a time and let the reader move between them. Sizes in percentages follow the container; pixel minimums do not.

## Right to left

In a right-to-left page the first panel is drawn on the right, and the arrow keys move the handle the way they point: ArrowLeft moves it left. Set the direction before the group mounts; a group whose direction changes while mounted keeps the order it measured, so give it a `key` that changes with the direction.

_Example: story `Stories.RightToLeft`._

## Accessibility

The handle is a focusable separator with the orientation of the rule: a side-by-side group has a vertical separator. Arrow keys resize, Home and End reach the bounds, Enter toggles a collapsible panel and F6 moves between handles. Name each handle with `aria-label` ("Resize the list"), especially when several splits are present; the default is "Resize". On a touch screen the handle takes a 24px hit area. Group and Panel expose native `elementRef`, `groupRef` and `panelRef` instead of translating them into a generic ref.

## Props

_Props: generated from `ResizablePanelGroup`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._
_Props: generated from `ResizablePanel`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._

_Props of `ResizableHandle`, generated from its types:_

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `withHandle` | `boolean` |  |  |

## Related

[Shell.Panel](?path=/docs/layout-shell--docs), [ScrollArea](?path=/docs/components-scrollarea--docs), [Separator](?path=/docs/components-separator--docs).

<!-- page: Components/ScrollArea (src/stories/components/ScrollArea.mdx) -->

# ScrollArea

**Status: Stable.**

A bounded region that scrolls with the kit's own bar, which the reader can see and drag, on [Base UI ScrollArea](https://base-ui.com/react/components/scroll-area) in shadcn's ScrollArea and ScrollBar composition.

## When to use it

Use it where the bar itself is the cue: a list in a resizable pane, a wide timeline in a card. A region with nothing to add scrolls with native overflow; a list or a strip that needs an arrow at each edge that can still scroll is a [Scroller](?path=/docs/components-scroller--docs). An overlay's scrolling content is its Body part (DialogBody, SheetBody), never a ScrollArea. [Choosing a part](?path=/docs/guidance-choosing-a-part--docs) has the whole table.

## Content

- Name a region that holds the reader's content with `viewportProps` (`role="region"` and an `aria-label` that says what it holds: "Activity", "Control text"), since a keyboard reader tabs into it to scroll.
- Give the region a height or a maximum its content can outgrow; a ScrollArea that never overflows draws no bar and adds nothing.

An unnamed region is a tab stop announced as nothing: name it through `viewportProps`.

_Example: story `Stories.DoDont`._

## Anatomy

`ScrollArea` renders the root, the viewport that scrolls, a vertical `ScrollBar` and the corner. Add `<ScrollBar orientation="horizontal" />` as a child for a region that scrolls sideways; overflow decides which bars show. Put sizing classes (a height, a maximum width, a border and radius) on `ScrollArea`.

_Example: story `Stories.Vertical`._

_Example: story `Stories.HorizontalAndRTL`._

## Accessibility

- **Keyboard.** The viewport is a tab stop while it overflows, so the arrow keys, Page Up and Page Down scroll it; a region that fits adds no stop. Base UI manages the bar's geometry and dragging.
- **A name.** Name the region through `viewportProps`, with `role="region"` and an `aria-label` that says what scrolls ("Evidence list").
- **Focus.** The root clips, so the viewport's focus ring is drawn inside it, following the root's corners.
- **Direction** follows LedgerProvider or an explicit `dir`, for the layout and the bar alike.
- **Forced colours.** The thumb is drawn in `CanvasText`, and `Highlight` under the pointer, so it stays visible when the system replaces the tokens.

## Props

`viewportProps` takes the viewport's native attributes and its ref: the element that actually scrolls, for a name, a role or a virtualizer. The root takes Base UI's ScrollArea props, including `render` and state-based `className` and `style`. ScrollBar takes `orientation` and `keepMounted`.

_Props of `ScrollArea`, generated from its types:_

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `overflowEdgeThreshold` | `number \| Partial<{ xStart: number; xEnd: number; yStart: number; yEnd: number; }>` | `0` | The threshold in pixels that must be passed before the overflow edge attributes are applied. Accepts a single number for all edges or an object to configure them individually. |
| `className` | `string \| ((state: ScrollAreaRootState) => string)` |  | CSS class applied to the element, or a function that returns a class based on the component's state. |
| `render` | `ReactElement<unknown, string \| JSXElementConstructor<any>> \| ComponentRenderFn<HTMLProps, ScrollAreaRootState>` |  | Allows you to replace the component's HTML element with a different tag, or compose it with another component. Accepts a `ReactElement` or a function that returns the element to render. |
| `style` | `CSSProperties \| ((state: ScrollAreaRootState) => CSSProperties)` |  | Style applied to the element, or a function that returns a style object based on the component's state. |
| `viewportProps` | `ScrollAreaViewportProps` |  | Native attributes and ref for the element that actually scrolls. |

### ScrollBar

_Props of `ScrollBar`, generated from its types:_

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `orientation` | `"horizontal" \| "vertical"` | `vertical` | Whether the scrollbar controls vertical or horizontal scroll. |
| `keepMounted` | `boolean` | `false` | Whether to keep the HTML element in the DOM when the viewport isn't scrollable. |
| `className` | `string \| ((state: ScrollAreaScrollbarState) => string)` |  | CSS class applied to the element, or a function that returns a class based on the component's state. |

| `style` | `CSSProperties \| ((state: ScrollAreaScrollbarState) => CSSProperties)` |  | Style applied to the element, or a function that returns a style object based on the component's state. |

## Related

<!-- page: Components/Scroller (src/stories/components/Scroller.mdx) -->

# Scroller

**Status: Stable.**

A bounded scrolling region with an arrow at each edge that can still scroll. Select, DropdownMenu, Combobox and horizontal line Tabs compose it, so a long list and a wide strip scroll alike.

## Anatomy

`Scroller` is the bounded box: it sets `orientation`, how an arrow scrolls (`scrollOn`) and the `surface` the arrows sit on. `ScrollerViewport` is the element that scrolls; `render` substitutes a list (Combobox does), and `viewport` on the root points at an element the Scroller does not render (Tabs passes its ScrollArea viewport). `ScrollerArrow` renders one edge: `start` or `end`.

An arrow appears only when the viewport overflows, only at an edge that can still scroll, and only where the pointer can hover (`hover: hover` and `pointer: fine`); touch readers swipe and see none. While arrows show they replace the native scrollbar, and the viewport keeps their thickness clear as scroll padding, so a focused or highlighted item scrolls out from under them. The arrows paint the surface the Scroller sits on (`utility.elevation.surface.current`: the page, or the Card, Dialog or Sheet that records itself), or the `surface` you name.

When a descendant receives keyboard focus, Scroller reveals it on its scrolling axis, including an item that was only partly visible. This moves its own viewport without scrolling the outer page; a nested Scroller handles its own focus reveal.

A horizontal strip keeps its current item in view: the selected tab (`aria-selected`), the current step (`aria-current`) or the pressed view (`aria-pressed`) scrolls back in if it ended outside, clear of the arrows. Until the reader scrolls, wheels, swipes, clicks, types or moves focus in the strip, that holds whenever the strip's size or content changes, so counts or labels that arrive after the first layout cannot push the current item out. After that only a strip that narrows (a window resize, a panel opening beside it) brings it back, and a strip that grows stays where the reader put it. A current item chosen from outside the strip, as a record's Overview does for its tabs, always scrolls in. Focus does not move.

_Example: story `Stories.KeepsCurrentInView`._

## Focus

The viewport clips on both axes, so every focus ring inside it is drawn inside its box, with the `outline-field-focused` geometry: an item's own outline, and a ring an item draws on a `::before` or `::after` overlay, as Stepper and Timeline steps do. A horizontal viewport also keeps `space.025` of padding, so a resting button's ring and shadow show whole. Do not add padding or an outline offset of your own for the ring.

`ScrollerViewport` is a tab stop only when the keyboard needs it: while it overflows and holds nothing the keyboard can reach (no link, button or field, and no option, menu item, tab, tree item or grid cell that a composite moves focus to), it takes `tabIndex={0}` so the arrow keys can scroll it. It is then a group named by your `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`, or "Content, scrolls" (the locale's `contentScrolls`) when it has none; your own `role` is kept. A strip that fits, or that holds a button, adds no stop. Pass `tabIndex` to decide yourself; a focusable viewport you did not name still takes the default name. Its own ring is drawn inside it as well.

_Example: story `Stories.KeyboardStop`._

Name a strip that can become a stop after what it holds. Unnamed, a keyboard reader hears "Content, scrolls", which says it scrolls and nothing of what is in it.

_Example: story `Stories.DoDont`._

## Vertical

Vertical scrollers scroll on hover unsaid: the arrow is a hover zone, hidden from assistive technology, and keyboard readers already move through the content. Menus use the `overlay` surface.

_Example: story `Stories.Vertical`._

A list more than five viewports tall keeps its native scrollbar and shows no arrows: at the hover speed it would take seconds to reach the end, and the reader can drag the bar instead.

_Example: story `Stories.LongList`._

## Horizontal

Horizontal scrollers step a page on click unsaid: the arrow is a labelled button outside the tab order that reads as one (a pointer cursor, a hover tint and a hairline on its inner edge), and it follows the locale's direction. Pass `scrollOn` to change either default.

_Example: story `Stories.Horizontal`._

## Composition

Select keeps Base UI's own scroll arrows, which step item by item and know the open method; they wear the Scroller arrow classes so the two cannot drift apart. Tabs sizes its arrows to the strip, and a line strip's arrows carry its hairline. Stepper, Timeline, Toolbar's saved views and DataTable's saved questions compose a horizontal Scroller. Do not add a second scroller, an overflow utility, a hand-drawn ring or a fade inside a part that already composes one.

Which scroller to use is in [Choosing a part](?path=/docs/guidance-choosing-a-part--docs): native overflow for a region with nothing to add, ScrollArea for a visible bar the reader drags, Scroller for edge arrows over a list or a strip.

## Props

_Props of `Scroller`, generated from its types:_

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `orientation` | `"horizontal" \| "vertical"` | `vertical` | Which axis scrolls. Vertical unsaid. |
| `scrollOn` | `"click" \| "hover"` |  | How an arrow scrolls: hovering scrolls continuously (a menu), clicking steps a page (a tab strip). Unsaid, vertical scrollers hover and horizontal ones click. |
| `surface` | `"default" \| "overlay" \| "raised"` | `default` | The surface the arrows sit on, so they cover the content they scroll. Unsaid, the surface the Scroller sits on (`utility.elevation.surface.current`). |
| `viewport` | `HTMLElement \| null` |  | The element that scrolls when it is not a ScrollerViewport child, such as a ScrollArea's viewport. Pass a state-held element, not a ref. |

_Props of `ScrollerViewport`, generated from its types:_

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `render` | `ReactElement<unknown, string \| JSXElementConstructor<any>> \| ComponentRenderFn<HTMLProps, {}>` |  | Allows you to replace the component's HTML element with a different tag, or compose it with another component. Accepts a `ReactElement` or a function that returns the element to render. |

_Props of `ScrollerArrow`, generated from its types:_

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `edge` (required) | `"end" \| "start"` |  | The edge this arrow scrolls toward. |

<!-- page: Components/SearchField (src/stories/components/SearchField.mdx) -->

# SearchField

**Status: Stable.**

One search input: the search icon, the query, and a clear button while there is a query. It narrows a list as the reader types, or runs a search on Enter. [Toolbar](?path=/docs/patterns-toolbar--docs) uses it for its search.

Use it wherever the reader finds or narrows records. Do not use it for a value the record keeps, such as a name or a reference: that is an [Input](?path=/docs/components-input--docs) in a [Field](?path=/docs/components-field--docs), which Escape and a clear button never erase. To pick one record from a list of options, use a [Combobox](?path=/docs/components-combobox--docs); to search the whole product, the [SearchDialog](?path=/docs/patterns-searchdialog--docs).

_Example: story `Stories.ClearAndEscape`._

## Keys and the clear button

| The reader               | What happens                                                                                                                                |
| ------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Types                    | `onValueChange` runs on every keystroke, as on Input.                                                                                       |
| Presses Enter            | Nothing, unless there is an `onSubmit`, which receives the query. Enter never submits a form around the field.                              |
| Presses Escape           | A query is cleared and focus stays in the field. With the field empty, Escape reaches whatever holds it: a dialog closes, a popover closes. |
| Presses the clear button | The query is cleared and focus goes to the field. The button shows only while there is a query and the field can change.                    |

Clearing sends the same input event typing does, so `onValueChange` receives `""`, native `onChange` runs, and a Field's dirty and filled state follow; `onClear` runs after it. A native form reset puts the default query back, and the clear button follows it. Enter or Escape that confirms or cancels an input method's composition is left to the input method, so cancelling a composition never erases the query. A caller's `onKeyDown` runs first, and `preventDefault()` in it skips the field's own handling of that key.

Enter never submits a surrounding form, with or without `onSubmit`, so a live filter inside a dialog's form cannot save the dialog when the reader presses Enter to search. The form's own primary still submits it.

_Example: story `Stories.InsideAForm`._
_Example: story `Stories.RunsOnEnter`._
_Example: story `Stories.InADialog`._

## Sizes and states

`medium` (32px) in a form, beside a medium Button; `small` (28px) in a toolbar, beside small buttons. `className` and `style` go to the field's frame, where its width is set; every other prop, the ref included, goes to the input. The value can be controlled (`value` with `onValueChange`) or not (`defaultValue`).

_Example: story `Stories.States`._

## In a Field

Inside a [Field](?path=/docs/components-field--docs) the FieldLabel names the search, the FieldDescription and FieldError describe it, and the Field's `invalid`, `required` and `disabled` reach it, with no ids written by hand. A disabled or read-only field has no clear button.

_Example: story `Stories.BoundInField`._

## Accessibility

- **A searchbox.** The input is `type="search"`, so it has the searchbox role, and `enterKeyHint="search"` puts a search key on a phone's keyboard.
- **Named.** By its FieldLabel, by `aria-label`, or else by its placeholder, and by the locale's "Search" when there is none. A placeholder that names what is searched ("Search controls") is enough in a toolbar; in a form, use a FieldLabel.
- **The clear button** is named "Clear search" (the `clearSearch` message). It is not a Tab stop, because Escape does the same from the keyboard, and a touch screen reader reaches it by swiping. Under a coarse pointer it takes a 24px target. Pressing it keeps focus in the field.
- **The icon is decorative**, hidden from assistive technology, and neither the frame nor the icon is a group: a screen reader meets one searchbox, not a searchbox inside unnamed groups.
- **Results are the caller's to announce.** The field does not know how many records matched; the list or table it narrows owns that result.
- **Landmark.** When this is the page's search, put it in a `<search>` element or a `<form role="search">`. Enter does not submit that form either, so run the search from `onSubmit` (or call the form's `requestSubmit()` there). A filter above a table is not a landmark.

The words it writes come from the locale (`search`, `clearSearch`), so a `LedgerProvider` translates them. Its spacing is logical, so right to left the icon sits at the right and the clear button at the left.

_Example: story `Stories.Localized`._
_Example: story `Stories.RightToLeft`._

## Props

_Props of `SearchField`, generated from its types:_

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `render` | `ReactElement<unknown, string \| JSXElementConstructor<any>> \| ComponentRenderFn<HTMLProps, InputState>` |  | Allows you to replace the component's HTML element with a different tag, or compose it with another component. Accepts a `ReactElement` or a function that returns the element to render. |
| `onValueChange` | `((value: string, eventDetails: { reason: "none"; event: Event; cancel: () => void; allowPropagation: () => void; isCanceled: boolean; isPropagationAllowed: boolean; trigger: Element; }) => void)` |  | Callback fired when the `value` changes. Use when controlled. |
| `value` | `string` |  | The query, when the caller owns it. Pair it with `onValueChange`. |
| `defaultValue` | `string` |  | The first query, when the field owns it. |
| `size` | `"medium" \| "small"` | `medium` | Medium (32px) in a form; small (28px) in a toolbar, beside small buttons. Medium by default. |
| `onSubmit` | `((value: string) => void)` |  | Runs the search on Enter, with the current query, for a search that does not narrow as the reader types. Enter never submits a form around the field, with or without it: a live filter inside a dialog's form leaves saving to the form's own primary. |
| `onClear` | `(() => void)` |  | Called after the clear button or Escape has emptied the field. `onValueChange` has already run with "". |
| `className` | `string` |  | Classes for the field's frame, where its width is set. The input's own props go to the input. @accepts layout |
| `style` | `CSSProperties` |  | Style for the field's frame, such as a width or a flex basis. |

<!-- page: Components/Select (src/stories/components/Select.mdx) -->

# Select

**Status: Stable.**

Choose one value, or a few, from a short list the reader does not need to search, with shadcn's Base UI Select parts. Ledger supplies the control geometry, the menu styling, locale direction and the Field binding.

```tsx
const statuses = { draft: "Draft", review: "In review" };

<Field>
  <FieldLabel>Status</FieldLabel>
  <Select name="status" items={statuses} defaultValue="draft">
    <SelectTrigger>
      <SelectValue placeholder="Choose a status" />
    </SelectTrigger>
    <SelectContent>
      <SelectItem value="draft">Draft</SelectItem>
      <SelectItem value="review">In review</SelectItem>
    </SelectContent>
  </Select>
</Field>;
```

## When to use it

Use a Select for a fixed set of four to a dozen values the reader recognises on sight: a status, a priority, a kind, a revision. The choice table under [Forms](?path=/docs/patterns-forms--docs) decides between the choice controls:

- Two or three options the reader should compare at a glance are a [RadioGroup](?path=/docs/components-radiogroup--docs), which shows every option at once.
- A long list, or records the reader finds by typing a name or an identifier, is a [Combobox](?path=/docs/components-combobox--docs).
- An on/off setting is a [Switch](?path=/docs/components-switch--docs) or a [Checkbox](?path=/docs/components-checkbox--docs).
- Actions and view options behind a button are a [DropdownMenu](?path=/docs/components-dropdownmenu--docs), never a Select whose change runs a command.

## Composition and states

Root owns the selected value, the open state, the form props and modality. Trigger owns the native button props, refs, render composition, layout and size, on the control scale Input, Combobox and Button share: `medium` is 32px, the default, and `small` is 28px, for a toolbar or a dense row. `data-size` says the same word, so InputGroup's rule keyed on `small` finds a small Select. `sm` and `default` are the deprecated shadcn spellings, kept for one version and renamed by `ledger/no-deprecated-name`. Value owns the placeholder and the displayed value.

Supply Root's `items` label map or array, object-value label conversion, or Value's children to format the selected value. Item children alone do not label the closed trigger. A label can contain the same Dot or Badge shown on the record. Group and Label identify sections; Separator divides them.

`disabled` prevents interaction and omits the value from submission. `readOnly` keeps the value submitted and the trigger focusable while preventing selection. Item's `disabled` prevents activation and stays reachable with the arrow keys. For decorated option children, give Item a plain-text `label` for typeahead. Classes, styles, render props and refs follow each Base UI part's native contract.

_Example: story `Stories.SelectMatrix`._

Inside a [Field](?path=/docs/components-field--docs) the trigger fills the Field, as Input and Combobox do. Elsewhere (a toolbar, a filter row, a rail) it fits its value. Either way it never grows past its container: a value longer than the room truncates inside the trigger, and the whole value is in the open list. A class or style width on Trigger wins.

_Example: story `Stories.Width`._

## Positioning and scrolling

Content includes Portal, Positioner, Popup, List and both scroll arrows. The list opens below its trigger, or above it where there is no room below, from the trigger's start edge with a 4px gap. It is at least as wide as the trigger (and at least 144px, `dimension.part.select`), and as wide as its longest option up to the 720px measure and the room in the viewport; past that an option wraps inside its row, including an unbroken identifier or digest, and never runs under the check mark. Near the edge of the window the list shifts back so it stays whole. Native style, className, render and ref props target Popup; `finalFocus` controls focus return.

`alignItemWithTrigger` opts into the list that opens over its trigger with the chosen option on the value, where space and the input device allow it. Use it only for a compact trigger whose list is short, since it covers the field's label and the fields around it; the side and alignment offsets apply only when it falls back to opening below. Content's `dir` overrides the inherited positioning direction as well as the text direction.

_Example: story `Stories.Placement`._

The inner List owns bounded scrolling so the hover arrows work in both placements. ScrollUpButton and ScrollDownButton wrap Base UI's hover scroll arrows, with their native props and refs, and wear the [Scroller](?path=/docs/components-scroller--docs) arrow look across the popup's inner box. They appear when the list can scroll and are omitted for touch input. Content includes them; the example composes them directly for a custom list geometry, beside the standard Content in right to left.

_Example: story `Stories.Scrolling`._

## Descriptions and disabled reasons

`description` on SelectItem adds a second line under the option, in smaller subtle text that wraps inside the list: what tells two similar options apart ("287 controls for a moderate-impact system"). The line is the option's accessible description, not part of its name, so typeahead finds the label alone and the closed trigger shows only the label.

An option that cannot be chosen takes `disabledReason` instead of `disabled`: the option is disabled, the arrow keys still reach it, a screen reader announces it as unavailable and reads the reason, and the reason shows as its description line, readable on the faded row. Write what would make it available. A tooltip cannot do this job in a list, and a disabled option without a reason leaves the reader guessing. A list where most options are unavailable is the wrong control; say what is missing beside the field instead.

_Example: story `Stories.Descriptions`._

## Forms and selection

Inside a [Field](?path=/docs/components-field--docs) the FieldLabel names the trigger and the open list, the hint and error describe the trigger, and the Field's `invalid`, `required` and `disabled` reach it, with no ids. Clicking the label opens the list, as clicking the trigger does, because the trigger is a button the label activates. Outside a Field, connect a label to Trigger with `htmlFor` and `id`, and put `aria-describedby`, `aria-invalid` and `aria-required` on Trigger. Root's `required` enables native constraint validation; the Field's `required` only announces. Native form props (`name`, `form`, `autoComplete`, `inputRef`) belong on Root. Root's id supplies the default trigger id; an explicit Trigger id takes precedence. `inputRef` targets the hidden form input.

Single selection accepts a value or `null`; `onValueChange(value, details)` can reject a change with `details.cancel()`. Cancellation keeps the value, and an item activation still closes a single-select popup. Add a `null` item when the reader needs to clear from the list. Value's placeholder appears when no value is selected.

`multiple` uses arrays and keeps the list open while the reader toggles options. FormData holds one entry per selected value under the same name. Object values supply `itemToStringLabel`, `itemToStringValue` and `isItemEqualToValue` for display, submission and identity. Root keeps generic single and multiple inference; Item and Value use the installed Base UI value contracts.

With Base UI 1.7, form reset is caller-owned: reset controlled values in the form's `onReset`. The example covers required values, cancelled changes, multiple numeric values and object identity.

_Example: story `Stories.InField`._

_Example: story `Stories.BoundInField`._

## Content

- A visible FieldLabel names the Select. The placeholder is never its only name: once a value is chosen the placeholder is gone, and nothing would say what the field is.
- The placeholder says the action and the noun: "Choose a status", "Choose a revision". It never says "Select…", "Optional" or repeats the label; the Field marks a required field.
- Option labels are short nouns in sentence case, the words the record shows. Put the difference between two similar options in `description`, not in a longer label.
- Order options by meaning (the workflow order of statuses, severity from high to low), and alphabetically only when they have no order of their own.
- A "No status" option is a `null` item at the end, after a separator, and only where clearing is allowed.

## Accessibility and dialogs

Trigger is a native button with combobox semantics, an expanded state and a listbox association. Options announce their selected and disabled states. Enter, Space and ArrowDown open; the arrow keys, Home and End move focus; typing matches labels; Enter and Space select. Closed single-select typeahead changes the selected value. Keep a visible Field label or an explicit accessible name on Trigger. Inside a Field the list is named by the label; name Content's list with `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` where another name is needed. These name the listbox as well as passing through to Popup.

Base UI coordinates nested Select, Dialog and Drawer popups. Escape dismisses the Select before the dialog and returns focus to the trigger; closing the dialog then returns to its opener.

_Example: story `Stories.Dialogs`._

## Props

Select follows [shadcn Select](https://ui.shadcn.com/docs/components/base/select) and [Base UI Select](https://base-ui.com/react/components/select), on the installed Base UI version. SelectContent adds five positioning props to Base UI's Popup; Ledger adds the token styling and the locale, Field and dialog integration.

<!-- page: Components/Separator (src/stories/components/Separator.mdx) -->

# Separator

**Status: Stable.**

A hairline between siblings: two blocks in a stack or two groups in a toolbar. Built on the shadcn Base UI Separator, with Ledger's `color.border` and parent-owned spacing. Rows, menus and tables already draw their own rules.

_Example: story `Stories.SeparatorMatrix`._

## When to use it

- **Between two groups that are siblings** where space alone does not part them: the groups of actions in a toolbar, two blocks in a stack that hold different kinds of content.
- **Vertical, in a flex row**, between groups of controls.

Not between rows, menu items or table rows: [Item](?path=/docs/components-item--docs).Group, the [DropdownMenu](?path=/docs/components-dropdownmenu--docs)'s own separator and a [Table](?path=/docs/components-table--docs) draw their rules. Not around a container that has an edge or a surface of its own, such as a [Card](?path=/docs/components-card--docs), and not under a heading: a [Section](?path=/docs/layout-section--docs) draws that rule with `divided`. Not to divide a form's sections with a word in the rule: that is a `FieldSeparator` ([Field](?path=/docs/components-field--docs), Parts). Not as a drag handle: that is [Resizable](?path=/docs/components-resizable--docs)'s.

## Content

- A separator says nothing of its own. What the groups are is said by their headings or labels, not by the rule.
- A rule a screen reader announces, such as the one between a toolbar's groups, may take an `aria-label` that says what it divides ("Editing actions", in Native composition below). A rule that only draws a line is `isDecorative`.
- One rule between two groups, never one at the start or the end of a list or a row.

A list of rows is an Item.Group or a Table, which draw their own hairlines, never text with a Separator between each row. A rule never opens or closes a stack: with nothing on one side it is a border, which the container draws. A vertical rule goes in a flex row such as an Inline, never in a column, where it has no height to stretch to and draws nothing.

_Example: story `Stories.Dont`._

## Anatomy

One `div` by default, with `data-slot="separator"` and `data-orientation`. The rule is one pixel: a top border spanning the container horizontally, or an inline-start border stretching to the height of a flex row vertically. Stack or Inline supplies the gap around it.

Ledger retains its existing border paint instead of the reference's background-filled line. Both orientations use `color.border`; the component requires no shadcn theme or state-selector aliases.

## Variants and composition

| Option                     | Behavior                                                                   |
| -------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `orientation="horizontal"` | Default. Spans its container between stacked blocks.                       |
| `orientation="vertical"`   | Stretches inside a flex row, such as an Inline or toolbar.                 |
| `isDecorative`             | Hides a purely visual rule from assistive technology. Defaults to `false`. |
| `render`                   | Replaces the default element or composes a custom component.               |
| `className` / `style`      | Accept a value or a callback receiving `{ orientation }`.                  |

Native props and refs reach the rendered element. Base UI merges props, event handlers, classes, styles and refs from a rendered element. A render callback or custom component must forward the supplied props and ref.

_Example: story `Stories.NativeComposition`._

```tsx
<Separator
  orientation="vertical"
  aria-label="Editing actions"
  className={({ orientation }) => (orientation === "vertical" ? "border-bold" : undefined)}
/>
```

## Accessibility

- By default the element has `role="separator"` and an `aria-orientation` matching its orientation.
- `isDecorative` supplies `role="none"`, `aria-hidden="true"` and no `aria-orientation`. Explicit native role and ARIA props override those defaults; keep them consistent with the intended semantics.
- The default separator has no tab stop. Use Resizable for a keyboard-operable resize handle.
- Place a separator between related groups. Avoid redundant rules around containers or between rows that already draw their own borders.

## Props

`SeparatorProps` includes the Base UI primitive props and Ledger's optional `isDecorative`. Separator takes native div props, its ref, `render`, and class and style callbacks, and carries `data-slot="separator"` and `data-orientation`. See the [Base UI API](https://base-ui.com/react/components/separator#api-reference) for native composition and state callbacks.

_Props of `Separator`, generated from its types:_

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `orientation` | `"horizontal" \| "vertical"` | `vertical` | The orientation of the separator. |
| `className` | `string \| ((state: SeparatorState) => string)` |  | CSS class applied to the element, or a function that returns a class based on the component's state. |
| `render` | `ReactElement<unknown, string \| JSXElementConstructor<any>> \| ComponentRenderFn<HTMLProps, SeparatorState>` |  | Allows you to replace the component's HTML element with a different tag, or compose it with another component. Accepts a `ReactElement` or a function that returns the element to render. |
| `style` | `CSSProperties \| ((state: SeparatorState) => CSSProperties)` |  | Style applied to the element, or a function that returns a style object based on the component's state. |
| `isDecorative` | `boolean` | `false` | Hide a purely visual rule from assistive technology. Native role and ARIA props can override these defaults. |

_Example: story `Stories.Playground`._

_Rendered in the Storybook: Controls._

## Related

- [Stack](?path=/docs/primitives-stack--docs) and [Inline](?path=/docs/primitives-inline--docs): the gap around the rule.
- [Toolbar](?path=/docs/patterns-toolbar--docs): groups separated vertically.
- [Item](?path=/docs/components-item--docs): rows with their own separators.
- [Resizable](?path=/docs/components-resizable--docs): an interactive resize handle.
- [Upgrading](?path=/docs/guidance-upgrading--docs#separator): the earlier API's spellings and what they are now.

# Sheet

**Status: Stable.**

A modal panel at an edge of the window: a selection, a review, or a task that must hold focus beside the page's context. Built on [Base UI Dialog](https://base-ui.com/react/components/dialog) with [shadcn’s Sheet composition](https://ui.shadcn.com/docs/components/base/sheet) and Ledger's tokens.

_Example: story `Stories.EdgesAndScrolling`._

## When to use it

- **A modal selection or review** that needs the height of the window, such as choosing many records ([PickerSheet](?path=/docs/patterns-pickersheet--docs)) or reviewing one ([PreviewSheet](?path=/docs/patterns-previewsheet--docs)).
- **Filters or a short form** that should sit at the edge while the reader keeps the page in mind.

Not for work beside a list the reader keeps using: that is the Shell's panel, which blocks nothing. Not for a create or edit form: that is a [Dialog](?path=/docs/components-dialog--docs). Not for a phone's bottom sheet with a swipe: that is a [Drawer](?path=/docs/components-drawer--docs).

## Anatomy

- **SheetContent** brings its portal, the blanket and a close button at the top end (an IconButton named Close, with no tooltip, first in the Tab order where it is drawn, while the first field still takes focus on open), and slides from `side`: `right` by default, `left`, `top` or `bottom`, or `start` and `end`, which follow the reading direction. It records the overlay surface as the current one, so a sticky header or pinned cell inside matches the sheet.
- **SheetHeader** holds the title (the sheet's h2, a [Heading](?path=/docs/primitives-heading--docs) at `overlay`, 15/22 medium; headings inside start at h3) and the description, which wrap an unbroken value. A record's name as the title is a PageHeader.Title rendered as SheetTitle, and keeps the page title's size.
- **SheetBody** is the one scrolling region, with the sheet's inset. A toolbar row that should not scroll sits between the header and the body.
- **SheetFooter** stays outside the scroll, on the sheet's own surface below a hairline. The header, the body and the footer share the sheet's `space.200` inline inset.
- **SheetPortal** and **SheetOverlay** are exported for a custom popup, as Dialog's are.

## Widths

`width` on SheetContent picks a step for a sheet at the start or end edge; do not set pixels in `style`.

| `width`      | Size               | For                                |
| ------------ | ------------------ | ---------------------------------- |
| `small`      | 320px              | Filters, a short form              |
| `medium`     | 420px, the default | A form, a record's details         |
| `large`      | 760px              | A table of about four columns      |
| `xlarge`     | 960px              | A table beside a preview           |
| `fullscreen` | The window         | A task that needs the whole window |

Each step is capped by the window. `large` and `xlarge` match Dialog's.

_Example: story `Stories.Widths`._

## Scrolling and short windows

The body takes the height the header, any toolbar row and the footer leave, at least 80px, and scrolls. Read-only content that overflows makes it a tab stop, "Content, scrolls". In a window under 30rem tall the sheet scrolls as one: the header and any toolbar scroll away with the body, and the footer stays at the bottom, so a list is never squeezed to a single row. The footer keeps its height as the sheet's scroll padding, so a control that takes focus scrolls clear of it.

## Pending

`pending` on the Sheet holds it while a command runs: Escape, the blanket, the close button and every SheetClose are cancelled or disabled, the close button and a SheetClose rendered as a kit Button stay focusable while they are (`aria-disabled`), and the popup is `aria-busy`. Close the sheet with `open={false}` when the command succeeds.

_Example: story `Stories.Pending`._

## Accessibility

- **Give the sheet a title.** Base UI traps focus, handles Escape and nested dialogs, and returns focus to the opener, or to `finalFocus` when the opener went away. A Sheet opened from state records the element that had focus as it opens, so focus comes back to it even when a field took focus as it mounted. Move focus to a field with `initialFocus`, never `autoFocus`.
- **Keep a close control available**; the content includes one by default.
- **The one stack.** An AlertDialog for the decision the sheet owns renders inside SheetContent; the sheet dims under it and the page keeps one blanket.
- **Forced colours keep the edge**: the popup draws a CanvasText outline, and the blanket stays a veil of Canvas.

_Example: story `Stories.NestedAndRTL`._

## Content

- The title names what the sheet holds: the record under review ("CTRL-0412 Segregation of duties"), or the selection and what it is for ("Add controls to Flight computer"). A selection's title, its trigger and its primary say the same words.
- The primary says the operation and its object ("Add 12 controls", "Apply filters"), never OK, Submit or Done alone; the secondary is Cancel, or Close for a sheet whose choices apply as they are made.
- The description says what the sheet acts on or what it leaves out ("Controls already in the baseline are not listed"), never an instruction the reader must keep in mind while the sheet is open.
- A title that names a record may hold its code, and wraps rather than running past the edge. A failure is said in the body, through an Alert, never in the title.

## Props

Sheet is Base UI Dialog at an edge, so it takes the same root props, `open`, `defaultOpen`, `onOpenChange` (with the change's `reason` and `cancel()` in its details), `onOpenChangeComplete`, `modal`, `disablePointerDismissal`, `actionsRef` and `handle`, and Ledger's `pending`. SheetContent takes the popup's `initialFocus`, `finalFocus`, `render`, `className` and `style`, and Ledger's `side`, `width` and `showCloseButton`. The types are in [Base UI's API reference](https://base-ui.com/react/components/dialog#api-reference).

_Props of `Sheet`, generated from its types:_

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `open` | `boolean` |  | Whether the dialog is currently open. |
| `defaultOpen` | `boolean` | `false` | Whether the dialog is initially open. To render a controlled dialog, use the `open` prop instead. |
| `modal` | `boolean \| "trap-focus"` | `true` | Determines if the dialog enters a modal state when open. - `true`: user interaction is limited to just the dialog: focus is trapped, document page scroll is locked, and pointer interactions on outside elements are disabled. - `false`: user interaction with the rest of the document is allowed. - `'trap-focus'`: focus is trapped inside the dialog, but document page scroll is not locked and pointer interactions outside of it remain enabled. When `modal` is `true` or `'trap-focus'`, render `<Dialog.Close>` inside `<Dialog.Popup>` so touch screen readers can escape the popup. |
| `onOpenChange` | `((open: boolean, eventDetails: DialogRootChangeEventDetails) => void)` |  | Event handler called when the dialog is opened or closed. |
| `onOpenChangeComplete` | `((open: boolean) => void)` |  | Event handler called after any animations complete when the dialog is opened or closed. |
| `disablePointerDismissal` | `boolean` | `false` | Whether to prevent the dialog from closing on outside presses. For non-modal dialogs, this also prevents the dialog from closing when focus moves outside of it. |
| `actionsRef` | `RefObject<DialogRootActions \| null>` |  | A ref to imperative actions. - `unmount`: Manually unmounts the dialog. Call this after any externally controlled closing animation finishes. - `close`: Closes the dialog imperatively when called. |
| `handle` | `DialogHandle<Payload>` |  | A handle to associate the dialog with a trigger. If specified, allows external triggers to control the dialog's open state. Can be created with the Dialog.createHandle() method. |
| `children` | `ReactNode \| PayloadChildRenderFunction<Payload>` |  | The content of the dialog. This can be a regular React node or a render function that receives the `payload` of the active trigger. |
| `triggerId` | `string \| null` |  | ID of the trigger that the dialog is associated with. This is useful in conjunction with the `open` prop to create a controlled dialog. There's no need to specify this prop when the dialog is uncontrolled (that is, when the `open` prop is not set). |
| `defaultTriggerId` | `string \| null` |  | ID of the trigger that the dialog is associated with. This is useful in conjunction with the `defaultOpen` prop to create an initially open dialog. |
| `pending` | `boolean` | `false` | A save or another command is in flight. Every request to close is cancelled before `onOpenChange` hears of it (Escape, the blanket, the close button, a SheetClose), the close controls are disabled (the built-in close button, and a close rendered as a kit Button, stay focusable with `aria-disabled`, so focus on them is kept), and the popup is `aria-busy`. An imperative close through `actionsRef`, or `open={false}`, still closes: end the pending state when the command settles. |

### SheetContent

By default, focus moves to the first tabbable element inside the popup, except when the dialog is opened by touch — then the popup itself is focused to avoid opening the virtual keyboard. - `false`: Do not move focus. - `true`: Move focus based on the default behavior (first tabbable element or popup). - `RefObject`: Move focus to the ref element. - `function`: Called with the interaction type (`mouse`, `touch`, `pen`, or `keyboard`). Each is capped by the window. `fullscreen` covers the window from any edge. A `style.maxWidth` still wins. |

# Skeleton

**Status: Stable.**

A placeholder that holds the space of loading content. It follows shadcn's native div contract, with Ledger's line, heading, circle and block options. Use [PageSkeleton](?path=/docs/layout-pageskeleton--docs) for a page's first paint and [Spinner](?path=/docs/components-spinner--docs) for an action in progress.

_Example: story `Stories.SkeletonMatrix`._

## Anatomy

The outer element is a `div` with `data-slot="skeleton"`, hidden from assistive technology by default. A single shape paints this element in `color.skeleton`. With `shape="line"` and `lines > 1`, the outer div groups the generated lines with `space.100` between them.

Native attributes, events and refs always belong to the outer div. IDs, labels and handlers are never copied to each generated line.

## Shapes and sizing

| Shape     | Default geometry                       | Use                                                                          |
| --------- | -------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `line`    | 12px tall, full width, `radius.small`  | Body text. Use `lines` for a paragraph.                                      |
| `heading` | 20px tall, full width, `radius.small`  | A title or record name.                                                      |
| `circle`  | 32px square, `radius.full`             | An avatar or icon. `width` also sets its height unless `height` is supplied. |
| `block`   | 96px tall, full width, `radius.medium` | A card, chart or image.                                                      |

`width` and `height` accept a number in pixels or a CSS length. On a single shape, explicit `style` values override those dimensions. Existing className overrides continue through the package's class merger.

For generated lines, `width` and `height` apply to **each line**; `className` and `style` apply to **the wrapper**. The last line is two thirds wide when `width` is omitted. An explicit `width` sizes every line equally, including the last.

## Native props and content

_Example: story `Stories.NativeAttributes`._

```tsx
<Skeleton
  ref={placeholderRef}
  id="record-placeholder"
  shape="block"
  height={120}
  data-record="preview"
/>
```

Native children render once. In multiline mode, supplied children replace the automatic lines; omitting children generates them. Explicit `null`, `false` or `0` are supplied content. Native HTML content also replaces automatic lines and follows React's normal content rules.

Skeleton uses a native div, as the shadcn reference does. It has no `render` or `asChild` prop. Compose a more specific loading layout with several Skeletons inside a normal container.

## Accessibility and motion

- `aria-hidden` defaults to `true` so placeholders do not announce meaningless shapes. Explicit native ARIA props can override the default.
- **Say the wait in words.** `aria-busy` on the waiting region holds a screen reader's announcements; it says nothing itself. Give the region a line that names the wait, visible or visually hidden ("Loading the record"), and say it once as it starts, with a Spinner's `label` or `announce`, where the reader should hear it. Clear the busy state when the content arrives.
- Keep placeholders noninteractive.
- Shapes pulse while waiting. Under reduced motion the pulse stops and the layout stays.
- In forced colours the shapes are GrayText, so a loading page is not blank.
- Match the size and amount of expected content, then replace the placeholders when it arrives.

## Props

`SkeletonProps` includes native div props plus `shape`, `lines`, `width` and `height`. Native attributes, events, children and refs reach the outer div, which carries `data-slot="skeleton"`; a multiline Skeleton's ref is its wrapper, not a line.

_Props of `Skeleton`, generated from its types:_

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `shape` | `"block" \| "circle" \| "heading" \| "line"` | `line` | `line` (12px, the default) for a line of body text; `heading` (20px) for a title; `circle` for an avatar or an icon, `width` its size; `block` for a card, a chart, an image, at `height`. |
| `lines` | `number` |  | Several lines stacked `space.100` apart. The last is two thirds wide unless width is supplied. Native content replaces these generated lines. Lines only. |
| `width` | `string \| number` |  | A number in px, or a CSS length. Full width by default; a circle is 32px (`dimension.part.skeletonCircle`). |
| `height` | `string \| number` |  | A number in px, or a CSS length. The shape's height by default; a block is 96px (`dimension.part.skeletonBlock`). |

_Example: story `Stories.Playground`._

_Rendered in the Storybook: Controls._

## Related

- [PageSkeleton](?path=/docs/layout-pageskeleton--docs): the page's first paint.
- [Spinner](?path=/docs/components-spinner--docs): progress for an action.
- [Chart](?path=/docs/patterns-chart-overview--docs): loading layouts for plots.
- [Empty](?path=/docs/components-empty--docs): a region with no content to load.
- [Upgrading](?path=/docs/guidance-upgrading--docs#skeleton): the earlier API's spellings and what they are now.

## Don't

Content on its way holds its shape with a Skeleton: a circle where the avatar will be, lines about as long as the text. Never a spinner in its place, one grey block for a row, or more lines than will arrive.

_Example: story `Stories.Dont`._

<!-- page: Components/Spinner (src/stories/components/Spinner.mdx) -->

# Spinner

**Status: Stable.**

Something is in flight and its length is unknown: a save, an export, a refresh. It sits beside what it is about, says its name once when it appears, and goes when the work ends.

_Example: story `Stories.Playground`._

## Choosing between them

| The wait                                             | Part                                                                                                                   |
| ---------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| The reader pressed a button and waits for its result | The Button's own `isLoading`, which draws a decorative Spinner and keeps focus                                         |
| Work beside a control or a row that is not a button  | `Spinner`, `small` beside text, `medium` alone in a row or a toolbar                                                   |
| A region's content on its way, whose shape is known  | [Skeleton](?path=/docs/components-skeleton--docs), or DataTable's loading rows                                         |
| A task that finishes and knows how far it has gone   | [Progress](?path=/docs/components-progress--docs)                                                                      |
| A file on its way up                                 | [Attachment](?path=/docs/components-attachment--docs) in its `uploading` state, started from a Button with `isLoading` |

A long background task (an upload, a package build) shows on the control that started it, with `isLoading`, never a disabled button whose label changes: that drops focus to the page and says nothing. Its end is said in the region, or as a [toast](?path=/docs/components-toaster--docs) when the reader has moved on.

## Anatomy

Lucide's Loader2 as an svg with `data-slot="spinner"`, `role="status"` and the name as its `aria-label`. Native svg attributes, events and the ref reach that element.

## Variants and sizes

`small` (12px, the default) beside text and in a button; `medium` (16px) alone in a row or a toolbar; `large` (24px) centred in a section that has nothing else while it loads. `appearance` is `subtle` on a surface, `inverse` on a bold fill, or `inherit` for the text colour around it.

_Example: story `Stories.SizesAndAppearance`._

## Delay

`delay` waits that many milliseconds before the spinner appears. The default, 0, shows it at once. Pass about 400 for a wait that is often shorter, so a fast one never flashes a spinner. Changing a pending delay restarts the wait; once shown, the spinner stays until it unmounts, so a new operation that should wait again takes a new `key`.

_Example: story `Stories.Delay`._

## Content

- **Name the wait for what it is**: "Saving", "Exporting the package". "Loading", the locale's default, is for a load with no better word.
- **Beside a word that already says it**, pass that word, so a screen reader and a sighted reader get the same one.
- **One spinner per wait.** Four charts refreshing together share one name, which is said once.

## Accessibility

- **It says its name once, politely, when it appears.** A status inserted with its name already set is announced by almost no screen reader, so the Spinner sends its name through the kit's live regions (`announce`) as it appears, after its delay; spinners that appear together with one name are said once. `aria-labelledby` says the referenced text instead.
- **`isDecorative`** hides it and says nothing, where its parent already carries the busy state: a loading Button, a region with its own status, a loading toast.
- **Reduced motion** stops the rotation; the status and its name stay.

_Example: story `Stories.Announced`._

## Props

_Props of `Spinner`, generated from its types:_

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `size` | `"large" \| "medium" \| "small"` | `small` | `small` (12px) beside text and in a button, the default; `medium` (16px) on its own in a row or a toolbar; `large` (24px) centred in a section that is empty while it loads. |
| `label` | `string` |  | What the wait is, for a screen reader: "Loading", the default; "Saving", "Exporting". Beside a word that already says it, pass that word. It is said once, politely, when the spinner appears. |
| `isDecorative` | `boolean` | `false` | Hide the graphic, and say nothing, when its parent already communicates the busy state: a loading Button, a region with its own status. |
| `appearance` | `"inherit" \| "inverse" \| "subtle"` | `subtle` | `subtle`, the default, on a surface; `inverse` on a bold fill; `inherit` takes the text colour around it, for a button. |
| `delay` | `number` | `0` | Milliseconds before it appears; 0, the default, shows it at once. Pass about 400 for a wait that is often shorter, so a fast one never flashes a spinner. Changing a pending delay restarts the wait; once shown, it stays visible until unmounted. |

Native svg props include `ref`, `id`, `strokeWidth`, `style`, `className`, ARIA and events; an explicit `aria-label` wins over `label`.

## Related

[Button](?path=/docs/components-button--docs), [Skeleton](?path=/docs/components-skeleton--docs), [Progress](?path=/docs/components-progress--docs), [Attachment](?path=/docs/components-attachment--docs), [Announcer](?path=/docs/components-announcer--docs).

Sources: [shadcn Spinner](https://ui.shadcn.com/docs/components/base/spinner), [implementation](https://github.com/shadcn-ui/ui/blob/main/apps/v4/registry/bases/base/ui/spinner.tsx), [Polaris Spinner](https://polaris-react.shopify.com/components/feedback-indicators/spinner).

## Don't

The button that started the work shows it with `isLoading`, keeping its label, its width and focus, never a disabled button whose label changes. Content on its way is a Skeleton, never a large spinner where it will be.

_Example: story `Stories.Dont`._

<!-- page: Components/Stat (src/stories/components/Stat.mdx) -->

# Stat

**Status: Stable.**

A number with its name. `Stat.Tile` is a label, a big tabular number and a one-line note, one cell of a `Stat.Grid`: the headline numbers at the top of a record, framed as a card, or a band between two sections. A tile with `link` is a count that opens the register it counts. A bare `Stat` is the number over its label for an unframed row inside a Section. Numbers are written in the reader's locale, and zero reads muted.

_Example: story `Stories.StatMatrix`._

## Anatomy

| Part  | What it is                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| ----- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Label | `font.body.small` in `color.text.subtle`: what the number counts. Above the number in a Tile, below it in a bare Stat.                                                                                                     |
| Value | A [Heading](?path=/docs/primitives-heading--docs) at `page` as a `div` (`font.heading.page`, 20/26 semibold), tabular. `color.text`, or the tone's text colour when the number is a status; zero in `color.text.subtlest`. |
| Note  | `font.body.small` in `color.text.subtle`, one line under the value. Tile only.                                                                                                                                             |
| Trend | Beside the value, `space.150` from it: a Chart.Sparkline of the same count over time, from `trend`. Tile only.                                                                                                             |
| Link  | With `link`, the link fills the tile and holds the label, value, trend and note, so the whole tile is one target. Tile only.                                                                                               |
| Grid  | Two to six cells across, hairline gutters painted with `color.border`. `card` is bordered and rounded; `band` runs between two rules.                                                                                      |

## Variants

| Variant               | Use                                                                                                    |
| --------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `Stat.Tile` in a Grid | The headline numbers of a record or a screen: at the top as a card, or as a band between two sections. |
| Linked `Stat.Tile`    | A dashboard count that opens its filtered register: "Open risks" opens the risk register, filtered.    |
| `Stat`                | A summary row inside a Section, where a framed grid would be a card inside a card.                     |

_Example: story `Stories.Linked`._

A count whose history matters takes a sparkline in `trend`, beside the number; the number stays the value, and the note says what the line shows ("Down from 14 in January"). A series read for its values is a [Chart](?path=/docs/patterns-chart-overview--docs).

_Example: story `Stories.WithATrend`._

Not built, and why: no delta or trend arrow ("+3 this week"), because a colour and an arrow for a change need a polarity the tile cannot know, and the note says it in words; no icon in the tile; no tinted tile, because the tone colours the number and a tinted tile would make every number read as a status; no link on a bare `Stat`, because a summary row inside a Section is read, not opened.

## Sizes

One type size, `font.heading.page`, the page title's. What varies is the grid: `cols` from two to six, the most it shows. The grid takes its columns from its own width, not the window's, so it reads the same on a page, in an aside and in a 320px panel on a wide screen. Each tile keeps at least 128px: six and five fold to three, every count folds to two, and one column below 257px, so a panel's body and a 320px phone show two across. A short last row shares its width, so the gutter never shows as an empty cell.

A parent that sizes the grid to its content (an items-start Stack, an Inline, a popover) makes it as wide as all its tiles side by side, up to the room it has, because each tile asks for its 128px. Up to `cols` tiles, that keeps them across. More tiles than `cols` still fold to `cols` columns, so each tile is wider than it needs: give that grid a width, such as the row's (`w-full`). A value wider than a tile takes a row of its own where the browser supports `calc-size()` and is clipped elsewhere, so keep values short (see Content).

_Example: story `Stories.SixAcross`._
_Example: story `Stories.InANarrowPanel`._
_Example: story `Stories.SizedToItsContent`._

## States

| State       | What changes                                                                                                                                                 |
| ----------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Neutral     | The number in `color.text`. The default, and most numbers.                                                                                                   |
| Toned       | The number in the tone's text colour, because the number is a status.                                                                                        |
| Zero        | The number in `color.text.subtlest`, whatever the tone: nothing is not a status.                                                                             |
| Loading     | `isLoading`: a heading-sized Skeleton where the number goes, `aria-busy` on the tile and a hidden "Loading" after the label. The label stays; nothing moves. |
| Unavailable | `value={<Absent label="Not available" />}` and a note that says what happened, "Could not load". The tile is not busy.                                       |
| Linked      | `link`: `elevation.surface.hovered` under the pointer, `elevation.surface.pressed` while pressed, the label underlined, the focus ring inside the tile.      |

A tile without a link does not hover, focus or disable. A tile that takes the reader somewhere takes `link`, never a link wrapped around it: the grid sizes its own children, so a wrapping link would stretch past the tile and its ring would be clipped by the frame. A linked tile holds no other control.

_Example: story `Stories.LoadingAndUnavailable`._

## Modifiers

- **`tone`** when the number is a status: overdue in `danger`, verified in `success`, held in `warning`. Most numbers stay neutral, so the one that is a status stands out.
- **`note`** for the one line under the number: what it is out of, the oldest, the next.
- **`cols`** and **`frame`** on the grid: `card` at the top of a record, `band` between sections.

_Example: story `Stories.Frames`._

## Content

_Example: story `Stories.NumbersInTheReadersLocale`._

- **The label is a noun phrase**, under three words when it can be: "Open findings", "Re-tests owed", "Verified".
- **The value is a number**, or a short string that reads as one: "80%", "41/80". Tabular, so a row of tiles aligns. Pass a number as a number: the tile writes it in the reader's locale from the LedgerProvider (1,234 in en-US, 1.234 in de-DE; en-US when there is no provider, never the machine's). A string shows as given.
- **Never a word in the number's place.** Loading is `isLoading`; a number that could not load is an Absent with its reason and a note, not "Loading…", "…" or "Unavailable" in heading type.
- **The note is one line** that qualifies the number: "298 of 372", "Oldest 12 days", "Nothing waiting on you". A note that decomposes a number belongs on the tile that holds the whole, not on a part.
- **Zero's note says what the zero means.** "Nothing waiting on you" is worth more than a muted 0.

## Style

| Element | Token                                                                                                               |
| ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Tile    | `utility.elevation.surface.current` · `space.200` inline · `space.150` block · `space.025` between lines            |
| Value   | `font.heading.page` · tabular · `color.text` / `color.text.<tone>` / `color.text.subtlest` at zero                  |
| Label   | `font.body.small` · `color.text.subtle`                                                                             |
| Note    | `font.body.small` · `color.text.subtle`                                                                             |
| Grid    | `gap-px` painted `color.border` · `card`: `color.border`, `radius.large` · `band`: `color.border` above and below   |
| Link    | `elevation.surface.hovered` · `elevation.surface.pressed` · the focus ring inside the edge · `motion.duration.fast` |
| Trend   | `space.150` from the number                                                                                         |
| Stat    | `space.100` block · `space.050` between value and label                                                             |

A tile paints the surface it sits on, `utility.elevation.surface.current`, so a grid on a card is the card's colour and one in a dialog the dialog's, in both modes.

_Example: story `Stories.OnACard`._

The toned value is Badge's text colour for the tone, so a danger count and a danger Indicator are the same red. In forced colours the grid paints its hairlines in the text colour and each tile sits on the reader's canvas, so the cells stay apart.

## Accessibility

- **Reading order is label then value in a Tile,** so a screen reader hears "Open findings, 17". A bare Stat reads value then label, "17, Open findings", which is how a summary row is scanned.
- **Zero is muted, not disabled.** `color.text.subtlest` still passes the contrast test; the a11y gate runs the zero row of the matrix.
- **The tone is not the only signal.** The label says what the number is, and the note says what it means; the colour ranks it.
- **A grid is a `div`**, not a table or a list: the tiles are read in order and there is nothing to navigate. Name a grid of headline numbers with `role="group"` and `aria-label`.
- **A linked tile is one link** whose name is the label, the number and the note: "Open risks, 4, Oldest 12 days, link". It is one Tab stop, Enter opens it, and its focus ring is drawn inside the tile, where the frame cannot clip it.
- **A loading tile is busy**: `aria-busy` on the tile, the Skeleton hidden and a hidden "Loading" (the locale's `loading`) read after the label. Put `aria-busy` on the grid too while any of its numbers load.

## Props

Stat, Stat.Tile and Stat.Grid forward native `div` props and refs to their outer elements, and name themselves last with `data-slot` (`stat`, `stat-tile`, `stat-grid`; a tile's link is `stat-link`, its trend `stat-trend`). IDs, ARIA, data attributes and events are preserved; `className` merges with each part’s defaults. Styles override the Grid’s default gutter background and accept ordinary sizing on all three parts. With `link`, the ref still reaches the tile; the link element keeps its own props, ref and handlers (`link={<Link to="/risks" search={{ status: "open" }} />}`).

Stat and Stat.Tile keep their configured `label`/`value`/`note` slots. Compose tiles through Stat.Grid’s children. Zero remains muted, and tones, responsive columns and frames retain their existing defaults. Stat.Tile and Stat.Grid are also exported by name, as `StatTile` and `StatGrid`.

_Props of `Stat`, generated from its types:_

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `label` (required) | `string` |  | What the number counts, in small subtle text: "Open findings". |
| `value` (required) | `ReactNode` |  | The number, or a short string such as "80%" or "41/80". A number is written in the reader's locale (1,234 in en-US); a string shows as given. Zero reads muted. |
| `tone` | `"danger" \| "information" \| "neutral" \| "success" \| "warning"` |  | A colour only when the number is a status: overdue in `danger`, verified in `success`. Most numbers stay `neutral`. |
| `isLoading` | `boolean` |  | The number is on its way: a Skeleton holds its place, the part is `aria-busy`, and a screen reader hears "Loading" after the label. The label stays. |
