<!-- page: Components/Stepper (src/stories/components/Stepper.mdx) -->

# Stepper

**Status: Stable.**

Progress through an ordered path: the RMF steps, a program's milestones, a wizard. One step is `current`, the steps behind it are `done`, the ones ahead `upcoming`, and `blocked` is the step that failed. The list knows each step's place and its neighbour's state, so the rail is in the success colour behind every completed step and a hairline ahead.

A path is fixed and has three or more steps. Two steps are a [Badge](?path=/docs/components-badge--docs); a percentage is a [Progress](?path=/docs/components-progress--docs) bar; a set of conditions that are met or not is [Gates](?path=/docs/patterns-gates--docs); events in time are a [Timeline](?path=/docs/components-timeline--docs).

_Example: story `Stories.StepperMatrix`._

## Anatomy

| Part   | What it is                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| ------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Marker | A 16px circle: a check on `color.background.success.bold` when done, a cross on `color.background.danger.bold` when blocked, a `color.border.selected` ring at the selected width when current, a `color.border.bold` ring when upcoming. `numbered` writes the step's number in it.                                    |
| Rail   | The line between markers: `color.border.success` behind a completed step, `color.border` ahead. It stops at the first and last markers.                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| Label  | One or two words, `font.body.small`: semibold in `color.text` when current, medium otherwise, `color.text.subtle` when upcoming, `color.text.danger` when blocked. Under the marker horizontally, beside it vertically. One line: a longer label is cut and shows whole on hover and while its step has keyboard focus. |
| Meta   | Under the label, `font.body.xsmall` in `color.text.subtle`: the date, the owner, why it is blocked. It may wrap.                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| Step   | The marker and its text together, one `li`: a button when the reader can move to it, a plain block when it only reports.                                                                                                                                                                                                |

## Variants

| Variant      | Use                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| ------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `horizontal` | Labels under markers on one line: a record's milestone header, the top of a form.                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `vertical`   | Markers down the start edge with labels beside them: a wizard's rail, a panel. Preferred wherever it fits, because the labels and metas can wrap.                                                                                                                |
| `responsive` | Follows its own container: vertical while the container is narrower than `@md` (`dimension.container.md`, 448px), horizontal from there. A wizard whose path sits in a rail beside the form on a wide screen and above the form on a narrow one.                 |
| `numbered`   | The marker shows the step's number; done and blocked keep their icon: numbers make the order plain on a long path.                                                                                                                                               |
| Interactive  | A step with `onSelect` is a button the reader can move to; a step without one only reports. Mix them: done steps open, the rest do not. While any step takes `onSelect`, the current step is a button too, and activating it runs its own `onSelect` or nothing. |

Not built, and why: a disabled state, because a step the reader cannot reach is `upcoming` without `onSelect`; a skeleton, because the steps are known before the data is.

A vertical step takes `children`: under the label, with the rail running past it, a Collapsible with the owner and the open task, a sentence, a Badge. That is a rail of milestones, where each step carries its record. A wizard's step carries nothing, because its content is the page it opens.

_Example: story `Stories.Milestones`._

## Sizes

One size: the marker 16px, the label `font.body.small`, the meta `font.body.xsmall`. Horizontally each step is one equal column of the list, which is 420px (`dimension.part.steps`) wide at least; give a longer path a wider minimum through `style`. Narrower than that, the strip scrolls inside its container, with an arrow at each edge where a pointer can hover and a swipe on touch. Vertically the list is as wide as its longest label and meta allow, and a step is `space.200` above the next.

_Example: story `Stories.Paths`._

_Example: story `Stories.Narrow`._

`responsive` reads the Stepper's own container, not the window, so the same path turns wherever its container changes width: a rail, a column above a form, a panel. It runs across only from `@md`, where four steps fit without scrolling, so it has no strip and no arrows. Its container sets its width (a grid track, a column), as for any container query: a Stepper whose parent sizes to its content has no width to read.

_Example: story `Stories.Responsive`._

## States

| State      | What changes                                                                                                                                                  |
| ---------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `done`     | The check on the success fill; the rail ahead of it in `color.border.success`; the label medium.                                                              |
| `current`  | The selected ring at the selected width; the label semibold; `aria-current="step"`. The rail behind it is in the success colour when the step before is done. |
| `upcoming` | A `color.border.bold` ring; the label in `color.text.subtle`; a hairline rail.                                                                                |
| `blocked`  | The cross on the danger fill; the label in `color.text.danger`; the meta says why.                                                                            |
| Hover      | On a step with `onSelect`: the label underlines.                                                                                                              |
| Focus      | On a step that is a button: the focus outline around the whole step; in a horizontal strip, which clips, it is drawn inside the step, so all of it shows.     |

## Modifiers

- **`orientation`**, **`numbered`** as in Variants; **`label`**, required, names the list.
- **`meta`** for the date, the owner or the reason under the label. It may wrap; the label does not.
- **`children`** for what a milestone carries under its label. Anything interactive in it is its own stop beside the step's button.
- **`onSelect`** on the steps the reader may move to. On a wizard that is every done step and the next one; on a milestone header, every step, to open the milestone.

## A wizard's rail

A wizard gives `onSelect` to every done step and to the next one. The step the reader activates in the rail becomes current and keeps focus, since the current step stays a button. When the step changes from outside the rail (Continue, Back, a link in the step), the wizard moves focus to the new step's heading, rendered with `tabIndex={-1}`, so a keyboard reader lands on the step they opened and a screen reader hears its name. The Stepper does not move focus itself: where the new step's content starts is the wizard's to say.

_Example: story `Stories.Wizard`._

## Content

- **Labels are one or two words** in sentence case, sixteen characters at most: "Categorize", "Select controls", "MS-C". A noun, or verb and noun. Never "Processing".
- **The meta is a date, a person or a reason**, in the product's date format: "3 Aug", "Priya Natarajan", "Baseline not approved".
- **A blocked step says why** in its meta. The marker alone is a red dot with no story.
- **Numbers on a long path.** Six RMF steps read better as 1 to 6; three steps do not need them.

## Style

| Element | Token                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| ------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Marker  | 16px · `radius.full` · done `color.border.success` on `color.background.success.bold` · blocked `color.border.danger` on `color.background.danger.bold` · current `color.border.selected` at `border.width.selected`, upcoming `color.border.bold`, both on the surface the path sits on (`utility.elevation.surface.current`: the page, a card, a dialog) |
| Number  | `font.body.xsmall` medium · `color.text.selected` when current, `color.text.subtle` when upcoming                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| Rail    | 1px · `color.border.success` behind a done step · `color.border` otherwise                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| Label   | `font.body.small` · current semibold `color.text` · done medium `color.text` · upcoming medium `color.text.subtle` · blocked medium `color.text.danger`                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| Meta    | `font.body.xsmall` · `color.text.subtle` · tabular                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| Spacing | horizontal: label `space.075` under the marker, `space.050` inline · vertical: `space.150` between marker and text, `space.200` under each step                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| Hover   | Label underline on a selectable step                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| Focus   | The focus outline, `radius.medium`, around the step; inside it across                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| Motion  | Marker colours in `motion.duration.fast`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |

Done is green and blocked is red, the product's status tones, because on a milestone header the states are the story and colour carries it alongside the icon. The upcoming ring is `color.border.bold`, 3:1 against the surface, so the path ahead reads as clearly as the path behind.

## Accessibility

- **The list is an ordered list**, `role="list"` so WebKit keeps the role once its markers are removed, and named by `label`; a screen reader hears "RMF steps, list, 6 items" and moves step by step. `label` is required, so no Stepper is an unnamed list.
- **Each step's name starts with its state.** The label is prefixed, visually hidden, with "Completed", "Current", "Not started" or "Blocked", then the label and the meta: "Current: Implement". The drawn number is not read; the list already says "3 of 6".
- **The current step carries `aria-current="step"`**: on its button where the path can be moved along, on its `li` where it only reports.
- **One button per step.** A step that can be moved to is a single button holding its marker and text, so it is one tab stop with one name. A step that only reports is not focusable.
- **Keyboard:** Tab moves between the step buttons, Enter or Space moves to one. Each reachable step is its own stop, not one stop with arrows inside it, which is what a wizard's rail of three or four wants.
- **The strip is a stop only when it must be.** A horizontal Stepper that overflows and holds no step button is one tab stop, a group named after the list ("Authorization steps, scrolls"), so the arrow keys scroll it; a strip that fits, or holds buttons, adds none.
- **Colour is never alone.** Done and blocked have their icon, current its weight and ring, and the words are read. In forced colours the icons, the ring's width and the weight remain.
- **Contrast:** the inverse check and cross pass on their fills; the danger label passes on the surface; the upcoming ring holds 3:1.

## Props

Native `ol` props and refs reach Stepper; native `li` props and refs reach Stepper.Item. IDs, data attributes, styles, classes and events reach those elements. An explicit `aria-label` overrides the root's `label`, and caller styles override the horizontal minimum width. Item's native `title` belongs to the `li`.

`onSelect` is the step's action. Use `onClickCapture` on the item or the list and call `event.preventDefault()` to cancel it before the button runs; a bubble-phase `onClick` runs after the button, in DOM order. The step's state owns `aria-current`.

_Props of `Stepper`, generated from its types:_

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `orientation` | `"horizontal" \| "responsive" \| "vertical"` |  | `horizontal` puts labels under markers on one line, for a header; `vertical` stacks them down the start edge, preferred wherever it fits: a wizard's rail, a panel. `responsive` reads its own container: vertical while it is narrower than `@md` (`dimension.container.md`, 448px), horizontal from there, for a wizard whose path sits in a rail beside the form on a wide screen and above it on a narrow one. |
| `numbered` | `boolean` |  | Markers show the step's number in place of the dot; done and blocked keep their icon: numbers make the order plain. The number is drawn, not read: the list already says "3 of 6". |
| `label` (required) | `string` |  | The list's accessible name, required so the path is never an unnamed list: "RMF steps", "Program setup". An `aria-label` overrides it. |

### Stepper.Item

_Props of `Stepper.Item`, generated from its types:_

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `state` (required) | `"blocked" \| "current" \| "done" \| "upcoming"` |  | `done`, `current`, `upcoming`, or `blocked` for the step that failed. |
| `label` (required) | `ReactNode` |  | One or two words, sentence case: "Categorize", "Select controls". Sixteen characters at most. A longer label is cut to one line and shows whole on hover and while its step has keyboard focus. |
| `meta` | `ReactNode` |  | Helper text under the label: a date, who has it, why it is blocked. It may wrap. |
| `onSelect` | `(() => void)` |  | Makes the step a button the reader can move to. Without it the step only reports, except the current step of a list where some step takes `onSelect`: it stays a button, which does nothing. |

### Playground

_Example: story `Stories.Playground`._

_Rendered in the Storybook: Controls._

## Related

- [Progress](?path=/docs/components-progress--docs): how much, as a bar.
- [Gates](?path=/docs/patterns-gates--docs): conditions met or not, in no order.
- [Timeline](?path=/docs/components-timeline--docs): what happened, in order, with no fixed end.
- [Tabs](?path=/docs/components-tabs--docs): sections the reader may take in any order.

## Don't

A Stepper is three or more steps in a fixed order, each one or two words with its date or owner under it, vertical in a rail, and a blocked step says why on itself. Two states are a Badge, never a path.

_Example: story `Stories.Dont`._

<!-- page: Components/Switch (src/stories/components/Switch.mdx) -->

# Switch

**Status: Stable.**

An on/off setting that takes effect the moment it moves, on Base UI with the shadcn composition. The thumb is included; the setting's label and hint come from a horizontal [Field](?path=/docs/components-field--docs), which ties them to the switch with no ids and centres the switch on the label's first line.

```tsx
<Field orientation="horizontal">
  <Switch checked={notify} onCheckedChange={setNotify} />
  <FieldContent>
    <FieldLabel>Notify the owner</FieldLabel>
    <FieldDescription>Email the owner when a finding changes status.</FieldDescription>
  </FieldContent>
</Field>
```

_Example: story `Stories.SwitchMatrix`._

## When to use it

- **Use a Switch** for a setting that applies at once: notifications, a digest, a display preference. The change saves itself and a status says so; there is no Save button.
- **Not for a choice that waits for a form's primary.** Inside a form that is submitted together, the answer is a [Checkbox](?path=/docs/components-checkbox--docs).
- **Not for one of several options.** That is a [RadioGroup](?path=/docs/components-radiogroup--docs), even when there are two.
- **Not for a fact.** A setting the reader cannot change is a labelled property ([KeyValue](?path=/docs/components-keyvalue--docs)), or a read-only switch with a hint that says why; never a disabled switch left to explain itself.

The [Forms](?path=/docs/patterns-forms--docs) page has the table of which control answers which question.

_Example: story `Stories.Settings`._

A switch inside a form that waits for Save looks applied before it is: there the answer is a Checkbox.

_Example: story `Stories.DoDont`._

## Sizes and state

| Size     | Track     | Thumb |
| -------- | --------- | ----- |
| `medium` | 32 × 20px | 16px  |
| `small`  | 24 × 16px | 12px  |

`medium` is the default; `small` fits a dense row. `sm` and `default` are the shadcn spellings of `small` and `medium`, deprecated and still rendered the same. The thumb moves toward the inline end when checked, follows the locale's direction, and stops animating when reduced motion is requested.

Use `defaultChecked` for local state or `checked` and `onCheckedChange(checked, details)` for controlled state. `details.cancel()` rejects a change. `disabled` blocks activation and removes the switch from the tab order; `readOnly` keeps it focusable while preventing changes. A read-only switch that is on takes the neutral fill instead of the brand one, and its hint says why it cannot change.

## Labels, Field and forms

In a Field the FieldLabel names the setting and toggles it when clicked, the FieldDescription and FieldError describe it, and the Field's `invalid`, `required` and `disabled` reach it, with no ids. Outside a Field, a wrapping `<label>` or a sibling `<label htmlFor={id}>` names it. A FieldSet's `disabled` disables the switches inside it.

_Example: story `Stories.BoundInField`._

`name`, `value`, `uncheckedValue`, `form` and `required` configure the hidden checkbox used for native submission and validation, for a settings page that also posts its state. Without `uncheckedValue`, an unchecked switch contributes no entry. `aria-required` (or the Field's `required`) describes the requirement; use Switch's native `required` when browser and Base UI validation are intended. Native form reset is caller-owned in Base UI 1.7: restore controlled `checked` state in the form's `onReset` handler.

_Example: story `Stories.NativeForm`._

## Content

- **Name the setting, not its state.** The label stays the same on and off ("Notify the owner"); the thumb shows the state.
- **Say what "on" does**, in the positive: "Weekly digest", not "Turn off the weekly digest".
- **Do not disable a switch to show a fact** (see When to use it).

## Accessibility

- The off track is `color.background.input.track`, 3:1 against every surface, with the thumb at 3:1 on it, so an off switch reads as a control and not a faint pill (WCAG 1.4.11). It is not `color.background.neutral`, the fill buttons and badges share. The thumb follows the Ledger colour tokens even without the optional `base.css` document defaults.
- An invalid switch draws the danger outline while it is not focused; keyboard focus replaces it with the focus outline, so focus stays visible.
- In forced colours, system-colour boundaries and contrasting thumbs keep both states visible.
- Every switch needs a visible label, `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`.

_Example: story `Stories.Boundary`._

## Native props and composition

The default visible root is a `<span role="switch">`, with a hidden checkbox beside it. `ref` targets the visible root; `inputRef` and `id` target the hidden input. Native event handlers and state-based `className`/`style` callbacks apply to the root.

For a native button root, pass `nativeButton` and `render={<button />}`. In that mode `id` targets the button, and refs and event handlers merge with those on the rendered element.

_Example: story `Stories.InRows`._

## Props

_Props of `Switch`, generated from its types:_

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | `string` |  | The id of the hidden input element. When `nativeButton` is `true`, the id is applied to the root element. |
| `checked` | `boolean` |  | Whether the switch is currently active. To render an uncontrolled switch, use the `defaultChecked` prop instead. |
| `defaultChecked` | `boolean` | `false` | Whether the switch is initially active. To render a controlled switch, use the `checked` prop instead. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | Whether the component should ignore user interaction. |
| `inputRef` | `Ref<HTMLInputElement>` |  | A ref to access the hidden `<input>` element. |
| `name` | `string` |  | Identifies the field when a form is submitted. |
| `form` | `string` |  | Identifies the form that owns the hidden input. Useful when the switch is rendered outside the form. |
| `onCheckedChange` | `((checked: boolean, eventDetails: { reason: "none"; event: Event; cancel: () => void; allowPropagation: () => void; isCanceled: boolean; isPropagationAllowed: boolean; trigger: Element; }) => void)` |  | Event handler called when the switch is activated or deactivated. |
| `readOnly` | `boolean` | `false` | Whether the user should be unable to activate or deactivate the switch. |
| `required` | `boolean` | `false` | Whether the user must activate the switch before submitting a form. |
| `value` | `string` |  | The value submitted with the form when the switch is on. By default, switch submits the "on" value, matching native checkbox behavior. |
| `uncheckedValue` | `string` |  | The value submitted with the form when the switch is off. By default, unchecked switches do not submit any value, matching native checkbox behavior. |
| `nativeButton` | `boolean` | `true` | Whether the component renders a native `<button>` element when replacing it via the `render` prop. Set to `false` if the rendered element is not a button (for example, `<div>`). |
| `className` | `string \| ((state: SwitchRootState) => string)` |  | CSS class applied to the element, or a function that returns a class based on the component's state. |
| `style` | `CSSProperties \| ((state: SwitchRootState) => CSSProperties)` |  | Style applied to the element, or a function that returns a style object based on the component's state. |
| `render` | `ReactElement<unknown, string \| JSXElementConstructor<any>> \| ComponentRenderFn<HTMLProps, SwitchRootState>` |  | Allows you to replace the component's HTML element with a different tag, or compose it with another component. Accepts a `ReactElement` or a function that returns the element to render. |
| `size` | `"default" \| "medium" \| "sm" \| "small"` | `medium` | `medium` (32 × 20px) by default; `small` (24 × 16px) in a dense row. `sm` and `default` are the deprecated spellings of `small` and `medium`. |

_Example: story `Stories.Playground`._

_Rendered in the Storybook: Controls._

# Table

**Status: Stable.**

The register, by hand: a header row, a row per record, a hairline between them. `Table` is the markup and its parts; it sorts, pages or selects only when the caller wires the state. A table with state to keep, sort, filters, pages, selection, pinned columns, nested or reordered rows, is a [DataTable](?path=/docs/patterns-data-table--docs), which draws these same parts from a TanStack instance. No route sorts, filters or pages by hand.

A few facts about one thing are a [KeyValue](?path=/docs/components-keyvalue--docs), not a two-column table; a list with one line per record is an [Item](?path=/docs/components-item--docs) list; a hierarchy without columns is a [Tree](?path=/docs/components-tree--docs).

_Example: story `Stories.TableMatrix`._

## Anatomy

| Part       | What it is                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| ---------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Frame      | The wrapper that scrolls: sideways always, and down past `maxHeight`, so the header sticks to it and not to the page. While it is scrolled sideways it carries `data-scrolled-start` and `data-scrolled-end`, and the pinned column at the edge shows its border. Its scroll padding covers the pinned columns and the sticky header, so the keyboard's focus is scrolled clear of them. |
| Header     | `Table.Header`: `dimension.row.header` 32px, sticky at the top of the frame, `font.body.small` at `font.weight.medium` in `color.text.subtle` on the current surface, a hairline under. Sortable, it holds a button that reports `aria-sort` and shows the arrow. A heading in a second header row sticks below the row above it.                                                        |
| Row        | `Table.Row`: the record, `dimension.row` 40px with a hairline under. It lights on hover and paints `color.background.selected` when chosen; `isStatic` for a row that is not a record.                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| Cell       | `Table.Cell`: `space.150` each side, one line, truncated; a cut value shows whole in the table's one tooltip, on hover, on keyboard focus and after a long press. `align` places its content, `wrap` lets it wrap, and `rowHeader` makes it the `th` that names its row.                                                                                                                 |
| Id         | `Table.Id`: the id in `Id`, `color.text.brand` on the row's hover, with the eye at the end of the cell that opens the record in the preview, named after the id: "Preview CTRL-0412". The id keeps clear of the eye, so it ends in an ellipsis before the eye, never under it.                                                                                                           |
| Name       | `Table.Name`: a record's name with what tells it apart at a glance: the kind's icon before it, one Badge after it, a second line under it in `font.body.small` `color.text.subtle`. The name is cut first and the badge keeps its width; the second line is cut on its own. DataTable's `c.text` and `c.id` draw it from their `icon`, `badge` and `description`.                        |
| List       | `Table.List`: several values on one line, the first by name and the rest as a count ("+2", spoken "and 2 more"), every one in a hover card with its meta line and status. The line is a button: its click is the row's preview when it has one, else it opens the card, so the list is reachable where any pointer is coarse. The whole list is its description.                         |
| Selection  | `Table.Selection`: the checkbox column, 32px; in the header it chooses every row and reads mixed when only some are. A click anywhere in the cell toggles the box.                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| Group      | `Table.Group`: a band on the sunken surface with a chevron, a title and a Count, holding its rows in a `tbody`. The band is its rows' header, `th scope="rowgroup"`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| Tree cell  | `Table.Tree`: the name cell of a hierarchy with columns, one `space.200` indent per level, the chevron on rows with children, a hint after the name.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| Disclosure | `Table.Disclosure`: the chevron as a leading cell of its own, centred, one narrow column whatever the depth. The disclosure is always the first column, never moves when a column is reordered, hidden or pinned, and never changes width as rows open and close; the indent belongs to the row's first value. What DataTable draws in tree mode.                                        |
| Detail row | `Table.Detail`: the row a record opens into, one cell across every column on the sunken surface.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| Handle     | `Table.Handle`: the grip cell of a row that drags into a new order.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |

## Variants

Table has one appearance. What varies is the parts a register takes:

| The register                                          | Use                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| ----------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Names that need the kind, a mark or a second line     | `Table.Name` in the name's cell: an icon, one Badge, a muted second line. Never an Inline or a Stack built by hand in the cell.                                                                                        |
| Records with nothing to sort, filter or page          | `Table` with `Table.Header`, `Table.Row`, `Table.Cell` and `Table.Id`; the id or the name is the row header, and the name is the link to the record.                                                                   |
| Rows the reader chooses for a batch action            | `Table.Selection` in the header and in each row; the bar above names the count and the verbs.                                                                                                                          |
| Records under headings                                | `Table.Group`, one per heading, opened and closed.                                                                                                                                                                     |
| A hierarchy with columns                              | A plain table with `Table.Disclosure` as the leading cell (or `Table.Tree` as the name cell); the caller flattens and folds, and Tab reaches each chevron. DataTable's tree mode is the treegrid, with the arrow keys. |
| A record that opens into more                         | `Table.Detail` under its row, a chevron in the row.                                                                                                                                                                    |
| Rows in an order the reader sets                      | `Table.Handle` as the first cell.                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| Sort, filters, pages, pinned columns, a thousand rows | `DataTable`.                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| A few facts about one thing                           | `KeyValue`.                                                                                                                                                                                                            |

_Example: story `Stories.RegisterStory`._

A row's click follows a link that is also in the row, the record's name, and is never the only way to open the record: a keyboard, a screen reader, a middle click and a copied link all use the link. The checkbox and the eye keep their clicks from the row. A Toolbar above the table keeps `space.200` from it, so the sticky header never covers the toolbar's focus rings.

There is no zebra striping: the hairline and the row's hover carry the eye across, and stripes fight the selected and the sunken surfaces. There is no radio selection of one row: the row's click opens the record, and one chosen row is that click. There is no expand-all chevron: a detail row loads what it needs when it opens, and opening every row at once gives that up.

## Sizes

Rows are `dimension.row` 40px, and the header `dimension.row.header` 32px. A table's `density` sets its own rows: `compact` resolves them to `dimension.row.compact` 36px, for a picker's table by design or a register the reader has set so. It is a table's setting, never the document's, so two tables on a page each keep their own; a DataTable offers the reader Compact rows in its Columns menu. See [Density](?path=/docs/components-density--docs).

Column widths are content. `width` in pixels on the header fixes a column (on the cells, in a table with no header row); one column takes the slack. `minWidth` gives a column a floor instead: give the name column one, 180 to 220, so in a narrow frame the table scrolls sideways under the pinned columns rather than squeezing the name to a sliver. The frame scrolls sideways when the columns are wider than the page, and a pinned column keeps its place.

_Example: story `Stories.FrameStory`._

_Example: story `Stories.RegisterPhone`._

## States

| State              | What changes                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| ------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Header, sortable   | The up-down chevron appears on hover and on focus, and stays where any pointer is coarse unless a column menu that sorts sits beside it; the text turns `color.text`.                                      |
| Sorted             | The arrow up or down stays and the text is `color.text`; `aria-sort` says which. An end-aligned heading leads with its arrow.                                                                              |
| Row hover          | `color.background.surface.hovered`; the id turns `color.text.brand`; the eye appears in `color.icon.subtle`. Where any pointer is coarse, the eye is always there.                                         |
| Selected           | `color.background.selected`, `color.background.selected.hovered` on hover, pinned cells included; `data-selected` on the row. In forced colours, a Highlight edge inside the row.                          |
| Active id          | The id in `color.text.brand` and the eye on `color.background.selected` inside a `color.border.selected` ring, `aria-pressed`: the row open in the preview. The ring tells it apart where every eye shows. |
| Static             | No hover, pinned cells included: a totals row, a form laid out as a table.                                                                                                                                 |
| Scrolled           | The frame carries `data-scrolled-start` or `-end`; a pinned column with `edge="scrolled"` draws its `color.border` edge only then.                                                                         |
| Group open, closed | The chevron turns and `aria-expanded` follows; closed, the rows are not rendered. The chevron's name stays the group's title.                                                                              |
| Expanded           | The chevron turns and its name says the next action and the row, "Collapse Ground segment"; the folded count goes. In DataTable's treegrid the row carries `aria-expanded`.                                |
| Disabled selection | The checkbox disabled; the row still opens.                                                                                                                                                                |

Loading, empty and error belong to the DataTable, which keeps the header and draws skeleton rows, an Empty or the error inside the frame. A bare Table shows what it is given: an empty register is an [Empty](?path=/docs/components-empty--docs) in its Section, not a table with no rows.

## Modifiers

- **`label`** names the table when no heading above does. A DataTable takes the same.
- **`maxHeight`** makes the frame scroll down inside itself; the header sticks to the frame.
- **`fill`** makes the frame take the rest of a bounded flex column and scroll inside it, the companion of Stack's `grow="fill"`; the DataTable's `fill` builds that column.
- **`density`** on the table: `compact` for 36px rows.
- **`align`** on a header and its column's cells: `start` (the default), `center` for a column-group heading, `end` for a number, which the cell draws in tabular numerals and the heading ends over. It is logical, so a right-to-left table mirrors it.
- **`wrap`** on a cell or a header, for a value that must be read whole: it wraps instead of ending in an ellipsis. A hash or a URN inside it is an `Id` with `break-all`, so it breaks anywhere.
- **`rowHeader`** on the one cell or `Table.Id` that names the row, the id or the name: it renders `th scope="row"`, drawn as a cell. A plain table says it on each row; DataTable draws its identity column so by itself.
- **`sort` and `onSort`** on a header. `useSort` gives a plain table `dir(key)` and `toggle(key)`; `usePage` with [TablePagination](?path=/docs/components-pagination--docs) pages it.
- **`sticky`, `pinned`, `offset`, `edge`** on a header and its cells: `pinned="start"` or `"end"`, `offset` the widths of the pinned columns before it, `edge` on the one that touches the middle, `true` for its edge at rest and `"scrolled"` for the edge only while the frame is scrolled. `sticky` is `pinned="start"` with no offset.
- **`width`** in pixels on the header, or on the cells of a table with no header row; **`minWidth`** for a floor the column keeps while it takes the slack above it.
- **`resize` and `trailing`** on a header are the DataTable's: a handle on the trailing edge, named after the column, and a control that shows on hover and focus, and always, beside the heading, where any pointer is coarse; there a DataTable that scrolls sideways draws the column 24px wider for each 20px control (less the 2px between two), so the heading keeps its room, and a responsive one keeps the author's width, so no column folds for it: the heading gives way and shows whole on hover and focus. An end-aligned heading keeps them at its start. By hand only in a header the DataTable cannot draw.
- **`isSelected` and `isStatic`** on a row.
- **`expanded` and `onExpandedChange`** on `Table.Group`, `Table.Tree` and `Table.Disclosure`: whether the rows under it show, and the call its chevron makes with the next state, the same pair [Tree](?path=/docs/components-tree--docs)'s items take (`isExpanded` there, beside `isSelected`). Table.Group's `open` and every part's `onToggle` are the deprecated names, still read for one version.
- **`tone="subtle"`** on `Table.Id` where the id is not the link, in a grouped listing; `onPreview` and `isActive` for the eye, and `label` for its name when the id is not a plain string.

`useSort` reads each sortable column through a function that returns the raw value: an ISO day or instant, a number, a Date or the text, never the label the cell formats, so 2 September sorts before 14 September. Text collates in the LedgerProvider's locale with numbers inside it read as numbers, and an absent value (`null`, `undefined`, `""`) sorts last in either direction. `usePage` clamps its page when the list shrinks.

_Example: story `Stories.SortedAndPaged`._

_Example: story `Stories.Groups`._

_Example: story `Stories.TreeStory`._

_Example: story `Stories.RichNamesStory`._

_Example: story `Stories.ListLineStory`._

_Example: story `Stories.TwoHeaderRows`._

_Example: story `Stories.ResizeHandles`._

_Example: story `Stories.WrapAndTitles`._

_Example: story `Stories.RightToLeft`._

## Content

- **Headers are one or two words**, sentence case, no trailing colon, no units when the cells carry them: Due, not "Due date:". A header that would wrap is a shorter word.
- **The id first, the name second, actions last.**
- **Text starts; a number ends**, in tabular numerals, and so does its header: `align="end"` on both. A number never centres.
- **A status is a Badge, a severity an Indicator, a person a Person**; a date is a [DateTime](?path=/docs/components-datetime--docs), in the reader's locale.
- **An absent value is `Absent`**, never a blank, a dash typed by hand or "N/A".
- **Cells hold one line.** A column that must wrap wraps as a column (`wrap`), and it is never the one sorted by eye. Long prose lives on the record.
- **The register is named** by the Section above it, or by `label`.

## Style

| Element     | Token                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| ----------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Frame       | full width · scrolls sideways · scrolls down past `maxHeight` or, with `fill`, inside the height its column gives it · scroll padding the width of the pinned columns and the height of the header                                                                                                                                       |
| Table       | `font.body` · tabular numerals throughout                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| Header      | `dimension.row.header` 32px · `font.body.small` `font.weight.medium` `color.text.subtle` · `elevation.surface.current` · `color.border` under, the cell's own so it stays while the frame scrolls · `space.150` sides                                                                                                                    |
| Sort button | `dimension.control.xsmall`, its least height when the heading wraps · `radius.small` · arrow 12px · hover `color.text` · `space.050` ring room on the side away from the column's text                                                                                                                                                   |
| Row         | `dimension.row` 40px, `dimension.row.compact` 36px · `color.border` hairline · hover `color.background.surface.hovered`                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| Selected    | `color.background.selected` · hover `color.background.selected.hovered`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| Cell        | `space.150` sides · `font.body` · one line, truncated · a link in it cut to the cell, its focus ring inside its edge                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| Id          | `Id` · hover and active `color.text.brand` · the eye `dimension.icon.small` in a 20px button over the cell's end, revealed on the row's hover, active on `color.background.selected` in a `color.border.selected` ring · `space.300` kept clear for it: always in a table laid out by its content, while it shows in a `table-fixed` one |
| Group band  | `elevation.surface.sunken` · `font.body` `font.weight.medium` · `space.100` × `space.075` · hover `color.background.surface.hovered`                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| Detail row  | `elevation.surface.sunken` · `space.200` × `space.150`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| Tree indent | `space.200` 16px per level · a 20px chevron button                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| Resize      | an 8px handle on the heading's end · a `color.background.brand.bold` guide on hover, focus and drag · the focus ring inside the handle                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| Touch       | The eye and the chevrons are `IconButton size="xxsmall"`, the kit's 20px row control, and the handle is 20px; each takes a 24px hit area wherever a pointer is coarse (`touch-target`); the layout does not move. A checkbox's hit area is 40 × 32px, in the header as in a row: the heading's ellipsis does not clip it                 |
| Pinned edge | `color.border`: at rest with `edge`, only while the frame is scrolled with `edge="scrolled"`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| Motion      | `motion.duration.fast` on the row's colours and the chevrons' turn; none under reduced motion                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |

## Accessibility

- **It is a table**: `table`, `thead`, `tbody`, `th`, `td`. `role="treegrid"` is DataTable's tree mode, which wires the arrow keys; `grid` only when cells are editable, which is the DataTable's editing mode. A hierarchy drawn by hand is a plain table, not a treegrid: a treegrid without its arrow keys is worse than none.
- **The name.** `label` sets `aria-label` when no heading names the table.
- **Row headers.** One cell per row, the id or the name, is `rowHeader`, so a screen reader announces the row's identity with every other cell and control in it. A group's band is its rows' `th scope="rowgroup"`.
- **Sorting.** The header's button reports `aria-sort`; Space or Enter sorts; the chevron shows on hover and on focus, so a keyboard user sees which headers sort. On a pointer that can hover there is no persistent sign that a table sorts, which is why the chevron follows focus; where any pointer is coarse it is always shown, unless the column's menu, which sorts, is beside it.
- **Keyboard.** Tab moves through the interactive elements in reading order: sort buttons, checkboxes, the eye, chevrons, links. That is enough for a table; only a treegrid takes arrow keys, and only DataTable's tree mode is one. A focused control is scrolled clear of the pinned columns and the sticky header.
- **Selection is a checkbox with a name**: "Select CTRL-0412", and the header's "Select all". The row's click opens the record and does not select; a click beside the box in its cell selects and does not open.
- **Every control is named.** The eye is "Preview CTRL-0412", after the row, and the table's one tooltip says "Preview" over it, so a row mounts no tooltip of its own; the chevrons say what they do in their names and carry none. The group's chevron is named by its title and `aria-expanded` says whether it is open; the tree's names its row and its action, "Expand Ground segment"; a detail row's chevron carries `aria-controls`; a resize handle is named after its column, "Resize Control".
- **A list line is a button** with the whole list as its description: each item, its meta and status, and the note, so the card is not the only way to them. "+2" is spoken "and 2 more". The lines share the table's one card: each opens it with its own list, so a closed card costs a row nothing, and a line whose row is open shows none.
- **A cut value shows whole for every reader.** The table holds one tooltip for its cells: a value its column cuts shows whole in it while the pointer rests on the cell, while the keyboard is on the cell or a link in it (a record's name), and after a long press on a touch screen, which then opens nothing. Only the cut parts show (a name, then its second line, a status Badge's words); a value that fits shows nothing more, and no cell carries a `title`. A one-line [Truncate](?path=/docs/components-truncate--docs) in a cell that truncates is the table's to show, so it mounts no tooltip of its own. The table sets one writing direction for its popups rather than one per popup. The tooltip is a visual copy of words the cell already holds, hidden from assistive technology; the pointer can move onto it and Escape closes it, going no further, except in a field, whose Escape stays its own. A cut heading shows whole the same way, on hover and while its sort button has focus. A value that must be read whole wraps.
- **Not colour alone.** Hover and selection have the checkbox and the id's colour beside the fill; the open row's eye has its ring; the sort has its arrow and `aria-sort`; the header text at `color.text.subtle` passes 4.5:1. In forced colours a chosen row keeps a Highlight edge and the open row's eye a Highlight fill.

## Props

Table, Table.Header, Table.Row and Table.Cell accept native element props and refs. Table's ref targets the table; frameRef targets its scroll container and supports React 19 callback cleanup. The frame tracks size changes in both itself and its table, so keyboard scroll access, pinned edges and the scroll padding update when content grows or shrinks.

_Example: story `Stories.DynamicFrame`._

_Example: story `Stories.FillFrame`._

## Related

- [DataTable](?path=/docs/patterns-data-table--docs): the same parts with their state; where a register sorts, filters, pages or chooses.
- [Toolbar](?path=/docs/patterns-toolbar--docs) above, [Pagination](?path=/docs/components-pagination--docs) below, [FilterChip](?path=/docs/components-filterchip--docs) in the toolbar.

- [Empty](?path=/docs/components-empty--docs): a register with nothing in it.

## Don't

Numbers end, in tabular numerals, and so does their header (`align="end"` on both), never centred. Selection is the checkbox column, never a row painted selected by its click, and an absent value is Absent, never a typed dash or N/A.

_Example: story `Stories.Dont`._

Native contracts follow [shadcn Table](https://github.com/shadcn-ui/ui/blob/main/apps/v4/registry/bases/base/ui/table.tsx); Ledger retains its register behavior.

# Tabs

**Status: Stable.**

Related views within one page, using [shadcn's Base UI Tabs](https://ui.shadcn.com/docs/components/base/tabs) and [Base UI Tabs](https://base-ui.com/react/components/tabs).

## When to use it

- **Views of one record or one page** that the reader moves between, each filling the panel: a record's Overview, Controls, Evidence and History.
- **A collection per view**, each a register of its own, with its count in the tab.

Not for narrowing the rows the reader is already in (All, Open, Closed): that is a [ToggleGroup](?path=/docs/components-togglegroup--docs), a filter or a saved view in the [Toolbar](?path=/docs/patterns-toolbar--docs). Not for steps taken in order: that is a [Stepper](?path=/docs/components-stepper--docs). Not for sections read down the page: those are [Sections](?path=/docs/layout-section--docs), or a [Collapsible](?path=/docs/components-collapsible--docs) for one the reader opens. Not for moving between the product's pages: that is the Shell's side nav.

**At most about seven primary tabs.** Each tab is a view a reader comes back to. Beyond about seven, group or fold: the strip scrolls rather than folding the rest into a menu, so the reader no longer sees every view at once and hunts for one. Merge views that hold the same kind of work into one tab under Section headings, fold a view read rarely into the Overview (its Details, or a section such as the record's activity), and fold a view with little of its own into the view it belongs with. A strip never wraps onto a second row.

## Content

- A tab is one or two words, a noun in sentence case that names what its panel shows ("Controls", "Evidence", "Activity"). Never a verb, and never the word tab.
- The tabs on a strip name views of the same thing, in the order the reader works through them, Overview first where there is one.
- A count after the label says how many records the panel holds: a [Count](?path=/docs/components-count--docs) with `max={9999}`, the one cap on every strip in a product, never a number written into the words. It shows `0` once the rows have loaded, and no count while they load or after they failed: a count is never a guess.
- A state after the label is a [Badge](?path=/docs/components-badge--docs) ("Draft"); an icon is decoration, never the only name.

## Anatomy

Compose `Tabs`, `TabsList`, `TabsTrigger` and `TabsContent`. Match each Trigger's `value` to its Content. Put counts, badges and icons in the Trigger's children: a count is a [Count](?path=/docs/components-count--docs) after the label, `max={9999}` (Content), and a state is a Badge. Name the List with `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`.

```tsx
<Tabs defaultValue="controls">
  <TabsList variant="line" activateOnFocus aria-label="Record views">
    <TabsTrigger value="controls">
      Controls <Count value={340} max={9999} />
    </TabsTrigger>
    <TabsTrigger value="history">History</TabsTrigger>
  </TabsList>
  <TabsContent value="controls">Control register</TabsContent>
  <TabsContent value="history">Change history</TabsContent>
</Tabs>
```

Routes compose Tabs, TabsList and TabsContent directly; route state controls the selected value. Supporting context can be contributed separately with Shell.Aside.

## Variants

`TabsList` supports shadcn's `default` filled strip and `line` underline. Ledger retains its color, spacing and focus tokens; line tabs remain 32px tall on a border, with a 2px brand underline. One Base UI Indicator follows the selected tab, sliding and resizing over the moderate motion duration (240ms). The filled strip moves its selected chip in the same way: the chip is outlined in `color.border.selected`, 3:1 against the track in both modes, since its fill alone is about 1.1:1. Horizontal line tabs fill the available width and align to the start. Their border continues across the container even when only a few tabs exist, and each tab's hit area reaches half way across the gap to its neighbour, so a click between two labels chooses the nearer tab.

Horizontal tabs, filled or line, use the kit's `ScrollArea` and horizontal `ScrollBar` inside a horizontal [Scroller](?path=/docs/components-scroller--docs), whose click arrows mark the overflowed edge for pointer readers and replace the scrollbar while they show; touch readers swipe with the bar. They stay on one row at every container width, including narrow preview panels. Touch, trackpad, scrollbar dragging and arrow-key focus can reach the overflowed tabs, and the Scroller reveals the focused tab clear of its arrows. The selected tab stays in view as the strip narrows, and as counts arrive after the first layout until the reader scrolls the strip; a tab chosen from outside the strip scrolls into view. Do not add `flex-wrap`, an overflow utility or another scroller to `TabsList`. Size the `Tabs` container when a bounded example is needed; the List handles its own width and scrolling.

The default filled strip fits its content and scrolls, from its start, in a container narrower than its tabs. Record pages and previews explicitly use `variant="line"`; `activateOnFocus` remains an independent choice. Vertical lists retain their vertical layout and do not receive a horizontal scroller. The exported `tabsListVariants` recipe supplies list styling; the `TabsList` component also supplies the horizontal scrolling composition.

_Example: story `Stories.Variants`._

_Example: story `Stories.ResponsiveWidths`._

_Example: story `Stories.LateCountsOnAPhone`._

Under a horizontal strip, filled or line, the panel's content starts `space.150` (12px) below the strip's edge. TabsContent carries that space as its own top padding, so it is the same on every screen and stays with the panel wherever the strip sits. Do not add padding, a margin or a gap to Tabs or TabsContent for it, and do not set `display: contents` on either, which drops the panel's entrance. Beside a vertical strip, Tabs puts `space.100` between the strip and the panel.

Set `orientation="vertical"` on Tabs for a vertical strip and Up/Down navigation. Direction follows LedgerProvider; `dir="ltr"` or `dir="rtl"` overrides both layout and keyboard direction.

_Example: story `Stories.Orientation`._

## Accessibility

Base UI owns the tablist, tab and tabpanel roles, selection, focus and panel associations. Keep a panel for the selected tab. Each strip is one Tab stop; arrows move within it and Home/End reach the ends. Focus wraps unless `loopFocus={false}` is set on the List. A horizontal strip clips, so a focused tab draws its ring inside itself; a vertical strip draws it outside, as other controls do.

Activation is **manual by default**: arrows move focus, then Enter or Space selects. `activateOnFocus` on the List selects as focus moves; use it when the panel can appear immediately. Disabled tabs remain arrow-focusable in the installed Base UI 1.7 contract and cannot activate.

A navigation tab uses `nativeButton={false}` and `render={<Link ... />}` or an anchor. It keeps its href and native modified-click navigation while receiving the tab role. The caller owns synchronization between route state and the controlled value.

_Example: story `Stories.Links`._

Inactive panels unmount by default. `keepMounted` retains their state; hidden panels remain hidden even with a display class, and Base UI makes their controls inert. The arriving panel fades from 0.65 opacity and rises 4px over the medium duration (150ms). The outgoing panel hides immediately so two views never occupy layout together. A controlled route that reuses one panel with a changing value replays its entrance without remounting children or resetting retained input state.

Reduced motion disables both indicator movement and panel entrance. The Motion story samples rendered frames for filled, line, RTL, vertical and reused-panel examples; the dark test project uses reduced motion. Keyboard, link and retained-state stories run in both color modes.

_Example: story `Stories.Motion`._

The indicator's position and size round to the layout unit (1/64px). A resize of the strip's container that leaves the tabs where they were, such as a record's Details rail leaving with its Overview, then writes the same values, so the slide runs once and arrives in its 240ms rather than starting over on every frame of the resize.

_Example: story `Stories.ResizeDuringChange`._

In forced-colors mode, system-color outlines and underlines preserve the selected tab in both variants.

## Props

The four parts expose their corresponding Base UI props, native refs, `render`, events, and state-based `className`/`style`. `TabsList` props and its ref still target the element with `role="tablist"`, inside the horizontal scroller. The scroller adds no separate Tab stop; keyboard users enter the tablist and arrows or Home/End reveal the focused tab. Public types are `TabsProps`, `TabsListProps`, `TabsTriggerProps` and `TabsContentProps`.

Root accepts `value`/`onValueChange` or `defaultValue`, including numeric values; `null` means no selection. `onValueChange(value, details)` can cancel user activation with `details.cancel()`. Uncontrolled selection falls back when a selected tab disappears or becomes disabled; those automatic notifications are not cancellable. For predictable server rendering, give an explicit enabled initial value.

_Example: story `Stories.EditingAndMounting`._

_Props of `Tabs`, generated from its types:_

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `value` | `any` |  | The value of the currently active `Tab`. Use when the component is controlled. When the value is `null`, no Tab will be active. |
| `defaultValue` | `any` | `0` | The default value. Use when the component is not controlled. When the value is `null`, no Tab will be active. |
| `orientation` | `"horizontal" \| "vertical"` | `horizontal` | The component orientation (layout flow direction). |
| `onValueChange` | `((value: any, eventDetails: TabsRootChangeEventDetails) => void)` |  | Callback invoked when new value is being set. The event `reason` is `'none'` for user-initiated changes, such as a click or keyboard navigation; `'initial'` for the first automatic selection or fallback in uncontrolled roots when `defaultValue` is omitted or `undefined`, including when the implicit initial value is disabled or missing; `'disabled'` for automatic fallback when the selected tab becomes disabled in uncontrolled roots; or `'missing'` for automatic fallback when the selected tab is removed, or when an explicit `defaultValue` never matches a mounted tab in uncontrolled roots. For automatic changes, the selected value can be `null` when no enabled Tab is available as a fallback. Automatic changes cannot be canceled; calling `eventDetails.cancel()` for `'initial'`, `'disabled'`, or `'missing'` has no effect. |
| `className` | `string \| ((state: TabsRootState) => string)` |  | CSS class applied to the element, or a function that returns a class based on the component's state. |
| `render` | `ReactElement<unknown, string \| JSXElementConstructor<any>> \| ComponentRenderFn<HTMLProps, TabsRootState>` |  | Allows you to replace the component's HTML element with a different tag, or compose it with another component. Accepts a `ReactElement` or a function that returns the element to render. |
| `style` | `CSSProperties \| ((state: TabsRootState) => CSSProperties)` |  | Style applied to the element, or a function that returns a style object based on the component's state. |

### TabsList

`variant` is `default`, a filled strip, or `line`, an underline that spans the content; both scroll in one row when horizontal. Each part names itself last with `data-slot` (`tabs`, `tabs-list`, `tabs-trigger`, `tabs-content`).

_Props of `TabsList`, generated from its types:_

Accepts a `ReactElement` or a function that returns the element to render. |
| `style` | `CSSProperties \| ((state: TabsListState) => CSSProperties)` |  | Style applied to the element, or a function that returns a style object based on the component's state. |
