<!-- page: Components/Textarea (src/stories/components/Textarea.mdx) -->

# Textarea

**Status: Stable.**

Several lines of free text: a note, description or implementation statement. This follows shadcn's native textarea implementation with Ledger styling.

## When to use it

- **Authored text of more than one line**: a description, a rationale, an implementation statement, a review note, a comment that is part of a form.
- **Text whose line breaks matter**: a statement whose paragraphs a [Prose](?path=/docs/components-typography--docs) block shows as written.

Not for one line, a name or a title: that is an [Input](?path=/docs/components-input--docs). Not for a comment or a message the reader sends, with suggestions as they type: that is a [Composer](?path=/docs/patterns-composer--docs). Not for one authored value edited where it is shown on a record: that is an [Editable](?path=/docs/patterns-editable--docs)'s multiline text. Not for code or a configuration excerpt shown to the reader: that is a [CodeBlock](?path=/docs/components-codeblock--docs).

## Content

- The label, the hint and the error are the Field's, in its words ([Field](?path=/docs/components-field--docs), Content).
- The hint says what the text is for and who reads it ("Explain the evidence supporting this decision"); a length the text must keep to is `characterLimit`'s count, not a sentence in the hint.
- `rows` is the length of the answer expected, so the box's height says how much to write: two lines for a note, four for a description, eight for a narrative.
- A placeholder is an example of the opening words, or nothing; never the label or an instruction.

## Anatomy

```tsx
<Field invalid={invalid} required>
  <FieldLabel>Review note</FieldLabel>
  <Textarea name="note" value={note} onChange={(event) => setNote(event.target.value)} rows={4} />
  <FieldDescription>Explain the evidence supporting this decision.</FieldDescription>
  <FieldError errors={errors} />
</Field>
```

Textarea is a native textarea on Base UI's Field.Control, so a [Field](?path=/docs/components-field--docs) binds it as it binds Input: label, hint and error with no ids, and the Field's `invalid`, `required` and `disabled`. It keeps the native textarea's props, events and ref.

_Example: story `Stories.BoundInField`._

## Variants and states

`rows` is the expected answer length and the box's height in lines: two for a note, four for a description, eight for a narrative, three by default. The reader can drag the box taller. Read-only is the sunken surface with a dashed edge and no hover; disabled and invalid use the shared control styling. A value that is never edited where it is shown is a [KeyValue](?path=/docs/components-keyvalue--docs), not a read-only Textarea. Use InputGroupTextarea when the editor has header or footer addons.

_Example: story `Stories.TextareaMatrix`._
_Example: story `Stories.Rows`._

`autoResize` grows the box with its text, from `rows` lines up to `maxRows`, where it scrolls, so a long statement or rationale is read without dragging a corner. The browser sizes it (`field-sizing: content`) where it can, and the Textarea measures it where it cannot. InputGroupTextarea takes both props.

_Example: story `Stories.AutoResize`._

## Length

`characterLimit` is a soft limit. A count under the box says how many characters are left, and past the limit how many too many, in the danger colour with the box's edge; the text stays whole, so a pasted statement never loses its tail. The count describes the box (with "Up to 2,000 characters." for assistive technology), is announced when the reader pauses typing, and fails native validation with its own words; the form's schema check on submit says what fixes it. Use it instead of `maxLength`, which cuts a paste off without a word. Put the limit in the count, not in the hint.

_Example: story `Stories.CharacterLimit`._
_Example: story `Stories.InField`._

## Accessibility

In a Field the label, hint, error, invalid state and requirement reach the textarea without ids. Outside one, use a label with `htmlFor` and the textarea’s `id`, `aria-describedby` for hints, and `aria-invalid` and `aria-required` explicitly. Keep labels and instructions visible. Native keyboard editing, selection and form submission remain available.

## Props

`TextareaProps` is the native textarea contract, including `ref`, `rows`, `name`, `value`, `defaultValue`, `onChange`, `onBlur`, `required` and ARIA attributes, plus `autoResize`, `maxRows` and `characterLimit`. Ref and event targets are HTMLTextAreaElement. It takes Input's API as well: `onValueChange(value, details)` beside the native `onChange`, `render` to replace or compose the element (which forwards its props and ref to a textarea), and `className` and `style` as a value or a function of the control's state (`focused`, `dirty`, `touched`, `valid`, `disabled`). With `characterLimit` the Textarea renders the count after the box, so the box and its count are siblings in the Field.

_Example: story `Stories.InputApi`._

_Props of `Textarea`, generated from its types:_

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `rows` | `number` |  | The expected answer length in lines, and the box's height: two for a note, four for a description, eight for a narrative. With `autoResize` it is the smallest the box gets. 3 by default. |
| `className` | `string \| ((state: FieldControlState) => string)` |  | A class, or a function of the control's state (`focused`, `dirty`, `valid`, `disabled` …), as on Input. |
| `style` | `CSSProperties \| ((state: FieldControlState) => CSSProperties)` |  | A style, or a function of the control's state, as on Input. |
| `render` | `ReactElement<unknown, string \| JSXElementConstructor<any>> \| ComponentRenderFn<HTMLProps, FieldControlState>` |  | Replaces the textarea, or composes it with another component, as Input's `render` does. The element must forward its props and ref to a textarea. |
| `onValueChange` | `((value: string, eventDetails: { reason: "none"; event: Event; cancel: () => void; allowPropagation: () => void; isCanceled: boolean; isPropagationAllowed: boolean; trigger: Element; }) => void)` |  | Called with the new text on every change, as on Input: `onValueChange(value, details)`, with the native event in `details.event`. The native `onChange` still runs. |
| `autoResize` | `boolean` | `false` | Grows the box with its text, from `rows` lines up to `maxRows`, where it starts to scroll. The reader never drags a corner to see what they wrote. |
| `maxRows` | `number` |  | With `autoResize`, the most lines the box grows to before it scrolls. Unlimited by default. |
| `characterLimit` | `number` |  | The most characters the answer may have, as a soft limit: a count under the box says how many are left, and past the limit how many too many, while the text stays whole, so a pasted statement never loses its tail unseen. The count describes the box, is announced when the reader pauses, and marks the box invalid for native validation. Prefer it to `maxLength`, which cuts a paste off silently. |

_Example: story `Stories.Playground`._

## Related

[Input](?path=/docs/components-input--docs) · [InputGroup](?path=/docs/components-inputgroup--docs) · [Field](?path=/docs/components-field--docs) · [shadcn Textarea](https://ui.shadcn.com/docs/components/base/textarea)

<!-- page: Components/TextLink (src/stories/components/TextLink.mdx) -->

# TextLink

**Status: Stable.**

Navigation that reads as text, with Ledger's brand color, hover underline and keyboard focus outline. Use `Button variant="link"` for actions.

## When to use it

- **A destination named in text**: a record's name in a row or a cell, a "See all" under a list, a link in a sentence.

Not for an action: that is a [Button](?path=/docs/components-button--docs), `variant="link"` where it reads as text. Not for navigation that looks like a button: that is a [LinkButton](?path=/docs/components-linkbutton--docs). Not for a destination the reader cannot open: that is plain text.

## Content

- The words name the destination: "Full timeline", "AC-2 Account management". Never "Click here" or "Read more", which name nothing heard on their own or in a list of the page's links.
- A link that opens a new tab is `newTab`, which says so after the name ("(opens in a new tab)").

_Example: story `Stories.DoDont`._

## Anatomy

TextLink renders an anchor by default. Compose a router link through Base UI `render`; the package has no router dependency.

```tsx
<TextLink href="/records">Records</TextLink>
<TextLink render={<Link to="/records" />}>Records</TextLink>
```

The rendered component must forward merged props and its ref. Supply its label as TextLink children.

## Variants and states

Omitted size inherits surrounding text. `small` and `medium` set the body scale; `weight="medium"` emphasizes a standalone destination. A link inside a sentence (a parent with its own text beside it, `data-in-text`) is underlined at rest, because its colour against the words beside it is about 2:1 in dark mode, and about 1.5:1 inside small subtle text, so colour alone would not mark it (WCAG 1.4.1); a standalone link underlines on hover. The kit owns the underline: give a link in prose no class for it. Keyboard focus adds the focus outline. Use plain text for unavailable destinations.

_Example: story `Stories.TextLinkMatrix`._
_Example: story `Stories.InProse`._

### Opening in a new tab

`newTab` opens the destination in a new tab and says so: `target="_blank"` and `rel="noopener noreferrer"`, an external-link icon joined to the last word, and "(opens in a new tab)" read after the name (the locale's `opensInNewTab`). A `target` or `rel` of your own wins. Open a new tab only when the destination is outside the product, or when leaving the page would cost the reader their place: a draft, a wizard step, an open dialog. Everything else opens in place, and the reader chooses a new tab themselves. Never set `target="_blank"` without `newTab`, which would move the reader without warning.

_Example: story `Stories.NewTab`._

## Accessibility

A real anchor retains Enter activation, copy-link and open-in-new-tab behavior. Space does not activate a link. Name the destination, such as “Full timeline”, rather than “Click here”. A link in prose carries its underline by itself; no class is needed. A `newTab` link's name ends with "(opens in a new tab)", so a screen reader hears where it will go before it goes; the icon is hidden.

## Long content

A link wraps with the text around it; its name is never truncated inside a sentence. A URL shown as the link's own words is an unbroken token: give the link `className="break-all"` so it wraps anywhere rather than widening its column. A record name in a row field (a table cell, an Item title, a KeyValue value) is cut by that field with an ellipsis and revealed on hover and keyboard focus: put the name in a [Truncate](?path=/docs/components-truncate--docs) inside the link where the field does not cut it itself. A `newTab` link in such a field sits inside the Truncate rather than holding one, so its icon is cut with the words instead of taking a line of its own.

Where any pointer is coarse, a standalone link takes an invisible hit area at least 24px tall across its own words (the shared `touch-target-block` band), so a name in a row or a "See all" footer is easy to tap; the area is never wider than the link, even when a long name wraps. A link with its sentence's text beside it keeps its words as the target, so it takes no taps from the lines around it. A container that hides its overflow clips the area to its own box; a [KeyValue](?path=/docs/components-keyvalue--docs) value truncates across only, so a link in it keeps the whole area.

_Example: story `Stories.RenderComposition`._

## Props

_Props of `TextLink`, generated from its types:_

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `render` | `ReactElement<unknown, string \| JSXElementConstructor<any>> \| ComponentRenderFn<HTMLProps, {}>` |  | Allows you to replace the component's HTML element with a different tag, or compose it with another component. Accepts a `ReactElement` or a function that returns the element to render. |
| `size` | `"medium" \| "small"` |  | Left unset, the link takes the surrounding size. |
| `weight` | `"medium" \| "regular"` |  |  |
| `newTab` | `boolean` | `false` | Opens the destination in a new tab and says so: `target="_blank"`, `rel="noopener noreferrer"`, an external-link icon after the last word, and "(opens in a new tab)" read after the name. For a destination outside the product, or one that would cost the reader their place (a draft, a wizard step, a dialog). A `target` or `rel` of your own wins. |

Native anchor attributes, events and refs pass through. `render` merges rendered-element refs and handlers; put element-specific props on the rendered component.

_Example: story `Stories.Playground`._
_Rendered in the Storybook: Controls._

## Related

[Button](?path=/docs/components-button--docs), [Breadcrumb](?path=/docs/components-breadcrumb--docs), [Item](?path=/docs/components-item--docs), [Upgrading](?path=/docs/guidance-upgrading--docs#textlink).

<!-- page: Components/TimeField (src/stories/components/TimeField.mdx) -->

# TimeField

**Status: Stable.**

A time of day, typed, held and reported as an ISO time (`"17:30"`, the contract of `input type="time"`) and shown on the LedgerProvider locale's clock: "5:30 PM" in en-US, "17:30" in de-DE. It has no date and no zone.

Use it for a wall time that stands on its own: a daily stand-up, office hours, a reminder time. A moment (evidence collected, due at 5 PM on a day) is a [DateTimeField](?path=/docs/components-datetimefield--docs), which pairs this input with a day and names the zone. A duration ("90 minutes") is a number field, not a time.

```tsx
<Field>
  <FieldLabel>Start time</FieldLabel>
  <TimeField name="start" value={start} onValueChange={setStart} min="08:00" max="18:00" />
  <FieldDescription>Between 8:00 AM and 6:00 PM.</FieldDescription>
</Field>
```

_Example: story `Stories.TypedEntry`._

## Entry

The reader types on either clock and the field reads it on Tab or Enter: "5pm", "5:30 p", "17:30", "1730", "9.15 Uhr" in German, the locale's own day periods ("오후 5:30") and its digits. The field then shows the time on the locale's clock, or on `hourCycle` (`"h12"` or `"h23"`) where a product sets one clock. A time with no day period is read on the 24-hour clock, so "5:30" is 5:30 AM, shown as such.

Text that is not a time, or a time outside `min` and `max`, stays as typed, the field reports `""` and says what fixes it under itself ("Enter a time such as 5:30 PM.", "Enter 8:00 AM or later."). The message is a FieldError inside the Field, so it describes the input and marks the Field invalid; `onEntryError` receives it too. Escape puts back the last time.

## Stepping

The input is a spinbutton that also takes typing. Up and Down move by `step` minutes (15 by default) on that grid, so 5:07 goes up to 5:15; Page Up and Page Down move an hour; both stay within `min` and `max`, and wrap at midnight without them. From empty they start at the step nearest the reader's clock. Its value is the minutes since midnight with the time's words as `aria-valuetext`, so a screen reader hears "5:15 PM" as it changes.

_Example: story `Stories.Clocks`._

## Values and forms

Use `value` and `onValueChange` for controlled state or `defaultValue` for uncontrolled. A value that is not an ISO time warns once and is treated as empty. A hidden input carries the time under `name`; put `name` on the TimeField, not on the Field, whose control is the visible text. A native form reset restores an uncontrolled default.

## Accessibility

- Inside a Field it is the Field's control: the FieldLabel names it, and the hint, the error and the Field's `invalid`, `disabled` and `required` reach it. Outside one, give it `aria-label`.
- The clock icon is decorative; the input's name and value carry everything.
- Nothing is validated while the reader types; the entry is read when they leave it or press Enter.

_Example: story `Stories.TimeFieldMatrix`._

## Props

_Props of `TimeField`, generated from its types:_

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `value` | `string` |  | The time as an ISO time of day ("17:30"), controlled; pair it with `onValueChange`. It has no date and no zone. |
| `defaultValue` | `string` |  | The starting time when uncontrolled, as an ISO time. |
| `onValueChange` | `((time: string) => void)` |  | Called with the new ISO time, or "" when cleared or when the typed text is not a time. |
| `min` | `string` |  | The earliest time the reader may enter, as an ISO time. Earlier is an error that names it. |
| `max` | `string` |  | The latest time the reader may enter, as an ISO time. |
| `step` | `number` | `15` | Minutes the Up and Down arrows move by, on that grid (Page Up and Page Down move an hour). A typed time is kept as typed. 15 by default. |
| `hourCycle` | `"h12" \| "h23"` |  | The clock the time reads on. By default the LedgerProvider locale's: 12-hour with a day period in en-US, 24-hour in de-DE. Typing either always works. |
| `name` | `string` |  | The form field's name; a hidden input carries the ISO time on submit. Put it here, not on the Field. |
| `form` | `string` |  | An external owning form, matching the native form attribute. |
| `onEntryError` | `((message: string \| null) => void)` |  | Called with the message when the typed text is not a time the field accepts, and with null once it is. The field then reports "" and shows the message under itself. |
| `size` | `"medium" \| "small"` | `medium` | `medium` (32px) in a form; `small` (28px) in a toolbar. |
| `className` | `string` |  | Layout only; reaches the field's frame. @accepts layout |
| `ref` | `Ref<HTMLInputElement>` |  |  |
| `style` | `CSSProperties \| ((state: InputState) => CSSProperties)` |  | Style applied to the element, or a function that returns a style object based on the component's state. |
| `render` | `ReactElement<unknown, string \| JSXElementConstructor<any>> \| ComponentRenderFn<HTMLProps, InputState>` |  | Allows you to replace the component's HTML element with a different tag, or compose it with another component. Accepts a `ReactElement` or a function that returns the element to render. |

### Playground

_Example: story `Stories.Playground`._

_Rendered in the Storybook: Controls._

## Don't

A TimeField holds a time of day that repeats, with no date. A moment in time is a DateTimeField, never a time alone, which loses the day and the zone.

<!-- page: Components/Timeline (src/stories/components/Timeline.mdx) -->

# Timeline

**Status: Stable.**

Events in order along one rail: a record's activity, a scope's history, an audit trail, a pipeline, a line of releases, a feed of what people did. Each event is a marker on the rail, what happened, who and when, and under it what the event carries: a sentence, a file, a note, two buttons. Vertical reads down, newest first, with sticky group labels over a week or a month; horizontal reads across, oldest first. The anatomy follows [Item](?path=/docs/components-item--docs): a row that opens is its title stretched over the row, and everything beside it is a separate stop.

A timeline is for events; things with a date are an Item list, and a fixed path with a current step is a [Stepper](?path=/docs/components-stepper--docs).

_Example: story `Stories.TimelineMatrix`._

## Anatomy

| Part        | What it is                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| ----------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Rail        | A hairline, `color.border`, through the centre of every marker. Each row draws its own piece of it in the marker column, so it runs from the first marker to the last whatever the rows hold and wherever the time sits.                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| Marker      | On the rail, at the list's size: a bare Dot in the tone at `small`; a ring on `elevation.surface.raised` holding a Dot at `medium` and `large`. With `icon`, a disc in the tone with the icon on it (a check, a cross, a play). Anything the slot holds as `marker`: an Avatar for who did it.                                                                                                                                            |
| Title       | What happened, `font.body` in `color.text`, one line unless the list says `wrap`: a longer title is cut and shows whole on hover and while its row has keyboard focus. Medium weight when emphasised or unread. It may be a sentence: the name in medium weight, the verb subtle, the record as a link. On a row that opens, this is the link or button, stretched over the row.                                                          |
| Time        | `font.body.xsmall` in `color.text.subtle`, as the reader would say it, where the list puts it: at the end of the title's line, above the title as a dated line, first in the footer, or in a column before the rail. Across, above or below the marker. A `<time>` when `dateTime` is given; with `dateTime` alone, the relative words in the reader's locale, kept current. The full stamp is read after the words and is their tooltip. |
| Meta        | Under the title, `font.body.xsmall` in `color.text.subtle`: who, and the kind. One line that is cut and shows whole on hover; it wraps where the list says `wrap`, and on a row that opens, whose link lies over it.                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| Description | Under the meta, `font.body.small` in `color.text.subtle`, wrapping: what the event amounts to, in a sentence.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| Body        | Under the description, `font.body`: the note, the diff, what was said; a file; two buttons; who is on it; a collapsible detail.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| Footer      | The last line: Badges for the kind and the state, or who did it; the time first, when it sits below.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| Trailing    | At the end of the title's line, beside the row's control: an unread Count, a chevron, a menu button.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| Group       | A run of events under a sticky Eyebrow with a count, on the current surface and on the title's column; the rail runs to its edge.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |

## Variants

| Variant      | Use                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| ------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `vertical`   | The default. Reads down, newest first, the rail at the start: a feed, a history, a log, a pipeline. Groups live here.                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `horizontal` | Reads across, oldest first, the rail on top: releases, a project's journey, a workflow's stages on a record header. `center`, the default, puts each marker mid-column with the time above, like a Stepper; `start` puts it at the column's start with the time below and the text under it, for stages with a body. |

A horizontal list is at least 420px (`dimension.part.steps`) wide, and `itemWidth="rail"` gives each event at least a rail's width (`dimension.layout.rail`) instead, for stages whose title and date must stay readable. Narrower than that it scrolls inside its container, with an arrow at each edge where a pointer can hover and a swipe on touch. `wrap` lets the titles across wrap too.

_Example: story `Stories.Stages`._

_Example: story `Stories.Narrow`._

Where the time sits, `timePosition` on the list:

| Position | Use                                                                                                                           |
| -------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `end`    | The default: at the end of the title's line. A history, an audit trail, anywhere the rows are one or two lines.               |
| `above`  | A dated line above the title: a log where the date is the point, and the rows carry a sentence and a file.                    |
| `below`  | First in the footer, with the kind and the state: a feed of people, where the title is who did what and the when is a detail. |
| `start`  | A column before the rail, on the title's line: releases by month, a changelog, where the reader scans the dates.              |

What a row does:

| The row        | Use                                                                                                                                 |
| -------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Opens a record | `link` with the router's Link: the title is the link, stretched over the row.                                                       |
| Opens in place | `onSelect`: the title is a button over the row; `isActive` marks the event open beside the list, with `aria-current` on the button. |
| Only reads     | Neither: a plain row.                                                                                                               |
| Is unread      | `isUnread`: the title in medium weight and "Unread" read before it; an unread Count in `trailing`.                                  |

_Example: story `Stories.People`._

_Example: story `Stories.Log`._

Not built, and why: alternating sides, because the rail is a list, not a poster; a collapsed "show more", because the group's count says how many and the page scrolls; a rating on an event, because a rating is a record's fact, not an event's; markers in the accent hues, a colour per row to tell rows apart, because the marker's colour is the tone and a colour that says nothing is a colour the reader tries to read.

## Sizes

| Size     | Slot | Marker                                                  | Row                         | Where                                                                                  |
| -------- | ---- | ------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `small`  | 16px | A bare 8px Dot; an `xsmall` Avatar; a 16px disc         | `space.050` above and below | A dense log, a changelog, a rail's recent activity.                                    |
| `medium` | 20px | A 12px ring with a Dot; an `xsmall` Avatar; a 20px disc | `space.075` above and below | The default: a record's history, an audit trail, a pipeline.                           |
| `large`  | 24px | A 16px ring with a Dot; a `small` Avatar; a 24px disc   | `space.100` above and below | A feed of people, where the avatar is the marker; a workflow's stages across a header. |

The size is the list's, not the row's: every marker in a list sits on the same rail. The title stays `font.body` at every size; what scales is the marker and the room around it. A vertical timeline is as wide as its container; in a rail it is the rail's width, on a record page a measure. A horizontal one gives each event an equal column, 420px in all at least, like a Stepper, or with `itemWidth="rail"` a rail's width each at least; in a scrolling area it can be as wide as its stages need.

_Example: story `Stories.Releases`._

_Example: story `Stories.Runs`._

_Example: story `Stories.Activity`._

_Example: story `Stories.RelativeTimes`._

_Example: story `Stories.LongContent`._

## States

| State          | What changes                                                                                                              |
| -------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Plain          | No hover. Text on the surface.                                                                                            |
| Link or button | `color.background.neutral.subtle.hovered` on hover across the row; the focus outline around the row.                      |
| Active         | `color.background.selected`, and its hovered step on hover: the event open beside the list. In forced colours, Highlight. |
| Emphasised     | The title medium: `emphasis` for the current one, where its words say why; `isUnread` for one the reader has not seen.    |

The feed in a Sheet, the count in its title, is the [In a sheet](?path=/story/components-timeline--in-a-sheet) story.

## Modifiers

- **`orientation`**, **`size`**, **`timePosition`** and, across, **`align`**, as in Variants and Sizes. All four are the list's, so every row agrees. **`wrap`**, also the list's, lets every title wrap: a feed whose sentences name a task or a file.
- **`tone`** colours the default marker's dot by the event's kind; **`icon`**, passed bare, turns the marker into a disc in the tone with the icon on it; **`marker`** replaces it.
- **`time`** as said; **`dateTime`**, the machine stamp, which makes it a `<time>`; **`timeTitle`**, the full stamp, read after the words and their tooltip. Beside an ISO `dateTime`, a missing `time` is the relative words ("5 minutes ago", "yesterday") in the reader's locale, and a missing `timeTitle` the moment in full in the reader's locale and zone.
- **`meta`** for who and the kind, one line; **`description`** for the sentence under it; **`children`** for what the event carries; **`footer`** for the Badges and the name last.
- **`link`**, **`onSelect`**, **`isActive`**, **`isUnread`**, **`emphasis`**, **`trailing`** as in Variants.
- **`itemWidth`**, across: `equal` columns, or at least a rail's width each.
- **Group `label`** and **`count`**; the label sticks to the top of the scrolling surface, over the rail and the markers, and is a heading at the level where the timeline sits.
- **`label`**, required, names the list: "Activity", "History", "Releases".

## Content

- **Newest first** down a page; oldest first across. The reader wants what just happened; the beginning is at the bottom.
- **The title says what happened**, in one line: "Verified", "Due date moved", "Evidence linked". As a sentence, who first: "Nadia Flores approved payout batch ACH-4182", the name in medium weight, the verb subtle, the record a link.
- **The meta says who and what changed**: "Dana Whitfield · 14 Sep → 18 Sep". **The description says why**, in one sentence.
- **The footer is the kind, then the state**: "Payout · Same day", "Risk · High". Or the name, when the title is the thing done: "Maya Brooks · Done".
- **The time matches its place**: "2h ago" and "Yesterday" at the end of the line or in the footer; "6 May 2026" above; "May 2025" in the column. The full stamp is read after the words and is their tooltip. Beside the title a stamp takes at most half the line and is cut first; a long stamp (a long locale, a day and a time) goes `below`, where it has a line of its own.
- **Group by period**: "This week", "August", "Earlier". A count on the group when there are more than a few.

## Style

| Element     | Token                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| ----------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Rail        | 1px · `color.border` · through the marker column's centre, each row its own piece, the first row's top and the last row's bottom hidden                                                                                                                                                                 |
| Marker      | slot 16, 20 or 24px · ring 12 or 16px `color.border` on `elevation.surface.raised` · Dot in the tone · disc the slot's size in `color.background.{tone}.bold` with a 12 or 16px icon in `color.text.inverse`, neutral in `color.background.neutral`                                                     |
| Row         | `space.050`, `space.075` or `space.100` block by size · `space.050` inline · `space.100` between marker and text · `space.150` between the time column and the marker · `radius.medium` when it clicks                                                                                                  |
| Across      | rail 1px `color.border` between markers · start-aligned, the marker and the text `space.050` in from the column's start, where a focused event's ring runs · time `space.050` above the marker or first under it · text `space.075` below · equal columns, 420px in all or a rail's width each at least |
| Title       | `font.body` · `color.text` · medium when emphasised                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| Time        | `font.body.xsmall` · `color.text.subtle` · tabular · end-aligned in the column · at most half the title's line beside it, at most 160px in the column, cut with the full stamp as its reveal                                                                                                            |
| Meta        | `font.body.xsmall` · `color.text.subtle` · one line                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| Description | `font.body.small` · `color.text.subtle`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| Footer      | `font.body.xsmall` · `color.text.subtle` · `space.075` between its parts · `space.025` above                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| Group       | Eyebrow · on the title column · `space.050` below, `space.150` above after the first · `elevation.surface.current` behind · above the marker column as it sticks                                                                                                                                        |
| Hover       | `color.background.neutral.subtle.hovered`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| Active      | `color.background.selected` · `color.background.selected.hovered`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |

Down the page the list is one CSS grid the rows share, time · marker · body, and each row a subgrid of it: the time column is as wide as its widest stamp, the marker column as wide as the size's slot, and the rail is drawn inside the marker column, so it is centred by construction.

## Accessibility

- **The list is an ordered list**, `role="list"` so WebKit keeps the role once its markers are removed, named by `label`, and every event an `li`; a group is an `li` holding a heading and its own list, labelled by the heading. `label` is required, so no Timeline is an unnamed list.
- **A group's label is a heading at the contextual level**: an h3 outside every HeadingLevelProvider, and inside a Section or a provider the level there, so a grouped timeline under an h1 or in an h3 section keeps the outline.
- **The title is the control.** A row that opens is a link or a button named by the title alone, with "Unread" before it on an unread event, and stretched over the row; the time, the meta, the description and the footer are read as the text beside it. Nothing interactive sits inside it: the trailing slot, a file's download, a menu and the buttons in the body are their own stops beside it.
- **The time is a `<time>`** when `dateTime` is given, so the machine stamp travels with the words. The full stamp is visually hidden text after the words, so a screen reader hears it however the row is reached, and it is the tooltip on hover. Where the stamp matters to a sighted reader on a keyboard or touch screen, show it: `time` is the full stamp, or it goes `above`.
- **The open event and the unread ones say so.** `isActive` puts `aria-current="true"` on the row's link or button (on the row itself when it does not open); `isUnread` reads "Unread" before the title.
- **Across, the strip is a stop only when it must be**: while it overflows and holds nothing focusable, it is one tab stop, a group named after the list ("Releases, scrolls"), so the arrow keys scroll it. Rows that open are the stops otherwise, and their rings are drawn inside the strip.
- **Tone is never alone.** The marker's colour says the kind; the title says what happened. A footer Badge says the state in a word. In forced colours, which drop the fill, an icon marker keeps its disc as an outline around the icon.
- **An Avatar as the marker is decorative** when the name is in the title, so the name is read once.
- **A plain row is not focusable.**

## Props

_Props of `Timeline`, generated from its types:_

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `label` (required) | `string` |  | The list's accessible name, required so the events are never an unnamed list: "Activity", "History", "Releases". An `aria-label` overrides it. |
| `orientation` | `"horizontal" \| "vertical"` |  | `vertical`, the default, reads down with the rail on the left: a feed, a history. `horizontal` reads across with the rail on top: releases, a journey. Groups are vertical only. |
| `size` | `"large" \| "medium" \| "small"` |  | The marker's scale, and with it the row. `medium` (20px) is the default: a ring holding a Dot, a disc with an icon, an `xsmall` Avatar. `small` (16px) is a bare Dot for a dense log. `large` (24px) is a `small` Avatar or a disc for a feed of people and a workflow's stages. |
| `timePosition` | `"above" \| "below" \| "end" \| "start"` |  | Where the time sits. Down the page: `end` of the title's line, the default; `above` the title as a dated line; `below` in the footer with the badges; `start` in a column before the rail. Across: `above` the marker, the default, or `below` it. |
| `wrap` | `boolean` |  | Titles wrap onto more lines instead of truncating: a feed, where the sentence names a task or a file; across, a stage whose name is long. |
| `align` | `"center" \| "start"` |  | Across only. `center`, the default, puts the marker mid-column with the rail either side, for a line of releases; `start` puts it at the column's start with the text under it, for stages with a body. |
| `itemWidth` | `"equal" \| "rail"` |  | Across only. `equal`, the default, gives every event an equal share of the list, which is `dimension.part.steps` (420px) wide at least; `rail` gives each event at least a rail's width (`dimension.layout.rail`), for stages whose title and date must stay readable, and the strip scrolls past that. |
| `children` (required) | `ReactNode` |  | Timeline.Item rows, or Timeline.Group sections of them. |
| `className` | `string` |  |  |

Each part takes its element's native props, a `className` and a ref, and names itself last with `data-slot` (`timeline`, `timeline-group`, `timeline-item`): the list, the group's row and the event's row. Across, the list sits inside a scroller.

### Timeline.Item

_Props of `TimelineItem`, generated from its types:_

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `marker` | `ReactNode` |  | Replaces the marker entirely: an Avatar, anything the size's slot holds (16, 20 or 24px). |
| `tone` | `"danger" \| "information" \| "neutral" \| "success" \| "warning"` | `neutral` | The colour of the default marker: the event's kind. A dot in a ring, or the disc behind `icon`. |
| `icon` | `ReactElement<{ className?: string; }, string \| JSXElementConstructor<any>>` |  | An icon in the marker, passed bare: a check for done, a cross for failed, a play for running. The marker becomes a disc in the tone with the icon on it. |
| `title` (required) | `ReactNode` |  | What happened, one line. It truncates, and shows whole on hover and on keyboard focus of the row while it is cut. On a row that opens, this is the link or button, stretched over the row. A Badge may sit inside it; a name may lead it. |
| `meta` | `ReactNode` |  | Under the title, subtle: who, and the kind. One line that shows whole on hover while it is cut; it wraps where the list's titles wrap and on a row that opens. |
| `description` | `ReactNode` |  | Under the meta, `font.body.small`, wrapping: what the event amounts to, in a sentence. |
| `time` | `ReactNode` |  | When, as the reader would say it: "2h ago", "28 Aug". Where it sits is the list's `timePosition`. A stamp longer than its place truncates. Left out beside `dateTime`, it is the relative words ("5 minutes ago", "yesterday") in the reader's locale, kept current. |
| `timeTitle` | `string` |  | The full stamp: "2026-09-02 14:10". A screen reader hears it after `time`, and it is the time's tooltip on hover. Left out beside an ISO `dateTime`, it is that moment in full in the reader's locale and time zone. |
| `dateTime` | `string` |  | The machine-readable stamp, an ISO day or instant, which makes the time a `<time>` element. |
| `link` | `ReactElement<{ id?: string; className?: string; children?: ReactNode; }, string \| JSXElementConstructor<any>> \| undefined` |  | A link element (a router's Link) that becomes the title and stretches over the row. Leave it empty to use title; supplied children override the link text. |
| `onSelect` | `(() => void)` |  | Makes the title a button that stretches over the row. |
| `isActive` | `boolean` |  | The event that is open beside the list: the selected fill, and `aria-current` on the row's link or button. |
| `isUnread` | `boolean` |  | An event the reader has not seen: the title in weight 500, and "Unread" read before it. |
| `emphasis` | `boolean` |  | The title in weight 500, for the current event, where its words already say why (a Current badge, "running"). An unread event is `isUnread`. |
| `trailing` | `ReactNode` |  | At the end of the title's line, beside the row's link or button: an unread Count, a chevron, a menu button. |
| `children` | `ReactNode` |  | Under the description: the note, the diff, what was said, an attachment, a collapsible detail. |
| `footer` | `ReactNode` |  | The last line: Badges for the kind and the state, or who did it. The time joins it when the list's `timePosition` is `below`. |

### Feed composition

Timeline.Item takes a marker, an icon, a tone, a sentence, metadata, a time, a body and a footer, which is all a feed needs. The feed's event kinds and their mapping belong to the application; a feed needs no wrapper of its own.

## Related

- [Item](?path=/docs/components-item--docs): rows that are things, not events.
- [Stepper](?path=/docs/components-stepper--docs): a fixed path with a current step, which a horizontal timeline resembles and is not; with a record under each milestone.
- [Collapsible](?path=/docs/components-collapsible--docs): a detail folded under a row.
- [Avatar](?path=/docs/components-avatar--docs): a person as the marker.
- [Badge](?path=/docs/components-badge--docs): the kind and the state in the footer.
- [Sheet](?path=/docs/components-sheet--docs): the feed from the page's edge.
- [Dot](?path=/docs/components-indicator--docs): the tone in the default marker.

## Don't

A Timeline runs newest first down a page. Its title says what happened, the meta who and what changed, the description why; a marker takes a tone only where the event has one, and records with a date are an Item list, never a Timeline.

_Example: story `Stories.Dont`._

Links compose through Base UI and retain caller ids, refs, styles and handlers. Leave a supplied link empty to use the event title; its own children override that default.

# Toaster

**Status: Stable.**

Short feedback after the reader's own act, which needs nothing more from them: "Evidence linked", "Export ready". It appears at the bottom end of the screen, leaves on its own, and never holds the only copy of anything the reader needs. The family is Base UI's Toast, with Ledger's surfaces, type, motion, words and defaults.

_Example: story `Stories.Playground`._

## Choosing between them

| The message                                                  | Part                                                              |
| ------------------------------------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------- |
| The result of the reader's act, which needs nothing more     | A toast                                                           |
| A failure the reader must act on, or a problem with a record | An [Alert](?path=/docs/components-alert--docs) beside what failed |
| A problem with one field, or with a submitted form           | [FieldError](?path=/docs/components-field--docs), ErrorSummary    |
| Something about the whole site, for every reader             | A [Banner](?path=/docs/components-banner--docs)                   |
| A decision the reader must take before going on              | An [AlertDialog](?path=/docs/components-alertdialog--docs)        |

A failure is a toast only when there is nowhere on the page to put it: the reader has moved on, or the work ran in the background.

## Anatomy

Mount one Toaster near the application root. It is the provider, the portal and the viewport, and draws each toast as Toast, ToastContent, the type's icon, ToastTitle, ToastDescription, ToastAction and ToastClose. The stack sits at the bottom end of the screen, `space.200` from its edges and at most 24rem wide.

```tsx
<Toaster />;
// From a workflow, after the provider mounts:
const id = toast.add({
  title: "Evidence linked",
  description: "Bank reconciliation, July",
  type: "success",
});
toast.update(id, { description: "Bank reconciliation, August" });
toast.close(id);
```

## Types and timing

`type` picks the icon: `success`, `information` (or Base UI's `info`), `warning`, `danger` (or `error`) and `loading`. The kit's tone words are stored as Base UI's, so a `danger` toast draws the danger icon and reads `error` from the manager; `ToastType` is the union.

| The toast           | Leaves                                                    |
| ------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------- |
| Any, by default     | After 5 seconds, the Toaster's `timeout`                  |
| An error (`danger`) | After 8 seconds                                           |
| One with an action  | Never on its own: when the reader acts on it or closes it |
| A loading toast     | When its work settles; it has no timer                    |
| `timeout: 0`        | Never on its own                                          |

An explicit `timeout` always wins. Hovering or focusing the stack, and the window losing focus, pause every timer.

_Example: story `Stories.Defaults`._

## Actions

`actionProps` takes the action's `children` and `onClick`. The action does not close its toast: call `close(id)` when it should, which lets an action update the toast or keep it while work continues. A toast with an action stays until it is used or closed, since a keyboard or screen-reader reader reaches it only through F6. Every action in a toast also exists on the page: Undo beside the record, View in the list. The toast is a shortcut to it, never its only home.

_Example: story `Stories.WithAction`._

`promise` shows the loading toast while the work runs and replaces it with the success or the error when it settles; it returns a promise of the original value and rethrows a rejection, so await or handle it as usual.

_Example: story `Stories.Working`._

## Content

- **The title says what happened**, in the past tense and the reader's words: "Evidence linked", "Package ready". Not "Success", not "Done!".
- **At most one short line under it**, naming the record: "Bank reconciliation, July". A toast leaves before a paragraph is read; the detail belongs in the record.
- **An error says what did not happen** ("Could not build the package") and, when the page can, points at where to fix it. The fix itself stays on the page.
- **One action at most**, named for what it does: Undo, View.

## Long content

A title or a description wraps inside the toast, and a code or a hash breaks where it must. The title and the description can be selected and copied, so an error message or a record's code can be pasted into a ticket; a swipe that starts on the text does not dismiss the toast.

## Stack and short windows

Four toasts show at once, the newest in front and the others behind it; hovering or focusing the stack opens it. In a window under 30rem tall the Toaster keeps two, so the open stack stays inside the window, and a toast past the limit leaves the page.

_Example: story `Stories.Stack`._

## Accessibility

- **F6 moves focus to the stack**, and Shift+Tab from it returns to where the reader was. Each toast has a localised Close button, and the stack is a region named "Notifications".
- **Toasts are announced politely**, after what the reader is hearing. Base UI's `priority: "high"` announces a toast at once, but hides it from assistive technology until the stack has focus, which leaves its Close and its action focusable under `aria-hidden`; the kit does not set it, and an urgent failure belongs in an Alert on the page.
- **The loading icon is decorative**: the toast's title already says what is running.
- **Keep what the reader needs on the page.** A toast leaves; anything the reader must read twice, act on or come back to is on the page as well. The stack works over an open dialog.

_Example: story `Stories.InDialog`._

## Props

_Props of `Toaster`, generated from its types:_

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `limit` | `number` | `3` | The maximum number of toasts that can be displayed at once. When the limit is exceeded, the oldest toasts are marked as `limited` (via the `data-limited` attribute) rather than removed, so they can be hidden or animated out. |
| `timeout` | `number` | `5000` | The default amount of time (in ms) before a toast is auto dismissed. A value of `0` will prevent the toast from being dismissed automatically. |
| `toastManager` | `ToastManager<Record<string, unknown>> \| ToastManager<any>` | `createToastManager()` | A manager from `createToastManager`, or Base UI's own. |

_Props of `ToastViewport`, generated from its types:_

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `className` | `string \| ((state: ToastViewportState) => string)` |  | CSS class applied to the element, or a function that returns a class based on the component's state. |
| `render` | `ReactElement<unknown, string \| JSXElementConstructor<any>> \| ComponentRenderFn<HTMLProps, ToastViewportState>` |  | Allows you to replace the component's HTML element with a different tag, or compose it with another component. Accepts a `ReactElement` or a function that returns the element to render. |
| `style` | `CSSProperties \| ((state: ToastViewportState) => CSSProperties)` |  | Style applied to the element, or a function that returns a style object based on the component's state. |

Toaster takes Base UI's provider props: `timeout` (5000), `limit` (4) and `toastManager`, and has no element of its own. For another placement or presentation, compose the exported parts under a `ToastProvider`: ToastViewport takes native div props, its ref, its direction and its accessible name, and every styled part keeps Base UI's `render`, ref and state callbacks for `className`. `createToastManager` makes a stack of its own, with the kit's defaults; `useToastManager` reads the nearest provider's toasts and methods, with the same defaults.

_Example: story `Stories.NativeOptions`._

## Don't

A failure the reader must act on is an [Alert](?path=/docs/components-alert--docs) beside what failed, never a toast: a toast leaves before a reader who looked away has read it. A toast is a title and at most one short line, never a paragraph.

_Example: story `Stories.Dont`._

<!-- page: Components/Toggle (src/stories/components/Toggle.mdx) -->

# Toggle

**Status: Stable.**

A two-state button built on Base UI with the shadcn composition API. Put icons and labels in `children`; give an icon-only toggle an `aria-label`.

```tsx
<Toggle aria-label="Bold">
  <Bold aria-hidden />
</Toggle>
```

_Example: story `Stories.ToggleMatrix`._

## When to use it

| Need                                                                                                               | Part                                                                                                       |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| One on/off state that changes how something is shown, in a toolbar or beside the content: Bold, Pin, Show as table | Toggle                                                                                                     |
| One choice among a few, shown at once: a view, a period, the colour mode                                           | [ToggleGroup](?path=/docs/components-togglegroup--docs)                                                    |
| A setting that takes effect at once, in a form or a settings list, with a label beside it                          | [Switch](?path=/docs/components-switch--docs)                                                              |
| A choice submitted with a form                                                                                     | [Checkbox](?path=/docs/components-checkbox--docs) or [RadioGroup](?path=/docs/components-radiogroup--docs) |
| An action that happens once: save, export, open                                                                    | [Button](?path=/docs/components-button--docs)                                                              |

## Content

- The label, or an icon-only toggle's `aria-label`, names the state it turns on ("Bold", "Pin to top", "Show as table"), and stays the same whether it is on or off: the pressed state says which.
- Never a verb that flips with the state ("Show"/"Hide"): a screen reader already says pressed or not pressed.

A label that flips with the state ("Show table", then "Hide table") says the state twice.

_Example: story `Stories.DoDont`._

## Variants and state

`variant="default"` is unbordered; `variant="outline"` adds a border. Sizes are the control scale's `small` (28px), `medium` (32px, the default) and `large` (36px), so a `small` toggle sits beside a `small` Button and a `medium` one beside a `medium` Button; `large` is a step Button does not have. `data-size` reports the word.

`sm`, `default` and `lg` are the deprecated spellings of `small`, `medium` and `large`, kept for one version; `ledger/no-deprecated-name` rewrites them.

_Example: story `Stories.DeprecatedSizes`._

Hover is the neutral tint. Pressed is the selected palette, `color.background.selected` with `color.text.selected`, and a 1px `color.border.selected` edge at 3:1 on that fill, so a pressed toggle never reads as a hovered one and its state does not rest on a faint fill. The default variant draws the edge out of the flow, so pressing never changes the toggle's size; the outline variant recolours its own border. In forced colours a pressed toggle is Highlight.

_Example: story `Stories.PressedAgainstHover`._

Use `defaultPressed` for local state, or `pressed` and `onPressedChange(pressed, details)` for controlled state. Calling `details.cancel()` rejects a change. `disabled` blocks activation and removes the toggle from the normal tab order.

Native attributes, event handlers and refs reach the button, and its `data-slot` comes after them, so a stray attribute never renames it. `render` composes another action element; it must forward props and refs. Set `nativeButton={false}` for a non-button action. `className` and `style` accept callbacks with `{ pressed, disabled }`. `toggleVariants({ variant, size, className })` exposes the shared styling recipe.

## Accessibility

The native button reports `aria-pressed`. Enter and Space toggle it; Tab moves to the next control. Keep its name stable when the pressed state changes: the name says what it turns on (“Table”), and `aria-pressed` says whether it is on, so never swap the name for the state (“Show as chart”). Icons supplied as children should be decorative when the label already names the action; an icon-only toggle takes an `aria-label` and a [Tooltip](?path=/docs/components-tooltip--docs) with the same words.

For coordinated selection, use [ToggleGroup](?path=/docs/components-togglegroup--docs). It provides one tab stop and arrow-key navigation among its items.

## Props

_Props of `Toggle`, generated from its types:_

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `pressed` | `boolean` |  | Whether the toggle button is currently pressed. This is the controlled counterpart of `defaultPressed`. |
| `defaultPressed` | `boolean` | `false` | Whether the toggle button is currently pressed. This is the uncontrolled counterpart of `pressed`. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | Whether the component should ignore user interaction. |
| `onPressedChange` | `((pressed: boolean, eventDetails: { reason: "none"; event: Event; cancel: () => void; allowPropagation: () => void; isCanceled: boolean; isPropagationAllowed: boolean; trigger: Element; }) => void)` |  | Callback fired when the pressed state is changed. |
| `value` | `string` |  | A unique string that identifies the toggle when used inside a toggle group. |
| `nativeButton` | `boolean` | `true` | Whether the component renders a native `<button>` element when replacing it via the `render` prop. Set to `false` if the rendered element is not a button (for example, `<div>`). |
| `className` | `string \| ((state: ToggleState) => string)` |  | CSS class applied to the element, or a function that returns a class based on the component's state. |
| `render` | `ReactElement<unknown, string \| JSXElementConstructor<any>> \| ComponentRenderFn<HTMLProps, ToggleState>` |  | Allows you to replace the component's HTML element with a different tag, or compose it with another component. Accepts a `ReactElement` or a function that returns the element to render. |
| `style` | `CSSProperties \| ((state: ToggleState) => CSSProperties)` |  | Style applied to the element, or a function that returns a style object based on the component's state. |
| `variant` | `"default" \| "outline" \| null` | `default` | `default` is unbordered; `outline` draws a border. |
| `size` | `ToggleSize \| null` | `medium` | `small` 28px, `medium` 32px (the default) or `large` 36px, Button's heights. `sm`, `default` and `lg` are the deprecated spellings of `small`, `medium` and `large`. |

_Example: story `Stories.Playground`._

_Rendered in the Storybook: Controls._

# ToggleGroup

**Status: Stable.**

A group of toggle buttons with shared selection and keyboard navigation. Compose each choice with `ToggleGroupItem`, using a unique `value` and explicit children for its label, icon or count.

```tsx
<ToggleGroup aria-label="View" defaultValue={["table"]} variant="outline">
  <ToggleGroupItem value="table">Table</ToggleGroupItem>
  <ToggleGroupItem value="board">Board</ToggleGroupItem>
</ToggleGroup>
```

_Example: story `Stories.ToggleGroupMatrix`._

## When to use it

| Need                                                                                                              | Part                                                                                                   |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| One choice among two to five, all shown, that changes the view at once: Table or Board, a period, the colour mode | ToggleGroup                                                                                            |
| Several independent on/off options side by side: Bold, Italic, Underline                                          | ToggleGroup with `multiple`, or a row of [Toggle](?path=/docs/components-toggle--docs)                 |
| One choice submitted with a form, or more than a handful of options                                               | [RadioGroup](?path=/docs/components-radiogroup--docs) or [Select](?path=/docs/components-select--docs) |
| Switching between panels of content                                                                               | [Tabs](?path=/docs/components-tabs--docs)                                                              |
| Related actions joined into one control                                                                           | [ButtonGroup](?path=/docs/components-buttongroup--docs)                                                |

## Content

- Each item is one or two words that name the choice ("Table", "Board", "Last 30 days"); the group's `aria-label` names what they choose between ("View", "Period").
- Items share a grammar and a length, so the group reads as one set, and the order is the order of the thing they choose (shortest period first, the default view first).
- A count after a label is a [Count](?path=/docs/components-count--docs), with the same `max` as the product's other counts.

A group without its `aria-label` is heard as buttons with no word for the choice they make.

_Example: story `Stories.DoDont`._

## Selection and layout

Selection is an array in both modes. By default, at most one item can be pressed; pressing it again clears the selection. Add `multiple` to allow several pressed items. A pressed item takes Toggle's pressed look, the selected fill with a 1px `color.border.selected` edge that follows a joined group's corners, so the current view never looks like a hovered one; in forced colours it is Highlight. `defaultValue` initializes local state; `value` and `onValueChange(values, details)` control it. Call `details.cancel()` to reject a change, such as clearing a required view: one choice that must stay active ignores or cancels an empty selection. The API is Base UI's array with `multiple`, not Radix's `type="single"`.

Group `variant` and `size` pass to its items. Variants are `default` and `outline`; sizes are Toggle's: `small` (28px), `medium` (32px, the default) and `large` (36px), with `sm`, `default` and `lg` as deprecated spellings for one version. `spacing` counts 4px steps on the space scale: the default `spacing={2}` is `space.100` (8px), `1` to `6`, `8`, `10`, `12` and `16` are the other steps, a number between two steps takes the smaller, and `spacing={0}` joins the items. `orientation="vertical"` stacks them and changes arrow navigation.

_Example: story `Stories.Spacing`._

The group and items support native attributes, refs, `render`, and state callbacks for `className` and `style`. Use `disabled` on an item or the whole group to block selection.

_Example: story `Stories.ViewsStory`._

A spaced group wraps its items onto the next line when its row is too narrow for them, so every choice stays in view and in reach. A joined group, a group in a table cell and a group in a horizontal Scroller keep one line, and the table's frame or the Scroller scrolls. Put a joined group in a horizontal [Scroller](?path=/docs/components-scroller--docs) when its row can be narrower than its items.

_Example: story `Stories.NarrowRow`._

## Accessibility

- The root has `role="group"`; each item is a button with `aria-pressed`. Name the group with `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`, and give icon-only items an accessible name.
- Tab enters and leaves the group as one stop. In a single-select group with a pressed item, that stop is the pressed item, as in a radio group, so the reader lands on the current choice; otherwise, and in a `multiple` group, it is the first enabled item. Arrow keys move focus; Enter or Space changes selection; Tab from any item leaves the group, and coming back lands on the pressed item again. A value changed from outside moves the stop with it. Disabled items are skipped.
- Horizontal arrows follow the Ledger locale direction; `dir` on the group overrides it. Vertical groups use Up and Down. Home and End reach the first and last enabled items.
- Focus wraps by default. Set `loopFocus={false}` to stop at the ends.
- An icon-only item has no visible name, so give it a [Tooltip](?path=/docs/components-tooltip--docs) with its name, as ModeSwitch does: `<Tooltip><TooltipTrigger render={<ToggleGroupItem value="dark">…</ToggleGroupItem>} /><TooltipContent>Dark</TooltipContent></Tooltip>`.

_Example: story `Stories.TabStopOnThePressedItem`._

## Props

_Props of `ToggleGroup`, generated from its types:_

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `value` | `readonly Value[]` |  | The pressed state of the toggle group represented by an array of the values of all pressed toggle buttons. This is the controlled counterpart of `defaultValue`. |
| `defaultValue` | `readonly Value[]` |  | The pressed state of the toggle group represented by an array of the values of all pressed toggle buttons. This is the uncontrolled counterpart of `value`. |
| `onValueChange` | `((groupValue: Value[], eventDetails: { reason: "none"; event: Event; cancel: () => void; allowPropagation: () => void; isCanceled: boolean; isPropagationAllowed: boolean; trigger: Element; }) => void)` |  | Callback fired when the pressed states of the toggle group changes. |

Accepts a `ReactElement` or a function that returns the element to render. |

| `variant` | `"default" \| "outline" \| null` |  | `default` is unbordered; `outline` draws a border. |
| `size` | `ToggleSize \| null` |  | `small` 28px, `medium` 32px (the default) or `large` 36px, Button's heights. `sm`, `default` and `lg` are the deprecated spellings of `small`, `medium` and `large`. |
| `spacing` | `number` | `2` | The gap between items in 4px steps on the space scale: 2 (8px, `space.100`) by default, 0 joins the items. 1 to 6, 8, 10, 12 and 16 are the steps; a number between two steps takes the smaller. |

| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | Whether the component should ignore user interaction. |
