<!-- page: Components/Tooltip (src/stories/components/Tooltip.mdx) -->

# Tooltip

**Status: Stable.**

A short visual label on hover or keyboard focus, using shadcn's Base UI composition. IconButton already draws one from its `label`; compose a separate tooltip only when its words differ, such as a keyboard shortcut.

```tsx
<Tooltip>
  <TooltipTrigger
    aria-keyshortcuts="Meta+K Control+K"
    render={<IconButton label="Search" icon={<Search />} isTooltipDisabled />}
  />
  <TooltipContent describe>
    Search <Kbd>K</Kbd>
  </TooltipContent>
</Tooltip>
```

_Example: story `Stories.Shortcut`._

## When to use it

- **The name of an icon-only control**, which IconButton draws itself from its `label`.
- **A keyboard shortcut**, or a few words that add to a control's name.
- **The whole of a value cut short**, which Truncate draws itself.

Not for anything the reader needs to finish the task: an instruction, a rule, an error or a required value sits on the page, in a Field's description, a FieldError or an Alert, since a tooltip shows only to a pointer that rests or a focus that lands. Not for a control or a link: a tooltip holds text, a record's preview is a [HoverCard](?path=/docs/components-hovercard--docs) and a small task a [Popover](?path=/docs/components-popover--docs). Not wrapped around a disabled control to explain it: the reason is the control's `disabledReason`, which keeps it in the Tab order and draws its own tooltip (Unavailable actions). [Overlays](?path=/docs/components-overlays--docs) compares them all.

A rule the reader needs is the Field's description, not a tooltip beside the field: a reader who never rests on the icon never meets it.

_Example: story `Stories.DoDont`._

## Content

- A few words in sentence case, with no full stop: the control's name or a short phrase ("Copy link", "Search").
- It says what the control does, not how to work the pointer: "Delete row", never "Click to delete".
- It adds to the visible label or names an icon; it never repeats a visible label word for word.

## Composition

Root owns open state. Trigger renders a button by default; `render` composes an existing button, link or span with its native props, handlers and ref. It does not give a rendered link or span button semantics, and has no `nativeButton` prop. A custom trigger must accept merged props and its ref, and brings its own focus ring: compose a kit Button, IconButton or TextLink rather than a bare element.

Content includes the portal, positioner and decorative arrow. Native props, `ref`, `render`, and state callbacks for `className` and `style` target the popup. Placement defaults to top and centre with `sideOffset={4}` and `alignOffset={0}`. Content also takes the positioner's `anchor` (an element, a ref or a virtual point, for a tooltip that belongs to a cell or a chart mark rather than to its trigger), `collisionPadding`, `collisionBoundary`, `collisionAvoidance`, `sticky` and `positionMethod`. Logical sides follow the Ledger locale or Content's explicit `dir`.

The surface is Ledger's bold neutral fill with inverse text in `font.body.small`, at most 320px wide (`dimension.part.tooltip`) within the available space; `style` overrides the width. The arrow is 8px with the small radius. In forced colours, where the fill and the shadow are replaced, the popup keeps a CanvasText outline. Content stays inside an enclosing dialog's portal boundary, so it remains visible and hoverable there. It sits on `layer.tooltip`, the top layer, above a toast, so a toast action's label shows over it.

_Example: story `Stories.TooltipMatrix`._

## Timing and interaction

TooltipProvider shares hover timing across a group: the first tooltip opens after `delay`, 300ms, and a neighbour opens at once for `timeout`, 300ms, after the last one closed. Shell mounts one, so every tooltip in an application shares it; a product without a Shell mounts one near its root. Outside any provider, Base UI waits 600ms and groups nothing.

Keyboard focus opens a tooltip at once, without the hover delay. Trigger accepts `delay`, `closeDelay` and `closeOnClick`; a Trigger's own `delay` overrides the provider's. Moving the pointer into the popup keeps it open; leaving both, moving focus away, clicking the trigger or pressing Escape dismisses it. Trigger clicks close it by default; `closeOnClick={false}` keeps it. A tap runs the trigger's action without opening a hover tooltip.

Use Root's `defaultOpen`, or controlled `open` with `onOpenChange(open, details)`. `details.cancel()` rejects a state change. Generic payloads let several triggers share one Root and provide content through its children function.

_Example: story `Stories.IconButtons`._

## Accessibility

- **A tooltip is visual only by default.** Base UI adds no `role="tooltip"` and no `aria-describedby`, so the trigger needs its own accessible name, and what the reader must know stays visible on the page.
- **`describe` says its words too.** On TooltipContent it renders a visually hidden copy that is always on the page and makes it the trigger's accessible description, so a screen reader hears the shortcut or the qualifier the name leaves out. Use it when the tooltip adds words to the name; a tooltip that only repeats the name needs no `describe`.
- **Name a shortcut with `aria-keyshortcuts`** on the trigger ("Meta+K Control+K"), as well as showing it with Kbd.
- **Keep controls and links out of the popup**; content the reader interacts with belongs in a Popover.
- **Inside a Dialog**, Escape closes an open tooltip first and keeps focus on its trigger; the next Escape can dismiss the dialog.

## Unavailable actions

Trigger's `disabled` stops the tooltip; it does not disable the rendered button. To explain an action that truly cannot run, give the Button or IconButton `disabledReason`: the button is disabled with `aria-disabled` but stays in the Tab order, the reason shows in a tooltip on hover, on keyboard focus and on a tap, and it becomes the button's accessible description. Do not wrap a disabled button in a focusable span, and do not put the reason in a `title`, which a disabled button never shows. Prefer an enabled action that explains itself on use, such as a submit that reports what is missing.

_Example: story `Stories.Unavailable`._

## Props

Props follow Base UI's [Provider](https://base-ui.com/react/components/tooltip#provider), [Root](https://base-ui.com/react/components/tooltip#root), [Trigger](https://base-ui.com/react/components/tooltip#trigger) and [Popup](https://base-ui.com/react/components/tooltip#popup), with the positioner's props on Content and Ledger's `describe`. See [shadcn Tooltip](https://ui.shadcn.com/docs/components/base/tooltip) for its source composition.

### TooltipContent

_Props of `TooltipContent`, generated from its types:_

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `className` | `string \| ((state: TooltipPopupState) => string)` |  | CSS class applied to the element, or a function that returns a class based on the component's state. |
| `render` | `ReactElement<unknown, string \| JSXElementConstructor<any>> \| ComponentRenderFn<HTMLProps, TooltipPopupState>` |  | Allows you to replace the component's HTML element with a different tag, or compose it with another component. Accepts a `ReactElement` or a function that returns the element to render. |
| `style` | `CSSProperties \| ((state: TooltipPopupState) => CSSProperties)` |  | Style applied to the element, or a function that returns a style object based on the component's state. |
| `sticky` | `boolean` | `false` | Whether to maintain the popup in the viewport after the anchor element was scrolled out of view. |
| `side` | `"bottom" \| "inline-end" \| "inline-start" \| "left" \| "right" \| "top"` | `top` | Which side of the anchor element to align the popup against. May automatically change to avoid collisions. |
| `align` | `"center" \| "end" \| "start"` | `start` | How to align the popup relative to the specified side. |
| `sideOffset` | `number \| OffsetFunction` | `4` | Distance between the anchor and the popup in pixels. Also accepts a function that returns the distance to read the dimensions of the anchor and positioner elements, along with its side and alignment. The function takes a `data` object parameter with the following properties: - `data.anchor`: the dimensions of the anchor element with properties `width` and `height`. - `data.positioner`: the dimensions of the positioner element with properties `width` and `height`. - `data.side`: which side of the anchor element the positioner is aligned against. - `data.align`: how the positioner is aligned relative to the specified side. @example ```jsx <Positioner sideOffset={({ side, align, anchor, positioner }) => { return side === 'top' \|\| side === 'bottom' ? anchor.height : anchor.width; }} /> ``` |
| `alignOffset` | `number \| OffsetFunction` | `0` | Additional offset along the alignment axis in pixels. Also accepts a function that returns the offset to read the dimensions of the anchor and positioner elements, along with its side and alignment. The function takes a `data` object parameter with the following properties: - `data.anchor`: the dimensions of the anchor element with properties `width` and `height`. - `data.positioner`: the dimensions of the positioner element with properties `width` and `height`. - `data.side`: which side of the anchor element the positioner is aligned against. - `data.align`: how the positioner is aligned relative to the specified side. @example ```jsx <Positioner alignOffset={({ side, align, anchor, positioner }) => { return side === 'top' \|\| side === 'bottom' ? anchor.width : anchor.height; }} /> ``` |
| `anchor` | `Element \| VirtualElement \| RefObject<Element \| null> \| (() => Element \| VirtualElement \| null) \| null` |  | An element to position the popup against. By default, the popup will be positioned against the trigger. |
| `collisionAvoidance` | `CollisionAvoidance` |  | Determines how to handle collisions when positioning the popup. `side` controls overflow on the preferred placement axis (`top`/`bottom` or `left`/`right`): - `'flip'`: keep the requested side when it fits; otherwise try the opposite side (`top` and `bottom`, or `left` and `right`). - `'shift'`: never change side; keep the requested side and move the popup within the clipping boundary so it stays visible. - `'none'`: do not correct side-axis overflow. `align` controls overflow on the alignment axis (`start`/`center`/`end`): - `'flip'`: keep side, but swap `start` and `end` when the requested alignment overflows. - `'shift'`: keep side and requested alignment, then nudge the popup along the alignment axis to fit. - `'none'`: do not correct alignment-axis overflow. `fallbackAxisSide` controls fallback behavior on the perpendicular axis when the preferred axis cannot fit: - `'start'`: allow perpendicular fallback and try the logical start side first (`top` before `bottom`, or `left` before `right` in LTR). - `'end'`: allow perpendicular fallback and try the logical end side first (`bottom` before `top`, or `right` before `left` in LTR). - `'none'`: do not fallback to the perpendicular axis. When `side` is `'shift'`, explicitly setting `align` only supports `'shift'` or `'none'`. If `align` is omitted, it defaults to `'flip'`. @example ```jsx <Positioner collisionAvoidance={{ side: 'shift', align: 'shift', fallbackAxisSide: 'none', }} /> ``` |
| `collisionBoundary` | `Boundary` | `'clipping-ancestors'` | An element or a rectangle that delimits the area that the popup is confined to. |
| `collisionPadding` | `Padding` | `5` | Additional space to maintain from the edge of the collision boundary. |
| `positionMethod` | `"absolute" \| "fixed"` | `'absolute'` | Determines which CSS `position` property to use. |
| `describe` | `boolean` | `false` | Also say the tooltip's words to assistive technology: a visually hidden copy, always on the page, becomes the trigger's accessible description (`aria-describedby`). For words the trigger's name leaves out, such as a keyboard shortcut; the trigger keeps its own name. A tooltip is visual only without it. |

### TooltipProvider

_Props of `TooltipProvider`, generated from its types:_

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `delay` | `number` | `300` | How long to wait before opening the tooltip on hover. Specified in milliseconds. |
| `closeDelay` | `number` |  | How long to wait before closing a tooltip. Specified in milliseconds. |
| `timeout` | `number` | `300` | Another tooltip will open instantly if the previous tooltip is closed within this timeout. Specified in milliseconds. |

## Related

[IconButton](?path=/docs/components-iconbutton--docs) · [Kbd](?path=/docs/components-kbd--docs) · [HoverCard](?path=/docs/components-hovercard--docs) · [Popover](?path=/docs/components-popover--docs) · [Overlays](?path=/docs/components-overlays--docs)

# Tree

**Status: Stable.**

A hierarchy the reader opens and closes: control families, a system's composition, a folder of evidence. The caller owns the data, the open set and the selection and renders one row per visible node; the tree draws the indent guides, the chevron on rows that have children, and owns the keyboard: one tab stop, the arrows move and open, Enter selects. The ARIA tree pattern is the model.

A tree is for two or more levels. One level is a collapsible [Item](?path=/docs/components-item--docs) list; a hierarchy with columns is [Table.Tree](?path=/docs/components-table--docs).

_Example: story `Stories.TreeMatrix`._

## Anatomy

| Part     | What it is                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| -------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Row      | One visible node, 32px (`small`) or 24px (`xsmall`), the tree item itself: focusable, selected on a click.                                                                                                                                                              |
| Guides   | One 16px column per ancestor level, a hairline down it while that ancestor's branch continues (`lines`).                                                                                                                                                                |
| Chevron  | On a branch: right while closed, down while open. A click on it opens or closes without selecting. A leaf has a small dot in its place.                                                                                                                                 |
| Icon     | Optional, before the label, 16px: a folder for a branch, a document for a leaf. On every row, or on none.                                                                                                                                                               |
| Label    | `font.body` in `color.text`, one line: a long label is cut with an ellipsis and shows whole on hover and while its row has keyboard focus. It is the row's accessible name, and nothing else is.                                                                        |
| Hint     | Optional, after the label, `font.body.small` in `color.text.subtle`: a code, a kind, the profile a system adopts. It takes only the room the label leaves, so it is cut first, and is its own tooltip on hover. Read as the row's description.                          |
| Trailing | At the end: a Count of what is beneath, a Badge for the row's state, a Dot. Read as the row's description after the hint; text in it gives way beside the label as the row narrows and is its own tooltip on hover, so the row's keyboard focus reveals only the label. |
| Actions  | After the trailing: the row's menu button. Each control is its own tab stop and is neither the row's name nor its description.                                                                                                                                          |

## Variants

Tree has one appearance. What varies:

| Variant    | Use                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| ---------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Selectable | Rows with `onSelect` and one `isSelected`: the tree is a navigator, and the selected row is where the reader is. The composition browser, the families rail.                             |
| Read-only  | No `onSelect` and no `isSelected`: the tree only shows shape, its rows carry no `aria-selected` and do not answer the pointer. Rare; a hierarchy worth drawing is usually worth opening. |
| With icons | An icon on every row, so labels at one level align; see Don't.                                                                                                                           |

_Example: story `Stories.ReadOnly`._

Not built, and why: multi-select with checkboxes, because bulk work on nodes is a table; drag to reorder, because nothing here is rearranged by hand; a tree that owns its data, because the callers already flatten a tree with rolled-up posture on every row.

## Sizes

| Size     | Row  | Where                                                           |
| -------- | ---- | --------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `small`  | 32px | The default: a composition browser, a families rail.            |
| `xsmall` | 24px | A deep tree that must show more at once; a tree inside a panel. |

Rows stack with no space between them. The indent is 16px per level, the guide down its middle.

_Example: story `Stories.Families`._

## States

| State    | What changes                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| -------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Plain    | Text on the surface.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| Hover    | `color.background.neutral.subtle.hovered` across a row that takes `onSelect`. A read-only row has no hover.                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| Selected | `color.background.selected` and a 2px bar at the row's start edge in the selected colour (`color.background.selected.bold`, 3:1 on the fill); `aria-selected`. The row is the initial tab stop; focus can move independently. If its branch is closed, the parent shows the selection instead. In forced colours the row is Highlight. |
| Focus    | The focus outline around the row, on keyboard focus.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| Open     | The chevron down; `aria-expanded="true"`; the children rendered under it by the caller.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| Closed   | The chevron right; `aria-expanded="false"`; a Count in `trailing` says how many are beneath.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |

## Modifiers

- **`depth`** and **`lines`**: how deep, and which ancestors' guides to draw. A last child under each ancestor clears that ancestor's line.
- **`hasChildren`**, **`isExpanded`**, **`onExpandedChange`** on a branch: the chevron, Right and Left call it with the branch's next state, as every disclosure in the kit does (Table.Group, Table.Tree, Table.Disclosure). **`isSelected`**, **`onSelect`** on a selectable row. `expanded` and `onToggle` are the deprecated names for `isExpanded` and `onExpandedChange`, still read for one version.
- **`hint`** for a code, a kind or a profile beside the name. It is cut before the label is.
- **`trailing`** for a Count, a Badge or a Dot. A click on it selects the row, as a click on the label does.
- **`actions`** for the row's controls: a menu button, a remove button. A click on one runs the control and leaves the selection alone.
- **`size`** on the tree; **`label`** names it.

## Content

- **Branch labels say what kind of children they hold**: "Finance", "Payables", "Ground segment".
- **Leaf labels say what the node is**: "CTRL-0412 Segregation of duties", "mission-api:2.1.4".
- **Icons on every row or none**: a folder and a document, and nothing else.
- **The count beneath a closed branch goes in `trailing`**, so a closed tree still says how big it is.
- **A code, a kind or a profile goes in `hint`**, never in `trailing` beside the Badge: at a phone's width the trailing slot would take the name's room.

_Example: story `Stories.LongNames`._

## Style

| Element  | Token                                                                                                                                                                      |
| -------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Row      | `dimension.control.medium` 32px `small` · `dimension.control.xsmall` 24px `xsmall` · `radius.medium` · `space.100` end padding · `space.075` between parts                 |
| Guide    | 16px column (`space.200`) · 1px `color.border`                                                                                                                             |
| Chevron  | `IconButton size="xxsmall"`, the kit's 20px row control, with no tooltip · `color.text.subtle`, `color.text` on hover · `radius.small` · rotates in `motion.duration.fast` |
| Leaf dot | 4px · `color.background.neutral.pressed`                                                                                                                                   |
| Label    | `font.body` · `color.text` · one line, cut with an ellipsis                                                                                                                |
| Hint     | `font.body.small` · `color.text.subtle` · one line, cut before the label                                                                                                   |
| Hover    | `color.background.neutral.subtle.hovered`                                                                                                                                  |
| Selected | `color.background.selected` · a 2px (`space.025`) bar in `color.background.selected.bold` at the start edge, `space.050` from the top and bottom                           |
| Focus    | The focus outline                                                                                                                                                          |

The selected fill is the one a table row and a list row take, so a selection reads the same everywhere; the bar at the start edge is its second cue, because the fill alone is about 1.1:1 against the surface. A table row's selection is carried by its checkbox instead. In a right-to-left tree the bar sits on the right and a closed branch's chevron points left.

_Example: story `Stories.SelectedAndRightToLeft`._

The tree retains one entry tab stop as rows are selected, removed or collapsed. Typing a label prefix moves focus without selecting. Flat visible rows receive inferred `aria-posinset` and `aria-setsize`; for partial or virtualized sibling sets, supply `posInSet` and `setSize` with the complete sibling position and count.

## Accessibility

- **It is a tree**: `role="tree"` named by `label`, every row a `treeitem` with `aria-level`, `aria-selected` on a row that can be selected, and `aria-expanded` on a branch: the ARIA pattern.
- **The row's name is its label.** The hint and the text or Count in `trailing` are its description, heard after the name ("Finance, 12"); the controls in `actions` are neither, so an arrow-key move reads the node and not its buttons.
- **One entry tab stop per tree.** Initially the selected row is tabbable, or the first row when none is. Arrow navigation moves that tab stop without selecting; returning to the tree retains the last focused row. Removing that row restores focus to a preceding visible row when focus would otherwise be lost.
- **Keyboard:** Down and Up move between visible rows; Right opens a closed branch, or moves into an open one; Left closes an open branch, or moves to the parent; Home and End go to the ends; Enter or Space selects. In a right-to-left tree Left and Right swap, so the key toward the reading direction's end opens.
- **The chevron is for the pointer.** It focuses and toggles the branch without selecting it. It is hidden from the keyboard and screen readers, which have Right and Left. Where any pointer is coarse its hit area is 24px, centred on the 20px chevron.
- **Row controls are outside the model.** A button in `actions` is its own tab stop, outside the arrow keys; keep to one per row where the tree is long.
- **The selection is never hidden.** When the selected row's branch is closed, the caller selects the parent, so the reader does not lose their place.

_Example: story `Stories.Keyboard`._

Tree and Tree.Item accept native div attributes, styles, events and refs, and name themselves last with `data-slot` (`tree`, `tree-item`). Caller handlers run before the built-in one, and `preventDefault()` cancels it: a reserved key, a locked selection. Use `onKeyDownCapture` on the root to reserve keys before the rows see them. Item's `onSelect` is the node-selection callback, not the native text-selection event. The roles and row levels are the tree's own. An explicit `aria-label` overrides the root's `label`, and on a row replaces the label as its name; `posInSet` and `setSize`, or native sibling metadata, override the inferred counts.

_Example: story `Stories.NativeAttributes`._

The keyboard behavior follows the [WAI-ARIA tree view pattern](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/treeview/). Root refs compose through [Base UI useRender](https://base-ui.com/react/utils/use-render#merging-refs).

## Props

_Props of `Tree`, generated from its types:_

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `label` (required) | `string` |  | The tree's accessible name: "Control families", "System composition". |
| `size` | `"small" \| "xsmall"` |  | `small` is the default, 32px rows; `xsmall` is 24px, for a deep tree that must show more at once. |

### Tree.Item

_Props of `Tree.Item`, generated from its types:_

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `depth` (required) | `number` |  | How deep the node sits, 0 at the root. One indent per level. |
| `posInSet` | `number` |  | Explicit sibling metadata for partial or virtualized trees. Otherwise inferred from visible rows. |
| `setSize` | `number` |  |  |
| `lines` | `boolean[]` |  | One flag per ancestor level: draw the guide at that depth. Defaults to every level. |
| `hasChildren` | `boolean` | `false` | A branch: the row takes a chevron and `aria-expanded`. |
| `isExpanded` | `boolean` |  | The branch is open. |
| `expanded` | `boolean` |  | The branch is open. @deprecated Use `isExpanded`, the name that matches `isSelected`; `expanded` is read for one version. |
| `onExpandedChange` | `((expanded: boolean) => void)` |  | Called with the branch's next state when the chevron, Right or Left opens or closes it. |
| `isSelected` | `boolean` |  | The row is selected. It is the initial tab stop; keyboard focus can move independently. A row that takes neither this nor `onSelect` is not selectable and carries no `aria-selected`. |
| `onSelect` | `(() => void)` |  | Selects the node: a click on the row, Enter or Space. |
| `hint` | `ReactNode` |  | Muted text after the label: a code, a kind, the profile a system adopts. It takes only the room the label leaves, so it is cut before the label is, and it is read as the row's description. |
| `trailing` | `ReactNode` |  | At the end of the row: a Count, a Badge, a Dot. It is read as the row's description; text in it truncates as the row narrows and is its own tooltip on hover. A control belongs in `actions`. |
| `actions` | `ReactNode` |  | Controls at the row's end, after `trailing`: the row's menu button. Each is a tab stop of its own, outside the tree's keyboard, and none is part of the row's name or description. |

## Don't

Icons go on every row or on none, and one level of nesting is a collapsible Item list, never a tree. A collapsed branch that holds the selected row takes `isSelected` itself, so the reader still sees where they are, and a tree item never holds a tree: entries with columns of their own are a Table.Tree.
