<!-- page: Components/Truncate (src/stories/components/Truncate.mdx) -->

# Truncate

**Status: Stable.**

Text cut to one, two or three lines (`maxLines`, as on Text) with an ellipsis, and the whole of it in a tooltip while it is cut. The tooltip opens on hover, and on keyboard focus of the link or button the text sits in or of a control inside it, so a keyboard reader can see a long record name from the list. Nothing opens while the text fits. The full text never leaves the DOM, so a screen reader reads all of it; the tooltip is a visual copy and is hidden from assistive technology.

```tsx
<TextLink render={<Link to="/controls/ac-2" />}>
  <Truncate>Automated temporary and emergency account management</Truncate>
</TextLink>
```

_Example: story `Stories.TruncateMatrix`._

## When to use it

- **A name in a row, a rail or a list** that must stay on its line: a record name in a register, a value in a KeyValue, a title in a narrow panel. KeyValue and a clamped [Text](?path=/docs/primitives-text--docs) (`maxLines`) already reveal themselves; use Truncate where neither applies.
- **Not for a sentence.** A statement, an objective, an error or a notification wraps: give Text no `maxLines`, or KeyValue `wrap`. A tooltip is for a name that does not fit, not for reading.
- **Not for a heading.** A page, section or dialog title wraps.
- **An identifier or a hash** wraps anywhere rather than being cut, where the row allows it (KeyValue `wrap`).

## Long content

The kit's rule for text longer than its room is the component library guide's Long content section (`docs/guides/component-library.md`), and Truncate is the reveal it relies on: where the rule lets a row's field cut its text, the field cuts through Truncate, KeyValue or a clamped Text, so the whole is always a hover or a focus away. The content pages (Badge, Count, Indicator, FilterChip, Id, TextLink, Typography, Fact, CodeBlock, Avatar, Attachment, DateTime and Diff) each say under Long content how their part applies the rule.

## How it reveals

| The reader           | What happens                                                                                                        |
| -------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Hovers the text      | The tooltip opens after the tooltip provider's delay, only while the text is cut.                                   |
| Tabs to its link     | A Truncate inside a link, button, tab, menu item, option or tree item opens as the host takes keyboard focus.       |
| Tabs into it         | A Truncate that holds a control (a TextLink in a KeyValue value) opens as the control takes keyboard focus.         |
| Presses Escape       | The tooltip closes; focus stays where it was.                                                                       |
| Taps it              | Nothing opens: a touch has no hover. Where the whole name matters on a phone, let the row open the record, or wrap. |
| Uses a screen reader | The whole text is read in place. The tooltip is `aria-hidden`.                                                      |

A `title` of your own replaces the tooltip rather than stacking a second one on it. `fullText` sets what the tooltip says when the element's own text is not the words to show.

_Example: story `Stories.RevealsOnKeyboardFocus`._

In a [Table](?path=/docs/components-table--docs)'s body cell that truncates, a one-line Truncate mounts no tooltip of its own: the table's one reveal shows a cut part of the cell whole, on hover, on keyboard focus and after a long press, so a register of status Badges and names mounts one tooltip rather than one per cell. The Truncate carries `data-reveal="cell"` there. A Truncate with `maxLines` of two or three or with `fullText`, one in a heading, one in a wrapping cell, one in a detail row and one in a card, a menu or a dialog the cell opens (drawn outside the table) keep their own tooltip.

_Example: story `Stories.InTableCell`._

## The element

A `span` set as a block by default. `render` makes it another element with its own props (`<dd />`, `<p />`), which keeps its own display; the one-line clamp needs a block or a flex item to cut. One line clips across only (`overflow-x: clip`), so a focus ring and a touch area inside it reach above and below the line; two and three lines clamp, which clips both ways. On one line the text also counts as cut when a child cuts its own text with an ellipsis, as a link that is a whole KeyValue value does, so the reveal still opens.

_Example: story `Stories.RenderedAs`._

## useIsTruncated

`useIsTruncated(ref, { maxLines })` reports whether an element you truncate yourself is cut right now. It measures after every render and whenever the element resizes or its text changes, so it follows a panel opening or a column resizing. Use it for a decision that depends on the cut (showing a "Show more", say); Truncate itself measures when it is about to reveal and needs no hook.

_Example: story `Stories.UseIsTruncatedHook`._

## Accessibility

- **The text is all there.** Truncation is CSS; a screen reader reads the whole, and the tooltip is not announced twice.
- **Keyboard reaches it through the control it belongs to.** A plain truncated value with nothing focusable around it is not made a tab stop; where a keyboard reader needs it whole, wrap it.
- **Touch has no reveal.** A truncated name in a list is fine when the row opens the record; anything a phone reader must read whole wraps.
- **Right to left**, the ellipsis sits at the logical end (the RightToLeft story). Reduced motion removes the tooltip's fade.

## Props

_Props of `Truncate`, generated from its types:_

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `children` | `ReactNode` |  | The text, or a composed value (a name and a code, a TextLink); the reveal shows its text. |
| `maxLines` | `1 \| 2 \| 3` |  | How many lines it keeps before the ellipsis, as Text's `maxLines`. 1 by default. |
| `fullText` | `string` |  | What the reveal shows when the text is cut. Defaults to the element's own text, whitespace collapsed. |
| `render` | `ReactElement<unknown, string \| JSXElementConstructor<any>>` |  | The element, with its own props: `<dd />`, `<p />`, a `Text`. A `span` set as a block by default. A given element keeps its own display. |
| `ref` | `Ref<HTMLElement>` |  |  |

### Playground

_Example: story `Stories.Playground`._

_Rendered in the Storybook: Controls._

## Related

- [Text](?path=/docs/primitives-text--docs): `maxLines` clamps a Text and reveals it the same way.
- [KeyValue](?path=/docs/components-keyvalue--docs): its label and value reveal themselves when cut.
- [Tooltip](?path=/docs/components-tooltip--docs): the surface the reveal uses.

## Don't

A name in a row is wrapped in Truncate, which shows the whole of it on hover and keyboard focus, never cut by a bare `truncate` class. A statement wraps, and is never cut to a line.

_Example: story `Stories.Dont`._

<!-- page: Components/Typography (src/stories/components/Typography.mdx) -->

# Typography

**Status: Stable.**

The small text parts a record page is made of, beyond body copy and titles. `Eyebrow` is the uppercase micro-label on `font.heading.xxsmall`: a section's name in a rail, a record's kind above its title, a callout's label. `Absent` is the muted dash where a value would be, which a screen reader hears as "Not recorded" or as the `label` it is given. `Prose` is authored text: one paragraph or several, with the line breaks it was written with, a safe Markdown subset on request, under an optional Eyebrow label. For body copy and titles, the [Text](?path=/docs/primitives-text--docs) and [Heading](?path=/docs/primitives-heading--docs) primitives; this page is the three parts between them.

_Example: story `Stories.TypographyMatrix`._

## Anatomy

| Part    | What it is                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Eyebrow | `font.heading.xxsmall`, uppercase, `color.text.subtle`; a tone colours it. A `div`, or the element `as` names.                                                                                                                             |
| Absent  | An em dash in `color.text.subtlest`, the size of its line. The dash is `aria-hidden`; beside it, [VisuallyHidden](?path=/docs/primitives-visuallyhidden--docs) text says what is missing: the `label`, else the locale's `absent` message. |
| Prose   | An optional Eyebrow, then the text in `font.body` (or `font.body.large` with `size="large"`) and `color.text`: `space.050` under the Eyebrow, `space.075` above a labelled Prose, `space.100` between paragraphs (`space.150` at large).   |

## Variants

| Part    | Use                                                                                                                                                                   |
| ------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Eyebrow | The name of a group of rows in a rail (`as="h3"`), the kind above a record's title, the label of a callout (with a tone), the label of a value in a grid (`as="dt"`). |
| Absent  | Any value that is not there: in a KeyValue, a Fact, a cell.                                                                                                           |
| Prose   | Authored text with or without a name: a rationale, an implementation statement, a control statement, a narrative. In a rail or a detail body.                         |

Not built, and why: a description-list primitive, because KeyValue and Fact are the two shapes of a pair; a "no data" word in place of the dash, because the dash is the product's one absent mark and reads in a column; an Eyebrow with an icon or a count, because it is a label and a count is a Count beside it.

## Sizes

One size each. The Eyebrow is `font.heading.xxsmall` whatever it heads; the Absent is its line's size; the Prose paragraph is `font.body`. A rail's Prose is as wide as the rail, a detail body's is the reading measure.

_Example: story `Stories.InRail`._

## Prose

A string is authored text. A blank line starts a paragraph, and a single line break stays in place, so a statement pasted from a document reads as it was written.

_Example: story `Stories.ProseParagraphs`._

`markdown` takes a safe subset: paragraphs; `-`, `*` and `1.` lists, nested by indentation; `*emphasis*` and `**strong**`; `` `inline code` `` and fenced code; `[links](https://…)` and `<https://…>`. Line breaks are kept. Anything else, headings, tables and HTML included, shows as the characters typed. The application renders its own markup (an OSCAL parameter insertion, say) on top of the text it passes in.

_Example: story `Stories.ProseMarkdown`._

Links render as TextLinks with native anchors; `renderLink` makes each one a router link, so the kit stays router-free.

_Example: story `Stories.ProseRouterLinks`._

A bare Absent is heard as the LedgerProvider's `absent` message, "Not recorded" in English; a `label` says more where the context knows more.

_Example: story `Stories.AbsentDefault`._

_Example: story `Stories.AbsentLabelled`._

## States

None. The three are text. The tone on an Eyebrow or a Prose is a colour for a callout, not a state.

## Modifiers

- **Eyebrow `tone`** for a callout's label: `warning` over a condition, `danger` over a finding. `neutral`, the default, is `color.text.subtle`.
- **Eyebrow `as`**: `h3` or `h4` when it heads a section, so the page's outline has it; `dt` when it labels a value; `span` inline.
- **Prose `label`** and **`tone`**: the text's name, and its colour when it is a callout. Leave the label out under a heading of its own.
- **Prose children as a string** are authored text: a blank line starts a paragraph, and a line break stays a line break (`white-space: pre-line`). Composed inline content (words and a TextLink) is one paragraph.
- **Prose `markdown`** renders a safe subset in place of the children, and **`renderLink`** sends its links through a router's link element.
- **Prose `size`**: `medium` in a rail, `large` for reading text at the measure.
- **Absent `label`**: what a screen reader hears for the empty value when the context says more than "Not recorded": "None", "No due date", "Not available".

## Content

- **An eyebrow is one to three words**, a noun: "Schedule", "By supplier origin", "Rationale". Uppercase is set by the component; write it in sentence case.
- **Prose keeps the author's paragraphs.** Pass the text as written; do not split it into several Prose to get paragraphs, and do not add `<br>`s.
- **The dash means nothing here.** "N/A" means not applicable, "Unknown" means unknown; those are values and are written as words.

## Long content

- **Prose always wraps.** It never truncates and never clamps: authored text is read whole. An unbroken token in it (a URL, a hash, an id) breaks where it must, so it never pushes its column wider. A long statement in a record body takes `size="large"` at the measure.
- **An Eyebrow is one to three words** and does not wrap in practice; a longer name is a heading.
- **Absent is one character** and has nothing to cut.

_Example: story `Stories.ProseLongContent`._

## Style

| Element | Token                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| ------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Eyebrow | `font.heading.xxsmall` · uppercase · `color.text.subtle` · `color.text.<tone>` when toned                                                                                                                   |
| Absent  | `color.text.subtlest` · the line's font                                                                                                                                                                     |
| Prose   | `font.body` or `font.body.large` · `color.text` · `space.050` under the eyebrow · `space.075` above · `space.100` or `space.150` between paragraphs · inline code `font.code` on `elevation.surface.sunken` |

An eyebrow is `color.text.subtle`, as all secondary text is; the Shell's section headings and the preview eyebrow take the same colour.

## Accessibility

- **An eyebrow that heads a section is a heading**, with `as="h3"` or `h4`, so the page's outline lists it and a screen reader can jump to it. As a `div` it is a label and is read in place.
- **Uppercase is styling**, so a screen reader reads the words, not the letters; write the text in sentence case.
- **Absent always speaks.** Screen readers skip an em dash at their default punctuation level, so a bare dash sounds like a skipped row. Absent hides the dash and reads words in its place: the `label` when one is given, else the LedgerProvider's `absent` message, "Not recorded" in English, which a product translates with the rest of the kit's words.
- **Prose Markdown injects no HTML.** The source is parsed into React elements; `<script>` and any other markup show as the characters typed. A link whose address is not http(s), mailto, tel or relative (a `javascript:` or `data:` address) shows as its words, not as a link. Links in Prose are underlined, so they are told apart from the text by more than colour.
- **Contrast:** `color.text.subtle` at 11px uppercase passes 4.5:1, and `color.text.subtlest` does for the dash; the gate runs every tone.

## Props

### Eyebrow

_Props of `Eyebrow`, generated from its types:_

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `children` (required) | `ReactNode` |  | One to three words, set in uppercase by the component: a section's name, a record's kind, a callout's label. |
| `tone` | `"danger" \| "information" \| "neutral" \| "success" \| "warning"` | `neutral` | A colour for a callout's label; `neutral`, the default, is the subtle text colour. |
| `as` | `"dd" \| "div" \| "dt" \| "em" \| "figcaption" \| "h2" \| "h3" \| "h4" \| "label" \| "legend" \| "li" \| "p" \| "small" \| "span" \| "strong"` | `div` | The element: `div` by default; `h3` or `h4` when the eyebrow heads a section, `dt` when it labels a value. |
| `ref` | `Ref<HTMLElement>` |  |  |

Eyebrow takes its element's native props and a ref, whichever `as` names, and names itself last with `data-slot="eyebrow"`. Absent and Prose take a span's and a div's.

_Example: story `Stories.EyebrowNativeAttributes`._

### Absent

_Props of `Absent`, generated from its types:_

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `label` | `string` |  | What a screen reader hears in place of the dash, when the context says more than the default: "None", "No due date", "Not available". Without it, the LedgerProvider's `absent` message, "Not recorded" in English. The dash itself is always hidden from assistive technology, which skips it at default punctuation settings. |

### Prose

_Props of `Prose`, generated from its types:_

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `label` | `string` |  | The text's name, as an Eyebrow: "Rationale", "Condition". Leave it out for a body of text under a heading of its own. |
| `tone` | `"danger" \| "information" \| "neutral" \| "success" \| "warning"` | `neutral` | Colours the label for a callout. |
| `children` | `ReactNode` |  | The text. A string is authored text: a blank line starts a paragraph and a line break stays a line break. Composed inline content (words with a TextLink) is one paragraph. |
| `markdown` | `string` |  | The text as a safe Markdown subset, in place of `children`: paragraphs, `-` and `1.` lists, `*emphasis*`, `**strong**`, `` `code` ``, fenced code and `[links](https://…)`. Line breaks are kept. Anything else, HTML included, shows as the characters typed. |
| `renderLink` | `((href: string) => ReactElement<unknown, string \| JSXElementConstructor<any>>)` |  | The element a Markdown link renders through, for a router: `(href) => <Link to={href} />`. A native anchor by default. |
| `size` | `"large" \| "medium"` | `medium` | `medium` (font.body, the default) in a rail; `large` (font.body.large) for reading text at the measure. |

### Playground

_Example: story `Stories.Playground`._

_Rendered in the Storybook: Controls._

## Related

- [Text](?path=/docs/primitives-text--docs), [Heading](?path=/docs/primitives-heading--docs): body copy and titles.
- [KeyValue](?path=/docs/components-keyvalue--docs), [Fact](?path=/docs/components-fact--docs): the two shapes of a labelled value.
- [Alert](?path=/docs/components-alert--docs): the callout an eyebrow with a tone often heads.

## Don't

An Eyebrow is one to three words, never an uppercase sentence. A labelled paragraph is Prose under its Eyebrow, never a bold run-in label with a colon, and a missing value is Absent, the muted dash, never N/A.

_Example: story `Stories.Dont`._

<!-- page: Layout/PageHeader (src/stories/layout/PageHeader.mdx) -->

# PageHeader

**Status: Stable.**

One composable page header for collections and records. Two columns: Heading, what names the page, on the left; Actions on the right; Lead across both above them. Native props and refs pass through every part.

_Example: story `Stories.Collection`._
_Example: story `Stories.Record`._
_Example: story `Stories.Constrained`._

Compose a Heading with a Title, an optional Lead and one primary action or an Actions menu. A breadcrumb is the Lead through `render={<Breadcrumb />}`; a category line is a Lead with text. A register's header is its name alone: its create action is the toolbar's primary. A record's header is the trail, the name and its actions: a code goes in the trail, and record fields, owner and status editors and property strips belong in the work area or the Aside, not in PageHeader or a preview header.

_Example: story `Stories.DoDont`._

Use PageHeader.Title once for the page's h1. Actions sit at the end of the title's row while the row can give the title its measure (14rem) beside them; when it cannot, on a phone or in a narrow panel, they take the next row, right-aligned, and the title wraps at its full width. The same rule holds on a page, in a Shell.Panel and in a Sheet (the Stacked story). Keep action groups on one line; use a menu when several actions compete for space.

## When to use

- **Every page and every preview's record.** A page's header names it; a preview's inner header names its record, below the panel's navigation-only header.
- **Not for a section of a page.** A titled block inside the page is a [Section](?path=/docs/layout-section--docs).
- **Not for a dialog's title.** A dialog or a sheet has its own header part; PageHeader.Title renders through it with `render` only where a sheet's body starts with a record header, as in PreviewSheet.

## Actions and their sizes

| Where                    | Actions                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| ------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| A register               | None. The create action is the Toolbar's small primary.                                                                                                                                            |
| A record page            | One default-size primary Button, or one default-size Actions menu: a Button labelled Actions with a trailing ChevronDown, its items the record's operations, and a link item for each destination. |
| A preview's inner header | One small primary, then the rest behind a subtle small IconButton that opens a menu.                                                                                                               |

A destination in an Actions menu is a link item (`DropdownMenuLinkItem`, or an item rendered as a router link), so it opens in a new tab; a Button in the header acts, never navigates.

_Example: story `Stories.WithDescription`._

Description is for a page outside the register and record shapes, such as a settings page or a setup step: one line of orientation under the title. It wraps, and a long unbroken value breaks rather than widening the page.

## Title levels

The Title is a [Heading](?path=/docs/primitives-heading--docs) at `page`, 20/26 semibold, and the h1 on a page. Inside a [HeadingLevelProvider](?path=/docs/primitives-heading--docs) it takes that level instead: a preview's inner record header, in a panel or a sheet whose outline starts at 2, renders the record's name as an h2 with the same type style. The content after that header goes one level below through a HeadingLevelProvider without `level`, so its Sections are h3s. `render` sets the element outright, `render={<h2 />}`, or a sheet's or a dialog's own title part where the surface needs its title for its accessible name; either keeps the `page` size. A title the PageHeader does not draw is a Heading at the size it matches, never a raw heading with the Title's classes: a change to the ramp would miss it.

_Example: story `Stories.TitleLevels`._

## Accessibility

- **Not a landmark.** The root is a `div`: the page's landmarks are the shell's (Main, the navigation, the Aside and the Panel), and a `header` element inside a dialog or a sheet would become a second banner. `render={<header />}` gives a page the element where it wants one.
- **One h1 a page.** The Title is the page's h1; a preview's record title is an h2 through the heading-level context, never a second h1.
- **The trail is navigation.** A Breadcrumb Lead is a named navigation landmark whose last level is the current page (see [Breadcrumb](?path=/docs/components-breadcrumb--docs)).
- **A page change is announced by the Shell.** When the route changes, `Shell locationKey` moves focus to Main and says the page's name; the header needs no focus handling of its own.
- **Actions keep their names.** An Actions menu's trigger is named by its visible label; an icon-only overflow takes a `label` that names the record ("More artifact actions").

## Props

No other part has props of its own: the root and Lead are a `div` or the element given to `render`, Heading and Actions are `div`s, and Description a `p`; each takes its element's native props and ref, and names itself last with `data-slot`. Title takes `render` and its element's props. Every part is also exported by name (`PageHeaderLead`, `PageHeaderHeading`, `PageHeaderTitle`, `PageHeaderDescription`, `PageHeaderActions`), the same component as the member.

_Props of `PageHeader`, generated from its types:_

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `render` | `ReactElement<unknown, string \| JSXElementConstructor<any>> \| ComponentRenderFn<HTMLProps, {}>` |  | Allows you to replace the component's HTML element with a different tag, or compose it with another component. Accepts a `ReactElement` or a function that returns the element to render. |

### PageHeader.Title

_Props of `PageHeaderTitle`, generated from its types:_

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `render` | `ReactElement<unknown, string \| JSXElementConstructor<any>> \| ComponentRenderFn<HTMLProps, {}>` |  | Allows you to replace the component's HTML element with a different tag, or compose it with another component. Accepts a `ReactElement` or a function that returns the element to render. |

### PageHeader.Lead

_Props of `PageHeaderLead`, generated from its types:_

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `render` | `ReactElement<unknown, string \| JSXElementConstructor<any>> \| ComponentRenderFn<HTMLProps, {}>` |  | Allows you to replace the component's HTML element with a different tag, or compose it with another component. Accepts a `ReactElement` or a function that returns the element to render. |

<!-- page: Layout/Pages (src/stories/layout/Pages.mdx) -->

# Page composition

Mount the application shell once around the router outlet. Routes compose normal primitives and components inside Main and contribute optional Aside or Panel content. There are no collection-page or record-page wrapper APIs. The stories here render the shapes the [Recipes](?path=/docs/guidance-recipes--docs) name, step by step.

## A record

The trail is `PageHeader.Lead` with the record's code as its last level, the name is the h1, and one Actions menu sits at the end of the title's row (a destination in it is a link item). Tabs follow when the record has more than one view. On Overview the body is Sections, a description is Prose, and the Details are the shell's Aside: an Inspector group named Details with the state, owner, identifiers and dates as KeyValue rows, the ones a reader changes in place as Editables. The Aside is rendered first in Overview's panel and carries the status as its `summary`: beside the Sections it is the rail, and on a phone a Details disclosure above them, closed, its row showing the status. It belongs to Overview and leaves with it; a tab that is a register starts with its Toolbar and table, with no heading over them, and fills the work area.

_Example: story `Stories.Record`._

## A register

A page that is one collection: the name alone in the PageHeader, then a DataTable with `fill`, which takes the rest of the window; on a narrow screen it folds lower-priority fields into each row's More fields ("+3") instead of scrolling sideways. Its [Toolbar](?path=/docs/patterns-toolbar--docs) is the table's `toolbar`: the search first, the saved views in `views`, the filters, Columns, Settings and the collection's overflow as its children, and the one small primary at the end. The name is a TextLink to the record. A failed refresh keeps the rows under one Alert with Retry.

_Example: story `Stories.Register`._

## A preview beside a register

The eye on a row's first value opens a Shell.Panel named by its `label`, never by the record. Its outer header holds global navigation only: [PreviewNavigation](?path=/docs/patterns-previewnavigation--docs) (previous, next, the position said with the record's name through `recordLabel`, and a real open-in-new-tab link) in Panel.Actions, then Panel.Close. The body starts with an inner PageHeader whose Title is the record's name, an h2 because the body of an untitled panel starts its outline at 2, beside one small primary and a subtle overflow menu; the properties follow, then the record's Sections one level down through a HeadingLevelProvider. Previous and next walk the table's displayed rows (`displayedRows`), across pages, turning the table to the row's page (`showRow`). The register stays mounted underneath, so its search and a draft in the panel survive; Close and Escape return focus to the eye.

_Example: story `Stories.QueueWithPanel`._
_Example: story `Stories.CompactQueue`._

## Filling the window

`fill` on a DataTable is the `fill-window` utility with `useFillWindow`: the block measures its own offset from the top of the document and takes the rest of the window above Main's bottom inset, its header sticks to its frame, its rows scroll inside and its pagination sits at the bottom. It is never shorter than its toolbar's row, a header, six rows and the pagination; past that the page scrolls again. The height follows the dynamic viewport, so a phone's browser bar never hides the pagination. A Table's `fill` only takes the rest of a bounded column: to fill the window with one, give its parent the `fill-window` class and set the parent's `--fill-top` to the pixels `useFillWindow(ref)` returns for it. Use it for the register that is the page's one block, including a tab that is a register; a register below other content takes its natural height.

## Focus and the sticky shell

The page keeps what focus or an anchor scrolls into view clear of the sticky banner and top nav: the document's scroll padding is their height and `space.200` at the top, and `space.1000` at the bottom. It is the document's own padding, so a dialog, a sheet, a panel or a list that scrolls inside the page brings a focused row wholly into its own view. Below 30rem of height, where the banner and top nav scroll away, the padding is `space.200`.

_Example: story `Stories.FocusStaysInView`._

## Regions and behavior

- **Main** contains the page header, filters, tabs and work area. Keep these visible controls in the route.
- **Aside** provides supporting context, such as a record's Details. It sits beside Main from the `aside` breakpoint (`dimension.breakpoint.aside`, 75rem: 1200px at the default root size), and from the large breakpoint whenever the side nav leaves Main its minimum width beside it: collapsed, or expanded at its default width. Below the aside breakpoint, wherever it would not sit beside Main (below the large breakpoint, beside a side nav the reader widened past that, beside an open Panel), it is a Details disclosure where the route rendered it in the page, closed until the reader opens it, its row carrying the record's state. From the aside breakpoint with a Panel open, it follows Main until the `wide` breakpoint (110rem, 1760px). The breakpoints are tokens; [Metrics](?path=/docs/tokens-metrics--docs) lists them.
- **Panel** holds a selected record or task. From the large breakpoint (64rem, 1024px) it is a resizable column beside Main that runs the full height of the window under the banner; the top nav stops at its edge. Up to the `panel` breakpoint (80rem, 1280px) an open panel shows the side nav collapsed, so the register stays in view beside it, and closing the panel gives the side nav back as the reader left it. Below the large breakpoint it replaces the visible work area under the top nav while Main stays mounted. Close or Escape returns focus to the opener when it still exists.
- **Sheet** is the modal surface for a workflow that needs focus containment. Compose it with the existing Base UI components.

A route contributes at most one Aside and one Panel. Their portal destinations remain stable across route updates. Route React context travels with the contribution, and unmounting the route removes it. Slots appear after mounting; server rendering does not render portaled region content. The application restores its browser workspace before rendering routes.

## Tabs and accessibility

Keep each tab's primary content inside its TabsContent. Supporting context is a separate labelled landmark and is conditional on the selected tab. Give pages one h1, panels an h2, and contextual regions meaningful names. The PageHeader is not a landmark, so the top nav is the page's one banner. Avoid placing modal semantics on a panel that leaves global navigation available.

The examples test route cleanup, retained context, tab relationships, queue state, preview order, resizing, focus return and the fill. Their example route buttons use a horizontal Scroller, so keyboard focus brings each route into view without widening the page on a phone. Responsive behavior is also checked in the application.

## Extending

Compose a new route from Stack, Inline, Grid, PageHeader and the controls it needs. Add a pattern when a repeated interaction earns one, for example record selection, coordinated filtering or calendar scheduling. Layout ownership stays in Shell.

## Related

- [Shell](?path=/docs/layout-shell--docs): the areas a page renders into.
- [Upgrading](?path=/docs/guidance-upgrading--docs#pages): the page shapes that were parts (IndexPage, ShowPage, RecordHeader, PreviewRail, Block) and what each is now.

<!-- page: Layout/PageSkeleton (src/stories/layout/PageSkeleton.mdx) -->

# PageSkeleton

**Status: Stable.**

What a screen looks like before its data arrives, in the shape of the page that is coming, drawn from the [Skeleton](?path=/docs/components-skeleton--docs)'s shapes so the real page lands on the same lines. The router shows it while a route is pending. A page loads progressively: a section that loads on its own draws its own Skeleton inside a page that has already landed.

_Example: story `Stories.PageSkeletonMatrix`._

## Anatomy

| Variant    | Parts                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| ---------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `register` | A heading shape where the PageHeader's title will be, nothing under it; the toolbar's row at `dimension.control.medium` (the search, two filters, the primary at the end); the table's header row and `rows` rows at the row heights DataTable's loading state keeps. |
| `record`   | A line for the trail; the title with an action at the end of its row; a tab strip over a rule; two sections at the reading measure. The Details rail is the shell's Aside, which arrives with the page.                                                               |

## Variants

- **`register`**, the default, for a collection page and for a route the router knows nothing about.
- **`record`**, for a record route: pass `<PageSkeleton variant="record" />` as its pending component.

_Example: story `Stories.Register`._
_Example: story `Stories.Record`._

Not built, and why: a dashboard shape, because a dashboard's widgets load on their own and each draws its own Skeleton; per-section skeletons, because those are the sections' own, drawn from Skeleton where they load.

## Sizes

`rows` sets how many table rows a register draws, 8 by default, about a screen. The skeleton is as wide as the page, and its lines follow the page's width below their own.

_Example: story `Stories.Narrow`._

## States

One state: waiting. It says what it is waiting for once, and the shapes stay until the page replaces it.

## Modifiers

- **`variant`** as in Variants.
- **`rows`** as in Sizes.
- **`label`**: what the wait is, "Loading page" by default (the `loadingPage` message). Name the page when the route knows it: "Loading risks".

## Content

- **The shape of the page that is coming.** A register has no sentence or tabs under its title; a record has a trail, actions and tabs. The swap to the real page moves nothing.
- **Shown after a short delay.** Give the router a pending delay (about 150ms) and a minimum time on screen, so a fast route never flashes it.
- **Never beside content.** It replaces the page; a section that loads later draws its own.

## Style

| Element  | Token                                                                               |
| -------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Title    | Skeleton heading, at most 240px (register) or 320px (record)                        |
| Toolbar  | `dimension.control.medium` high · `space.100` between · `space.200` above the table |
| Rows     | `dimension.row.header`, then `dimension.row` each · `color.border` under every row  |
| Tabs     | three Skeleton lines · `space.250` apart · `color.border` rule · `space.150` under  |
| Sections | a line, then three lines · `space.150` between · at `dimension.layout.measure`      |
| Layout   | `space.300` between the parts                                                       |

## Accessibility

- **Said once.** On mount it sends its `label` to the kit's persistent polite live region (`announce`), which a screen reader has registered before the message arrives; a status region inserted with its words already in it is heard by almost none. Several skeletons that appear together are said once.
- **Found by browsing.** The root is a `role="status"` holding the same words as visually hidden text, so a reader who moves through the page meets them.
- **The shapes are hidden** from assistive technology; the words carry the meaning.
- **Forced colours** draw every shape in `GrayText`, so the page is never blank.
- **Reduced motion stops the pulse**; the shapes stay.

## Props

_Props of `PageSkeleton`, generated from its types:_

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `variant` | `"record" \| "register"` | `register` | The page's shape. `register`, the default: a title, a toolbar row, then a table's rows. `record`: a trail, a title with its actions, a tab strip, then sections. The router shows the default for a route it knows nothing about; a record route passes `record` as its pending component. |
| `rows` | `number` | `8` | How many table rows a register draws, 8 by default: about a screen. |
| `label` | `string` |  | What the wait is, for a screen reader: "Loading page" by default. It is said once, politely, when the skeleton appears. |

### Playground

_Example: story `Stories.Playground`._

_Rendered in the Storybook: Controls._

## Related

- [Skeleton](?path=/docs/components-skeleton--docs): the shapes it is drawn from.
- [Pages](?path=/docs/layout-pages--docs): the pages it stands in for.
- [Spinner](?path=/docs/components-spinner--docs): a wait on an action, not a page.

## Don't

A page on its way is a PageSkeleton in the page's shape, never a spinner. A section that loads on its own draws its own Skeleton, never the page skeleton under a section that has loaded.

_Example: story `Stories.Dont`._

<!-- page: Layout/Section (src/stories/layout/Section.mdx) -->

# Section

**Status: Stable.**

Optional presentation for a titled block of a page. `title`, `count`, `description` and `action` render the built-in header (a count of rows takes `countMax={9999}`, the cap a tab strip's counts take, where Count's own is 99); leave `title` out and compose Section.Header, Section.Heading, Section.Title, Section.Description and Section.Actions yourself when the heading needs a badge or two actions. Native section props and refs pass through every part.

The title is a [Heading](?path=/docs/primitives-heading--docs) at `section`, semibold at body size (13/18), and a one-line title sits centred on its action's row. A rule is opt-in with `divided`: it is drawn inside the header's end, `space.100` above the content, so the content starts clear of it and keeps its own flow.

_Example: story `Stories.Presentation`._
_Example: story `Stories.Composed`._
_Example: story `Stories.Untitled`._

The header wraps by its own width, not the window's, so it behaves the same on a page, in a Shell.Panel and in a Sheet. The Heading keeps a readable measure of about 12rem, or its own width when shorter, and grows; when the row cannot hold that beside the Actions, the Actions take the next row, at the end, and the title keeps its words whole. A short title keeps its action on its row even in a narrow panel.

_Example: story `Stories.InANarrowPanel`._

## Heading levels

A Section's title takes the contextual heading level and its content one level below, so the outline follows the nesting without a level at every call site:

- On a page, where nothing sets a level, the title is an h2 under the PageHeader's h1, and a Section inside it is an h3.
- In a titled Shell.Panel the body starts at 3, under the panel's h2; in a panel with no title (a preview, whose record title is the body's first heading) it starts at 2. The panel starts its own outline wherever in the route it is rendered from (the In a titled panel and In a preview panel stories).
- Under a record title in a preview or a dialog, wrap the content after the header in a [HeadingLevelProvider](?path=/docs/primitives-heading--docs) so its Sections sit one below the title.
- `Section.Title render={<h4 />}` still sets an element outright. An untitled Section changes nothing.

_Example: story `Stories.Nested`._

## Landmarks

A titled Section at the top of its outline, its title an h2, is a region named by its title, so a page's landmark list names its main parts and stays shorter than its heading list. Everywhere else it is a titled block in the heading outline only: under another titled Section, in a titled panel, in a dialog or a sheet, and under a preview's record title. `landmark` decides it outright: `landmark` makes a nested Section a region a reader should be able to jump to, and `landmark={false}` keeps a page-level one out of the list. An untitled Section is never a landmark, whatever `landmark` says.

_Example: story `Stories.Landmarks`._

## Collapsible

`isCollapsible` folds the content under the title: the collapsed Details section for provenance, counts and derivation a reader opens when they need them. The title and its count become a button inside the heading, a chevron after them turns while the content is open, and the action stays in the header, outside the heading. It is closed until `defaultOpen`, or controlled with `open` and `onOpenChange`. Closed content stays mounted and hidden until found, so a draft inside survives and find-in-page opens it. It needs `title`; compose a [CollapsibleHeader](?path=/docs/components-collapsible--docs) for a disclosure that is not a Section.

_Example: story `Stories.Collapsible`._

Use it where a page body has a block the reader may not need. Do not build one from a subtle Button with a ChevronDown or a native `<details>`: neither is in the heading outline, and neither chevron turns. In a rail of facts, the collapsed group is [Inspector.Group](?path=/docs/patterns-inspector--docs) with `defaultOpen={false}`.

_Example: story `Stories.DoDont`._

Use Stack or Grid directly when no titled region is needed. Section imposes no distinction between work, reference, forms or narrative.

## Accessibility

- A titled Section at the top of its outline is a region named by its title; nested, in a panel or under a record title it is a titled block, and `landmark` overrides either (see Landmarks). Untitled, it is a plain container, and `aria-labelledby` never points at a title that is not there.
- `divided` is decoration: the rule carries no meaning of its own, and in forced colours it takes the system's border colour.
- The level follows the outline, as above; check a new composition with a heading list, which should read as a map of the page.
- A collapsible Section's button carries `aria-expanded`, and `aria-controls` while the content is open; Enter and Space toggle it and focus stays on it. The chevron is decoration and holds still under reduced motion.

_Props of `Section`, generated from its types:_

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `title` | `ReactNode` |  | The heading, for the built-in header. Leave it out and compose Section.Header, Section.Heading, Section.Title and Section.Actions yourself. |
| `count` | `string \| number \| null` |  |  |
| `countMax` | `number` |  | The most a number in `count` shows before it reads as `max+`, as Count's `max`: `9999` for a count of rows, as on a tab strip. 99 unsaid. |
| `description` | `ReactNode` |  |  |
| `action` | `ReactNode` |  |  |
| `divided` | `boolean` |  | Draw a rule under the heading when the content needs separation; the content starts `space.100` below it. |
| `landmark` | `boolean` |  | Whether a titled Section is a region landmark named by its title. By default it is one where it heads a part of the page, at the top of its outline (its title an h2): a Section under another titled Section, in a titled panel, in a dialog or under a preview's record title is a titled block in the heading outline only, so the landmark list stays a short map of the page. `true` or `false` decides it outright. An untitled Section is never one. |
| `isCollapsible` | `boolean` |  | Folds the content under the title: the title becomes a button inside the heading, with a chevron after it that turns while the content is open, and the content stays hidden until the reader opens it. For provenance, counts and derivation a reader opens when they need them. Needs `title`. |
| `defaultOpen` | `boolean` |  | With `isCollapsible`, whether it starts open. Closed by default. |
| `open` | `boolean` |  | With `isCollapsible`, the open state, when the caller controls it. |
| `onOpenChange` | `((open: boolean, eventDetails: CollapsibleRootChangeEventDetails) => void)` |  | With `isCollapsible`, called when the reader opens or closes it, with Base UI's event details (`details.cancel()` keeps the state). |

_Props of `Section.Header`, generated from its types:_

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `divided` | `boolean` | `false` | Draw a rule under the heading when the content needs separation; the Section's content starts `space.100` below it. |

Heading, Description and Actions take only their element's native props; Title takes `render` for another element.

<!-- page: Layout/Shell (src/stories/layout/Shell.mdx) -->

# Shell

**Status: Stable.**

The persistent application frame, inspired by [Atlassian's navigation layout](https://atlassian.design/components/navigation-system/layout/). It owns navigation, page gutters, responsive placement and panel scrolling. Product code supplies navigation links and route content.

_Example: story `Stories.Frame`._
_Example: story `Stories.ComposedPanel`._

Mount Shell once in a shared router layout. Place Banner, TopNav, SideNav and Main there. Child routes render Shell.Aside or Shell.Panel to contribute to the frame's stable region slots. Contributions preserve route React context and disappear when their route unmounts. They mount on the client after slot destinations exist. The root is a grid of named areas, so its children are those areas: anything else, such as a dialog, a toast or an alert, portals out of it or goes inside an area, since the grid places a stray child in its first free cell.

Every part renders one element and forwards its native props and its ref to it; AppLogo, Profile, SideNav.Item and Panel.Title take Base UI `render` where the element may change, so Profile is a menu's trigger through `render` and a side nav item is a router link. The SideNav.ToggleButton is a child of TopNav.Start and places itself; TopNav.Search goes in TopNav.Middle and opens the product's [SearchDialog](?path=/docs/patterns-searchdialog--docs); TopNav.End is a named group that renders its children as given, and its TopNav.Item children fold into one More menu when the top nav is narrow (see the end slot below).

Aside contains supporting context. Panel contains dismissible selected-record or task content. With `title` (and `actions`) it renders its built-in header, close and resizer; without them compose Panel.Header, Panel.Back, Panel.Title, Panel.Actions, Panel.Close, Panel.Body and Panel.Splitter yourself, as Composed panel shows, to change the heading's level, the labels or the padding. Panel.onClose is required either way and the Title names the landmark. From the large breakpoint (`dimension.breakpoint.lg`, 64rem: 1024px at the default root size; see [Metrics](?path=/docs/tokens-metrics--docs)) the panel is the last column for the height of the window under the banner: the top nav stops at its edge and the panel's header sits level with it, so opening it narrows everything and covers nothing. A banner spans the whole width, over the panel's column too (With banner and panel). From there to the `panel` breakpoint (`dimension.breakpoint.panel`, 80rem: 1280px) an open panel shows the side nav collapsed, as its icon rail with `collapsedSideNav="icons"` or hidden, so the register stays in view beside the panel; closing the panel gives the side nav back as the reader left it, and the preference `persist` remembers never changes; SideNav's `onCollapse` and `onExpand` are not called for it. A reader who expands the side nav while the panel is open keeps it expanded until the panel closes (Panel beside Main at 1200px). Below the large breakpoint the panel replaces the visible Main area under the top nav while retaining Main's state. Global navigation remains available; use Sheet for modal work.

_Example: story `Stories.PanelBesideMain`._

Aside sits beside Main from the `aside` breakpoint (`dimension.breakpoint.aside`, 75rem), and from the large breakpoint whenever the side nav leaves Main its minimum width beside it (see Main's minimum width below): collapsed, as the icon rail or hidden, it always does, and expanded at its default width it does. With a panel open it sits beside Main from the `wide` breakpoint (110rem); between the aside and the wide breakpoints it follows Main and starts where Main's content ends. Beside Main its divider runs the page's height, however short its content (Record rail at 1100px).

Below the aside breakpoint, wherever it would not sit beside Main (on a phone, beside a side nav the reader widened, beside an open panel), the Aside is a Details disclosure where the route rendered it in the page, closed until the reader opens it: one row over a hairline that reads "Details" (`heading` changes it) and carries `summary`, the record's state as its status badge. The state is one tap from the top and the body keeps its place. So render the Aside where a record's Details belong on a phone: right after the PageHeader, or first in a tabbed record's Overview panel, rendered only while that tab is selected. Where it is rendered it leaves an empty marker that takes no room (`display: contents`), so it adds no gap to the Stack around it; its content portals into the rail or the disclosure. The row is an h2's button with `aria-expanded`; Enter and Space toggle it, and find-in-page opens it. The content sits one level below, and an Inspector.Group named as the disclosure is its content, with no second title. Inside Main the Aside is a region named by its `label`, since a complementary landmark belongs at the top level. The content moves between the rail and the disclosure without mounting again, so a draft in an Editable survives a resize or a panel opening, and it moves as it is, at once: only the reader's own toggle folds it on the kit's motion. Focus on a control inside stays on it as the display changes, the disclosure opening around it; a control the change replaces (a group's title, an h2 in the rail and an h3 in the disclosure) hands focus to the first control left (Record details at 390px, Record rail beside a wide side nav). When a route replaces one record's page with another's, the next record's Details mount in the document, so what measures itself as it mounts measures in the page (Record change at 390px).

```tsx
<Stack space="space.200">
  <PageHeader>…</PageHeader>
  <Shell.Aside label="Task details" summary={<Badge variant="secondary">In progress</Badge>}>
    <Inspector>
      <Inspector.Group title="Details">…</Inspector.Group>
    </Inspector>
  </Shell.Aside>
  <Stack space="space.300">…the record's sections…</Stack>
</Stack>
```

_Example: story `Stories.RecordRailPhone`._
_Example: story `Stories.RecordRailLaptop`._
_Example: story `Stories.RecordRailWideSideNav`._
_Example: story `Stories.RecordChangePhone`._

The panel's focus contract holds at every width. When it opens while focus is on the page, on its opener or nowhere, focus moves into it (the labelled `aside`, or the element `initialFocus` names), so Escape and the next keys act in the preview; `initialFocus={false}` leaves focus where it is while Main is still visible beside the panel. When it closes with focus inside, focus returns to the control the reader last used in Main: the opener, or another row's eye pressed while the panel was open; `finalFocus` names another element, or `false` leaves it to the caller. Escape closes the panel unless it comes from a field inside it (a text input, a search field, a textarea, a select or an editable region), where it belongs to the field, so a table's search inside the panel clears its query and the panel stays (Table in a panel); from a tooltip, a menu, a list or a dialog open in the panel, which closes first; from text an input method is still composing; or from a part inside that handled it (`preventDefault`). Where the panel replaces Main, it is the page's region: Main, its h1 and its landmark are out of the page until the panel closes, so the panel's title or `label` says where the reader is. See Panel focus.

`defaultWidth` is the panel's own width while it is open and the reader has not resized a panel: a width they dragged or keyed, which `persist` remembers, outranks it, and it is never remembered itself, so each register's preview opens at its own default (Panel widths). A splitter step or a drag lands at once; the columns ease only as the panel opens and closes. Close and the splitter are named after the panel's `label` ("Close Requirement preview", "Resize Requirement preview"), or "Close details" and "Resize details" without one; their `label` props override that. The header stays in view as the panel scrolls, and the panel's scroll padding follows its measured height, so a control that takes focus never stops under a header that wraps. In a window under 30rem tall the header scrolls away with the content instead (Panel in a short window), and beside the page the panel holds the window's whole height once the banner has scrolled away, as the side nav does (Panel in a short wide window).

_Example: story `Stories.PanelFocus`._
_Example: story `Stories.PanelWidths`._
_Example: story `Stories.PanelShortWindow`._
_Example: story `Stories.PanelTable`._

Every default name (Banner, Top navigation, Side navigation, Main content, Page context, Details, Actions, Search, More, Switch product, the toggle's two labels, the splitters' and the skip links') is a locale message, so a product translates them once with `LedgerProvider`; a `label` prop overrides one instance. The splitters follow the window-splitter pattern: the arrow keys step 16px, with Shift or Page Up and Page Down 64px, Home goes to the minimum and End to the maximum, and Enter collapses the side nav (as a double-click does). Left and Right move the handle in that physical direction, including right-to-left layouts. Each splitter names the area it resizes (`aria-controls`), and `onResizeStart` and `onResizeEnd` report a drag that moved or a key that changed the width, never a key at the limit. Restored widths retain the reader’s desktop preference: the current desktop layout caps them (see Main's minimum width below), and opening the shell on a phone does not overwrite that preference. On a phone the side nav's overlay is at most 90vw wide.

_Example: story `Stories.PersistedWidths`._
_Example: story `Stories.RightToLeftSplitters`._

Main uses document scrolling; Panel scrolls inside the available viewport. A register that is the page fills the rest of the window with DataTable `fill`: Main publishes its bottom inset as `--shell-inset-bottom`, and the layout otherwise owns placement, so content patterns do not add nested page frames. A column of a page's grid that stays in view under the banner and the top nav, a wizard's steps beside its form, is a [StickyRail](?path=/docs/layout-stickyrail--docs). The Shell styles its areas by their `data-slot`, never by a class a product writes, so the grid, the areas' stickiness and the panel's container are its own.

Set `collapsedSideNav="icons"` on Shell to keep a 56px navigation rail when collapsed on desktop. The default, `"hidden"`, hides the side nav, and hovering the toggle flies it out over the page. Supply meaningful icons for top-level items and expandable groups. In icon mode, destination names remain accessible and appear in tooltips on hover or focus; the active destination and profile avatar remain visible. Section headings and nested destinations are visually hidden. Custom SideNav.Header content, such as navigation search, is hidden in the rail and returns when expanded. Activating an expandable group expands the shell and opens that group. Hovering the toggle does not open a flyout in this mode. With the default app mark, the collapsed expand control occupies the mark’s position and appears on hover or keyboard focus; on a touch screen (`(any-pointer: coarse)`, the kit's touch predicate: a tablet in landscape, a touchscreen laptop) it shows at rest in the mark’s place. Otherwise the mark is visible at rest, and the product name keeps its position through collapse and expansion and still leads home. The top nav's start slot eases between the side nav's width and its own on the side nav's curve (Start slot motion). Phone navigation keeps its separate visible toggle. Expanding brings the splitter back with the remembered width; on a phone the side nav is the overlay described under Accessibility. `shellScript` and `shellScriptFor` preserve the compact rail before hydration when collapse state is stored. See [Icon rail](?path=/story/layout-shell-icon-rail--desktop) for keyboard, RTL, phone and first-paint examples.

The current page is SideNav.Item's `isActive` (`aria-current="page"`): the selected fill, text and icon, distinct from hover's neutral tint, with a bar on the row's start edge in `color.background.selected.bold`, 3:1 on the fill and on the side nav's surface in light and dark, so the row is told apart by more than its fill's colour; in forced colours the Highlight fill marks it. A SideNav.Expandable that holds the current page takes `isActive` too: it starts open, and its row takes the current colour and bar wherever the item is out of view, while the group is closed and in the rail. In the rail a `badge` stays in its item's name and a dot on the icon says it is there. A label the side nav's width cuts shows its whole name in a tooltip, and so does the profile's name, with its description when that is cut too; AppLogo's `name` and `secondaryName` show whole the same way, on hover and on keyboard focus, when the start slot cuts them (Current page, Long names).

_Example: story `Stories.CurrentPage`._
_Example: story `Stories.LongNames`._

`Shell.Panel.actions` places route-owned controls immediately before Close in the built-in header. Collection previews compose `Panel.Header`, `Panel.Actions` and `Panel.Close` for a navigation-only outer bar: previous/next through the displayed rows and a native full-record link, and for a nested frame `Panel.Back`, the header's first child. Back is an arrow ("Back to previous record"), not the chevron Previous uses, and it leads the bar, set apart from the navigation and Close at its end; in a panel under 400px wide whose title takes the first row it leads the second (Panel back). Put the visible record name and domain commands in a `PageHeader` at the beginning of `Panel.Body`, using an h2 and `PageHeader.Actions`. Give the panel an accessible `label` when its outer bar has no `Panel.Title`. The route owns row order, destinations and endpoint availability; Shell only supplies placement. The Record header narrow story exercises both headers at the minimum panel width.

_Example: story `Stories.PanelBack`._
_Example: story `Stories.PanelBackNarrow`._

## Main's minimum width

However the side nav and the panel are sized, Main keeps room for its content: one list column (`dimension.layout.list`) inside its desktop gutters (`space.300` each side), 388px with the default tokens. Each area is capped at half the viewport, and also where Main would fall under that minimum. The splitters stop there, and `aria-valuemax` says where, so End is the widest the area can be now. A remembered or default width that no longer fits is narrowed by the layout, not rewritten: when the panel opens beside a wide side nav, the panel's column gives way first, down to its own 240px minimum, and the side nav is capped so that the three always fit without a sideways scroll. The panel's column opens and closes on the standard curve.

_Example: story `Stories.MainMinimum`._

## Page changes

Give Shell the router's location as `locationKey` (a pathname or a route id) and it handles a client-side page change at every width, without importing a router: it closes the phone overlay or the desktop flyout, moves focus to Main without scrolling, and announces the page's title through the [Announcer](?path=/docs/components-announcer--docs) it mounts. Focus stays where it is when it is on a control in the page that survived the change, such as a pager or a next-record link. Focus in a menu or a dialog outside the shell, such as a command palette, follows the popup's own return: when it hands focus back to its trigger in the top nav, or drops it, the shell takes it on to Main. The title is `document.title`, read once the new page has rendered, else Main's first h1; `getPageTitle` chooses other words or returns null to say nothing. Pass a key that changes with the page and not with a tab or a filter that writes to the URL, or a tab click would move focus to Main. Without `locationKey` the shell does none of this.

```tsx
const { pathname } = useLocation();
<Shell locationKey={pathname}>…</Shell>;
```

_Example: story `Stories.PageChange`._

On a phone, choosing a link in the side nav closes the overlay and moves focus to Main even without `locationKey`, so the reader lands on the page they chose; a click that opens a new tab or window leaves it open. Set `closeOnNavigate={false}` on SideNav for links that change the page in place and should keep the overlay open; a change of `locationKey` still closes it. Any other close from inside the overlay (its Close, `useSideNav().collapse()`, Escape, the blanket) returns focus to the toggle once the rest of the shell accepts input again. SideNav's `onCollapse` and `onExpand` receive the `trigger` and `isOverlay`, true for the phone overlay, and fire only when the side nav's state changes: a close caused by a page change has the trigger `"navigation"`, and one caused by the window growing past the large breakpoint `"viewport"`. Keep a remembered collapsed state from the calls whose `isOverlay` is false. `useSideNav().isOverlay` says whether the side nav is the overlay now, so a product never repeats the breakpoint.

_Example: story `Stories.PageChangePhone`._
_Example: story `Stories.DestinationPhone`._
_Example: story `Stories.KeepOpenPhone`._

See [page composition](?path=/docs/layout-pages--docs) for route and tab examples.

## Accessibility

Each area is a landmark with a locale default name: the Banner a region ("Banner"), TopNav a `header` ("Top navigation"), SideNav a `nav` ("Side navigation"), Main a `main` ("Main content"), Aside a complementary region ("Page context"; a region inside Main while it is the Details disclosure) and Panel a complementary region its title or `label` names. Visually hidden skip links come first in the tab order, one per area in the areas' order, and each moves focus to its area; the side nav's link is there only while the side nav shows beside the page, inline or as the icon rail (Skip links). Shell mounts the kit's TooltipProvider: the first tooltip waits 300ms, and the next opens at once for 300ms after the last closed.

Below the large breakpoint the side nav is a modal overlay. Opening it moves focus to the current page's item, else the first link; Tab and Shift+Tab go round inside it; the Banner, the top nav, Main, Aside, Panel and the skip links are inert until it closes. The overlay covers the toggle that opened it, so its own Close takes the toggle's place. Close, Escape and the blanket close it and return focus to the toggle, and choosing a destination closes it and hands focus to Main. The blanket closes the overlay on a press but is no control: it is hidden from assistive technology and out of the tab order. A menu or a dialog opened from inside the overlay keeps its own Tab and Escape, and closing it leaves the overlay open (Overlay focus at 390px).

_Example: story `Stories.OverlayFocusPhone`._

Profile's avatar is decoration beside the name: Profile hides it from assistive technology, so the button is named by the person's `name` and `description`, and the Avatar inside needs no name of its own. Its chevron says it opens a menu: it shows while the button is a menu's trigger (`aria-haspopup="menu"`, which a DropdownMenuTrigger sets through `render`), and `indicator` decides otherwise. A Profile that opens a dialog says so with `aria-haspopup="dialog"` and has no chevron.

The Banner wraps its message on a narrow screen, and the shell measures the banner area, so the top nav, the side nav and the panel sit under its real height (Banner at 390px). In a window under 30rem tall (a phone on its side, a page zoomed to 400%) the banner and the top nav scroll away with the page instead of pinning a share of the height (Short window).

_Example: story `Stories.BannerPhone`._
_Example: story `Stories.ShortWindow`._

## Persistence

`persist` remembers, in this browser, the reader's collapsed state and the widths they dragged or keyed on a splitter; a SideNav's or a Panel's `defaultWidth` is the width until the reader resizes, and is never stored, so a changed default reaches every reader who has not resized (Default widths). What an open panel shows between the large and the panel breakpoints is not the reader's choice and is not stored either. `persist={true}` uses one key, `ledger.shell`, for every Shell on the origin, so two frames on one origin with different `collapsedSideNav` (an icon rail in one, a hidden side nav in the other) share one collapsed state and one pair of widths; give the second a key of its own (`persist="ledger.shell.inspector"`) and its head script `shellScriptFor` that key.

_Example: story `Stories.DefaultWidths`._

The parts with props of their own. The others (SideNav.Header, Body and Footer, TopNav.Middle, Mark, Panel.Header, Actions and Body) take only their element's native props; Panel.Title takes `render`.

By default it shows while the button opens a popup it announces (`aria-haspopup`, which a DropdownMenuTrigger sets through `render`), so a Profile that runs an action or opens a dialog has none; `true` or `false` decides. |

### The end slot at narrow widths

`TopNav.End` never shrinks, so what it holds decides the top nav's width. Give each action or destination as a `TopNav.Item` (an icon, a `label`, and `onClick`, or `href` or a router link through `render` for a destination). When the top nav is narrower than 48rem, measured on the row itself so that a panel open beside it counts, the items leave the row for one More menu at End's end: the same icons and names, in the row's order, a destination still a link and an item with a `disabledReason` still saying why. Anything in End that is not an item stays in the row at every width, and so does an item marked `persistent`: keep the colour mode's ModeSwitch as a plain child, since a toggle group cannot become a menu row. An item that opens its own menu or popover is `persistent` and is the trigger through the trigger's `render` (`<DropdownMenuTrigger render={<Shell.TopNav.Item persistent … />} />`), since its popup anchors to the button in the row; an item forwards its native props and its ref to that button, so the trigger's wiring reaches it. Narrowed while an item has focus, focus moves to More, which now holds it, never to a persistent item beside it; widened while More has focus, it moves back to the first item that left. Budget the persistent children for the narrowest window the product serves.

The fold reads the top nav's own width because the top nav is a size container (`container-type: inline-size`, named `topnav`). Inside Shell its width comes from the grid; a top nav placed outside a Shell needs a width from its parent, as a block or a stretched flex item, because it no longer takes one from its contents.

_Example: story `Stories.EndItemsFold`._

`overflow` is the older, all-or-nothing spelling: below the `md` breakpoint one menu of the product's stands in for every child, the colour mode included (the Record rail at 390px story). Items inside an End with `overflow` never fold; `overflow` still decides.

```tsx
<Shell.TopNav.End>
  <ModeSwitch />
  <Shell.TopNav.Item icon={<CircleHelp />} label="Help" onClick={openHelp} />
  <Shell.TopNav.Item icon={<Bell />} label="My work" render={<Link to="/work" />} />
  <Shell.TopNav.Item icon={<Settings />} label="Settings" onClick={openSettings} />
</Shell.TopNav.End>
```

### The search

`TopNav.Search` is the top nav's way into the product's [SearchDialog](?path=/docs/patterns-searchdialog--docs). In a top nav at least 48rem wide it is a field-shaped button that reads its `label` and shows the shortcut's keys; narrower, a Search icon button with the label in its tooltip, so the middle slot never squeezes a field under the create action. Both are one button to assistive technology, named by `label`, with `aria-haspopup="dialog"` and `aria-keyshortcuts`, and both call `onOpen`. So does the shortcut, ⌘K on Apple platforms and Ctrl+K elsewhere (`shortcut`, `null` for none), from anywhere on the page; it ignores a held key's repeats, other modifiers and text still being composed, and does nothing while a dialog is open, so it never stacks a second dialog over a draft. The search is a button, not a text field: there is one search surface, the dialog, and nothing typed is lost when the row changes width. When the row narrows while the field has focus, focus moves to the icon. One key opens one dialog: `useCommandPalette` also binds ⌘K, and its shortcut cannot be changed, so a page with both gives TopNav.Search another `shortcut`, or `shortcut={null}`.

```tsx
const [open, setOpen] = useState(false);
<Shell.TopNav.Middle>
  <Shell.TopNav.Search label="Search records" onOpen={() => setOpen(true)} />
</Shell.TopNav.Middle>;
<SearchDialog open={open} onOpenChange={setOpen} results={records} onSelect={openRecord} />;
```

The [Search at 320px](?path=/story/layout-shell--narrow-search) story shows the row at a phone's width: the toggle, the switcher, the mark, Search, Create and More in one row.

_Example: story `Stories.SearchShortcut`._

### Narrow panel headers

Panel header slots respond to the panel container, including a manually resized desktop panel. Below 400px, a title with actions occupies a full row and navigation/Close share the row beneath; title-only headers keep Close beside the title. A PageHeader inside the panel follows its own rule: its actions take the row under the title when the row cannot hold the title's measure beside them. The normal desktop header remains one row. See the 240px, 320px and 640px Panel header stories, composed-slot forwarding and Panel record header examples.
