<!-- page: Layout/Shell/Icon rail (src/stories/layout/ShellIconRail.mdx) -->

# Shell icon rail

Set `collapsedSideNav="icons"` on Shell to retain destination icons, the active destination and the profile avatar in a 56px rail on desktop. Names remain accessible and appear in tooltips on hover or focus. Activating an expandable group restores the full navigation and opens its children. The default collapsed mode remains `"hidden"`. With the default app mark, the collapsed expand control occupies the mark’s existing position and appears on hover or keyboard focus; on a touch screen (`(any-pointer: coarse)`, the kit's touch predicate: a tablet in landscape, a touchscreen laptop) it shows at rest in the mark’s place. Otherwise the mark is visible at rest, and the product name keeps its position through collapse and expansion and still leads home. Phone navigation keeps its separate visible toggle.

_Example: story `Stories.Desktop`._

Expand and minimize animate the sidebar width over Ledger's moderate duration. The page follows the sidebar while the app mark stays fixed; resizing follows the pointer immediately. Reduced motion and restoring a remembered layout skip the transition.

_Example: story `Stories.WidthMotion`._

On phones, navigation slides in and out with a fading scrim, and returns focus to its toggle when dismissed. Choosing a destination in it closes it and moves focus to Main (see [Page changes](?path=/docs/layout-shell--docs#page-changes)). Closing navigation stops accepting input immediately, and reversing the action continues from its current position. The rail does not take space from the page.

_Example: story `Stories.Mobile390`._

The RTL and persisted first-paint stories verify logical placement and restoration before hydration. See [Shell](?path=/docs/layout-shell--docs) for composition, persistence, keyboard behavior and the complete API.

<!-- page: Layout/StickyRail (src/stories/layout/StickyRail.mdx) -->

# StickyRail

**Status: Stable.**

A column of a page's grid that stays in view under the shell's banner and top nav while the page scrolls: a wizard's steps beside its form. It stops `space.300` under them (the Shell's `--shell-top`; outside a Shell, the top nav's height) and is at most the window's height under them. In a scroller of its own, a dialog's body or a panel, it sticks to that scroller instead: an ancestor sets `--rail-top`, where the rail stops in it, and `--rail-max-height`, the scroller's height.

`from="lg"` is for a rail the page's Grid puts beside the content from the large breakpoint and stacks above it below: below `lg` it stays in the flow and scrolls away with the page, so a phone never keeps the steps over the form. Without `from` it always sticks.

A rail that the grid stacks above the content on a phone and has no `from` sticks there too, and covers the form the reader is filling in.

_Example: story `Stories.DoDont`._

```tsx
<Grid gap="space.300" templateColumns={{ lg: "200px minmax(0,1fr)" }}>
  <StickyRail from="lg">
    <Stepper orientation="responsive" label="Program setup">
      …
    </Stepper>
  </StickyRail>
  <Stack space="space.250">…the step's form…</Stack>
</Grid>
```

_Example: story `Stories.WizardSteps`._
_Example: story `Stories.Always`._

## When to use it

- **Use it** for a short column that orients the reader while they work down a long page beside it: a wizard's steps, the contents of a long document.
- **Not** for a record's Details: those are the [Shell](?path=/docs/layout-shell--docs)'s Aside, which the Shell places beside Main and turns into a Details disclosure on a phone.
- **Not** for a list beside its detail: that is a [WorkPane](?path=/docs/patterns-workpane--docs), whose list sticks the same way.
- **Not** for a page frame or a register's table: Main scrolls the page, and DataTable `fill` takes the rest of the window.

## Accessibility

The rail is a plain `div`: it adds no landmark or role. What it holds names itself, as a Stepper's list does by its `label`. Its content keeps the reading and tab order of where it is rendered, before the content beside it.

## Props

_Props of `StickyRail`, generated from its types:_

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `from` | `"lg"` |  | The breakpoint it sticks from. `lg` for a rail the page's Grid puts beside the content from the large breakpoint (`templateColumns={{ lg: … }}`) and stacks above it below, where it stays in the flow. Without it the rail always sticks. |

StickyRail renders one `div`, forwards its native props, a `className` and its ref to it, shrinks in its grid track (`min-w-0`) and names itself last with `data-slot="sticky-rail"`.

## Related

- [Shell](?path=/docs/layout-shell--docs): the banner and the top nav it stops under, and the Aside for a record's Details.
- [Stepper](?path=/docs/components-stepper--docs): a wizard's steps.
- [Grid](?path=/docs/primitives-grid--docs): the page's columns.
- [Upgrading](?path=/docs/guidance-upgrading--docs#layout-classes): `lg:sticky-rail` and `sticky-rail` are a StickyRail.

<!-- page: Patterns/ActionBar (src/stories/patterns/ActionBar.mdx) -->

# ActionBar

**Status: Deprecated.** No product screen uses ActionBar; it stays for one version and then leaves the package. A record page's header is a [PageHeader](?path=/docs/layout-pageheader--docs), with the record's state in its Details rail: [Shell.Aside](?path=/docs/layout-shell--docs) holding an [Inspector](?path=/docs/patterns-inspector--docs).

A work surface's header pinned above the work: the trail ending in the record's id, the title with a few words of context, the record's state axes as facts, and the actions that change that state. It is composed from [PageHeader](?path=/docs/layout-pageheader--docs)'s parts, so it keeps PageHeader's wrap rule.

_Example: story `Stories.Blocked`._

## Anatomy

| Part    | What it is                                                                                                                                      |
| ------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Trail   | `crumbs`, the parents as BreadcrumbItems with separators between them; the bar appends `id` as the current crumb.                               |
| Title   | `title`, the page's h1, with `context` after it: the scope, the owner.                                                                          |
| States  | `states`, one fact per axis under the title: the first a Badge, the headline; the rest an Indicator. A state with a `control` shows it instead. |
| Actions | `actions`, the verbs that change the state, one primary, beside the title or on the next row when the title needs its measure.                  |
| Reasons | Under the actions, each blocked action's reason, "Mark satisfied: 2 findings still open".                                                       |
| Tabs    | `tabs`, the strip under the bar.                                                                                                                |

## States

An action with `blocked` stays in the row, disabled, with its reason written under it: hiding it would hide the rule. A blocked action is still a Tab stop (`aria-disabled`), and its reason is its accessible description, so a keyboard or screen-reader user reaches it and hears why it cannot run. When every action can run, nothing is written under the row.

_Example: story `Stories.Ready`._

## Accessibility

- **One h1**, the title. The trail is a breadcrumb navigation whose last crumb, the id, is the current page.
- **A blocked action is reachable.** It keeps its place in the tab order with `aria-disabled`, does nothing when pressed, and is described by its reason.
- **State is words.** Each axis is a label and a value; the tone is never the only signal.

## Props

_Props of `ActionBar`, generated from its types:_

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `crumbs` | `ReactNode` |  | The parents as BreadcrumbItem elements with BreadcrumbSeparator between them; the header appends the id as the last crumb. |
| `id` (required) | `ReactNode` |  | The record's id: the last crumb of the trail. |
| `title` (required) | `ReactNode` |  | The record's name, the h1. |
| `context` | `ReactNode` |  | After the title, a few words: the scope, the owner. |
| `states` (required) | `ActionBarState[]` |  | The state axes, as facts under the title: the first a Badge, the headline; the rest a dot and a word. |
| `actions` | `ActionBarAction[]` |  | The actions that change the state, one primary. A blocked action stays, disabled, with its reason under the row. |
| `tabs` | `ReactNode` |  | The tab strip under the bar. |

## Related

# Chart

**Status: Stable.**

Data drawn on the chart tokens. `Chart` is the Frame: the figure that names a plot, keys it, holds its states, keeps the way back from a drill-down, and lays the same numbers out as a table one toggle away. Each kind of plot is its own part with its own page: [Bar](?path=/docs/patterns-chart-bar--docs), [Line](?path=/docs/patterns-chart-line--docs), [Area](?path=/docs/patterns-chart-area--docs), [Donut](?path=/docs/patterns-chart-donut--docs), [Sparkline](?path=/docs/patterns-chart-sparkline--docs), [Scatter](?path=/docs/patterns-chart-scatter--docs), [Treemap](?path=/docs/patterns-chart-treemap--docs) and [Heatmap](?path=/docs/patterns-chart-heatmap--docs). Recharts draws; the kit decides the paint, the marks, the grid, the tooltip, the legend and the motion, so a chart reads like the rest of the page in both modes. The colour rules follow the data-visualization method, and the categorical order is validated, not eyeballed.

_Example: story `Stories.Framed`._

## Kinds

The data's job picks the kind, and sometimes the right kind is not a chart: one number is a [Stat](?path=/docs/components-stat--docs), one ratio against a limit is a [Progress](?path=/docs/components-progress--docs) bar, and more than seven classes that all carry meaning is a [Table](?path=/docs/components-table--docs).

| The reader must                            | Part                                                            | Colour job                              |
| ------------------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------- |
| Compare sizes across categories            | [`Chart.Bar`](?path=/docs/patterns-chart-bar--docs)             | One hue; `horizontal` for long names    |
| See parts of each whole                    | `Chart.Bar` stacked                                             | Status tones, or the categorical set    |
| Read actual against planned                | `Chart.Bar` with `target`                                       | The series' tone; the target is ink     |
| See when things happen                     | `Chart.Bar` horizontal with `[from, to]` values                 | One hue                                 |
| Follow a trend                             | [`Chart.Line`](?path=/docs/patterns-chart-line--docs)           | `brand`, or a tone per series           |
| Follow parts of a whole over time          | [`Chart.Area`](?path=/docs/patterns-chart-area--docs) stacked   | Status tones, or the categorical set    |
| See one number against its whole           | [`Chart.Donut`](?path=/docs/patterns-chart-donut--docs)         | The parts' tones on the track           |
| Read a score against a scale               | `Chart.Donut` `arc="half"`                                      | The tone the score earns                |
| See a trend beside a number                | [`Chart.Sparkline`](?path=/docs/patterns-chart-sparkline--docs) | One tone                                |
| Place things on two measures               | [`Chart.Scatter`](?path=/docs/patterns-chart-scatter--docs)     | `brand`, or at most three groups        |
| See how a total splits, and splits again   | [`Chart.Treemap`](?path=/docs/patterns-chart-treemap--docs)     | The categorical set, one hue per branch |
| Read how much across two dimensions        | [`Chart.Heatmap`](?path=/docs/patterns-chart-heatmap--docs)     | `sequential`: one hue, light to dark    |
| Read above and below across two dimensions | `Chart.Heatmap` `scale="diverging"`                             | Two hues around grey                    |
| Read status by place                       | `Chart.Heatmap` with a tone function                            | The Badge's fills, values printed       |

Not built, and why: no pie (a ring with the number in the middle says more, and a two-slice pie is a Stat); no second value axis (two measures of different scale are two charts, or one indexed; a dual axis invents a correlation); no gauge with a needle (the half ring reads the same and its number is text); no radar, boxplot, histogram, lollipop, alluvial, word cloud, circle pack or map (none of the four products has asked, and a histogram is a bar chart of bins the data layer makes); no zoom, brush or export toolbar (a range is a control in the Frame's `actions`, a drill-down is the Frame's `path`, and the chart's own export is one Download menu: the table twin as CSV and the plot as PNG; a register's export stays the register's).

## Anatomy

| Part        | What it is                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| ----------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Title       | `font.body` medium in `color.text`, a noun phrase: what the chart shows. It names the figure and the plot to a screen reader, and is a heading at the level around it (`titleLevel` sets one).                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| Description | `font.body.small` in `color.text.subtle`, one line under the title: the period, the unit, the source.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| Path        | A [Breadcrumb](?path=/docs/components-breadcrumb--docs) under the description while a drill-down is open: every level so far, every crumb but the last a way back.                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| Legend      | Swatch and label per series, `font.body.small` in `color.text.subtle`, at the end of the header. A square for a fill, a stroke for a line, a dot for a point. Present for two or more series; a single series needs none, the title names it. Unless the Frame is given `series`, it keys what the part draws: its series, a scatter's groups, a ring's slices, a treemap's branches. |
| Actions     | Controls at the end of the header: a range, a filter. Then the tools: the Values toggle on a colour-scale Heatmap, the Table toggle, the Download menu (the table twin as CSV, the plot as PNG), the Expand button.                                                                                                                                                                   |
| Plot        | The part's marks on a hairline grid. Ticks are `font.body.xsmall` in `color.text.subtlest`; grid lines and the axis line are `color.border`, solid, 1px. A tab stop when it chooses (`onSelect`, `details`), with the kit's focus ring on the keyboard only; an image named by the title when it does not.                                                                            |
| Tooltip     | The overlay surface. The category first, then every series at that point: the name, then the value in `font.body.small` medium, keyed by the mark's swatch. A stack adds the total of its parts; a line over it is not one of them.                                                                                                                                                   |
| Card        | The details on a chosen mark: a Popover anchored to it, the kit's head (swatch, name, category, value; or every series at a category), then whatever the caller adds.                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| Table       | The same numbers as a [Table](?path=/docs/components-table--docs), one toggle away, laid out by the kind: the category heading each row, then a column per series the legend shows; a scatter's points, one row each; a ring's slices with their shares; a treemap's leaves, a column per level; a heatmap pivoted.                                                                   |

## Variants

| Variant                              | Use                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| ------------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Chart` (the Frame)                  | Every chart on a page. Title, description, legend, actions, the states, the path, the table twin, the legend's interaction.                                                                                                                                                              |
| `legend="top"`, `"bottom"`, `"none"` | The legend at the end of the header (the default for two or more series), under the plot when the header is busy, or nowhere for one series.                                                                                                                                             |
| `path`                               | The Frame of a drill-down: the levels so far as crumbs, the last being the current one.                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `download`, `expandable`             | The tools: a Download menu with the table twin as a CSV and the plot as a PNG at twice the pixel density, with the title, the line and the legend above it; an Expand button that opens the same chart in a large Dialog, the plot redrawn at `large`.                                   |
| `columns`                            | Columns for the table twin and the CSV beyond the series, each a key in the datum: a name beside the category (`place: "before"`), a total, a share, an owner after the series. Facts the plot does not draw, so the twin is the record's table and not only the plot's.                 |
| `syncId`                             | Charts that share their hover: small multiples, one hover across them, on one `domain`.                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `texture`                            | Every series wears a pattern as well as its colour, in the plot, the legend, the tooltip and the card.                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `Chart.Legend`                       | The key on its own, outside a Frame: beside a Donut, under a stacked bar. Inside a Frame it is the interactive one.                                                                                                                                                                      |
| The parts                            | One per kind, each on its own page. A part inside the Frame inherits its name, its formats, its size, its loading state and its legend's state; a Bar, Line or Area also its `data`, `x` and `series`. It tells the Frame what it draws, so the legend, the table and the CSV follow it. |

## Said once

Data, size and format are given once, to whichever holds them best. Given to the Frame, the part inside takes them when it sets none: a bare `<Chart.Bar />` draws the Frame's `data`, `x` and `series` at the Frame's `size`, in its `format`. Given to the part, the Frame learns them from it: its legend keys the part's series under the part's swatch (a stroke for a Line, a dot for a Scatter), and its table and CSV print the part's records in the part's format, so the plot, the tooltip and the table never disagree. The Frame's own props always win, and a part's own props win over what it inherits, except in the expanded Dialog, where every plot draws at `large`.

_Example: story `Stories.SaidOnce`._

The Frame follows the part it holds. When the part changes, the legend, the table and the CSV change with it; a series hidden from the legend stays hidden while its key is still drawn. When the caller puts something that is no part in its place, the legend and the Table toggle leave with the part rather than describe a plot that is gone. An empty or failed Frame keeps the last legend, so its header does not shift. One Frame holds one part.

_Example: story `Stories.FollowsItsPart`._

_Example: story `Stories.Drilldown`._
_Example: story `Stories.Details`._
_Example: story `Stories.Filtering`._
_Example: story `Stories.Linked`._
_Example: story `Stories.Downloads`._
_Example: story `Stories.Textured`._
_Example: story `Stories.Legends`._

## Sizes

| Size     | Height | Where                                                                         |
| -------- | ------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `small`  | 120px  | A rail, a card in a grid of them, a cell of the matrix.                       |
| `medium` | 200px  | A Section. The default.                                                       |
| `large`  | 320px  | The one chart a page is about: the scatter of risks, the treemap of findings. |

The height is the whole plot, axis band included, so a card never scrolls inside itself. `height` takes pixels when a layout must. The Frame's states stand in at the same height, so nothing moves when the data arrives. A Donut and a Sparkline are sized in pixels, since they sit inline, and narrow to a container narrower than that; a Heatmap's `size` is its cell's height.

The width is the container's. In a Frame narrower than 32rem the header wraps: the tools stay on the title's row, the legend and the actions take the next row from the start, and the plot keeps its height. A column chart keeps a label under every bar, on two lines or cut with an ellipsis where the category is narrow; a line's or an area's labels fit the room between their points the same way, and step over whole points only where a point cannot hold three characters. Reference and band labels move apart rather than overlap and stay within the plot's width, clear of the axis ticks, shortening with an ellipsis when the row is too short for them, and while a mark's details card is open the tooltip stands down, so on a phone the two never stack. An expanded chart is the same Frame at `large` in a Dialog at its `xlarge` width, 960px at most, and the plot inside redraws at `large` whatever size it was given inline: 320px high, a ring 320px across at least, a heatmap's cells at 40px. Hidden series and the chart/table choice are shared with the original: expanding preserves them, and changes made in the dialog remain after it closes.

_Example: story `Stories.Narrow`._

On a dashboard the charts are in the page's outline: inside a HeadingLevelProvider or a titled Section the title is a heading at that level, and `titleLevel` sets one outright.

_Example: story `Stories.Headings`._

## States

| State      | What changes                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| ---------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Hover      | The tooltip, for every series at that point; a hovered bar and a hovered slice take the tone's `hovered` step, a slice grows 2px, a line's marker appears. Synced charts show their tooltips together. A legend item under the mouse or keyboard focus dims the other series to `opacity.disabled`, faded over `motion.duration.fast`; a tap does not. |
| Hidden     | A clicked legend item hides its series in the plot and in the table; its swatch, a square or a stroke, hollows, the series left keep their colours and the value axis its scale, and none is dimmed for the one just hidden. Clicking the last visible one shows everything again.                                                                     |
| Chosen     | A clicked mark, or the category Enter or Space chose on the focused plot: the other marks dim, the card opens on it. Escape or a click outside closes the card and focus returns to the plot.                                                                                                                                                          |
| Loading    | The plot's own silhouette in `color.skeleton`, pulsing, at the plot's height: columns, a line, a ring, dots, tiles. The header stays.                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| Refreshing | The last plot stays, dimmed to `opacity.loading`, with a Spinner beside the title. For a refetch, so the reader keeps what they had.                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| Empty      | The kit's compact [Empty](?path=/docs/components-empty--docs) at the plot's height: "Nothing to show yet", one line of why (`statusText`) and an action (`statusAction`). A Frame `ready` with `data` that holds no records says it too, instead of drawing bare axes.                                                                                 |
| Error      | An [Alert](?path=/docs/components-alert--docs) in the danger tone, `role="alert"`, at the plot's height, as a failed table has: "The chart could not load", why, and Try again (`onRetry`) beside it.                                                                                                                                                  |
| Table      | The Table toggle swaps the plot for the same numbers as a Table; the legend and the actions stay.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |

_Example: story `Stories.States`._

## Modifiers

- **`legend`**, **`swatch`**, **`actions`**, **`state`**, **`statusTitle`**, **`statusText`**, **`onRetry`**, **`statusAction`** on the Frame. `state` is the word DataTable uses for the same thing (`ready`, `loading`, `empty`, `error`, and `refreshing` for a refetch that keeps the last plot); `status` is its deprecated name, which `ledger/no-deprecated-name` renames. The figure carries `data-slot="chart-frame"` and `data-state`.
- **`path`** on the Frame for a drill-down; each crumb's `onSelect` goes back.
- **`download`** (`["csv", "png"]`) and **`expandable`** for the tools; **`summary`** for the sentence a screen reader hears; **`titleLevel`** for the title's heading level; **`syncId`** to share the hover; **`texture`** for the patterns.
- **`data`**, **`x`**, **`xLabel`** on the Frame, for the table, and for a Bar, Line or Area inside that is given none. Unsaid, the table takes the part's own.
- **`format`** and **`formatX`** for the numbers and the categories, set once on the Frame and inherited by the part, the tooltip, the card and the table. A part's own format wins in the plot, and the table follows it.
- **`size`** and **`height`** on the Frame, for the part that sets neither and for the states that stand in for the plot.
- On every part: **`label`** to name a plot outside a Frame, **`loading`** to draw its skeleton, **`onSelect`** to hear a choice, **`details`** to open a card on it. A Bar, Line, Area and Sparkline, and Chart.Legend and Chart.Scale, take their box's native props and a ref, and `aria-describedby` describes the plot's svg. Each part's page lists its own.

## Choosing a mark

A chart that answers "what is this?" and "show me more" is the point of a platform's charts, and the kit does it one way everywhere:

- **`onSelect`** hears a choice: a bar, a point, a slice, a tile, a cell. It filters what is under the chart, or drills down.
- **`details`** opens a card on the choice: the kit renders its head (the swatch, the name, the category, the value; for a whole category, every series' value) and the caller renders the rest under it, facts and a way to the record. The card is a Popover anchored to the mark: Escape and a click outside close it, and focus returns to the plot.
- **A drill-down** is a Frame whose `path` grows: the click redraws the same plot one level down, the marks moving to their new places, and the path holds the way back. Two or three levels is the ceiling; past that the reader wants a table with filters.
- **The keyboard gets the same.** A plot that chooses is focusable: on a Bar, a Line or an Area one tab stop, named by the title, whose arrow keys walk the categories with the tooltip (Left and Right; Up and Down too on a horizontal bar chart), Home and End go to either end, and Enter or Space chooses the one the keys are on, even with a pointer resting on another; each step is said in a polite live region, and back on the plot the tooltip shows where the keys left it. A Treemap's tiles and a Heatmap's cells are buttons and do it themselves. A plot that chooses nothing is no tab stop.
- **A pointer over a mark that chooses is a pointer.** A plot with neither `onSelect` nor `details` shows the default cursor and no focus ring on a click, so nothing promises what it cannot do.

## Small multiples

Two measures of different scale, or more than six series, are several small charts, not one big one. The Frame makes them honest: give every chart the same `domain`, so a bar's height means the same thing on each, and the same `syncId`, so a hover on one shows the same category on all. A cumulative that needs its own scale says so in its description and keeps `baseline="auto"`.

## Textures

Colour is never the only channel, and in print, under colour-vision loss and in a forced-colours mode it is not a channel at all. `texture` on the Frame gives every series a pattern in its own colour, in a fixed order the legend and the tooltip repeat: the first series solid, then hatch, back-hatch, dots, cross, lines, columns. The pattern is the colour at 30% under 1.5px marks in the colour, 8px across, so the series still reads as its hue. Bars, areas and rings take it; a line's stroke stays solid, since a 2px line has no room for a pattern and its marker and end label already set it apart. Turn it on for a chart that will be printed or exported, or everywhere in a product that must meet a print or high-contrast requirement.

## Motion

Marks arrive once, over `motion.duration.slow` (400ms) on the standard curve: bars grow from the baseline, lines draw in, a ring sweeps round. A sparkline draws in place: it sits in rows and tiles by the dozen. A change of data moves the marks the same way, which is what makes a drill-down read as the same chart one level down rather than a new one. The tooltip follows the pointer over `motion.duration.fast`; a legend hover fades the other series over the same. Under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` the marks draw in place and nothing fades. Nothing loops, nothing pulses but a skeleton, and no number counts up.

_Example: story `Stories.Motion`._

## Series and tones

Every series names a `color.chart.*` token through its `tone`. A status tone on a chart is data, the same rule as a Badge or a Stat, and a series that is not a status never wears one.

| Tone                                          | Use                                                                                                                      |
| --------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `success`, `warning`, `danger`, `information` | The series carries a status: satisfied, at risk, overdue, in progress.                                                   |
| `brand`                                       | The one series the reader is asked to look at.                                                                           |
| `neutral`                                     | Context: totals, the remainder, last period, the plan. Also a target line and Other.                                     |
| `categorical.1` to `categorical.6`            | Categories with no status, in this order: blue, orange, teal, red, purple, green. The default when a series has no tone. |
| `categorical.7`                               | Other: the fold for everything past the sixth. Grey.                                                                     |

The order is not cosmetic. It was chosen by enumerating every order of the six hues and keeping the ones whose neighbours stay apart under deutan and protan vision: the worst neighbouring pair sits at ΔE 12.7 in both modes, above the floor of 8, and the first three validate against each other in every pairing, which is why a Scatter takes three groups at most. Assign in order, never by rank: a filter that hides a series must not repaint the survivors. Past six, fold the tail into Other, split into small charts, or make a table; never a seventh hue.

Two more scales exist for a Heatmap: `color.chart.sequential.1` to `5`, blue from light to dark for how much; and `color.chart.diverging.negative.bold`, `negative`, `midpoint`, `positive`, `positive.bold`, red against blue around grey for above and below.

_Example: story `Stories.Emphasis`._

## Content

- **The title is a noun phrase**: "Coverage by control family", "Findings over time". Not a sentence, not a verb.
- **The description is the period, the unit or the source**, one line: "Opened in the month", "Sized by exposure in $K". While a drill-down is open it says the level: "Components of Payments".
- **A crumb is the level's name**: "All systems", then "Payments".
- **A series label is what the legend, the tooltip, the card and the table call it**: "Other than satisfied", not "other". Sentence case, no acronyms the reader would not say.
- **The numbers are formatted once**, on the Frame: grouped, two decimals at most, compact from ten thousand. A unit goes in `format`, so the axis, the tooltip, the labels, the card and the table agree.
- **A card's body is facts and one way onward**: two or three KeyValues and a button to the record. Not a form, not a second chart.
- **A reference says what it is**: "Target", "Limit", "Today", "Milestone C"; a date band says what happened in it: "Assessment window".
- **A summary is one sentence with the numbers in it**: "Open findings fell from 14 in January to 5 in September." A screen reader hears it after the description; nobody sees it.

## Style

| Element      | Token                                                                                                                                                   |
| ------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Series       | `color.chart.<tone>` · the same step in both modes                                                                                                      |
| Grid, axis   | `color.border` · 1px solid                                                                                                                              |
| Ticks        | `font.body.xsmall` · `color.text.subtlest` · tabular                                                                                                    |
| Axis titles  | `font.body.xsmall` · `color.text.subtle`                                                                                                                |
| Labels       | `font.body.xsmall` · `color.text.subtle` · tabular                                                                                                      |
| Tooltip      | `elevation.surface.overlay` · `color.border` · `radius.medium` · `elevation.shadow.overlay` · `space.150` inline, `space.100` block                     |
| Card         | The [Popover](?path=/docs/components-popover--docs)'s surface, anchored to the mark · the value in `font.heading.page` at medium                        |
| Hover cursor | `color.background.neutral.subtle.hovered` behind a bar · `color.border.bold` across a line chart                                                        |
| Reference    | `color.chart.<tone>` · 1px dashed 4 3 · label `font.body.xsmall` in `color.text.subtlest`, above the plot for a vertical line                           |
| Hovered mark | `color.chart.<tone>.hovered`: one step darker in light, one lighter in dark                                                                             |
| Texture      | The series colour at 30% under 1.5px marks in the colour · 8px repeat · `radius` 2px on a swatch                                                        |
| Dimmed       | `opacity.disabled`, over `motion.duration.fast`                                                                                                         |
| Refreshing   | `opacity.loading`                                                                                                                                       |
| Skeleton     | `color.skeleton` and `color.skeleton.subtle`, pulsing                                                                                                   |
| Focus        | `color.border.focused` on the plot, keyboard only                                                                                                       |
| Motion       | `motion.duration.slow` on `motion.easing.standard` for the marks (a sparkline's draw in place) · `motion.duration.fast` for the tooltip and the dimming |

Every series tone, the categorical set and Other, and each one's hovered step, clears 3:1 as a mark on every surface a chart sits on, in every mode; the contrast test holds them. A Heatmap's scales run down to the surface on purpose, so their faint steps do not: `color.chart.sequential.1` to `3`, `color.chart.diverging.negative`, `midpoint` and `positive`, and zero's `color.chart.track` fall under 3:1 in light, in dark or in both. A cell or a key's swatch in one of them wears a 1px `color.border.bold` edge, which holds 3:1, and an empty cell is a dashed edge with no fill, so no cell sinks into the page or passes for a low value; the values are one Values press away and in the table. A wash (an area's fill, a band, a ring's track) is decoration beside a mark that holds 3:1. Text never wears a chart colour: values, labels and legends stay in the text tokens, and a coloured mark beside them carries identity. The one place text sits on a chart colour is a status Heatmap cell, which is the Badge's fill and text, already in the contrast test.

## Accessibility

- **The Frame is a figure named by its title and described by its line and its summary.** A screen reader hears "Coverage by control family, figure", then the title as a heading where the page has an outline, the description, the path as a Breadcrumb, the legend as a list of toggle buttons, then the plot. The summary is the figure's description only, so it is not heard twice.
- **The table is one toggle away, for everyone.** Every kind in a Frame lays the same numbers out as a Table when the Table toggle is pressed: a Bar, Line or Area by category, a Scatter by point, a Donut by slice with each share, a Treemap by leaf with every level, a Heatmap pivoted. The toggle is a toggle button whose name stays "Table" while `aria-pressed` says whether the table shows, so a voice command that says what the reader sees still works, and the plot's markup is not the only copy of the data. While the table shows, the part stays and draws nothing, so the table follows its data. The tooltip enhances; it never gates.
- **A colour-scale Heatmap's values are one press away.** In a Frame, a Values toggle prints them on their cells, for keyboard, touch and magnifier readers who cannot hover.
- **A plot that chooses is one tab stop.** A Bar, Line or Area with `onSelect` or `details` is `role="application"` with the role description "chart", named by the Frame's title (or its own `label`) and described by its keys: "Left and right arrows move between categories, Home and End go to the first and the last, Enter chooses." Each step of the keys is said in the plot's polite live region, the category and every visible value, then a stack's total: "AU: Satisfied 18, Partial 4, Other than satisfied 3, Not assessed 1, total 26". Enter or Space chooses it, opening its card when the plot has one. The focus ring shows on the keyboard, not on a click.
- **A plot that chooses nothing is an image** named by the title, with no tab stop: its numbers are the table twin's. A plot with no name is decoration: hidden from a screen reader and not focusable, so a sparkline beside a number says nothing twice. One that chooses with no name is named "Chart" and warns in development: put it in a Frame.
- **The card is a dialog** named "[the plot's name], details"; focus moves into it and back to the plot when it closes; Escape closes it.
- **Loading says so.** A loading plot is `aria-busy` and named "[the plot's name], loading"; a refreshing one is `aria-busy` over the last plot.
- **A summary is the chart in a sentence.** With `summary`, the figure is described by it, so a screen reader hears the trend without walking the table.
- **Textures are the second channel.** With `texture`, a series is its colour and its pattern, in the plot, the legend and the PNG, so a stack reads in greyscale print. In a forced-colours mode the marks keep their colours, and so do the legend's, the tooltip's and the card's swatches, outlined in the system's text colour, so a name still maps to its mark. The categorical order is still validated for colour vision; textures are the belt to that brace.
- **The tools are buttons.** Download is a menu of two items, Expand opens a Dialog that returns focus when it closes, and both are disabled while the plot is loading, empty or failed. The CSV starts with a byte order mark, so a spreadsheet reads accented and non-Latin names, and a text cell that a spreadsheet would run as a formula (`=`, `+`, `-`, `@`) is written as text; its file name keeps letters in any script. Download PNG is disabled, with its reason, for a part that draws no image (a Heatmap is a table), and a PNG that cannot be drawn says so in an alert under the header.
- **Colour is never the only channel.** Two or more series have a legend; a status series has its word in the legend, the tooltip and the table; a Heatmap's status cells print their value; a target is ink, not a hue; a gap in a line is a gap.
- **The categorical order is validated** for deutan and protan vision (Machado 2009, severity 1.0) and for normal vision, both modes. A Scatter's groups stop at three for the same reason.
- **Motion respects the reader.** Under reduced motion the marks draw in place and nothing fades.
- **The axe gate runs every kind's matrix** in both modes.

## Props

The Frame, `Chart`, accepts native figure attributes, events, styles and refs. `title` remains the visible chart title. Native DOM ids, refs and handlers belong to the original figure; expanding creates a separately named figure without duplicating those attributes or moving the caller's ref. Internal PNG export still reads the same figure.

_Props of `Chart.Frame`, generated from its types:_

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `title` (required) | `string` |  | What the chart shows, as a noun phrase: "Coverage by control family". It names the plot to a screen reader. |
| `titleLevel` | `1 \| 2 \| 3 \| 4 \| 5 \| 6` |  | The title's heading level, so a dashboard's charts are in the page's outline. Unsaid, the level the surrounding HeadingLevelProvider or titled Section gives, and plain text outside every one. |
| `description` | `ReactNode` |  | One line under the title: the period, the unit, the source. With `summary`, the figure's description. |
| `summary` | `string` |  | One sentence for a screen reader that says what the chart shows: "Open findings fell from 14 in January to 5 in September." Part of the figure's description. Not shown. |
| `path` | `ChartCrumb[]` |  | The levels drilled into so far, from the top: `[{ label: "All families", onSelect }, { label: "AC" }]`. A Breadcrumb under the title; every crumb but the last goes back. |
| `series` | `ChartSeries[]` |  | The series, for the legend and the table, and for a Bar, Line or Area inside that is given none. Unsaid, the legend keys what the part inside draws: its series, its groups, its slices or its branches. |
| `legend` | `"bottom" \| "none" \| "top"` |  | Where the legend sits. `top` when there are two or more series, `none` for one: the title names it. At a narrow width the header wraps, the tools stay on the title's row and the legend starts on the next. |
| `swatch` | `"dot" \| "line" \| "square"` |  | The legend's swatch: a square for bars and areas, a stroke for lines, a dot for points. Unsaid, the part inside says which. |
| `texture` | `boolean` |  | Every series wears a pattern as well as its colour, in the plot and in the legend: for print, colour-vision loss and forced colours. |
| `syncId` | `string` |  | Charts with the same id share their hover: the tooltip moves on all of them. For small multiples. |
| `actions` | `ReactNode` |  | Controls at the end of the header: a range, a filter. A retry belongs beside the error, in `onRetry`. |
| `download` | `("csv" \| "png")[]` |  | The files the reader can take away, as a Download menu in the header: the table twin as a CSV for a spreadsheet, the plot as a PNG at twice the pixel density with the title and the legend above it. |
| `expandable` | `boolean` |  | An Expand button in the header that opens the same chart in a large Dialog, the plot redrawn at `large`. |
| `state` | `"empty" \| "error" \| "loading" \| "ready" \| "refreshing"` |  | `loading` draws the plot's skeleton at its height; `refreshing` keeps the last plot, dimmed, with a spinner in the header; `empty` and `error` say so in the plot's place. The same word as DataTable's `state`. With `ready` and `data` that has no records, the Frame says it is empty. |
| `status` | `"empty" \| "error" \| "loading" \| "ready" \| "refreshing"` |  | The plot's state, under its old name. `state` wins when both are set. @deprecated Use `state`, the name DataTable uses; `ledger/no-deprecated-name` fixes it. |
| `statusTitle` | `string` |  | What an empty or failed plot says. "Nothing to show yet" and "The chart could not load" when unsaid. |
| `statusText` | `string` |  |  |
| `onRetry` | `(() => void)` |  | A failed plot's Try again, beside its message, as DataTable's error has. |
| `statusAction` | `ReactNode` |  | An action beside an empty or failed plot's message: the create action, Clear filters. |
| `data` | `ChartDatum[]` |  | The records and the category key: what a Bar, Line or Area inside draws when it is given none, and what the table twin and the CSV lay out. Unsaid, the twin takes the part's own: every kind has one, one toggle away. |
| `x` | `string` |  |  |
| `xLabel` | `string` |  | What the table calls the category column: "Month", "Family"; for a Donut its slices, for a Treemap its top level. The part's axis title, else the key, when unsaid. |
| `columns` | `ChartColumn[]` |  | Columns for the table twin and the CSV beyond the series, each a key in the datum: a name beside the category (`place: "before"`), a total, a share, an owner after the series. Facts the plot does not draw, so the twin is the record's table and not only the plot's. A Scatter's twin takes them too, beside its point columns. |
| `format` | `Formatter` |  | The number format the plot, the tooltip and the table share. A part's own `format` wins in the plot, and the table follows it. |
| `formatX` | `CategoryFormatter` |  |  |
| `size` | `"large" \| "medium" \| "small"` |  | The plot's height: the part inside takes it when it sets neither `size` nor `height`, and the states stand in at it. |
| `height` | `number` |  |  |
| `children` (required) | `ReactNode` |  | The plot. |

### Chart.Legend

_Props of `Chart.Legend`, generated from its types:_

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `series` (required) | `ChartSeries[]` |  |  |
| `swatch` | `"dot" \| "line" \| "square"` | `square` | A square for bars and areas, a stroke for lines, a dot for points. |
| `texture` | `boolean` |  | The swatches carry each series' pattern. The Frame's `texture` sets it. |

## Don't

Two measures of different scale are two charts, one axis each, never one plot. Every chart sits in its Frame with a title, a period and its table, and loading holds the plot's height with its silhouette, never a spinner.

<!-- page: Patterns/Chart/Area (src/stories/patterns/ChartArea.mdx) -->

# Area

**Status: Stable.**

A [Line](?path=/docs/patterns-chart-line--docs) with a wash under it: the hue at 12%, so the plot says "how much" where a line alone says "which way". Stacked, the washes are parts of a whole over time, and the top edge is the total. Everything a Line takes, an Area takes; the difference is the fill and `stacked`. It lives in a [Chart](?path=/docs/patterns-chart-overview--docs) Frame.

_Example: story `Stories.AreaMatrix`._

## Anatomy

| Part     | What it is                                                                                                                                                       |
| -------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Line     | 2px in the series' tone, round joins, as on a Line.                                                                                                              |
| Wash     | The series' tone at 12% from the line to the baseline; in a stack, from the line to the series below. With `texture`, the series' pattern in its colour instead. |
| Marker   | 8px ringed, on hover, or on every point with `dots`.                                                                                                             |
| The rest | End labels, bands, references, gaps and axes as on a Line.                                                                                                       |

## Variants

| Variant                                                                                   | Use                                                                                                                                                                           |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| One series                                                                                | A count whose size matters: open findings, month by month. The wash gives it weight.                                                                                          |
| `stacked`                                                                                 | Parts of a whole over time: open and closed as parts of the month's total. The tooltip totals the stack, and each end label sits on its band's top with the band's own value. |
| `texture`                                                                                 | Each wash its pattern: four assessors stacked read apart in print.                                                                                                            |
| `curve="smooth"`, `labels="end"`, `domain`, `scale="time"`, `delta`, `bands`, `reference` | As on a Line.                                                                                                                                                                 |

_Example: story `Stories.Single`._
_Example: story `Stories.Stacked`._
_Example: story `Stories.Textured`._

## Sizes

`size` is the plot's height: `small` 120px, `medium` 200px (the default), `large` 320px, or `height` in pixels; unsaid, the Frame's, and `large` in the Frame's expanded Dialog. As on a Line, `data`, `x` and `series` may be left to the Frame, or given here and learned by it, and every category keeps a label fitted to the room up to the next point.

_Example: story `Stories.LongCategories`._

The value axis starts at zero, since a wash measures from it: a cropped wash exaggerates as a cropped bar does. There is no `baseline` here (the prop is ignored, and deprecated); a trend where the change matters more than the size is a [Line](?path=/docs/patterns-chart-line--docs) with `baseline="auto"`.

## States

| State    | What changes                                                                                                                                                                            |
| -------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Hover    | A hairline across the plot at the category, a marker on every line there, the tooltip.                                                                                                  |
| Hidden   | A series hidden from the Frame's legend leaves the plot and the table; a stack closes up, and the value axis keeps its scale.                                                           |
| Chosen   | With `onSelect` or `details`: a click in a category's column, or Enter on the focused plot, chooses it; the card opens on the point. On an unstacked area every series is ringed there. |
| Loading  | A skeleton line with a `color.skeleton.subtle` wash, pulsing, at the plot's height.                                                                                                     |
| Entering | The areas draw in over `motion.duration.slow`.                                                                                                                                          |

_Example: story `Stories.Details`._

## Modifiers

- **`stacked`** for parts of a whole; **`texture`** for the patterns.
- **`curve`**, **`dots`**, **`labels`**, **`bands`**, **`reference`**, **`connectNulls`**, **`xLabel`**, **`yLabel`**, **`format`**, **`formatX`**, **`onSelect`**, **`details`**, **`loading`**, **`label`** as on a Line, and its native props and ref.

## Content

- **Stack only parts of one whole.** Series that are not parts (three assessors' counts) are lines.
- **Two series that cross are lines**, not two washes: where washes overlap they mix into a colour on nobody's legend.
- **One series or a stack**; never several unstacked areas.
- The rest as on a Line: label the end, declare a cropped axis, keep a gap.

## Style

| Element  | Token                                                                             |
| -------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Line     | `color.chart.<tone>` · 2px · round joins                                          |
| Wash     | `color.chart.<tone>` at 12% · or its pattern: the colour at 30% under 1.5px marks |
| Marker   | 8px · 2px ring in the surface it sits on                                          |
| Skeleton | `color.skeleton` path over a `color.skeleton.subtle` wash                         |
| The rest | As on a Line                                                                      |

## Accessibility

- **As a Line**: named by the Frame or `label`; one tab stop with the arrow keys, Home, End, Enter and a live region when it chooses, an image with no tab stop when it does not; the table one toggle away, a legend for two or more series, `aria-busy` while loading.
- **A stack's total is a column in the table**, since the top edge is the only place the plot shows it.
- **The wash is decoration**: the line carries the value, so a wash at 12% that fails 3:1 against the surface costs nothing.

## Props

_Props of `Chart.Area`, generated from its types:_

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `className` | `string` |  |  |
| `data` | `ChartDatum[]` |  | Plain records, in the order they are drawn. Inside a Frame, the Frame's `data` when unsaid. |
| `details` | `((selection: ChartSelection) => ReactNode)` |  | More about the chosen point, in a card anchored to it. The card's head (the category and every series' value) is the kit's. |
| `label` | `string` |  | The plot's accessible name. Unneeded inside a Frame, which names it after its title; a plot with neither is hidden from a screen reader. |
| `onSelect` | `((selection: ChartSelection) => void)` |  | Called when a point is clicked (anywhere in its column), or Enter chooses the focused one. The selection carries no series: a point is every series at that category. With it, the plot is a tab stop whose arrow keys walk the points. |
| `size` | `"large" \| "medium" \| "small"` |  | The plot's height. The Frame's when unsaid, else `medium` (200px); `large` in the expanded Dialog. |
| `height` | `number` |  | A height in pixels when a layout must, in place of `size`. |
| `format` | `Formatter` |  | The number format for the value axis, the tooltip, the labels and the Frame's table. The Frame's, else the kit's. |
| `scale` | `"category" \| "time"` | `category` | `category` spaces the points evenly and prints their labels; `time` reads `x` as dates, spaces the points by time, and picks the ticks by the span: hours, days, months or years, in the reader's time zone (calendar days, "2026-09-04", read the same everywhere). |
| `x` | `string` |  | The key that names each datum along the category axis: a label, or a Date on a time axis. Inside a Frame, the Frame's `x` when unsaid. |
| `loading` | `boolean` |  | Draws the plot's skeleton in place of the marks. The Frame sets it from `state="loading"`. |
| `dots` | `boolean` |  | A marker on every point, for a series with few points. Hover shows one either way. |
| `series` | `ChartSeries[]` |  | One entry per value key. A series' own `format` wins over the plot's. Inside a Frame, the Frame's `series` when unsaid. |
| `labels` | `"end" \| "none"` | `none` | `end` prints each series' last value after its line. |
| `domain` | `ChartDomain` |  | The value axis' ends, to share a scale across charts; wins over `baseline`. A value below zero extends the axis and draws the zero line. With both ends pinned the ticks are round steps through zero. |
| `xLabel` | `string` |  | Titles for the axes, when the keys and the Frame's title do not say enough: the unit on the value axis. |
| `yLabel` | `string` |  |  |
| `texture` | `boolean` |  | Every series wears a pattern in its wash as well as its colour (an Area; a Line's stroke stays solid). The Frame's `texture` sets it. |
| `syncId` | `string` |  | Charts with the same id share their hover. The Frame's `syncId` sets it. |
| `formatX` | `CategoryFormatter` |  | The format for a category. On a time axis the ticks choose their own; this formats the tooltip and the card. |
| `reference` | `ChartReference[]` |  | Lines across the plot: a target, a limit, a milestone. |
| `curve` | `"linear" \| "smooth"` | `linear` | `linear` joins the points; `smooth` eases between them without overshooting. |
| `bands` | `ChartBand[]` |  | Bands across the plot: between two values (the acceptable range) or two categories or dates (an assessment window). |
| `connectNulls` | `boolean` |  | Join across a missing value. Off, a gap says the data was not there. |
| `delta` | `boolean` | `false` | Print each series' change from the point before in the tooltip and the card: "+3". |
| `stacked` | `boolean` |  | Stack the series: parts of a whole over time. End labels sit on each band's top and print the band's value; the tooltip adds the total. |
| `baseline` | `"auto" \| "zero"` |  | Ignored: an area's wash measures from zero, so its value axis always starts there. For a cropped trend where the change matters more than the size, use a Line with `baseline="auto"`. @deprecated An Area always starts at zero; remove the prop. Kept for one version. |
