<!-- page: Patterns/Chart/Bar (src/stories/patterns/ChartBar.mdx) -->

# Bar

**Status: Stable.**

Bars per category: the size of each thing, compared. Several series sit side by side or stack into parts of a whole; a bar runs down the side when its name is long; a value that is a `[from, to]` pair floats, which is how a phase window is drawn. Simple, grouped, stacked, horizontal and bullet bar charts are all this one part; a histogram is a bar chart of bins the data layer makes. It lives in a [Chart](?path=/docs/patterns-chart-overview--docs) Frame, which names it, keys it and lays it out as a table.

_Example: story `Stories.BarMatrix`._

## Anatomy

| Part         | What it is                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| ------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Bar          | 24px thick at most, the data end rounded 2px and the baseline end square; `barCategoryGap` a quarter of the slot. Grouped bars sit 2px apart.                                                                                                                                                                  |
| Segment      | In a stack, a part of the bar in its series' tone, with a 2px gap in the surface it sits on from the next, so the parts count. A part below zero stacks down from zero.                                                                                                                                        |
| Floating bar | A `[from, to]` value: the bar starts at `from`. For windows in time.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| Negative bar | A value below zero hangs from the zero line, which is drawn in `color.border.bold`; its rounded end and its label are at the data end, below.                                                                                                                                                                  |
| Texture      | With `texture`, each series' fill is its pattern in its colour; the first series stays solid.                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| End label    | The value at the bar's end in `font.body.xsmall` and `color.text.subtle`, outside the bar; on a stack, its total at its end. Left out where it is wider than its bar's share of the category.                                                                                                                  |
| Target       | A 2px mark in `color.text` across the bar at the datum's `target` value: actual reads against planned.                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| Line         | A series drawn as a 2px line over the bars on the same axis: a cumulative, a rate, a plan. It is never part of a stack's total.                                                                                                                                                                                |
| Axes         | The category axis with a hairline, a label for every category, on two lines or cut with an ellipsis where the band is narrow; the value axis from zero, no line, ticks in `color.text.subtlest`, round steps through zero on a pinned `domain`. Titles in `color.text.subtle` when the keys do not say enough. |
| Tooltip      | The category, every series at it keyed by a square, and the total of the stacked parts when stacked. A hovered bar takes its tone's `hovered` step.                                                                                                                                                            |

## Variants

| Variant             | Use                                                                                                                            |
| ------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| One series          | Findings by source. `brand` when the reader is asked to look, `neutral` when it is context. No legend; the title names it.     |
| Grouped             | Two or three series side by side, in the categorical set. Past three the groups blur: stack, or emphasise one as a Line.       |
| `stacked`           | Parts of each whole, in the status tones or the categorical set. The tooltip totals them, and `labels="end"` prints the total. |
| `horizontal`        | Long names, or many categories: the names read whole down the side.                                                            |
| `target`            | A mark across each bar at its target: a bullet chart, without the qualitative bands.                                           |
| `[from, to]` values | Floating bars: phase windows, with `horizontal` and a `reference` for today.                                                   |
| `line`              | One series as a line over the bars, on the same axis: closed against the plan.                                                 |
| Below zero          | Variance, change, balance: the bars hang from the zero line. The axis reaches below zero on its own.                           |
| `domain`            | The value axis pinned, so charts side by side share a scale: small multiples. Its ticks are round steps through zero.          |
| `texture`           | Patterns as well as colours, for print and colour-vision loss.                                                                 |

_Example: story `Stories.Single`._
_Example: story `Stories.Grouped`._
_Example: story `Stories.Stacked`._
_Example: story `Stories.Horizontal`._
_Example: story `Stories.Targets`._
_Example: story `Stories.Windows`._
_Example: story `Stories.Combo`._
_Example: story `Stories.Negatives`._
_Example: story `Stories.Rates`._
_Example: story `Stories.Textured`._

## Sizes

`size` is the plot's height: `small` 120px, `medium` 200px (the default), `large` 320px, or `height` in pixels; unsaid, the Frame's, and `large` in the Frame's expanded Dialog. A bar never grows past 24px however wide the plot; the slots grow instead, so a wide chart of four bars still reads as four bars and not four slabs. A horizontal chart gives its category axis the width its longest name needs, to 160px, and cuts the rest with the whole name in a title. A column chart keeps a label under every bar: when a name will not fit its category it takes two lines, broken at a space, and each line past its band is cut with an ellipsis, the whole name in the tick's title, the tooltip and the table.

_Example: story `Stories.EveryCategory`._

## States

| State    | What changes                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| -------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Hover    | The tooltip for the category; a `color.background.neutral.subtle.hovered` band behind the slot; the bar under the pointer in its tone's `hovered` step (a textured bar at 85%). Synced charts hover together.              |
| Hidden   | A series hidden from the Frame's legend leaves the plot and the table; the others keep their colours, a stack closes up over zero, and the value axis keeps its scale.                                                     |
| Chosen   | With `onSelect` or `details`: the bars take the pointer, a click on one chooses it and the other categories dim; Enter or Space on the focused plot chooses the category the arrow keys are on. The card opens on the bar. |
| Loading  | Eight skeleton columns on a hairline, pulsing, at the plot's height; five skeleton bars when `horizontal`.                                                                                                                 |
| Entering | The bars grow from the baseline over `motion.duration.slow`; a change of data moves them.                                                                                                                                  |

_Example: story `Stories.Details`._

## Modifiers

- **`stacked`**, **`horizontal`**, **`labels="end"`**, **`target`**, **`line`** as in Variants.
- **`xLabel`**, **`yLabel`** print axis titles: the unit on the value axis when the title does not say it.
- **`domain`** pins the value axis, `[0, "auto"]` when unsaid; a value below zero extends it on its own. **`texture`** and **`syncId`** as on the Frame. A series' own **`format`** wins over the plot's in the tooltip, the card and the table: a fraction printed as a percentage.
- **`reference`** draws dashed lines: a target across every bar, a milestone on the category axis, labelled at the end. A `y` reference on a horizontal chart is a vertical line, labelled above the plot.
- **`format`**, **`formatX`** for the numbers and the categories, inherited from the Frame; the Frame's table prints the plot's.
- **`data`**, **`x`**, **`series`**: Inside a Frame, `data`, `x` and `series` may be left to the Frame, and the Frame learns them from the part when they are given here instead: say them once, to either.
- **`onSelect`** and **`details`** as in States; the selection is `{ datum, series?, index }`, and `series` is absent when Enter chose the whole category.
- **`loading`** draws the skeleton; the Frame sets it from `state="loading"`.
- **`label`** names the plot outside a Frame.

## Content

- **Categories are short**: a code, a name, a month. A long name goes down the side with `horizontal`.
- **Print a value only at the end** of a few bars, or a stack's total at its end. A stack's parts are the tooltip's and the table's.
- **A target is a fact about the datum**, in its own key, not a series: the mark is ink.
- **The value axis starts at zero.** A bar's length is its meaning; there is no `baseline="auto"` here on purpose. Below zero is allowed, and the zero line is drawn, because a negative bar's length still means something.

## Style

| Element   | Token                                                                                                      |
| --------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Bar       | `color.chart.<tone>` · 24px at most · `radius` 2px at the data end · hover in `color.chart.<tone>.hovered` |
| Zero line | `color.border.bold` · 1px                                                                                  |
| Texture   | The colour at 30% under 1.5px marks · 8px repeat                                                           |
| Stack gap | 2px of the surface it sits on (`utility.elevation.surface.current`)                                        |
| Group gap | 2px                                                                                                        |
| End label | `font.body.xsmall` · `color.text.subtle` · tabular · 4px off the end                                       |
| Target    | `color.text` · 2px · 24px across                                                                           |
| Line      | `color.chart.<tone>` · 2px · round joins · a ringed 8px marker on hover                                    |
| Cursor    | `color.background.neutral.subtle.hovered` behind the slot                                                  |
| Dimmed    | `opacity.disabled`, over `motion.duration.fast`                                                            |
| Skeleton  | `color.skeleton` columns on a `color.border` hairline                                                      |

## Accessibility

- **A plot that chooses is one tab stop.** With `onSelect` or `details`, the svg is named by the Frame's title (or `label`), with the role description "chart" and its keys as its description. Left and Right move between the categories of a column chart; Up and Down (and Left and Right) down the rows of a horizontal one; Home and End go to the first and the last. Each step says the category and every visible value in a polite live region: "AU: Satisfied 18, Partial 4, Other than satisfied 3, Not assessed 1, total 26". Enter or Space chooses it; the card that opens is a dialog, and focus returns to the plot after.
- **A plot that chooses nothing is an image**, named by the Frame's title, with no tab stop: the table twin carries its numbers. Unnamed, it is decoration; one with `onSelect` or `details` and no name is named "Chart" and warns in development.
- **The table is the other copy** of the same numbers, one toggle away in the Frame; a stack's parts and its total are columns there.
- **A status series says its status** in the legend, the tooltip and the table; the tone reinforces.
- **The target is a mark in ink**, not a colour, so it reads under every vision.
- **Loading is `aria-busy`** and named "[the plot's name], loading".
- **`texture` gives a stack a second channel**, so its parts read in print and where fills are flattened.

## Props

_Props of `Chart.Bar`, generated from its types:_

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `data` | `ChartDatum[]` |  | Plain records, in the order they are drawn. Inside a Frame, the Frame's `data` when unsaid. |
| `x` | `string` |  | The key that names each datum along the category axis. Inside a Frame, the Frame's `x` when unsaid. |
| `series` | `ChartSeries[]` |  | One entry per value key. A series' own `format` wins over the plot's. Inside a Frame, the Frame's `series` when unsaid. |
| `stacked` | `boolean` |  | Stack the series in one bar per category, parts of a whole. A part below zero stacks down from zero. |
| `horizontal` | `boolean` |  | Categories down the side, values across: for long names, or many categories. |
| `labels` | `"end" \| "none"` | `none` | `end` prints each bar's value at its end, or a stack's total at the stack's end. On a column chart too narrow for every label to fit its bar's share of the category, none prints; the tooltip and the table hold them. |
| `target` | `string` |  | A key in each datum holding a target: drawn as a mark across the bar, so actual reads against planned. |
| `line` | `ChartSeries` |  | A series drawn as a line over the bars on the same axis: a cumulative, a rate, a plan. It is not part of a stack's total. |
| `domain` | `ChartDomain` |  | The value axis' ends, to share a scale across charts. `[0, "auto"]` when unsaid; a value below zero extends the axis below it and draws the zero line. With both ends pinned the ticks are round steps through zero. |
| `xLabel` | `string` |  | Titles for the axes, when the keys and the Frame's title do not say enough: the unit on the value axis. |
| `yLabel` | `string` |  |  |
| `texture` | `boolean` |  | Every series wears a pattern as well as its colour, so a stack reads in print and under colour-vision loss. The Frame's `texture` sets it for the legend too. |
| `syncId` | `string` |  | Charts with the same id share their hover. The Frame's `syncId` sets it. |
| `size` | `"large" \| "medium" \| "small"` |  | The plot's height. The Frame's when unsaid, else `medium` (200px); `large` in the expanded Dialog. |
| `height` | `number` |  | A height in pixels when a layout must, in place of `size`. |
| `format` | `Formatter` |  | The number format for the value axis, the tooltip, the labels and the Frame's table. The Frame's, else the kit's. |
| `formatX` | `CategoryFormatter` |  | The format for a category: a date, a code. |
| `reference` | `ChartReference[]` |  | Lines across the plot: a target, a limit, a milestone. |
| `label` | `string` |  | The plot's accessible name. Unneeded inside a Frame, which names it after its title; a plot with neither is hidden from a screen reader. |
| `loading` | `boolean` |  | Draws the plot's skeleton in place of the marks. The Frame sets it from `state="loading"`. |
| `onSelect` | `((selection: ChartSelection) => void)` |  | Called when a bar is clicked, or Enter chooses the focused category: to drill down, or to filter what is under the chart. With it, the plot is a tab stop whose arrow keys walk the categories. |
| `details` | `((selection: ChartSelection) => ReactNode)` |  | More about what was chosen, in a card anchored to it: facts, a link to the record. The card's head (the category, the series, the value) is the kit's. |
| `className` | `string` |  |  |

<!-- page: Patterns/Chart/Donut (src/stories/patterns/ChartDonut.mdx) -->

# Donut

**Status: Stable.**

A ring of slices on a `color.chart.track`, with a number in the middle: one number against its whole, the parts around it. Half a ring is a gauge, a score against a scale with the number at its base. It sits inline, sized in pixels, beside a Stat or in a tile, and scales down in a narrower container; in a [Chart](?path=/docs/patterns-chart-overview--docs) Frame it inherits the name and the legend's interaction. There is no pie: the number in the middle is what a pie could not say, and a ring of two slices for one number is a Stat.

_Example: story `Stories.DonutMatrix`._

## Anatomy

| Part    | What it is                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Track   | The full ring in `color.chart.track`, under the slices, so a single slice reads against its whole; with `max`, the part of the whole no slice takes. It neither hovers nor keys.                                   |
| Slice   | An arc in its tone, clockwise from the top, with a 2px `elevation.surface` gap from the next, and 3° at least. A hovered slice grows 2px and takes its tone's `hovered` step; with `texture` it wears its pattern. |
| Center  | The number in the middle (`centerLabel`), `font.heading.overlay` in `color.text`: the total, the share, the one that matters.                                                                                      |
| Caption | One word under the number in `font.body.xsmall` and `color.text.subtle`: what it counts.                                                                                                                           |
| Tooltip | The slice's name and value, keyed by a square.                                                                                                                                                                     |
| Card    | On a chosen slice: the slice, its value and its share of the whole, then the caller's facts.                                                                                                                       |

## Variants

| Variant       | Use                                                                                                |
| ------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Ring          | Parts of a whole with the whole in the middle: coverage, with the satisfied share printed.         |
| One value     | `value` against `max`: 62% assessed, the rest the track. `tone` is the value's status, or `brand`. |
| `arc="half"`  | A gauge: `value` against `max`, the number at the base, the slice in the tone the score earns.     |
| Beside a Stat | The ring at 120 with its legend as a `Chart.Legend`, the Stat carrying the words.                  |

_Example: story `Stories.BesideStat`._
_Example: story `Stories.Gauge`._

## Sizes

| `size` | `thickness` | Where                                                   |
| ------ | ----------- | ------------------------------------------------------- |
| 64     | 8           | A cell, a list row, a card's corner: done against left. |
| 120    | 12          | Beside a Stat. The default.                             |
| 160    | 16          | A tile of its own, with a number and a caption inside.  |
| 200    | 20          | A gauge that is a section's point.                      |

A gauge is half as tall as it is wide, plus 4px for the base. The number fits inside a ring of 120 or more; at 64 it sits beside the ring.

`size` is the most a ring takes. In a container narrower than that, a block, a grid tile or a flex row, the ring scales down with its thickness and keeps its ratio, as an image does; the number and the caption keep their type size. In a Frame's expanded Dialog the ring draws at 320px across at least, the `large` plot's height, its thickness in proportion.

_Example: story `Stories.Narrow`._

## States

| State    | What changes                                                                                                                                      |
| -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Hover    | The slice grows 2px outward; the tooltip.                                                                                                         |
| Isolated | A slice hidden from the Frame's legend leaves the ring; the others keep their angles and the track shows through.                                 |
| Focused  | With `onSelect` or `details`, on the keyboard: an arc in `color.border.focused` along the slice's inner edge, in the hole.                        |
| Chosen   | With `onSelect` or `details`: a click, or Enter or Space on a focused slice, chooses it and the others dim; the card opens at the slice's middle. |
| Loading  | A skeleton ring at the size and thickness, pulsing.                                                                                               |
| Entering | The slices sweep round from the top over `motion.duration.slow`.                                                                                  |

_Example: story `Stories.Details`._

In a [Chart](?path=/docs/patterns-chart-overview--docs) Frame the ring needs nothing repeated: the Frame's legend keys its slices, a hover dims the others and a click hides one, and its Table toggle lays them out, a row per slice with its value and its share of the whole, headed by the Frame's `xLabel`. A slice hidden from the legend leaves the ring and stays in the table, which is the data.

_Example: story `Stories.Framed`._
_Example: story `Stories.SmallShare`._

## Modifiers

- **`arc="half"`** for the gauge; **`size`** (the largest diameter) and **`thickness`** in pixels; **`texture`** for the patterns.
- **`slices`**, or **`value`** with **`tone`** for one value; **`max`** for the whole they are parts of, the rest of it the track. Without `max` the whole is the slices' sum, the hidden ones included, so a share is always of the same whole.
- **`centerLabel`** and **`caption`** for the middle.
- **`label`** names the ring, as it names every plot; the Frame's title when unsaid. For one version the earlier spelling still works, with a warning in development: `name` names the ring and is deprecated for `label`, and with no `centerLabel` a `label` beside `name`, or one that is not a string, draws the middle and is deprecated for `centerLabel`. `ledger/no-deprecated-name` rewrites both.
- **`format`** for the tooltip, the card and the Frame's table. The Frame's, else the kit's.
- **`onSelect`** and **`details`** as in States; the selection is `{ slice, share, index }`.
- **`loading`** draws the skeleton; the Frame sets it from `state="loading"`.
- Native props and a ref reach the ring's box, and `aria-describedby` describes the ring: its svg when it chooses nothing, its group when its slices are the tab stops.

_Example: story `Stories.Naming`._
_Example: story `Stories.NativeAttributes`._

## Content

- **Four slices at most, five with Other.** Past that the angles stop reading; the data is a Bar.
- **The number in the middle is the point**: the share, the total, the score. The slices explain it.
- **A caption is one word**: "satisfied", "open", "posture".
- **Slices in status tones when they are statuses**, the categorical set when they are kinds. A remainder is `max`'s track, never a made-up slice.
- **A gauge's slice wears the tone its score earns**: `success` past the target, `warning` near it, `danger` below.
- **A sliver still draws**: 3° at least when more than one slice shows, so 1 of 372 can be hovered; its value and share stay true in the tooltip, the card and the table.

## Style

| Element  | Token                                                                                            |
| -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Track    | `color.chart.track`                                                                              |
| Slice    | `color.chart.<tone>` · 2px `elevation.surface` gap · hover +2px in `color.chart.<tone>.hovered`  |
| Center   | `font.heading.overlay` · `color.text`                                                            |
| Caption  | `font.body.xsmall` · `color.text.subtle`                                                         |
| Dimmed   | `opacity.disabled`, over `motion.duration.fast`                                                  |
| Focused  | A 3px arc in `color.border.focused` inside the slice's inner edge; `Highlight` in forced colours |
| Skeleton | `color.skeleton` ring                                                                            |

## Accessibility

- **Named by `label` or the Frame**, a ring that chooses nothing is an image (`role="img"`) with no tab stop; unnamed it is decoration beside its Stat, hidden from a screen reader so the number reads once.
- **One value against `max` is a meter**: `role="meter"` named by the ring, with its value, its range and its value in words ("72 of 100"). The number in the middle is then hidden, so it is heard once.
- **The number is text**, in the middle, not drawn: a screen reader reads it, and it never wears a chart colour.
- **The legend carries the names**; a slice's tone reinforces its word. Beside a Stat, the legend is a `Chart.Legend`.
- **The table is one toggle away** in a Frame: every slice with its value and its share, so the angles are never the only way to read the parts.
- **With `onSelect` or `details`, each slice is a button** and a tab stop, named with its value and share ("Partial: 40, 11%"); Enter and Space choose it as a click does, and the ring itself is no tab stop. A ring that chooses and has no name is named "Chart", with a warning in development.
- **A chosen slice's card is a dialog**: the slice says it opens one (`aria-haspopup`, `aria-expanded`), and focus returns to that slice when it closes.
- **Loading is `aria-busy`** and named "[the ring's name], loading".

## Props

_Props of `Chart.Donut`, generated from its types:_

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `slices` | `DonutSlice[]` |  | The parts, in order from the top, clockwise. |
| `value` | `number` |  | One value against `max`, in place of `slices`: a gauge's score, a single share. It is one slice, named by the ring, in `tone`. |
| `tone` | `ChartTone` |  | The tone of `value`'s slice: the tone the score earns. `brand` when unsaid. |
| `max` | `number` |  | The whole the slices are parts of: the slices take their share of it, and the rest of the ring is the track. The slices' sum when unsaid. |
| `centerLabel` | `ReactNode` |  | The number in the middle: the total, the share, the one that matters. |
| `label` | `ReactNode` |  | The ring's accessible name, as `label` names every plot. The Frame's title when unsaid. For one version the earlier spelling still draws the middle: with no `centerLabel`, a `label` that is not a string, or one beside the deprecated `name`, is the centre text, with a warning in development. Write the middle as `centerLabel`; `ledger/no-deprecated-name` fixes it. |
| `caption` | `string` |  | One word under the number: what it counts. |
| `arc` | `"full" \| "half"` | `full` | `full` is a ring; `half` is a gauge, open at the bottom, the number at its base. |
| `size` | `number` | `120` | The largest diameter in pixels. In a narrower container the ring scales down, keeping its proportions; the number keeps its type size. In the expanded Dialog it draws at 320px, the `large` plot's height, at least. |
| `thickness` | `number` | `12` | The ring's thickness in pixels at `size`; it scales with the ring. |
| `format` | `Formatter` |  | The number format in the tooltip. |
| `name` | `string` |  | The ring's accessible name. @deprecated Use `label`, which names every plot; `ledger/no-deprecated-name` fixes it. |
| `texture` | `boolean` |  | Every slice wears a pattern as well as its colour. The Frame's `texture` sets it. |
| `loading` | `boolean` |  | Draws the ring's skeleton in place of the slices. The Frame sets it from `state="loading"`. |
| `onSelect` | `((selection: DonutSelection) => void)` |  | Called when a slice is clicked, or activated with Enter or Space. |
| `details` | `((selection: DonutSelection) => ReactNode)` |  | More about the chosen slice, in a card anchored to it. The card's head (the slice, its value and its share) is the kit's. |
| `className` | `string` |  |  |

<!-- page: Patterns/Chart/Heatmap (src/stories/patterns/ChartHeatmap.mdx) -->

# Heatmap

**Status: Stable.**

A grid of rows by columns with a value painted in each cell: how much, across two dimensions. One hue from light to dark for a magnitude; two hues around grey for above and below; or the status tones by place, which is the risk matrix. It is a table, in the markup as on the page, so a screen reader reads it as one and the keyboard walks it. `Chart.Scale` is its key. It lives in a [Chart](?path=/docs/patterns-chart-overview--docs) Frame.

_Example: story `Stories.HeatmapMatrix`._

## Anatomy

| Part    | What it is                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| ------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Cell    | `radius.xsmall`, 2px from its neighbours, its fill the value's step on the scale; a faint step (one close to the surface) adds a `color.border.bold` edge. With `zeroStep`, a zero is `color.chart.track`. A cell with no value is a dashed edge with no fill and no number. |
| Value   | Printed in the cell on a status scale (the tone's text on its fill); on a colour scale a screen-reader-only text, or with `showValues` the number on an `elevation.surface` chip.                                                                                            |
| Headers | Column names across the top, row names down the side, in `font.body.xsmall` and `font.body.small`; the corner names the rows.                                                                                                                                                |
| Scale   | `Chart.Scale`: the five steps in a row with the ends or the thresholds named, the midpoint's word on a diverging one, or the status tones with their words. Under the grid, `space.150` away.                                                                                |
| Tooltip | The cell's title: row, column, value.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| Card    | On a chosen cell: the row and column, the value, then the caller's facts.                                                                                                                                                                                                    |

## Variants

| Variant              | Use                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| -------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `scale="sequential"` | How much: findings by family and month, in `color.chart.sequential.1` to `5`. The default.                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `scale="diverging"`  | Above and below a `midpoint`: schedule variance in days, red below and blue above around grey.                                                                                                                                                                      |
| A tone function      | Status by place: the risk matrix, each cell the tone its position earns, the count printed.                                                                                                                                                                         |
| `showValues`         | The value printed on a colour scale too, when the reader must read every cell: on a surface chip in `color.text`, since text never sits on a chart colour. Unsaid, a Frame around the grid offers the reader a Values toggle that prints them; `false` offers none. |

_Example: story `Stories.Sequential`._
_Example: story `Stories.Diverging`._
_Example: story `Stories.Status`._

## Sizes

| `size`   | Cell height | Where                                                         |
| -------- | ----------- | ------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `small`  | 24px        | Many rows: families by month in a rail.                       |
| `medium` | 32px        | A Section. The default.                                       |
| `large`  | 40px        | A five-by-five matrix that is a page's point, values printed. |

A cell is at least 40px wide, and every value column takes the widest heading's width, so a long heading does not make its column look weighted. Past the width it has, the grid scrolls sideways inside its own box with the row names held at the start; while it overflows the box is a named region and a tab stop, so a keyboard can scroll it. In a Frame's expanded Dialog the cells are `large`.

_Example: story `Stories.Narrow`._

## States

| State    | What changes                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Hover    | The cell's title as a tooltip.                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| Chosen   | With `onSelect` or `details` the cells with a value but zero are buttons (`selectable` says which otherwise): a click, Enter or Space chooses one, it takes the focus ring, the others dim, and the card opens on it.           |
| Linked   | With `link` the cells with a value but zero are the links it returns (`selectable` says which otherwise): the register filtered to the cell's row and column. A link takes the focus ring and navigates; it never opens a card. |
| Loading  | Every cell in `color.skeleton`, pulsing, at the grid's size. The Frame sets it from `state="loading"`.                                                                                                                          |
| Isolated | Not applicable: a heatmap has no series to hide.                                                                                                                                                                                |

_Example: story `Stories.Details`._

A cell that opens a register is a link, not a button: `link` returns the link element for a cell (a router's Link, or `<a href>`) and the cell becomes it, so a modifier or middle click opens a new tab. Both axes are levels in words, in the order given, so a risk matrix lists likelihood from the top and impact across. The table twin's values link to the same places.

_Example: story `Stories.Links`._

## Modifiers

- **`scale`**, **`domain`**, **`midpoint`**, **`showValues`** as in Variants.
- **`zeroStep`** gives zero a step of its own, so none reads apart from a few. Give the Scale the same.
- **`rowLabel`**, **`columnLabel`** name the dimensions: the corner cell, and what a screen reader hears.
- **`format`** for the values, the tooltip, the card and the Frame's table. The Frame's, else the kit's.
- **`onSelect`** and **`details`** as in States; the selection is `{ row, column, value }`. **`selectable`** says which cells choose or link.
- **`link`** returns the link a cell opens, from the same selection, or `undefined` to leave the cell as it is. A cell it links does not also choose.
- **`loading`** draws the skeleton, the grid keeping its rows and columns; the Frame sets it from `state="loading"`.
- **`label`** names the grid, a table; the Frame's title when unsaid. Native props and a ref reach the grid's box, its scroller, and `aria-describedby` describes the table.

_Example: story `Stories.NativeAttributes`._

_Example: story `Stories.Loading`._

## Content

- **A magnitude is one hue.** Never a status tone for a count: nine findings is not "danger".
- **Diverging needs a true midpoint**: zero variance, the plan, last year. Without one the data is sequential.
- **Status by place prints its count**: the tone's text on the tone's fill is the Badge's, already in the contrast test.
- **Name the dimensions**: "Likelihood" by "Impact", "Family" by "Month".
- **The scale's ends are words**: "0" and "12 findings"; "−12 days", "On plan", "+12 days".
- **Give the key the grid's `domain`**, so it prints the value at each step's edge and reads as the grid is binned; the grid's `domain` is the data's own when unsaid, which the key cannot know.
- **A status grid has a status key**: `scale="status"` with each tone and what it means, so the risk level is never carried by colour and place alone.

## Style

| Element        | Token                                                                                                                                                                            |
| -------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Cell           | `color.chart.sequential.<step>` · `color.chart.diverging.<step>` · or `color.background.<tone>` with `color.text.<tone>` · `radius.xsmall` · 2px apart                           |
| Faint step     | `color.chart.sequential.1` to `3`, `color.chart.diverging.negative`, `midpoint`, `positive` and `color.chart.track` add a 1px `color.border.bold` edge, in the cells and the key |
| Empty          | No fill · a 1px dashed `color.border.bold` edge                                                                                                                                  |
| Headers        | `font.body.xsmall` medium `color.text.subtlest` across · `font.body.small` `color.text.subtle` down                                                                              |
| Scale          | Five steps 24 by 8, 32 by 8 with thresholds · `radius.xsmall` · labels in `font.body.xsmall` `color.text.subtlest` · status swatches 12px in the cells' fills                    |
| Forced colours | A cell and a step keep their fill, outlined in `CanvasText`; an empty cell is a dashed `GrayText` box                                                                            |
| Chosen         | `color.border.focused` outline                                                                                                                                                   |
| Dimmed         | `opacity.disabled`                                                                                                                                                               |
| Skeleton       | `color.skeleton`                                                                                                                                                                 |

## Accessibility

- **It is a table**: a `table` named by `label`, column headers across and row headers down, the corner naming the rows and, for a screen reader, the columns ("Likelihood by Impact"). A screen reader reads each cell as "row, column, value".
- **Every cell has its value in text**: printed on a status scale, screen-reader-only on a colour scale, so the colour is never the only channel. In a forced-colours mode a colour-scale cell keeps its fill, outlined, rather than turning to the system background.
- **No cell sinks into the page.** The steps close to the surface fall under 3:1 on it in one mode or the other, so they wear a `color.border.bold` edge, which holds 3:1; an empty cell's edge is dashed and it has no fill, so it never passes for a low value.
- **A colour scale's values are one press away** in a Frame: Values, a toggle button whose name stays "Values" while `aria-pressed` says whether they show, prints every value on its cell for keyboard, touch and magnifier readers alike. The reader's choice holds across the table view and the expanded Dialog.
- **The table twin is the grid pivoted**: the Frame's Table toggle and CSV lay it out as a row per row and a column per column in the grid's order, headed by `rowLabel`, every value printed and no colour.
- **Cells that choose are buttons**, focusable in reading order, with the kit's focus ring, each named by its place and value ("Likely, Critical: 3"); a zero is no tab stop unless `selectable` says so. A cell that opens a card says so (`aria-haspopup="dialog"`) and whether it is open (`aria-expanded`). The card is a dialog and focus returns to the cell when it closes.
- **Cells that open a register are links**, named the same way, and the table twin carries the same links, so the reader who reads the numbers as a table can open them too.
- **The words are the locale's**: the cell's title ("SC, Jun: 12", "AU, Apr: none") and the dimensions ("Likelihood by Impact") come from `LedgerProvider` messages.
- **The scale's swatches are `aria-hidden`**: its words are text, and the values are in the cells.
- **Loading is `aria-busy`** and named "[the grid's name], loading".

## Props

_Props of `Chart.Heatmap`, generated from its types:_

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `rows` (required) | `string[]` |  | The row names, top to bottom. |
| `columns` (required) | `string[]` |  | The column names, left to right. |
| `value` (required) | `(row: string, column: string) => number \| null \| undefined` |  | The value at a row and column. `undefined` or `null` leaves the cell empty. |
| `scale` | `HeatmapScale` | `sequential` | `sequential` paints how much in one hue; `diverging` paints above and below `midpoint` in two; a function says which status tone a cell carries, from its value or its row and column, and the cell prints its value. |
| `domain` | `readonly [number, number]` |  | The values at the ends of the scale. The data's own when unsaid. Give `Chart.Scale` the same `domain`, so the key's thresholds are the grid's. |
| `midpoint` | `number` | `0` | The value that reads as nothing on a diverging scale. Zero when unsaid. |
| `zeroStep` | `boolean` |  | On a sequential scale, zero takes a step of its own in `color.chart.track`, so none reads apart from a few; every other value bins as before. Give `Chart.Scale` the same `zeroStep`. |
| `showValues` | `boolean` |  | Print the value in each cell. On for a status scale, where the tone's fill carries its text. On a colour scale a printed value sits on a surface chip; unsaid there, a Frame around the grid offers the reader a Values toggle that prints them, and the Frame's table twin carries them either way. `false` keeps them hidden and offers no toggle. |
| `size` | `"large" \| "medium" \| "small"` | `medium` | The cell's height: `small` 24px, `medium` 32px, `large` 40px. `large` in the expanded Dialog. |
| `format` | `Formatter` |  | The value's format in the cells, the tooltip, the card and the table twin. The Frame's, else the kit's. |
| `label` | `string` |  | The grid's accessible name: it is a table. The Frame's title when unsaid. |
| `rowLabel` | `string` |  | What the rows and the columns are: the corner cell, and the description a screen reader hears. |
| `columnLabel` | `string` |  |  |
| `loading` | `boolean` |  | Draws skeleton cells in place of the values, the grid keeping its rows and columns. The Frame sets it from `state="loading"`. |
| `onSelect` | `((selection: HeatmapSelection) => void)` |  | Makes the cells buttons: called when one is clicked or chosen with Enter or Space. |
| `details` | `((selection: HeatmapSelection) => ReactNode)` |  | More about the chosen cell, in a card anchored to it. The card's head (the row, the column and the value) is the kit's. |
| `link` | `((selection: HeatmapSelection) => ChartLink)` |  | The link element (a router's Link, or `<a href>`) a cell opens: the register filtered to the cell's row and column. The cell becomes that link, named by its place and value, so a modifier or middle click opens it in a new tab; the table twin's value links to the same place. Return `undefined` to leave a cell as it is. A cell that links does not also choose: `onSelect` and `details` apply to the cells it returns nothing for. |
| `selectable` | `((selection: HeatmapSelection) => boolean)` |  | Which cells choose or link, when `onSelect`, `details` or `link` is set. Every cell with a value but zero when unsaid: a zero has nothing to open. |
| `className` | `string` |  |  |

### Chart.Scale

The key under the grid. `scale="sequential"` or `"diverging"` draws the ramp with `min`, `mid` and `max` as words; given the Heatmap's `domain`, a sequential key prints the value at each step's edge in `format` (the Frame's, else the kit's), `max` replacing the top when it is a word, and `zeroStep` adds zero's swatch before the five. `scale="status"` takes `steps`, each a tone and what it means.

_Example: story `Stories.Keys`._

_Props of `Chart.Scale`, generated from its types:_

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `scale` (required) | `"diverging" \| "sequential" \| "status"` |  | Which key: the sequential or diverging ramp, or the status tones of a tone-function Heatmap. |
| `min` | `string` |  | What the low end and the high end read as: "0" and "40 findings"; "−20%" and "+20%". With `domain`, they replace the end thresholds. |
| `max` | `string` |  |  |
| `mid` | `string` |  | The midpoint's word on a diverging scale: "On plan". |
| `domain` | `readonly [number, number]` |  | The Heatmap's `domain`: on a sequential key, the value at each step's edge is printed, in `format`, so the key reads as the grid is binned. |
| `format` | `Formatter` |  | The thresholds' format. The Frame's, else the kit's. |
| `zeroStep` | `boolean` |  | The Heatmap's `zeroStep`: zero's own swatch, in `color.chart.track`, before the five. |
| `steps` | `ChartScaleStep[]` |  | For `scale="status"`: each tone the cells wear, with what it means, in order. |

## Don't

A count is one hue from light to dark, never painted in the status tones. A status grid prints its counts on its cells, never leaving the reader to hover each one.

<!-- page: Patterns/Chart/Line (src/stories/patterns/ChartLine.mdx) -->

# Line

**Status: Stable.**

A line per series over an ordered axis: a trend, a burndown, one measure against its plan. Two pixels wide with round joins, a ringed marker on hover, the last value printed after the line when asked. Straight segments by default, because the points are what was counted; a smooth curve never overshoots them. It lives in a [Chart](?path=/docs/patterns-chart-overview--docs) Frame, which names it, keys it and lays it out as a table.

_Example: story `Stories.LineMatrix`._

## Anatomy

| Part      | What it is                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| --------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Line      | 2px in the series' tone, round caps and joins. `curve="smooth"` is a monotone curve through the same points.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| Marker    | 8px across, ringed 2px in the surface so it reads over the line. On hover always; on every point with `dots`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| End label | The series' last value after its line, `font.body.xsmall` in `color.text.subtle`; labels that would collide are pushed apart by a line's height, and one pushed off its line's end leads with a stroke of the series' colour, so it still says whose it is.                                                                                          |
| Gap       | A missing value breaks the line. `connectNulls` joins across it, for a gap that is not data.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| Band      | A 10% wash between two values (the tolerable range, labelled at its top edge) or between two categories or dates (an assessment window, labelled above its middle).                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| Reference | A dashed hairline at a value (a target, a limit) or at a category (a milestone), labelled at the end or above the plot.                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| Axes      | The category axis with a hairline, or a time axis whose ticks are hours, days, months or years by the span, at the starts of those units in the reader's time zone; the value axis from zero, cropped to the data with `baseline="auto"`, or pinned with `domain`, whose ticks are round steps through zero. A value below zero draws the zero line. |
| Tooltip   | The category, every series at it keyed by a stroke, and with `delta` each change from the point before. The cursor is a `color.border.bold` hairline across the plot.                                                                                                                                                                                |
| Chosen    | The chosen category ringed on every line, in each series' tone.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |

## Variants

| Variant              | Use                                                                                                                     |
| -------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Plain                | Two or three series, each a tone. Findings open and closed.                                                             |
| `curve="smooth"`     | A few points that are readings of one continuous thing. Never for counts that jump.                                     |
| `dots`               | A marker on every point, when each point is an event and there are few of them.                                         |
| `labels="end"`       | The last value after each line: the number the reader takes away. The default for a trend in a Frame.                   |
| `baseline="auto"`    | The value axis cropped to the data: a cumulative in the hundreds where the slope is the story. The description says so. |
| `bands`, `reference` | A burndown: the tolerable range as a band, the limit in `danger`, a milestone on the category axis.                     |
| Emphasis             | One series in `brand`, the rest in `neutral`: the honest answer to "make this clearer".                                 |
| `scale="time"`       | `x` holds dates: the points are spaced by time, the ticks pick their unit, and a band or a reference takes a date.      |
| `domain`             | The value axis pinned, so charts side by side share a scale: small multiples, with `syncId` for one hover.              |
| `delta`              | Each series' change from the point before, in the tooltip and the card.                                                 |

_Example: story `Stories.Lines`._
_Example: story `Stories.Smooth`._
_Example: story `Stories.Burndown`._
_Example: story `Stories.Cropped`._
_Example: story `Stories.Gaps`._
_Example: story `Stories.Dates`._
_Example: story `Stories.Deltas`._

## Sizes

`size` is the plot's height: `small` 120px, `medium` 200px (the default), `large` 320px, or `height` in pixels; unsaid, the Frame's, and `large` in the Frame's expanded Dialog. Every category keeps a label fitted to the room up to the next one printed: whole, on two lines broken at a space, or cut with an ellipsis and its whole text as its title; at the plot's ends a label may run into the margin, and moves in from the edge rather than past it. Only where a point's slot cannot hold three characters do the labels step over whole slots, evenly from the first, so months in a card read Jan, Mar, May rather than J, F, M. A time axis draws at most eight ticks, each at a unit's start, and keeps its first and its last as the width narrows: months step by one, two, three, six or twelve from January, so a quarter's tick is a quarter's start, and the first tick and every tick that starts a new year carry the year in full ("Feb 2025", "May", … "Jan 2026"), which a two-digit year would not ("Apr 26" reads as a day). Calendar days ("2026-09-04") read the same in every zone; instants are read in the reader's `timeZone`. The right margin holds the widest end label.

The labels above the plot share one row: where a milestone's and a window's would overlap in a narrow plot, they move apart, the milestone's staying closest to its line, and milestones on one date share one label, joined with a middle dot. Each stays over its mark (a window's middle over its window) and within the plot's width, clear of the axis ticks; where the row is too short for them so, a window's label shortens before a milestone's wherever that makes room, each only as far as the row needs, with an ellipsis and its whole text as its title, and one with no room for three characters is left out. Labels inside the plot are drawn over the lines, ringed in the surface, so a line that crosses one runs behind the words.

_Example: story `Stories.LongCategories`._
_Example: story `Stories.NarrowLabels`._
_Example: story `Stories.Zones`._

## States

| State    | What changes                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Hover    | A hairline across the plot at the category, a marker on every line there, the tooltip.                                                                                                                                                            |
| Hidden   | A series hidden from the Frame's legend leaves the plot and the table; the value axis keeps its scale, so the others do not jump.                                                                                                                 |
| Chosen   | With `onSelect` or `details`: a click anywhere in a category's column, or Enter or Space on the focused plot, chooses it. Every series is ringed there and the card opens on the point. The selection carries no series: a point is the category. |
| Loading  | A skeleton line on a hairline, pulsing, at the plot's height.                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| Entering | The lines draw in over `motion.duration.slow`; a change of data moves them.                                                                                                                                                                       |

_Example: story `Stories.Details`._

## Modifiers

- **`curve`**, **`dots`**, **`labels`**, **`baseline`**, **`bands`**, **`reference`**, **`connectNulls`** as in Variants and Anatomy.
- **`scale="time"`**, **`domain`**, **`delta`** as in Variants; **`syncId`** and **`texture`** as on the Frame (a line's stroke stays solid); a series' own **`format`**.
- **`xLabel`**, **`yLabel`** print axis titles.
- **`format`**, **`formatX`** for the numbers and the categories, inherited from the Frame; the Frame's table prints the plot's.
- **`data`**, **`x`**, **`series`**: Inside a Frame, `data`, `x` and `series` may be left to the Frame, and the Frame learns them from the part when they are given here instead: say them once, to either. The Frame's legend takes a Line's stroke swatch from it.
- **`onSelect`** and **`details`** as in States; the selection is `{ datum, index }`.
- **`loading`** draws the skeleton; the Frame sets it from `state="loading"`.
- **`label`** names the plot outside a Frame; native props and a ref reach the plot's box, and `aria-describedby` describes its svg.

## Content

- **The category axis is ordered**: months, weeks, versions. Unordered categories are a Bar. Real dates go on a time axis, so a gap in the sampling is a gap in the plot.
- **Label the end**, never every point. The tooltip carries the rest.
- **A cropped axis is declared** in the description: "the axis starts at the first month's count".
- **A gap is a gap.** Say why in the description; do not join across it unless the gap is a sampling artefact.
- **A limit is `danger`**, a target is `neutral`, a milestone is `neutral` on the category axis, each labelled with its name.

## Style

| Element   | Token                                                                           |
| --------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Line      | `color.chart.<tone>` · 2px · round caps and joins                               |
| Marker    | 8px · 2px ring in the surface it sits on                                        |
| End label | `font.body.xsmall` · `color.text.subtle` · tabular · 8px after the line         |
| Band      | `color.chart.<tone>` at 10% · label `font.body.xsmall` in `color.text.subtlest` |
| Reference | `color.chart.<tone>` · 1px dashed 4 3                                           |
| Cursor    | `color.border.bold` · 1px across the plot                                       |
| Zero line | `color.border.bold` · 1px                                                       |
| Delta     | `font.body.small` · `color.text.subtlest` · tabular · signed                    |
| Chosen    | The series' tone: an 8px marker in a 16px halo at 20%                           |
| Dimmed    | `opacity.disabled`, over `motion.duration.fast`                                 |
| Skeleton  | `color.skeleton` · 2px path on a `color.border` hairline                        |

## Accessibility

- **A plot that chooses is one tab stop.** With `onSelect` or `details`, the svg is named by the Frame's title (or `label`), with the role description "chart" and its keys as its description; Left and Right move between the points, Home and End go to the first and the last, and each step says the category and every visible value in a polite live region. Enter or Space chooses it; the card that opens is a dialog, and focus returns to the plot after.
- **A plot that chooses nothing is an image**, named by the Frame's title, with no tab stop: the table twin carries its numbers.
- **The table is the other copy** of the same numbers, one toggle away in the Frame.
- **Two or more series have a legend**, and each end label is a number in the text colour, not the series colour.
- **A gap is visible under every vision**: it is an absence, not a colour.
- **Loading is `aria-busy`** and named "[the plot's name], loading".

## Props

_Props of `Chart.Line`, generated from its types:_

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `data` | `ChartDatum[]` |  | Plain records, in the order they are drawn. Inside a Frame, the Frame's `data` when unsaid. |
| `x` | `string` |  | The key that names each datum along the category axis: a label, or a Date on a time axis. Inside a Frame, the Frame's `x` when unsaid. |
| `series` | `ChartSeries[]` |  | One entry per value key. A series' own `format` wins over the plot's. Inside a Frame, the Frame's `series` when unsaid. |
| `scale` | `"category" \| "time"` | `category` | `category` spaces the points evenly and prints their labels; `time` reads `x` as dates, spaces the points by time, and picks the ticks by the span: hours, days, months or years, in the reader's time zone (calendar days, "2026-09-04", read the same everywhere). |
| `curve` | `"linear" \| "smooth"` | `linear` | `linear` joins the points; `smooth` eases between them without overshooting. |
| `dots` | `boolean` |  | A marker on every point, for a series with few points. Hover shows one either way. |
| `labels` | `"end" \| "none"` | `none` | `end` prints each series' last value after its line. |
| `baseline` | `"auto" \| "zero"` | `zero` | `zero` starts the value axis at zero; `auto` crops to the data, for a trend where the change matters more than the size. |
| `domain` | `ChartDomain` |  | The value axis' ends, to share a scale across charts; wins over `baseline`. A value below zero extends the axis and draws the zero line. With both ends pinned the ticks are round steps through zero. |
| `bands` | `ChartBand[]` |  | Bands across the plot: between two values (the acceptable range) or two categories or dates (an assessment window). |
| `connectNulls` | `boolean` |  | Join across a missing value. Off, a gap says the data was not there. |
| `delta` | `boolean` | `false` | Print each series' change from the point before in the tooltip and the card: "+3". |
| `xLabel` | `string` |  | Titles for the axes, when the keys and the Frame's title do not say enough: the unit on the value axis. |
| `yLabel` | `string` |  |  |
| `texture` | `boolean` |  | Every series wears a pattern in its wash as well as its colour (an Area; a Line's stroke stays solid). The Frame's `texture` sets it. |
| `syncId` | `string` |  | Charts with the same id share their hover. The Frame's `syncId` sets it. |
| `size` | `"large" \| "medium" \| "small"` |  | The plot's height. The Frame's when unsaid, else `medium` (200px); `large` in the expanded Dialog. |
| `height` | `number` |  | A height in pixels when a layout must, in place of `size`. |
| `format` | `Formatter` |  | The number format for the value axis, the tooltip, the labels and the Frame's table. The Frame's, else the kit's. |
| `formatX` | `CategoryFormatter` |  | The format for a category. On a time axis the ticks choose their own; this formats the tooltip and the card. |
| `reference` | `ChartReference[]` |  | Lines across the plot: a target, a limit, a milestone. |
| `label` | `string` |  | The plot's accessible name. Unneeded inside a Frame, which names it after its title; a plot with neither is hidden from a screen reader. |
| `loading` | `boolean` |  | Draws the plot's skeleton in place of the marks. The Frame sets it from `state="loading"`. |
| `onSelect` | `((selection: ChartSelection) => void)` |  | Called when a point is clicked (anywhere in its column), or Enter chooses the focused one. The selection carries no series: a point is every series at that category. With it, the plot is a tab stop whose arrow keys walk the points. |
| `details` | `((selection: ChartSelection) => ReactNode)` |  | More about the chosen point, in a card anchored to it. The card's head (the category and every series' value) is the kit's. |
| `className` | `string` |  |  |
