<!-- page: Unpatched hypervisor (src/stories/patterns/ChartScatter.mdx) -->

# Scatter

**Status: Stable.**

A point per record on two value axes: where each thing sits on two measures at once. Findings by how long they have been open and what they expose; systems by cost and open findings. Points fall into groups of a tone, three at most; a bubble's area follows a third value; two references make quadrants. Each point is a record, so a click opens its card. It lives in a [Chart](?path=/docs/patterns-chart-overview--docs) Frame.

_Example: story `Stories.ScatterMatrix`._

## Anatomy

| Part      | What it is                                                                                                                                       |
| --------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Point     | 8px across in its group's tone, ringed 2px in the surface so overlapping points stay apart, with a hit area 24px across.                         |
| Bubble    | With `z`, a point whose area follows the value (twice the value, twice the ink), at 70% so what is under it shows.                               |
| Axes      | Both value axes, a hairline on the category side, ticks in `color.text.subtlest`, titles in `color.text.subtle` when the keys do not say enough. |
| Grid      | Hairlines both ways, since both axes are values.                                                                                                 |
| Reference | A dashed hairline at a value on either axis; one on each makes quadrants.                                                                        |
| Tooltip   | The point's name and group, then each axis as name and value in its format, then any other point at the same place. Per point, not per column.   |
| Card      | On a chosen point: its name, group and axes, then the caller's facts and a way to the record.                                                    |

## Variants

| Variant   | Use                                                                                                                     |
| --------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| One tone  | Every point in `brand`: the shape of the cloud is the point.                                                            |
| `groups`  | Up to three groups by a key, each a tone: status groups in the status tones, kinds in the first three categorical hues. |
| `z`       | A bubble: exposure, cost, count.                                                                                        |
| Quadrants | A `reference` on each axis: the four corners the reader names ("treat", "accept").                                      |

_Example: story `Stories.Groups`._
_Example: story `Stories.Bubbles`._

## Sizes

`size` is the plot's height: `small` 120px, `medium` 200px, `large` 320px (the right one for a scatter that is a page's point), or `height` in pixels. Unsaid, it is the Frame's; in the Frame's expanded Dialog it is `large`. Bubbles range from 64 to 900 square pixels whatever the plot's size.

## States

| State    | What changes                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Hover    | The tooltip at the point. No cursor band, since there is no category.                                                                                                                                               |
| Isolated | A group hidden from the Frame's legend leaves the plot.                                                                                                                                                             |
| Focused  | With `onSelect` or `details`, on the keyboard: a 2px ring in `color.border.focused` around the point, outside its surface ring.                                                                                     |
| Chosen   | With `onSelect` or `details`: the points take the pointer, a click, Enter or Space chooses one, the others dim and the chosen one gains a halo; the card opens on it, and offers any other point at the same place. |
| Loading  | Eight skeleton dots on two hairlines, pulsing, at the plot's height.                                                                                                                                                |
| Entering | The points arrive over `motion.duration.slow`.                                                                                                                                                                      |

_Example: story `Stories.Details`._
_Example: story `Stories.SamePlace`._
_Example: story `Stories.AsATable`._

## Modifiers

- **`z`** for a bubble, **`zLabel`** for what its size is called; **`nameKey`** for the key that names a point. For one version `name` still names the key, with a warning in development, and is deprecated for `nameKey`: `label` names the plot on every part.
- **`groupBy`** and **`groups`** for the groups and their tones; **`tone`** for every point when there are none.
- **`xDomain`** and **`yDomain`** pin an axis' ends (a number or `"auto"` each); with both ends pinned the ticks are round steps across them, and **`xTicks`** and **`yTicks`** set them outright.
- **`format`** for every axis without its own; **`formatX`**, **`formatY`** and **`formatZ`** for each axis, in its ticks, the tooltip, the card and the table.
- **`reference`**, **`xLabel`**, **`yLabel`** as on the other parts.
- **`onSelect`** and **`details`** as in States; the selection is `{ datum, group, index }`.
- **`loading`** draws the skeleton; the Frame sets it from `state="loading"`.
- **`label`** names the plot outside a Frame; native props and a ref reach the plot's box, and `aria-describedby` describes the plot: its svg when it chooses nothing, its group when its points are the tab stops.

_Example: story `Stories.NativeAttributes`._

## Content

- **Both axes are measures.** A category on one axis is a Bar or a strip; two categories are a Heatmap.
- **Three groups at most.** The first three hues validate against each other in every pairing; a fourth does not. Finer distinctions are the tooltip's or a filter's.
- **Name the points** with `nameKey`, so the tooltip, the card and a point's button say which record.
- **Pin a bounded measure's axis**: a 0–100 score takes `yDomain={[0, 100]}`, so the plot does not run past the scale.
- **Points that share a place are listed together**: the tooltip and the card name each, and the card offers the others. Where many share places, the data is a Heatmap.
- **Title the axes** when the keys are not words the reader would say: "Likelihood", "Impact".
- **A quadrant's meaning is in the description**, not drawn: "the lines split the register into quadrants".

## Style

| Element   | Token                                                                                   |
| --------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Point     | `color.chart.<tone>` · 8px · 2px `elevation.surface` ring · 24px hit area               |
| Bubble    | The same at 70% · area from 64 to 900 square pixels                                     |
| Grid      | `color.border` · 1px both ways                                                          |
| Reference | `color.chart.neutral` · 1px dashed 4 3                                                  |
| Chosen    | The point's tone: a halo 8px wider at 20%                                               |
| Dimmed    | `opacity.disabled`, over `motion.duration.fast`                                         |
| Focused   | 2px `color.border.focused` ring, 3px out from the point · `Highlight` in forced colours |
| Skeleton  | `color.skeleton` dots on `color.border` hairlines                                       |

## Accessibility

- **Named by the Frame**, or by `label`: a scatter that chooses nothing is an image (`role="img"`) with no tab stop, and the table is the way in: one row per point, a column per axis. When `onSelect` or `details` is set, the plot is a group and each point a named button and a tab stop ("POA-102, Open: Days open 212 d, Exposure $420K"); Enter and Space choose it as a click does. One that chooses and has no name is named "Chart", with a warning in development.
- **The table is one toggle away.** In a Frame the scatter lays its points out as the Frame's table twin and CSV: the point's name (its `nameKey`) under "Point", its group's label under "Group", the Frame's `columns` with `place: "before"`, a column per axis headed by `xLabel`, `yLabel` and `zLabel`, then the columns after. The groups stay one column of words: the legend's groups never become a column each. The legend keys the groups when the Frame is given no `series`.
- **A chosen point's card is a dialog**: the point says it opens one (`aria-haspopup`, `aria-expanded`), and focus returns to that point when it closes.
- **Three groups keep every pair apart** under deutan and protan vision; the legend carries their names, and the tooltip and the card say the group in words.
- **A point's hit area is 24px** whatever its size, so a small point still takes a click.
- **Loading is `aria-busy`** and named "[the plot's name], loading".

## Props

_Props of `Chart.Scatter`, generated from its types:_

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `data` (required) | `ChartDatum[]` |  |  |
| `x` (required) | `string` |  | The key on the horizontal axis. |
| `y` (required) | `string` |  | The key on the vertical axis. |
| `z` | `string` |  | A key whose value sizes the point: a bubble. Area, not radius, so twice the value is twice the ink. |
| `nameKey` | `string` |  | The key that names a point in the tooltip, the card, the table and its button. |
| `name` | `string` |  | The key that names a point. @deprecated Use `nameKey`: `label` names the plot, as on every plot. `ledger/no-deprecated-name` fixes it. |
| `groupBy` | `string` |  | The key that puts each point in a group, and the groups with their tones. At most three, so any two points stay apart. |
| `groups` | `ChartScatterGroup[]` |  |  |
| `tone` | `ChartTone` | `brand` | The tone of every point when there are no groups. |
| `reference` | `ChartReference[]` |  | Lines across the plot: a limit on either axis, or both for quadrants. |
| `xLabel` | `string` |  | Axis titles, when the keys do not say enough. They head the table twin's axis columns too. |
| `yLabel` | `string` |  |  |
| `zLabel` | `string` |  | What `z` is called in the tooltip, the card and the table twin: "Exposure". The key when unsaid. |
| `xDomain` | `ChartDomain` |  | Each axis' ends: a number or `"auto"`. The data's, rounded, when unsaid. With both ends pinned, the ticks are round steps across them. |
| `yDomain` | `ChartDomain` |  |  |
| `xTicks` | `readonly number[]` |  | The ticks on each axis, when round steps are not the right ones. |
| `yTicks` | `readonly number[]` |  |  |
| `size` | `"large" \| "medium" \| "small"` |  | The plot's height. The Frame's when unsaid, else `medium` (200px); `large` in the expanded Dialog. |
| `height` | `number` |  |  |
| `format` | `Formatter` |  | The number format of every axis that has none of its own: the ticks, the tooltip, the card and the table. |
| `formatX` | `CategoryFormatter` |  | The horizontal axis' format, in its ticks, the tooltip, the card and the table. `format` when unsaid. |
| `formatY` | `Formatter` |  | The vertical axis' format. `format` when unsaid. |
| `formatZ` | `Formatter` |  | `z`'s format. `format` when unsaid. |
| `label` | `string` |  | The plot's accessible name. The Frame's title when unsaid. |
| `loading` | `boolean` |  | Draws the plot's skeleton in place of the points. The Frame sets it from `state="loading"`. |
| `onSelect` | `((selection: ScatterSelection) => void)` |  | Called when a point is clicked, or activated with Enter or Space. |
| `details` | `((selection: ScatterSelection) => ReactNode)` |  | More about the chosen point, in a card anchored to it. The card's head (the point's name, its group and each axis) is the kit's. |
| `className` | `string` |  |  |

<!-- page: Patterns/Chart/Sparkline (src/stories/patterns/ChartSparkline.mdx) -->

# Sparkline

**Status: Stable.**

A trend with no axes, no grid and no legend, beside the number it belongs to: in a Stat tile, in a table's trend column, after a count. The number carries the value; the sparkline carries the shape. A line by default, a wash or bars when asked, with an end dot for the last point and a hairline for a reference. Ninety-six by twenty-four pixels. Unnamed it is decoration; named, it is an image with a tooltip.

_Example: story `Stories.SparklineMatrix`._

## Anatomy

| Part      | What it is                                                                                                     |
| --------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Line      | 1.5px in its tone, round joins; `area` adds the tone at 12% under it; `bars` is a column per point, 1px apart. |
| End dot   | A 6px marker ringed in the surface on the last point: where the series is now.                                 |
| Reference | A dashed hairline at a value in `color.chart.neutral`: last period, the limit.                                 |
| Tooltip   | Only when named: the point's value, called by `seriesLabel` (else the label), under its category from `x`.     |

## Variants

| Variant             | Use                                                                                       |
| ------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `appearance="line"` | The default: a count over time.                                                           |
| `appearance="area"` | A count whose size matters, with a reference for the limit.                               |
| `appearance="bars"` | A count per period, where each period is discrete: closed per month.                      |
| In a tile           | In a Stat.Tile's `trend`, `space.150` from the number, which stays the value.             |
| In a row            | The trend column of a Table, 80 by 20, unnamed, so a screen reader hears the number once. |

_Example: story `Stories.InTiles`._
_Example: story `Stories.InRows`._

## Sizes

| `width` × `height` | Where                                                      |
| ------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------- |
| 80 × 20            | A table row.                                               |
| 96 × 24            | Beside a Stat's value. The default.                        |
| 120 × 28           | Bars, which need the width.                                |
| 160 × 40           | A card's corner, when the trend is the card's second fact. |

Anything larger is a [Line](?path=/docs/patterns-chart-line--docs) in a Frame, with axes. `width` is the most a sparkline takes: in a narrower cell, tile or row beside its number it narrows and keeps its height.

_Example: story `Stories.Narrow`._
_Example: story `Stories.Baseline`._

## States

| State   | What changes                                                       |
| ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Hover   | Nothing, unless named: then a marker and the tooltip at the point. |
| Loading | A skeleton bar at the size, pulsing.                               |

A sparkline draws in place, on mount and when its data changes: it sits in rows and tiles by the dozen, where an entrance per sparkline would cost a render per frame for each. A named one's tooltip still follows the pointer.

A sparkline does not choose: nothing to click, nothing to open. The number beside it is the way to the record.

## Modifiers

- **`appearance`**, **`tone`**, **`endDot`**, **`reference`** as in Anatomy.
- **`x`** names the category key, the heading of a named sparkline's tooltip; without it the tooltip prints the value alone.
- **`baseline`**: `auto` crops the scale to the data, so a trend on a high base (96% to 99%, 340 to 360) still shows; `zero` starts it at zero. Unsaid, `auto` for a line or an area, `zero` for bars, whose length is their value.
- **`seriesLabel`** is what the tooltip calls the value: "Covered". The label, else "Value", when unsaid.
- **`width`**, **`height`** in pixels.
- **`format`** for the tooltip.
- **`label`** names it: "Open findings, nine months". Unsaid, it is decoration.
- **`loading`** draws the skeleton; the Frame sets it from `state="loading"`.
- Native props and a ref reach its box: an `id`, `data-*` for a test.

## Content

- **Always beside a number.** A sparkline alone says only "up" or "down".
- **One tone, the number's status** when it has one: `danger` beside open findings, `success` beside closed; `brand` or `neutral` otherwise. Never a categorical hue.
- **Six to twelve points.** Fewer is a number; more is a Line.
- **A reference is one value**: last period, the limit. Not a band, not a target series.

## Style

| Element   | Token                                                      |
| --------- | ---------------------------------------------------------- |
| Line      | `color.chart.<tone>` · 1.5px · round joins                 |
| Wash      | `color.chart.<tone>` at 12%                                |
| Bars      | `color.chart.<tone>` · `radius` 1px at the top · 1px apart |
| End dot   | 6px · 2px ring in the surface it sits on                   |
| Reference | `color.chart.neutral` · 1px dashed 3 2                     |
| Skeleton  | `color.skeleton` · `radius.xsmall`                         |

## Accessibility

- **Unnamed, it is `aria-hidden`** and not focusable: the number beside it is the fact, and a screen reader hears it once.
- **Named, it is an image** with that name, never a tab stop: the number beside it is on the page, and the tooltip is for the pointer. Name it only where no number says the same thing.
- **Never the only carrier of a value.** If the shape matters enough to say, say it in the tile's note: "Down from 14 in January".
- **The tone is not the meaning**: the number's word or Badge is.

## Props

_Props of `Chart.Sparkline`, generated from its types:_

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `data` (required) | `ChartDatum[]` |  |  |
| `y` (required) | `string` |  | The value key. |
| `x` | `string` |  | The category key, for the tooltip's heading. Without it the tooltip prints the value alone. |
| `appearance` | `"area" \| "bars" \| "line"` | `line` | `line` is a stroke; `area` adds a wash; `bars` is a column per point. |
| `tone` | `ChartTone` | `brand` |  |
| `reference` | `number` |  | A dashed hairline at a value: last period, the target. |
| `endDot` | `boolean` |  | A ringed marker on the last point. |
| `baseline` | `"auto" \| "zero"` |  | Where the scale starts. `auto`, for a line or an area, crops to the data, so a trend on a high base (96% to 99%, 340 to 360) still shows; `zero`, for bars, starts at zero, since a bar's length is its value. Unsaid, `auto` for a line or an area and `zero` for bars. |
| `width` | `number` | `96` | The most it takes, in pixels: in a narrower container (a cell, a grid track, a flex row) it narrows and keeps its height. |
| `height` | `number` | `24` |  |
| `format` | `Formatter` |  | The number format in the tooltip. |
| `label` | `string` |  | The accessible name: "Open findings, nine months". Unsaid, the sparkline is decoration beside its number. |
| `seriesLabel` | `string` |  | What the tooltip calls the value: "Open". The label, else "Value", when unsaid. |
| `loading` | `boolean` |  | Draws a skeleton in the sparkline's place. The Frame sets it from `state="loading"`. |
| `className` | `string` |  |  |

### Playground

_Example: story `Stories.Playground`._

_Rendered in the Storybook: Controls._

## Related

- [Chart](?path=/docs/patterns-chart-overview--docs): the Frame, the tones, the motion.
- [Stat](?path=/docs/components-stat--docs): the number it sits beside.
- [Line](?path=/docs/patterns-chart-line--docs): the same series with axes, when it needs to say more.
- [Table](?path=/docs/components-table--docs): the trend column.

## Don't

A sparkline sits beside the number it trends, in one tone, the number's status, never alone and made bigger, or in a categorical hue beside a status number.

_Example: story `Stories.Dont`._

<!-- page: Patterns/Chart/Treemap (src/stories/patterns/ChartTreemap.mdx) -->

# Treemap

**Status: Stable.**

Part-to-whole with a hierarchy: a tile per leaf, sized by value, in the tone of its top-level branch. Findings by system and component; controls by family and enhancement. Where the total goes, and where inside that. A name shows on a tile when it fits; the rest is the tooltip's. A click on a tile drills into its branch, or opens its card. It lives in a [Chart](?path=/docs/patterns-chart-overview--docs) Frame, whose legend names the branches.

_Example: story `Stories.TreemapMatrix`._

## Anatomy

| Part    | What it is                                                                                                                                           |
| ------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Tile    | A leaf, `radius` 2px, in its branch's tone, with a 2px `elevation.surface` gap from its neighbours. Sized by value, 4:3 as far as the layout allows. |
| Name    | The tile's name on an `elevation.surface` chip at 92% in `color.text`, when the tile is at least 64 by 28; cut to fit, the whole in the tooltip.     |
| Tooltip | The tile's name, the branch it sits in and its value, keyed by a square in its tone.                                                                 |
| Card    | On a chosen tile: its name, its branch and its value, then the caller's facts.                                                                       |

## Variants

| Variant    | Use                                                                                                                               |
| ---------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Branches   | Two levels: systems in the categorical set, their components inside each in the same hue.                                         |
| One branch | One system alone, its components in its one hue: the level under a drill-down.                                                    |
| Drill-down | A click on a tile redraws the treemap with its branch, the way back in the Frame's `path`; a click on a component opens its card. |

_Example: story `Stories.Systems`._
_Example: story `Stories.Drilldown`._

## Sizes

`size` is the plot's height: `small` 120px, `medium` 200px, `large` 320px (the right one: tiles need room for their names), or `height` in pixels. A treemap should be at least 420px wide; narrower, most names fall to the tooltip.

## States

| State    | What changes                                                                                                                    |
| -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Hover    | The tooltip.                                                                                                                    |
| Focused  | With `onSelect` or `details`, on the keyboard: a 2px ring in `color.border.focused` inside the tile, between two surface bands. |
| Isolated | A branch hidden from the Frame's legend leaves the treemap; the rest re-tile. A hovered legend item dims the other branches.    |
| Chosen   | With `onSelect` or `details`: the tiles take the pointer, a click chooses one, the others dim; the card opens on the tile.      |
| Loading  | Four skeleton tiles, pulsing, at the plot's height.                                                                             |
| Entering | The tiles arrive over `motion.duration.slow`; a drill-down re-tiles the same way.                                               |

_Example: story `Stories.Details`._
_Example: story `Stories.SameNames`._

In a Frame the treemap's leaves are its table twin and its CSV: a row per leaf in the tree's order, a column per level holding the names on its way down, then its value. `levels` names the columns (`["System", "Component"]`); unsaid, the top level takes the Frame's `xLabel`, else "Group", and the leaves "Name". The legend keys the top-level branches when the Frame is given no `series`, and a branch hidden from it stays in the table, which is the data.

_Example: story `Stories.AsATable`._

## Modifiers

- **`data`** as nodes: a name, a value on a leaf, children on a branch, a `tone` on a top-level node when the categorical order is not wanted.
- **`levels`** for the table twin's headings, one per level from the top.
- **`format`** for the tooltip, the card and the Frame's table.
- **`size`** or **`height`**: the Frame's when unsaid; `large` in the Frame's expanded Dialog.
- **`onSelect`** and **`details`** as in States; the selection is `{ name, value, group, path, id }`: `group` the top-level branch, `path` the names on the way down to the tile, and `id` the node's own when it has one. A chosen tile is matched by `id`, else by `path`, so two components of the same name in two systems stay apart.
- **`id`** on a node, for a record's identity when names repeat.
- **`loading`** draws the skeleton; the Frame sets it from `state="loading"`.
- **`label`** names the plot outside a Frame; native props and a ref reach the plot's box, and `aria-describedby` describes the plot: its svg when it chooses nothing, its group when its tiles are the tab stops.

_Example: story `Stories.NativeAttributes`._

## Content

- **A hierarchy, or nothing.** A flat list of five is a Bar; a treemap earns its place when the reader asks "where, and where inside that".
- **Six branches at most**, in the categorical set; more folds into Other.
- **Names are short**: a component, a family. What does not fit is the tooltip's, and the table's.
- **Values are one thing**: a count, a cost. Not a score.

## Style

| Element  | Token                                                                                                          |
| -------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Tile     | `color.chart.<tone>` · `radius` 2px · 2px `elevation.surface` gap                                              |
| Name     | `font.body.xsmall` · `color.text` on an `elevation.surface` chip at 92% · `radius` 2px                         |
| Dimmed   | `opacity.disabled`, over `motion.duration.fast`                                                                |
| Focused  | 2px `color.border.focused` inset 2px in the tile, `elevation.surface` inside it; `Highlight` in forced colours |
| Skeleton | `color.skeleton` tiles                                                                                         |

## Accessibility

- **Named by the Frame**, or by `label`: a treemap that chooses nothing is an image (`role="img"`) with no tab stop, and the table carries its numbers; unnamed, it is decoration. When `onSelect` or `details` is supplied, the plot is a group and each leaf a named button reachable with Tab; Enter and Space perform the same action as a click. Its accessible name is the path and the value ("Payments, Ledger API: 18"), even when the visible label is shortened. One that chooses and has no name is named "Chart", with a warning in development.
- **The keyboard's ring is drawn inside the tile**, the last thing it paints, so the next tile cannot cover it, the plot's edge cannot cut it, and its surface bands keep it apart from a tile of the same hue. The pointer's tooltip stands down while the keyboard is on a tile.
- **Text never sits on a tile's colour**: the name is on a surface chip, in the text colour.
- **A tile that opens a card says so** (`aria-haspopup="dialog"`, `aria-expanded`).
- **The table is one toggle away** in a Frame: every leaf, every level named, every value, so the areas are never the only way to read the sizes.
- **A chosen tile's card is a dialog**, and focus returns to that tile when it closes, or the first available tile if it was removed.
- **Keyboard drill-down preserves the chosen leaf's focus** when Recharts replaces its branch, or focuses the first available tile when that leaf no longer exists.
- **Loading is `aria-busy`** and named "[the plot's name], loading".

## Props

_Props of `Chart.Treemap`, generated from its types:_

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `data` (required) | `TreemapNodeInput[]` |  |  |
| `levels` | `string[]` |  | What each level of the hierarchy is called, from the top, for the table twin's headings: `["System", "Component"]`. The Frame's `xLabel` for the top level, then "Group" and "Name", when unsaid. |
| `size` | `"large" \| "medium" \| "small"` |  | The plot's height. The Frame's when unsaid, else `medium` (200px); `large` in the expanded Dialog. |
| `height` | `number` |  |  |
| `format` | `Formatter` |  |  |
| `label` | `string` |  | The plot's accessible name. The Frame's title when unsaid. |
| `loading` | `boolean` |  | Draws the plot's skeleton in place of the tiles. The Frame sets it from `state="loading"`. |
| `onSelect` | `((selection: TreemapSelection) => void)` |  | Called when a tile is clicked or activated with Enter/Space: to drill into its branch, or to filter what is under the chart. |
| `details` | `((selection: TreemapSelection) => ReactNode)` |  | More about the chosen tile, in a card anchored to it. The card's head (the tile, its branch and its value) is the kit's. |
| `className` | `string` |  |  |

### Playground

_Example: story `Stories.Playground`._

_Rendered in the Storybook: Controls._

## Related

- [Chart](?path=/docs/patterns-chart-overview--docs): the Frame, the tones, choosing a mark, the motion.
- [Bar](?path=/docs/patterns-chart-bar--docs): parts compared without a hierarchy.
- [Donut](?path=/docs/patterns-chart-donut--docs): parts of one whole with the whole in the middle.
- [Tree](?path=/docs/components-tree--docs): the same hierarchy as an outline, when the reader wants to walk it.

## Don't

A treemap is for a hierarchy. A flat list of five is a Bar, never a treemap whose small tiles lose their names.

_Example: story `Stories.Dont`._

<!-- page: Patterns/CommandPalette (src/stories/patterns/CommandPalette.mdx) -->

# CommandPalette

**Status: Stable.**

A ⌘K palette over a page or a record: a field at the top, the commands under headings, a shortcut at the end of the ones that have one, the keys in the footer. Choosing a command closes the palette and runs it. The commands are plain objects the caller supplies, so the palette stays presentational and every page can reuse it; `useCommandPalette` holds the open state and toggles it on ⌘K on Apple platforms and Ctrl+K elsewhere, anywhere on the page. It runs a command; it does not pick a record, which is the [RecordPicker](?path=/docs/patterns-recordpicker--docs), and it does not search the product, which is the [SearchDialog](?path=/docs/patterns-searchdialog--docs) behind the top nav's search.

_Example: story `Stories.CommandPaletteStory`._

## Anatomy

| Part    | What it is                                                                                        |
| ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Field   | "Type a command…" (`placeholder`), focused on open, with the field's focus ring on its row.       |
| Heading | The group's name, over its commands: Record, Go to, Preferences.                                  |
| Command | A verb and its object; a `hint` and the `shortcut`'s keys at the end in `font.body.xsmall`.       |
| Empty   | "No commands match." (`noResults`).                                                               |
| Failure | An Alert above the commands, with Try again when `onRetry` is given.                              |
| Footer  | The keys: the arrows to move, Enter to run (`chooseHint`), Escape to close (a button, for touch). |

_Example: story `Stories.CommandPaletteMatrix`._

## Variants

CommandPalette has one appearance. What varies is the commands, which are the page's: a record's verbs first, the places to go after, the preferences last.

Not built, and why: search across records in the palette, because a record is found by the top nav's search and picked by the RecordPicker; nested pages of commands, because a command with choices is a Dialog of its own; recent commands at the top, because the order is the page's and it should read the same every time; icons before the commands, because the heading says the kind.

## Sizes

One: the Command dialog at its medium width, 560px (`dimension.part.command`), over the page at the top.

## States

| State    | What changes                                                                                                 |
| -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Closed   | Not rendered. ⌘K opens it.                                                                                   |
| Open     | Over the page at the top, the field focused, every group shown.                                              |
| Filtered | The commands whose label, heading or hint match, best first, under their headings; empty groups go.          |
| None     | The empty sentence.                                                                                          |
| Loading  | `loading`: Searching… under any commands listed, the list busy; never the empty sentence.                    |
| Failed   | `error` (`true` for the default words) above the commands listed, with Try again; said at once, assertively. |
| Run      | The palette closes, then the command runs.                                                                   |

_Example: story `Stories.MatchesLabelsNotIds`._

_Example: story `Stories.LoadingAndFailure`._

_Example: story `Stories.Failure`._

## Modifiers

- **`commands`**: id, group, label, shortcut, hint, run. Commands with the same group in sequence share a heading. The `id` is identity only: it is never shown and never matched, so a UUID there cannot make a short query match every command.
- **`title`**, **`description`**, **`placeholder`**, **`noResults`** and **`chooseHint`** relabel the dialog, the field, the empty sentence and Enter's verb; every default comes from the locale.
- **`loading`**, **`error`** and **`onRetry`** for commands that arrive late or fail.
- **`useCommandPalette({ shortcut })`** returns `open` and `setOpen`, and binds `shortcut` ("Mod+K" by default; `null` for none) while mounted.

## Content

- **A command is a verb and its object**: "Record an assessment", "Export the SSP", "Switch the colour mode". Never a noun alone.
- **The headings are kinds of command**: "Record" for what the record does, "Go to" for places, "Preferences" for the reader's own.
- **A shortcut goes in `shortcut`**, written once for every platform ("Shift+E"), and is drawn in the platform's glyphs. `hint` is for other words the reader hears with the label, such as a count.
- **The page's verbs first**, the places after, the preferences last.

## Style

| Element | Token                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| ------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Dialog  | CommandDialog: `radius.xxlarge` · `elevation.surface.overlay` · `elevation.shadow.overlay` · `color.blanket`                                                                           |
| Field   | CommandInput: `dimension.control.large` · `color.border` below · `color.border.focused` ring while focused                                                                             |
| Heading | CommandGroup's: `font.heading.xxsmall` uppercase · `color.text.subtlest`                                                                                                               |
| Command | CommandItem: `dimension.control.medium` · `radius.medium` · `color.background.neutral.subtle.hovered` when selected, with the `color.border.focused` outline while the field has focus |
| Hint    | `font.body.xsmall` · `color.text.subtle` · at the end                                                                                                                                  |
| Footer  | CommandFooter: `elevation.surface.sunken` · `font.body.xsmall` · KbdShortcut for each key                                                                                              |

## Accessibility

- **A dialog named by `title`**, "Command palette" by default, read with its `description`; focus moves to the field on open and returns to where it was on close.
- **The list is a listbox** with the headings as group labels, so a screen reader hears "Record, group, Record an assessment". A command's shortcut is its `aria-keyshortcuts`, not part of its name.
- **The active descendant follows the selection**, on open, after every keystroke and after every arrow, and the count of matches is spoken once the query holds still (see [Command](?path=/docs/components-command--docs)).
- **The arrows move, Enter runs, Escape closes**, and the footer says so with KbdShortcut, each key named in full.
- **The shortcut follows the platform**: ⌘K on Apple platforms, Ctrl+K elsewhere, so Ctrl+K keeps its text-editing meaning on a Mac. It is ignored on a held key's repeats, with another modifier held, while composing text, when a handler has already taken the key, and while another dialog is open, so it never stacks a modal on a draft. One ⌘K per page: beside TopNav.Search, give one of the two another `shortcut` or `null`.
- **Running closes first**, so a command that opens a dialog does not stack one over the other.

## Props

_Props of `CommandPalette`, generated from its types:_

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `open` (required) | `boolean` |  |  |
| `onClose` (required) | `() => void` |  |  |
| `commands` (required) | `PaletteCommand[]` |  | In the order they show, grouped by `group`. The page's verbs first, the places after. |
| `placeholder` | `string` |  | The field's placeholder. "Type a command…" by default. |
| `title` | `string` |  | The dialog's name and the field's. "Command palette" by default. |
| `description` | `string` |  | Read after the name when the palette opens. "Search for a command to run." by default. |
| `noResults` | `ReactNode` |  | What the list says when the query matches no command. "No commands match." by default. |
| `chooseHint` | `string` |  | What Enter does, in the footer. "to run" by default. |
| `loading` | `boolean` | `false` | Commands still arriving. Commands already listed stay usable, with Searching… under them, and the palette never says nothing matched while they load. |
| `error` | `ReactNode` |  | The commands could not load: `true` for the default message, or the words to show. It shows above any commands listed, with Retry when `onRetry` is given. |
| `onRetry` | `(() => void)` |  | Loads the commands again. Focus returns to the field. |

### useCommandPalette

The palette's open state, toggled by its shortcut anywhere on the page. Takes `{ shortcut }`, "Mod+K" by default and `null` for none; returns `{ open, setOpen }`.

_Example: story `Stories.CommandPaletteStory`._

## Related

- [Command](?path=/docs/components-command--docs): the dialog and the list.
- [RecordPicker](?path=/docs/patterns-recordpicker--docs): the same CommandDialog, picking one record instead of running a command.
- [Kbd](?path=/docs/components-kbd--docs): the keys in the footer and the hints.

## Don't

A command is a verb and its object, under a heading that names its kind, never nouns in one list.

_Example: story `Stories.Dont`._

<!-- page: Patterns/Composer (src/stories/patterns/Composer.mdx) -->

# Composer

**Status: Stable.**

A shared text composer for messages, comments and other short drafts. Ledger owns keyboard completion, submission progress and recovery. The consuming application owns recipients, permissions, persistence, suggestion identity and serialized text. Owner: Ledger maintainers; consumers own their adapters.

_Example: story `Stories.ComposerMatrix`._

## When to use it

- **A comment on a record**: the Composer sits at the top of the record's Comments section, above the [Timeline](?path=/docs/components-timeline--docs) that lists them newest first. Its `label` names the record ("Comment on this task") and `submitLabel` the action ("Comment"). A send that lands clears the draft and keeps focus in the field for the next one; a rejected send keeps the draft, and its `errorMessage` says whether sending again could post it twice.
- **A short message or note** that is written and sent where the reader is, with no other fields to fill.

Not for a record's fields or a longer form with more than the text: that is a Dialog with a Textarea in a Field. Not for a value edited in place: that is [Editable](?path=/docs/patterns-editable--docs).

## Anatomy

A named textarea, optional leading marker, contextual fields above, instructions below, optional `actions` before the buttons (a second thing to do with the draft), optional cancel action, and primary submission action. Suggestions float under the field in the kit's positioner; a rejected send puts its message under the field.

## Variants

One composition, with optional suggestion and leading slots. No event taxonomy or built-in mention syntax. The example below uses a `#` adapter and stable topic identifiers to demonstrate a non-person use case.

_Example: story `Stories.Suggestions`._

## Sizes

Three initial textarea rows. The layout follows its container. The suggestion list is 280px wide and at most 240px tall, bounded by the width and the height the window leaves; it scrolls when taller. It is portaled, so a panel, dialog or card that clips its content cannot cut it, and it opens above the field where the window ends below it. Long option labels truncate visually while retaining their accessible text.

_Example: story `Stories.SuggestionsAtTheEdge`._

Inside a Dialog, Sheet or Popover the list belongs to that overlay: choosing an option leaves it open, and Escape closes the list before the overlay.

_Example: story `Stories.SuggestionsInDialog`._

## States

Empty drafts cannot submit. Nonempty drafts submit with the button or Ctrl/⌘ + Enter. While pending, the textarea is read-only and repeat submission and cancellation are blocked. Fulfillment clears the submitted draft and returns focus to the field for the next message; rejection retains the draft with its message under the field. A newer controlled draft is retained when an earlier request resolves. A disabled composer cannot be edited or submitted.

_Example: story `Stories.SaveRecovery`._

## Modifiers

`value` and `onValueChange` select caller-owned state; `defaultValue` supplies an uncontrolled initial draft. Do not switch ownership while mounted. `ref`, `id`, and `name` target the visible textarea. `leading`, `hint`, `children` and `actions` are rendered slots; `actions` sits before the cancel and primary buttons, for a secondary Button the caller wires to the draft it keeps through `value`.

`getSuggestions(text, caret)` returns UTF-16 replacement offsets and ordered options, or null. The caller provides unique option IDs, accessible labels, exact insertion strings, filtering and result limits. Invalid ranges are ignored. The adapter is synchronous; fetching remote candidates belongs to the caller. No rich-text document model is implied.

`errorMessage` is the message after a rejected send, or a function of the rejection that returns it, to show the server's reason.

_Example: story `Stories.ServerReason`._

## Content

Supply a descriptive `label` independently of placeholder text. `submitLabel`, `cancelLabel`, `suggestionsLabel`, `errorMessage` and `hint` default to the LedgerProvider's messages (Send, Cancel, Suggestions, "Could not send. Try again." and "Ctrl/⌘ + Enter to send"), so a translated provider translates them; pass your own words where the task names its action, such as Comment. The default keyboard hint is left out on a touch screen (a coarse primary pointer), which has no key to press it with; `hint={null}` shows none anywhere. Use stable identities when your product serializes references; a display name need not be an identity. Resolve `onSubmit` only when your application's promised save boundary succeeds; throw or reject on failure.

## Style

Textarea and Button provide the control styling. Layout uses `space.100`; suggestions use the overlay surface, default border and overlay shadow, and the active option `color.background.neutral.subtle.hovered`. In forced colours the active option is Highlight with HighlightText. Pending and error states remain understandable without animation or color alone.

## Accessibility

The textarea keeps focus while suggestions are navigated, and has `aria-haspopup="listbox"`, `aria-autocomplete="list"`, `aria-controls` and `aria-activedescendant` while the list is open. Up/Down selects an option, Enter or Tab inserts it, Shift+Tab leaves the field and closes the list, and Escape closes the list without dismissing a containing overlay. Because Tab inserts while the list is open, the list says so when it appears: a polite announcement gives the count and the keys ("2 suggestions. Up and Down to choose, Enter or Tab to insert."), and each move names the option and its place ("Delivery, 2 of 2"). IME confirmation does not insert or submit. Suggestions expose listbox and option semantics. Pointer selection returns focus to the textarea. Instructions and a rejected send's message describe the textarea, and the rejection is also announced at once. After a send lands, focus returns to the textarea, since Send is unavailable with an empty draft. The completion key handling and save recovery run in both color modes and in forced colours.

## Props

_Props of `Composer`, generated from its types:_

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `value` | `string` |  |  |
| `onValueChange` | `((value: string) => void) \| ((value: string) => void)` |  |  |
| `defaultValue` | `string` |  |  |
| `label` (required) | `string` |  | Accessible name of the textarea; independent of its placeholder. |
| `onSubmit` (required) | `(text: string) => void \| Promise<void>` |  | Receives trimmed, nonempty text. Fulfillment clears the submitted draft and returns focus to the field; rejection preserves the draft and shows errorMessage. |
| `getSuggestions` | `((text: string, caret: number) => ComposerSuggestions \| null)` |  | Synchronous suggestion adapter. Return a replacement range and options, or null to close. No mention syntax is built in. |

| `className` | `string` |  |  |

## Don't

The `hint` says when the message is saved (Saved when Send succeeds), never a promise of autosave when the message is sent only on request.
