# Editable

**Status: Stable.**

A value edited where it sits. The reader clicks it, changes it, and it saves: no form, no dialog. It commits at once and shows the save beside the value; a refused save puts the old value back with the reason under it and keeps what the reader wrote, with Try again and Discard. **Editable.Text** (`EditableText`) edits text, with `multiline` for paragraphs; **Editable.Select** (`EditableSelect`) is one of a fixed set, drawn as the record draws it; **Editable.Date** (`EditableDate`) is a calendar day, a due date or a planned completion.

It is for one value on a record that already exists: the owner in the rail, the next action in a table's cell, the status as a Badge. A record that does not exist yet is a [form](?path=/docs/patterns-forms--docs); several values that change together are a form in a Dialog; a paragraph uses `EditableText multiline`.

_Example: story `Stories.Rail`._

## Anatomy

| Part     | What it is                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| -------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Row      | A button 24px tall, `dimension.control.xsmall`, the field's height, across its cell. The value sits flush on the text column; under the pointer the row tints, reaching `space.050` past it on both sides.                                                                                      |
| Value    | The committed value in `font.body`, one line that truncates. Empty, the `placeholder` in `color.text.subtlest`, or the muted dash.                                                                                                                                                              |
| Mark     | At the end of the row: a Spinner while saving, a check in `color.icon.success` for a moment after, a warning in `color.icon.danger` after a refusal. A chevron on a Select.                                                                                                                     |
| Field    | Text, editing: an input of `dimension.control.xsmall` in the value's place, its box reaching `space.050` past the column so the text stays on it. Multiline, a textarea that grows with its text. Date: the same input reading a typed day, with a 20px button at its end that opens the month. |
| Actions  | Under the field while editing: Cancel and Save, as 24px icon buttons named by the action and the field. Always on a paragraph, where any pointer is coarse, and after a refused leave.                                                                                                          |
| Menu     | Select, editing: the options under the row, the current one marked, and nothing else; a short set uses Select; a long set uses Combobox with its search input inside the popup.                                                                                                                 |
| Message  | Under the row in `font.body.xsmall` and `color.text.danger`: what `validate` refused, or why the save failed. It wraps, also under a value that truncates.                                                                                                                                      |
| Recovery | After a refused save, under the message: Try again, which sends the refused value again, and Discard, which drops it. Both xsmall Buttons.                                                                                                                                                      |
| Reason   | While `lockedReason` is set, the row's description; shown under it in `color.text.subtle` once the reader tries to edit.                                                                                                                                                                        |
| Edit     | Multiline, at rest: the paragraph is text, and a subtle xsmall Edit button with a pencil at its end opens the field.                                                                                                                                                                            |

## Variants

Three, by what the value is. **Text** for a value the reader writes: a name, an acronym, a next action. **Select** for one of a fixed set: a status, a method, an owner from a roster, drawn by `render` as the record draws it, a Badge or a Person, so the rail and the table agree. **Date** for a calendar day: a due date, a planned completion.

Where it lives: in a [KeyValue](?path=/docs/components-keyvalue--docs) row of the rail, in a [Fact](?path=/docs/components-fact--docs), in a [Table](?path=/docs/components-table--docs) cell under the column's heading. A [DataTable](?path=/docs/patterns-data-table--docs) column with `editable` draws these itself.

_Example: story `Stories.InTable`._

**Multiline** is for criteria, statements and other paragraphs. At rest the whole value wraps as text the reader can select and copy, and the Edit button beside it opens the field; the row is not one large button. Editing, Enter adds a newline, Ctrl/Cmd+Enter or Save saves, Escape or Cancel puts the old value back, and leaving the field saves. Validation and save recovery are those of a single line.

_Example: story `Stories.Multiline`._

**Options with labels.** When the stored value is an id, give `options` as `{ value, label }`: the list shows, searches and announces the label, commits the value, and `render` receives both. `emptyLabel` adds a first choice that clears the value ("Unassigned"), and an empty value at rest is the `placeholder`, the `emptyLabel` or the muted dash, never a bare chevron.

_Example: story `Stories.Options`._

**Dates.** `Editable.Date` holds an ISO day ("2026-10-14"), the contract of [DatePicker](?path=/docs/components-datepicker--docs), and shows it in the reader's words ("Oct 14, 2026") as a `time` element. A day is a calendar day, never an instant: it does not move with the reader's time zone. Editing, the field reads a typed day in the locale ("10/20/2026", "Oct 20", "2026-10-20"); its button, or Alt+Down, opens the month, with Today and Clear under it. Enter or leaving commits the typed day, a day chosen in the month commits at once, and an empty field clears the day. `min`, `max` and `isDateUnavailable` disable days in the month with their reason and refuse a typed one with it ("Enter Oct 1, 2026 or later."); text that is not a day says what one looks like. Either keeps the field open with the message, as `validate` does. `placeholder` is what an empty value says at rest ("No due date"). The save, the refused value with Try again and Discard, the lock and the draft callbacks are Editable.Text's; `onDraftChange` receives the day the text reads as, or the text itself while it reads as no day.

_Example: story `Stories.Dates`._

**A due day.** With `due`, the resting row says where the day stands beside it, as [DateLabel](?path=/docs/components-datetime--docs) says it in a register: Overdue, Due today, Due tomorrow or Due in 2 days, with the state's icon and tone, judged against the reader's today in the LedgerProvider's zone. The words are part of the row's name ("Due: Oct 1, 2026, Overdue"), and a narrow row puts them under the day. `complete` says the work is done: the day then shows plainly, as DateLabel's `complete` does.

_Example: story `Stories.DueDates`._

## Sizes

One: 24px, `dimension.control.xsmall`, the field's height, so opening the field does not move the rail. The value is a line of body text centred in it. The width is the cell's, less `space.050` at the end: the tint, the field and the focus ring reach that far past the value, and the Editable keeps the reach inside its own box, so a KeyValue or a cell that truncates never takes it for cut text and reveals it in a tooltip. At the start the reach passes the text column, so the value lines up with the plain values around it: a [KeyValue](?path=/docs/components-keyvalue--docs) whose value is an Editable does not clip it, and a table cell's padding holds it, so the tint, the focus ring and the field keep their sides in every browser (the Rail story).

Each instance accepts one save at a time. While saving, the row cannot reopen for another edit. A rejected save restores its previous value only while this request still owns the current value; an external update is preserved. Completion after unmount is ignored. The caller remains responsible for reconciling server updates to the record.

## States

| State   | Look                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| ------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Rest    | The value, flush. Nothing says it edits until the pointer arrives; the rail's rows all edit, so nothing needs to. A paragraph has its Edit button.                                     |
| Hover   | The row tints `color.background.neutral.subtle.hovered`; pressed, `.pressed`.                                                                                                          |
| Focus   | The kit's focus outline on the row.                                                                                                                                                    |
| Editing | Text: the field in the value's place, focused, the existing value ready to edit, with Cancel and Save under it where they show. Select: the listbox or searchable popup under the row. |
| Invalid | Editing, the field's border `color.border.danger` and the message under it, as the reader types. The commit is refused while it shows.                                                 |
| Saving  | The new value shows at once and a Spinner sits at the end of the row.                                                                                                                  |
| Saved   | A check for `motion.duration.slower` twice, then nothing.                                                                                                                              |
| Refused | The old value is back, the warning mark at the end, the reason under the row, and Try again and Discard under it. Reopening the field shows the refused value. It stays until either.  |
| Locked  | Unchanged to the eye; the row is `aria-disabled`, described by the reason, and shows it when the reader tries to edit.                                                                 |
| Empty   | The placeholder in `color.text.subtlest`, or the muted dash. Never a grey instruction.                                                                                                 |

There is no disabled state. A value the reader can never change is plain text in the same row, which lines up with the editable ones; a value that may not change for now, while another saves, takes `lockedReason`. A form of Editables is never disabled around a save: a disabled field loses its focus.

_Example: story `Stories.EditableMatrix`._

## Modifiers

- **`validate`**: a function of the draft that returns a message or null. It runs as the reader types and again at the commit, so a rule is seen before Enter is refused.
- **`save`**: a promise. Resolved, the check; rejected, the rollback, the error's message, and the refused value kept for Try again. `onValueChange` is called at once with the new value, and again with the old one when the save fails, so the caller's state is always what the reader sees. `onChange` is its deprecated spelling, called only where `onValueChange` is not given; `ledger/no-deprecated-name` renames it.
- **`onEditingChange`**, **`onDraftChange`** and **`onCancel`**: what a host needs for draft protection, without reading the field's DOM. `onDraftChange` receives the unsaved draft as it changes (what is typed while it differs from the value, or a refused value kept for another try) and `null` once it is saved, put back, discarded or unmounted; feed a route blocker and `beforeunload` from it. `onEditingChange` says the field opened or closed; `onCancel`, that the reader dropped an edit.
- **`lockedReason`**: a temporary lock with its reason, for one change at a time: while one value saves, the host locks the others. A field already open keeps its draft, and its save stays the host's to refuse.
- **`placeholder`**: what goes here, as a noun.
- **`options`**, **`render`** and **`emptyLabel`** on Select: the set (values or `{ value, label }`), how a value is drawn, and the choice that clears it.
- **`label`**: the field's name for a screen reader. The KeyValue or the column shows the visible one.

_Example: story `Stories.Validation`._

_Example: story `Stories.Failing`._

_Example: story `Stories.Locked`._

## Content

- **The label is the field's name as the rail shows it:** "Owner", "Next action". The same word as the KeyValue's label or the column's heading.
- **A placeholder says what goes here, as a noun:** "Unassigned", "Add next action". Not "Click to edit", not "Enter a value".
- **A validation message says the rule, in one sentence:** "Two to twelve letters, digits or hyphens." Not "Invalid".
- **A save failure says why, from the server's message when it has one,** and "Could not save" when it does not.
- **A lock's reason says what to wait for:** "Wait for the change to Title to finish saving."
- **A Select's options are the record's words,** drawn as the record draws them; an id is never a label.
- **Every word the part writes itself** (Try again, Discard, Edit, the action names, the multiline hint, "Not saved") comes from the LedgerProvider's messages.

## Style

| Element  | Token                                                                                                                                                                             |
| -------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Row      | `dimension.control.xsmall` 24px · `space.025` block · `space.075` gap · `radius.small` · tint reaching `space.050` past the column · `space.050` at the end of the Editable's box |
| Value    | `font.body` · `color.text` · `color.text.subtlest` for the placeholder                                                                                                            |
| Tint     | `color.background.neutral.subtle.hovered`, `.pressed` · `motion.duration.fast` on `motion.easing.standard`                                                                        |
| Field    | `dimension.control.xsmall` · `color.background.input` · `color.border.input`, `color.border.focused` focused, `color.border.danger` invalid                                       |
| Mark     | `dimension.icon.small` 14px · `color.icon.success` · `color.icon.danger` · the Spinner                                                                                            |
| Actions  | xsmall IconButtons, subtle Cancel and primary Save · `space.050` gap, at the end of the row                                                                                       |
| Message  | `font.body.xsmall` · `color.text.danger`; the lock's reason `color.text.subtle`                                                                                                   |
| Recovery | xsmall Buttons, secondary Try again and subtle Discard · `space.050` gap                                                                                                          |
| Focus    | The kit's focus outline, `color.border.focused`                                                                                                                                   |

## Accessibility

- **Touch:** the row is 24px tall, and where any pointer is coarse its `::after` is a hit area at least 24px tall across the value (the shared `touch-target-block-after` band); `::before` holds the hover tint. A touch keyboard has no Escape, so where any pointer is coarse the field shows Cancel and Save. A press on either keeps focus in the field, so leaving does not commit first.
- **The row is named by the label and the value:** "Owner: Dana Whitfield". The label is read before the value, so a screen reader hears what the field is where a sighted reader reads the KeyValue's label beside it.
- **The field is named by the label** (`aria-label`) and, invalid, is `aria-invalid` and described by the message. A paragraph's Edit button is named "Edit" and the label.
- **Keyboard:** Tab reaches the row; Enter or Space opens the field with the existing value; Enter commits and Escape puts the old value back, and either returns focus to the row. Escape stops at the field, so a Dialog, Sheet or Popover around it stays open; the next Escape, from the row, reaches it (In dialog). Leaving the field by Tab or a click commits and focus goes where the reader sent it; Tab into its own Cancel and Save does not. Switching to another window or tab is not leaving: the field keeps its draft. A refused leave keeps the field open with its message and shows Cancel. Date: the field is named by the label, and its button by the label too ("Choose a date for Due"); Alt+Down opens the month, arrows move between days, Enter chooses and commits, and Escape closes the month and returns to the field. Select and searchable Combobox triggers expose the native combobox role. Enter, Space or Down opens the options; arrows move between them and Enter chooses. Escape closes without changing the value. While saving, the row stays focusable and read-only, with `aria-disabled` announcing that another edit must wait.
- **After a refused save** focus stays on the row, which is `aria-invalid` and described by the reason. Try again and Discard are named with the field ("Try again to save Owner", "Discard the change to Owner") and return focus to the row.
- **A locked row** stays in the tab order and in place: `aria-disabled`, described by the reason, which also shows when the reader clicks or presses Enter on it. Nothing is disabled, so focus never drops to the page.
- **In a DataTable:** Enter moves to the next row only after accepting a valid text commit. Invalid input keeps focus, and an IME composition confirmation neither saves nor changes rows.
- **A landed save is announced:** "Saved", or "Not saved: " and the reason, from a status region under the row; the Spinner says "Saving". The region is visually hidden inside the Editable's own positioned wrapper, so in a table that scrolls sideways it stays in the table's frame and never widens the page (In table).
- **The stories** exercise validation, refused leaves, window switches, keyboard selection, search, save rejection with the refused value kept, Try again and Discard, the draft callbacks, the lock, labelled options, Escape inside a Dialog, rollback, pending guards and focus restoration.

_Example: story `Stories.InDialog`._

## Props

Editable keeps its value, validation and save contract while composing the shared Input, Textarea, Select, Combobox and DatePicker's month. The searchable popup follows [shadcn](https://ui.shadcn.com/docs/components/base/combobox#popup) and [Base UI](https://base-ui.com/react/components/combobox#input-inside-popup). Each part is exported by name and as a member of `Editable`.

### EditableText

_Props of `EditableText`, generated from its types:_

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `label` (required) | `string` |  | The field's name, for a screen reader: "Owner", "Status". The KeyValue or the column shows the visible one; this names the control. |
| `value` (required) | `string` |  | The committed value, shown at rest. |
| `onValueChange` | `((next: string) => void)` |  | Called with the next value at once, before the save settles, and with the old one again if the save fails. |
| `onChange` | `((next: string) => void)` |  | @deprecated Use `onValueChange`, called with the same values. `onChange` is still called, for one version, when `onValueChange` is not given. |
| `validate` | `((next: string) => string \| null)` |  | Return a message to block the commit, or null when the value is valid. It runs as the reader types and again at the commit. |
| `save` (required) | `(next: string) => Promise<unknown>` |  | Saves the value. A rejected promise rolls the value back, shows the error's message under it and keeps the refused value, with Try again and Discard. |
| `onEditingChange` | `((editing: boolean) => void)` |  | Called with `true` when the editor opens (Text's field, Select's options) and `false` when it closes. |
| `onDraftChange` | `((draft: string \| null) => void)` |  | Called with the unsaved draft whenever it changes: the text being typed while it differs from the value, or a refused value kept for another try; `null` once it is saved, put back or discarded, and when the Editable unmounts. A host feeds its draft guard (a route blocker, `beforeunload`) from it rather than from the field's DOM events. |
| `onCancel` | `(() => void)` |  | Called when the reader drops an edit without saving: Escape or Cancel in Text's field, or Discard after a refused save on either. Closing a Select's options without a choice changes nothing, so it is not a cancel. |
| `lockedReason` | `string` |  | A temporary lock with its reason, while the value may not change for now: "Wait for the change to Title to finish saving." The row stays in place and focusable, is `aria-disabled`, is described by the reason, and shows the reason when the reader tries to edit. A field already open keeps its draft, and its save stays the host's to refuse. A value that never changes is plain text instead, and a whole form is never disabled around a save. |
| `placeholder` | `string` |  | What to add, as a noun, shown in the field while it is empty and at rest in place of the dash: "Unassigned", "Add next action". |
| `multiline` | `boolean` | `false` | A paragraph: the value wraps at rest as text the reader can select, with an Edit button beside it, and edits in a textarea with Cancel and Save. Enter adds a line; Ctrl/Cmd+Enter saves. |

| `render` | `((value: T, label: string) => ReactNode)` |  | Draws a value, given its label too: a Badge for a status, a Person for an owner. Used for the committed value and every option, including searchable lists. Unsaid, the label as text. |
| `searchable` | `boolean` |  | A list worth searching: a search field above the same rendered options. On by itself past eight options. |
| `emptyLabel` | `string` |  | Offers a first choice that clears the value, named by this: "Unassigned", "No owner". Choosing it commits the empty string. |
| `placeholder` | `string` |  | Shown at rest in `color.text.subtlest` while the value is empty, as a noun: "Unassigned". Unsaid, the `emptyLabel`, else the muted dash. |

## Related

- [KeyValue](?path=/docs/components-keyvalue--docs) and [Fact](?path=/docs/components-fact--docs): the rows an Editable sits in.
- [DataTable](?path=/docs/patterns-data-table--docs): columns with `editable`, and Enter moving down the column.
- [Forms](?path=/docs/patterns-forms--docs): a record that does not exist yet, and values that change together.

- [Badge](?path=/docs/components-badge--docs): what a status Select renders.

## Don't

A record that does not exist yet is a form, with Fields and a primary that creates it, never a column of Editables. An empty value's placeholder says what goes there, never an instruction ("Click to edit"). A value from a fixed set is an `Editable.Select`, never typed text.

_Example: story `Stories.Dont`._

<!-- page: Patterns/Forms (src/stories/patterns/Forms.mdx) -->

# Forms

**Forms is a pattern**, composed from Field, input controls, layout primitives and buttons. There is no standalone Form component. TanStack Form owns form state and validation; Ledger owns the presentation.

How the form controls go together: which control answers which question, how a form is laid out, how required fields and errors work, and where the buttons go. Each control has its own page; this one is the choice between them and the rules they share.

_Example: story `Stories.Fields`._

## Variants

| The answer                                               | The control                                                                                                                                                      |
| -------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| One line of free text: a name, an email, a number        | [Input](?path=/docs/components-input--docs), with `type` for the value's kind.                                                                                   |
| Several lines: a note, a description, a narrative        | [Textarea](?path=/docs/components-textarea--docs), with `rows` for the expected length, `autoResize` for a long one and `characterLimit` for a stored limit.     |
| A search                                                 | [SearchField](?path=/docs/components-searchfield--docs).                                                                                                         |
| A number, with a unit or a format                        | [NumberField](?path=/docs/components-numberfield--docs); a fixed unit beside an Input is an [InputGroup](?path=/docs/components-inputgroup--docs).               |
| One answer from visible choices                          | [RadioGroup](?path=/docs/components-radiogroup--docs).                                                                                                           |
| One of four to a dozen plain words                       | [Select](?path=/docs/components-select--docs).                                                                                                                   |
| One of a short list whose options carry a Dot or a Badge | [Select](?path=/docs/components-select--docs).                                                                                                                   |
| One of many, or names the reader would type              | [Combobox](?path=/docs/components-combobox--docs).                                                                                                               |
| Several things that can each be true                     | A [CheckboxGroup](?path=/docs/components-checkboxgroup--docs) of Checkboxes under a FieldLegend.                                                                 |
| An on/off setting that applies at once                   | [Switch](?path=/docs/components-switch--docs), in a horizontal Field. Inside a submitted form it is a Checkbox.                                                  |
| A day to schedule                                        | [DatePicker](?path=/docs/components-datepicker--docs). A remembered date is an Input with the format in the hint.                                                |
| A moment: a day and a time                               | [DateTimeField](?path=/docs/components-datetimefield--docs), in the reader's zone. A time of day alone is a [TimeField](?path=/docs/components-timefield--docs). |
| A period                                                 | [DateRangePicker](?path=/docs/components-daterangepicker--docs).                                                                                                 |
| A record: a person, a control, a requirement             | Combobox, or a [RecordPicker](?path=/docs/patterns-recordpicker--docs) when the choice needs more than a row.                                                    |

_Example: story `Stories.Pickers`._

## Anatomy

Compose each [Field](?path=/docs/components-field--docs) from a FieldLabel, the control, a FieldDescription and a FieldError. The Field ties them together: no ids, no `htmlFor`, no `aria-describedby`. A group of choices is a Field around a FieldSet (or a CheckboxGroup) with a FieldLegend. The Fields stack `space.200` apart, or sit in a Grid when the answers are short. The buttons come last.

| Part    | What it is                                                                                                                   |
| ------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Field   | Label, control, message. The label is a noun in sentence case; the hint a sentence; the error what fixes it.                 |
| Group   | A Field around a FieldSet or CheckboxGroup: a legend over the choices, with the hint and the error for the group.            |
| Section | Group related fields under a clear heading, with `space.300` between sections.                                               |
| Buttons | An Inline at the end of the form, aligned to the end: Cancel as a subtle Button, then the primary. The primary says the act. |

_Example: story `Stories.Choices`._

## Sizes

- **Labels above by default.** Horizontal and responsive fields support compact choices and settings rows.
- **Each field as wide as its answer.** In a six-column Grid, an acronym takes two columns, a name four, an owner three, a description the row. A field wider than its answer lies about the answer.
- **One column in a narrow form.** Put the Grid in a FieldGroup, a size container, and give each cell the whole row until the form is 28rem wide: `col-span-6 @md/field-group:col-span-2`. The form collapses by its own width, in a phone, a narrow dialog or a panel, not by the window's; the order stays. A two-column pair is `grid-cols-1 @md/field-group:grid-cols-2` on the same container.
- **`space.200`** (16px) between fields, **`space.300`** (24px) between sections, **`space.100`** (8px) between the choices of a group.
- **The first field takes focus** in a dialog or a sheet that exists to fill the form, through `initialFocus` on its content, never `autoFocus`, which leaves focus nowhere when the surface closes. On a page, nothing does.

_Example: story `Stories.Layout`._

## Modifiers

- **Required is marked, optional is not.** Pass `required` to the Field: the control announces it and the label shows the asterisk, hidden from its name. The form checks on submit.
- **When most of a form is required, mark nothing** (`FieldLabel required={false}`), and say "Optional." in the hint of the few that are. The rule is per product, not per form: the products' record forms mark required.
- **Choose one validation presentation.** Use `noValidate` when the application supplies its own messages and [ErrorSummary](?path=/docs/components-errorsummary--docs). The Field's `required` is not a native constraint; native `required` on the control makes the browser and Base UI check it too, so leave it off when the form library validates.

## States

- **TanStack Form owns state.** Create the form with `useForm`, bind each control through a `form.Field` render prop, and submit a native `<form>` with `form.handleSubmit()`.
- **Validate with Zod, on submit, then on change.** The main example uses `onDynamic` with `revalidateLogic({ mode: "submit", modeAfterSubmission: "change" })`: nothing is marked until the first submission, then each field clears as the reader repairs it. One validation slot avoids stale messages from another mode. A product that validates on blur passes `mode: "blur"`. The Required on submit example uses only `onSubmit`, which does not update as the reader repairs a value.
- **Keep the primary available for incomplete values.** While the form submits, the primary shows `isLoading` (read with `form.Subscribe`) and is never also `disabled`, so it keeps focus; a surface around the form holds itself with `pending`. Show success only after persistence completes. The examples save locally for demonstration.
- **Mark the field, say what fixes it.** Pass `invalid` to the Field and the messages to FieldError; the control is marked and described by them. After a failed submission, focus the first invalid control; when the form is long or spans steps, show an ErrorSummary above it instead, which takes focus and lists every issue.
- **Reset deliberately.** Use `form.reset()` for an explicit Reset action. Preserve the draft after a server failure.

_Example: story `Stories.RequiredOnSubmit`._

## Content

- **Cancel, then the primary**, at the end of the row, aligned to the end. The primary's label is the act: Create program, Save statement, Assign. Never OK or Submit.
- **A form that saves as it goes has no buttons**: an [Editable](?path=/docs/patterns-editable--docs) value on a record, a Switch in a settings list.
- **A destructive act is not a form's primary**; it is a danger Button with an [AlertDialog](?path=/docs/components-alertdialog--docs).

## Style

| Form                                   | Where                                                                                                           |
| -------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| A focused create or edit task          | Dialog, with first-field focus and a DialogFooter outside the scrolling body.                                   |
| A multi-step setup                     | A page wizard when the workflow needs several stages.                                                           |
| One contextual filter or reason        | Popover at its trigger.                                                                                         |
| One value on a record                  | Editable, read in place and edited on activation.                                                               |
| A selection or parent-owned draft task | A specifically documented Sheet or RecordBrowser workflow; not a second default for ordinary create/edit forms. |

Use Cancel as a subtle button before the operation's primary. Preserve dirty drafts and pending saves when closing or navigating. In Program Assurance, the product contract names the closed exception list; field count alone never switches a create/edit task between Dialog and Sheet.

## Related

- [Field](?path=/docs/components-field--docs): the label, hint and error around one control or one group.
- [ErrorSummary](?path=/docs/components-errorsummary--docs): every issue in one place after a failed submission.
- [CheckboxGroup](?path=/docs/components-checkboxgroup--docs): several choices under one legend, with select-all.
- [Input](?path=/docs/components-input--docs), [Textarea](?path=/docs/components-textarea--docs), [InputGroup](?path=/docs/components-inputgroup--docs): the fields.
- [Checkbox](?path=/docs/components-checkbox--docs), [Switch](?path=/docs/components-switch--docs), [RadioGroup](?path=/docs/components-radiogroup--docs): the choice controls.
- [Select](?path=/docs/components-select--docs), [Combobox](?path=/docs/components-combobox--docs), [DatePicker](?path=/docs/components-datepicker--docs), [Calendar](?path=/docs/components-calendar--docs): the pickers.
- [Button](?path=/docs/components-button--docs): the primary and its Cancel.

## Accessibility

Use a visible label for every control. Inside a Field the label, hint and error reach the control without ids; custom controls that render a Ledger control, or forward native props to one, take the binding too. Groups use a fieldset and legend. On failed submit, focus the first invalid field, or an ErrorSummary that lists every error when a form spans several sections or steps. Inline errors are not live regions; the summary is. Keep submitted values after a server failure.

## Form libraries

Forms is a composition pattern, with no component props of its own. Import `useForm` from `@tanstack/react-form` and `z` from `zod` (Zod 3.25+ or 4 supports Standard Schema). Applications declare these dependencies themselves; Ledger's controls do not depend on a form library.

### TanStack and shadcn anatomy

This follows the [Base UI TanStack guide](https://base-ui.com/react/handbook/forms#tanstack-form) and the [TanStack validation documentation](https://tanstack.com/form/latest/docs/framework/react/guides/validation). Field uses the flat label, description and error parts; FieldGroup, Stack or Grid supplies layout. The Field takes `invalid` from the field's meta and wires the rest.

```tsx
const form = useForm({
  defaultValues: { title: "" },
  validationLogic: revalidateLogic({ mode: "submit", modeAfterSubmission: "change" }),
  validators: {
    onDynamic: z.object({ title: z.string().trim().min(1, "Enter a task title.") }),
  },
  onSubmit: async ({ value }) => {
    await saveRecord(value);
  },
});

<form
  noValidate
  onSubmit={(event) => {
    event.preventDefault();
    void form.handleSubmit();
  }}
>
  <Stack space="space.200">
    <form.Field name="title">
      {(field) => {
        const invalid = field.state.meta.isTouched && !field.state.meta.isValid;
        return (
          <Field invalid={invalid} required>
            <FieldLabel>Task title</FieldLabel>
            <Input
              name={field.name}
              value={field.state.value}
              onBlur={field.handleBlur}
              onValueChange={field.handleChange}
            />
            <FieldError errors={invalid ? field.state.meta.errors : []} />
          </Field>
        );
      }}
    </form.Field>
    <Button type="submit" variant="primary">
      Create task
    </Button>
  </Stack>
</form>;
```

The live examples use `noValidate` and let the schema report every error. The Field's `required` announces and marks without a native constraint. Native constraints on the control (`required`, `type`, `pattern`) are also checked by Base UI inside a Field: after an Enter in the field, or on each change once the form has marked it invalid. Leave them off the control when the form library already checks the same rule.

Bind Input, and Textarea with `value`, `onBlur={field.handleBlur}` and `onChange` passing `event.target.value`. Select and RadioGroup use `value` and `onValueChange={field.handleChange}`; Checkbox and Switch use boolean `checked` and `onCheckedChange`; a checkbox’s mixed presentation uses the separate boolean `indeterminate` prop. Combobox uses Root `value`/`onValueChange` and forwards blur through ComboboxInput; DatePicker, DateRangePicker, TimeField and DateTimeField use `value`/`onValueChange` as well, reporting ISO strings. Forward blur to the focusable control. For checkbox arrays, use `form.Field` with `mode="array"` and TanStack's `pushValue`/`removeValue` helpers.

### Validation and recovery

The recovery example combines native inputs, an InputGroup, a custom input, Select and Combobox. TanStack owns editable values and metadata; native form submission also includes a control associated from outside the form. A failed submission shows an ErrorSummary, which takes focus and leads to each field. The Zod schema requires an owner only for Assigned status, so changing that status clears the obsolete error and the Field's `required` follows it. A local async validator simulates a server rejection for `taken@example.test`; the rejected value is kept until the reader changes it, because TanStack clears a submit-time error on the field's next blur. Reset clears the draft and validation state.

_Example: story `Stories.ValidationRecovery`._

## Don't

Do not disable submit merely because values are incomplete, discard a draft after failure, use placeholders as labels, or announce success before saving. Do not put a button inside a link. Keep essential instructions visible, and let long translated labels wrap.

<!-- page: Patterns/Gates (src/stories/patterns/Gates.mdx) -->

# Gates

**Status: Stable.**

The conditions an action waits on, what a record still needs, a phase's entry and exit criteria. A met gate is a check and its label, muted. An unmet gate is a Dot in its tone, the label, the reason under it and the action that meets it. A list, never a score: the reader sees which, and why. The nearest thing elsewhere is a pull request's merge checks: a set, where a progress tracker is a sequence.

_Example: story `Stories.GatesStory`._

## Anatomy

| Part   | What it is                                                                                  |
| ------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Mark   | A 16px box: a check in `color.icon.success` when met, the 6px Dot in the tone when not.     |
| Label  | `font.body.small`: the condition. `color.text.subtle` when met, `color.text` when not.      |
| Reason | `font.body.xsmall` in `color.text.subtle` under the label: what is missing, or the finding. |
| Action | At the end of the row: a link Button or a TextLink, the one thing that meets the gate.      |
| List   | A `ul` with `role="list"`, `space.050` between rows, `space.100` between mark and label.    |

_Example: story `Stories.GatesMatrix`._

## Variants

Gates has one appearance. What varies is the unmet tone, and where the list lives.

| Unmet tone | Use                                                                                    |
| ---------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `warning`  | The default: the gate can be met from this record, and the reason says how.            |
| `danger`   | Nothing on this record can move it: the source gives no reason, the PM has not signed. |

| Where                         | What                                                                                     |
| ----------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| A record's rail               | Under a Collapsible titled Gates with the unmet count: what the requirement still needs. |
| A Needs block on the overview | Unmet gates only, each with its action.                                                  |
| A revision's submit gates     | Every gate, met and not, under the revision's facts.                                     |

What is not a gate: a workflow's steps, which are a [Stepper](?path=/docs/components-stepper--docs); a checklist the reader ticks, which is a group of [Checkbox](?path=/docs/components-checkbox--docs); a fraction met, which is a score and belongs to nothing here.

## Sizes

One size: the row is one line of `font.body.small`, and a second of `font.body.xsmall` when there is a reason. The list is as wide as its rail or block; a long reason wraps under its label, never beside it.

## States

| State          | What changes                                                                                |
| -------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Met            | The check, the label in `color.text.subtle`, no reason unless the finding is worth reading. |
| Unmet, warning | The warning Dot, the label in `color.text`, the reason, the action if there is one.         |
| Unmet, danger  | The danger Dot; otherwise the same.                                                         |
| All met        | Every row a check: a quiet list, which is the point of a list that is done.                 |

_Example: story `Stories.AllMet`._

## Modifiers

- **`met`** on each item: what the mark, the label's colour and the spoken state follow.
- **`tone`** for the unmet colour: `danger` when nothing here can move it.
- **`reason`** for the sentence under the label. On an unmet gate always; on a met one only when the finding is worth reading, such as who signed and when.
- **`action`** for the one link that meets it, on the gates the reader can meet from here.
- **`aria-labelledby`** on Gates for the heading shown above the list ("Submit gates"), or `aria-label` when none shows, so the list is announced by name.

_Example: story `Stories.InRail`._

## Content

- **The label names the condition as a noun phrase:** "Owner", "Success criterion", "Contested overlays resolved". Not a verb ("Add an owner") and not a question.
- **The reason is one sentence:** what is missing, or the finding. "Nothing decides that it is met." "SI-7(1) gives no reason."
- **The action is a verb and the gate it meets:** "Add success criterion", "Resolve overlays". It goes to where the gate is met. A bare "Add" down the list gives every row's action the same name.
- **The order is the order they are checked**, met and unmet together, not sorted by state. The reader learns the list.

## Style

| Element | Token                                                                                            |
| ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Mark    | 16px box · check `dimension.icon.small` in `color.icon.success` · Dot 6px in `color.icon.<tone>` |
| Label   | `font.body.small` · `color.text.subtle` met · `color.text` unmet                                 |
| Reason  | `font.body.xsmall` · `color.text.subtle` · `space.025` under the label                           |
| Row     | `space.100` between mark, text and action · `space.050` between rows                             |
| Action  | The link Button's or TextLink's own style                                                        |

The Dot is Badge's, so an unmet gate in `warning` is the same amber as a warning Indicator.

## Accessibility

- **It is a list**: `ul` and `li`, with `role="list"` so WebKit keeps it without markers, and a screen reader announces the count and moves row by row. Name it with `aria-labelledby` when a heading shows above it.
- **The state is spoken.** "Met:" or "Not met:" is visually hidden before each label, from the locale's `gateMet` and `gateNotMet` (`Met: {label}`), so a translation keeps its own word order; the check and the Dot are hidden from assistive technology, so nothing is said twice.
- **The unmet tone is not spoken.** A danger gate's reason says that nothing here can move it, in words.
- **The action is the only focusable part**, named by its own text, which names the gate: a list of actions read out of context ("Add success criterion") still says which gate each meets.
- **No live region.** Gates change when the record changes, and the page re-renders; an Alert says what happened if something must be announced.

## Props

_Props of `Gates`, generated from its types:_

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `children` (required) | `ReactNode` |  | Gates.Item rows, in the order they are checked. |
| `aria-label` | `string` |  | The list's name when no heading shows it: "Submit gates". |
| `aria-labelledby` | `string` |  | The id of the heading that names the list, when one shows above it ("Submit gates", "Exit criteria"). A screen reader then announces the list by that name. |
| `className` | `string` |  |  |

### Gates.Item

_Props of `GateItem`, generated from its types:_

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `met` (required) | `boolean` |  | Whether the condition holds. A met gate is a check and a muted label; an unmet one a Dot in its tone. |
| `tone` | `"danger" \| "information" \| "neutral" \| "success" \| "warning"` | `warning` | The unmet colour. `warning` is the default; `danger` for a gate nothing on this record can move. |
| `label` (required) | `ReactNode` |  | The condition, as a noun phrase: "Owner", "One shall", "Success criterion". |
| `reason` | `ReactNode` |  | One short sentence under the label: what is missing, or the finding. An unmet gate's; a met one carries it only when the finding is worth reading. |
| `action` | `ReactNode` |  | The one thing that meets it, at the end of the row: a link Button or a TextLink named for the gate ("Add success criterion"). |

## Don't

A reason goes under an unmet gate only, the gates are a list that says which and why, never a score, and a gate the reader can meet from here has one link named for it, never a primary button on every gate.

_Example: story `Stories.Dont`._

<!-- page: Patterns/Glance (src/stories/patterns/Glance.mdx) -->

# Glance

**Status: Stable.**

A compact record summary: an id and status, a title, a meta line and selected facts. It supplies content for a [HoverCard](?path=/docs/components-hovercard--docs); the product chooses the facts and the link's destination.

_Example: story `Stories.GlanceStory`._

## Anatomy

| Part          | Behavior                                                                              |
| ------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Id and status | The id uses small subtle text; the optional status sits at the other end of the line. |
| Title         | Medium body text, clamped to two lines.                                               |
| Meta          | Small subtle text for kind, path, owner or other context.                             |
| Facts         | Up to four KeyValue rows with 88px labels. Additional facts are omitted.              |

Use a Badge or Indicator with a text label for status. Select facts that help readers decide whether to open the record; keep any essential information available at the destination.

A status is never a Dot alone, whose colour is its only signal, and a Glance is given no more than four facts: it shows the first four and leaves the rest out without a word.

_Example: story `Stories.DoDont`._

_Example: story `Stories.GlanceMatrix`._

## Surface and interaction

Glance supplies content and has no width or open state of its own. These examples use a 300px surface. A HoverCard defaults to 256px; set `style={{ width: 300 }}` on `HoverCardContent` when the summary needs more space.

HoverCard opens after delayed pointer hover or keyboard focus on its trigger, and dismisses on leaving, outside press or Escape. Its content does not add a Tab stop or move focus. Use the trigger link to reach the destination, where the summary's information and actions remain available.

When rendered on a page, Glance's text reads in order: id, status, title, meta, then facts. The component has no interactive controls.

## Props

_Props of `Glance`, generated from its types:_

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` (required) | `ReactNode` |  | The record's id, first on the first line. |
| `title` (required) | `ReactNode` |  | The record's name, at most two lines. |
| `meta` | `ReactNode` |  | The record's meta line: kind, path, owner. One line. |
| `status` | `ReactNode` |  | One status, at the end of the id's line. A Badge or an Indicator. |
| `facts` | `{ label: string; value: ReactNode; }[]` | `[]` | At most four, label and value; the rest belong to the peek. |

_Example: story `Stories.Playground`._

_Rendered in the Storybook: Controls._

## Related

[HoverCard](?path=/docs/components-hovercard--docs) · [PreviewSheet](?path=/docs/patterns-previewsheet--docs) · [KeyValue](?path=/docs/components-keyvalue--docs) · [Pages](?path=/docs/layout-pages--docs)

# Inspector

**Status: Stable.**

Groups of a record's facts: state, owner, identifiers and dates, as label and value rows under a title that folds. It is the Details rail beside a record's work area, and the Details block in a preview or a panel. The surrounding layout owns where it sits and how it scrolls.

`Inspector` is the root: it holds `Inspector.Group` children in the order the reader needs them, then a `footer`. Each group is one name and its facts as children, with an action beside its title. A group's KeyValue rows go in one [KeyValue.Group](?path=/docs/components-keyvalue--docs), so a screen reader hears one list of pairs per group, and the group gives them one label width; KeyValues given directly, and nothing else, become one KeyValue.Group. A row of Badges or a short list sits beside or instead of it.

```tsx
<Inspector
  footer={
    <Button size="small" variant="link">
      Edit properties
    </Button>
  }
>
  <Inspector.Group title="Ownership">
    <KeyValue label="Owner">Dana Whitfield</KeyValue>
    <KeyValue label="Sponsor">Alex Morgan</KeyValue>
  </Inspector.Group>
  <Inspector.Group title="Schedule">
    <KeyValue label="Due">30 Sept 2026</KeyValue>
  </Inspector.Group>
</Inspector>
```

_Example: story `Stories.Composition`._

`groups` is deprecated: the same groups as data (`{ title, rows: [{ label, value }] }`), which the root renders as open Inspector.Groups before any children. It goes in the next minor version; compose the groups instead, which also gives each group its action, its `defaultOpen` and rows that are more than a label and a value. `ledger/no-deprecated-name` reports it.

## Group

Each group's title is a [CollapsibleHeader](?path=/docs/components-collapsible--docs): a button inside a heading, the title at the start and a chevron at the end that turns while the group is open. A group is open by default; `defaultOpen={false}` makes the collapsed Details a reader opens when they need provenance, counts or derivation, and `open` with `onOpenChange` hands the state to the caller. The action, an IconButton or a link button, sits beside the title while the whole title fits beside it on one line, and takes the next row, at the end, otherwise.

_Example: story `Stories.Group`._

_Example: story `Stories.Controlled`._

## Heading level

A group's heading takes the contextual level, an h3 when nothing sets one. In a [Shell](?path=/docs/layout-shell--docs) Aside rail the groups sit under the page's h1, so the Aside starts its content at 2 and the groups are h2s; in a titled Shell.Panel the body already starts at 3, under the panel's h2; under a preview's h2 record title, the content after the header goes one below with a HeadingLevelProvider, and the groups are h3s. A rail outside the Shell sets the level itself with `HeadingLevelProvider level={2}`.

_Example: story `Stories.InARail`._

## In the Details disclosure

Below the aside breakpoint a record's Shell.Aside is a Details disclosure in the page, closed until the reader opens it (Shell's Record details at 390px). Its row is the h2 and its content one level below, so the groups there are h3s. A group named as the disclosure ("Details", or the Aside's `heading`) is the disclosure's own content: its title, which would repeat the row's, steps aside, and its rows show while the disclosure is open. Its action stays, at the end of a row above them. The other groups keep their titles and fold as in the rail.

## When to use it

- **Use it** for the handful of facts that identify a record and its state, beside the work or at the top of a preview.
- **Not** for a record's own content, the statement, the narrative, the evidence: those are [Section](?path=/docs/layout-section--docs)s in the work area. **Not** for editing more than one fact at a time: that is a form in a Dialog; a single supported fact is an [Editable](?path=/docs/patterns-editable--docs) in a row.
- **Not** for linked records: a [Related](?path=/docs/patterns-related--docs) card lists them with their own links.
- On a page body, a collapsed block of details is a collapsible [Section](?path=/docs/layout-section--docs); in a rail of facts, it is an Inspector.Group with `defaultOpen={false}`.

## Accessibility

- Every group title is a button inside a heading, so the rail is in the heading outline and each group's state is announced ("Provenance, collapsed, button"). Enter and Space toggle it; focus stays on it.
- A group's facts are one definition list ("list, 4 items"), not one list per fact.
- Open and closed look different by more than colour: the chevron turns. Under reduced motion it turns without moving and the rows appear without the fold.
- The action is its own tab stop after the title, outside the heading, and names what it acts on ("Edit details").
- Give the rail's region a label (Shell.Aside's `label`), and set the level so the groups sit under the right parent, as above.

## Props

_Props of `Inspector`, generated from its types:_

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `children` | `ReactNode` |  | The groups, Inspector.Group parts, in the order the reader needs them. |
| `groups` | `InspectorGroupData[]` |  | @deprecated Compose Inspector.Group children instead (`<Inspector><Inspector.Group title="Ownership"><KeyValue label="Owner">…</KeyValue></Inspector.Group></Inspector>`); the data form goes in the next minor version. The groups as data, each an open Inspector.Group with its rows, before any children. |
| `footer` | `ReactNode` |  | Under the groups: a link button, "Edit properties". |

### Inspector.Group

_Props of `InspectorGroup`, generated from its types:_

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `title` (required) | `string` |  | The group's name, a noun for the kind of fact: "Ownership", "Exposure". |
| `children` (required) | `ReactNode` |  | The facts: a KeyValue.Group of a handful of KeyValue rows; a row of Badges; a short list. KeyValues given directly, and nothing else, become one KeyValue.Group. |
| `action` | `ReactNode` |  | At the top end of the group, before the rows: an IconButton ("Edit properties") or a link button. |
| `defaultOpen` | `boolean` | `true` | Whether the group starts open: `true` by default. `false` for the collapsed Details a reader opens when they need provenance, counts or derivation. |
| `open` | `boolean` |  | The open state, when the caller controls it. |
| `onOpenChange` | `((open: boolean, eventDetails: CollapsibleRootChangeEventDetails) => void)` |  | Called when the reader opens or closes the group, with Base UI's event details (`details.cancel()` keeps the state). |
| `className` | `string` |  |  |

Inspector and Inspector.Group take their root's native `div` props, a `className` and a ref, and name themselves last with `data-slot` (`inspector`, `inspector-group`). `InspectorGroup` is the same part by name.

_Example: story `Stories.NativeAttributes`._

_Example: story `Stories.Playground`._

_Rendered in the Storybook: Controls._

## Don't

_Example: story `Stories.Dont`._
