<!-- page: Patterns/PickerSheet (src/stories/patterns/PickerSheet.mdx) -->

# PickerSheet

**Status: Stable.**

Choosing many from hundreds: the association panel. A [Sheet](?path=/docs/components-sheet--docs) whose toolbar is a search field and the filters, whose body is a [DataTable](?path=/docs/patterns-data-table--docs) with sortable headers and a selection, and whose footer names how many are chosen and the one thing to do with them. The selection survives search and filters. When the chosen rows need fields of their own, a second frame of the same sheet shows them as a compact table with editable cells and a defaults row applied to all; `onBack` returns to the first frame with the selection kept. The kit owns the frame; the caller owns the columns, the rows and the selection. When the many are found by name rather than by attribute, a [Combobox](?path=/docs/components-combobox--docs) is the picker, and when there is one to pick, the [RecordPicker](?path=/docs/patterns-recordpicker--docs).

_Example: story `Stories.PickerSheetStory`._

## Anatomy

```tsx
function AllocateRequirements() {
  const table = useDataTable({ columns, data: requirements, getRowId, selectable: true });
  return (
    <PickerSheet
      open={open}
      onClose={guard.close}
      title="Allocate requirements"
      subtitle="Flight computer"
      table={table}
      search={{ placeholder: "Search requirements" }}
      pending={saving}
      error={saveError}
      action={{ label: `Allocate ${count} to Flight computer`, onClick: allocate }}
    >
      <DataTable table={table} />
    </PickerSheet>
  );
}
```

Back is rendered only when `onBack` is supplied. The toolbar and its divider are omitted when `search`, `filters` and `toolbar` are all absent.

| Part     | What it is                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| -------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Back     | A chevron before the title on the second frame.                                                                                                                                                                             |
| Title    | The task: "Allocate requirements".                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| Subtitle | What the chosen rows will be attached to: "Flight computer · 14 allocated today".                                                                                                                                           |
| Toolbar  | The kit's Toolbar: the search field, then the filters, which fold into More when the sheet is narrow; then the caller's `toolbar` row. On the second frame, the defaults row. It does not scroll, except in a short window. |
| Body     | A SheetBody. Frame one: the DataTable with Table.Selection. Frame two: the chosen rows with editable cells.                                                                                                                 |
| Error    | `error`, a danger Alert above the footer's buttons, outside the scroll.                                                                                                                                                     |
| Count    | At the start of the footer, a polite status: "12 of 28 selected", "0 of 28 selected", or the chosen record's name for a single choice, with Clear beside it. RecordBrowser counts the same way.                             |
| Actions  | At the end of the footer: a lesser button, Cancel (a subtle Button), then the primary named in full.                                                                                                                        |

## Variants

| Frame    | Use                                                                                                                            |
| -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Choosing | Search, filters, the sortable table, the selection, the count. The primary continues or attaches.                              |
| Details  | The chosen rows as a compact table with editable cells and a defaults row; "Does not apply" per row; back keeps the selection. |

Not built, and why: a Combobox with hundreds of options, because the many are found by attribute and a table sorts and filters; the selection lost on search, because the reader searches several times before attaching; a wizard of three frames, because choosing and describing are the two steps there are; a picker that attaches one at a time, because the footer attaches all at once and says how many.

## The table owns the search

Pass the DataTable as `table` and give it the whole collection as `data`. The search field then drives the table's global filter, so a search that matches nothing shows the table's own filtered empty, "Nothing matches" with Clear filters, and never the empty for a collection with nothing to add. The count, the total and Clear come from the table unless `selected`, `total` and `onClear` are given: the count is its selection, which survives the search, and the total every row that can be chosen, search and filters aside, nested rows included and group bands left out, so a chosen row the search hides is still one of it. Without `table`, `search` takes `value` and `onChange` and the caller filters; filter the table, never the rows handed to it.

_Example: story `Stories.SearchWithNoMatch`._

## Sizes

`width` takes a Sheet step: `large`, 760px and room for a table of four columns, unsaid; `xlarge`, 960px, for more. A number of pixels still works; prefer a step. On a narrow screen the sheet takes the full width. The DataTable fits the sheet, as every DataTable does unless it says `responsive={false}`: give the column the reader chooses by (the name, the statement) `priority: 0` and a readable minimum of about 180 to 220px, and the table keeps it in the row and moves the lower-priority columns into each row's More fields ("+3") instead of scrolling sideways. In a window under 30rem tall (a landscape phone, 400% zoom) the sheet scrolls as one: the header and the toolbar scroll away with the rows and the footer stays, so the list is never squeezed to a single row, and a row that takes focus scrolls clear of the footer.

Past about a hundred candidates, give the table a `pageSize` (or `virtualize` it) so the sheet draws a page at a time; the selection still counts every chosen row across pages, and the header's select-all chooses the rows on the page, not the whole collection. Choosing the rest is a second, explicit step: once the page's rows are chosen and more are on offer, `secondary` holds a "Select all 538" Button (the locale's `selectAllCount`) that calls `table.toggleAllRowsSelected(true)`, as the DataTable's SelectionBar offers it. The command that applies a large selection writes it in one request, so it lands whole or not at all.

_Example: story `Stories.ShortWindow`._

## States

| State          | What changes                                                                                                                                         |
| -------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Nothing chosen | The footer says how many there are to choose from, "0 of 28 selected"; the primary waits, disabled.                                                  |
| Some chosen    | The count and Clear; the primary is live and names the number.                                                                                       |
| One chosen     | A table that chooses one (`selectable: "single"`): the chosen record's name.                                                                         |
| Filtered       | The count keeps its total, every row there is to choose from, and the selection is kept. Folded into More, the filters that apply are counted on it. |
| Loading        | `state="loading"`: the table's skeleton rows; the count says only what is chosen, "0 selected", never "0 of 0".                                      |
| Load failed    | `state="error"`: the table's error with Try again; the count still waits for the rows.                                                               |
| No match       | The table's filtered empty with Clear filters; the selection is kept.                                                                                |
| Pending        | `pending`: the sheet holds, the rows and toolbar are locked, the primary works.                                                                      |
| Failed         | `error` above the buttons; the choice and the fields are kept for a retry.                                                                           |
| Frame two      | The back chevron; the toolbar is the defaults row.                                                                                                   |

`pending` holds the sheet while the action's command runs: Escape, the blanket, the close button and Cancel do nothing and `onClose` is not called; Back and Clear are disabled but keep focus; the toolbar and the rows are inert; the sheet is `aria-busy`; and the primary shows `isLoading` (the action's own `isLoading` wins). When the command fails, end `pending` and set `error` to what went wrong and what to do; when it succeeds, close the sheet.

_Example: story `Stories.PendingAndFailure`._

`state` says where the rows on offer are, as the DataTable's `state` does, and the sheet passes nothing to the table for it: give both the same value. While the rows load, and when they fail to load, what there is to choose from is not known, so the footer counts only what is chosen ("0 selected") and never says "0 of 0", which reads as an empty library. A failed refresh that keeps its rows still counts them.

_Example: story `Stories.LoadingAndFailedLoad`._

In a sheet too narrow for its filters they fold into the toolbar's More, which counts the filters that apply and says so in its name ("More filters, 1 applied"), so a narrowed list never reads as all of it. With `table` the count is its column filters; a caller who filters the rows itself passes `activeFilters`.

_Example: story `Stories.FoldedFilters`._

One record to choose is a table with `selectable: "single"`: a radio per row and no select-all. The footer names the chosen record by the table's `rowLabel` instead of counting it; `summary` overrides it.

_Example: story `Stories.SingleChoice`._

## Modifiers

- **`table`** for the DataTable the search filters and the count reads.
- **`search`**, **`filters`**, **`toolbar`** for the row that stays put: the search and the filters are the kit's Toolbar, so a narrow sheet folds the filters into More, and More counts the filters that apply: the table's column filters, or **`activeFilters`**.
- **`selected`**, **`total`**, **`onClear`** for the footer's count when there is no `table`, or to override it; **`summary`** in place of the count, such as the chosen record's name for a single choice; **`state`** while the rows load or have failed to load.
- **`action`** (with `isLoading`), **`secondary`** for the footer's buttons; **`pending`** and **`error`** for the command; **`onBack`** for the second frame; **`width`**.
- **`initialFocus`** and **`finalFocus`** as on SheetContent; **`onClose`** receives Base UI's details, whose `reason` says whether Escape, the blanket, or the close button or Cancel asked.

## Content

- **The title is the task**, a verb and its object: "Allocate requirements", "Tailor the baseline".
- **The subtitle is what the rows attach to**, and a read-out: "Flight computer · 14 allocated today".
- **The primary is named in full**: "Allocate 12 to Flight computer", "Continue with 12". Never "OK", "Submit", "Done".
- **The count is a sentence of numbers**, the one phrase PickerSheet and RecordBrowser share: "12 of 28 selected" where the rows on offer are known, "12 selected" while they are not.
- **The secondary is the lesser way through**: "Continue without details".

## Style

| Element | Token                                                                                                                                  |
| ------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Sheet   | Sheet's: `elevation.surface.overlay` · `elevation.shadow.overlay` · `color.blanket` behind                                             |
| Toolbar | `space.200` inline · `space.100` block · `color.border` under · `space.100` between its rows                                           |
| Search  | The Toolbar's search field, small                                                                                                      |
| Body    | The DataTable without its own frame, edge to edge                                                                                      |
| Footer  | `elevation.surface.sunken` · `color.border` above · `font.body.small` `color.text.subtle` count, tabular · `space.100` between buttons |

## Accessibility

- **A dialog named by the task** and described by the subtitle; focus moves to the search field on open, or to `initialFocus` (a rationale field), and returns to the opener on close, or to `finalFocus` when choosing hands over to the next surface. Never `autoFocus` a field in the toolbar: it becomes where focus returns, and focus falls to the page on close.
- **The table is the DataTable's**: the selection column's checkboxes, or a single choice's radios, are named by the row's name: the table's `rowLabel` ("Select REQ-0101"), else the text of its identity column. Give the table a `rowLabel` when that text is not the name a reader knows the row by, as when statements repeat and the code tells them apart. Sortable headers say their order.
- **The count is a polite status**: a screen reader hears it after each choice, once the page is quiet.
- **The primary is disabled until something is chosen** and named with the number, so the reader hears what will happen to how many.
- **Escape empties the search first**, then closes the sheet on either frame; the back chevron goes to the first frame with the selection kept.
- **A failure is announced**: `error` is an Alert with `role="alert"`, where a sighted reader sees it too, beside the primary.
- **The words are the locale's**: the count, Back, Search, Clear and Cancel come from the LedgerProvider's messages (`selectedCount` and `selectedCountOf`), so a translated provider translates the sheet.

## Props

_Props of `PickerSheet`, generated from its types:_

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `open` (required) | `boolean` |  |  |
| `initialFocus` | `boolean \| RefObject<HTMLElement \| null> \| ((openType: InteractionType) => boolean \| void \| HTMLElement \| null)` |  | Where focus goes when the sheet opens, as on SheetContent: a rationale field, say. The search field, or the first control, unsaid. |
| `finalFocus` | `boolean \| RefObject<HTMLElement \| null> \| ((closeType: InteractionType) => boolean \| void \| HTMLElement \| null)` |  | Override focus return when choosing opens the next workflow surface. |
| `onClose` (required) | `(details?: DialogRootChangeEventDetails \| undefined) => void` |  | The reader asked to close: Escape, the blanket, the close button or Cancel. Base UI's details say which (`details.reason`). Not called while `pending`. |
| `onBack` | `(() => void)` |  | Back to the choosing frame from the details frame. |
| `title` (required) | `ReactNode` |  | The task, a verb and its object: "Allocate requirements". |
| `subtitle` | `ReactNode` |  | What the chosen rows will be attached to: "Flight computer · 14 allocated today". |
| `table` | `DataTableInstance<TData>` |  | The DataTable the reader chooses from. The search field drives its global filter, so a search with no match shows the table's own filtered empty with Clear filters, never "nothing to add"; and, unless they are given, `selected` is its selection, `total` every row that can be chosen, search and filters aside, and `onClear` clears its selection. Pass the whole collection as the table's `data`. |
| `search` | `PickerSheetSearch` |  | The search field in the toolbar. With `table` it filters the table; without, the caller filters the rows. |
| `filters` | `ReactNode` |  | Filters after the search field, such as `DataTable.Filter`s. They fold into the toolbar's More when the sheet is too narrow for them. |
| `activeFilters` | `number` |  | How many filters apply: More counts them and says so in its name ("More filters, 2 applied") while the filters are folded, so a narrowed list never reads as all of it. The table's column filters unsaid. |
| `toolbar` | `ReactNode` |  | A row under search and filters that does not scroll: a default applied to every chosen row. |
| `selected` | `number` |  | How many rows are chosen. The footer reads it out and the action waits for it. From `table` unsaid. |
| `total` | `number` |  | How many rows there are to choose from, search and filters aside: the "28" of "3 of 28 selected". From `table` unsaid. |
| `state` | `"empty" \| "error" \| "loading" \| "ready" \| "refreshing"` | `ready` | Where the rows on offer are, as the DataTable's `state`. While they are `loading`, and when they failed to load (`error` with none on offer), what there is to choose from is not known, so the footer counts only what is chosen ("0 selected") and never says "0 of 0". A failed refresh that keeps its rows still counts them. `ready` unsaid. |
| `summary` | `ReactNode` |  | The footer's read-out in place of the count. A `table` that chooses one record (`selectable: "single"`) reads the chosen row's `rowLabel` unsaid. |
| `onClear` | `(() => void)` |  | Clears the selection; a link in the footer beside the count. From `table` unsaid. |
| `action` (required) | `{ label: ReactNode; onClick: () => void; disabled?: boolean \| undefined; isLoading?: boolean \| undefined; }` |  | The one thing the footer does, named in full: "Allocate 12 to Flight computer". It waits, disabled, until something is chosen. `isLoading` (the sheet's `pending` unsaid) shows it working. |
| `secondary` | `ReactNode` |  | A second, lesser button before Cancel: "Continue without details". |
| `pending` | `boolean` | `false` | The action's command is in flight. The sheet holds: Escape, the blanket, the close button and Cancel do nothing (`onClose` is not called), Back and Clear are disabled, the toolbar and the rows cannot change, and the sheet is `aria-busy`. End it when the command settles. |
| `error` | `ReactNode` |  | What went wrong with the last attempt and what to do, as one sentence: shown as a danger Alert above the footer's buttons, outside the scroll, so it is seen however long the list is. The choice and the fields are kept for a retry. |
| `width` | `number \| SheetWidth` | `large` | A SheetContent width step: `large` (760px, room for a table of four columns) unsaid, `xlarge` (960px) for more. A number of pixels still works; prefer a step. |
| `children` (required) | `ReactNode` |  | Frame one: a DataTable with a selection. Frame two: a DataTable of the chosen rows with editable cells. |

## Related

- [Recipes · Choosing records](?path=/docs/guidance-recipes--docs#choosing-records): which picker for which choice, and what the kit owns and the caller owns.
- [DataTable](?path=/docs/patterns-data-table--docs): frame one is a DataTable in the sheet.
- [Sheet](?path=/docs/components-sheet--docs): the frame. [Overlays](?path=/docs/components-overlays--docs): how the sheets, dialogs and anchored overlays relate.
- [RecordPicker](?path=/docs/patterns-recordpicker--docs): picking one record from a list.
- [Combobox](?path=/docs/components-combobox--docs): choosing by name.
- [Upgrading](?path=/docs/guidance-upgrading--docs#pickersheet-and-recordbrowser): the one count phrase and what `total` counts.

## Don't

The footer counts what is chosen and names the one thing to do with it, in full, never OK without a count. With nothing chosen the action waits, disabled, and the footer says how many there are to choose from.

_Example: story `Stories.Dont`._

<!-- page: Patterns/PreviewNavigation (src/stories/patterns/PreviewNavigation.mdx) -->

# PreviewNavigation

**Status: Stable.**

The collection controls for a record preview beside a register: previous and next through the table's displayed results, the announced record and position, and a link that opens the full record in a new tab. It belongs in the preview's outer bar, `Shell.Panel.Actions`, immediately before Close. That bar is navigation only: the record's visible name and its actions are an inner PageHeader at the start of the panel's body, its title an h2, as [Shell](?path=/docs/layout-shell--docs) describes.

_Example: story `Stories.Collection`._

## In the panel

```tsx
<Shell.Panel label="Requirement preview" onClose={closePreview}>
  <Shell.Panel.Header>
    <Shell.Panel.Actions>
      <PreviewNavigation
        position={position}
        total={rows.length}
        recordLabel={record.name}
        onPrevious={position > 1 ? showPrevious : undefined}
        onNext={position < rows.length ? showNext : undefined}
        openLink={<Link to={recordPath} target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer" />}
      />
    </Shell.Panel.Actions>
    <Shell.Panel.Close />
  </Shell.Panel.Header>
  <Shell.Panel.Body>
    <PageHeader>
      <PageHeader.Heading>
        <PageHeader.Title>{record.name}</PageHeader.Title>
      </PageHeader.Heading>
      <PageHeader.Actions>
        <Button size="small" variant="primary">
          Edit requirement
        </Button>
      </PageHeader.Actions>
    </PageHeader>
    {/* Labelled properties, then the record's sections. */}
  </Shell.Panel.Body>
</Shell.Panel>
```

The outer bar has no `Shell.Panel.Title`, so the panel takes its accessible name from `label`, and its body's outline starts at 2: the PageHeader.Title is the h2. Do not repeat the record's name in the outer bar, and do not repeat the full-record link at the bottom of the body. A nested record frame adds Back before the navigation.

_Example: story `Stories.InPanel`._

## What the caller owns

The application owns selection, the row order and real record destinations; the part imports no router and holds no rows. The order is the whole filtered and sorted set, with expanded tree rows in place, not the table's current page: supply a one-based `position` and the `total` of that set, and a callback for each adjacent record. When Next crosses the edge of a table page, the caller turns the table to the page that holds the new record, so the active row stays in view. Leave a callback out at an endpoint, or pass a position at the end, and that button is unavailable. Pass the record's name as `recordLabel`, so the announcement says which record arrived.

A position and a total counted on the table's current page are wrong as soon as the result has a second page: the reader hears 3 of 25 where the result holds 62, and Next stops at the page's end. Without `recordLabel` every step is heard as a number alone.

_Example: story `Stories.DoDont`._

`openLink` is an anchor or router link with the record's real destination, `target="_blank"` and `rel="noopener noreferrer"`; it must lead to that record, not its collection. The part gives it its icon, accessible name and tooltip. A preview inside a selection task (RecordBrowser, PickerSheet) belongs to the task and opens no record of its own: leave `openLink` out, and the bar is previous and next alone.

_Example: story `Stories.InTask`._

## Outside the results

If filtering removes the selected record, keep the preview open with `position={0}`. Both navigation buttons are unavailable and say why in their tooltip ("Record outside the current results"), which opens on hover, on keyboard focus and on a tap; the status says so too. The full-record link stays available.

_Example: story `Stories.OutsideResults`._

## Showing the position

The position is always announced. `showPosition` draws it as well, before the buttons ("2 of 6"), and "Not in results" while the record is outside them. Turn it on where the bar has the room: it adds about four characters' width, more for large totals.

_Example: story `Stories.VisiblePosition`._

## Focus and announcements

- The controls are a group named "Record navigation": "Previous record", "Next record" and "Open full record in new tab", each with its name in a tooltip.
- A polite status says the record and its position, "Access review evidence, 2 of 6 records", when the preview opens and on each step. It mounts empty and speaks once assistive technology has seen it, so the first record is heard too.
- Focus stays on the control the reader used while the preview's content changes, so arrowing through a collection needs no hunt for the button.
- At an endpoint the control the reader used stays focused and says it is unavailable (`aria-disabled`); pressing it again does nothing, so a repeated Enter at the last record stays put instead of walking back. Tab still reaches both buttons, and Escape still reaches the panel or sheet around them. In forced colours an unavailable button is GrayText, as a native disabled one is.

## Words

Every label and template is a LedgerProvider message (`previousRecord`, `nextRecord`, `openFullRecord`, `recordNavigation`, `recordPosition`, `recordPositionNamed`, `recordPositionShort`, `recordOutsideResults`, `recordOutsideResultsNamed`, `recordNotInResults`), translated once for the product; see [Locale](?path=/docs/components-locale--docs). Numbers follow the locale. In a right-to-left provider the chevrons turn to face the reading direction, as Pagination's do.

_Example: story `Stories.Localized`._

_Props: generated from `Stories.Collection`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._

<!-- page: Patterns/PreviewSheet (src/stories/patterns/PreviewSheet.mdx) -->

# PreviewSheet

**Status: Stable.**

A modal record task surface built from shadcn's Base UI Sheet. It supports focused work such as evidence-version review. Collection browsing normally uses Shell.Panel with PreviewNavigation. The outer header holds global navigation and Close. The body begins with an inner PageHeader for the record's name and commands; metadata follows below it.

_Example: story `Stories.CollectionTask`._

The following specimen demonstrates generic metadata options and frame replacement for consumers with a different product contract.

_Example: story `Stories.PreviewSheetStory`._

## Anatomy

| Slot                        | Purpose                                                                                                                                                            |
| --------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| title                       | The inner PageHeader's title, rendered as the SheetTitle: the h2 that names the modal. The body's sections sit one level below it.                                 |
| actions                     | Record commands in PageHeader.Actions beside the title; use small controls.                                                                                        |
| id, status, subtitle, facts | Optional body metadata below the record header; absent content leaves no placeholder rows.                                                                         |
| onBack                      | Return to the previous frame: an arrow, "Back to previous record", at the start of the outer header, apart from previous and next.                                 |
| backFocus                   | The control in the parent frame that opened this frame, where Back returns focus.                                                                                  |
| navigation                  | Global controls in the outer header, normally PreviewNavigation with previous/next and a full-record link. With it, `openTo` may be left out.                      |
| openTo                      | The full-record link in the outer header when navigation is absent. Empty children read "Open the full record" (`openTheFullRecord`); required without navigation. |
| links                       | Related destination links in the footer; no repeated full-record link.                                                                                             |
| children                    | The work area after the record header and metadata, in the sheet's SheetBody: its one scroller.                                                                    |
| initialFocus, finalFocus    | Native Base UI focus targets for the consuming workflow.                                                                                                           |

## Variants and states

Choose this surface when the current task benefits from containing focus; use Shell.Panel for selected work alongside a queue. Both support record actions in the inner record header. The sheet defaults to 720px (`dimension.part.previewSheet`) and fits narrower screens. Keep commands concise: one small primary action and an overflow menu for additional commands.

The outer header never repeats the visible record name or holds record commands. It contains Back when provided, collection navigation or the fallback full-record link, and Close. Supplying `navigation` suppresses `openTo`; include the full-record destination in that navigation. The footer, when present, contains related links only.

_Example: story `Stories.DoDont`._

The caller controls `open` and owns dismissal, in-progress work and the related-record stack. Close and Escape dismiss the whole preview from any frame: `onClose` ends every frame, so the next open starts at the root, and focus returns to the control that opened the sheet. Back is the only way to pop one frame. It returns focus to `backFocus`, the control in the parent frame that opened the nested one; give that control a ref, which a parent frame rendered again still fills. Without `backFocus`, focus stays on Back while a deeper frame keeps one, else it goes to the parent frame's title. Keep browser history aligned when that stack is represented in the URL.

_Example: story `Stories.CompleteReview`._

## Accessibility

Base UI provides the dialog semantics, modal focus containment, Escape dismissal and focus return. By default, PreviewSheet focuses its title so users encounter the identity before the record's structured content. Back and the navigation's buttons show their names in tooltips; Close is the X every Sheet closes with and, like Sheet's own, shows none, so Escape on it closes the sheet at once. The Back arrow turns in a right-to-left provider. Use `initialFocus` for an appropriate field in a task-oriented form, and `finalFocus` when completing work removes the opener. A short supplied subtitle becomes the description; an absent subtitle creates no empty description.

The visible Close remains available in the outer header. Keep pending/unsaved-work handling in the caller, including dismissal guards where the actual workflow needs them. Navigation uses named anchors; record commands use buttons in the inner header.

Sources: [shadcn Base Sheet](https://ui.shadcn.com/docs/components/base/sheet), [implementation](https://github.com/shadcn-ui/ui/blob/main/apps/v4/registry/bases/base/ui/sheet.tsx), [Base UI Dialog](https://base-ui.com/react/components/dialog), [WAI-ARIA dialog guidance](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/dialog-modal/).

## Props

_Props of `PreviewSheet`, generated from its types:_

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `open` (required) | `boolean` |  |  |
| `onClose` (required) | `() => void` |  | Close and Escape: dismiss the whole preview, every frame, and return focus to the opener. |
| `onBack` | `(() => void)` |  | Back to the previous frame of the stack: the only control that pops one frame. |
| `backFocus` | `RefObject<HTMLElement \| null>` |  | Where Back sends focus: the control in the parent frame that opened this one, read once the parent frame shows. Without it, focus stays on Back while there is one, else goes to the parent frame's title. |
| `id` | `ReactNode` |  | The record's id, beside its status in the body metadata. |
| `title` (required) | `ReactNode` |  | The record's name in the inner record header; also names the modal. |
| `subtitle` | `ReactNode` |  | The record's meta line: kind, path, owner. |
| `status` | `ReactNode` |  | One status, beside the id. A Badge or an Indicator. |
| `facts` | `ReactNode` |  | At most three Facts under the meta line: the ones the reader acts on. |
| `links` | `ReactNode` |  | Related destination TextLinks in the footer. Do not repeat the full-record link. |
| `actions` | `ReactNode` |  | Record commands in the inner PageHeader.Actions, beside the title. Use small controls. |
| `width` | `number` |  | Pixels, 720 by default (`dimension.part.previewSheet`): about half the screen. |
| `initialFocus` | `boolean \| RefObject<HTMLElement \| null> \| ((openType: InteractionType) => boolean \| void \| HTMLElement \| null)` |  | Native focus overrides for workflows whose opener disappears or whose first task is an input. |
| `finalFocus` | `boolean \| RefObject<HTMLElement \| null> \| ((closeType: InteractionType) => boolean \| void \| HTMLElement \| null)` |  |  |
| `children` (required) | `ReactNode` |  | Focused record content, editable properties or actions. |
| `navigation` | `ReactNode \| ReactElement<unknown, string \| JSXElementConstructor<any>>` |  | Global collection navigation in the outer header, before Close. Includes the full-record link. |
| `openTo` | `PreviewSheetLink` |  | Full-record link in the outer header when navigation is absent. Empty children default to "Open the full record". |

<!-- page: Patterns/RecordBrowser (src/stories/patterns/RecordBrowser.mdx) -->

# RecordBrowser

**Status: Stable.**

Find, compare and select related records without leaving the current record. Use this for evidence, assessment objectives and other collections where a compact picker cannot show enough information to make a decision.

_Example: story `Stories.BrowseAndLink`._

## Anatomy

A Base UI Dialog occupies 90% of the viewport. Its header names the relationship task; the body is a DialogBody holding the results and the preview side by side. The optional `context` opens the results and scrolls with them; the Toolbar (search, column filters, Columns and the permanent `actions`) sits above a selectable, responsive DataTable. The results take the height the dialog leaves them: the toolbar and the pagination stay in view and the rows scroll under the table's sticky header. The eye on each row's naming cell opens the preview pane, which holds a readable code, previous and next, the way back to the results, the record's name as its heading, the complete record, and a Select checkbox. The name is a PageHeader.Title, an h3 under the dialog's h2 title, and `renderPreview` renders a level under it, so a Section in the preview is titled with an h4. The footer keeps the selection count, a polite status in the phrase PickerSheet uses ("2 of 14 selected", "2 selected" while the records load), a subtle Cancel and the linking action visible.

The caller supplies eligible records, columns, the record's name (`recordTitle` and, when that is markup or the ids are database keys, `recordLabel`), preview content and the linking callback. The pattern owns the temporary search, filters, sort, pagination, selection and preview state. Business rules and record content stay in the application.

## Names, never keys

A record's `id` keys its row and nothing else: the reader never sees it or hears it. `recordLabel` names the row's checkbox and eye ("Select Firewall ruleset export"), the preview's Select checkbox and what previous and next say; it defaults to `recordTitle` when that returns a string. `recordCode` is the readable identifier shown over the preview's name, such as EV-0412. `previewColumn` names the column that names the record: it leads the row and its cell carries the eye. Give that column `priority: 0` and a readable width (about 180 to 220px), so a narrow browser keeps it in the row and moves the other fields into each row's More fields.

_Example: story `Stories.ReadableNames`._

A `recordTitle` that returns markup gives no words to name a row by, so without `recordLabel` the checkbox, the eye and previous and next are named by the record's `id`: a screen reader hears a database key.

_Example: story `Stories.DoDont`._

## Behavior

Previewing never selects or links a record. Checkboxes select; only the footer confirms. Selection survives search, filtering, pagination and preview navigation. Clear selection resets it. By default, closing the dialog discards the selection; each opening starts a new session, and the last one stays drawn through the dialog's exit. Callers can retain selection across a related creation workflow with `selectedIds` and `onSelectionChange`. Link failures show a danger Alert and preserve selection for retry.

While confirmation is pending, Cancel, Escape, the close control and outside clicks cannot dismiss the browser: the Dialog's `pending` lock marks the browser `aria-busy` and Close and Cancel `aria-disabled`. The results are inert and `aria-busy`, and the preview's Select checkbox and Clear selection wait, so the records being linked are the ones on screen. Confirmation is serialized. If the application closes the browser itself, a late completion from that session cannot close or update a subsequently opened session.

_Example: story `Stories.PendingConfirmation`._

## Nothing to link, loading and failure

`state` says where the records are. `loading` draws skeleton rows under the toolbar; `refreshing` keeps the rows while new ones arrive; `error` shows the caller's `error`: in place of the rows when none loaded, above the rows it keeps after a failed refresh, with Try again when `onRetry` is given. With no eligible records at all, the browser says so with `empty` in place of the table: a title, one line on why and what makes a record, the caller's `actions` as its step (or `empty.action`), and an optional quieter `secondary`. The context stays above it. A search or a filter that matches nothing is not this: it is the table's own filtered state, with Clear filters.

_Example: story `Stories.NothingToLink`._

_Example: story `Stories.LoadingAndNoMatch`._

## Preview navigation

Previous and next walk every row the search and filters leave, in the table's order, across its pages: a step past the last row of a page turns the table to the next one. A polite status names the record and its place ("Verification artifact 21, 21 of 24 records"). At either end the control keeps focus and says it is unavailable. When the previewed record is outside the filtered results, both are unavailable, the status says so, and its selection remains available. Closing the preview returns focus to the eye of the record being read.

_Example: story `Stories.PreviewAcrossPages`._

## Narrow and short windows

Below the split container size (`dimension.container.split`, 50rem) the preview replaces the results while keeping the table mounted. The way back leads the preview's header as a chevron, Back to results, away from the dialog's Close; beside the results it is the X at the end of that header.

_Example: story `Stories.Phone`._

In a window under 30rem tall (a landscape phone, 400% zoom) the whole dialog scrolls as one, with the footer held at the bottom: the title and Close come back into view when it is scrolled up, the results are not squeezed behind fixed rows, and a control that takes focus scrolls clear of the footer. The preview scrolls with it.

_Example: story `Stories.ShortWindow`._

The table fits its pane: the fields that do not fit beside an open preview move into each row's More fields instead of a sideways scroll.

_Example: story `Stories.FitsItsPane`._

## Accessibility

The dialog uses the existing [shadcn Base UI composition](https://ui.shadcn.com/docs/components/base/dialog) and [Base UI focus management](https://base-ui.com/react/components/dialog). Opening a preview focuses its heading; closing it restores the eye of the record being read. Escape closes the internal preview first, then the dialog. Nested filter menus and a focused control's tooltip consume their own Escape. Closing the dialog returns focus to its opener. The preview is a region named by the record; its body is a tab stop only while it overflows with nothing focusable in it.

The words are the locale's: Search records, Back to results, Previous record, Next record, the position, the count, Clear selection, Cancel and the failure come from the LedgerProvider's messages (`recordBrowser…`, `recordPositionNamed`, `selectedCount`, `selectedCountOf`).

## Props

_Props of `RecordBrowser`, generated from its types:_

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `open` (required) | `boolean` |  |  |
| `onClose` (required) | `() => void` |  |  |
| `title` (required) | `string` |  |  |
| `description` (required) | `string` |  |  |
| `records` (required) | `readonly T[]` |  |  |
| `columns` (required) | `readonly DataTableColumn<T>[]` |  |  |
| `filters` | `readonly string[]` |  | Filterable column IDs. The table owns sorting, search, filters and selection. |
| `recordTitle` (required) | `(record: T) => ReactNode` |  | The record's name as the preview's heading: PageHeader.Title, an h3 under the dialog's title. |
| `recordLabel` | `((record: T) => string)` |  | The record's name as text, never a database key: it names the row's checkbox and eye ("Select Firewall ruleset export"), the preview's Select checkbox, and what is said as the preview steps. `recordTitle` when that returns a string unsaid, else the record's id: give it whenever `recordTitle` returns markup or the ids are keys. |
| `recordCode` | `((record: T) => ReactNode)` |  | A readable identifier over the preview's name, such as "EVD-001". Nothing unsaid; never a database key. |
| `previewColumn` | `string` |  | The column that names the record: it leads the row and its cell carries the preview eye. Give it `priority: 0` too, so a narrow browser keeps it in the row. Unsaid, the columns keep their order and the eye sits on the first column that holds a value. |
| `renderPreview` (required) | `(record: T) => ReactNode` |  | What the preview shows under the record's name. Record content stays inside this dialog; do not render another modal here. The name is an h3 under the dialog's title, and headings inside take the level under it (a Section's title is an h4). |
| `onConfirm` (required) | `(records: T[]) => void \| Promise<void>` |  |  |
| `confirmLabel` (required) | `string` |  |  |
| `context` | `ReactNode` |  | Optional context, such as the relationship target. It scrolls with the results. |
| `actions` | `ReactNode` |  | Permanent actions, such as creating a new record. The empty state offers them too. |
| `searchPlaceholder` | `string` |  | The search field's placeholder and name, what is searched: "Search evidence". "Search records" unsaid. |
| `state` | `"error" \| "loading" \| "ready" \| "refreshing"` |  | Where the records are: `loading` draws skeleton rows under the toolbar, `refreshing` keeps the rows while new ones arrive, `error` says `error`: in place of the rows when none loaded, above the rows it keeps after a failed refresh. `ready` unsaid. |
| `error` | `ReactNode` |  | What a failed load says, with `state="error"`: what went wrong and what to do. |
| `onRetry` | `(() => void)` |  | With `state="error"`, Try again in the error runs this: refetch what failed. None unsaid. |
| `empty` | `RecordBrowserEmpty` |  | With no eligible records at all (a load that is done and found none), what the browser says in place of the table, with `actions` as its step. A search or a filter that matches nothing is the table's own filtered state, with Clear filters. |
| `selectedIds` | `readonly string[]` |  | Own selection across related workflows that temporarily close the browser. |
| `onSelectionChange` | `((ids: string[]) => void)` |  | Reports selection changes. Pair with selectedIds for controlled selection. |

`records` contains eligible records with stable IDs. `columns` uses `defineColumns`; `filters` names filterable columns. `onConfirm` receives all selected records, including selections hidden by filters or pagination; it may return a promise. `confirmLabel` names the action. `searchPlaceholder` names what is searched. `context` is optional relationship context; `actions` holds permanent controls such as Create evidence artifact.

`selectedIds` and `onSelectionChange` optionally let the caller own selection. This supports a sequential create flow that closes the browser temporarily and returns with the earlier selections intact. The caller decides when to clear its controlled selection. The default behavior is unchanged when these props are omitted.

_Example: story `Stories.RetainedSelection`._

## Related

Use RecordPicker for quick single-record selection. PickerSheet is for allocation workflows with extra relationship fields. RecordBrowser is the comparison and bulk-linking experience; it composes Dialog, Toolbar and DataTable. [Upgrading](?path=/docs/guidance-upgrading--docs#pickersheet-and-recordbrowser) gives the one count phrase both share.

_Example: story `Stories.FailedLink`._

<!-- page: Patterns/RecordPicker (src/stories/patterns/RecordPicker.mdx) -->

# RecordPicker

**Status: Stable.**

Pick one record from a list: evidence to link, a requirement to derive from, a person to assign. A [Command](?path=/docs/components-command--docs) dialog whose rows are the code, the name with its meta under it and one badge at the end, with the count of matches in the field and the keys in the footer. Presentational: the caller supplies the records and gets the chosen one back, and the picker closes itself. For choosing many by attribute, the [PickerSheet](?path=/docs/patterns-pickersheet--docs); for choosing by name inside a form, a [Combobox](?path=/docs/components-combobox--docs).

_Example: story `Stories.RecordPickerStory`._

## Anatomy

| Part   | What it is                                                                                        |
| ------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Field  | The search, focused on open, with the count of matches at its end, which describes it.            |
| Error  | `error`, a danger Alert above the rows, with Try again when `onRetry` is given.                   |
| Row    | The `code` (the `id` unsaid) in `color.text.subtle`; the name, the meta line under it; one badge. |
| Empty  | `empty` when there are no records at all; `emptyHint` when the query finds none.                  |
| Footer | The keys: the arrows to move, Enter to choose, Escape to close.                                   |

_Example: story `Stories.RecordPickerMatrix`._

## Variants

RecordPicker has one appearance. What varies is the record: with a badge for its state or freshness, without; with a meta line, without; with keywords that match the query and are never shown. A record whose `id` is a database key carries a `code`, the identifier a person reads, and the key never reaches the screen.

Not built, and why: picking several with checkboxes, because many are chosen by attribute in a PickerSheet; a "create new" row, because a record is created on its own page; groups by kind, because the records offered are one kind and the caller narrows them; a preview of the chosen record, because the row says enough to choose and the link on the record after says the rest.

## Sizes

One: the Command dialog at its large width, 640px, the list at most 46% of the viewport's height so the field and the footer stay in view. The code is bounded to 40% of the row, so a long identifier truncates, with its whole text as the title, before the name does; the name takes the rest of the row, and a cut name or meta line shows whole on hover.

_Example: story `Stories.LongNames`._

## States

| State      | What changes                                                                                                 |
| ---------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Closed     | Not rendered.                                                                                                |
| Open       | Over the page at the top, the field focused, every record listed.                                            |
| Filtered   | The rows that match, the count in the field.                                                                 |
| No match   | `emptyHint`, "Nothing matches" unsaid.                                                                       |
| No records | `empty`, "Nothing to choose from" unsaid.                                                                    |
| Loading    | `loading`: Searching… under any rows listed; the picker never says nothing matched.                          |
| Failed     | `error` above the rows, said at once, with Try again when `onRetry` is given; with nothing listed, no count. |
| Chosen     | The picker closes, focus goes back to the opener, and the caller has the record.                             |

_Example: story `Stories.States`._

## Modifiers

- **`records`**: id, code, title, meta, badge, keywords.
- **`title`**, **`placeholder`**, **`description`**, **`empty`**, **`emptyHint`** as in Content.
- **`loading`**, **`error`** and **`onRetry`** for records that arrive from a request.

## Content

- **The title is the task**: "Link evidence", "Assign to", "Derive from".
- **The placeholder says what to type**: "Search evidence…", "Search people…". Not "Search…".
- **The meta is kind, source, date** in a few words: "Evidence · 12 Aug 2026".
- **One badge**, the state or the freshness the choice turns on: Fresh, Stale, Draft.
- **Keywords are for matching**, never shown: "dr disaster recovery" under "Backup restore drill".
- **The description says what the picker finds**: "Find a record by its name or its identifier." unsaid.
- **The two empties differ**: `empty` says there is nothing to choose and what makes something; `emptyHint` says the query missed and what to try.

## Style

| Element | Token                                                                                                        |
| ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Dialog  | CommandDialog: `radius.xxlarge` · `elevation.surface.overlay` · `elevation.shadow.overlay` · `color.blanket` |
| Row     | CommandItem, as tall as two lines · `space.100` block · `color.background.selected` when selected            |
| Id      | Id · `color.text.subtle`                                                                                     |
| Meta    | `font.body.xsmall` · `color.text.subtle`                                                                     |
| Badge   | Badge, xsmall                                                                                                |
| Footer  | CommandFooter: `elevation.surface.sunken` · `font.body.xsmall` · Kbd for each key                            |

## Accessibility

- **A dialog named by the title and described by `description`**; focus moves to the field on open, which is the dialog's first control, and returns to the opener on close, by Escape, by Enter on a record and by a click. Never `autoFocus` the field: it becomes where focus returns.
- **The list is a listbox** and each row an option named by its text: the code (or the id), the name, the meta and the badge, so "EV-0412 Firewall ruleset export Evidence 12 Aug 2026 Fresh". With a `code`, a database key never reaches the name.
- **The arrows move, Enter chooses, Escape closes**, and the footer says so with Kbd, each key named in full for a screen reader.
- **The count of matches is text** in the field's hint, which describes the field, and it is said once the query holds still. A failure is said at once.

## Props

_Props of `RecordPicker`, generated from its types:_

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `open` (required) | `boolean` |  |  |
| `onClose` (required) | `() => void` |  |  |
| `onPick` (required) | `(record: PickerRecord) => void` |  | The chosen record. The picker closes itself after. |
| `records` (required) | `PickerRecord[]` |  | The records on offer, already narrowed by the caller to the ones that may be picked. |
| `title` (required) | `string` |  | The dialog's name, the task: "Link evidence", "Assign to". |
| `placeholder` (required) | `string` |  | The field's placeholder, what the reader types: "Search evidence…". |
| `description` | `string` |  | Read after the title as the picker opens. "Find a record by its name or its identifier." unsaid. |
| `emptyHint` | `string` |  | What to say when the query matches nothing. "Nothing matches" unsaid. |
| `empty` | `string` |  | What to say when there are no records at all, before any query. "Nothing to choose from" unsaid. |
| `loading` | `boolean` | `false` | Records still arriving: the ones listed stay usable with Searching… under them, and the picker never says nothing matched while they load. |
| `error` | `ReactNode` |  | The records could not load: `true` for the default words, or the words to show. Above any records listed, with Try again when `onRetry` is given. |
| `onRetry` | `(() => void)` |  | Loads the records again. Focus returns to the field. |

## Related

- [Command](?path=/docs/components-command--docs): the dialog and the list.
- [PickerSheet](?path=/docs/patterns-pickersheet--docs): choosing many by attribute.
- [CommandPalette](?path=/docs/patterns-commandpalette--docs): the same CommandDialog, running a command instead of picking a record.
- [Combobox](?path=/docs/components-combobox--docs): one by name, inside a form.

## Don't

A row is the id, the name, a line of meta and one badge, and the placeholder says what to type, never a paragraph and three badges a row, or Search….

_Example: story `Stories.Dont`._

# Related

**Status: Stable.**

A card of linked records, in a rail or in the body of a page. Its header is the kind of record, a Count and the way to add one. Its body is a row per record in a rail, or a card per record on a page: the name as the link, a mark, one status, the properties the reader decides by, and the actions that show on hover. Its footer is "See all" when it shows a handful of many. When nothing is linked it is a proper [Empty](?path=/docs/components-empty--docs), the mark, a statement and the way to fill it, never a line of grey text.

On the body of a page: a header with the kind and "+ Add", a card per related record with its name as the link and up to six properties, the actions in a menu that shows on hover, "view all" at the bottom. In the rail, one row per record. A card is metadata with actions on hover, and a card that carries actions of its own cannot be one click target. So the title is the link and the actions are stops of their own, in both layouts.

_Example: story `Stories.RelatedMatrix`._

## Anatomy

The header and the footer are the card's; the rows are [Item](?path=/docs/components-item--docs)s; the cards are `Related.Card`.

| Part              | What it is                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| ----------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Title             | The kind of record, a noun, a heading in `font.body` semibold at the contextual level (an h3 when nothing sets one): "Linked findings", "Systems", "Team". A long one wraps.                                                |
| Count             | After the title: how many are linked.                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| Action            | At the end of the header's line: one small button, "Add" or "Link" with a plus, or a TextLink. The way to add one; it stays when the card is empty.                                                                         |
| Row (`list`)      | An Item, flush: a mark or an id, the name as the link, and the state or the date at the end. The hairlines and the hover fill span the card; the text sits at its inset.                                                    |
| Card (`cards`)    | A `Related.Card` in a grid: the mark, the name as the link, the status and the meta under it, the properties, the actions at the top end, a line of its own under.                                                          |
| Card · Leading    | The mark before the name, 32px, spanning the name and the meta line: a medium Avatar, square for a thing, round for a person.                                                                                               |
| Card · Title      | The record's name, `font.body` medium, one line; a name that is cut shows in full on hover and on keyboard focus. With `link`, the link, underlined on hover.                                                               |
| Card · Meta       | Under the name, `font.body.small` subtle: kind, path, owner.                                                                                                                                                                |
| Card · Status     | One Badge or Indicator at the start of the meta line.                                                                                                                                                                       |
| Card · Properties | Label and value pairs under the head, KeyValue rows with a 96px label: four fit, six is the most.                                                                                                                           |
| Card · Actions    | Icon buttons at the top end, their space kept so nothing shifts: open in a new tab, a menu with the rest. Hidden until the card is hovered or focused, always shown on a touch screen, kept shown while their menu is open. |
| Card · Children   | A line of its own under the properties: a row of Badges, a sentence.                                                                                                                                                        |
| Footer            | Under the rows or the cards, after a rule: "See all 14" as a TextLink.                                                                                                                                                      |
| Empty             | Where the rows would be: a compact Empty with a link icon, the title, a line and an action, from `empty`.                                                                                                                   |

## Variants

| Layout          | Use                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| --------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `list`          | A rail beside a record: one Item row per record, compact. What a row can carry at 270px is an id, a name and one thing at the end.                                                              |
| `cards`         | The body of a page: a grid of cards, as many across as fit at 240px each, sharing the row's width. A card carries the mark, the name, the status and the meta, four properties and the actions. |
| A related table | When the records need columns to compare: a Table in a [Card](?path=/docs/components-card--docs), headed by CardHeader. Not a Related; it is a section of the page.                             |

_Example: story `Stories.RelatedTable`._

Not built, and why: the whole card as the link, because a card that carries its own actions cannot be one click target and the actions are here; a card that scrolls, because a rail shows a handful and the footer says See all; search, sort and filters in the header, because a card long enough to need them is the record's tab, where the Table has them; a card that folds, because a handful of rows has nothing to fold; drag to reorder, because links have no order of their own.

## Sizes

| Size      | Row                             | Where                                           |
| --------- | ------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------- |
| `compact` | 28px for one line, the default. | The rail beside a record's overview.            |
| `default` | 36px for one line.              | A list beside a page's body, in a wider column. |

The size is the list's; every row in one card is the same height. A card in the grid is at least 240px wide and as many share a row as fit; it is as tall as its properties, and four properties keep a row of cards one height. The inset is `space.150` in a card, `space.200` in the header.

## States

| State           | What changes                                                                                                                       |
| --------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Hover on a card | `elevation.shadow.raised` under it; the actions appear; the name underlines under the pointer.                                     |
| Focus in a card | The actions appear while anything in the card has focus, so a keyboard reaches them; the focus ring is on the name or the button.  |
| Touch           | The actions are always shown where any pointer is coarse (a phone, a tablet, a touch laptop too); there is nothing to reveal them. |
| A menu open     | The actions stay shown while the card's menu is open, after the pointer and the focus have left the card.                          |
| Hover on a row  | The Item's: `color.background.neutral.subtle.hovered` across the row.                                                              |
| Empty           | The compact Empty where the rows would be; the header and its action stay.                                                         |

## Modifiers

- **`title`**, **`count`**, **`action`**, **`footer`**, **`layout`**, **`size`**, **`empty`** as in Anatomy. **`countMax`** is the count's cap, Count's `max`: 99 unsaid, `9999` for a count of rows. `empty` is a string, the Empty's title, or the Empty's title, description, action and icon. Without it the title is the locale's `relatedEmpty`, "Nothing linked yet" in en-US, so a LedgerProvider translates it. Children that render nothing (empty arrays, `false`, empty fragments) are nothing linked.
- **The rows** take the Item's props: `id`, `leading`, `title`, `meta`, `trailing`, `link` or `onSelect`.
- **The cards** take **`leading`**, **`title`**, **`link`**, **`meta`**, **`status`**, **`properties`**, **`actions`** and children.

## Content

- **The title is a noun**, the kind of record: "Linked findings", "Systems", "Team". Never a sentence.
- **A row is an id and a name**, and one thing more: the state as a word, or the date, at the end. A rail is too narrow for meta beside the name; a role beside a person's name is as much as fits. In a preview, where the rows are of more than one kind (the subsystems and components a system contains), the one thing is the row's kind as its `meta`, and nothing trails: a summary of what is inside, not a collection to count or work through.
- **A card is the name, the meta, one status and four properties**: the ones the reader decides by. Six is the most; past that the record has them.
- **The actions are what is done to the link**, not to the record: open in a new tab, edit the link, unlink. Never "Open"; the name is that. Unlink is the menu's last item, in danger.
- **A handful, then See all.** Five rows in a rail, a row of cards on a page; the footer says how many there are, and the record's tab lists them.
- **The empty state says what would be here and how to fill it**: "Nothing linked yet", "Not in a package yet", with the line and a link button. The header's action stays, so the way to add one is there twice at most, never nowhere.
- **People are neutral.** A round Avatar and the name; colour is for state.

## Style

| Element    | Token                                                                                                                                                                |
| ---------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Card frame | Card: `radius.large` · `color.border` · `elevation.surface.raised`                                                                                                   |
| Header     | `font.body` semibold · `color.text` · Count · `space.200` inline · `space.100` block · `color.border` rule under                                                     |
| Rows       | Item, `compact`, flush: `space.050` block · `space.200` inline · `color.border` hairlines across the card · `space.050` above and below the list                     |
| Grid       | `space.200` inset · `space.150` between cards · columns of at least 240px, as many as fit, sharing the width                                                         |
| Card       | `radius.large` · `color.border` · `elevation.surface.raised` · `space.150` inset · `space.100` between the head and the properties · hover `elevation.shadow.raised` |
| Card name  | `font.body` medium · `color.text` · underline on hover                                                                                                               |
| Card meta  | `font.body.small` · `color.text.subtle`                                                                                                                              |
| Properties | KeyValue, label 96px · `space.025` between                                                                                                                           |
| Actions    | IconButton, subtle, small · opacity 0 to 1 in `motion.duration.fast` · `space.025` between                                                                           |
| Footer     | `font.body.small` · `color.border` rule above · `space.200` inline · `space.100` block                                                                               |
| Empty      | Empty, compact · `space.200` inline · `space.150` block                                                                                                              |

## Accessibility

- **The heading takes the contextual level**: an h3 when nothing sets one, one below a titled Section, an h2 in a rail that starts its outline at 2 (`HeadingLevelProvider level={2}`). The rows or the cards are a list named by it: a screen reader hears "Systems, list, 3 items".
- **The name is the link**, in a row and in a card, named by the record's name alone; the id, the status, the meta and the properties are read as the text beside it, and a row's id and meta are its link's description. A row's link is stretched over the row, with its focus ring drawn inside the card's edge; a card's is the name, because the card has actions of its own, and where any pointer is coarse the name takes a hit area at least 24px tall.
- **The actions are always in the tab order.** They are hidden by opacity, not removed, and they show while any of them has focus; a keyboard reader reaches "Open Ground segment in a new tab" and "More for Ground segment" after the name. On a touch screen they are always shown.
- **Each action is a labelled icon button** that names the record: "Unlink" alone would be six identical buttons on a page of cards.
- **The count is text**, read after the title; the footer's link says how many.
- **The empty state is text, then the action**: the icon is hidden, the title and the line are read first, the button is a stop after them.
- **The hover shadow is decoration.** Nothing is said by it.

_Example: story `Stories.HeadingLevelAndSurface`._

_Example: story `Stories.ActionsWhileAMenuIsOpen`._

_Example: story `Stories.NothingLinked`._

_Example: story `Stories.LongNames`._

A Related.Card paints the raised surface and records it as the current one, as Card does, so a child that matches its surface with `bg-surface-current` (a sticky header, a fade at an edge) paints the card's colour rather than the page's.

## Props

_Props of `Related`, generated from its types:_

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `title` (required) | `ReactNode` |  | The kind of record linked, a noun: "Linked findings", "Systems", "Team". A heading at the contextual level, an h3 outside every HeadingLevelProvider; a long one wraps. |
| `count` | `number` |  | A Count after the title: how many are linked. |
| `countMax` | `number` |  | The most `count` shows before it reads as `max+`, as Count's `max`: `9999` for a count of rows. 99 unsaid. |
| `action` | `ReactNode` |  | At the end of the heading's line: one small button ("Link", "Add") or a TextLink. |
| `footer` | `ReactNode` |  | Under the rows, after a rule: "See all 14" as a TextLink when the card shows a handful of many. |
| `layout` | `"cards" \| "list"` |  | `list`: an Item row per record, for a rail. `cards`: a grid of Related.Card, for the body of a page. |
| `size` | `"compact" \| "default"` |  | The list's row height, `compact` by default; `default` beside a page's body. |
| `empty` | `RelatedEmpty` |  | What to show when nothing is linked, drawn as a compact Empty with a link icon: the locale's `relatedEmpty`, "Nothing linked yet" in en-US, by default. |
| `children` | `ReactNode` |  | Item rows in the list layout; Related.Card in the cards layout. |

### Related.Card

Also exported by name as `RelatedCard`, with `RelatedCardProps`, `RelatedEmpty` and `RelatedLayout`. A card's title link composes the supplied link's native props and ref through Base UI: leave the link empty to show the card's title, or give it children to say something else.

_Props of `Related.Card`, generated from its types:_

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `leading` | `ReactNode` |  | The mark before the title, 32px: a medium Avatar, square for a thing and round for a person. It spans the title and the meta line. |
| `title` (required) | `ReactNode` |  | The record's name, one line. With `link`, it is the link. A name that is cut shows in full in a tooltip on hover and on keyboard focus of the link. |
| `link` | `ReactElement<{ className?: string; children?: ReactNode; }, string \| JSXElementConstructor<any>>` |  | A link element (a router's Link) that becomes the title. Leave it empty to use title; supplied children override the link text. |
| `meta` | `ReactNode` |  | Under the title, subtle: kind, path, owner. |
| `status` | `ReactNode` |  | One status at the start of the meta line: a Badge or an Indicator. |
| `properties` | `{ label: string; value: ReactNode; }[]` |  | Label and value pairs under the head: the properties the reader decides by. Four fit; six is the most. |
| `actions` | `ReactNode` |  | Icon buttons at the top end, shown on hover, on focus and always on a touch screen, their space kept so nothing shifts: open in a new tab, unlink, more. Never the way to the record; the title is. |
| `children` | `ReactNode` |  | A line under the properties: a row of Badges, a sentence. |
