<!-- page: Patterns/SearchDialog (src/stories/patterns/SearchDialog.mdx) -->

# SearchDialog

**Status: Stable.**

The product's search: find a record of any type by its name or its identifier and open it. A dialog over the page, a field at the top, the results under their record type, each row the identifier, the name with a line of meta under it and one status at the end, and the keys in the footer. It opens from the top nav's [TopNav.Search](?path=/docs/layout-shell--docs) or ⌘K (Ctrl+K elsewhere). It finds a record; it does not run a command, which is the [CommandPalette](?path=/docs/patterns-commandpalette--docs), and it does not pick a record for a field or a link, which is the [RecordPicker](?path=/docs/patterns-recordpicker--docs) (one record from one kind) or a [Combobox](?path=/docs/components-combobox--docs) (by name, inside a form). A search that narrows one register is that register's [Toolbar](?path=/docs/patterns-toolbar--docs) search.

_Example: story `Stories.SearchDialogStory`._

## Anatomy

| Part    | What it is                                                                                                                                                              |
| ------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Field   | Focused on open; the placeholder says what to type. A spinner at its end while a search runs.                                                                           |
| Heading | The record type over its rows: `group` on the results. Consecutive results with the same group share one.                                                               |
| Row     | `identifier` in `color.text.subtle`, the `title` with its `meta` under it, both wrapping, and one `badge`. An unavailable row adds its `disabledReason` under the meta. |
| Message | Before a query, the prompt; while a search with no results yet runs, Searching…; after one, No results for.                                                             |
| Failure | An Alert above any results, with Try again when `onRetry` is given.                                                                                                     |
| Footer  | The keys: the arrows to move, Enter to open, Escape to close (a button, for touch); the count at the end.                                                               |

## Two ways to search

**The dialog matches.** Hand over every record in `results`; the dialog shows the ones whose title, identifier, meta, group or keywords contain every word of the query, ignoring case and accents. The `id` is never matched and never shown, so a UUID there cannot make a short query match everything (the Matching story: "de" finds a name and a meta, not an id). Pass `filter` for another rule.

**The caller searches.** Pass `filter={null}`, own the `query` with `onQueryChange`, and hand over each query's results with `loading` while they come. Set `loading` in `onQueryChange`, in the same update as the query, and debounce only the request: a query shown before `loading` is set, with no results yet, reads as No results. Results already listed stay usable while the next ones load (the Remote search story checks both).

_Example: story `Stories.RemoteSearch`._

## States

| State       | What shows                                                                                                          |
| ----------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Before      | `initialResults` (recent or suggested records) under their own heading, else the `prompt`.                          |
| Results     | The rows, the first highlighted so Enter opens the best match; the count in the footer.                             |
| Searching   | With results listed, they stay and the list is busy. With none, Searching…, never No results.                       |
| No results  | No results for “…” and a hint, or `noResults`. A different state from a search in flight.                           |
| Failed      | `error` above the rows (`true` for the default words), with Try again; the rows already listed stay.                |
| Unavailable | A row with `disabledReason` (or `disabled`) stays listed and the arrows reach it; it says why and cannot be chosen. |
| Chosen      | The dialog closes, then `onSelect` runs with the result, so a navigation or a dialog it opens does not stack.       |

_Example: story `Stories.NoResults`._
_Example: story `Stories.Failure`._
_Example: story `Stories.BeforeAQuery`._
_Example: story `Stories.UnavailableRecord`._

## Content

- **The placeholder names what is searched**: "Search programs, risks and controls". The default, "Type a name or an identifier", is for a product with one kind of record.
- **The identifier is the one people use**: PRG-014, AC-2. A UUID goes in `id`, which is never shown.
- **The meta is the type and one fact** in a few words: "Risk · High", "Program · Sarah Chen". Put the type there when the heading does not say it.
- **One badge**, the status the choice turns on.
- **Keywords are for matching**: other names, codes, tags. They are never shown.

## Accessibility

- **A modal dialog named by `title`**, "Search" by default, with the `description` read after it. Focus moves to the field on open and returns to the opener on close, or to `finalFocus`.
- **Base UI's Autocomplete, inline.** The field is a combobox that controls a listbox; the arrows move through the rows across the headings, Enter opens the highlighted row, and Escape closes the dialog. Home and End move the caret in the field.
- **The active descendant follows the highlight.** The field's `aria-activedescendant` names the highlighted row on open, after every keystroke and after each arrow, so a screen reader always hears the row Enter will open. The first row is highlighted as results arrive.
- **The count is spoken.** Once the results hold still for 600ms, the page's [Announcer](?path=/docs/components-announcer--docs) says "12 results", or the no-results sentence; a failure is said at once, assertively. Shell mounts the Announcer; the dialog works without one.
- **Headings are groups.** Each heading labels its rows, so a screen reader hears "Risks, group" before a risk.
- **Retry is described by the failure** and returns focus to the field, so the next keystroke searches.
- **An unavailable row is reached, not skipped.** It is `aria-disabled`, its `disabledReason` is its description (not part of its name), and Enter or a press does nothing, as a DropdownMenuItem with a `disabledReason` behaves.
- **One ⌘K per page.** TopNav.Search binds ⌘K (Ctrl+K elsewhere) by default, and so does `useCommandPalette`. A page with both gives one of them another `shortcut`, or `shortcut={null}`, so one key does not open two dialogs.
- **The field shows its focus.** Its row draws the field's focus ring while the field has focus. The dialog sits 80px from the top, or a tenth of the window's height where that is less, so a landscape phone keeps room for the results.
- **The highlighted row keeps its mark in forced colours**: it is Highlight with HighlightText inside, and an unavailable row GrayText. Names and meta wrap inside the row; nothing is cut off.

## Props

_Props of `SearchDialog`, generated from its types:_

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `open` (required) | `boolean` |  | Whether the dialog is open. TopNav.Search's `onOpen` opens it. |
| `onOpenChange` (required) | `(open: boolean) => void` |  | Called with `false` on Escape, a press outside, the footer's close and after a choice. |
| `results` (required) | `SearchResult[]` |  | The records to search, which the dialog matches against the query; with `filter={null}`, the results of the caller's own search for `query`. |
| `onSelect` (required) | `(result: SearchResult) => void` |  | The chosen record. The dialog closes first, then this runs, so a navigation or a dialog it opens does not stack on the search. |
| `initialResults` | `SearchResult[]` |  | What the dialog lists before anything is typed: recent or suggested records. Without them it shows the prompt. |
| `query` | `string` |  | The query, controlled. Pair it with `onQueryChange`; a remote search runs from here. |
| `defaultQuery` | `string` |  | The query on open, uncontrolled. The query empties when the dialog has closed. |
| `onQueryChange` | `((query: string) => void)` |  | Every change to the query, as typed. Debounce a remote search here. |
| `filter` | `((result: SearchResult, query: string) => boolean) \| null` |  | Which results match the query. By default every word of the query must appear, ignoring case and accents, in the title, the identifier, the meta, the group or the keywords (never the id). `null` matches nothing itself: `results` are already the caller's results for the query. |
| `loading` | `boolean` | `false` | A search in flight. Results already listed stay usable; with none, the dialog says it is searching instead of saying nothing matched. |
| `error` | `ReactNode` |  | The search failed: `true` for the default message, or the words to show. It shows above any results already listed, with Retry when `onRetry` is given. |
| `onRetry` | `(() => void)` |  | Runs the search again. Focus returns to the field. |
| `title` | `string` |  | The dialog's name and the field's, "Search" by default. |
| `description` | `string` |  | Read after the name when the dialog opens. "Find a record by its name or its identifier." by default. |
| `placeholder` | `string` |  | What to type, in the field: "Search programs, risks and findings". "Type a name or an identifier" by default. |
| `prompt` | `ReactNode` |  | What the dialog says before anything is typed, when there are no `initialResults`. The description by default. |
| `noResults` | `ReactNode` |  | What the dialog says when the query finds nothing. By default "No results for “…”" and a hint. |
| `finalFocus` | `boolean \| RefObject<HTMLElement \| null> \| ((closeType: InteractionType) => boolean \| void \| HTMLElement \| null)` |  | Where focus goes when the dialog closes: the element that opened it by default. |
| `className` | `string` |  | On the dialog's surface, for its width. @accepts layout |
| `style` | `CSSProperties` |  | On the dialog's surface. The width is 640px at most by default. |
| `ref` | `Ref<HTMLDivElement>` |  | The dialog's surface. |

A result is `{ id, title, identifier?, meta?, badge?, group?, keywords?, disabled?, disabledReason? }`: `id` is identity only, `title` is the name, and the rest are described above.

_Example: story `Stories.Playground`._

## Related

- [Shell](?path=/docs/layout-shell--docs): TopNav.Search, the button and the shortcut that open this dialog.
- [CommandPalette](?path=/docs/patterns-commandpalette--docs): the same kind of dialog for running a command.
- [RecordPicker](?path=/docs/patterns-recordpicker--docs): picking one record of one kind for a link or a field.
- [Announcer](?path=/docs/components-announcer--docs): where the count is spoken.

## Don't

Records are found in a SearchDialog, each its identifier, its name, a line of meta and one status, never as commands in the CommandPalette.

_Example: story `Stories.Dont`._

<!-- page: Patterns/TaskRow (src/stories/patterns/TaskRow.mdx) -->

# TaskRow

**Status: Experimental.** No product screen uses a TaskRow, so its API can still change before it is stable; owner: Ledger maintainers.

A shared completion row for checklists and work queues. The package owns the completion control, row layout and independent navigation/actions. The application owns its task model, status vocabulary, deadlines and persistence. Consumers own the state mappings.

_Example: story `Stories.TaskRowMatrix`._

## Anatomy

A completion checkbox, text title, optional contextual meta, and trailing owner/date/status content. Actions and title navigation are separate interactive targets. TaskRow renders a list item: place it inside Item.Group for list headings, aligned columns and empty content.

## Variants

The same presentation supports interactive completion or a row without a completion control. Omitting `onCompletedChange` removes that control. Status is caller-rendered content; the package has no waiting/blocked enum.

## Sizes

Inherits the surrounding Item.Group's default or compact density. There is no second independent row-size scale. The title truncates within the row; dense metadata should be kept concise in narrow layouts.

## States

`completed` is caller-owned and strikes through the title. `onCompletedChange` requests the next boolean; it does not persist or optimistically change the row. Use `completionDisabled` while the application is saving and explain that state in `status`. Read-only rows can still navigate or expose separate actions.

_Example: story `Stories.Completion`._

## Modifiers

`assignee`, `due`, `status`, `meta` and `actions` are content slots. `dueDateTime` adds a semantic time element around due content. Without it, relative words remain plain content. The caller computes overdue status and supplies the corresponding styling. `link` or `onSelect` makes the title interactive; choose one. Completion and action controls remain siblings of the title control.

## Content

Use a short action as the title, such as “Review draft.” Supply formatted date content and a machine-readable date where possible. The checkbox is named for the task, the title by default; `completionLabel` replaces that name when the title alone is ambiguous, and it stays the same as the row is completed and reopened. Keep status wording and owner identity in the application.

## Style

Item supplies the shared row grid and interactive hit areas. Checkbox supplies focus and checked styling. Completed titles use subtle text and a line-through; due content retains tabular numerals. The product supplies any semantic status or deadline tone.

## Accessibility

Completion is a controlled checkbox with Space-key operation, named for the task (“Review draft, checkbox, checked”): the name stays the same and the checked state says whether it is done. Completing a task does not activate its row navigation. Title and action buttons are independent keyboard stops, without nested interactive elements. Completed rows without a checkbox are read with the locale’s `taskRowCompleted` (`{title}, completed`) or `completedLabel`, so the strike-through is not the only completion cue.

## Props

_Props of `TaskRow`, generated from its types:_

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `link` | `ReactElement<{ id?: string; className?: string; children?: ReactNode; }, string \| JSXElementConstructor<any>> \| undefined` |  | A link element (a router's Link) that becomes the row's title and stretches over the row. |
| `meta` | `ReactNode` |  | Inline after the title, muted: the kind, the size, the state as a word. It keeps its words while the title gives way, and is cut, with its reveal, only past half the line. |
| `onSelect` | `(() => void)` |  | Makes the title a button that stretches over the row. |
| `actions` | `ReactNode` |  | Buttons at the end of the row, beside the row's link or button, never inside it. |
| `title` (required) | `string` |  | The action to complete. Plain text also provides the default checkbox name. |
| `completed` | `boolean` | `false` | Caller-owned completion, independent of the product's status vocabulary. |
| `onCompletedChange` | `((completed: boolean) => void)` |  | Requests completion or reopening. Omit for a row without a completion control. |
| `completionLabel` | `string` |  | The completion checkbox's accessible name, the title by default. It names the task, not the next action, so it stays the same as the row is completed and reopened; the checked state says which. |
| `completedLabel` | `string` |  | What a screen reader hears for a completed row without a checkbox, so the strike-through is not the only cue: a sentence with `{title}` where the title goes, the locale's "{title}, completed" by default. Words without `{title}` ("Done") are said after the title. |
| `completionDisabled` | `boolean` | `false` | Disables only the completion control, for example while the caller persists a change. |
| `assignee` | `ReactNode` |  | Rendered owner content, such as Person or Avatar; no person data model is imposed. |
| `due` | `ReactNode` |  | Rendered due-date content. The caller decides wording, formatting and overdue styling. |
| `dueDateTime` | `string` |  | Machine-readable timestamp for due; without it, due is plain content rather than a time element. |
| `status` | `ReactNode` |  | Caller-rendered status, such as a Badge. No waiting/blocked state taxonomy is built in. |

_Example: story `Stories.Playground`._
_Rendered in the Storybook: Controls._

## Related

- [Item](?path=/docs/components-item--docs) for general rows and groups.
- [Checkbox](?path=/docs/components-checkbox--docs) for independent boolean input.
- [Badge](?path=/docs/components-badge--docs) for caller-owned status content.
- A product maps its own task states, owner names and overdue presentation onto `completed`, `assignee`, `due` and `status`; create-task workflows stay in the product.

## Don't

The status is your product's words, given as content, and completion a separate boolean, never a storage code on screen or every field packed into the title.

_Example: story `Stories.Dont`._

<!-- page: Patterns/Toolbar (src/stories/patterns/Toolbar.mdx) -->

# Toolbar

**Status: Stable.**

The row above a table: search first, saved views next, filters after them, and display controls and actions at the end. Everything in it is the small size, so the row is one height and the table starts right under it. A [DataTable](?path=/docs/patterns-data-table--docs) takes it as `toolbar`, above its frameless rows; a plain [Table](?path=/docs/components-table--docs) puts it above, `space.200` apart as the DataTable does, so the table's sticky header never covers the ring of a focused control in the row.

It is a row of controls, not a heading. A standalone register has a PageHeader; an embedded register can use a Section. Toolbar contains controls only.

_Example: story `Stories.ToolbarMatrix`._

## Anatomy

| Part    | What it is                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Search  | A small [SearchField](?path=/docs/components-searchfield--docs), up to 240px (`dimension.part.search`), named by its placeholder, with a clear button while it holds a query. Only with `onSearch`.                             |
| Views   | `views`, after search: saved-view controls that never fold into More; a strip wider than its space scrolls inside it, arrows at the edges where a pointer can hover.                                                            |
| Filters | `filters`, after saved views: [FilterChips](?path=/docs/components-filterchip--docs), a [ToggleGroup](?path=/docs/components-togglegroup--docs) of lenses, a small Select that narrows.                                         |
| Display | `children`, before the actions: Columns, Settings, a grouping Select, an overflow of collection commands. They fold into More after the filters.                                                                                |
| More    | The one overflow: a small Button, "More", that appears only when something has folded. Its popover holds the filters, then the display controls under a divider. With `activeFilters`, it counts the folded filters that apply. |
| Actions | `actions`, pushed to the end: small Buttons with the primary last, or a count as text, "12 of 340 controls". They never fold.                                                                                                   |

## Variants

Toolbar has one appearance. What varies is which parts the register needs:

| The register                       | Use                                                                                                                                |
| ---------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Searched, filtered, acted on       | Search, chips, actions.                                                                                                            |
| Seen through lenses                | No search; a ToggleGroup in `filters`, a count at the end.                                                                         |
| One thing to choose about the view | A small Select in `children`.                                                                                                      |
| A yes or no about the rows         | A [FilterChip](?path=/docs/components-filterchip--docs) toggle (`isActive`) in `filters`.                                          |
| Which rows there are to ask about  | A small Select in `views`: a revision, an edition or a scope. It never folds, because it changes what every other control acts on. |
| Only a count or an Export          | `actions` alone.                                                                                                                   |
| Rows chosen for a batch action     | Not a Toolbar: the DataTable's SelectionBar takes the Toolbar's place in the table's `toolbar` slot while rows are chosen.         |

There is no title in a Toolbar, no tall Toolbar (the kit's rows are one height and so is the row above them), and no collapsed search that opens from an icon: a register that is searched shows its field.

## Sizes

One height: every control in the row is small, `dimension.control.small` 28px, so a Button and a SelectTrigger in it say `size="small"`. The caller owns surrounding spacing.

The toolbar measures its container, not the window, so it responds the same in a panel as on a phone. When the row cannot hold everything it folds instead of stacking. `filters` move into More first; if the row still cannot hold the display controls (`children`), they follow, under a divider, and each still opens its own menu from inside More. A choice that closes a menu opened there closes More with it, as a parent menu would; a toggle, a submenu, or an item that keeps its menu open keeps More open. The search, the saved views and `actions` never fold, and the primary keeps its whole label.

When search, views, More and the actions still cannot share one row, the row wraps into two in the same order: the search with the saved views, then More with the actions at the end. Every register takes the same two rows at a given width, a views menu keeps its label, count and chevron, and the primary keeps its whole label. The toolbar stays at two rows while More and the primary fit side by side; narrower than that, as in a panel at its minimum width, the actions take a line of their own under More, still at the end, and nothing overlaps. The search gives up room first, down to 128px; below that, the saved views take what is left: a views menu shortens its label with an ellipsis, its full label in its title, and keeps its count and chevron, and a strip of several views scrolls. A toolbar without a search stays one row, and actions that do not fit wrap inside their group, labels whole: another reason to keep to five. While More is open it keeps what it holds, even if its container widens; the row takes everything back when it closes. A filter the reader changes inside More is measured again as More closes, so a label that shrank there lets the filters back into the row when they now fit.

_Example: story `Stories.Live`._
_Example: story `Stories.Constrained`._
_Example: story `Stories.Phone`._
_Example: story `Stories.PhoneLongPrimary`._
_Example: story `Stories.Frame`._
_Example: story `Stories.NarrowestFrame`._
_Example: story `Stories.PanelMinimum`._

When the filters fold, the list can still be narrowed by them. Pass `activeFilters`, the number of filters that apply (with a DataTable, `table.state.columnFilters.length`): while the filters are folded, More shows it as a [Count](?path=/docs/components-count--docs) and says it in its name, "More filters, 2 applied". At 0, or while the filters are in the row where each shows its own state, nothing is added.

_Example: story `Stories.AppliedFiltersFolded`._

## States

The toolbar has no states of its own; its controls have theirs. The search field is empty (the placeholder names what is searched), typed, or focused, and the table under it narrows on every keystroke. A DataTable says the result once the reader stops typing, filtering or paging ("8 of 24 tasks", "No matching tasks") through the page's announcer. Over a plain Table the caller says it: a count at the end in a polite `role="status"`, as in Live, or `announce()`.

The search is live, so Enter does nothing: a toolbar inside a form, as in a dialog that links the records a reader picks, never submits the form when the reader presses Enter to search. The clear button and Escape empty the search through `onSearch("")` and keep focus in it; with the search empty, Escape reaches the dialog or popover around the toolbar.

_Example: story `Stories.InAForm`._

A saved view focused from the search shows its whole ring: the views strip scrolls sideways, and the focus ring of a control inside it is drawn inside the strip rather than cut off.

_Example: story `Stories.FocusedView`._

## Modifiers

- **`search`, `onSearch`, `placeholder`**: the field, its value, and what it searches. Without `onSearch` there is no field. The clear button and Escape call `onSearch("")`.
- **`defaultSearch`**: the first query when the toolbar owns it. Pass `onSearch` without `search` and the field keeps what the reader types; pass `search` to own the query.
- **`views`**: saved-view controls immediately after search. They never fold.
- **`filters`**: filters, after saved views. The first to fold into More.
- **`activeFilters`**: how many filters apply. While they are folded, More counts them and names the count.
- **`children`**: display controls, such as grouping, columns, settings and an overflow of collection commands. They fold into More after the filters.
- **`actions`**: what sits at the end. They never fold.
- **`className`** for a frame's own padding; inside a DataTable the frame gives it.
- **Native div props and a ref** reach the row: an `id`, `data-` attributes, and a role with a name where the row is the page's search (`role="search"` with an `aria-label`). The row keeps its own `data-slot`.

_Example: story `Stories.NativeAttributes`._

## Content

- **The placeholder names what is searched**: "Search controls", "Control or title". Not "Search…".
- **Filters are nouns**: Owner, Status, Gaps.
- **Up to five actions**; more go under a More menu. The primary last.
- **A count reads "12 of 340 controls"**, tabular, `font.body.small` in `color.text.subtle`. It is text, not a Badge or a Count.

More's own words come from the locale, like the other labels the kit writes; the caller writes the placeholder, the filters and the actions in the reader's language.

_Example: story `Stories.Localized`._

## Style

| Element | Token                                                                                                                                                           |
| ------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Row     | flex, one row, or two when it has a search (three when More and the primary cannot share one) · gap `space.100` · container-driven fold into More               |
| Search  | up to 240px on one row; on two, the first row up to the saved views · `dimension.control.small` · the search icon `dimension.icon.small` in `color.icon.subtle` |
| Actions | at the end · gap `space.100`                                                                                                                                    |
| Count   | `font.body.small` `color.text.subtle` · tabular numerals                                                                                                        |

## Accessibility

- **A plain row, not the ARIA `toolbar` role.** That role promises arrow-key movement between its controls; a row of a search field, chips and buttons is better served by Tab in reading order, so Toolbar renders a plain layout div.
- **The search field is named** by its placeholder through `aria-label`; the icon is decorative. Its clear button is named "Clear search" and is not a Tab stop, since Escape does the same; see [SearchField](?path=/docs/components-searchfield--docs).
- **Focus stays visible** on every control in the row, the saved views included: the views strip draws a focused control's ring inside itself.
- **The result is said, not only shown.** A DataTable announces it after a search, a filter or a page; over a plain Table the caller's count at the end is a polite status (States).
- **The chips say pressed**; a chip that opens a popover says expanded. See FilterChip.
- **Order:** search, saved views, filters, display controls, actions. The reader narrows first and acts last, and Tab follows. Two rows are the same order wrapped, so Tab and a screen reader read the same sequence at every width.
- **More says what it holds**: "More filters", "More display options" or "More filters and display options", and with `activeFilters` how many of the folded filters apply: "More filters, 2 applied". Its popover is a dialog named by its title: Filters, Display, or Filters and display; below filters, the display controls are a group named Display. Each name is a locale message (`moreFilters`, `moreDisplay`, `moreFiltersAndDisplay`, `moreFiltersApplied`, `moreFiltersAndDisplayApplied`, `filters`, `display`, `filtersAndDisplay`, and `more` for the visible label), so a `LedgerProvider` translates them. It uses ordinary Tab navigation, so nested filters and menus keep their own behavior. Escape closes one layer at a time: an inner menu first, back to its trigger, then More, back to More.
- **Focus never falls to the page.** A control that folds while it has focus hands it to More; when More goes away, focus moves to the first control that came back. Closing More returns focus to it, unless the reader has moved on, as into a dialog that a command in More opened.

## Props

_Props of `Toolbar`, generated from its types:_

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `search` | `string` |  | The query, when the caller owns it. Pair it with `onSearch`. |
| `defaultSearch` | `string` |  | The first query, when the toolbar owns it: pass `onSearch` without `search`. |
| `onSearch` | `((value: string) => void)` |  | Called with the query as the reader types, clears or presses Escape. Without it there is no search field. |
| `placeholder` | `string` |  | What is searched: the field's placeholder and its accessible name. "Search" when unsaid. |
| `views` | `ReactNode` |  | Saved-view controls immediately after search. They stay visible and scroll inside their space. |
| `children` | `ReactNode` |  | Display controls, such as grouping, columns and settings, at the end. They fold into More, after the filters, when the row cannot hold them. |
| `filters` | `ReactNode` |  | Filters, after saved views. They are the first to move into More when the row cannot hold everything. |
| `activeFilters` | `number` |  | How many filters apply, such as a DataTable's `table.state.columnFilters.length`. While the filters are folded, More shows the number and says it in its name ("More filters, 2 applied"), so a folded filter still shows the list is narrowed. Nothing shows at 0. |
| `actions` | `ReactNode` |  | The row's actions, last. They always stay visible with their full labels. |

## Related

- [Table](?path=/docs/components-table--docs) below it; [Pagination](?path=/docs/components-pagination--docs) under the table.
- [DataTable](?path=/docs/patterns-data-table--docs): `DataTable.Filter`, `.Presets`, `.Sort`, `.Columns` and `.Settings` are the parts a toolbar holds when the table has state, and the toolbar's own search takes `table.state.globalFilter` and `table.setGlobalFilter`; `DataTable.Search` is for a composition without a Toolbar. `.SelectionBar` takes the Toolbar's place in the `toolbar` slot while rows are chosen.
- [SearchField](?path=/docs/components-searchfield--docs): the search, on its own.
- [FilterChip](?path=/docs/components-filterchip--docs), [ToggleGroup](?path=/docs/components-togglegroup--docs): the filters.
- [PageHeader](?path=/docs/layout-pageheader--docs) names a standalone register; Section can name an embedded collection.

## Don't

Every control in the row is the small size, up to five actions sit at the end with the primary last, and the primary goes in `actions`, never as a child beside the search, a default-size Button among small ones, or seven actions in a row.

_Example: story `Stories.Dont`._

<!-- page: Patterns/WorkPane (src/stories/patterns/WorkPane.mdx) -->

# WorkPane

**Status: Stable.**

Master-detail, as a mail client draws it: a list of records that is the navigation, and the chosen record's detail beside it. Choosing a row never leaves the page, and the list holds still while the detail changes. Use it where the reader works through a long list one record at a time, deciding each as they go: tailoring a catalog's controls, setting its parameters. A list the reader scans, sorts and filters is a [DataTable](?path=/docs/patterns-data-table--docs); a preview of one row of a register is the register's panel.

_Example: story `Stories.WorkPaneStory`._

## Layout

The pane measures its own width, not the window's, so it behaves the same in a page, a dialog or a panel.

| Pane width     | Layout                                                                                                                                                                              |
| -------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 768px and more | Side by side: the list column at `dimension.layout.list` (or `listWidth`), a hairline, the detail. Choosing a row changes the detail and focus stays on the row.                    |
| Narrower       | A drill-in: the list alone; choosing a row puts its detail in the list's place with a Back button above it, and focus moves to the detail's first heading. Back returns to the row. |

Side by side, the list sticks where the reader scrolls: under the shell's header on a page, at the top of its own scroller in a dialog's body or a panel, and never taller than that scroller, so its last rows stay reachable. The label and the toolbar stay put above the rows, and a focused row always scrolls in below them.

## Anatomy

| Part       | What it is                                                                                                                         |
| ---------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Label      | `listLabel`: what the list is. It names the list's landmark and the list. Text, or a VisuallyHidden when a dialog's title says it. |
| Toolbar    | `listToolbar`, under the label: the search, a filter, the count.                                                                   |
| Rows       | `list`: WorkPane.Row, or Items that select in place, in one Item.Group.                                                            |
| List empty | `listEmpty`: a compact Empty with the way out when the search leaves no rows.                                                      |
| Detail     | `detail`: the chosen row's record, with its heading first.                                                                         |
| Empty      | `empty`: an Empty beside the list while nothing is chosen; `detail` stays undefined until something is.                            |
| Back       | Stacked only, above the detail: `backLabel`, "Back to list" by default from the locale.                                            |

A row (WorkPane.Row) is a Dot for its state, the title, and under it the id and the `meta`, the state in words. Its name is the id and the title together ("AC-2, Account management"), because rows can share a title.

## Drill-in

_Example: story `Stories.DrillIn`._

Stacked, the pane shows one side at a time. The detail stays mounted while the list shows, and the list while the detail shows, so a half-written rationale and the list's search survive Back. When a primary outside the pane (a dialog's footer) submits the detail's form while the list shows, the detail comes back and focus stays put, so the form can take it to the field that needs fixing. A chosen row's `onSelect` may return a promise, for a guard that asks before it discards a draft: the detail opens once it settles, and not when it resolves `false`. Keep editing leaves the reader where they were, with focus back on the row they chose.

_Example: story `Stories.GuardedChoice`._

The pane keeps which side shows. A caller that decides it, such as a dialog that opens on a chosen row, passes `defaultView="detail"`, or controls it with `view` and `onViewChange`: a chosen WorkPane.Row asks for `detail`, and Back for `list`. A change of `view` from outside moves focus the same way. When the pane narrows under the reader (a resize, a zoom), the side that holds focus stays on screen; when the detail goes while it holds focus, focus returns to the list.

## Keyboard

_Example: story `Stories.OneTabStop`._

The list is one Tab stop: the row last focused, else the open row, else the first. Up and Down move between rows, Home and End go to the first and the last, and typing the start of a name goes to the next row that has it. Enter or Space chooses. Tab leaves the list for the detail.

## In a dialog

_Example: story `Stories.InADialog`._

In a dialog the list sticks to the dialog's body. Keep the sticky part short, a search and a count, so a short window still shows rows under it; a filter with several choices belongs in the dialog's header or a Filters popover. The dialog's primary submits the detail's form through `form`, as any dialog form does; stacked, a submit from the list brings the detail back for its errors.

## States

_Example: story `Stories.NothingChosenAndNoMatches`._

| State          | What shows                                                              |
| -------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Nothing chosen | `empty` beside the list; stacked, the list alone.                       |
| Chosen         | The row's selected fill and `aria-current`, and its detail.             |
| No rows        | `listEmpty` in the list's place, with the action that brings rows back. |

## Content

- **The label names the list** in a few words: "Catalog controls", "Parameters". The search, the filter and the count go in `listToolbar`.
- **A row's meta says its state in words**: "In effective set", "No recorded value". The Dot repeats it as a colour; a `tone` other than `neutral` needs the `meta` that says it.
- **The detail starts with a heading** that names the record, so the drill-in has somewhere to put focus.
- **`backLabel` says where Back goes**: "Back to controls".

## Accessibility

- The list is a complementary landmark and an ordered list, both named by `listLabel` ("List" from the locale when there is none).
- Each row is one button (or link), named by its id and title, described by its meta, with `aria-current="true"` on the open row.
- The list costs one Tab stop, whatever its length; the arrow keys, Home, End and type-ahead move within it.
- Stacked, choosing moves focus to the detail's first heading and Back returns it to the row that opened it, scrolled into view.
- A focused row scrolls in below the label and the toolbar that stay put over the rows.

## Props

_Props of `WorkPane`, generated from its types:_

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `listLabel` | `ReactNode` |  | What the list is: "Catalog controls". It names the list's landmark and the list itself, and stays put above the rows while they scroll. Text, or a VisuallyHidden when the dialog's title already says it. |
| `listToolbar` | `ReactNode` |  | Above the rows, under the label, staying put with it: the list's search, its filter, its count. Never its name, which is `listLabel`. |
| `list` (required) | `ReactNode` |  | The rows: WorkPane.Row, or Items that select in place. They stack in one list. |
| `listEmpty` | `ReactNode` |  | What the list shows when it has no rows: a compact Empty with the way out ("Clear the search"). |
| `detail` | `ReactNode` |  | The detail of the chosen row, beside the list or, stacked, in its place. Leave it undefined while nothing is chosen, and `empty` shows beside the list. |
| `empty` | `ReactNode` |  | What the detail shows when nothing is chosen, beside the list: an Empty. Stacked, the list shows alone until a row is chosen. |
| `listWidth` | `number` |  | The list column in pixels, `dimension.layout.list` (340) by default: narrower for a list of short names. |
| `view` | `"detail" \| "list"` |  | Stacked, the pane that shows. Controlled; a WorkPane.Row that is chosen asks for `detail` and Back for `list` through `onViewChange`. |
| `defaultView` | `"detail" \| "list"` |  | Stacked, the pane that shows first: `detail` when the pane opens on a chosen row. `list` by default. |
| `onViewChange` | `((view: WorkPaneView) => void)` |  | Stacked, a row was chosen (`detail`) or Back pressed (`list`). |
| `backLabel` | `string` |  | Stacked, the Back button's words: "Back to controls". "Back to list" by default, from the locale. |

### WorkPane.Row

_Props of `WorkPaneRow`, generated from its types:_

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `tone` | `"danger" \| "information" \| "neutral" \| "success" \| "warning"` | `neutral` | The Dot before the title: the row's state as a colour. A colour is never the state alone, so a tone other than `neutral` needs the `meta` that says it in words. |
| `meta` | `ReactNode` |  | After the id, subtle: the state as a word, the method, how long ago. |
| `id` (required) | `ReactNode` |  | The record's id, under the title with the meta. It is also part of the row's name ("AC-2, Account management"), since rows can share a title. |
| `title` (required) | `ReactNode` |  | The row's name, one line. |
| `isActive` | `boolean` |  | The row whose detail is open: a selected fill, and `aria-current` on its button. |
| `onSelect` (required) | `() => boolean \| void \| Promise<unknown>` |  | Chooses the row. Return a promise to open the detail once it settles (a guard that asks first), and resolve `false` to stay on the list. |

## Related

- [Item](?path=/docs/components-item--docs): the row and the list WorkPane is built on.

## Don't

The label names the list and the search sits in `listToolbar`, never a search as the label. Nothing chosen is an Empty in the detail, never a grey sentence.

_Example: story `Stories.Dont`._

# Tokens

Every design value is a token. The utility is the Tailwind class the lint allows; the CSS variable carries the light and dark values. Deprecated tokens are rejected by `ledger/no-deprecated-token`.

# Public exports

Every value and type exported from `@ledger/design-system`, from the public API baseline (`api/public-api.json`), grouped by the layer that declares it. Product code imports these from the package root and never declares a local copy (`ledger/no-kit-shadow`). A name not listed here is not an export: a story helper such as `Matrix`, `Specimens` or `Pair` included.

## Primitives

Values: `Bleed`, `Box`, `Flex`, `Grid`, `Heading`, `HeadingLevelProvider`, `Inline`, `Stack`, `Text`, `useHeadingLevel`, `VisuallyHidden`.
